children.text: sa evāpratirūpavadanenānumitaḥ sa prajāpatervāci gataḥ pāpmā, kāraṇānuvidhāyi hi kāryamiti //2//
children.translated_text: That same [evil], inferred through the speaking of improper things, is the evil that has entered the speech of <s>Prajāpati</s> [i.e. his creation], for the effect follows the cause. (2)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.2:] The gods, having thus determined, said to Speech — the deity presiding over speech — 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us; perform the act of chanting.' Having seen that the deity of speech was capable of accomplishing the <s>Udgītha</s>, and [recognizing] that very deity as the one to be invoked by the <s>japa</s>-mantras and to be meditated upon — 'Lead me from the unreal to the real' (BṛUp 1.3.28) — [they addressed her]. Here, the deities of speech and the rest are intended as agents of meditation and action. Why? Because, in the ultimate sense, all transactional usage of knowledge and action belongs to the agent pertaining to that [sense faculty]. For [the text] will declare in the sixth [chapter] at length that there is no agency of the <s>Ātman</s>: 'It thinks as it were, it moves as it were' (BṛUp 4.3.7). Here too, at the end of this very chapter, [the text] will conclude that the entire aggregate of action, agent, instrument, and result — consisting of the unmanifest and the rest — 'This [universe] is indeed threefold: name, form, and action' (BṛUp 1.6.1) — belongs to the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). But what is beyond the unmanifest, called the <s>Paramātman</s>, the object of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), devoid of name, form, and action — that [the text] will conclude separately by the negation of everything else: '<s>neti neti</s>' ('not this, not this') (BṛUp 2.3.6). And as for the transmigrating self (<s>saṃsāryātman</s>) that is imagined through the limiting adjunct of the aggregate of speech and the rest — [the text] will show that it too belongs to the side of the aggregate of speech and the rest: 'Rising from these beings, [the self] is destroyed along with them' (BṛUp 2.4.12). Therefore, it is proper that the intention is to ascribe the agency of knowledge, action, and the attainment of their fruits to speech and the rest alone. 'So be it' — having been so addressed by the gods, Speech chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them, for the supplicants, for their benefit. What then was the specific result accomplished by Speech through the act of chanting for the gods? This is stated — whatever enjoyment, whatever benefit accrues to the aggregate of speech and the rest through the activity of speaking and the like, with Speech as the cause — that is it. For the enjoyment, the fruit produced by the activity of speaking, is common to all. That [enjoyment], having been placed [by Speech] in the three <s>Pavamāna</s> [stotras], in the remaining nine stotras, whatever beautiful, excellent speech it utters — whatever phonemes it produces — that [it keeps] for itself alone. For that which is the distinctive action of the deity of speech — the correct pronunciation of phonemes — is singled out here as 'whatever beautiful thing it speaks.' But the result of speaking that benefits the entire aggregate — that indeed belongs to the sacrificer. There, finding an opening through the connection with the attraction toward the beautiful sounds pertaining to the deity — they, the <s>Asuras</s>, knew. How? 'By this <s>Udgātṛ</s>, through the light of knowledge and action born of scripture, having overcome us — our natural knowledge — they will surpass us, they will prevail.' Having thus understood, they rushed upon the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, approached [it], and pierced it, struck it, joined it with their own evil characterized by attachment — this is the meaning.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.3-6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.3-6]

children.text:
atha ha prāṇam ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti |
tatheti tebhyaḥ prāṇa udagāyat |
yaḥ prāṇe bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat |
yat kalyāṇaṃ jighrati tad ātmane |
te 'vidur anena vai na udgātrātyeṣyantīti |
tam abhidrutya pāpmanāvidhyan |
sa yaḥ sa pāpmā yad evedam apratirūpaṃ jighrati |
sa eva sa pāpmā || BrhUp_1,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then they said to the Breath (nose): 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us.' 'So be it.' The Breath chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them. Whatever enjoyment there is in the breath (smell), that it chanted for the gods; whatever beautiful thing it smells, that [it kept] for itself. They knew: 'By this <s>Udgātṛ</s> they will surpass us.' They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil. That evil which [makes one] smell what is improper — that is that evil. (BṛUp 1.3.3)

children.text:
atha ha cakṣur ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti |
tatheti tebhyaś cakṣur udagāyat |
yaś cakṣuṣi bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat |
yat kalyāṇaṃ paśyati tad ātmane |
te 'vidur anena vai na udgātrātyeṣyantīti |
tam abhidrutya pāpmanāvidhyan |
sa yaḥ sa pāpmā yad evedam apratirūpaṃ paśyati |
sa eva sa pāpmā || BrhUp_1,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: Then they said to the Eye: 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us.' 'So be it.' The Eye chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them. Whatever enjoyment there is in the eye, that it chanted for the gods; whatever beautiful thing it sees, that [it kept] for itself. They knew: 'By this <s>Udgātṛ</s> they will surpass us.' They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil. That evil which [makes one] see what is improper — that is that evil. (BṛUp 1.3.4)

children.text:
atha ha śrotram ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti |
tatheti tebhyaḥ śrotram udagāyat |
yaḥ śrotre bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat |
yat kalyāṇaṃ śṛṇoti tad ātmane |
te 'vidur anena vai na udgātrātyeṣyantīti |
tam abhidrutya pāpmanāvidhyan |
sa yaḥ sa pāpmā |
yad evedam apratirūpaṃ śṛṇoti |
sa eva sa pāpmā || BrhUp_1,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: Then they said to the Ear: 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us.' 'So be it.' The Ear chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them. Whatever enjoyment there is in the ear, that it chanted for the gods; whatever beautiful thing it hears, that [it kept] for itself. They knew: 'By this <s>Udgātṛ</s> they will surpass us.' They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil. That evil which [makes one] hear what is improper — that is that evil. (BṛUp 1.3.5)

children.text:
atha ha mana ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti |
tatheti tebhyo mana udagāyat |
yo manasi bhogas taṃ devebhya āgāyat |
yat kalyāṇaṃ saṃkalpayati tad ātmane |
te 'vidur anena vai na udgātrātyeṣyantīti |
tam abhidrutya pāpmanāvidhyan |
sa yaḥ sa pāpmā |
yad evedam apratirūpaṃ saṃkalpayati |
sa eva sa pāpmā |
evam u khalv etā devatāḥ pāpmabhir upāsṛjan |
evam enāḥ pāpmanāvidhyan || BrhUp_1,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Then they said to the Mind: 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us.' 'So be it.' The Mind chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them. Whatever enjoyment there is in the mind, that it chanted for the gods; whatever beautiful thing it imagines, that [it kept] for itself. They knew: 'By this <s>Udgātṛ</s> they will surpass us.' They rushed upon it and pierced it with evil. That evil which [makes one] imagine what is improper — that is that evil. Thus indeed these deities were afflicted with evils; thus they were pierced with evil. (BṛUp 1.3.6)

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.3-6 tathaiva ghrāṇādidevatā udgīthanirvartatvājjapamantraprakāśyā upāsyāśceti kameṇa parīkṣitavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.3-6:] In the same manner, the deities of smell and the rest — because they are capable of accomplishing the <s>Udgītha</s> and are to be invoked by the <s>japa</s>-mantras and meditated upon — were tested in sequence.

children.text: devānāṃ caitanniścitamāsīt- vāgādidevatāḥ kameṇa parīkṣyamāṇāḥ kalyāṇaviṣayaviśeṣātmasambandhāsaṅgahetorāsurapāpmasaṃsargād udgīthanirvartanāsamarthāḥ /
children.translated_text: The gods had determined this — that the deities of speech and the rest, being tested in sequence, because of the connection with the evil of the <s>Asuras</s> caused by their attachment to the specific objects of what is beautiful — were incapable of accomplishing the <s>Udgītha</s>.

children.text: ato 'nabhidheyāḥ"asato mā sadgamaya"ityanupāsyāśca, aśuddhatvāditarāvyāpakatvācceti /
children.translated_text: Therefore they are not to be invoked by 'Lead me from the unreal to the real' (BṛUp 1.3.28), nor are they to be meditated upon, because of their impurity and because they do not pervade the others.

children.text: evamu khalvanuktā apyetāstvagādidevatāḥ kalyāṇākalyāṇākāryadarśanādevaṃ vāgādideva, enāḥ pāpmanāvidhyanpāpmanā viddhavanta iti yaduktaṃ tatpāpmabhirupāsṛjanpāpmabhiḥ saṃsargaṃ kṛtavanta ityetat //3-6 //
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, though unstated [individually], these deities of skin and the rest too — from the observation of their engagement with both beautiful and non-beautiful objects, just like the deities of speech and the rest — they were pierced by evil, meaning they had contact with evil — that which was stated. They were afflicted by evils — they had contact with evils — this is the meaning. (3-6)

children.text: vāgādidevatā upāsīnā api mṛtyatigamanāyāśaraṇāḥ santo devāḥ krameṇa-
children.translated_text: The deities of speech and the rest, even when meditated upon, being helpless for crossing beyond death, the gods in sequence —

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.7]

children.text:
atha hemam āsanyaṃ prāṇam ūcus tvaṃ na udgāyeti |
tatheti tebhya eṣa prāṇa udagāyat |
te 'vidur anena vai na udgātrātyeṣyantīti |
tam abhidrutya pāpmanāvivyatsan |
sa yathāśmānam ṛtvā loṣṭo vidhvaṃsetaivaṃ haiva vidhvaṃsamānā viṣvañco vineśuḥ |
tato devā abhavan, parāsurā |
bhavaty ātmanā, parāsya dviṣan bhrātṛvyo bhavati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: Then they said to this breath in the mouth: 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us.' 'So be it.' This breath chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> for them. They knew: 'By this <s>Udgātṛ</s> they will surpass us.' They rushed upon it and tried to pierce it with evil. Just as a clod of earth would be shattered upon striking a stone, even so they were shattered and scattered in all directions. Thereupon the gods prevailed, and the <s>Asuras</s> were defeated. He prevails through himself, and his hateful rival is defeated — he who knows this. (BṛUp 1.3.7)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.7 athānantaraṃ ha imamityabhinayapradarśanārtham /
āsanyamāsye bhavamāsanyaṃ mukhāntarbilasthaṃ prāṇamūcustvaṃ na udgāyeti /
tathetyevaṃ śaraṇamupagatebhyaḥ sa eṣa prāṇo mukhya udagāyadityādi pūrvavat /
pāpmanāvivyatsanvedhanaṃ kartumiṣṭavantaste ca doṣāsaṃsargiṇaṃ santaṃ mukhyaṃ prāṇam /
svena āsaṅgadoṣeṇa vāgādiṣu labdhaprasarāstadabhyāsānuvṛttyā saṃsrakṣyamāṇā vineśurvinaṣṭā vidhvastāḥ /
kathamiva? iti dṛṣṭānta ucyate- sa yathā sa dṛṣṭānto yathā loke 'śmānaṃ pāṣāṇamṛtvā gatvā prāpya, loṣṭaḥ pāṃsupiṇḍaḥ pāṣāṇacūrṇanāyāśmani nikṣiptaḥ svayaṃ vidhvaṃseta vistraṃseta vicūrṇībhavet, evaṃ haiva yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānta evameva, vidhvaṃsamānā viśeṣeṇa dhvaṃsamānā viṣvañco nānāgatayo vineśurvinaṣṭā yataḥ, tatastasmādāsuravināśāddevatvapratibandhabhūtebhyaḥ svābhāvikāsaṅgajanitapāpmabhyo viyogād asaṃsargadharmimukhyaprāṇāśrayabalād devā vāgādayaḥ prakṛtā abhavat /
kimabhavan? svaṃ devatārūpamagnyādyātmakaṃ vakṣyamāṇam /
pūrvamaṣyagnyādyātmana eva santaḥ svābhāvikena pāpmanā tiraskṛtavijñānāḥ piṇḍamātrābhimānā āsan /
te tatpāpmaviyogādujjhitvā piṇḍamātrābhimānaṃ śāstrasamarpitavāgādyagnyādyātmābhimānā babhūvurityarthaḥ /
kiñca te pratipakṣabhūtā asurāḥ parābhavannityanuvartate /
parābhūtā vinaṣṭā ityarthaḥ /
yathā purākalpena varṇitaḥ pūrvayajamāno 'tikrāntakālikaḥ etāmevākhyāyikārūpāṃ śrutiṃ dṛṣṭvā tenaiva krameṇa vāgādidevatāḥ parīkṣya, tāścāpohyāsaṅgapāpmāspadadoṣavattvenādoṣāspadaṃ mukhyaṃ prāṇamātmatvenopagamya vāgādyādhyātmikapiṇḍamātraparicchinnātmābhimānaṃ hitvā vairājapiṇḍābhimānaṃ vāgādyagnyādyātmaviṣayaṃ vartamānaprajāpatitvaṃ śāstraprakāśitaṃ pratipannaḥ, tathaivāyaṃ yajamānastenaiva vidhinā bhavati prajāpatisvarūpeṇātmanā /
parā cāsyā prajāpatitvapratipakṣabhūtaḥ pāpmā dviṣanbhrātṛvyo bhavati /
children.translated_text: And his adversary who is the impediment to [his] <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood — the evil, the hateful rival — is defeated.

children.text: yato 'dveṣṭāpi bhavati kaścid bhrātṛvyo bharatāditulyaḥ, yastvindriyaviṣayāsaṅgajanitaḥ pāpmā bhrātṛvyo dveṣṭā ca, pāramārthikātmasvarūpatiratiraskaraṇahetutvāt sa ca parābhavati viśīryate loṣṭavātprāṇapariṣvaṅgāt /
children.translated_text: For there may be some rival like <s>Bharata</s> and the like who does not [actually] hate; but the evil born of attachment to sense-objects — [that] is the rival and the hater, because of being the cause of obscuring the true nature of the supreme Self — and that is defeated, is destroyed, like a clod of earth, through the embrace of the <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: kasyaitatphalam? ityāha- ya evaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: Whose is this fruit? It is said — he who knows this.

children.text: yathoktaṃ prāṇamātmatvena pratipadyate pūrvayajamānavadityarthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: He who accepts the <s>prāṇa</s> as the Self in the manner described, just like the ancient sacrificer — this is the meaning. (7)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.7:] 'Then' — next. 'This' — [said] with the purpose of demonstrating by gesture. <s>Āsanya</s> — situated in the mouth (<s>āsya</s>); the breath in the mouth, the chief <s>prāṇa</s> dwelling within the cavity of the mouth — to it they said: 'You chant the <s>Udgītha</s> for us.' 'So be it' — thus, having been approached as a refuge by those gods, this chief <s>prāṇa</s> chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> — and so on, as before. They tried to pierce it with evil — they wished to strike it. But [the evil,] finding the chief <s>prāṇa</s> free from contact with defects, was itself destroyed. By its own defect of attachment, having found an opening in the deities of speech and the rest, continuing the habit of that approach, [the evil,] attempting to contaminate [the <s>prāṇa</s>], was destroyed — shattered, obliterated. Like what? An illustration is given — just as in the world, a clod of earth — a lump of dust — having gone to, reached, struck a stone, placed upon a stone for the purpose of pulverizing the stone, would itself be shattered, would disintegrate, would be reduced to powder — even so, being thoroughly shattered, scattering in all directions, they were destroyed. Because of this, because of the destruction of the <s>Asuras</s> — through separation from the evils born of the natural attachment that had been the impediment to their godhood, and by the strength of taking refuge in the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, which has the nature of being free from contamination — the gods, namely Speech and the rest who are the subject [here], prevailed. What did they become? Their own form as deities — having the nature of <s>Agni</s> and the rest, which will be described. Previously too, even while having the nature of <s>Agni</s> and the rest, their knowledge being obscured by their natural evil, they had only the consciousness of being mere bodily aggregates. Through separation from that evil, having cast off the consciousness of being mere bodily aggregates, they came to possess the consciousness of being <s>Agni</s> and the rest as presented by scripture — this is the meaning. Moreover, the <s>Asuras</s> who were their adversaries were 'defeated' — this word carries over. They were defeated, destroyed — this is the meaning. Just as the ancient sacrificer, described through the narrative of the past cycle, having seen this very narrative-form scripture, having tested the deities of speech and the rest in the same sequence, and having rejected them as flawed by the defect of being susceptible to attachment, having accepted the chief <s>prāṇa</s> as the Self — casting off the consciousness of self limited to the mere bodily aggregate of speech and the rest pertaining to the individual, and accepting the current state of <s>Prajāpati</s>, namely the consciousness of self in the cosmic aggregate (<s>Vairāja</s> body) pertaining to <s>Agni</s> and the rest as illumined by scripture — so too this sacrificer, by that very procedure, becomes one with the nature of <s>Prajāpati</s> himself.

children.text: phalamupasaṃhṛtyādhunākhyāyikārūpamevāśrityāha- kasmāccahetorvāgādīnmuktā mukhya eva prāṇa ātmatvenāśrayitavyaḥ? iti tadupapattinirūpaṇāya yasmādayaṃ vāgādīnāṃ piṇḍādīnāṃ ca sādhāraṇa ātmā, ityetamarthamākhyāyikayā darśayantyāha śrutiḥ-
children.translated_text: Having concluded with the fruit, now relying on the narrative form itself, [the text] says — for what reason should the chief <s>prāṇa</s> alone, and not the deities of speech and the rest nor the bodily aggregates, be resorted to as the Self? In order to ascertain the ground for this — because this [<s>prāṇa</s>] is the common Self of the deities of speech and the rest and of the bodily aggregates — to demonstrate this meaning through the narrative, the <s>śruti</s> says —

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.8]

children.text:
te hocuḥ -- kva nu so 'bhūd yo na ittham asakteti |
ayam āsye 'ntar iti |
so 'yāsya āṅgiraso 'ṅgānāṃ hi rasaḥ || BrhUp_1,3.8 ||
children.translated_text: They said: 'Where indeed was he who thus kept us safe?' [He is] 'here, within the mouth.' Therefore he is called <s>Āyāsya Āṅgirasa</s>, for he is the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>). (BṛUp 1.3.8)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.8 te prajāpatiprāṇā mukhyena prāṇena pariprāpitadevasvarūpā hocuruktavantaḥ phalāvasthāḥ /
kim? ityāha- kva nviti vitarke /
kva nu kasminnu so 'bhūt /
kaḥ? yo no 'smānitthamevamasakta sañjitavāndevabhāvamātmatvenopagamitavān /
smaranti hi loke kenacidupakṛtā upakāriṇam /
lokavadeva smaranto vicārayamāṇāḥ kāryakaraṇasaṃghāte ātmanyevopalabdhavantaḥ /
katham? ayamāsye 'ntariti, āsye mukhe ya ākāśastasminnantarayaṃ pratyakṣo vartata iti /
sarvo hi loko vicāryādhyavasyati, tathā devāḥ /
yasmādayamantarākāśe vāgādyātmatvena viśeṣamanāśritya vartamāna upalabdho devaiḥ, tasmātsaprāṇo 'yāsyo viśeṣānāśrayācca asakta sañjitavānvāgādīn /
ata evāṅgirasa ātmā kāryakaraṇānām /
kathamāṅgirasaḥ? prasiddhaṃ hyetadaṅgānāṃ kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇānāṃ rasaḥ sāra ātmetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: How is he <s>Āṅgirasa</s>? For this is well-known: he is the <s>rasa</s> (essence, sap) of the <s>aṅgas</s> (limbs), i.e., the body and organs — the essence, the core, the self — this is the meaning.

children.text: kathaṃ punaraṅgarasatvam? tadapāye śoṣaprāpteriti vakṣyāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: But how is he the essence of the limbs? 'Because upon his departure, desiccation ensues' — this we shall state [later].

children.text: yasmāccāyamaṅgarasatvādviśeṣāmāśritatvācca kāryakaraṇānāṃ sādhāraṇa ātmā viśuddhaśca, tasmādvāgādīnapāsya prāṇa evātmatvenāśrayitavya iti vākyārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And because this one, by virtue of being the essence of the limbs and of not resorting to any particular [identity], is the common self of the body and organs, and is pure — therefore, setting aside speech and the others, one should resort to <s>prāṇa</s> alone as the self — this is the meaning of the passage.

children.text: ātmā hyātmatvenopagantavyo 'viparītabodhācchreyaḥprāpteḥ, viparyaye svāniṣṭaprāptidarśanāt //8//
children.translated_text: For the self should be resorted to as the self, since from correct knowledge comes the highest good, and in the contrary case, the attainment of what is undesirable is seen. // 8 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.8: Those <s>prāṇas</s> of <s>Prajāpati</s>, having attained their true divine nature through the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, said — being in the state of [receiving] the fruit. What [did they say]? He says: 'Where indeed' — this is a deliberative [particle]. 'Where indeed, in what [place] was he?' Who? 'He who thus, unattached, won us over to the divine state and made us his own self.' For in the world, those who have been helped by someone remember the helper. Just as in the world, remembering and deliberating thus, they found [him] in the aggregate of body and organs — in the self itself. How? 'This one is within the mouth' — in the mouth, in the oral cavity, the space within it — this one is directly present. For everyone in the world, upon deliberation, ascertains [this], and so did the gods. Because this one was found by the gods as abiding in the inner space [of the mouth] without resorting to any particular identity as speech and the like, therefore this one, being with <s>prāṇa</s>, is of the mouth, and because of not resorting to any particular [identity], he, being unattached, won over speech and the others. Hence he is <s>Āṅgirasa</s> — the self of the aggregate of body and organs.

children.text:
syānmataṃ prāṇasya viśuddhirasiddheti /
nanu parihṛtametadvāgādīnāṃ kalyāṇavadanādyāsaṅgavatprāṇasya āsaṅgāspadatvābhāvena /
vāḍham, kiṃ tvāṅgirasatvena vāgādīnāmātmatvoktyā vāgādidvāreṇa śavasṛṣṭitatspṛṣṭerivāśuddhatā śaṅkyate- ityāha- śuddha eva praṇaḥ /
kutaḥ?
children.translated_text: [Objection:] One might think that the purity of <s>prāṇa</s> is not established. [Reply:] But was this not already addressed — by [showing] that, unlike [the contact of] speech and the others with the auspicious and so forth, there is no basis for such contact in the case of <s>prāṇa</s>? True, but by the statement that he is <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, the self of speech and the others, impurity might be suspected through the medium of speech and the others, as if touching a corpse-created [impurity]. Therefore he says: <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed pure. How so?

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.9
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.9]

children.text:
sā vā eṣā devatā dūr nāma |
dūraṃ hy asyā mṛtyur |
dūraṃ ha vā asmān mṛtyur bhavati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,3.9 ||
children.translated_text: This deity is indeed named <s>Dūr</s> (the distant one). For death is far from it. Death is indeed far from one who knows this. // BṛhUp 1.3.9 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.9 sā vā eṣā devatā dūrnāma /
yaṃ prāṇaṃ prāpyāśmānamiva loṣṭavadvidhvastā asurāstaṃ parāmṛśati seti /
saivaiṣā yeyaṃ vartamānayajamānaśarīrasthā devairnirdhāritā"ayamāsye 'ntaḥ"iti /
devatā ca sā syāt, upāsanakriyāyāḥ karmabhāvena guṇabhūtatvāt /
yasyātmā dūrnāma dūrityevaṃ khyātā /
nāmaśabdaḥ khyāpanaparyāyaḥ /
tasmātprasiddhāsyā viśuddhidūrnāmatvāt /
kutaḥ punardūrnāmatvam? ityāha- dūraṃ dūreḥ hi yasmādasyāḥ prāṇadevatāyāḥ mṛtyurāsaṅgalakṣaṇaḥ pāpmā /
asaṃśleṣadharmitvātprāṇasya samīpasthāsyāpi dūratā mṛtyostasmād dūrityevaṃ khyātiḥ, evaṃ prāṇasya viśuddhirjñāpitā /
viduṣaḥ phalamucyate- dūraṃ ha vā asmānmṛtyurbhavati /
asmādevaṃvidaḥ, ya evaṃ veda tasmādevamiti prakṛtaṃ viśuddhiguṇopetaṃ prāṇamupāsta ityarthaḥ /
upāsanaṃ nāma upāsyārthavāde yathā devatādisvarūpaṃ śrutyā jñāpyate tathā manasopagamya āsanaṃ cintanaṃ laukikapratyayāvyavadhānena yāvattaddevatādisvarūpātmābhimānābhivyaktiriti laukikātmābhimānavat /
"devo bhūtvā devānapyeti" (bṛ.u.4 / 1 / 2) "kindevato 'syāṃ prācyāṃ diśyasi" (bṛ.u.3 / 9 / 20) ityevamādiśrutibhyaḥ //9//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.9: 'This deity' — this very <s>prāṇa</s>, upon reaching which, the <s>Asuras</s> were shattered like a clod of earth against a rock — [the text] refers back to it with 'this.' This very one, which is present in the body of the current sacrificer, was ascertained by the gods as 'this one is within the mouth.' It is a deity — because worship, being an act, has the nature of a subsidiary, it would serve as its object. Its self is named <s>Dūr</s> — known as '<s>Dūr</s>' (distant). The word '<s>nāma</s>' is a synonym for '<s>khyāpana</s>' (making known). Therefore, because its well-known purity [makes it] named <s>Dūr</s>. But why is it named <s>Dūr</s>? He says: 'Far' — because death, evil characterized by contact [with sense objects], is far from this <s>prāṇa</s> deity. Because <s>prāṇa</s>'s nature is non-attachment, even though death is in close proximity, it is far — hence the designation '<s>Dūr</s>.' Thus the purity of <s>prāṇa</s> is made known. The fruit for the knower is stated: 'Death is indeed far from one who knows this' — from such a knower. 'One who knows thus' — he who thus knows and meditates upon <s>prāṇa</s> endowed with the quality of purity as described — this is the meaning. Meditation (<s>upāsana</s>) means: just as the nature of the deity and the like is made known by <s>śruti</s> in the context of the object of meditation, so [the meditator], having mentally approached [that nature], performs <s>āsana</s> (sitting, i.e., contemplation), thinking without interruption by worldly cognitions, until the manifestation of self-identification with that deity and the like — just as with worldly self-identification. [As stated in <s>śruti</s>:] 'Having become a god, he enters the gods' (BṛUp 4.1.2), 'Of which deity are you in this eastern direction?' (BṛUp 3.9.20) — from such <s>śruti</s> passages. // 9 //

children.text:
sā vā eṣā devatā dūraṃ ha vā asmānmṛtyurbhavatītyuktam /
kathaṃ punarevaṃvido dūraṃ mṛtyurbhavati? ityucyate- evaṃvittvavirodhāt /
indriyaviṣayasaṃsargāsaṅgajo hi pāpmā prāṇātmābhimānino hi virudhyate, vāgādiviśeṣātmābhimānahetutvāt svābhāvikājñānahetutvācca /
śāstrajanito hi prāṇātmābhimānaḥ /
tasmādevaṃvidaḥ pāpmā dūraṃ bhavatīti yuktaṃ virodhāt /
tadetatpradarśayati-
children.translated_text: It was said: 'This deity — death is indeed far from this one who knows thus.' But how is death far from such a knower? This is explained: because of the contradiction with such knowledge. For evil born of contact between senses and their objects is contradicted by the self-identification with <s>prāṇa</s>, since [evil] is caused by self-identification with particular [organs] such as speech and the like, and since it is caused by natural ignorance. For the self-identification with <s>prāṇa</s> is born of scripture. Therefore, it is reasonable that evil is far from such a knower, because of the contradiction. This is now illustrated:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.10
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.10]

children.text:
sā vā eṣā devataitāsāṃ devatānāṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum apahatya yatrāsāṃ diśām antas tad gamayāṃ cakāra |
tad āsāṃ pāpmano vinyadadhāt |
tasmān na janam iyān nāntam iyān net pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum anvavāyānīti || BrhUp_1,3.10 ||
children.translated_text: This deity, having repelled the evil of death from these deities, carried them beyond death to where the directions end. There it deposited their evils. Therefore one should not go to people [there], nor go to the frontier, lest one encounter the evil of death. // BṛhUp 1.3.10 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.10 sā vā eṣā devatetyuktārtham /
etāsāṃ vāgādīnāṃ devatānāṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyuṃ svābhāvikājñānaprayuktendriyaviṣayasaṃsargāsaṅgajanitena hi pāpmanā sarvo mriyate, sa hyato mṛtyuḥ, taṃ prāṇātmābhimānamātratayaiva prāṇo 'pahantetyucyate /
virodhādeva tu pāpmaivaṃvido dūraṃ gato bhavati /
kiṃ punaścakāra devatānāṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyumapahatya? ityucyate- yatra yasminnāsāṃ prācyādīnāṃ diśāmanto 'vasānaṃ tattatra gamayāñcakāra gamanaṃ kṛtavānityetat /
nanu nāsti diśāmantaḥ kathamantaṃ gamitavān? ityucyate- śrautavijñānavajjanāvadhinimittakalpitatvāddiśāṃ tadvirodhijanāvyuṣita eva deśo diśāmantaḥ, deśānto 'raṇyamiti yadvadityadoṣaḥ /
tattatra gamayitvā āsāṃ devatānām, pāpmana iti dvitīyābahuvacanam, vinyadadhādvividhaṃ nyagbhāvenadadhātsthāpitavatī prāṇadevatā /
prāṇātmābhimānaśūnyeṣu antyajaneṣviti sāmarthyāt /
indriyasaṃsargajo hi sa iti prāṇyāśrayatāvagamyate /
tasmāttamantyaṃ janaṃ neyānna gacchetsambhāṣaṇadarśanādibhirna saṃsṛjet /
tatsaṃsarge pāpmanā saṃsargaḥ kṛtaḥ syātpāpmāśrayo hi saḥ /
tajjananivāsaṃ cāntaṃ digantaśabdavācyaṃ neyājjanaśūnyamapi, janamapi taddeśaviyuktamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor should one go to the frontier — the place designated by the word 'end of the directions,' the dwelling-place of those people — even if it is uninhabited by people, and [one should avoid] people too even if separated from that region — this is the intent.

children.text: nediti paribhayārthe nipātaḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Ned</s>' is an indeclinable in the sense of apprehensive caution.

children.text: itthaṃ janasaṃsarge pāpmānaṃ mṛtyumanvavāyānīti /
children.translated_text: Thus, [lest] through association with those people, one encounter the evil of death.

children.text: anu ava ayānītyanugaccheyamiti, evaṃ bhīto na janamantaṃ ceyāditi pūrveṇa sambandhaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: '<s>Anu ava āyānī</s>' — 'may I follow [it]' — thus fearing, one should not go to the people or the frontier — this connects with the preceding. // 10 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.10: 'This deity' — this has been explained. Having repelled the evil of death from these deities of speech and the like — for by the evil, the contact between senses and objects, prompted by natural ignorance — everyone dies through that evil, and therefore it is death — that [evil], <s>prāṇa</s> repels merely by the self-identification with <s>prāṇa</s>, it is said. For it is by contradiction alone that evil is removed from such a knower. Now, what did [the deity] do after repelling the evil of death from the deities? This is said: to where the directions end — to the frontier, the limit of the directions such as the east — there it carried [the evil], made it go. But is there not no end to the directions? How then did it carry [evil] to their end? This is explained: just as the directions are imagined on the basis of the limits of human habitation, through the force of <s>śruti</s>-based understanding, similarly, the frontier uninhabited by people, in contradiction with [habitation], is the end of the directions — [as when] the end of the region is said to be the wilderness — there is no fault. Having carried [the evil] there, [it deposited] the evils of those deities — the second case plural — it deposited them, placed them firmly in a downward [i.e., degraded] manner — the <s>prāṇa</s> deity did. [This means:] among the outcaste people who are devoid of self-identification with <s>prāṇa</s> — this is implied by the context. For since [evil] is born of sense-contact, it is understood as having its locus in living beings. Therefore, one should not go to those people — one should not go, should not associate with them through conversation, sight, and the like. Through association with them, association with evil would be produced — for they are the locus of evil.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.11
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.11]

children.text: sā vā eṣā devataitāsāṃ devatānāṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum apahatyāthainā mṛtyum atyavahat || BrhUp_1,3.11 ||
children.translated_text: This deity, having repelled the evil of death from these deities, then carried them beyond death. // BṛhUp 1.3.11 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.11 sā vā eṣā devatā, tadetatprāṇātmajñānakarmaphalaṃ vāgādīnāmagnyādyātmatvamucyate /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.11: 'This deity' — this, the fruit of the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s> as the self, is now stated as the attainment by speech and the others of their [true nature as] <s>Agni</s> and the like.

children.text: athainā mṛtyumatyavahat tasmādādhyātmikaparicchedakaraḥ pāpmā mṛtyuḥ prāṇātmavijñānenapahatastasmātsaprāṇo 'pahantā pāpmano mṛtyoḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Then it carried them beyond death' — therefore, the evil that causes delimitation in the individual sphere (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), which is death, is repelled by the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s> as the self. Therefore, this <s>prāṇa</s> is the repeller of evil, of death.

children.text: tasmātsa eva prāṇa enā vāgādidevatāḥ prakṛtaṃ pāpmānaṃ mṛtyumatītya avahatprāpayatsvaṃ svamaparicchinnamagnyādidevātātmarūpam //11//
children.translated_text: Therefore, that very <s>prāṇa</s> — these deities of speech and the like — having transcended the evil, death, which is the topic — carried them, led them to their own unlimited nature as <s>Agni</s> and other deities. // 11 //

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.12
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.12]

children.text:
sā vai vācam eva prathamām atyavahat |
sā yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata so 'gnir abhavat |
so 'yam agniḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrānto dīpyate || BrhUp_1,3.12 ||
children.translated_text: It carried speech first. When speech was freed from death, it became fire. This fire, having gone beyond death, shines. // BṛhUp 1.3.12 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.12. sa vai vācameva prathamāmatyavahat /
sa prāṇo vācameva prathamāṃ pradhānāmityetat /
udgīthakarmaṇītarakaraṇāpekṣayā sādhakatamatvaṃ prādhānyaṃ tasyāḥ /
tāṃ prathamāmatyavahadvahanaṃ kṛtavān /
tasyāḥ punarmṛtyumatītyoḍhāyāḥ kiṃ rūpam? ityucyate- sā vāgyadā yasminkāle pāpmānaṃ mṛtyum atyamucyatātītyāmucyata mocitā svayameva, tadāsognirabhavat /
sā vākpūrvamapyagnireva satī mṛtyuviyoge 'pyagnirevābhavat /
children.translated_text: That speech, even before, was indeed <s>Agni</s>; and upon separation from death too, it became <s>Agni</s> again.

children.text: etāvāṃstu viśeṣo mṛtyuviyoge /
children.translated_text: But this much is the distinction upon separation from death:

children.text: soyamatikrānto 'gniḥ pareṇamṛtyuṃ parastānmṛtyordīpyate /
children.translated_text: This <s>Agni</s>, having transcended death, shines — beyond death, on the other side of death.

children.text: prāṅmokṣānmṛtyupratibaddho adhyātmavāgātmanā nedānīmiva dīptimānāsīt, idānīṃ tu mṛtyuṃ pareṇa dīpyate mṛtyuviyogāt //12//
children.translated_text: Before liberation, [speech], bound by death in its individual-self form as speech, was not as resplendent as it is now. But now it shines beyond death, due to separation from death. // 12 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.12: 'It carried speech first.' That <s>prāṇa</s> carried speech first — 'first' meaning principal — this is the sense. Its preeminence [is established] because, in the activity of the <s>Udgītha</s>, it is the most effective instrument compared to the other organs. It carried that principal [speech] — performed the carrying. What then is the nature of that speech, once carried beyond death? This is said: when speech — at the time when — was freed from the evil of death, was liberated — it became fire. Then it became this <s>Agni</s> (fire).

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.13
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.13]

children.text:
atha prāṇam atyavahat |
sa yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata sa vāyur abhavat |
so 'yaṃ vāyuḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrāntaḥ pavate || BrhUp_1,3.13 ||
children.translated_text: Then it carried the [nasal] <s>prāṇa</s>. When it was freed from death, it became wind. This wind, having gone beyond death, blows. // BṛhUp 1.3.13 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.13 tathā prāṇo ghrāṇam- vāyurabhavat /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.13: Similarly, <s>prāṇa</s> [carried] the sense of smell — it became wind.

children.text: sa tu pavate mṛtyuṃ pareṇātikrāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: That [wind] blows, having gone beyond death.

children.text: sarvamanyaduktārtham //13//
children.translated_text: Everything else has been explained. // 13 //

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.14
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.14]

children.text:
atha cakṣur atyavahat |
tad yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata sa ādityo 'bhavat |
so 'sāv ādityaḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrāntas tapati || BrhUp_1,3.14 ||
children.translated_text: Then it carried the eye. When the eye was freed from death, it became the sun. That sun, having gone beyond death, shines. // BṛhUp 1.3.14 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.14 tathā cakṣurādityo 'bhavatsa tu tapati //14//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.14: Similarly, the eye became the sun; it shines. // 14 //

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.15
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.15]

children.text:
atha śrotram atyavahat |
tad yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata tā diśo 'bhavan |
tā imā diśaḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrāntāḥ || BrhUp_1,3.15 ||
children.translated_text: Then it carried the ear. When the ear was freed from death, they became the directions. These directions, having gone beyond death, [persist]. // BṛhUp 1.3.15 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.15 tathā śrotraṃ diśo 'bhavat /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.15: Similarly, the ear became the directions.

children.text: diśaḥ prācyādivibhāgenāvasthitāḥ //15//
children.translated_text: The directions are established in their division as east and so forth. // 15 //

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.16
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.16]

children.text:
atha mano 'tyavahat |
tad yadā mṛtyum atyamucyata sa candramā abhavat |
so 'sau candraḥ pareṇa mṛtyum atikrānto bhāti |
evaṃ ha vā enam eṣā devatā mṛtyum ativahati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,3.16 ||
children.translated_text: Then it carried the mind. When the mind was freed from death, it became the moon. That moon, having gone beyond death, shines. Thus indeed this deity carries beyond death one who knows this. // BṛhUp 1.3.16 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.16 manaścandramā bhāti /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.16: The mind [became] the moon; it shines.

children.text: yathā pūrvayajamānaṃ vāgādyagnyādibhāvena mṛtyumatyavahat, evamenaṃ vartamānayajamānamapi ha vā eṣā prāṇadevatā mṛtyumativahati vāgādyagnyādibhāvena /
children.translated_text: Just as [the deity] carried the former sacrificer beyond death [by transforming] speech and the others into <s>Agni</s> and the other [cosmic forms], so too this <s>prāṇa</s> deity carries even the present sacrificer beyond death [by transforming] speech and the others into <s>Agni</s> and the other [cosmic forms].

children.text: evaṃ yo vāgādipañcakaviśiṣṭaṃ prāṇaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: Thus, for one who knows <s>prāṇa</s> as endowed with the five [functions] of speech and the others.

children.text: "taṃ yathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati"iti śruteḥ //16//
children.translated_text: Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'Whatever he meditates upon, that he becomes.' // 16 //

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.17
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.3.17]

children.text:
athātmane 'nnādyam āgāyat |
yad dhi kiñcānnam adyate 'nenaiva tad adyate |
iha pratitiṣṭhati || BrhUp_1,3.17 ||
children.translated_text: Then he sang for himself food. For whatever food is eaten is eaten by this [<s>prāṇa</s>] alone. He is established here. // BṛhUp 1.3.17 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.17 yathā vāgādibhirātmārthamāgānaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā mukhyo 'pi prāṇaḥ sarvaprāṇasādhāraṇaṃ prājāpatyaphalamāgānaṃ kṛtvā triṣu pamāneṣu, athānantaraṃ śiṣṭeṣu navasu, stotreṣu, ātmane ātmārthamannādyamannaṃ ca tadādyaṃ cānnādyamāgāyat /
kartuḥ kāmasaṃyogo vācanika ityuktam /
kathaṃ punastadannādyaṃ prāṇenātmārthamāgītamiti gamyate? ityatra hetumāha- yatkiñceti sāmānyānnamātraparāmarśārthaḥ /
hīti hetau /
yasmālloke prāṇibhiryadkiñcidannamadyatebhakṣyate tadanenaiva /
ana iti prāṇasyākhyā prasiddhā anaḥ śabdaḥ sāntaḥ śakaṭavācī, yastvanyaḥ svarāntaḥ sa prāṇaparyāyaḥ /
prāṇenaiva tadadyata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: By <s>prāṇa</s> alone that food is eaten — this is the meaning.

children.text: kiñca na kevalaṃ prāṇenādyata evānnādyam, tasmiñcharīrākārapariṇate 'nnādya iha pratitiṣṭhati prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, not only is the food eaten by <s>prāṇa</s>, but in that food — when it has been transformed into the form of the body — <s>prāṇa</s> is established here.

children.text: tasmātprāṇenātmanaḥ pratiṣṭhārthamāgītamannādyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the food was sung by <s>prāṇa</s> for the purpose of its own establishment.

children.text: yadapi prāṇenānnādanaṃ tadapi pratiṣṭhārthameveti na vāgādiṣviva kalyāṇasaṅgajapātmasambhavaḥ prāṇe 'sti //17//
children.translated_text: And the eating of food by <s>prāṇa</s> is also for the purpose of establishment alone — therefore, there is no arising of taint from contact with the auspicious [or inauspicious] in <s>prāṇa</s>, as there is in speech and the others. // 17 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.3.17: Just as the singing was done by speech and the others for the sake of the self, so too the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, having performed the singing for the fruit common to all <s>prāṇas</s> — the fruit pertaining to <s>Prajāpati</s> — in the three <s>pavamāna</s> [recitations], thereupon in the remaining nine <s>stotras</s>, he sang for himself the food — both the food and its edibility, i.e., the capacity to be eaten. 'The agent's connection with desire is verbal' — this was stated [elsewhere]. But how is it understood that the food was sung by <s>prāṇa</s> for its own sake? To this he gives the reason: 'Whatever' — this is for the purpose of referring to food in general. The word 'hi' indicates a reason. Because in the world, whatever food is eaten — consumed — by living beings, it is eaten by this [<s>prāṇa</s>] alone. '<s>Ana</s>' — the well-known designation of <s>prāṇa</s>; the word '<s>ana</s>' ending in a short vowel denotes a cart, but the other [word] ending in a long vowel is a synonym for <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text:
nanvavadhāraṇamayuktaṃ prāṇenaiva tadadyata iti, vāgādīnāmapi annanimittopakāradarśanāt /
naiṣa doṣaḥ, prāṇadvāratvāttadupakārasya /
kathaṃ prāṇadvārako 'nnakṛtau vāgādīnāmupakāra ityetamarthaṃ pradarśayannāha-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But is not the exclusive restriction — 'by <s>prāṇa</s> alone it was eaten' — unjustified, since the assistance of speech and the other [senses] is also observed in the context of food? This is not a fault, because their assistance is mediated through <s>prāṇa</s>. To show how the assistance of speech and the other [senses] in the production of food is mediated through <s>prāṇa</s>, [the text] says:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.18
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.18]

children.text:
te devā abruvan |
etāvad vā idaṃ sarvaṃ yad annam |
tad ātmana āgāsīḥ |
anu no 'sminn anna ābhajasveti |
te vai mābhisaṃviśateti |
tatheti taṃ samantaṃ pariṇyaviśanta |
tasmād yad anenānnam atti tenaitās tṛpyanti |
evaṃ ha vā enaṃ svā abhisaṃviśanti bhartā svānāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ puraetā bhavaty annādo 'dhipatir ya evaṃ veda |
ya u haivaṃvidaṃ sveṣu pratir bubhūṣati na haivālaṃ bhāryebhyo bhavati |
atha ya evaitam anubhavati yo vaitam anu bhāryān bubhūrṣati sa haivālaṃ bhāryebhyo bhavati || BrhUp_1,3.18 ||
children.translated_text: The gods said: 'This is indeed all — that which is food. You have obtained it for yourself. Give us a share in this food.' 'Then enter into me' — [he said]. 'So be it' — [they said,] and they entered into him, surrounding him on all sides. Therefore, whatever food one eats through this [<s>prāṇa</s>], by that they are satisfied. Thus indeed do his kinsmen gather around one who knows this: he becomes the nourisher of his kinsmen, the chief, the leader, the eater of food, the overlord — one who knows thus. And whoever among his kinsmen tries to rival such a knower — he is not able to support his dependents. But one who follows this [knower] and who, following him, wishes to nourish his dependents — he indeed is able to support his dependents. (BṛUp 1.3.18)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.18 te vāgādayo devāḥ, svaviṣayadyotanāddevāḥ, abruvannuktavanto mukhyaṃ prāṇam idametāvannāto 'dhikamasti /
vā iti smaraṇārthaḥ /
idaṃ tatsarvametāvadeva, kim? yadannaṃ prāṇasthitikaramadyate loke tatsarvamātmana ātmārthamāgāsīḥ āgītavānasi āgānenātmasātkṛtamityarthaḥ /
vayaṃ cānnamantareṇa sthātuṃ notsāmahe /
ato 'nu paścānnosmānasminnanne ātmārthe tavānne ābhajasva ābhājayasva /
ṇico 'śravaṇaṃ chāndasam /
asmāṃścānnabhāginaḥ kuru /
itara āha- te yūyaṃ yadyannārthino vai, mā māmabhisaṃviśata samantato māmābhimukhyena niviśata /
ityevamuktavati prāṇe tathetyevamiti, taṃ prāṇaṃ pariveṣṭya niviṣṭavanta ityarthaḥ /
tathā niviṣṭānāṃ prāṇānujñayā teṣāṃ prāṇe naivādyamānaṃ prāṇasthitikaraṃ sadannaṃ tṛptikaraṃ bhavati na svātantryeṇa /
tasmādyuktamevāvadhāraṇam anenaiva tadadyata iti /
tadeva cāha- tasmādyasmātprāṇāśrayatayaiva prāṇānujñayābhisanniviṣṭā vāgādidevatāḥ tasmādyadannamanena prāṇenātti lokastenānnenaitā vāgādyāstṛpyanti /
vāgādyāśrayaṃ prāṇaṃ yo veda vāgādayaśca pañca prāṇāśrayā iti tamapyevamevaṃ ha vai svā jñātasya abhisaṃviśanti vāgādaya iva prāṇam /
jñātīnāmāśrayaṇīyo bhavatītyabhiprāyaḥ /
abhisanniviṣṭānāṃ ca svānāṃ prāṇavadeva vāgādīnāṃ svānnena bhartā bhavati /
tathā śreṣṭhaḥ puro 'grata etā gantā bhavati vāgādīnāmiva prāṇaḥ /
tathānnādo 'nāmayāvītyarthaḥ /
adhipatiradhiṣṭhāya ca pālayitā svatantraḥ patiḥ prāṇavadeva vāgādīnām /
ya evaṃ prāṇaṃ veda tasyaitadyathoktaṃ phalaṃ bhavati /

kiñca ya u haivaṃvidhaṃ prāṇavidaṃ prati sveṣu jñātīnāṃ madhye pratiḥ pratikūlo bubhūrṣati pratispardhī bhavitumicchati, sosurā iva, prāṇapratispardhino na haivālaṃ na paryāpto bhāryebhyo bharaṇīyebhyo bhavati bhartumityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, whoever — among the kinsmen of such a knower of <s>prāṇa</s> — tries to be a rival, wishes to become hostile among his kinsmen, like the <s>Asuras</s> who were rivals of <s>prāṇa</s> — he is not sufficient, not able, to support his dependents — that is the meaning.

children.text: atha punarya evaṃ jñātīnāṃ madhye evaṃvidaṃ vāgādaya iva prāṇam anu anugato bhavati, yo vaitamevaṃvidamanvevānuvartayanneva ātmīyānbhāryān bubhūrṣati bhartumicchati, yathaiva vāgādayaḥ prāṇānuvṛttyātmabubhūrṣava āsan /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But on the other hand, one among the kinsmen who follows such a knower, just as speech and the rest [followed] <s>prāṇa</s> — who follows and conforms to [the knower], and who wishes to nourish his own dependents — just as speech and the rest wished to sustain themselves by following <s>prāṇa</s> —

children.text: sa haivālaṃ paryāpto bhāryebhyo bharaṇīyebhyo bhavati bhartuṃ netaraḥ svatantraḥ /
children.translated_text: he indeed is sufficient, is able, to support his dependents — and not the other, the independent one.

children.text: sarvametatprāṇaguṇavijñānaphalamuktam //18//
children.translated_text: All this has been stated as the fruit of knowing the qualities of <s>prāṇa</s>. (18)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.18:] Those deities — speech and the rest — 'deities' because they illuminate their respective domains — spoke, said to the chief <s>prāṇa</s>: 'This is so much and no more' — meaning nothing beyond this. '<s>Vai</s>' is for the purpose of recollection. All this is just so much — what? That which is food, that which sustains <s>prāṇa</s>, that is eaten in the world — all that you have obtained for yourself; you have appropriated it — the meaning is: you have made it your own by your <s>āgāna</s> (singing). And we are unable to stand without food. Therefore, afterwards, give us — in this food that is for yourself, in your food — a share; grant [us] a share. The non-hearing of the <s>ṇic</s> [causative suffix] is Vedic usage. 'Make us sharers in food.' The other [<s>prāṇa</s>] said: 'If you indeed desire food — well then, enter into me, surround me on all sides, facing me.' When <s>prāṇa</s> thus spoke, [they said] 'so be it,' and having surrounded <s>prāṇa</s>, they settled in — this is the meaning. When they were thus settled, with the permission of <s>prāṇa</s>, the food that sustains <s>prāṇa</s>, even while not being consumed [directly by them], becomes satisfying for them — not independently. Therefore, the exclusive restriction 'by this alone it was eaten' is indeed justified. And this itself [the text] says: 'therefore' — because the deities of speech and the rest are settled in dependency upon <s>prāṇa</s>, by the permission of <s>prāṇa</s> — therefore whatever food is eaten by this <s>prāṇa</s> of a person, by that food these — speech and the rest — are satisfied. One who knows <s>prāṇa</s> as the basis of speech and the rest, and [knows that] the five [senses] are dependent on <s>prāṇa</s> — to him also, just so, his kinsmen gather around, just as speech and the like [gathered around] <s>prāṇa</s>. The idea is: he becomes a person worthy of being depended upon by his kinsmen. And of those kinsmen who have gathered around, he becomes the nourisher, like <s>prāṇa</s> of speech and the rest. Likewise, the chief — the foremost leader — among them, like <s>prāṇa</s> of speech and the rest. Likewise, the eater of food — meaning free from illness. And the overlord — the sovereign who governs independently, like <s>prāṇa</s> of speech and the rest. For one who thus knows <s>prāṇa</s>, this is the stated fruit.

children.text:
kāryakaraṇānāmātmatvapratipādanāya prāṇasyāṅgirasatvamupanyastaṃ so 'yāsya āṅgirasa iti /
asmāddhetorayamāṅgirasa ityāṅgirasatve heturnoktaḥ /
taddhetusiddhyarthamārabhyate, taddhetusiddhyāyattaṃ hi kāryāṇātmatva prāṇasya /
anantaraṃ ca vāgādīnāṃ prāṇādhīnatoktā sā ca kathamupapādanīyā? ityāha-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the purpose of establishing that <s>prāṇa</s> is the self of the body and its instruments, the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>-nature of <s>prāṇa</s> was introduced: 'He is the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> of this [mouth].' But the reason for this <s>Āṅgirasa</s>-nature — 'because of this, he is <s>Āṅgirasa</s>' — was not stated. In order to establish that reason, [this passage] is begun, for the selfhood of <s>prāṇa</s> with respect to the body and organs depends on the establishment of that reason. And immediately [before this], the dependence of speech and the rest on <s>prāṇa</s> was stated — how is that to be demonstrated? [The text] says:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.19
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.19]

children.text:
so 'yāsya āṅgiraso 'ṅgānāṃ hi rasaḥ |
prāṇo vā aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ |
prāṇo hi vā aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ |
tasmād yasmāt kasmāccāṅgāt prāṇa utkrāmati tad eva tac chuṣyati |
eṣa hi vā aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ || BrhUp_1,3.19 ||
children.translated_text: He is the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> of this [mouth], for he is the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of the limbs (<s>aṅga</s>). <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the essence of the limbs. <s>Prāṇa</s> is verily the essence of the limbs. Therefore, from whichever limb <s>prāṇa</s> departs, that very [limb] dries up. For he is indeed the essence of the limbs. (BṛUp 1.3.19)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.19 so 'yāsya āṅgirasa ityādi yathopanyastamevopādīyate uttarārtham'prāṇo vā aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ'ityevamantaṃ vākyaṃ yathāvyākhyārthameva punaḥ smārayati /
katham? 'prāṇo vā aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ'iti /
'prāṇo hi'-hiśabdaḥ prasiddhau- aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ /
prasiddhametatprāṇasyāṅgarasatvaṃ na vāgādīnām /
tasmādyuktaṃ prāṇo vā iti smāraṇam /
kathaṃ punaḥ prasiddhatvam? ityata āha /
tasmācchabda upasaṃhārārtha uparitvena sambadhyate /
yasmādyato 'vayavātkasmādanuktaviśeṣāt, yasmātkasmādyataḥ kutaścicca aṅgāccharīrāvayavādaviśeṣitātprāṇa utkrāmatyapasarpati tadeva tatraiva tadaṅgaṃ śuṣyati nīrasaṃ bhavati śoṣamupaiti /
tasmādeṣa hi vā aṅgānāṃ rasaḥ ityupasaṃhāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore: 'he is indeed the essence of the limbs' — this is the summation.

children.text: ataḥ kāryakaraṇānāmātmā prāṇa ityetatsiddham /
children.translated_text: From this, it is established that <s>prāṇa</s> is the self of the body and its instruments.

children.text: ātmāpāye hi śeṣo maraṇaṃ syāttasmāttena jīvanti prāṇinaḥ sarve /
children.translated_text: For upon the departure of the self, the remainder would be death; therefore, all living beings live by that [<s>prāṇa</s>].

children.text: tasmādapāsya vāgādīnprāṇa evopāsya iti samudāyārthaḥ //19//
children.translated_text: Therefore, setting aside speech and the rest, <s>prāṇa</s> alone should be meditated upon — this is the purport of the entire [passage]. (19)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.19:] 'He is the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> of this [mouth]' and so on — what was introduced [earlier] is taken up as it was, for the following purpose. The sentence ending with '<s>prāṇa</s> indeed is the essence of the limbs' is repeated for the purpose of explaining what was [previously] stated. How? '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the essence of the limbs.' The word '<s>hi</s>' is used in the sense of indicating something well-known — <s>prāṇa</s> is the essence of the limbs. This <s>Āṅgirasa</s>-nature (being the essence of the limbs) of <s>prāṇa</s> is well-known, not [that] of speech and the rest. Therefore, the recollection '<s>prāṇa</s> indeed' is justified. But how is it well-known? To this [the text] says: the word 'therefore' is used in the sense of summing up, and is connected with what follows. From whichever limb — from any unspecified bodily part, from whatever bodily limb without distinction — <s>prāṇa</s> departs, withdraws, that very limb there dries up, becomes devoid of essence, withers away.

children.text:
na kevalaṃ kāryakaraṇayorevātmā prāṇo rūpakarmabhūtayoḥ /
kiṃ tarhi? ṛgyajuḥsāmnāṃ nāmabhūtānāmātmeti sarvātmakatayā prāṇaṃ stuvanmahīkarotyupāsyatvāya-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Prāṇa</s> is not merely the self of the body and organs, which are its effects and instruments in the form of actions. Rather, [it is also the self] of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s>, which have the nature of names — praising <s>prāṇa</s> by [declaring] its universal selfhood, he magnifies it for the purpose of meditation:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.20

eṣa u eva bṛhaspatiḥ |
vāg vai bṛhatī |
tasyā eṣa patis tasmād u bṛhaspatiḥ || BrhUp_1,3.20 ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. Speech (<s>vāc</s>) is indeed <s>Bṛhatī</s>. He is its lord (<s>pati</s>); therefore he is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>. (BṛUp 1.3.20)
[Start of BṛUp 1.3.20]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.20 eṣa u eva prakṛta āṅgiraso bṛhaspatiḥ /
kathaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ? ityucyate- vāgvai bṛhatī bṛhatīcchandaḥ ṣaṭtriṃśadakṣarā /
anuṣṭupca vāk /
katham? "vāgvā anuṣṭup"(nṛsi.pū.1 / 1) iti śruteḥ /
sā ca vāganuṣṭubbṛhatyāṃ chandasyantarbhavati /
ato yuktaṃ vāgvai bṛhatīti prasiddhavadvaktum /
bṛhatyāṃ ca sarvā ṛco 'ntarbhavanti prāṇasaṃstutatvāt /
"prāṇo bṛhatī prāṇa ṛca ityeva vidyāt"iti śrutyantarāt /
vāgātmatvāccarcā prāṇe 'ntarbhāvaḥ /
tatkatham? ityāha- tasyā vāco bṛhatyā ṛca eṣa prāṇaḥ patiḥ /
tasyā nirvartakatvāt /
kauṣṭhyāgnipreritamārutanirvartyā hi ṛk /
pālanādvā vācaḥ patiḥ /
children.translated_text: Or, he is the lord of speech because he protects it.

children.text: prāṇena hi pālyate vāk /
children.translated_text: For speech is protected by <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: aprāṇasya śabdoccāraṇasāmarthyābhāvāt /
children.translated_text: Because one who is without <s>prāṇa</s> lacks the capacity to utter sounds.

children.text: tasmā bṛhaspatirṛcāṃ prāṇa ātmetyarthaḥ //20//
children.translated_text: Therefore, [he is] <s>Bṛhaspati</s> — the meaning is: <s>prāṇa</s> is the self of the <s>Ṛg</s> verses. (20)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.20:] 'He, this very one under discussion, the <s>Āṅgirasa</s>, is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.' How is he <s>Bṛhaspati</s>? It is said: speech is indeed <s>Bṛhatī</s> — the <s>Bṛhatī</s> meter, consisting of thirty-six syllables. And speech is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>. How? Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'Speech indeed is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>' (<s>Nṛsiṃhapūrvatāpanīya</s> 1.1). And that speech, the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>, is subsumed under the <s>Bṛhatī</s> meter. Therefore it is proper to speak as if it were well-established that 'speech is indeed <s>Bṛhatī</s>.' And in the <s>Bṛhatī</s>, all the <s>Ṛg</s> verses are subsumed, because they are praised as being of the nature of <s>prāṇa</s>. [This follows] from another <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Bṛhatī</s>; <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Ṛc</s> — one should know thus.' The subsumption of the <s>Ṛg</s> verses in <s>prāṇa</s> is because they have the nature of speech. How so? [The text] says: of that speech, the <s>Bṛhatī</s>, i.e. the <s>Ṛg</s> verse — this <s>prāṇa</s> is the lord (<s>pati</s>). Because it is the producer thereof, for the <s>Ṛg</s> verse is produced by the air impelled by the fire in the stomach.

children.text:
tathā yajuṣām /
katham?
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, of the <s>Yajus</s> [formulae]. How?

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.21
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.21]

children.text:
eṣa u eva brahmaṇaspatiḥ |
vāg vai brahma |
tasyā eṣa patis tasmād u brahmaṇaspatiḥ || BrhUp_1,3.21 ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>. Speech is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. He is its lord; therefore he is <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>. (BṛUp 1.3.21)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.21 eṣa u eva brahmaṇaspatiḥ /
vāgvai brahma, brahma yajuḥ, tacca vāgviśeṣa eva /
tasyā vāco yajuṣo brahmaṇa eṣa patistasmādu brahmaṇaspatiḥ pūrvavat /
kathaṃ punaretadavagamyate bṛhatībrahmaṇorṛgyajuṣṭvaṃ na punaranyārthatvam? ityucyate- vāco 'nte sāmasāmānādhikaraṇyanirdeśāt"vāgvai sāma"(1 / 3 / 22) iti /
tathā ca'vāgvai bṛhatī' 'vāgvai brahma'iti ca vāksamānādhikaraṇayorṛgyajuṣṭvaṃ yuktam /
pariśeṣācca- sāmni abhihite ṛgyajuṣī eva pariśiṣṭe /
vāgviśeṣatvācca- vāgviśeṣo hi ṛgyajuṣī /
tasmāt tayorvācā samānādhikaraṇatā yuktā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the co-referential usage of those two with speech is justified.

children.text: aviśeṣaprasaṅgācca- sāmodgītha iti ca spaṣṭaṃ viśeṣābhidhānatvam, tathā bṛhatībrahmaśabdayorapi viśeṣābhidhānatvaṃ yuktam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And because of the need for specificity — '<s>Sāma</s> is the <s>Udgītha</s>' is a clear specification, so likewise for the words '<s>Bṛhatī</s>' and '<s>Brahman</s>' it is proper that they specifically indicate [the <s>Ṛg</s> and <s>Yajus</s>].

children.text: anyathā anirdhārita viśeṣayorānarthakyāpatteśca viśeṣābhidhānasya vāṅmātratve cobhayatra paunaruktyāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, if the specificity of the two [terms] were left undetermined, the fault of meaninglessness would arise; and if both simply meant 'speech' in general, there would be redundancy in both cases.

children.text: ṛgyajuḥsāmodgīthaśabdānāṃ ca śrutiṣvevaṅkramadarśanāt //21//
children.translated_text: And because in the <s>śruti</s> passages, the sequential ordering of the words <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and <s>Udgītha</s> is observed [to follow this pattern]. (21)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.21:] He is indeed <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>. Speech is indeed <s>Brahman</s> — <s>Brahman</s> means the <s>Yajus</s>, and that is indeed a particular form of speech. He is the lord of that speech, the <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> — therefore he is <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, as before. But how is it understood that <s>Bṛhatī</s> and <s>Brahman</s> refer to the <s>Ṛg</s> and <s>Yajus</s> respectively, and not to something else? It is said: because at the end [of this series on speech], the <s>Sāman</s> is indicated in co-reference with speech — 'speech is indeed <s>Sāman</s>' (1.3.22). And thus, for '<s>vāg vai bṛhatī</s>' and '<s>vāg vai brahma</s>' — where [<s>Bṛhatī</s> and <s>Brahman</s>] are in co-reference with speech — it is proper that they refer to the <s>Ṛg</s> and <s>Yajus</s>. And by the principle of elimination — since the <s>Sāman</s> has been mentioned, the <s>Ṛg</s> and <s>Yajus</s> alone remain. And because they are particular forms of speech — for the <s>Ṛg</s> and <s>Yajus</s> are indeed particular forms of speech.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.22
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.22]

children.text:
eṣa u eva sāma |
vāg vai sāmaiṣa sā cāmaś ceti tat sāmnaḥ sāmatvam |
yad v eva samaḥ pluṣiṇā samo maśakena samo nāgena sama ebhis tribhir lokaiḥ samo 'nena sarveṇa tasmād v eva sāma |
aśnute sāmnaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatām |
ya evam etat sāma veda || BrhUp_1,3.22 ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the <s>Sāman</s>. Speech is indeed the <s>Sāman</s>. It is <s>sā</s> (she) and <s>ama</s> (he) — that is the <s>Sāman</s>-nature of the <s>Sāman</s>. Or, because he is equal (<s>sama</s>) to a white ant, equal to a mosquito, equal to an elephant, equal to these three worlds, equal to this entire [universe] — therefore he is indeed the <s>Sāman</s>. One who thus knows this <s>Sāman</s> attains union with, co-residence with, the <s>Sāman</s>. (BṛUp 1.3.22)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.22 eṣa u eva sāma /
katham? ityāha vāgvai sā yatkiñcitstrīśabdābhidheyaṃ sā vāk /
sarvastrīśabdābhidheyavastuviṣayo 'maḥ śabdaḥ /
"kena me paiṃsnāni nāmānyāpnoṣīti, prāṇeneti brūyātkena me strīnāmānīti vācā"(kauṣī.u 1 / 7) iti śrutyantarāt vākprāṇābhidhānabhūto 'yaṃ sāmaśabdaḥ, tathā prāṇanirvartyasvarādisamudāyamātraṃ gitiḥ sāmaśabdenābhidhīyate;ato na prāṇavāgvyatirekeṇa sāmanāmāsti kiñcit, svaravarṇādeśca prāṇanirvartyatvātprāṇatantratvācca /
eṣa u eva prāṇaḥ sāma /
yasmātsāma sāmeti vākprāṇātmakam- sā cāmaśceti, tattasmātsāmno gītirūpabhya svarādisamudāyasya sāmatvaṃ tatpragītaṃ bhuvi /
yad u eva samastulyaḥ sarveṇa vakṣyamāṇena prakāreṇa, tasmādvā sāmetyanena sambandhaḥ /
vāśabdaḥ sāmaśabdalābhanimittaprakārāntaranirdeśasāmarthyalabhyaḥ /
kena punaḥ prakāreṇa prāṇasya tulyatvam? ityucyate- samaḥ pluṣiṇā puttikāśarīreṇa samo maśakena maśakaśarīreṇa, samo nāgena hastiśarīreṇa, sama ebhistribhirlokaistrailokyaśarīreṇa prājāpatyena, samo 'nena jagadrūpeṇa hairaṇyagarbheṇa /
puttikādiśarīreṣu gotvādivatkārtsnyena parisamāpta iti samatvaṃ prāṇasya;na punaḥ śarīramātraparimāṇenaiva, amūrtatvātsarvagatatvācca /
na ca ghaṭaprāsādādipradīpavatsaṃkocavikāsitayā śarīre tāvanmātraṃ samatvam /
"ta ete sarva eva samāḥ sarve 'nantāḥ"(bṛha.u.1 / 5 / 13) iti śruteḥ /
sarvagatasya tu śarīraparimāṇavṛttilābho na virudhyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For something all-pervading, there is no contradiction in obtaining a function limited to the measure of a body.

children.text: evaṃ samatvātsāmākhyaṃ prāṇaṃ veda yaḥśratiprakāśitamahacvaṃ taspaitatphalam-aśnute vyāpnoti sāmnaḥ prāṇasya sāyujyaṃ sayugbhāvaṃ samānadehendriyābhimānatvam, sālokyaṃ samānalophatāṃ vā bhāvanāviśeṣataḥ, ya evametadyathoktaṃ sāma prāṇaṃ veda-ā prāṇātmābhimānābhivyakterupāste ityarthaḥ //22//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One who thus knows <s>prāṇa</s> as <s>Sāman</s>, due to its equality, whose greatness has been revealed by <s>śruti</s> — for him this is the fruit: he attains, reaches, union (<s>sāyujya</s>) with the <s>Sāman</s>, i.e. <s>prāṇa</s> — the state of sharing the same body and sense-faculties; or co-residence (<s>sālokatā</s>), the attainment of the same realm, due to a particular degree of meditation — one who thus knows this <s>Sāman</s>, <s>prāṇa</s>, as described, meditates upon it up to the point of the manifestation of self-identification with the <s>prāṇa</s>-self — this is the meaning. (22)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.22:] He is indeed the <s>Sāman</s>. How? [The text] says: speech is indeed <s>sā</s> — whatever is denoted by a feminine word is <s>sā</s>, i.e. speech. The word '<s>ama</s>' pertains to everything denoted by a masculine word. From another <s>śruti</s>: 'By what do I obtain masculine names? By <s>prāṇa</s>, one would say. By what, feminine names? By speech' (<s>Kauṣītakī Upaniṣad</s> 1.7). Thus, this word '<s>Sāman</s>' denotes speech and <s>prāṇa</s>. Similarly, the <s>gīti</s> (song), which is merely an aggregate of notes and the like produced by <s>prāṇa</s>, is designated by the word '<s>Sāman</s>.' Therefore, apart from <s>prāṇa</s> and speech, there is nothing called <s>Sāman</s>, since notes, syllables, and the rest are produced by <s>prāṇa</s> and are dependent on <s>prāṇa</s>. This very <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Sāman</s>. Because <s>Sāman</s> consists of speech and <s>prāṇa</s> — '<s>sā</s> and <s>ama</s>' — that is the <s>Sāman</s>-nature of the <s>Sāman</s>, the sung form of the aggregate of notes and the like, [known as such] in the world. Or indeed, because it is equal (<s>sama</s>), i.e. the same, with everything in the manner about to be described — therefore indeed it is <s>Sāman</s>, and this connection [is established]. The word '<s>vai</s>' indicates the capacity to point to another reason for obtaining the name <s>Sāman</s>. By what manner is <s>prāṇa</s> equal? It is said: equal to a <s>pluṣin</s> (white ant), to the body of a white ant; equal to a mosquito, to the body of a mosquito; equal to an elephant, to the body of an elephant; equal to these three worlds, to the cosmic body of <s>Prājāpatya</s> [consisting of three worlds]; equal to this entire [universe], to the cosmic body of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. The equality of <s>prāṇa</s> in the bodies of white ants and the rest is [in the sense that] it is completely present in its totality, like cow-ness [in individual cows] — not merely in the measure of the body, because [<s>prāṇa</s>] is formless and all-pervading. And it is not like a lamp in a pot or palace, expanding and contracting to match the size of the container. [This is so] because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'These are all equal, all infinite' (BṛUp 1.5.13).

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.23
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.3.23]

children.text:
eṣa u vā udgīthaḥ |
prāṇo vā ut prāṇena hīdaṃ sarvam uttabdham |
vāg eva gīthā |
uc ca gīthā ceti |
sa udgīthaḥ || BrhUp_1,3.23 ||
children.translated_text: 'This indeed is the <s>Udgītha</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is "ut," for by <s>prāṇa</s> all this is upheld. Speech indeed is "gīthā." "Ut" and "gīthā" — that is the <s>Udgītha</s>.' // BṛhUp 1.3.23 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.23 eṣa u vā udgīthaḥ /
udgītho nāma sāmāvayavo bhaktiviśeṣo nodgānam, sāmādhikārāt /
kathamudgīthaḥ prāṇaḥ? prāṇo vā utprāṇena hi yasmādidaṃ sarvaṃ jagaduttabdhamūrdhvaṃ stabdhamuttambhitaṃ vidhṛtamityarthaḥ /
uttabdhārthāvadyotako 'yamucchabdaḥ prāṇaguṇābhidhāyakaḥ, tasmādutprāṇaḥ /
vāgeva gīthāśabdaviśeṣatvādudgīthabhakteḥ /
gāyateḥ śabdārthatvātsā vāgeva /
children.translated_text: Since the root '<s>gāyati</s>' has the meaning of 'producing sound,' that [gīthā] is indeed speech.

children.text: na hyudgīthabhakteḥśabdavyatirekeṇa kiñcidrūpamutprekṣyate /
children.translated_text: For no form of the <s>Udgītha</s> division can be conceived apart from sound.

children.text: tasmādyuktamavadhāraṇaṃ vāgeva gītheti /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the emphatic determination 'speech alone is gīthā' is appropriate.

children.text: ucca prāṇo gīthā ca prāṇatantrā vāgityubhayamekena śabdenābhidhīyate sa udgīthaḥ //23//
children.translated_text: 'Ut' is <s>prāṇa</s>, and 'gīthā' is speech that is dependent on <s>prāṇa</s> — both are denoted by one word: that is the <s>Udgītha</s>. // 23 //

[Commentary:] 'This indeed is the <s>Udgītha</s>' — the <s>Udgītha</s> is a particular division of the <s>Sāman</s>, not the act of singing (<s>udgāna</s>), since <s>Sāman</s> is the topic. How is <s>prāṇa</s> the <s>Udgītha</s>? '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is "ut"' — because by <s>prāṇa</s> this entire universe is upheld, propped up, supported, sustained — this is the meaning. The syllable 'ut,' which illuminates the meaning of 'being upheld,' denotes a quality of <s>prāṇa</s>; therefore, 'ut' is <s>prāṇa</s>. Speech indeed is 'gīthā,' because the <s>Udgītha</s> division [of the <s>Sāman</s>] consists of particular sounds.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.24
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.3.24]

children.text:
tad dhāpi brahmadattaś caikitāneyo rājānaṃ bhakṣayann uvāca |
ayaṃ tyasya rājā mūrdhānaṃ vipātayatād yad ito 'yāsya āṅgiraso 'nyenodagāyad iti |
vācā ca hy eva sa prāṇena codagāyad iti || BrhUp_1,3.24 ||
children.translated_text: 'In this regard, <s>Brahmadatta Caikitāneya</s>, while drinking the <s>Soma</s> for the king, said: "May this king cause the head of that man to fall off, if <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s> chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> by any other [means] than this." For he chanted it with speech and with <s>prāṇa</s> indeed.' // BṛhUp 1.3.24 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.24 taddhāpi tattatraitasminnukter'the hāpyākhyāyikāpi śrūtaye hasma /
brahmadatto nāmataḥ cikitānasyāpatyaṃ caikitānastadapatyaṃ yuvā caikitāneyaḥ, rājānaṃ yajñe somaṃ bhakṣayannuvāca /
kim? ayaṃ camasastho mayābhakṣyamāṇo rājā tyasya tasya mamānṛtavādino mūrdhānaṃ śiro vipātayatādvispaṣṭaṃ pātayatu /
torayaṃ tātaṅṅādeśaḥ āśipi loṭ, vipātayatāditi /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>tya</s>' is a substitute for '<s>tad</s>' in the <s>āśiṣ</s> (benedictive) form of the imperative: '<s>vipātayatāt</s>.'

children.text: yadyahamanṛtavādī syāmityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'If I were to be a speaker of falsehood' — this is the meaning.

children.text: kathaṃ punaranṛtavāditvaprāptiḥ? ityucyate-yadyadīto 'smātprakṛtāt prāṇādvāksaṃyuktāt, ayāsyaḥ-mukhyaprāṇābhidhāyakena ayāsyāṅgirasaśabdenābhidhīyate viśvasṛjāṃ pūrvarṣīṇāṃ satre udrātāso 'nyena devatāntareṇa vākprāṇavyatiriktenodagāyadudgānaṃ kṛtavān, tato 'hamanṛtavādī syām, tasya mama devatā viparītapratipatturmūrdhānaṃ vipātayatu, ityevaṃ śapathaṃ cakāreti vijñāne pratyayadārḍhyakartavyatāṃ darśayati /
children.translated_text: How would the charge of speaking falsehood arise? It is said: if from this — from the well-known <s>prāṇa</s> under discussion, combined with speech — <s>Ayāsya</s>, who is designated by the word '<s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s>' denoting the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> by any other deity, one different from speech and <s>prāṇa</s>, at the <s>satra</s> (sacrificial session) of the <s>Viśvasṛjs</s>, the ancient sages — then I would be a speaker of falsehood; may the deity cause the head of me, the one who has wrongly understood the deity, to fall off. Thus he made an oath — [the text] shows that firm conviction should be established regarding this knowledge.

children.text: tamimamākhyāyikānirdhāritamarthaṃ svena vacasopasaṃharati śrutiḥ-vācā ca prāṇapradhānayā prāṇena ca svasyātmabhūtena so 'yāsya āṅgirasa udgātodagāyadityeṣor'tho nirdhāritaḥ śapathena //24//
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> itself summarizes with its own words the meaning established by this narrative: with speech, which has <s>prāṇa</s> as its predominant [element], and with <s>prāṇa</s>, which is its own essential nature — that <s>Ayāsya Āṅgirasa</s>, the <s>Udgātṛ</s> (chanter), chanted the <s>Udgītha</s> — this meaning has been established by the oath. // 24 //

[Commentary:] 'In that regard' — there, in that matter of the stated meaning, there is even a narrative too, to be heard. <s>Brahmadatta</s> by name, the offspring of <s>Cikitāna</s> was <s>Caikitāna</s>, and his offspring, the young <s>Caikitāneya</s> — while drinking the <s>Soma</s>, the king [of drinks], at a sacrifice, he said. What? 'May this king, contained in the cup and being drunk by me, cause the head of that person — the one who speaks falsely about me — to fall off, to drop down clearly.'

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.25
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.3.25]

children.text:
tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ svaṃ veda bhavati hāsya svam |
tasya vai svara eva svam |
tasmād ārtvijyaṃ kariṣyan vāci svaram iccheta |
tayā vācā svarasampannayārtvijyaṃ kuryāt |
tasmād yajñe svaravantaṃ didṛkṣanta eva |
atho yasya svaṃ bhavati |
bhavati hāsya svaṃ ya evam etat sāmnaḥ svaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,3.25 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of this very <s>Sāman</s>, one who knows its "own" (<s>sva</s>) — he indeed has his own. Its own is indeed the voice (<s>svara</s>). Therefore, one who is about to perform priestly functions should desire good voice quality in speech. With that voice endowed with good tone, he should perform the priestly function. Therefore, at a sacrifice, people wish to see one who has a good voice. Also, one who has his "own" [wealth] — he indeed has his own. One who knows this "own" of the <s>Sāman</s> thus — he indeed comes to have his own.' // BṛhUp 1.3.25 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.25 tasyeti prakṛtaṃ prāṇamabhisamvadhnāti /
haitasyeti mukhyaṃ vyapadiśatyabhinayena /
sāmnaḥ sāmaśabdavācyasyaprāṇasyayaḥsvaṃ dhanaṃ veda, tasya ha kiṃ syāt? bhavati hāsyasvam /
phalena pralobhyābhimukhīkṛtya śuśrūṣave āha-tasya vai sāmnaḥ svara eva svam /
svara iti kaṇṭhagataṃ mādhuryaṃ tadevāsya svaṃ vibhūṣaṇam /
tena hi bhūṣitamṛddhimallakṣyataudgānam /
yasmādevaṃ tasmādārtvijyaṃ ṛtvikkarmodgānaṃ kariṣyanvāci viṣaye vāci vāgāśritaṃ svaramiccheta icchet sāmno dhanavattāṃ svareṇa cikīrṣurudgātā /
idaṃ tu prāsaṅgikaṃvidhīyate;sāmnaḥ sausvaryeṇa svaravacvapratyayekartavye icchāmātreṇa sausvaryaṃ na bhavatīti dantadhāvanatailapānādi sāmarthyātkartavyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But this is taught incidentally: since the confidence that the <s>Sāman</s> has good voice cannot be produced by mere desire alone, [therefore] practices such as teeth-cleaning, oil-drinking, and so forth should be performed as appropriate — this is the meaning.

children.text: tathaivaṃ saṃskṛtayā vācā svarasampannayārtvijyaṃ kuryāt /
children.translated_text: Similarly, with speech thus prepared, endowed with good voice, one should perform the priestly function.

children.text: tasmādyasmātsāmnaḥ svabhūtaḥ svarastena svena bhūṣitaṃ sāma ato yajñe svaravantamudgātāraṃ didṛkṣanta eva draṣṭumicchanta eva dhanināmava laukikāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore — because the voice is the 'own' (<s>sva</s>) of the <s>Sāman</s> — people at a sacrifice wish to see, desire to behold, an <s>Udgātṛ</s> who has a good voice, just as worldly people [wish to see] wealthy men.

children.text: prasiddhaṃ hi loke 'tho api yasya svaṃ dhanaṃ bhavati taṃ dhaninaṃ didṛkṣante iti siddhasya guṇavijñānaphalasambandhasya upasaṃhāraḥ kriyate- bhavati hāsya svaṃ ya evametatsāmnaḥ svaṃ vedeti //25//
children.translated_text: For it is well known in the world that people wish to see a wealthy man — one who has his own, his wealth. This is the application of the already established connection between the quality, its knowledge, and its fruit: 'He indeed has his own — one who knows this "own" of the <s>Sāman</s> thus.' // 25 //

[Commentary:] 'Of this' — he connects [the discussion] back to the <s>prāṇa</s> under discussion. 'Of this very' — he points to the chief [<s>prāṇa</s>] by gesture. Of the <s>Sāman</s>, of <s>prāṇa</s> which is denoted by the word '<s>Sāman</s>' — one who knows its 'own' (<s>sva</s>), its wealth — what would happen for him? He indeed comes to have his own. Having enticed [the listener] with the fruit and made him attentive, [the text] tells the eager listener: its own, of that <s>Sāman</s>, is indeed the voice (<s>svara</s>). Voice means the sweetness residing in the throat — that itself is its own, its ornament. For the chanting (<s>udgāna</s>) adorned by it is perceived as prosperous. Since this is so, therefore one who is about to perform the priestly function, i.e., the chanting that is the <s>Udgātṛ</s>'s duty — should desire good voice quality in speech, in the domain of speech; the <s>Udgātṛ</s> desiring to make the <s>Sāman</s> wealthy through voice [should desire this].

children.text:
athānyo guṇaḥ suvarṇavattālakṣaṇo vidhīyate /
asāvapi sausvaryameva /
etāvānviśeṣaḥ- pūrvaṃ kaṇṭhagatamādhuryamidaṃ tu lākṣaṇikaṃ suvarṇaśabdavācyam /
children.translated_text: Now another quality, characterized by having good gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>), is taught. This too is essentially about having good voice. The distinction is: the previous [quality] was sweetness residing in the throat, while this one is figurative, denoted by the word '<s>suvarṇa</s>' (good color/gold).

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.26
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.3.26]

children.text:
tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ suvarṇaṃ veda bhavati hāsya suvarṇam |
tasya vai svara eva suvarṇam |
bhavati hāsya suvarṇaṃ ya evam etat sāmnaḥ suvarṇaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,3.26 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of this very <s>Sāman</s>, one who knows its gold (<s>suvarṇa</s>) — he indeed comes to have gold. Its gold is indeed the voice (<s>svara</s>). One who knows this gold of the <s>Sāman</s> thus — he indeed comes to have gold.' // BṛhUp 1.3.26 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,3.26 tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ suvarṇaṃ veda bhavati hāsya suvarṇam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Of this very <s>Sāman</s>, one who knows its gold — he indeed comes to have gold.'

children.text: suvarṇa śabdasāmānyātsvarasuvarṇayoḥ lokikameva suvarṇaṃ guṇavijñānaphalaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Due to the commonality of the word between 'voice' (<s>svara</s>) and 'gold' (<s>suvarṇa</s>), worldly gold itself becomes the fruit of this knowledge of the quality — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasya vai svara eva suvarṇam /
children.translated_text: 'Its gold is indeed the voice.'

children.text: bhavati hāsya suvarṇaṃ ya evametatsāmnaḥ suvarṇaṃ vedeti pūrvavatsarvam //26//
children.translated_text: 'He indeed comes to have gold — one who knows this gold of the <s>Sāman</s> thus' — everything is as before. // 26 //

children.text: tathā pratiṣṭhāguṇaṃ vidhitsannāha-
children.translated_text: Similarly, wishing to teach the quality of foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), he says:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.27

tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhati |
tasya vai vāg eva pratiṣṭhā |
vāci hi khalv eṣa etat prāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhito gīyate |
anna ity u haika āhuḥ || BrhUp_1,3.27 ||
children.translated_text: 'Of this very <s>Sāman</s>, one who knows its foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) — he indeed becomes firmly established. Its foundation is indeed speech. For this <s>prāṇa</s>, being established in speech, is sung. But some say it is food.' // BṛhUp 1.3.27 //
[Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.3.27]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.27 tasya haitasya sāmno yaḥ pratiṣṭhāṃ veda /
pratitiṣṭhatyasyāmiti pratiṣṭhā vāktāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ sāmno guṇaṃ yo veda sa pratitiṣṭhati ha /
"taṃ yathā yathopāsate"iti śrutestadguṇatvaṃ yuktam /

pūrvavatphalena pratilobhitāya kā pratilobhitāya kā pratiṣṭheti śuśrūpave āha- tasya vai sāmno vāgeva, vāgiti jihvāmūlīyādīnāṃ sthānānāmākhyā, saiva pratiṣṭhā, tadāha- vāci hi jihvāmūlīyādiṣuhi yasmātpratiṣṭhitaḥ sanneṣa prāṇa etadgānaṃ gīyate gītibhāvamāpadyate tasmātsāmnaḥ pratiṣṭhā vāk /
children.translated_text: As before, to one enticed by the fruit [the text] tells the eager listener: its foundation, of that <s>Sāman</s>, is indeed speech — 'speech' is the designation for the places of articulation such as the root of the tongue and so forth — that itself is the foundation. Hence it says: in speech — because being established in [the places of articulation such as] the root of the tongue and so forth, this <s>prāṇa</s> is sung, attains the state of being a song — therefore speech is the foundation of the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: anne pratiṣṭhito gīyata ityu haike 'nye āhuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It is sung while established in food' — thus some others say.

children.text: iha pratitiṣṭhatīti yuktam /
children.translated_text: 'One becomes established here' — this is appropriate.

children.text: aninditatvādekīyapakṣasya vikalpena pratiṣṭhāguṇavijñānaṃ kuryād vāgvā patiṣṭhānnaṃ veti //27//
children.translated_text: Since the alternative view is not censured, one should optionally perform the meditation on the quality of foundation — either speech is the foundation, or food is. // 27 //

[Commentary:] 'Of this very <s>Sāman</s>, one who knows its foundation' — that in which it is established is its foundation, i.e., speech. One who knows this foundation, this quality of the <s>Sāman</s>, becomes firmly established. Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'As one meditates upon it, so one becomes' — its having that quality is appropriate.

children.text:
evaṃ prāṇavijñānavato japakarma vidhitsyate /
yadvijñānavato japakarmaṇyadhikārastadvijñānamuktam /
children.translated_text: Thus, for one who has the knowledge of <s>prāṇa</s>, the practice of <s>japa</s> (silent recitation) is about to be taught. That knowledge which qualifies one for the <s>japa</s> practice has been stated.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,3.28
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.3.28]

children.text:
athātaḥ pavamānānām evābhyārohaḥ |
sa vai khalu prastotā sāma prastauti |
sa yatra prastuyāt tad etāni japet |
asato mā sad gamaya, tamaso mā jyotir gamaya, mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayeti |
sa yad āhāsato mā sad gamayeti |
