mṛtyur vā asat sad amṛtaṃ mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayāmṛtaṃ mā kurv ity evaitad āha |
tamaso mā jyotir gamayeti |
mṛtyur vai tamo jyotir amṛtaṃ mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayāmṛtaṃ mā kurv ity evaitad āha |
mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamayeti |
nātra tirohitam ivāsti |
atha yānītarāṇi stotrāṇi teṣv ātmane 'nnādyam āgāyet |
tasmād u teṣu varaṃ vṛṇīta |
yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayet tam |
sa eṣa evaṃvid udgātātmane vā yajamānāya vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate tam āgāyati |
tad dhaital lokajid eva |
na haivālokyatāyā āśāsti ya evam etat sāma veda || BrhUp_1,3.28 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, the ascending chant of the <s>Pavamāna</s> [hymns]. The <s>Prastotṛ</s> (initiating priest) indeed chants the <s>Sāman</s>. When he is about to chant, let him recite these [verses]: "Lead me from the unreal to the real; lead me from darkness to light; lead me from death to immortality." When he says "lead me from the unreal to the real" — death indeed is the unreal, and immortality is the real; "lead me from death to immortality, make me immortal" — this is what he says. "Lead me from darkness to light" — death indeed is darkness, and immortality is light; "lead me from death to immortality, make me immortal" — this is what he says. "Lead me from death to immortality" — there is nothing hidden, as it were, in this. Now, whatever other <s>stotras</s> (hymns of praise) there are — in them one should chant for obtaining food for oneself. Therefore, in them one should choose a boon, whatever desire one may desire. This <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows thus — whatever desire he desires, either for himself or for the sacrificer, that he obtains by chanting. This indeed is world-conquering. There is no hope of being without a world for one who knows this <s>Sāman</s> thus.' // BṛhUp 1.3.28 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,3.28 athānantaraṃ yasmāccaivaṃ viduṣā prayujyamānaṃ devabhāvāyābhyārohaphalaṃ japakarma, atastasmāttadvidhīyata iha /
tasya codgīthasambandhātsarvatra prāptau pavamānānāmiti vacanāt pavamāneṣu triṣvapi kartavyatāyāṃ prāptāyāṃ punaḥ kāla saṃkocaṃ karoti- sa vai khalu prastotā sāma prastauti /
sa prastotā yatra yasminkāle sāma prastuyātprārabheta tasminkāla etāni japet /
asya ca japakarmaṇa ākhyā abhyāroha iti /
ābhimukhyenārohatyanena japakarmaṇaivaṃvid devabhāvātmānamityabhyārohaḥ /
etānīti bahuvacanāttrīṇi yajūṃṣi /
dvitīyānirdeśād brāhmaṇotpannatvācca yathāpaṭhita eva svaraḥ prayoktavyo na māntraḥ /
yājamānaṃ japakarma /
etāni tāni yajūṃṣi-'asato mā sadgamaya''tamaso mā jyotirgamaya' 'mṛtyormāmṛtaṃ gamaya'iti /
mantrāmarthastirohito bhavatīti svayameva vyācaṣṭe brāhmaṇaṃ mantrārtham- sa mantro yadāha yaduktavānko 'sāvarthaḥ? ityucyate-'asato mā sadgamaya'iti mṛtyurvā asat- svābhāvikakarmavijñāne mṛtyurityucyete, asad atyantādhobhāvahetutvāt /
sadamṛtam- sacchāstrīyakarmavijñāne agaraṇahetutvādamṛtam /
tasmādasato asatkarmaṇo 'jñānācca mā māṃ sacchāstrīyakarmavijñāne gamaya devabhāvasādhanātmabhāvamāpādayetyarthaḥ /
tatra vākyārthamāha- amṛtaṃ mā kurvityevaitadāheti /
tathā tamaso mā jyotirgamayeti mṛtyurgamayeti /
mṛtyurvai tamaḥ sarvaṃ hyajñānamāvaraṇātmakatvāttamaḥ tadeva ca maraṇahetutvānmṛtyuḥ /
jyotiramṛtaṃ pūrvoktaviparītaṃ daivaṃ svarūpam /
prakāśātmakatvājjñānaṃ jyotiḥ, tadevāmṛtamavināśātmakatvāt /
tasmāt tamaso mā jyotirgamayeti pūrvavanmṛtyormāmṛtaṃ gamayetyādi /
amṛtaṃ mā kurvityevaitadāha- daivaṃ prājāpatyaṃ phalabhāvamāpādayetyarthaḥ /
pūrvo mantro 'sādhanasvabhāvāt sādhanabhāvamāpādayeti /
dvitīyastu sādhanabhāvādapi ajñānarūpāt sādhyabhāvamāpādayeti /
mṛtyormāmṛtaṃ gamayeti pūrvayoreva mantrayoḥ samucitor'thastṛtīyena mantreṇocyata iti prasiddhārthataiva /
nātra tṛtīye mantre tirohitamantarhitamivārtharūpaṃ pūrvayoriva mantrayorasti, yathāśruta evārthaḥ /
yājamānamudgānaṃ kṛtvā pavamāneṣu triṣu, athānantaraṃ yānītarāṇi śiṣṭāni stotrāṇi teṣvātmane 'nnādyamāgāyet prāṇavidudgātāprāṇabhūtaḥ prāṇavadeva /
yasmātsa eva udgātaivaṃ prāṇaṃ yathoktaṃ vetti, ataḥ prāṇavadeva taṃ kāmaṃ sādhayituṃ samarthaḥ /
tasmādyajamānasteṣu stotreṣu prayujyamāneṣu varaṃ vṛṇīta, yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayeta taṃ kāmaṃ varaṃ vṛṇīta prārthayeta /
yasmātsa eṣa evaṃvidudgāteti tasmācchabdātprāgeva sambadhyate /
ātmane vā yajamānāya vā yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate icchatyudgātā tamāgāyatyāgānena sādhayati /
evaṃ tāvajjñānakarmabhyāṃ prāṇātmāpattirityuktam /
tatra nāstyāśaṅkāsambhavaḥ /
ataḥ karmāpāye prāṇāpattirbhavati vā na vā? ityāśaṅkate /
tadāśaṅkānivṛttyarthamāha- taddhaitalokajideveti /
taddhatadetatprāṇadarśanaṃ karmaviyuktaṃ kevalamapi, lokajideveti lokasādhanameva /
na ha evālokyatāyai alokārhatvāya āśā āśaṃsanaṃ prārthanaṃ naivāsti ha /
na hi prāṇātmani utpannātmābhimānasya tatprāptyāśaṃsanaṃ sambhavati /
na hi grāmasthaḥ kadā grāmaṃ prāpnutāmityaraṇyastha ivāśāste /
asannikṛṣṭaviṣaye hyanātmanyāśaṃsanam, na tatsvātmani sambhavati /
children.translated_text: For aspiration pertains to a distant object that is not the Self; it cannot arise regarding one's own Self.

children.text: tasmānnāśāsti kadācitprāṇātmabhāvaṃ na prapadyeyamiti /
children.translated_text: Therefore there is no apprehension: 'I might at some time fail to attain the state of the <s>prāṇa</s>-self.'

children.text: kasyaitat? ya evametatsāma prāṇaṃ yathoktaṃ nirdhāritamahimānaṃ veda- ahamasmi prāṇa indriyaviṣayāsaṅgairāsuraiḥ pāpmabhiradharṣaṇīyo viśuddhaḥ, vāgādipañcakaṃ ca madāśrayatvādagnyādyātmarūpaṃ svābhāvikavijñānotthendriyaviṣayāsaṅgajanitāsurapāpmadoṣaviyuktaṃ sarvabhūteṣu ca madāśrayānnādyopayogabandhanam, ātmā cāhaṃ sarvabhūtānāmāṅgirasatvāt, ṛgyajuḥ sāmodgīthabhūtāyāśca vāca ātmā tadvayāptestannirvartakatvācca, mama sāmno gītibhāvamāpadyamānasya bāhyaṃ dhanaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ sausvaryaṃ tato 'pyāntaraṃ sauvarṇyalākṣaṇikaṃ sausvaryam, gītibhāvamāpadyamānasya mama kaṇṭhādisthānāni pratiṣṭhā /
children.translated_text: To whom does this [fruit] belong? To one who knows this <s>Sāman</s>, [which is] the <s>prāṇa</s> whose glory has been determined as described — [thinking:] 'I am <s>prāṇa</s>, invulnerable by the demonic evils of attachment to sense-objects, pure; and the pentad of speech and the rest, because of depending on me, has the nature of <s>Agni</s> and the rest, freed from the demonic defect of evil born of natural attachment to sense-objects — the cognition of which is generated by perception and inference; and because of depending on me, [the pentad] is bound to the benefit of all beings in the form of food-consumption; and I am the Self of all beings because of being <s>Āṅgirasa</s> (the essence of the limbs); and I am the Self of speech which has become the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāma</s>, and <s>Udgītha</s>, because of pervading it and because of being its accomplisher; and when I, the <s>Sāman</s>, assume the form of song, the external wealth is adornment, the beauty of voice; and more internal than that is the beauty characterized by golden and ruby-like [qualities of voice]; and when I assume the form of song, the throat and other locations are my foundation.'

children.text: evaṃ guṇo 'haṃ puttikādiśarīreṣu kārtsnyena parisamāpto 'mūrtatvātsarvagatatvācca- iti ā evamabhimānābhivyaktervedopāsta ityarthaḥ //28//
children.translated_text: One of such qualities, I am completely present in bodies of ants and the like, because of being formless and all-pervading — thus, [one should meditate] up to the manifestation of this self-identification; the meaning is: one should meditate in this manner as taught by the <s>Veda</s>. (28)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.3.28:] Then, next — since the <s>japa</s>-ritual (recitation), performed by one who knows thus, has as its fruit the ascent to the state of godhood, therefore it is enjoined here. And since it is connected with the <s>Udgītha</s>, when its applicability to all [stotras] has been established by the statement 'of the <s>Pavamānas</s>,' and when the obligation to perform it in all three <s>Pavamāna</s> [stotras] has been established, [the text] further restricts the time: 'The <s>Prastotṛ</s> (initiator) indeed chants the <s>Sāman</s>.' The <s>Prastotṛ</s> — at whatever time he begins to chant the <s>Sāman</s> — at that time one should recite these [mantras]. And the designation of this recitation-ritual is '<s>abhyāroha</s>' (ascent). By 'ascent' is meant: through this recitation-ritual, one who knows thus ascends face-forward toward the state of godhood as one's Self. 'These' — from the plural [form], three <s>Yajus</s>-formulae [are meant]. Because they are referred to in the accusative case, and because they originate in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [portion], the accent (<s>svara</s>) is to be employed as actually recited [in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>], not the <s>mantra</s>-accent. The <s>japa</s>-ritual belongs to the sacrificer. These are the <s>Yajus</s>-formulae: '<s>asato mā sad gamaya</s>' ('Lead me from the unreal to the real'), '<s>tamaso mā jyotir gamaya</s>' ('Lead me from darkness to light'), '<s>mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamaya</s>' ('Lead me from death to immortality'). Since the meaning of the mantras is hidden, [the text] itself explains the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>-meaning of the mantras — the mantra says what it has said; what is its meaning? It is explained: '<s>asato mā sad gamaya</s>' — death indeed is the unreal (<s>asat</s>). The natural knowledge and action [of the senses] are called death, [called] the unreal because they are the cause of an extremely downward course. The real (<s>sat</s>) is the immortal — the scriptural knowledge and action are immortal because they are the cause of non-sinking. Therefore, 'from the unreal' — from unreal (unscriptural) action and ignorance — 'lead me' — lead me to the real scriptural knowledge and action; bring me to the state of self that is the means of [attaining] godhood — this is the meaning. Therein, [the text] states the sentence-meaning: 'Make me immortal' — that is what this [mantra] says. Similarly, '<s>tamaso mā jyotir gamaya</s>' — 'from darkness lead me to light,' [means:] from death lead me. Death indeed is darkness — for all ignorance, being of the nature of obscuration, is darkness; and that very [ignorance], being the cause of dying, is death. Light is the immortal — the opposite of what was previously described — the divine nature. Because knowledge, being of the nature of illumination, is light; and that very [knowledge] is the immortal, because of being of the nature of non-destruction. Therefore, '<s>tamaso mā jyotir gamaya</s>' — as before. '<s>mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamaya</s>' and so on — 'Make me immortal' — that is what this says; the meaning is: bring me to the state of <s>Prajāpati</s>, which is the divine fruit. The first mantra, from the nature of the unsanctified [state], brings one to the state of being sanctified [by scriptural means]. The second, even from the state of being sanctified [by means] that still has the form of ignorance, brings one to the state of the goal [itself]. '<s>Mṛtyor māmṛtaṃ gamaya</s>' — the combined meaning of the first two mantras is expressed by the third mantra — hence it is of well-known meaning. In this third mantra there is no hidden, concealed meaning as in the first two mantras; the meaning is just as heard. Having performed the chanting for the sacrificer in the three <s>Pavamāna</s> [stotras], then next, in the remaining other stotras, he should chant for himself the obtaining of food — the <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows <s>prāṇa</s> [does so], being identified with <s>prāṇa</s>, just like <s>prāṇa</s> itself. Since he, the <s>Udgātṛ</s>, thus knows <s>prāṇa</s> as described, therefore, just like <s>prāṇa</s>, he is capable of accomplishing that desire. Therefore, the sacrificer, while those stotras are being performed, should choose a boon — whatever desire he desires, that desire he should choose as a boon, should pray for. Because 'he is this <s>Udgātṛ</s> who knows thus' — from this word 'therefore,' the preceding [statement] is connected. Either for himself or for the sacrificer — whatever desire the <s>Udgātṛ</s> desires, he chants for it, accomplishes it through chanting. Thus far, the attainment of the <s>prāṇa</s>-self through knowledge and action together has been stated. Therein, there is no possibility of doubt. Hence [the question arises]: when action falls away, does the attainment of the <s>prāṇa</s> [self] occur or not? To remove that doubt, [the text] says: 'That indeed is the conqueror of worlds.' That — this vision of <s>prāṇa</s>, even when separated from action, even by itself alone — is indeed the conqueror of worlds, the means of attaining the worlds. There is no hope, no aspiration, for non-attainment of worlds, for being unworthy of worlds. For one in whom the consciousness of being the <s>prāṇa</s>-self has arisen, there cannot be an aspiration for non-attainment [of that state]. For one who dwells in a village does not hope, like one dwelling in a forest, 'When shall I reach the village?'

children.text: iti prathamādhyāye tṛtīyamudgīthabrāhmaṇam //3//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>Udgītha Brāhmaṇa</s> in the first <s>adhyāya</s>. (3)

children.text:
jñānakarmabhyāṃ samucitābhyāṃ prajāpatitvaprāptirvyākhyātā kevalaprāṇadarśanena ca'taddhaitallokajideva'ityādinā /
prajāpateḥ phalabhūtasya sṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāreṣu jagataḥ svātantryādivibhūtyupavarṇanena jñānakarmaṇorvaidikayoḥ phalotkarṣo varṇayitavya ityevamarthamārabhyate /
tena ca karmakāṇḍavihitajñānakarmastutiḥ kṛtvā bhavetsāmarthyāt /
vivakṣitaṃ tvetat- sarvamapyetajjñānakarmaphalaṃ saṃsāra eva, bhayāratyādiyuktatvaśravaṇāt, kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇatvācca sthūlavyaktānityaviṣayatvācceti /
brahmavidyāyāḥ kevalāyā vakṣyamāṇāyā mokṣahetutvamityuttarārthaṃ ceti /
na hi saṃsāraviṣayātsādhyasādhanādibhedalakṣaṇād aviraktasya ātmaikatva jñānaviṣaye 'dhikāraḥ, atṛṣitasyeva pāne /
tasmājjñānakarmaphalotkarṣopavarṇanamuttarārtham /
tathā ca vakṣyati-"tadetatpadanīyamasya"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 7) "tadetatpreyaḥ putrāt" (bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 8) ityādi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood through knowledge and action combined has been explained, and also through the vision of <s>prāṇa</s> alone by 'That indeed is the conqueror of worlds' and so forth. Through the description of the sovereignty and other glories of <s>Prajāpati</s> — who is the fruit — in creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the world, the excellence of the fruit of Vedic knowledge and action is to be described — for this purpose [the next section] is begun. And by that, the praise of knowledge and action enjoined in the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual section) is accomplished through [their] capacity. But what is actually intended is this: all this fruit of knowledge and action is <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence) alone, since we hear that it is accompanied by fear, dissatisfaction, and the like, and since it is of the nature of cause and effect, pertaining to the gross, manifest, and impermanent. [The intention is] that <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) alone, which is to be expounded hereafter, is the cause of liberation — and this serves the purpose of what follows. For one who is not disenchanted with [the realm of] <s>saṃsāra</s>, characterized by the distinction of means and ends, has no qualification for the knowledge of the oneness of the Self — just as one who is not thirsty [has no qualification] for drinking. Therefore, the description of the excellence of the fruit of knowledge and action serves the purpose of what follows. And thus [the text] will state: 'That is the step to be reached' (BṛUp 1.4.7), 'That is dearer than a son' (BṛUp 1.4.8), and so on.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,4.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.4.1]

children.text:
ātmaivedam agra āsīt puruṣavidhaḥ |
so 'nuvīkṣya nānyad ātmano 'paśyat |
so 'ham asmīty agre vyāharat |
tato 'haṃnāmābhavat |
tasmād apy etarhy āmantrito 'ham ayam ity evāgra uktvāthānyan nāma prabrūte yad asya bhavati |
sa yat pūrvo 'smāt sarvasmāt sarvān pāpmana auṣat tasmāt puruṣaḥ |
oṣati ha vai sa taṃ yo 'smāt pūrvo bubhūṣati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: The Self alone was this [universe] in the beginning, in the form of a person (<s>puruṣa</s>). He, looking around, saw nothing other than himself. He first said: 'I am.' From that, the name 'I' (<s>aham</s>) came into being. Therefore, even now, when addressed, one first says 'It is I' and then declares whatever other name one has. Because he, before all this [creation], burned up all evils — therefore [he is called] <s>Puruṣa</s>. He who knows this burns up anyone who wishes to be before him. (BṛUp 1.4.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,4.1 ātmaivātmeti prajāpatiḥ prathamo 'ṇḍajaḥ śarīryabhidhīyate /
vaidikajñānakarmaphalabhūtaḥ sa eva kim? idaṃ śarīrabhedajātaṃ tena prajāpatiśarīreṇāvibhaktam /
ātmaivāsīdagre prākśarīrāntarotpatteḥ /
sa ca puruṣavidhaḥ puruṣaprakāraḥ śiraḥprāṇyādilakṣaṇo virāṭ /
sa eva prathamaḥ sambhūto 'nuvīkṣyānvālocanaṃ kṛtvā, ko 'haṃ kiṃlakṣaṇo vāsmīti, nānyadvastvantaram, ātmanaḥ prāṇapiṇḍātmakāryakaraṇarūpānna apaśyanna dadarśa /
kevalaṃ tvātmānameva sarvātmānamapaśyat /
tathā pūrvajanmaśrautavijñānasaṃskṛtaḥ, so 'haṃ prajāpatiḥ sarvātmāhamasmītyagre vyāharadvyāhṛtavān /
tatastasmādyataḥ pūrvajñānasaṃskārād ātmānamevāhamityabhyadhādagre tasmādahaṃnāmābhavat /
tasyopaniṣadamiti śrutipradarśitameva nāma vakṣyati /
tasmādyasmātkāraṇe prajāpatāvevaṃ vṛttaṃ tasmāt, tatkāryabhūteṣu prāṇiṣu etarhyetasminnapi kāla āmantritaḥ kastvamityuktaḥ sannahamayamityevāgra uktvā kāraṇātmābhidhānena ātmānamabhidhāyāgre punarviśeṣanāmajijñāsave 'thānantaraṃ viśeṣapiṇḍābhidhānaṃ devadatto yajñadatto veti prabūte kathayati yannāmāsya viśeṣapiṇḍasya mātāpitṛkṛtaṃ bhavati tatkathayati /
sa ca prajāpatiratikrāntajanmani samyakkarmajñānabhāvanānuṣṭhānaiḥ sādhakāvasthāyāṃ yadyasmātkarmajñānabhāvanānuṣṭhānaiḥ prajāpatitvaṃ pratipitsūnāṃ pūrvaḥ prathamaḥ san asmātprajāpatitvapratipitsusamudāyātsarvasmād ādau auṣadadahat /
kim? āsaṅgājñānalakṣaṇānsarvānpāpmanaḥ prajāpatitva pratibandhakāraṇabhūtān /
yasmādevaṃ tasmātpuruṣaḥ, pūrvamauṣaditi puruṣaḥ /
yathāyaṃ prajāpatiroṣitvā prativandhakānpāpmanaḥ sarvānpuruṣaḥ prajāpatirabhavat, evamanyo 'pi jñānakarmabhāvanānuṣṭhānavahninā kevalaṃ jñānabalādvauṣati bhasmīkaroti ha vai sa tam;kam? yo 'smādviduṣaḥ pūrvaḥ prathamaḥ prajāpatirbubhūṣati bhavitumicchati tamityarthaḥ /
taṃ darśayati ya evaṃ vedeti /
sāmarthyājjñānabhāvanāprakarṣavān /
nanvanarthāya prājāpatyapratipipsā, evaṃvidā ceddahyate /
naiṣa doṣaḥ, jñānabhāvanotkarṣābhāvātprathamaṃ prajāpatitvapratipattya bhāvamātratvāddāhasya /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault, because of the absence of superiority in the cultivation of knowledge, the burning is merely the non-attainment of <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood first.

children.text: utkṛṣṭasādhanaḥ prathamaṃ prajāpatitvaṃ prāpnuvan nyūnasādhano na prāpnotīti, sa taṃ dahatītyucyate /
children.translated_text: One with superior means attains <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood first; one with inferior means does not attain [it first] — that is what is meant by 'he burns him.'

children.text: na punaḥ pratyakṣamutkṛṣṭasādhanena itaro dahyate /
children.translated_text: It is not that the other is actually, directly burned by the one with superior means.

children.text: yathā loke ājisṛtāṃ yaḥ prathamamājimupasarpati tenetare dagdhā ivāpahṛtasāmarthyā bhavanti tadvat //1//
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, among those running a race, when one reaches the race [goal] first, the others are as though burned — [meaning] their capability is removed — so it is here. (1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.4.1:] '<s>Ātman</s>' — '<s>Ātman</s>' refers to <s>Prajāpati</s>, the first egg-born embodied being. He who is the fruit of Vedic knowledge and action — what was he? This aggregate of bodily forms — that was undifferentiated, [being one] with the body of <s>Prajāpati</s>. The Self alone existed in the beginning, before the origination of other bodies. And he was <s>puruṣavidha</s> — of the form of a person, characterized by head, vital breaths, and the like — [he was] <s>Virāṭ</s>. He, having first come into being, looking around, having examined — 'Who am I? What are my characteristics?' — saw nothing other, no other entity, than himself — [nothing] other than the form of his own <s>prāṇa</s>-aggregate consisting of causes and effects. He saw only the Self alone, the Self of all. Thus, refined by the impressions of Vedic knowledge from his previous birth, he, <s>Prajāpati</s>, 'I am the Self of all' — this he first uttered, declared. From that — because, from the impression of previous knowledge, he first designated himself as 'I' (<s>aham</s>) — therefore the name '<s>aham</s>' came into being. The <s>Upaniṣad</s> (secret name) of that [<s>Prajāpati</s>] — [the text] will declare the name as shown by the <s>śruti</s> itself. Therefore — because this occurred in <s>Prajāpati</s> — for this reason, among beings who are his effects, even now, at this time, when addressed — when asked 'Who are you?' — one first says 'It is I' — first designating oneself by the name of the causal Self — and then, to one who further wishes to know the specific name, declares afterward the specific bodily designation: '<s>Devadatta</s>' or '<s>Yajñadatta</s>' — whatever name of that specific bodily form was given by mother and father, that one declares. And that <s>Prajāpati</s>, in a previous birth, through the proper cultivation and practice of knowledge and action — in his preparatory state — because, being the first among the entire community of those aspiring to <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood, through the practice of knowledge and action, he was the first, the foremost — he burned up (<s>auṣat</s>). What? All evils — characterized by attachment and ignorance — that were the causes obstructing <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood. Because this is so, therefore [he is called] <s>Puruṣa</s> — because he burned first (<s>pūrvam auṣat</s>), [he is] <s>Puruṣa</s>. Just as this <s>Prajāpati</s>, having burned all evils that were obstructions, became <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s> — so too another, through the fire of cultivating and practicing knowledge, by the power of knowledge alone, burns, reduces to ashes — whom? Anyone who wishes to be the first, before this knower, who desires to become <s>Prajāpati</s> — him, that is the meaning. [The text] shows that one: 'he who knows this.' [Such a one is] preeminent through the superiority of his cultivation of knowledge. [Objection:] But the aspiration to [attain] <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood leads to harm, if one is burned by such a knower.

children.text: yadidaṃ tuṣṭūṣitaṃ karmakāṇḍavihitajñānakarmaphalaṃ prājāpatyalakṣaṇaṃ naiva tatsaṃsāraviṣayamatyakrāmaditīmamartha pradarśayiṣyannāha-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In order to demonstrate that the fruit of knowledge and action enjoined in the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> — characterized as <s>Prajāpati</s>-hood — which has thus been praised, does not at all transcend the domain of <s>saṃsāra</s> — intending to show this meaning, [the text] says:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,4.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.4.2]

children.text:
so 'bibhet tasmād ekākī bibheti |
sa hāyam īkṣāṃ cakre, yan mad anyan nāsti kasmān nu bibhemīti |
tata evāsya bhayaṃ vīyāya |
kasmād dhy abheṣyat |
dvitīyād vai bhayaṃ bhavati || BrhUp_1,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: He was afraid. Therefore, one who is alone is afraid. He reflected: 'Since there is nothing other than me, of what am I afraid?' Thereupon his fear departed. For what should he have feared? It is from a second that fear arises. (BṛUp 1.4.2)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,4.2 so 'bibhetsa prajāpatiryoyaṃ prathamaḥ śarīri puruṣavidho vyākhyātaḥ /
so 'bibhedbhītavānasmadādivadevetyāha /
yasmādayaṃ puruṣavidhaḥ śarīrakaraṇavān ātmanāśaviparītadarśanavatvād abibhet, tasmāttatsāmānyādadyatve 'pyekākī bibheti /
kiñcāsmadādivadeva bhayahetuviparītadarśanāpanodakāraṇaṃ yathābhūtātmadarśanam /
so 'yaṃ prajāpatirīkṣāmīkṣaṇaṃ cakre kṛtavān ha /
katham? ityāha- yadyasmānmattonyadātmavyatirekeṇa vastvantaraṃ pratidvandībhūtaṃ nāsti, tasminnātmavināśahetvabhāve kasmānnu bibhemīti /
tata eva yathābhūtātmadarśanādasya prajāpaterbhayaṃ vīyāya vispaṣṭamapagatavat /
tasya prajāpateryadbhayaṃ tatkevalāvidyānimittameva paramārthadarśane 'nupapannamityāha- kasmāddhyabheṣyat kimityasau bhītavānparamārthanirūpaṇāyāṃ bhayamanupapannamevetyabhiprāyaḥ /
yasmād dvitīyadvastvantaraddhi bhayaṃ bhavati /
dvitīyaṃ ca vastvantaramavidyāpratyupasthāpitameva;na hyadṛśyamānaṃ dvitīyaṃ bhayajanmano hetuḥ"tatra ko mohaḥ kaḥ śokaḥ ekatvamanupaśyataḥ"(īśā.7) iti mantravarṇāt /
yaccaikatvadarśanena bhayamapanunoda tadyuktam /
kasmāt? dvitīyādvastvantarādvai bhayaṃ bhavati, tadekatvadarśanena dvitīyadarśanamapanītamiti nāsti yataḥ /
atra codayanti- kutaḥ prajāpaterekatvadarśanaṃ jātam? ko vāsmai upadideśa? athānupadiṣṭameva prādurabhūt, asmadāderapi tathā prasaṅgaḥ /
atha janmāntarakṛtasaṃskārahetukam, ekatvadarśanānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ /
yathāprajāpateratikrāntajanmāvasthasya ekatvadarśanaṃ vidyamānamapyavidyābandhakāraṇaṃ nāpaninye, yataḥ avidyāsaṃyukta evāyaṃ jāto 'bibhet, evaṃ sarveṣāmekatvadarśanānarthakyaṃ prāpnoti /
antyameva nivartakamiti cenna, pūrvavatpunaḥ prasaṅgenānaikāntyāt /
tasmādanarthakamevaikatvadarśanamiti /
naiṣa doṣaḥ, utkṛṣṭahetūdbhavatvāllokavat /
children.translated_text: This is not a fault, because [the knowledge] arises from a superior cause — just as in the world.

children.text: yathā puṇyakarmodbhavairviviktaiḥ kāryakaraṇaiḥ saṃyukte janmani sati prajñāmedhāsmṛtivaiśāradyaṃ dṛṣṭam, tathā prajāpateḥ dharmajñānavairāgyaiśvaryaviparītahetusarvapāpmadāhāt viśuddhaiḥ kāryakaraṇai saṃyuktamutkṛṣṭaṃ janma tadudbhavaṃ cānupadiṣṭameva yuktamekatvadarśanaṃ prajāpateḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as when one is born with a body and sense-organs that are refined, produced by meritorious <s>karma</s>, wisdom, intelligence, memory, and expertise are observed, similarly, for <s>Prajāpati</s> — who has a supreme birth endowed with body and sense-organs purified by the burning away of all sins through the causes opposite [to sin], namely <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and <s>aiśvarya</s> (lordship) — the perception of oneness that arose from that [superior birth] without external instruction is fitting.

children.text: tathā ca smṛtiḥ-"jñānamagratidhaṃ yasya vairāgyaṃ ca jagatpateḥ /
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Knowledge, supreme, of the Lord of the world, and dispassion,

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ caiva dharmasya sahasiddhaṃ catuṣṭayam //
children.translated_text: and lordship along with <s>dharma</s> — these four arise simultaneously [with Him].'

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.4.2:] 'He was afraid' — this <s>Prajāpati</s>, the first embodied being, who has been described as having a human form, was afraid — he became frightened, just like us, it says. Since this human-formed being, possessing body and sense-organs, was afraid due to the erroneous perception of the destruction of the self, therefore, by analogy with that, even now one who is alone is afraid. Moreover, just as for us, the means for removing the cause of fear — the erroneous perception — is the perception of the self as it truly is. This <s>Prajāpati</s> reflected — made a deliberation. How? He [thought]: 'Since there is no other thing, no second entity opposed to Me apart from Myself, in the absence of a cause for the destruction of the self, why should I be afraid?' From that very perception of the self as it truly is, the fear of this <s>Prajāpati</s> departed — clearly went away. He says that the fear of that <s>Prajāpati</s> was caused by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) alone and is untenable in the presence of the perception of ultimate reality: 'Why indeed would he have been afraid?' — what was the reason for his fear? The import is: upon examination of ultimate reality, fear is indeed untenable. For fear arises from a second thing, another entity. And that second thing, that other entity, is presented by <s>avidyā</s> alone; for an unseen second [entity] is not the cause of the birth of fear — from the mantra text: 'What delusion, what sorrow can there be for one who perceives the oneness?' (Īśā Up. 7). And that he dispelled fear through the perception of oneness is appropriate. Why? Because fear arises from a second thing, another entity — and through the perception of oneness, the perception of a second [entity] has been removed, so there is nothing from which [fear could arise]. Here they raise an objection: whence did the perception of oneness arise for <s>Prajāpati</s>? Or who taught it to him? If it appeared without instruction, then the same consequence would apply to us and others. If it was caused by purificatory impressions (<s>saṃskāra</s>) from previous births, then the consequence would be that the perception of oneness is futile. For just as <s>Prajāpati</s>'s perception of oneness — even though existing in a past birth-state — did not remove the cause of the bondage of <s>avidyā</s>, since he was born conjoined with <s>avidyā</s> and was afraid, so too for everyone, the perception of oneness would turn out to be futile. [If one says] that only the final [realization] is the remover [of ignorance], no — because of the non-conclusiveness [of this argument], since the same problem would recur as before.

sahasiddhatve bhayānupapattiriti cet /
na hyādityena saha tama udeti /

vedāntaśravaṇamanananididhyāsanānāṃ ca sākṣājjñeyaviṣayatvāt /
children.translated_text: And because hearing, reflection, and meditation on <s>Vedānta</s> have the object to be known as their direct [content],

children.text: pāpādipratibandhakṣaye cātmamanasorbhūtārthajñānanimittasvābhāvyāt /
children.translated_text: and because when the obstruction of sins and the like is removed, the self and mind naturally [have the capacity] to be the cause of knowledge of reality as it is,

children.text: tasmādahetutvaṃ na jātu jñānasya śraddhāpraṇipātādīnāmiti //2//
children.translated_text: therefore, faith, prostration, and the like are never without being causes of knowledge. // 2 //

[Objection:] If [these four] arise simultaneously, then fear is untenable — for darkness does not rise together with the sun. No — because the sentence about simultaneous arising has a different, uninstructed meaning. [Objection:] If faith, devoted attention, prostration, and the like are not causes [of knowledge], then it would follow that the causes of knowledge enjoined in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> — such as 'The faithful one obtains knowledge, being devoted and with senses controlled' (BhG 4.39), 'Know that by prostration' (BhG 4.34), and the like — are not causes; [and this would be so] if knowledge [is caused] by <s>dharma</s> accumulated in previous births, as in the case of <s>Prajāpati</s>. No — because differences based on the alternatives, combinations, and the qualified and unqualified nature of causes are tenable. For in the world, the causes of effects that have [specific] causes are varied in multiple ways as alternatives. Similarly, there are combinations of causes. And among those that are alternatives and those that are combined, there are further differences based on the qualified and unqualified nature [of the causes]. For example, in the case of color-perception — an effect that has a cause: in darkness, without light, the contact of the eye with form is the cause of color-perception for nocturnal creatures. For <s>yogins</s>, the mind alone is the cause of color-perception. But for us, the causes are combined — the contact [of eye and object] together with light — and further differentiated by differences of light such as sunlight, moonlight, and so forth. Similarly, there would be differences based on the qualified and unqualified nature of [various types of] light. In exactly this way, for the knowledge of the oneness of the self too, in some cases <s>karma</s> accumulated in previous births is the cause, as for <s>Prajāpati</s>. In some cases, austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is the cause — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Seek to know through austerity' (ChāUp 3.2.1). In some cases, from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> passages such as 'A person who has a teacher knows' (ChāUp 6.14.2), 'The faithful one obtains knowledge' (BhG 4.39), 'Know that by prostration' (BhG 4.34), 'From the teacher alone' (ChāUp 4.1.3), 'It is to be seen, to be heard' (BṛUp 2.4.5), and so forth — faith and the rest are the exclusive causes for attaining knowledge, because they serve as causes for the removal of obstacles such as <s>adharma</s> and the like.

children.text: itaśca saṃsāraviṣaya eva prājāpatitvam, yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, the state of <s>Prajāpati</s> belongs to the realm of <s>saṃsāra</s> alone — because:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,4.3
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 1,4.3

children.text:
sa vai naiva reme |
tasmād ekākī na ramate |
sa dvitīyam aicchat |
sa haitāvān āsa yathā strīpumāṃsau sampariṣvaktau |
sa imam evātmānaṃ dvedhāpātayat |
tataḥ patiś ca patnī cābhavatām |
tasmād idam ardhabṛgalam iva sva iti ha smāha yājñavalkyaḥ |
tasmād ayam ākāśaḥ striyā pūryata eva |
tāṃ samabhavat |
tato manuṣyā ajāyanta || BrhUp_1,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: He indeed did not delight. Therefore one who is alone does not delight. He desired a second. He was as large as a man and wife in close embrace. He caused this very self to fall into two parts. From that arose husband (<s>pati</s>) and wife (<s>patnī</s>). Therefore this [body] is like a half-piece of a split whole, as <s>Yājñavalkya</s> used to say. Therefore this space is filled by a wife. He united with her. From that, human beings were born. // BṛhUp 1.4.3 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,4.3 sa prāpatirvai naiva reme ratiṃ nānvabhavat, aratyāviṣṭo 'bhūdityarthaḥ, asmādādideva yataḥ, idānīmapi tasmādekākitvādidharmavattvādekākī na ramate ratiṃ nānubhavati /
ratirnāmeṣṭārthasaṃyogajā krīḍā, tatprasaṃgina iṣṭaviyogānmanasyākulībhāvo 'ratirityucyate /
sa tasyā araterapanodāya dvitīyam aratyapaghātasamarthaṃ strīvastvaicchadgṛddhimakarot /
tasya caivaṃ strīviṣayaṃ gṛdhyataḥ striyā pariṣvaktasyevātmano bhāvo babhūva /
sa tena satyepsutvād etāvānetatparimāṇa āsa babhūva ha /
kiṃparimāṇaḥ? ityāha- yathā loke strīpumāṃsau aratyapanodāya sampariṣvaktau yatparimāṇau syātāṃ tathā tatparimāṇau babhūvetyarthaḥ /
sa tathā tatparimāṇameva iyamātmānaṃ dvedhā dviprakāramapātayatpātitavān iyamevetyavadhāraṇaṃ mūlakāraṇādvirājo viśeṣaṇārtham /
na kṣīrasya sarvopamardena dadhibhāvāpattivadvirāṭ sarvopamardenaitāvānāsa;kiṃ tarhi? ātmanā vyavasthitasyaiva virājaḥ satyasaṃkalpatvādātmavyatiriktaṃ strīpuṃsapariṣvaktaparisāṇaṃ śarīrāntaraṃ babhūva /
sa eva ca virāṭ tathābhūtaḥ sa haitāvānāseti sāmānādhikaraṇyāt /
tatastasmātpātanātpatitaśca patnī cābhavatāmiti dampatyornirvacanaṃ laukikayoḥ /
ata eva tasmāt, yasmādātmana evārdhaḥ pṛthagbhūtoyeyaṃ strī, tasmādidaṃ śarīramānor'dhabṛgalamardhaṃ ca tad bṛgalaṃ vidalaṃ ca tadardhabṛgalam ardhavidalamevetyarthaḥ /
prākstryudvahanātkasyārdhabṛgalam? ityucyate- sva ātmana iti /
evamāha smoktavānkila yājñavalkyaḥ, yajñasya valko vaktā yajñavalkastasyāpatyaṃ yājñavalkyo daivarātirityarthaḥ /
brahmaṇo vāpatyam /
children.translated_text: Or [he is] the offspring of <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: yasmādayaṃ puruṣārdha ākāśaḥ stryardhaśūnyaḥ punarudvahanāttasmātpūryate stryardhena, punaḥ sampuṭīkaraṇeneva vidalārdhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since this male half — the <s>puruṣa</s> — the space that is empty of the female half, is filled again by the female half through [re-]marriage, therefore it is filled, as if making a whole again from the half of a split piece.

children.text: tāṃ sa prajāpatirmanvākhyaḥ śatarūpākhyāmātmano duhitaraṃ patnītvena kalpitāṃ samabhavanmaithunamupagatavān /
children.translated_text: That <s>Prajāpati</s>, named <s>Manu</s>, united with her — named <s>Śatarūpā</s>, his own daughter who was conceived as a wife — he had sexual intercourse [with her].

children.text: tatastasmāttadupagamanād manuṣyā ajāyantotpannāḥ //3//
children.translated_text: From that — from that union — human beings were born, i.e. came into existence. // 3 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.4.3:] That <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed 'did not delight' — did not experience delight; the meaning is that he was seized by restlessness — just like us. And since he has properties such as being alone and the like, therefore even now one who is alone does not delight — does not experience delight. Delight is the play born of the union with a desired object; the mental agitation arising from the separation of a desired object connected with it is called restlessness (<s>arati</s>). He, for the removal of that restlessness, desired a second — a female entity capable of dispelling his restlessness — he became desirous [of it]. And while he was thus longing for a woman, the state of his self became as if it were embraced by a woman. He, due to that desire being true, was of such measure — became of that extent. Of what measure? It is said: just as in the world a man and a woman are of a particular measure when they are in close embrace for the removal of restlessness — he became of that very measure; this is the meaning. He, being of that very measure, caused this self to fall into two — into two forms. The emphatic determination 'this very' is for the purpose of distinguishing [this creation] from the [creation of] <s>Virāj</s> from the root cause. It is not that <s>Virāj</s> became of this extent through a total transformation [of itself], as milk [totally transforms] into curd; rather, while <s>Virāj</s> remained as himself, through the power of true will (<s>satyasaṃkalpa</s>), a second body in the measure of a man and woman in embrace — different from himself — came into being. And that very <s>Virāj</s>, being in that state, 'was of such measure' — from the co-referentiality [of the terms]. From that splitting, a fallen one (<s>pati</s> = husband) and a fallen one (<s>patnī</s> = wife) came to be — this is the etymological derivation of 'husband and wife' in worldly usage. For this very reason — since this woman is half [of the self] that has become separate from the self — therefore this body is like a 'half-piece' — a half (<s>ardha</s>), and that is a 'piece' (<s>bṛgala</s>), a 'split piece' (<s>vidala</s>) — [the compound] '<s>ardhabṛgala</s>' means 'half of a split piece'; this is the meaning. Before the marriage of a wife, whose half-piece is it? It is answered: '<s>sva</s>' — of oneself. Thus <s>Yājñavalkya</s> used to say — <s>Yajña</s>'s speaker (<s>valka</s>) is <s>Yajñavalka</s>, and his descendant is <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, [meaning] the son of <s>Daivarāti</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,4.4
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 1,4.4

children.text:
so heyam īkṣāṃ cakre -- kathaṃ nu mātmana eva janayitvā sambhavati |
hanta tiro 'sānīti |
sā gaur abhavad vṛṣabha itaraḥ |
tāṃ sam evābhavat |
tato gāvo 'jāyanta |
vaḍavetarābhavad aśvavṛṣa itaraḥ |
gardabhītarā gardabha itaraḥ |
tāṃ sam evābhavat |
tata ekaśapham ajāyata |
ajetarābhavad basta itaraḥ |
avir itarā meṣa itaraḥ |
tāṃ sam evābhavat |
tato 'jāvayo 'jāyanta |
evam eva yad idaṃ kiñca mithunam ā pipīlikābhyas tat sarvam asṛjata || BrhUp_1,4.4 ||
children.translated_text: She reflected: 'How can he unite with me after having produced me from his very self? Well, let me hide myself.' She became a cow; the other became a bull. He united with her. From that, cattle were born. One became a mare, the other a stallion; one became a she-donkey, the other a male donkey. He united with her. From that, single-hoofed animals were born. One became a she-goat, the other a he-goat; one became a ewe, the other a ram. He united with her. From that, goats and sheep were born. Thus indeed, whatever pairs there are, down to the ants — all that he created. // BṛhUp 1.4.4 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,4.4 sā śatarūpā u ha iyaṃ seyaṃ duhitṛgamane smārtaṃ pratiṣedhamanusmarantīkṣāñcake /
kathaṃ nvidamakṛtyaṃ yanmā māmātmana eva janayitvotpādya sambhavatyupagacchati /
yadyapyayaṃ nirghṛṇo 'haṃ hantedānīṃ tiro 'sāni jātyantareṇa tiraskṛtā bhavāni /
ityevamīkṣitvāsau gaurabhavat /
utpādyaprāṇikarmabhiścodyamānāyāḥ punaḥ punaḥ saivamatiḥ śatarūpāyā manoścābhavat /
tataśca ṛṣabha itaraḥ /
tāṃ samevābhadityādi pūrvavat /
tato gāvo 'jāyanta /
tathā baḍavetarābhavadaśvavṛṣa itaraḥ /
tathā gardabhītarā gardabha itaraḥ /
tatra baḍavāśvavṛṣādīnāṃ saṅgamāttata ekaśaphamekagvuram aśvāśvataragardabhākhyaṃ trayamajāyata /
tathā ajetarābhavadvastaśchāga itaraḥ, tathā aviritarā meṣa itaraḥ, tāṃ samevābhavat /
tāṃ tāmiti vīpsā /
children.translated_text: The repetition '<s>tāṃ tām</s>' ('with her, with her') is distributive.

children.text: tāmajāṃ tāmaviñcetisamabhavadevetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: he united with that she-goat and with that ewe.

children.text: tato 'jāśvāvayaścājāvayo 'jāyanta /
children.translated_text: From that, goats and sheep were born.

children.text: evameva yadidaṃ kiñca yatkiṃñcedaṃ mithunaṃ srīpuṃsalakṣaṇaṃ dvandam, ā pipīlikābhyaḥ pipīlikābhiḥ sahānenaivanyāyena tatsarvamasṛjata jagatsṛṣṭavān //4//
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, whatever and whichever pairs there are — having the characteristic of male and female — down to the ants, inclusive of the ants — by this very process, all that he created, he brought the world into existence. // 4 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.4.4:] She — <s>Śatarūpā</s> — this very one, this daughter, recalling the <s>smṛti</s> prohibition against going to one's daughter, reflected. 'How is this — this improper thing — that he, having produced me — having generated me from his own self — unites with me, approaches me? Even though he is shameless, well, let me now hide myself — let me become concealed by assuming another species.' Having thus reflected, she became a cow. And the other — driven by the <s>karma</s> of the beings to be created — again and again, this same thought and intention arose in <s>Śatarūpā</s>'s mind. And so the other [<s>Prajāpati</s>] became a bull. 'He united with her' and so forth — as before. From that, cattle were born. Similarly, one became a mare, the other a stallion. Similarly, one became a she-donkey, the other a male donkey. There, from the union of the mare and the stallion and the rest, from that, single-hoofed [animals] were born — the three classes known as horses, mules, and donkeys, having a single hoof. Similarly, one became a she-goat, the other a he-goat (<s>vasta</s>, i.e. <s>chāga</s>); similarly, one became a ewe, the other a ram. He united with her.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,4.5

so 'ved ahaṃ vāva sṛṣṭir asmy ahaṃ hīdaṃ sarvam asṛkṣīti |
tataḥ sṛṣṭir abhavat |
sṛṣṭyāṃ hāsyaitasyāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,4.5 ||
children.translated_text: He knew: 'I indeed am creation, for I created all this.' Therefore he became [known as] creation. One who knows this thus comes to be in this creation of his. // BṛhUp 1.4.5 //
START BrhUp 1,4.5

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,4.5 sa prajāpatiḥ sarvamidaṃ jagatsṛṣṭvā avet /
katham? ahaṃ vāvāhameva sṛṣṭiḥ, sṛjyate iti sṛṣṭaṃ jagaducyate sṛṣṭiriti /
yanmayāsṛṣṭaṃ jaganmadabhedatvādahamevāsmi na matto vyatiricyate /
children.translated_text: The world that was created by me, being non-different from me, is myself alone — it does not differ from me.

children.text: kuta etat? ahaṃ hi yasmādidaṃ sarvaṃ jagadasṛkṣi sṛṣṭavānasmi tasmādityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: How is this? Because I — since I created all this world — therefore; this is the meaning.

children.text: yasmātsṛṣṭiśabdena ātmānamevābhyadhātprajāpatiḥ, tatastasmātsṛṣṭirabhavat sṛṣṭināmābhavat /
children.translated_text: Since <s>Prajāpati</s> designated his very self by the word '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' (creation), therefore — from that — he became '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' — he came to have the name 'creation.'

children.text: sṛṣṭyāṃ jagati, hāsya prajāpategetasyāmetasmiñjagati, sa prajāpativatsraṣṭā bhavati svātmano 'nanyabhūtasya jagataḥ, kaḥ? ya evaṃ prajāpativadyathoktaṃ svātmano 'nanyabhūtaṃ jagatsādhyātmādibhūtādhidaivaṃ jagadahamasmīti veda //5//
children.translated_text: in this creation, in this world — of this <s>Prajāpati</s>, in this world — he becomes a creator like <s>Prajāpati</s>, of the world that is non-different from his own self. Who? One who thus knows — as <s>Prajāpati</s> [knew] — that the world of the individual realm (<s>ādhyātma</s>) and the cosmic realm (<s>adhidaiva</s>), which is non-different from one's own self, 'I am [all this].' // 5 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.4.5:] That <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created all this world, knew. How? 'I myself alone am the creation' — what is created is called '<s>sṛṣṭi</s>' (creation), meaning the created world.

children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.4.6]

children.text:
athety abhyamanthat |
sa mukhāc ca yoner hastābhyāṃ cāgnim asṛjata |
tasmād etad ubhayam alomakam antarataḥ |
alomakā hi yonir antarataḥ |
tad yad idam āhur amuṃ yajāmuṃ yajety ekaikaṃ devam etasyaiva sā visṛṣṭiḥ |
eṣa u hy eva sarve devāḥ |
atha yat kiñcedam ārdraṃ tad retaso 'sṛjata |
tad u soma |
etāvad vā idaṃ sarvam annaṃ caivānnādaś ca |
soma evānnam agnir annādaḥ |
saiṣā brahmaṇo 'tisṛṣṭiḥ |
yac chreyaso devān asṛjatātha yan martyaḥ sann amṛtān asṛjata tasmād atisṛṣṭir |
atisṛṣṭyāṃ hāsyaitasyāṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_1,4.6 ||
children.translated_text: Then he churned. From his mouth and from his hands, which are the [creative] openings, he created fire. Therefore both of these are hairless on the inside — for the [creative] opening is hairless on the inside. When they say 'sacrifice to this deity, sacrifice to that deity' — naming each deity separately — this is merely his differentiated creation, for he alone is all the deities. Now, whatever here is moist, that he created from his semen — and that is <s>Soma</s>. This entire [universe] is just this much: food and the eater of food. <s>Soma</s> is the food, <s>Agni</s> is the eater of food. This is the surpassing creation of <s>Brahman</s>: that he created deities superior to himself; and that, being mortal, he created immortals — therefore it is a surpassing creation. One who knows this comes to be in this surpassing creation. // BṛhUp 1.4.6 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,4.6 evaṃ sa prajāpatirjagadidaṃ mithunātmakaṃ sṛṣṭā brahmaṇādivarṇaniyanvardevatāḥ sisṛkṣurādau, ayeti śabdadvayamabhinayapradarśanārtham, anena prakāreṇa mukhe hastau prakṣityābhyamanyadābhimukhyena manyanapakarot /
sa mukhahastābhyāṃ mathitvā mukhācca yonerhastābhyāṃ ca yonibhyāmagniṃ brāhmaṇajāteranugrahakartāramasṛjata sṛṣṭavān /
yasmāddāhakasyāgneryoniretadubhayaṃ hastau mukhaṃ ca, tasmādbhaya mapyetadalomakaṃ lomavivarjitam /
kiṃ sarvameva? na, antarato 'bhyantarataḥ;asti hi yonyā sāmānyamubhayasyāsya /
kim? alomakā hi yonirantarataḥ strīṇām /
tathā brāhmaṇo 'pi mukhādeva jajhe prajāpateḥ /
tasmādekayonitvājjayeṣṭhenevānujo 'nugṛhyate agninā brāhmaṇaḥ /
tasmādbrāhmaṇo 'gnidevatyo mukhavīryaśceti śrutismṛtisiddham /
tathā balāśrayābhyāṃ bāhubhyāṃ balabhidādikaṃ kṣanniyajātiniyantarāṃ kṣanniyaṃ ca /
tasmādaindraṃ kṣatraṃ bāhuvīryaṃ ceti śrutau smṛtau cāvagatam /
tathoruta īhā ceṣṭā tadāśrayādvasvādilakṣaṇaṃ viśo niyantāraṃ viśaṃ ca /
tasmātkṛṣyādiparo vasvādidevatyaśca vaiśyaḥ /
tathā pūṣaṇaṃ pṛthvīdaivataṃ śūdraṃ ca padbhyāṃ paricaraṇakṣamamasṛjateti śrutismṛtiprasiddheḥ /
tatra kṣatrādidevatāsargamihānuktaṃ vakṣyamāṇamamapyuktavadupasaṃharati sṛṣṭisākalyānukīrtyai /
yatheyaṃ śrutirvyavasthitā tathā prajāpatireva sarve devā iti niścitor'thaḥ /
sraṣṭurananyatvātsṛṣṭānām /
prajāpatinaiva tu sṛṣṭatvād devānām /
athaivaṃ prakaraṇārthe vyavasthite tatstutyabhiprāyeṇāvidvanmatāntaranindopanyāsaḥ, anyanindānyastutaye /
tattatra karmaprakaraṇe kevalayājñikā yāgakāle yadidaṃ vaca āhuḥ -'amumagniṃ yajāsumindraṃ yaja'ityādi - nāmaśastrastotrakarmādibhinnatvādbhinnamevāgnyādidevamevaikaṃ manyamānā āhurityabhiprāyaḥ /
tanna tathā vidyāt, yasmādetasyaiva prajāpateḥ sā visṛṣṭirdevabhedaḥ sarva eṣa u hyeva prajāpatireva prāṇaḥ sarve devāḥ /
atra vipratipadyante - para eva hiraṇyagarbhe ityeke /
saṃsārītyapare /
paraṃ eva tu mantravarṇāt /
"indraṃ mitraṃ varuṇamagnimāhuḥ"iti śruteḥ /
"eṣa brahmaiṣa indra eṣa prajāpatirete sarve devāḥ"(ai.u.5 / 3) iti ca śruteḥ /
smṛteśca -"etameke vadantyagniṃ manumanye prajāpatim"(manu.12 / 123) iti"yo 'sāvatīndriyo 'grāhyaḥ sūkṣmo 'vyaktaḥ sanātanaḥ /
sarvabhūtamayo 'cintyaḥ sa eva svayamudbabhau" /
(manu.1 / 7) iti /
saṃsāryeva vā syāt /
"sarvainpāpmana aupat"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 1) iti śruteḥ /
na hyasaṃsāriṇaḥ pāpmadāhaprasaṅgo 'sti /
bhayāratisaṃyogaśravaṇāt /
"atha yanmartyaḥ sannamṛtānasṛjata"(bṛ.u.1 / 4 / 6) iti ca /
"hiraṇyagarbhaṃ paśyati jāyamānam"(śve.u.4 / 12) iti ca mantravarṇāt /
smṛteśca karmavipākaprakriyāyām -"brahmā viśvasṛjo dharmo mahānavyaktameva ca /
uttamāṃ sātvikīmetāṃ gatimāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ"(manu.12 / 50) iti /
athaivaṃ viruddhārthānupapatteḥ prāmāṇyavyāghāta iti cet? na, kalpanāntaropapatteravirodhāt /
upādhiviśeṣasambandhādviśeṣakalpanāntaramupapadyate /
"āsīno dūraṃ vrajati śayāno yāti sarvataḥ /
kastaṃ madāmadaṃ devaṃ madanyo jñātumarhati"(ka.u.1 / 2 / 21) ityevamādiśrutibhya upādhivaśātsaṃsāritvaṃ na paramārthataḥ /
svato 'saṃsāryeva /
evamekatvaṃ nānātvaṃ ca hiraṇyagarbhasya /
tathā sarvajīvānām, tattvamasi (chā.u.6 / 8 -16) iti śruteḥ /
hiraṇyagarbhastu upādhiśuddhyatiśayāpekṣayā prāyaśaḥ para eveti śrutismṛtivādāḥ pravṛttāḥ /
saṃsāritvaṃ tu kvacideva darśayanti /
jīvānāṃ upādhigatāśuddhibāhulyātsaṃsāritvameva prāyaśo 'bhilapyate /
vyāvṛttakṛtsnopādhibhedāpekṣayā tu sarvaḥ paratvenābhidhīyate śrutismṛtivādaiḥ /
tārkikaistu parityaktāgamabalairasti nāsti kartākartetyādi viruddhaṃ bahu tarkapadbhirākulīkṛtaḥ śāstrārthaḥ, tenārthaniścayo durlabhaḥ /
ye tu kevalaśāstrānusāriṇaḥ śāntadarpāsteṣāṃ pratyakṣaviṣaya iva niścitaḥ śāstrārthe devatādiviṣayaḥ /
tatra prajāpaterekasya devasyātrādyalakṣaṇo bhedo vivakṣita iti tatrāgnirukto 'ttā, ādyaḥ soma idānīmucyate - atha yatkiñcedaṃ loka ārdraṃ dravātmakaṃ tadretasa ātmāno bījādasṛjata;retasa āpaḥ (ai.u.1 / 4) iti śruteḥ /
dravātmakaśca somaḥ /
tasmādyadārdraṃ prajāpatinā retasaḥ sṛṣṭaṃ tadu soma eva /
etāvadvai etāvadeva nāto 'dhikamidaṃ sarvam /
kiṃ tat? annaṃ caiva somo dravātmakatvādāpyāyakam /
annādaścāgnirauṣṇyād rūkṣatvācca /
tatraivadhriyate, soma evānnaṃ yadadyate tadeva soma ityarthaḥ /
ya evāttā sa evāgniḥ arthabalāddhyavadhāraṇam /
agnirapi kvacid hūyamānaḥ somapakṣasyaiva /
somo 'pījyamāno 'gnirevāttṛtvāt /
evamagnīṣomātmakaṃ jagadātmatvena paśyanta kenaciddoṣeṇa lipyate, prajāpatiśca bhavati /
children.translated_text: Thus, one who sees the world consisting of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s> as one's own self is not tainted by any defect, and becomes <s>Prajāpati</s>.

children.text: saiṣā brahmaṇaḥ prajāpateratisṛṣṭirātmano 'pyatiśayā /
children.translated_text: This is the surpassing creation (<s>atisṛṣṭi</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, i.e. <s>Prajāpati</s> — surpassing even his own self.

children.text: kā sā ityāha - yacchreyasaḥ praśasyatarānātmanaḥ sakāśādyasmādasṛjata devāṃstasmāddevasṛṣṭiratisṛṣṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: What is that? He says: because he created, from himself, deities who are more excellent, more praiseworthy than himself — therefore the creation of the deities is a surpassing creation.

children.text: kathaṃ punarātmano 'tiśayā sṛṣṭiḥ ityata āha - atha yadyasmānmartyaḥ sanmaraṇadharmā sannamṛtānamaraṇadharmiṇo devān karmajñānavahninā sarvānātmanaḥ pāpmana oṣitvāsṛjata, tasmādetāmatisṛṣṭiṃ prajāpaterātmabhūtāṃ yo veda sa etasyāmatisṛṣṭyāṃ prajāpatiriva bhavati prajāpativadeva sraṣṭā bhavati //6//
children.translated_text: But how is this creation surpassing his own self? To this he says: moreover, because he, being mortal — subject to death — created immortals, deities not subject to death, by the fire of action and knowledge, having burned away all evils from himself — one who knows this surpassing creation, which has become the self of <s>Prajāpati</s>, becomes like <s>Prajāpati</s>, becomes a creator just like <s>Prajāpati</s>. // 6 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.4.6: Thus, that <s>Prajāpati</s>, having created this world consisting of pairs, wishing to create the four classes (<s>varṇas</s>) beginning with <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> together with their governing deities — first, the two words 'atha iti' serve to indicate a gesture; by this manner, placing the hands before the mouth, he churned — he performed the act of churning, facing forward. Having churned with the mouth and hands, from the mouth and from the hands, which are the [creative] openings, he created <s>Agni</s>, the benefactor of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> class. Because the mouth and hands are both the sources of the burning fire, therefore both of these are hairless — devoid of hair. Is it entirely so? No, [only] on the inside, on the inner surface — for there is a commonality of both with the [creative] opening. In what respect? Because the [creative] opening of women is hairless on the inside. Similarly, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> too was born from the very mouth of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Therefore, because of having the same source, the younger [<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>] is favored by the elder, <s>Agni</s>. Therefore, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has <s>Agni</s> as his deity and the strength of the mouth — this is established in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. Similarly, from the arms, the seat of strength, [he created] the governing deity of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class, <s>Indra</s>, and the <s>Kṣatriya</s>. Therefore, 'sovereignty belongs to <s>Indra</s>' and 'strength of the arms' — this is known in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. Similarly, from the thighs, the seat of exertion and activity, [he created] the governing deity of the <s>Vaiśya</s> class, the <s>Vasus</s> and the like, and the <s>Vaiśya</s>. Therefore, the <s>Vaiśya</s> is devoted to agriculture and the like and has the <s>Vasus</s> and other deities. Similarly, from the feet, capable of service, he created <s>Pūṣan</s>, whose deity is the earth, and the <s>Śūdra</s> — this is well known in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>. Therein, the creation of the <s>Kṣatriya</s> and other deities, though not stated here but to be stated [elsewhere], is summarized as if already stated, for the sake of recounting the totality of creation. As this <s>śruti</s> is established, the conclusion is definite that <s>Prajāpati</s> alone is all the deities — because the created beings are non-different from the creator. For the deities were created by <s>Prajāpati</s> alone. Now, with the topic of the section thus established, the censure of the view of the ignorant is introduced with the intention of praising [the correct view] — for the censure of one is for the praise of another. There, in the context of ritual, the mere ritualists (<s>yājñikas</s>), at the time of sacrifice, say these words: 'Sacrifice to <s>Agni</s>; sacrifice to <s>Indra</s>' — and so forth — thinking that each deity such as <s>Agni</s> is distinct, due to the difference in the ritual acts of <s>nāmaśastra</s>, <s>stotra</s>, and the like — this is the intent. One should not know it thus, for this differentiation of deities is merely the differentiated creation of this very <s>Prajāpati</s>. All these — this <s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>prāṇa</s>, is indeed all the deities. Here [scholars] disagree: some say [<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> is] the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone; others say he is a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being). But from the <s>mantra</s> text, [he is] indeed the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>]. Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'They call him <s>Indra</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Agni</s>.' And from the <s>śruti</s>: 'This is <s>Brahman</s>, this is <s>Indra</s>, this is <s>Prajāpati</s>; these are all the deities' (<s>Aitareya Upaniṣad</s> 5.3). And from <s>smṛti</s>: 'Some call him <s>Agni</s>, others <s>Manu</s>, others <s>Prajāpati</s>' (<s>Manu</s> 12.123); 'He who is beyond the senses, ungraspable, subtle, unmanifest, eternal, consisting of all beings, inconceivable — he himself manifested' (<s>Manu</s> 1.7). Or he could be a <s>saṃsārin</s> — because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'He burned away all evils' (BṛUp 1.4.1), for the burning away of evil does not apply to one who is not in <s>saṃsāra</s>. And because fear and grief are heard [of him]. And because of [the text]: 'Though mortal, he created the immortals' (BṛUp 1.4.6). And from the <s>mantra</s> text: 'They see <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> being born' (<s>Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad</s> 4.12). And from <s>smṛti</s>, in the context of the maturation of <s>karma</s>: '<s>Brahmā</s>, the world-creators, <s>dharma</s>, the great unmanifest — the wise call this the highest <s>sāttvika</s> destiny' (<s>Manu</s> 12.50). [Objection:] If there is an impossibility of reconciling contradictory meanings, the authority [of scripture] would be compromised. [Reply:] No, because reconciliation is possible through an alternative construction — there is no contradiction. Through the association with different limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>), an alternative particular construction is possible. From <s>śruti</s> passages such as: 'Seated, he travels far; lying down, he goes everywhere. Who other than I can know that god who is both intoxicated and sober?' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.21) — [we understand that] the state of being in <s>saṃsāra</s> is due to limiting adjuncts, not in ultimate reality. By his own [nature], he is indeed not in <s>saṃsāra</s>. Thus [are to be understood] both the oneness and the multiplicity of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. Similarly for all individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>), because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'You are that' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.8-16). But for <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, because of the superior purity of his limiting adjuncts, <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> statements generally speak of him as the supreme [<s>Brahman</s>]. They show his state of being in <s>saṃsāra</s> only occasionally. For individual souls, because of the preponderance of impurity in their limiting adjuncts, the state of being in <s>saṃsāra</s> is generally stated. But with reference to the transcendence of all divisions of limiting adjuncts, everything is declared to be the supreme by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> statements. But by the logicians who have abandoned the power of scripture, much that is contradictory — 'it exists,' 'it does not exist,' 'it is an agent,' 'it is not an agent' — has been introduced by arguments, confounding the meaning of scripture, and therefore a definitive conclusion is difficult to reach. But for those who follow scripture alone, who are free from pride, the meaning of scripture regarding deities and the like is as clear as a matter of direct perception. Therein, regarding the one deity <s>Prajāpati</s>, the differentiation characterized as food and eater of food is intended. <s>Agni</s>, the eater, having been stated as the first, <s>Soma</s>, the food, is now stated. Now, whatever here in the world is moist — of a liquid nature — that he created from semen, from his own seed; [as stated in the <s>śruti</s>:] 'From semen [arise] waters' (<s>Aitareya Upaniṣad</s> 1.4). And <s>Soma</s> is of a liquid nature. Therefore, whatever is moist, created by <s>Prajāpati</s> from semen, that is <s>Soma</s> itself. 'This much' — just this much, no more — is this entire [universe]. What is that? Food — <s>Soma</s>, because of being of liquid nature and nourishing. And the eater of food — <s>Agni</s>, because of heat and dryness. Therein, this is restated: <s>Soma</s> alone is the food — whatever is eaten, that is <s>Soma</s> — this is the meaning. And whatever eats, that is <s>Agni</s> — the emphasis is from the force of the meaning.

children.text:
sarvaṃ vaidikaṃ sādhanaṃ jñānakarmalakṣaṇaṃ kartrādyanekakārakāpekṣaṃ prajāpatitvaphalāvasānaṃ sādhyametāvadeva yadetadvyākṛtaṃ jagatsaṃsāraḥ /
athaitasyaiva sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇasya vyākṛtasya jagato vyākaraṇātprāgbījāvasthā yā tāṃ nirdidijñatyaṅkurādikāryānumitāmiva vṛkṣasya, karmabījo 'vidyākṣetro hyasau saṃsāravṛkṣaḥ samūla uddhartavya iti /
taduddharaṇe hi puruṣārthaparisamāptiḥ /
tathā coktam -"ūrdhvamūlo 'vākśākhaḥ"iti kāṭhake /
gītāsu ca"ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥ śākham"iti /
purāṇe ca"brahmavṛkṣaḥ sanātanaḥ"iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] All Vedic means — characterized by knowledge and action, dependent on many factors such as the agent and other causal factors, culminating in the fruit of attaining the state of <s>Prajāpati</s> — to be accomplished is just this much: this differentiated world, which is <s>saṃsāra</s>. Now, [the text] wishes to indicate the seed-state of this very differentiated world — which has the nature of what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment — prior to its differentiation, as if inferred from the effects like sprouts and the like, just as [one infers] the [seed of a] tree. For this tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> has <s>karma</s> (action) as its seed and <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) as its field — it is to be uprooted entirely, with its roots. For in its uprooting lies the culmination of the human goal. And thus it has been said: 'Having its roots above, its branches below' — in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s>). And in the <s>Gītā</s>: 'With roots above, branches below.' And in the <s>Purāṇa</s>: 'The eternal tree of <s>Brahman</s>.'
