tad etan nabhyaṃ yad ayam ātmā |
pradhir vittam |
tasmād yady api sarvajyāniṃ jīyata ātmanā cej jīvati pradhināgād ity evāhuḥ || BrhUp_1,5.15 ||
children.translated_text: That year — <s>Prajāpati</s> — of sixteen digits is indeed this very person who knows thus. His wealth alone is the fifteen digits. The self itself is his sixteenth digit. He is filled and diminished by wealth alone. This self is the hub of the wheel; wealth is the rim. Therefore, even if one loses everything, if one lives by the self alone, they say: 'He has lost only the rim [of the wheel].' // BṛhUp 1.5.15 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.15 yo vai parokṣābhihitaḥ saṃvatsaraḥ prajāpatiḥ ṣoḍaśakalaḥ sa naivātyantaṃ parokṣo mantavyaḥ, yasmādayameva sa pratyakṣa upalabhyate /
ko 'sāvayam? yo yathektaṃ tryannātmakaṃ prajāpatimātmabhūtaṃ vetti sa evaṃvitpuruṣaḥ /
kena sāmānyena prajāpatiriti taducyate - tasyaivaṃvidaḥ puruṣasya gavādi vittameva pañcadaśa kalā upacayāpacayadharmitvāt;tadvittasādhyaṃ ca karma /
tasya kṛtsnatāyai ātmaiva piṇḍa evāsya viduṣaḥ ṣoḍaśī kalā dhruvasthānīyā /
sa candravadvittenaivāpūryate cāpakṣīyate ca - tadetalloke prasiddham /
tadetannabhyam, nābhyai hitaṃ nabhyaṃ nābhiṃ vā arhatīti /
kiṃ tat? yadayaṃ yo 'yamātmā piṇḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: What is that? This — that which is the self, the body.

children.text: pradhirvittaṃ parivārasthānīyaṃ bāhyaṃ cakrasyevāranemyādi /
children.translated_text: The rim (<s>pradhi</s>) is the wealth — occupying the place of the outer retinue, like the felly and rim of a wheel.

children.text: tasmādyadyapi sarvajyāniṃ sarvasvāpaharaṇaṃ jīyate hīyate glāniṃ prāpnoti, ātmanā cakranābhisthānīyena cedyadi jīvati pradhinā bāhyena parivāreṇāyamagātkṣīṇo 'yaṃ yathā cakramaranemivimuktamevamāhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, even if one suffers the loss of everything — the confiscation of all possessions — one is diminished and reaches a state of decline; yet if one lives by the self — which occupies the place of the hub of the wheel — [they say] 'This one has lost only the rim (<s>pradhi</s>), the outer retinue' — just as a wheel [that has lost] its felly and rim — thus they say.

children.text: jīvaṃśced aranemisthānīyena vittena punarupacīyata ityabhiprāyaḥ //15//
children.translated_text: The import is: as long as one lives, one can be replenished again with wealth, which occupies the place of the felly and rim. // 15 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.5.15:] That <s>Prajāpati</s> described indirectly as the year of sixteen digits should not be regarded as entirely remote, for he is perceived right here in a directly apprehensible form. Who is this? He who knows the three-food-constituted <s>Prajāpati</s> as his own self, as described — he is the person who knows thus. By what commonality is he <s>Prajāpati</s>? This is stated: the wealth of this person who knows thus — cattle and the like — constitutes the fifteen digits, because it shares the property of increase and decrease; and action accomplished through that wealth [is also included]. For his completeness, the self — the body itself — of this knower is the sixteenth digit, occupying the place of the fixed [digit]. He, like the moon, is filled and diminished by wealth alone — this is well-known in the world. This is the hub (<s>nabhya</s>) — fit for the hub, worthy of the hub, or [something that] serves the hub.

children.text:
evaṃ pāṅktena daivavittavidyāsaṃyuktena karmaṇā tryannātmakaḥ prajāpatirbhavatīti vyākhyātam /
anantaraṃ ca jāyādivittaṃ parivārasthānīyamityuktam /
tatra putrakarmāparavidyānāṃ lokaprāptisādhanatvamātraṃ sāmānyenāvagatam, na putrādīnā lokaprāptiphalaṃ prati viśeṣasambandhaniyamaḥ /
so 'yaṃ putrādīnāṃ sādhanānāṃ sādhyaviśeṣasambandho vaktavya ityuttarakaṇḍikā praṇīyate -
children.translated_text: Thus it has been explained that <s>Prajāpati</s>, whose self consists of the three foods, comes into being through five-fold action combined with divine wealth and knowledge. And next it was stated that wife and wealth and the rest occupy the place of the retinue. In that regard, while it has been understood in general that sons, action, and lower knowledge are means for attaining worlds, the specific connection of sons and the rest with the specific fruits of world-attainment has not [been established]. This specific connection of the means — sons and the rest — with the specific goals is to be stated, and so the next section is introduced:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.16
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 1,5.16

children.text:
atha trayo vāva lokā manuṣyalokaḥ pitṛloko devaloka iti |
so 'yaṃ manuṣyalokaḥ putreṇaiva jayyo nānyena karmaṇā |
karmaṇā pitṛlokaḥ |
vidyayā devalokaḥ |
devaloko vai lokānāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ |
tasmād vidyāṃ praśaṃsanti || BrhUp_1,5.16 ||
children.translated_text: Now, there are indeed three worlds: the human world, the world of the ancestors, and the world of the gods. This human world is to be won through a son alone, not through any other action. The world of the ancestors [is to be won] through action. The world of the gods through knowledge. The world of the gods is indeed the best of the worlds. Therefore they praise knowledge. // BṛhUp 1.5.16 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.16 atheti vākyopanyāsārthaḥ /
trayaḥ, vāvetyavadhāraṇārthaḥ /
traya eva śāstroktasādhanārhā lokāḥ, na nyūnā nādhikā vā /
ke te? ityucyate - manuṣyalokaḥ pitṛloko deloka iti /
teṣāṃ so 'yaṃ manuṣyalokaḥ putreṇaiva sādhanena jayyo jetavyaḥ sādhyaḥ - yathā ca putreṇa jetavyastathottaratra vakṣyāmaḥ, - nānyena karmaṇā, vidyayā veti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
karmaṇā agnihotrādilakṣaṇena kevalena pitṛloko jetavyo na putreṇa nāpi vidyayā /
children.translated_text: Through action alone — characterized by <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like — the world of the ancestors is to be won; not through a son, nor through knowledge.

children.text: vidyayā devaloko na putreṇa nāpi karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: Through knowledge, the world of the gods — not through a son, nor through action.

children.text: devaloko vai lokānāṃ trayāṇāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ praśasyatamaḥ /
children.translated_text: The world of the gods is indeed the best, the most praiseworthy, of the three worlds.

children.text: tasmāttatsādhanatvādvidyāṃ praśaṃsanti //16//
children.translated_text: Therefore, because it is the means for attaining that [best world], they praise knowledge. // 16 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.5.16:] '<s>Atha</s>' serves to introduce the sentence. 'Three' — '<s>vāva</s>' is for the purpose of emphasis. Three alone are the worlds worthy of the means stated in scripture — no fewer and no more. Which are they? It is said: the human world, the world of the ancestors, and the world of the gods. Among them, this human world is to be won — conquered, attained — through a son alone as the means. And how it is to be won through a son, we shall explain later. Not through any other action, or through knowledge — this is the remainder of the sentence.

children.text:
evaṃ sādhyalokatrayaphalabhedena viniyuktāni putrakarmavidyākhyāni trīṇi sādhanāni /
jāyā tu putrakarmārthatvānna pṛthaksādhanamiti pṛthaṅnābhihitā /
vittaṃ ca karmasādhanatvānna pṛthaksādhanam /
vidyākarmaṇorlokajayahetutvaṃ svātmapratilābhenaiva bhavatīti prasiddham /
putrasya tvakriyātmakatvātkena prakāreṇa lokajayahetutvamiti na jñāyate /
atastadvaktavyamityathānantaramārabhyate -
children.translated_text: Thus the three means — called sons, action, and knowledge — have been assigned through the differentiation of fruits to the three goal-worlds. But the wife, since she serves the purpose of sons and action, is not a separate means, and hence is not separately mentioned. And wealth, since it is an instrument of action, is not a separate means [either]. It is well established that the capacity of knowledge and action to conquer worlds operates through the recovery of one's own self alone. But since a son is not of the nature of action, by what mode does he serve as the cause of world-conquest? This is not known. Therefore, that [question] is to be answered, and the next section commences immediately:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.17
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 1,5.17

children.text:
athātaḥ samprattiḥ |
yadā praiṣyan manyate 'tha putram āha -- tvaṃ brahma tvaṃ yajñas tvaṃ loka iti |
sa putraḥ pratyāhāhaṃ brahmāhaṃ yajño 'ham loka iti |
yad vai kiñcānūktaṃ tasya sarvasya brahmety ekatā |
ye vai ke ca yajñās teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ yajña ity ekatā |
ye vai ke ca lokās teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ loka ity ekatā |
etāvad vā idaṃ sarvam |
etan mā sarvaṃ sann ayam ito bhunajad iti |
tasmāt putram anuśiṣṭaṃ lokyam āhuḥ |
tasmād enam anuśāsati |
sa yadaivaṃvid asmāl lokāt praity athaibhir eva prāṇaiḥ saha putram āviśati |
sa yady anena kiñcid akṣṇayā kṛtaṃ bhavati tasmād enaṃ sarvasmāt putro muñcati tasmāt putro nāma |
sa putreṇaivāsmil loke pratitiṣṭhati |
athainam ete devāḥ prāṇā amṛtā āviśanti || BrhUp_1,5.17 ||
children.translated_text: Now then, the <s>sampratti</s> (transmission). When [the father] perceives that he is about to depart, he says to his son: 'You are <s>Brahman</s>, you are the sacrifice, you are the world.' The son replies: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>, I am the sacrifice, I am the world.' Whatever has been recited — the oneness of all that is in [the word] '<s>Brahman</s>.' Whatever sacrifices there are — the oneness of all of them is in [the word] 'sacrifice.' Whatever worlds there are — the oneness of all of them is in [the word] 'world.' This much indeed is all this. 'Let him, being this all, protect me from here' — therefore they call a son who has been instructed '<s>lokya</s>' (a person of the world, i.e. one who secures the worlds). Therefore one instructs him. When one who knows this departs from this world, he enters his son together with these very <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths). If anything has been done amiss by him, from all that the son frees him — therefore [he is called] '<s>putra</s>' (son). By the son alone he is established in this world. Then these divine, immortal <s>prāṇas</s> enter him. (BṛUp 1.5.17)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.17 sampratiḥ sampradānam;samprattiriti vakṣyamāṇasya karmaṇo nāmadheyam /
putro hi svātmavyāpārasampradānaṃ karotyanena prakāreṇa pitā, tena samprattisaṃjñakamidaṃ karma /
tatkasminkāle kartavyam? ityāha - sa pitā yadā yasmin kāle praiṣyan mariṣyan mariṣyāmītyapariṣṭādidarśanena manyate, atha tadā putramāhūyāha - tvaṃ brahma tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ loka iti /
sa evamuktaḥ putraḥ pratyāha;sa tu pūrvamevānuśiṣṭo jānāti mayaitatkartavyamiti, tenāha - ahaṃ brahmāhaṃ yajño 'haṃ loka ithi /
etadvākyatrayam /
etasyārthastirohita iti manvānā śrutirvyākhyānāya pravartate /
yadvai kiñca yatkiñcāvaśiṣṭamanūktamadhītamanadhītaṃ ca, tasya sarvasyaiva brahmetyetasminpade ekatā ekatvam yo 'dhyayanavyāpāro mama kartavya āsīdetāvantaṃ kālaṃ vedaviṣayaḥ, sa ita ūrdhvaṃ tvaṃ brahma tvatkartṛko 'stvityarthaḥ /
tathā ye vai ke ca yajñā anuṣṭheyāḥ santo mayā anuṣṭhitāścānanuṣṭhitāśca, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ yajña ityetasminpade ekataikatvam, matkartṛkā yajñā ya āsan, te ita ūrdhvaṃ tvaṃ yajñaḥ - tvatkartṛkā bhavantvityarthaḥ /
ye vai ke ca lokā mayā jetavyāḥ santo jitā ajitāśca, teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ loka ityetasminpade ekatā /
ita ūrdhvaṃ mayādhyayanayajñalokajayakartavyakratustvayi samarpitaḥ, ahaṃ tu mukto 'smi kartavyatābandhanaviṣayātkratoḥ /
sa ca sarvaṃ tathaiva pratipannavānputro 'nuśiṣṭatvāt /
tatremaṃ piturabhiprāyaṃ manvānā ācaṣṭa śrutiḥ - etāvadetatparimāṇaṃ vai idaṃ sarvaṃ yadgṛhiṇā kartavyam, yaduta vedā adhyetavyāḥ, yajñā yaṣṭavyāḥ, lokāśca jetavyāḥ /
etanmā sarvaṃ sannayam - sarvaṃ hīmaṃ bhāraṃ madadhīnaṃ matto 'pacchidya ātamani nidhāya, ito 'smāllokānmā mām abhunajatpālayiṣyatīti /
ḷḍarthe laṅ, chandasi kālaniyamābhāvāt /
yasmādevaṃ sampannaḥ putraḥ pitaram asmāllokātkartavyatābandhanato mocayiṣyati, tasmātputramanuśiṣṭaṃ lokyaṃ lokahitaṃ piturāhurbrāhmaṇāḥ /
ata eva hyenaṃ putramanuśāsati, lokyo 'yaṃ naḥ syāditi, pitaraḥ /
sa pitā yadā yasminkāle evaṃvitputrasamarpitakartavyatākratuḥ, asmāllokātpaiti mriyate, atha tadaibhireva prakṛtairvāṅmanaḥprāṇaiḥ putramāviśati putraṃ vyāpnoti /
adhyātmaparicchedahetvapagamāt piturvāṅmanaḥprāṇāḥsvena ādhidaivikena rūpeṇa pṛthivyagnyādyātmanā bhinnaghaṭapradīpaprakāśavatsarvamāviśanti /
taiḥ prāṇaiḥ saha pitātyāviśati, vāṅmanaḥprāṇātmabhāvitvātpituḥ /
ahamasmyanantā vāṅmanaḥprāṇā adhyātmādibhedavistārā ityevaṃ bhāvito hi pitā /
tasmāttatprāṇānuvṛttitvaṃ piturbhavatīti yuktamuktam - ebhireva prāṇaiḥ saha putramāviśatīt;sarveṣāṃ hyasāvātmā bhavati putrasya ca /
etaduktaṃ bhavati - yasya piturevamanuśiṣṭaḥ putro bhavati so 'sminneva loke vartate putrarūpeṇa, naiva mṛto mantavya ityarthaḥ /
tathā ca śrutyantare -"so 'syāyamitara ātmā puṇyebhyaḥ karmabhyaḥ pratidhīyate"(ai.u.4 / 4) iti /
athedānīṃ putranirvacanamāha - sa putro yadi kadācidanena pitrā akṣṇyā koṇacchidrato 'ntarā akṛtaṃ bhavati kartavyam, tasmāt, kartavyatārūpātpitrā akṛtāt sarvasmāllokaprāptipratibandharūpātputro muñcati mocayati tatsarvaṃ svayamanutiṣṭhanpūrayitvā /
tasmātpūraṇena trāyate sa pitaraṃ yasmāttasmātputro nāma /
idaṃ tatputrasya putratvaṃ yatpituśchidraṃ pūrayitvā trāyate /
sa pitaivaṃvidhena putreṇa mṛto 'pi sannamṛto 'sminneva loke pratitiṣṭhati, evamasau pitā putreṇemaṃ manuṣyalokaṃ jayati /
na tathā vidyākarmabhyāṃ devalokapitṛlokau svarūpalābhasattāmātreṇa;na hi vidyākarmaṇī svarūpalābhavyatirekeṇa putravadvyāpārāntarāpekṣayā lokajayahetutvaṃ pratipadyete /
atha kṛtasamprattikaṃ pitaramenamete vāgādayaḥ prāṇā daivā hairaṇyagarbhā amṛtā amaraṇadharmāṇa āviśanti kathamiti vakṣyati pṛthivyai cainamityādi /
evaṃ putrakarmāparavidyānāṃ manuṣyalokapitṛlokadeva lokasādhyārthatā pradarśitā śrutyā svayameva /
atra kecidvāvadūktāḥ śrutyuktaviśeṣaviniyogopasahāreṇa ca /
tasmādṛṇaśrutiravidvadviṣayā na paramātmavidviṣayeti siddham /
vakṣyati ca -"kariṣyāmo yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ lokaḥ" (4 / 4 / 22) iti /
kecittu pitṛlokadevalokajayo 'pi pitṛlokadevalokābhyāṃ vyāvṛttireva;tasmātputrakarmāparavidyābhiḥ samucityānuṣṭhitābhistribhya etebhyo lokebhyo vyāvṛttaḥ paramātmavijñānena mokṣamadhigacchatīti paramparayā mokṣārthānyeva putrādisādhanānīcchanti /
teṣāmapi mukhāpidhānāyeyameva śrutiruttarā kṛtasamprattikasya putriṇaḥ karmiṇaḥ tryannātmavidyāvidaḥ, phalapradarśanāya pravṛttā /
na cedameva phalaṃ mokṣaphalamiti śakyaṃ, vaktum, tryannasambandhāt, medhātapaḥkāryatvāccānnānām,'punaḥ punarjanayate'iti darśanāt; 'yaddhaitanna kuryātkṣīyeta ha'iti ca kṣayaśravaṇāt /
śarīraṃ jyotīrūpamiti ca kāryakaraṇatvopapatteḥ /
'trayaṃ vā idam'iti ca nāmarūpakarmātmakatvenopasaṃhārāt /
na cedameva sādhanatrayaṃ saṃhataṃ satkasyacinmokṣārthaṃ kasyacit tryannātmaphalamityasmādeva vākyādavagantu śakyam, putrādisādhanānāṃ tryannātmaphaladarśanenaivopakṣīṇatvād vākyasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 1.5.17:] '<s>Sampratti</s>' means transmission (<s>sampradāna</s>); '<s>sampratti</s>' is the designation of the ritual about to be described. For through this procedure, the father makes the son the recipient of the transmission of his own activities — therefore this ritual is called <s>sampratti</s>. At what time should it be performed? It is said: the father, when (<s>yadā</s>) — at whatever time — perceiving that he is about to depart, about to die — [perceiving] 'I am going to die' through signs such as unfavorable omens and the like — then, at that time, having called his son, he says: 'You are <s>Brahman</s>, you are the sacrifice, you are the world.' The son, thus addressed, replies; but he, having been instructed beforehand, knows 'this is to be done by me,' and therefore says: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>, I am the sacrifice, I am the world.' These are the three sentences. Thinking that the meaning of these is hidden, the <s>śruti</s> proceeds to explain. 'Whatever' — whatever has been left over, recited or unrecited, studied or unstudied — the oneness of all that is in the word '<s>Brahman</s>': whatever Vedic study was to be done by me for such and such a period — henceforth, 'you are <s>Brahman</s>' — let it be done by you; this is the meaning. Similarly, whatever sacrifices were to be performed by me, both those performed and those not performed — the oneness of all of them is in the word 'sacrifice': the sacrifices that were to be done by me — henceforth, 'you are the sacrifice' — let them be done by you; this is the meaning. Whatever worlds were to be conquered by me, both those conquered and those not conquered — the oneness of all of them is in the word 'world.' Henceforth, the ritual duties pertaining to Vedic study, sacrifice, and the conquest of worlds that were mine — [all of] that has been entrusted to you; I am now freed from the bond of obligation regarding those duties. And the son has accepted all that in exactly this way, because of having been instructed. Therein, understanding the father's intention, the <s>śruti</s> explains: this much — this is the measure — indeed is all this, all that is to be done by a householder — namely, the <s>Vedas</s> are to be studied, sacrifices are to be performed, and worlds are to be conquered. 'Being this all, let him protect me from here' — [the father thinks:] 'Having taken from me the entire burden dependent on me, having placed it upon himself, let him protect me, going from this world.' The past tense (<s>laṅ</s>) is used in the sense of the optative, because in the <s>Vedic</s> language there is no restriction on tenses. Since a son who has thus received [the transmission] will free the father from the bondage of obligation to this world, therefore they, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, call a son who has been instructed '<s>lokya</s>' — one who secures the welfare of the world for the father. For this very reason fathers instruct the son, [thinking:] 'May this one be a <s>lokya</s> for us.' When that father, at whatever time — having entrusted the ritual duties to the son who knows thus — departs from this world, dies, then, with these very [previously mentioned] <s>prāṇas</s> of speech, mind, and vital breath, he enters the son, he pervades the son. Because the cause of individual limitation for the father has ceased, the father's speech, mind, and <s>prāṇas</s>, in their divine (<s>adhidaivika</s>) form — having the nature of earth-fire and the rest — pervade everything, like the light of a broken lamp spreading everywhere. Together with those <s>prāṇas</s>, the father enters [the son], because the father is of the nature of speech, mind, and <s>prāṇa</s>. For the father was imbued with [the thought]: 'I am infinite speech, mind, and <s>prāṇa</s>, spread out in the differentiation of <s>adhyātma</s> (individual) and other [levels].' Therefore, it is proper to say that the father continues through those <s>prāṇas</s> — 'he enters the son together with these very <s>prāṇas</s>'; for he becomes the Self of all, and of the son [as well]. The meaning of this is: the father who has a son thus instructed continues to exist in this very world in the form of the son — he should not be considered dead. And thus another <s>śruti</s>: 'This other self of his is deposited for meritorious deeds' (Aitareya Upaniṣad 4.4). Now the etymology of 'son' (<s>putra</s>) is given: if at any time something has been done amiss by the father — [done] '<s>akṣṇayā</s>,' meaning crookedly, from the corner, or left undone of what was obligatory — from all that, from the obligation not fulfilled by the father, which is of the nature of an obstruction to the attainment of the worlds — the son frees him, liberates him, by himself completing and fulfilling [the obligation]. Because [the son] protects (<s>trāyate</s>) by filling (<s>pūraṇa</s>) — therefore [he is called] '<s>putra</s>' (son). This is the son's sonship — that he protects the father by filling his deficiencies. That father, even though dead, by means of such a son, is established in this very world as if not dead. Thus the father conquers this human world through the son. Not in the same way [does he conquer] the world of the gods and the world of the ancestors through <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>karma</s> (action) — merely through the attainment of their own nature. For <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> do not achieve the conquest of worlds by requiring further activity beyond the attainment of their own nature, as a son does. Then — these <s>prāṇas</s> of speech and the rest, divine, belonging to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, immortal, of the nature of not-dying — enter him, the father who has performed the <s>sampratti</s>. How [they enter], [the text] will state: 'From earth and from fire' and so forth. Thus, the <s>śruti</s> itself has demonstrated the purpose of sons, action, and lower knowledge as the means for the human world, the world of the ancestors, and the world of the gods [respectively]. Therein, some [interpreters] have been refuted by the specific application stated by the <s>śruti</s>. Therefore, it is established that the <s>śruti</s> about debts pertains to the ignorant, not to one who knows the <s>Paramātman</s>. And [the text] will state: 'We shall do — for whom this Self is our world' (BṛUp 4.4.22). But some [hold that] the conquest of the world of the ancestors and the world of the gods is also [merely] the turning away from the world of the ancestors and the world of the gods. Therefore, having turned away from these three worlds through the combined practice of sons, action, and lower knowledge, one attains liberation through the knowledge of the <s>Paramātman</s> — thus they wish [to maintain] that sons and other means are indirectly for the sake of liberation. To close the mouths of even those [interpreters], this very subsequent <s>śruti</s> — about the father who has performed the <s>sampratti</s>, who has a son, who performs ritual action, who knows the three-food-self <s>vidyā</s> — has been introduced for the purpose of showing the fruit. For this fruit cannot be said to be the fruit of liberation, because of the connection with the three foods; because the foods are the effects of intelligence (<s>medhā</s>) and austerity (<s>tapas</s>); because of the [śruti's] statement 'he generates again and again'; and because the exhaustion [of the fruit] is heard — 'if he were not to do this, it would be exhausted.' And because the body in the form of light is of the nature of cause and effect. And because [the text] will conclude with 'This [universe] is indeed threefold' as consisting of name, form, and action. And from this very passage, it cannot be understood that this same threefold means, taken together, leads to liberation for some and to the three-food-self fruit for others — because the passage is concluded by showing the three-food-self fruit of the means [consisting of] sons and the rest.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.18

pṛthivyai cainam agneś ca daivī vāg āviśati |
sā vai daivī vāg yayā yad yad eva vadati tat tad bhavati || BrhUp_1,5.18 ||
children.translated_text: From the earth and from fire, the divine speech enters him. That indeed is the divine speech by which whatever one says comes to be. (BṛUp 1.5.18)
[Start of BṛUp 1.5.18]

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,5.18 pṛthivyai pṛthivyāḥ ca enam agneśca daivī adhidaivātmikā vāgenaṃ kṛtasamprattikamāviśati /
sarveṣāṃ hi vāca upādānabhūtā daivī vākpṛthivyagnilakṣaṇā, sā hyādhyātmikāsaṅgādidoṣairniruddhā /
children.translated_text: For the divine speech, characterized as earth and fire, is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of all [individual] speech; it was [previously] obstructed by the individual-level defects of attachment and the like.

children.text: viduṣastaddoṣāpagame āvaraṇabhaṅga ivodakapradīpaprakāśavacca vyāpnoti /
children.translated_text: Upon the removal of those defects for the knower, [the divine speech] pervades [all] — like the breaking of a covering, or like [the spreading of] water or lamp-light.

children.text: tadetaducyat - pṛthivyā agneścainaṃ daivī vāgāviśatīti /
children.translated_text: This is what is stated — 'From the earth and from fire, the divine speech enters him.'

children.text: sā ca daivī vāganṛtādidoṣarahitā śuddhā, yayā vācā daivyā yadyadeva ātmane parasmai vā vadati tattadā bhavati, amoghā apratibaddhā asya vāgbhavatītyarthaḥ //18//
children.translated_text: That divine speech is pure, free from the defects of falsehood and the like. By whatever the divine speech speaks — whether for oneself or for another — that very thing comes to be. His speech becomes infallible, unobstructed — this is the meaning. (18)
[Commentary on BṛUp 1.5.18:] From the earth and from fire, the divine speech — pertaining to the <s>adhidaiva</s> (cosmic divine) level — enters him, the one who has performed the <s>sampratti</s>.

divaś cainam ādityāc ca daivaṃ mana āviśati |
tad vai daivaṃ mano yenānandy eva bhavaty atho na śocati || BrhUp_1,5.19 ||
children.translated_text: From heaven and from the sun, the divine mind enters him. That indeed is the divine mind by which one becomes blissful and does not grieve. (BṛUp 1.5.19)

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,5.19 divaścainamādityācca daivaṃ mana āviśati - tacca daivaṃ manaḥ;svabhāvanirmalatvāt;yena manasā asau ānandyeva bhavati sukhyeva bhavati;atho api na śocati, śokādinimittāsaṃyogāti //19//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 1.5.19:] From heaven and from the sun, the divine mind enters him — that divine mind, because of being naturally pure, by which mind one becomes blissful, becomes happy; and moreover, one does not grieve — because of the non-connection with causes of grief and the like. (19)

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.20
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 1.5.20]

children.text:
adbhyaś cainaṃ candramasaś ca daivaḥ prāṇa āviśati |
sa vai daivaḥ prāṇo yaḥ saṃcaraṃś cāsaṃcaraṃś ca na vyathate 'tho na riṣyati |
sa eṣa evaṃvit sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām ātmā bhavati |
yathaiṣā devataivaṃ saḥ |
yathaitāṃ devatāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny avanty evaṃ haivaṃvidaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāny avanti |
yad u kiñcemāḥ prajāḥ śocanty amaivāsāṃ tad bhavati |
puṇyam evāmuṃ gacchati |
na ha vai devān pāpaṃ gacchati || BrhUp_1,5.20 ||
children.translated_text: From the waters and from the moon, the divine <s>prāṇa</s> enters him. That indeed is the divine <s>prāṇa</s> which, whether moving or not moving, is not agitated and is not harmed. One who knows this becomes the Self of all beings. As this deity is, so is he. As all beings sustain this deity, so all beings sustain the one who knows this. Whatever suffering these creatures experience — that remains with them alone. Only merit goes to him. No evil goes to the gods. (BṛUp 1.5.20)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.20 adbhayaścainaṃ candramasaśca daivaḥ prāṇa āviśati /
sa vai daivaḥ prāṇaḥ kiṃllakṣaṇaḥ? ityucyate-yaḥ sañcaran prāṇibhedeṣva sañcaransamaṣṭivya ṣṭirūpeṇa--athavā sañcarana jaṅgameṣu asañcaransthāvareṣu, na vyathate na duḥkhanimittena bhayena yuḍyate /
athāṃ api na riṣyati na vinaśyati na hiṃsāmāpadyate /
saḥ--yo yathoktamevaṃ vetti vyannātmadarśanaṃ saḥ-sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇo bhavati, sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mano bhavati, sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ vāgbhavati-ityevaṃ sarvābhūtātmatayā sarvajño bhavatītyarthaḥ;sarvakṛcca /
tathaipā pūrvasidvā hiraṇyagarbhadevatā evameva nāsya sarvajñatve sarvakṛttave vā kkacitpratighātaḥ /
sa iti dārṣṭāntikanirdeśaḥ /
kiñca yathaitāṃd diraṇyagarbhadevatāmijyādibhiḥ sarvāṇi bhūtānyavanti pālayanti pūjyanti, evaṃ ha evaṃvidaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtānyavanti-ijyādilakṣaṇāṃ pūjāṃ satataṃ prayapañjata ityarthaḥ /
athedamāśaṅkayate-sarvaprāṇināmātmā bhavatītyuttkam, tasya ca sarvaprāṇikāryakaraṇātmatve sarvaprāṇisukhaduḥkhaiḥ sambadhyeteti /
tanna, aparicchinnabudvitvāt paricchinnātmabudvīnāṃ hyākrośādau duḥkhasambandho dṛṣṭaḥ- anenāhamākruṣṭa iti /
asya tu sarvātmano ya ākruśyate yaścākrośati yatorātmatvabudviviśeṣābhāvānna tannimittaṃ duḥkhamupapadyate /

maraṇaduḥkhavacca nimittābhāvāt yathā hi kasmiṃścinmṛte kasyacid duḥkhamutpadyate-mamāsauputrobhrātāceti, putrādinimittam;tannimittābhāve tanmaraṇadarśino 'pi naiva duḥkhamupajāyate, tatheśvarasyāpyaparicchinnātmano mamatavatādiduḥkhanimittamidhyājñānādidopābhāvānnaiva duḥkhamupajāyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And just as with the suffering caused by death — because of the absence of a cause: just as, when someone dies, suffering arises for a particular person [who thinks] 'he was my son, my brother' — the cause being the son and the like; in the absence of that cause, even one who witnesses that death does not experience suffering. Similarly, for <s>Īśvara</s> too, whose self is unlimited, suffering does not arise because of the absence of the cause of suffering such as the sense of 'mine' and the like — because of the absence of defects such as false knowledge.

children.text: tadetaducyate-yadu kiñcayat kiñca imāḥ prajāḥ śocantyamaiva sahaiva prajābhistacchokādinimittaṃ duḥkhaṃ saṃyuktaṃ bhavatyāsāṃ prajānāṃ paricchinnabudvijanitatvāt /
children.translated_text: This is what is stated: whatever and whichever suffering these beings grieve over — that suffering, whose cause is grief and the like, is conjoined with the beings themselves — because it is produced by their delimited intellect.

children.text: sarvātmanastu kena saha kiṃ saṃyukta bhavedviyukta vā? amuṃ tu prājāpatye pade vartamānaṃ puṇyameva śubhamevaphalamabhipretaṃ puṇyamiti-niratiśayaṃ hi tena puṇyaṃ kṛtam;tena tatphalameva gacchati /
children.translated_text: But for the self of all — with whom could anything be conjoined or from whom separated? As for this [being] who abides in the station of <s>Prajāpati</s> — only auspicious, only good is the intended fruit, which is merit — for he has performed unsurpassed merit; therefore he attains that very fruit.

children.text: na ha vai devānpāpaṃ gacchati, pāpaphalasyāvasarābhāvāt pāpaphalaṃ duḥkha na gacchatītyathaḥ //20//
children.translated_text: 'Evil does not reach the gods' — because there is no occasion for the fruit of evil, the meaning is that the suffering that is the fruit of evil does not reach [him]. // 20 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 1.5.20:] From the waters and from the moon, the divine <s>prāṇa</s> enters him. What is the nature of that divine <s>prāṇa</s>? It is said: that which, whether moving — among the different species of living beings — or not moving — in its collective-individual form — or alternatively, moving among mobile beings and not moving among immobile beings — is not agitated, is not afflicted with fear caused by suffering; and moreover, is not harmed, is not destroyed, does not undergo injury. He — who knows thus, the vision of the three-food-self as described — becomes the <s>prāṇa</s> of all beings, becomes the mind of all beings, becomes the speech of all beings — thus, through being the Self of all beings, he becomes omniscient — this is the meaning; and omnipotent as well. Just as this previously established deity of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — even so, there is no obstruction whatsoever to his omniscience or omnipotence. The word 'he' [in 'so is he'] refers to the one illustrated [by the analogy]. Moreover, just as all beings sustain, protect, and honor this deity of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> through sacrifice and the like, so all beings sustain the one who knows this — meaning they constantly offer him worship in the form of sacrifice and the like. Now an objection is anticipated: it was stated that he becomes the Self of all living beings; and if his body-and-organs become [identical with those of] all living beings, he would be connected with the pleasures and pains of all living beings. This is not so, because of his having unlimited awareness. For only those with limited self-awareness are observed to be connected with suffering upon being abused and the like — [thinking] 'I have been abused by this one.' But for this one who is the Self of all, since there is no specific awareness of difference between the one who abuses and the one who is abused — [because both are his Self] — suffering caused by that is not tenable.

children.text:
'ta ete sarva eva samāḥ sarve 'nantāḥ'ityaviśeṣeṇa vāṅmanaḥprāṇānāmupāsanamuktam, nānyatamagato veśeṣa uktaḥ /
kimevameva pratipattavyam? kiṃ vā vicāryamāṇe kaścidviśeṣo vratamupāsanaṃ prati pratitapattuṃ śakyate? ityucyate-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'These are all equal, all infinite' — thus, the meditation on speech, mind, and <s>prāṇa</s> was stated without distinction, no specific distinction regarding any one [of them] was stated. Should it be understood just thus? Or, upon investigation, can some distinction be discerned regarding the observance for meditation? This is addressed:

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.21
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.5.21]

children.text:
athāto vratamīmāṃsā |
prajāpatir ha karmāṇi sasṛje |
tāni sṛṣṭāny anyo 'nyenāspardhanta |
vadiṣyāmy evāham iti vāg dadhre |
drakṣyāmy aham iti cakṣuḥ |
śroṣyāmy aham iti śrotram |
evam anyāni karmāṇi yathākarmam |
tāni mṛtyuḥ śramo bhūtvopayeme |
tāny āpnot |
tāny āptvā mṛtyur avārundha |
tasmāc chrāmyaty eva vāk |
śrāmyati cakṣuḥ |
śrāmyati śrotram |
athemam eva nāpnot yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ |
tāni jñātuṃ dadhrire |
ayaṃ vai naḥ śreṣṭho yaḥ saṃcaraṃś cāsaṃcaraṃś ca na vyathate 'tho na riṣyati |
hantāsyaiva sarve rūpaṃ bhavāmeti |
ta etasyaiva sarve rūpam abhavan |
tasmād eta etenākhyāyante prāṇā iti |
tena ha vāva tat kulam ācakṣate yasmin kule bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
ya u haivaṃvidā spardhate 'nuśuṣyati |
anuśuṣya haivāntato mriyata ity adhyātmam || BrhUp_1,5.21 ||
children.translated_text: Now the inquiry into the observance (<s>vrata</s>). <s>Prajāpati</s> created the organs of action. These, once created, competed with one another. 'I alone shall speak!' — thus speech resolved. 'I shall see!' — thus the eye. 'I shall hear!' — thus the ear. And so the other organs, each according to its function. Death, having become weariness, seized them. It overtook them. Having overtaken them, Death held them back. Therefore speech becomes weary; the eye becomes weary; the ear becomes weary. But it did not overtake this one — the central <s>prāṇa</s>. They resolved to know him: 'This one is indeed the best among us — he who, whether moving or not moving, does not suffer and is not harmed. Come, let us all become his very form.' They all became his very form. Therefore they are called '<s>prāṇas</s>' after him. Whatever family one belongs to who knows this — they call that family by his name. One who competes with a knower of this withers away. Having withered away, he finally dies. This is with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>). // BṛhUp 1.5.21 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.21 athāto 'nantaraṃ vratamīmāṃsā upāsanakarmavicāraṇetyarthaḥ /
eṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ kasya karma vratatvena dhārayitavyamiti mīmāṃsā pravartate /
tatra prajāpatirha - haśabdaḥ kilārthe - prajāpatiḥ kila prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā karmāṇi karaṇāni vāgādīni - karmāthāni hi tānīti karmāṇītyucyante - sasṛje sṛṣṭavānvāgādīni karaṇānītyarthaḥ /
tāni punaḥ sṛṣṭānyanyonyena itaretaramaspardhanta spardhāṃ saṃgharṣaṃ cakruḥ /
katham? vadiṣyāmyeva svavyāpārādvadanādanuparataivāhaṃ syāmiti vāgvrataṃ dadhre dhṛtavatī - yadyanyo 'pi matsamo 'sti svavyāpārādanuparantuṃ śaktaḥ, so 'pi darśayatvātmano vīryamiti /
tathā drakṣyāmyahamiti cakṣuḥ, śroṣyāmyahamiti śrotram;evamanyāni karmāṇi karaṇāni yathākarma - yadyadyasya karma yathākarma /
tāni karaṇāni mṛtyurmārakaḥ śramaḥ śramarūpī bhūtvā upayeme sañjagrāha /
katham? tāni karaṇāni svavyāpāre pravṛttānyāpnot, śramarūpeṇātmānaṃ darśitavān /
āptvā ca tānyavārundha avarodhaṃ kṛtavānmṛtyuḥ - svakarmabhyaḥ pracyāvitavānityarthaḥ /
tasmādadyatve 'pi vadane svakarmaṇi pravṛttā vāk śrāmyatvena śramarūpiṇā mṛtyunā saṃyuktā svakarmataḥ pracyavate /
tathā śrāmyati cakṣuḥ, śrāmyati śrotram /
athemameva mukhyaṃ prāṇaṃ nāpnonna prāptavānmṛtyuḥ śramarūpī, yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇastam /
tenādyatve 'pyaśrānta eva svakarmaṇi pravartate /
tānītarāṇi karaṇāni taṃ jñātuṃ dadhrire dhṛtavanti manaḥ /
ayaṃ vai no 'smākaṃ madhye śreṣṭhaḥ praśasyatamo 'bhyadhikaḥ, yasmādyaḥ sañcaraṃścāsañcaraṃśca na vyathate 'tho na riṣyati - hantedānīmasyaiva prāṇasya sarve vayaṃ rūpamasāma prāṇamātmatvena pratipadyemahi - evaṃ viniścitya te etasyaiva sarve rūpamabhavan;prāṇarūpamevātmatvena pratipannāḥ, prāṇavratameva dadhrire - asmadvratāni na mṛtyorvāraṇāya paryāptānīti /
yasmātprāṇena rūpeṇa rūpavantītarāṇi karaṇāni calanātmanā svena ca prakāśātmanaḥ, na hi prāṇādanyatra calanātmakatvopapattiḥ;calanavyāpārapūrvakāṇyeva hi sarvadā svavyāpāreṣu lakṣyante;tasmādete vāgādaya etena prāṇābhidhānena ākhyāyante 'bhidhīyante prāṇā ityevam /
ya evaṃ prāṇātmatāṃ sarvakaraṇānāṃ vetti prāṇaśabdābhidheyatvaṃ ca, tena ha vāva tenaiva viduṣā tatkulamācakṣate laukikāḥ /
yasminkule sa vidvāñjāto bhavati tatkulaṃ vidvāñjāto bhavati tatkulaṃ vidvannāmnaiva prathitaṃ bhavatyamuṣyadaṃ kulamiti, yathā tāpatya iti /
children.translated_text: In whatever family that knower is born — that family becomes renowned by the name of the knower, [as when one says] 'this is such-and-such's family' — just as [one says] '<s>Tāpatya</s>' (descendant of <s>Tapas</s>).

children.text: ya evaṃ yathoktaṃ veda vāgādīnāṃ prāṇarūpatāṃ prāṇākhyatvaṃ ca tasyaitatphalam /
children.translated_text: One who knows thus — as described — the <s>prāṇa</s>-nature and <s>prāṇa</s>-designation of speech and the rest — for him this is the fruit.

children.text: kiñca yaḥ kaścidu haivaṃvidā prāṇātmadarśinā spardhate tatpratipakṣī san, so 'sminneva śarīre 'nuśuṣyati śoṣamupagacchati /
children.translated_text: Moreover, whoever competes with — becomes an adversary of — such a knower who perceives the self as <s>prāṇa</s>, he withers away — becomes desiccated — in this very body.

children.text: anuśuṣya haiva śoṣaṃ gatvaiva antato 'nte mriyate na sahasānupadruto mriyate ityaivamuktamadhyātmaṃ prāṇātmadarśanamityuktopasaṃhāro 'dhidaivatapradarśanārthaḥ //21//
children.translated_text: Having withered away — having become desiccated — he dies at the end, i.e., finally — he does not die suddenly as if smitten. Thus what has been stated — the vision of the self as <s>prāṇa</s> with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>) — is summarized, for the purpose of presenting the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>) [counterpart]. // 21 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.5.21: 'Now the inquiry into the observance' — the meaning is: now, subsequently, the <s>vratamīmāṃsā</s> is the investigation of the action that is the observance (<s>upāsanakarma</s>). The inquiry proceeds: whose function, among these <s>prāṇas</s>, should be maintained as the observance? There, <s>Prajāpati</s> indeed — the word 'ha' is used in the sense of 'it is said' — <s>Prajāpati</s>, it is said, having created beings, created the actions (<s>karmāṇi</s>), i.e. the organs (<s>karaṇāni</s>) — speech and the like — for they are called 'actions' because they are instrumental for action. He created the organs of speech and the like — this is the meaning. Those, once created, competed with one another — engaged in mutual rivalry. How? 'I shall speak without ceasing from my own function of speaking!' — thus speech resolved, held firm — 'If there is another equal to me, able not to cease from his own function, let him too display his prowess.' Similarly, 'I shall see!' — thus the eye; 'I shall hear!' — thus the ear; and so the other organs, each according to its function — whatever is the function of each, accordingly. Those organs — Death, the killer, having become weariness — having assumed the form of weariness — seized them. How? Those organs, engaged in their own functions, he overtook — he manifested himself in the form of weariness. And having overtaken them, Death held them back — confined them — that is, caused them to deviate from their own functions. Therefore, even now, speech engaged in its own function of speaking becomes weary — being seized by Death in the form of weariness, it deviates from its function. Similarly, the eye becomes weary; the ear becomes weary. But this one, the chief <s>prāṇa</s>, he did not overtake — Death in the form of weariness did not reach this central <s>prāṇa</s>. Therefore, even now, he continues untiringly in his own function. Those other organs resolved to know him. 'This one is indeed the best among us, the most praiseworthy, superior — because he who, whether moving or not moving, neither suffers nor is harmed. Come now, let us all become his very form — let us accept <s>prāṇa</s> as our self.' Having thus resolved, they all became his very form — they accepted the form of <s>prāṇa</s> as their self-identity; they maintained the observance of <s>prāṇa</s> alone — [thinking] 'our observances are not sufficient to ward off Death.' Because the other organs derive their form — their moving nature — from <s>prāṇa</s>'s own nature of movement, and their self-luminous nature from his own; for the property of being of the nature of movement is not tenable anywhere other than in <s>prāṇa</s>; and all [organs] are always observed to function preceded by the activity of movement. Therefore, these — speech and the others — are designated, called by the name of this <s>prāṇa</s>: '<s>prāṇas</s>.' Whoever knows thus — the <s>prāṇa</s>-selfhood of all organs and their being designated by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>' — worldly people call that family by his name.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.22
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.5.22]

children.text:
athādhidevataṃ:
jvaliṣyāmy evāham ity agnir dadhre |
tapsyāmy aham ity ādityaḥ |
bhāsyāmy aham iti candramāḥ |
evam anyā devatā yathādevatam |
sa yathaiṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇa evam etāsāṃ devatānāṃ vāyuḥ |
mlocanti hy anyā devatā na vāyuḥ |
saiṣānastamitā devatā yad vāyuḥ || BrhUp_1,5.22 ||
children.translated_text: Now with reference to the divine: 'I alone shall blaze!' — thus fire resolved. 'I shall give heat!' — thus the sun. 'I shall shine!' — thus the moon. And so the other deities, each according to its [function]. As the central <s>prāṇa</s> is among these <s>prāṇas</s>, so is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) among these deities. The other deities set — but not <s>Vāyu</s>. That deity which never sets is <s>Vāyu</s>. // BṛhUp 1.5.22 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.22 athānantaram adhidaivataṃ devatāviṣayaṃ darśanamucyate /
kasya devatāviśeṣasya vratadhāraṇaṃ śreyaḥ? iti mīmāsyate /
adhyātmavatsarvam /
jvaliṣyāmyevāhamityagnirdadhre /
tapsyāmyahamityādityaḥ;bhāsyāmyahamiti candramāḥ;evamanyā devatā yathādaivatam /
children.translated_text: 'I shall give heat!' — thus the sun. 'I shall shine!' — thus the moon. And so the other deities, each according to its [nature].

children.text: so 'dhyātmaṃ vāgādīnāmeṣāṃ prāṇo mṛtyunā anāptaḥ svakarmaṇo na pracyāvitaḥ svena prāṇavratenābhagnavrato yathā;evametāsāmagnyādīnāṃ devatānāṃ vāyurapi /
children.translated_text: Just as, in the individual sphere, <s>prāṇa</s> was not overtaken by Death among speech and the others — was not made to deviate from its own function — remained unbroken in its <s>prāṇa</s>-observance — so too, among these deities of <s>Agni</s> and the rest, <s>Vāyu</s> [is similarly unbroken].

children.text: mlocantyastaṃ yanti svakarmebhya uparamante - yathādhyātmaṃ vāgādayo 'nyā devatā agnyādyāḥ, na vāyurastaṃ yāti - yathā madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ, ataḥ saiṣā anastamitā devatā yadvāyuryo 'yaṃ vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: They set — the other deities, <s>Agni</s> and the rest, like speech and the others in the individual sphere, go to their setting, cease from their functions — but <s>Vāyu</s> does not set, just as the central <s>prāṇa</s> [does not]. Therefore, this deity that never sets is <s>Vāyu</s> — this very <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: evamadhyātmamadhidaivaṃ ca mīmāṃsitvā nirdhāritam - prāṇavāyyvātmano vratamabhagnamiti //22//
children.translated_text: Thus, having investigated both the individual and the divine [aspects], it has been determined: the observance of [him who has] the nature of <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> is unbroken. // 22 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.5.22: Now, subsequently, the divine (<s>adhidaivatam</s>) — the vision pertaining to deities — is stated. Which particular deity's observance is best to maintain? — this is being investigated. Everything is as in the individual [case]. 'I alone shall blaze!' — thus fire resolved.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,5.23
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 1.5.23]

children.text:
athaiṣa śloko bhavati --
yataś codeti sūryo 'staṃ yatra ca gacchatīti |
prāṇād vā eṣa udeti prāṇe 'stam eti |
taṃ devāś cakrire dharmaṃ sa evādya sa u śva iti |
yad vā ete 'murhy adhriyanta tad evāpy adya kurvanti |
tasmād ekam eva vrataṃ caret prāṇyāc caivāpānyāc ca |
nen mā pāpmā mṛtyur āpnavad iti |
yady u caret samāpipayiṣet teno etasyai devatāyai sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati || BrhUp_1,5.23 ||
children.translated_text: Now there is this verse: 'From where the sun rises and where it sets' — from <s>prāṇa</s> indeed it rises and in <s>prāṇa</s> it sets. The gods made it their law (<s>dharma</s>) — that [law which is] the same today and the same tomorrow. What they resolved then, they do even now. Therefore, one should practice one observance alone: one should breathe in and breathe out, [thinking] 'lest the evil of death overtake me.' And if one undertakes it, one should bring it to completion. Thereby one wins union with and co-residence with this deity. // BṛhUp 1.5.23 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,5.23 athaitasyaivārthasya prakāśaka eṣa śloko mantro bhavati /
yataśca yasmādvāyorudetyudgacchati sūryaḥ, adhyātmaṃ ca cakṣurātmanā prāṇād astaṃ ca yatra vāyau prāṇe ca gacchatyaparasaṃdhyāsamaye svāpasamaye ca puruṣasya, taṃ devāstaṃ dharmaṃ devāścakrire dhṛtavanto vāgādayo 'gnyādayaśca prāṇavrataṃ ca purā vicārya /
sa evādyedānīṃ śvo 'pi bhaviṣyatyapi kāle 'nuvartyate 'nuvartiṣyate ca devairityabhiprāyaḥ /
tatremaṃ mantraṃ saṃkṣepato vyācaṣṭa brāhmaṇam - prāṇādvā eṣa sūrya udeti prāṇe 'stameti /
taṃ devāścakrire dharmaṃ sa evādya sa u śva ityasya kor'thaḥ? ityucyate - yadvai ete vratamamurhi amuṣminkāle vāgādayo 'gnyādayaśca prāṇavrataṃ vāyuvrataṃ cādhriyanta, tadevādyāpi kurvantyanuvartate 'nuvartiṣyante ca /
vrataṃ tairabhagnameva /
yattu vāgādivratamagnyādivrataṃ ca tadbhagnameva, teṣāmastamanakāle svāpakāle ca vāyau prāṇe ca nimsuktidarśanāt /
athaitadanyatroktam"yadā vai puraṣaḥ svapiti prāṇaṃ tarhi vāgapyeti prāṇaṃ manaḥ prāṇaṃ cakṣuḥprāṇaṃ śrotraṃ yadā prabudhyate prāṇādevādhi punarjāyanta ityadhyātmamathādhidaivataṃ yadā vā agniranugacchati vāyuṃ tarhyanūdvāti yadādityo 'stameti vāyuṃ tarhi praviśati vāyuṃ candramā vāyau diśaḥ pratiṣṭhitā vāyorevādhi punarjāyante"iti /
yasmāde etadeva vrataṃ vāgādiṣvagnyādiṣu cānugataṃ yadetadvāyośca prāṇasya ca parispandātmakatvaṃ sarvedevairuvartyamānaṃ vratam tasmādanyo 'pyokameva vrataṃ caret /
kiṃ tata? prāṇyātprāṇanavyāpāraṃ kuryādapānyādapānanadhyāpāraṃ ca;na hi prāṇāpānavyāpārasya prāṇanāpānanalakṣaṇasyoparamo 'sti /
tasmāttadevaikaṃ vrataṃ careddhitvendriyāntaravyāpāraṃ nenmā māṃ pāpmā mṛtyuḥ śramarūpyāpnuvadāpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one should practice that one observance alone, abandoning the functions of the other senses — lest the evil of death in the form of weariness overtake me.

children.text: necchabdaḥ paribhaye -'yadyahamasmād vratātpracyutaḥ syām, grasta evāhaṃ mṛtyunā'ityevaṃ trasto dhārayetprāṇavratamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The word '<s>ned</s>' [indicates] apprehensive caution — 'if I were to deviate from this observance, I would be seized by Death' — thus frightened, one should maintain the <s>prāṇa</s>-observance — this is the intent.

children.text: yadi kadācid u caretprārabheta prāṇavratam, samāpipayiṣetsamāpayitumicchet;yadi hyasmād vratāduparametprāṇaḥ paribhūtaḥ syāddevāśca;tasmātsamāpayedeva /
children.translated_text: If at any time one undertakes — begins — the <s>prāṇa</s>-observance, one should wish to complete it — should desire to bring it to completion. For if one were to desist from this observance, <s>prāṇa</s> would be dishonored, and the gods too; therefore, one should certainly complete it.

children.text: tena u tenānena vratena prāṇātmapratipattyā sarvabhūteṣu - vāgādayo 'gnyādayaśca madātmakā eva, ahaṃ prāṇa ātmā sarvaparispandakṛt - evaṃ tenānena vratadhāraṇena etasyā eva prāṇadevatāyāḥ sāyujyaṃ sayugbhāvamekātmatvaṃ salokatāṃ samānalokatāṃ vā ekasthānatvam - vijñānamāndyopekṣametat - jayati prāpnotīt //23//
children.translated_text: Thereby — by this observance, by the realization of the self as <s>prāṇa</s> among all beings — 'Speech and the rest, <s>Agni</s> and the rest, are of my nature; I am <s>prāṇa</s>, the self, the cause of all vibration' — thus, by this maintenance of the observance, one wins union (<s>sāyujya</s>) with this very <s>prāṇa</s>-deity — the state of sharing the same body, i.e., oneness; or co-residence (<s>sālokatā</s>), the state of sharing the same world, i.e., single abode — this [difference in fruit] depends on the degree of intensity of knowledge. One wins, one attains. // 23 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 1.5.23: Now, this verse — this <s>mantra</s> — illuminates this very meaning. From where — from <s>Vāyu</s> — the sun rises, goes up; and in the individual sphere, the eye [rises] as a form of <s>prāṇa</s>, from <s>prāṇa</s>; and sets — where, in <s>Vāyu</s>, and in <s>prāṇa</s>, at the time of the evening twilight and at the time of sleep for the person. The gods — speech and the others, <s>Agni</s> and the others — made that [function] their <s>dharma</s> (law), having previously investigated the <s>prāṇa</s>-observance and the <s>Vāyu</s>-observance. That [law which is] the same today and the same tomorrow — it will be observed in the future too by the gods — this is the intent. There, [the text] briefly explains this <s>mantra</s> with the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>: 'From <s>prāṇa</s> indeed this sun rises; in <s>prāṇa</s> it sets.' What is the meaning of 'the gods made it their law; that which is the same today and the same tomorrow'? This is stated: what these — speech and the others, <s>Agni</s> and the others — in that former time, resolved as their observance — the <s>prāṇa</s>-observance and the <s>Vāyu</s>-observance — that they continue to do even now; they follow [it] and will continue to follow [it]. Their observance has never been broken. But the observance of speech and the rest, of <s>Agni</s> and the rest — that has been broken, since at the time of setting and the time of sleep, they are seen to dissolve into <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>. And this has been stated elsewhere: 'When a person sleeps, speech enters <s>prāṇa</s>; mind [enters] <s>prāṇa</s>; the eye [enters] <s>prāṇa</s>; the ear [enters] <s>prāṇa</s>. When he wakes, they are born again from <s>prāṇa</s> — this is with reference to the individual. And with reference to the divine: when fire goes out, it enters <s>Vāyu</s>; when the sun sets, it enters <s>Vāyu</s>; the moon [enters] <s>Vāyu</s>; the directions are established in <s>Vāyu</s>; they are born again from <s>Vāyu</s>.' Since this very observance is followed among speech and the rest and <s>Agni</s> and the rest — this nature of being vibration (<s>parispanda</s>) that belongs to <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>, the observance followed by all the gods — therefore another person too should practice one observance alone. What then? One should perform the function of breathing in (<s>prāṇana</s>) and the function of breathing out (<s>apānana</s>); for there is no cessation of the <s>prāṇa</s>-<s>apāna</s> function, characterized by breathing in and breathing out.

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye prathamādhyāye pañcamaṃ saptānnabrahmaṇam //5//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth [section], the <s>Saptānna Brāhmaṇa</s> (the section on the seven foods), in the first <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s>. // 5 //

children.text: yadetadavidyāviṣayatvena prastutaṃ sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇaṃ vyākṛtaṃ jagat prāṇātmaprāptyantotkarṣavadapi phalam, yā caitasya vyākaraṇātprāgavasthā avyākṛtaśabdavācyā vṛkṣabījavatsarvametat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which has been introduced as belonging to the domain of <s>avidyā</s> — the differentiated world characterized as what is to be accomplished and its means, whose fruit at its highest is the attainment of the <s>prāṇa</s>-self — and the state prior to its differentiation, denoted by the word 'undifferentiated' (<s>avyākṛta</s>), like a seed of a tree — all this [is now to be discussed].

children.text: START BrhUp 1,6.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.6.1]

children.text:
trayaṃ vā idaṃ nāma rūpaṃ karma |
teṣāṃ nāmnāṃ vāg ity etad eṣām uktham |
ato hi sarvāṇi nāmāny uttiṣṭhanti |
etad eṣāṃ sāma |
etad dhi sarvair nāmabhiḥ samam |
etad eṣāṃ brahma |
etad dhi sarvāṇi nāmāni bibharti || BrhUp_1,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: 'This [world] is indeed threefold: name, form, and action. Of these names, "speech" is their <s>uktha</s> (hymn of praise, source). For from it all names arise. It is their <s>Sāman</s> (equalizing element). For it is equal to all names. It is their <s>Brahman</s> (sustaining principle). For it sustains all names.' // BṛhUp 1.6.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,6.1 trayam;kiṃ tattrayam? ityucyate /
nāma rūpaṃ karma cetyanātmaiva /
nātmā yatsākṣādaparokṣādbrahma /
tasmādasmādvirajyetetyevamarthastrayaṃ vā ityādyārambhaḥ na hyasmādanātmano 'vyāvṛtticittasya ātmānameva lokamahaṃ brahmāsmītyupāsituṃ buddhiḥ pravartate /
bāhyapratyagātmapravṛttyorvirodhāt /
tathā ca kāṭhake -"parāñci khāni vyatṛṇatsvayambhūstasmātparāṅpaśyati nāntarātman /
kaściddhīraḥ pratyagātmānamaikṣadāvṛttacakṣuramṛtatvamicchan" (ka.u.2 / 1 / 1) ityādi /
kathaṃ punarasya vyākṛtāvyākṛtasya kriyākārakaphalātmanaḥ saṃsārasya nāmarūpakarmātmakataiva? na punarātmatvam? ityetatsambhāvayituṃ śakyata iti;atrocyate - teṣāṃ nāmnāṃ yathopanyastānāṃ vāgiti śabdasāmānyamucyate /
"yaḥ kaśca śabdo vāgeva sā"(1 / 5 / 3) ityuktatvādvādityetasya śabdasya yor'thaḥ śabdasya śabdasāmānyamātram etadeteṣāṃ nāmaviśeṣāṇāmukthaṃ kāraṇamupādānam, saindhavalavaṇakaṇānāmiva saindhavācalaḥ /
tadāha - ato hyasmānnāmasāmānyātsarvāṇi nāmāni yajñadatto devadatta ityevamādipravibhāgānyuttiṣṭhantyutpadyante pravibhajyante, lavaṇācalādiva lavaṇakaṇāḥ;kāryaṃ ca kāraṇenāvyatiriktam /
tathā viśeṣāṇāṃ ca sāmānye 'ntarbhāvāt /
kathaṃ sāmānyaviśeṣabhāva iti etacchabda sāmānyameṣāṃ nāmaviśeṣāṇāṃ sāma /
samatvātsāma, sāmānyamityarthaḥ, etaddhi yasmātsarvairnāmabhirātmaviśeṣaiḥ samam /
kiñca ātmalābhāviśeṣācca nāmaviśeṣāṇām /
yasya ca yasmādātmalābho bhavati sa tenāpravibhakto dṛṣṭaḥ, yathā ghaṭādīnāṃ mṛdā /
kathaṃ nāmaviśeṣāṇāmātmalābho vāca ityucyate yata etadeṣāṃ vākchabdavācyaṃ vastu brahma ātmā, tato hyātmalābho nāmnām, śabdavyatiriktasvarūpānupapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: How do the particular names obtain their existence from speech? It is said: because this entity denoted by the word 'speech' is their <s>Brahman</s>, their self — from it the names obtain their being, since no essential nature apart from sound can be established [for them].

children.text: tatpratipādayati - yataśchabdasāmānyaṃ hi yasmācchabdaviśeṣānsarvāṇi nāmāni bibharti dhārayati svarūpapradānena /
children.translated_text: This is explained: because the universal of sound, since [it is the <s>Brahman</s> of names], sustains, upholds, all names — all particular sounds — by granting them their essential nature.

children.text: evaṃ kāryakāraṇatvopapatteḥ sāmānyaviśeṣopapatterātmapradānopapattaśca nāmaviśeṣāṇāṃ śabdamātratā siddhā /
children.translated_text: Thus, since the relationship of effect and cause is established, the relationship of universal and particular is established, and the granting of being is established — the reducibility of all particular names to mere sound is proven.

children.text: evamuttarayorapi sarvaṃ yojyaṃ yathoktam //1//
children.translated_text: In the same way, everything is to be applied to the remaining two [form and action] as described. // 1 //

[Commentary:] 'Threefold' — what is that threefold? It is said: name, form, and action — this is the non-self alone. Not the self, which is the immediately present, directly known <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, [the purpose of] beginning with 'this is threefold' is that one should become dispassionate toward this [non-self]. For the intellect of one whose mind has not turned away from this non-self does not proceed to meditate 'the self alone is [my] world, I am <s>Brahman</s>.' Because there is a contradiction between outward-directed and inward-directed orientation. And thus in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>: 'The self-born pierced the openings outward; therefore one looks outward, not at the inner self. A certain wise one, desiring immortality, looked inward with averted gaze' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 2.1.1) and so forth. How then can it be established that this <s>saṃsāra</s>, both differentiated and undifferentiated, whose nature is action, agent, and fruit, is only of the nature of name, form, and action — and not of the nature of the self? Here it is said: of those names, as presented, 'speech' is what is called the universal of sound. Since it was stated 'whatever sound there is, that is speech alone' (1.5.3), the meaning of the word 'speech' (<s>vāc</s>) is merely the universal of sound. This is the <s>uktha</s> — the cause, the material [source] — of these particular names, just as a mountain of rock salt [is the source] of grains of rock salt. Hence [the text] says: from this, from the universal of names, all names — particular differentiations such as '<s>Yajñadatta</s>,' '<s>Devadatta</s>,' and so forth — arise, are produced, are differentiated, just as grains of salt [emerge] from a mountain of salt. And the effect is non-different from the cause. Likewise, because the particulars are subsumed within the universal. How does the relationship of universal and particular [obtain]? This sound-universal is the <s>Sāman</s> of these particular names. It is <s>Sāman</s> because of 'sameness' (<s>samatva</s>) — meaning universality. For this [sound-universal] is equal to, the same as, all particular names. Moreover, because all particular names obtain their existence from it.

children.text: START BrhUp 1,6.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.6.2]

children.text:
atha rūpāṇāṃ cakṣur ity etad eṣām uktham |
ato hi sarvāṇi rūpāṇy uttiṣṭhanti |
etad eṣāṃ sāma |
etad dhi sarvai rūpaiḥ samam |
etad eṣāṃ brahma |
etad dhi sarvāṇi rūpāṇi bibharti || BrhUp_1,6.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, of forms, the eye is their <s>uktha</s>. For from it all forms arise. It is their <s>Sāman</s>. For it is equal to all forms. It is their <s>Brahman</s>. For it sustains all forms.' // BṛhUp 1.6.2 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_1,6.2 athedānīṃ rūpāṇāṃ sitāsitaprabhṛtīnāṃ cakṣuriti cakṣurviṣayasāmānyaṃ cakṣuḥśabdābhidheyaṃ rūpasāmānyaṃ prakāśyamātramabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, of forms — white, dark, and so forth — 'the eye' — the universal of the objects of the eye, denoted by the word 'eye,' the universal of form — mere visibility — is what is referred to.

children.text: ato hi sarvāṇi rūpāṇyittiṣṭhanti, etadeṣāṃ sāma, etaddhi sarvai rūpeḥ samam, etadeṣāṃ brahma, etaddhi sarvāṇi rūpāṇi bibharti //2//
children.translated_text: 'From it all forms arise; it is their <s>Sāman</s>; for it is equal to all forms; it is their <s>Brahman</s>; for it sustains all forms.' // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 1,6.3

atha karmaṇām ātmety etad eṣām uktham |
ato hi sarvāṇi karmāṇy uttiṣṭhanti |
etad eṣāṃ sāma |
etad dhi sarvaiḥ karmabhiḥ samam |
etad eṣāṃ brahma |
etad dhi sarvāṇi karmāṇi bibharti |
tad etat trayaṃ sad ekam ayam ātmā |
ātmo ekaḥ sann etat trayam |
tad etad amṛtaṃ satyena channam |
prāṇo vā amṛtam |
nāmarūpe satyam |
tābhyām ayaṃ prāṇaś channaḥ || BrhUp_1,6.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Now, of actions, the self [body] is their <s>uktha</s>. For from it all actions arise. It is their <s>Sāman</s>. For it is equal to all actions. It is their <s>Brahman</s>. For it sustains all actions. This triad, being one, is this self. The self, being one, is this triad. That is the immortal, concealed by the real. <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the immortal. Name and form are the real (<s>satya</s>). By these two, this <s>prāṇa</s> is concealed.' // BṛhUp 1.6.3 //
[Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 1.6.3]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_1,6.3 athedānīṃ sarvakarmaviśeṣāṇāṃ mananadarśanātmakānāṃ calanātmakānāṃ ca kriyāsāmānyamātre 'ntarbhāva ucyate /
katham? sarveṣaṃ karmaviśeṣāṇāmātmā śarīraṃ sāmānyamātmā, ātmanaḥ karma ātmetyucyate /
'ātmanā hi śarīreṇa karma karoti'ityuktam /
śarīre ca sarvaṃ karmābhivyajyat /
ataḥ tātsthyāttacchabdaṃ karmakarmasāmānyamātraṃ sarveṣāmukthamityādi pūrvavat /
tadetadyathoktaṃ nāma rūpaṃ karma trayamitaretarāśrayam, itaretarābhivyaktikāraṇam, itaretarapralayaṃ saṃhataṃ tridaṇḍaviṣṭambhavat sadekam /
kenātmanaikatvam? ityucyate - ayamātmāyaṃ piṇḍaḥ kāryakaraṇātmasaṅghātaḥ tathānnatraye vyākhyātaḥ'etanmayo vā ayamātmā'ityādinā;etāvaddhīdaṃ sarvaṃ vyākṛtamavyākṛtaṃ ca yaduta nāma rūpaṃ karmeti, ātmā u eko 'yaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṅghātaḥ sannadhyātmādhibhūtādhidaivabhāvena vyavasthitametadeva trayaṃ nāma rūpaṃ karmeti /
tadetadvakṣyamāṇam /
amṛtaṃ satyenacchannamityetasya vākyasyārthamāha - prāṇo vā amṛtaṃ karaṇātmako 'ntarupaṣṭambhaka ātmabhūto 'bhūto 'vināśī;nāmarūpe satyaṃ kāryātmake śarīrāvasthe;kriyātmakastu prāṇastayorupaṣṭambhako bāhy bāhy ābhyāṃ śarīrātmakābhyāmupajanāpāyadharmibhyāṃ martyābhyāṃ channo 'prakāśīkṛtaḥ /
etadevasaṃsārasatatvamavidyāviṣayaṃ pradarśitam /
ata
ūrdhvaṃ vidyāviṣaya ātmādhigantavya ithi caturthaṃ ārabhyate //3 // //
children.translated_text: from here onward, the self that belongs to the domain of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) is to be ascertained — and so the fourth [chapter] is begun. // 3 //

[Commentary:] Now, of all particular actions — those of the nature of cognition and perception, and those of the nature of movement — their subsumption within the mere universal of action is stated. How? The self, the body, is the universal of all particular actions — the self [here means] the body; action is [expressed as] 'of the self' because 'one performs action with the body,' as was stated. And all action is manifested in the body. Therefore, by contiguity, [the body receives] the designation [of action]; the mere universal of action [is called] the <s>uktha</s> of all — and so forth, as before. This triad as described — name, form, and action — is mutually dependent, mutually the cause of each other's manifestation, mutually dissolved into each other, combined, like a tripod standing by mutual support — [it] is one. By what self is it one? It is said: this self — this physical aggregate, the conglomerate of body and organs — thus explained in the section on the three foods: 'this self is indeed constituted of these' and so forth. For this much indeed is all this — both the differentiated and the undifferentiated — namely name, form, and action. And this self — this one conglomerate of body and organs — being one, constituted as <s>adhyātma</s> (individual), <s>adhibhūta</s> (elemental), and <s>adhidaiva</s> (divine) — is this very triad of name, form, and action. This is what is about to be stated. [The text] gives the meaning of the sentence 'the immortal is concealed by the real (<s>satya</s>)': <s>prāṇa</s> indeed is the immortal — in the nature of the organs, the inner support, self-nature, unborn, imperishable. Name and form are the <s>satya</s> (the real, the phenomenal) — of the nature of effects, the bodily modifications. And <s>prāṇa</s>, which is of the nature of activity, being the external support of those two — is concealed, not made manifest, by these two bodily [realities], which are mortal, subject to origination and destruction. This very nature of <s>saṃsāra</s>, belonging to the domain of <s>avidyā</s>, has been displayed. Hence,

children.text: iti prathamādhyāye ṣaṣṭhamukthabrāhmaṇam //6//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth [section], the <s>Uktha Brāhmaṇa</s>, in the first <s>adhyāya</s>. // 6 //

children.text: ADHYAYA 2
children.translated_text: [ADHYĀYA 2]

children.text:
ātmetyevopāsīta tadanveṣaṇe ca sarvamanviṣṭaṃ syāttadeva cā'tmatattvaṃ sarvasmātpreyastvādanveṣṭavyam /
ātmānamevāvedahaṃ brahmāsmītyātmatattvamekaṃ vidyāviṣayaḥ /
yastu bhedadṛṣṭiviṣayaḥ so 'nyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmīti na sa vedetyavidyāviṣayaḥ /
"ekadhaivānudraṣṭavyam" "mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati"ityevamādibhiḥ pravibhatkau vidyāviṣayau sarvopaniṣatsu /
tatra cāvidyāviṣayaḥ sarva eva sādhyasādhanādibhedaviśeṣaviniyogena vyākhyātaḥ-ā tṛtīyādhyāyaparisamāpteḥ /
sa ca vyākhyāto 'vidyāviṣayaḥ sarva eva dviprakāraḥ- antaḥ prāṇa upaṣṭambhako gṛhasyeva stambhādilakṣaṇaḥ prakāśako 'mṛtaḥ /
bāhyaśca kāryalakṣaṇo 'prakāśaka upajanāpāyadharmakastṛṇakuśamṛttikāsamo gṛhasyeva satyaśabdavācyo martyaḥ tenāmṛtaśabdavācyaḥ prāṇaśchanna iti copasaṃhratam /
sa eva ca prāṇo bāhyādhāramedeṣvanekadhā vistṛtaḥ; prāṇa eko deva ityucyate /
tasyaiva bāhyaḥ piṇḍa ekaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ---virāḍ vaiśvānara ātmā puruṣavidhaḥ prajāpatiḥ ko hiraṇyagarbha ityādibhiḥ piṇḍapradhānaiḥ śabdairākhyāyate sūryādipravibhaktakaraṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'One should meditate as the self alone' — and in that inquiry, everything would have been investigated. And that self-reality alone is to be investigated, because of being dearer than everything. 'He knew the self — I am <s>Brahman</s>' — the one self-reality is the domain of knowledge. But that which is the domain of the vision of difference — 'he is one and I am another' — 'he does not know' — that is the domain of ignorance. By [statements] such as 'it should be seen as one alone,' 'he who sees multiplicity here goes from death to death' — the domains of knowledge and ignorance have been extensively distinguished in all the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. There, the entire domain of <s>avidyā</s> has been explained through the specific application of the distinctions of what is to be accomplished and the means of accomplishment — up to the completion of the third <s>adhyāya</s>. And that entire explained domain of <s>avidyā</s> is of two kinds: the internal <s>prāṇa</s>, the support — like the pillars, rafters, and the like of a house — the illuminator, the immortal. And the external — characterized as the effect, not self-luminous, subject to origination and destruction, comparable to grass, rushes, and clay [of a house] — denoted by the word '<s>satya</s>' (the real/phenomenal), the mortal. By that [mortal element], the one denoted by the word 'immortal,' the <s>prāṇa</s>, is concealed — thus it has been summarized. And that very <s>prāṇa</s>, extended manifoldly in the external material substrates, is called 'the one god, <s>prāṇa</s>.' And its one external physical aggregate — the common [cosmic body] — <s>Virāj</s>, <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, <s>Ātman</s>, person-shaped, <s>Prajāpati</s>, or <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — is designated by these words emphasizing the physical aggregate, with organs differentiated as the sun and the like.

children.text:
ekaṃ cānekaṃ ca brahma etāvadeva, nātaḥ paramasti pratyekaṃ ca śarīrabhedeṣu parisamāptaṃ cetanāvatkartṛ bhoktṛ cetyavidyāviṣayameva ātmatvenopagato gārgyo brāhmaṇo vaktā upasthāpyate ; tadviparītātmadṛgajātaśatruḥ śrotā; evaṃ hi yataḥ pūrvapakṣasiddhāntākhyāyikārūpeṇa samarpyamāṇor'thaḥ śrotuścittasya vaśameti; viparyaye hi tarkaśāstravat kevalārthānugamavākyaiḥ samarpyamāṇo durvijñeyaḥ syādatyantasūkṣmatvādvastunaḥ /
tathā ca kāṭhake-"śravaṇāyāpi bahubhiryo na labhyaḥ"ityādivākyaiḥ su saṃskṛtadevabuddhigamyatvaṃ sāmānyamātrabuddhyāgamyatvaṃ ca saprapañcaṃ darśitam /
"ācāryavānpuruṣo veda""ācāryāddhaiva vidyā"iti cacchāndogye /
"upadekṣyanti te jñānaṃ jñāninastattvadarśinaḥ"iti ca gītāsu /
ihāpi ca śākalyayājñavalkyasaṃvādena atigahvaratvaṃ mahatā saṃrambheṇa brahmaṇo vakṣyati-tasmāścilaṣṭa eva ākhyāyikārūpeṇa pūrvapakṣasiddhāntarūpamāpādya vasyusamarpaṇārtha ārambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Both the one and the many are <s>Brahman</s> — this much only, there is nothing beyond this — and in each [being], in the individual bodily distinctions, it is complete; being possessed of consciousness, [it is] agent and enjoyer — this domain of <s>avidyā</s> alone is presented as the self by <s>Gārgya</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> speaker, who is set up [as the interlocutor for the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>]. <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the listener, sees the self that is the opposite [of <s>Gārgya</s>'s view]. For when the meaning is presented in the form of a narrative with a <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (opponent's thesis) and <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion), it enters the mind of the listener. In the reverse case — when presented by sentences conveying only the bare meaning, as in treatises on logic — the subject matter would be difficult to understand, because of the extreme subtlety of the reality. And thus in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s>: 'He who is not available even to be heard by many' — by such statements, it has been extensively shown that [this knowledge] is accessible only to a well-refined divine intellect, and not accessible to mere ordinary understanding. 'A person who has a teacher knows' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s> 6.14.2); 'From the teacher alone is knowledge [obtained]' (<s>Chāndogya Upaniṣad</s>). 'The knowers, the seers of truth, will teach you knowledge' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 4.34). And here too, through the dialogue of <s>Śākalya</s> and <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, [the text] will show the extreme profundity of <s>Brahman</s> with great vehemence. Therefore, the deliberate beginning in the form of a narrative, presenting [the matter] in the form of <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> and <s>siddhānta</s>, is for the purpose of conveying the reality.

children.text:
ācāravidhyupadeśārthaśca--evamācāravatorvattkṛśrokrorākhyāyikānugater'tho 'vagamyate /
kevalatarkabudviniṣedhārthā cākhyāyikā--"naiṣā tarkeṇa matirāpaneyā""na tarkaśāstradagdhāya"iti śrutismṛtibhyām /
śradvā ca brahmavijñāne paramaṃ sādhanamityākhyāykārthaḥ /
tathā hi gārgyājātaśatravoratīva śradvālutāddṛśyate ākhyāyikāyām;"śradvāṃllabhate jñānam"iti ca smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: And [the narrative form is] for the purpose of teaching proper conduct — for one who follows the conduct of teachers, the meaning is understood from following the narrative of the well-conducted. The narrative also serves to negate mere logic — from <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>: 'This understanding cannot be attained by reasoning alone' (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s> 1.2.9); 'Not for one scorched by the treatises of logic.' And faith is the supreme means for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the purpose of the narrative. For the extreme devotion of <s>Gārgya</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s> is visible in the narrative. And <s>smṛti</s>: 'One with faith obtains knowledge' (<s>Bhagavadgītā</s> 4.39).

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 2.1.1]

children.text:
dṛptabālākir hānūcāno gārgya āsa |
sa hovācājātaśatruṃ kāśyaṃ -- brahma te bravāṇīti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- sahasram etasyāṃ vāci dadmaḥ, janako janaka iti vai janā dhāvantīti || BrhUp_2,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Dṛptabālāki</s>, a learned <s>Gārgya</s>, lived [at a certain time]. He said to <s>Ajātaśatru</s> of <s>Kāśi</s>: "Let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>." <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: "We give a thousand [cows] for this speech. [For people usually] run about [saying] "<s>Janaka</s>! <s>Janaka</s>!" [i.e., praising <s>Janaka</s> as a patron of learning]."' // BṛhUp 2.1.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_2,1.1
tatra pūrvapakṣavādī avidyāviṣayabrahmavid dṛptabālākiḥ dṛpate garvito 'sabhyagbrahmavittavādev balākāyā apatyaṃ bālākirdṛptaścāsau bālākiśceti dṛptabālārkiḥ, haśabda etihyārtha ākhyāyikāyām, anūcānaḥ anuvacasamartho vattkāvāggamī;gārgyo gonnataḥ, āsa babhūva kvacitkālaviśeṣe /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There, the speaker of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> in the domain of <s>avidyā</s> — <s>Dṛptabālāki</s>: '<s>dṛpta</s>' means proud, arrogant, because of knowing <s>Brahman</s> improperly. He is the son of <s>Balākā</s>, hence <s>Bālāki</s>; proud and a <s>Bālāki</s> — hence <s>Dṛptabālāki</s>. The word '<s>ha</s>' has the sense of 'tradition' in a narrative. '<s>Anūcāna</s>' means one capable of discoursing, fluent in speech. <s>Gārgya</s> — descendant of <s>Garga</s>. He lived — existed — at some particular time.

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatrumajātaśatrunāmānaṃ kāśyaṃ kāśirājamabhigamya-brahma te bravāṇīti brahma te tubhyaṃ bravāṇi kathayāni /
sa evamukto 'jātaśatruruvāca-sahasraṃ gavāṃ dadbha etasyāṃ vāci- yāṃ māṃ pratyavoco brahma te bravāṇīti, tāvanmātrameva gosahasrapradāne nimittamityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He said to <s>Ajātaśatru</s> — to the one named <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, the king of <s>Kāśī</s>, having approached him: 'Let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s> — let me speak to you about <s>Brahman</s>, let me explain it.' He, <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, thus addressed, said: 'We give a thousand cows for this speech — for the very speech in which you said to me "let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>" — just this much alone is the occasion for the gift of a thousand cows' — this is the intent.

children.text: sākṣādbrahmakathanameva nimittaṃ kasmānnāpekṣyate sahasradāne? brahma te bravāṇītīyameva tu vāg nimittamapekṣyate? ityucyate;yataḥ śrutireva rājño 'bhiprāyamāha-janako dātā janakaḥ śroteti caitasminvākyadvaye padadvayamabhyasyate janako janaka iti /
children.translated_text: Why is the mere declaration about <s>Brahman</s> not regarded as the occasion for the gift of a thousand, [but only] the actual telling of <s>Brahman</s>? Yet [the king] regards this very speech 'let me tell you about <s>Brahman</s>' as the occasion? It is said: because the <s>śruti</s> itself states the king's intent — '<s>Janaka</s>' [means] a giver, '<s>Janaka</s>' [means] a listener — and the two words in these two sentences are repeated: '<s>Janaka</s>, <s>Janaka</s>.'

children.text: vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhāvadyotanārthaḥ;janako ditsurjanakaḥ śuśrūṣuriti brahma śuśrūṣavo vivakṣavaḥ pa3tijighṛkṣavaśca janādhāvantyabhigacchanti /
children.translated_text: The particle '<s>vai</s>' is for the purpose of indicating what is well-known. [The meaning is:] <s>Janaka</s> is generous; <s>Janaka</s> is eager to listen — people desirous of <s>Brahman</s>, wishing to speak [about it], and wishing to grasp [it], come running to him. // 1 //

children.text: tasmāttatsarvaṃ mayyapi sambhāvitavānasīti //1//
children.translated_text: Therefore, 'You should consider all of that as possible in me too' [said <s>Ajātaśatru</s>].

children.text: evaṃ rājānaṃ śuśrūṣumabhimukhībhūtam-
children.translated_text: Thus, when the king had become favorably disposed and was ready to listen —

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.2
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.2

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāsāv āditye puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatrur -- mā maitasminsaṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
atiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā rājeti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste 'tiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā rājā bhavati || BrhUp_2,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) that is in the sun — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the one who surpasses [all], the head and king of all beings.' One who meditates on him thus becomes the one who surpasses, the head and king of all beings. // BṛhUp 2.1.2 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.2
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.2:]

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ-ya eva asau āditye cakṣuṣi caiko 'bhimānī cakṣurdvāreṇeha hṛdi praviṣṭaḥ 'ahaṃ bhoktā kartā ca'ityavasthitaḥ, etamevāhaṃ brahma paśyāmi, asminkāryakaraṇasaṅghāte upāse /
tasmāttamahaṃ puruṣaṃ brahma tubhyaṃ bravībhyupāḥsveti /
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: the single presiding deity who is in the sun and in the eye, who has entered into the heart here through the gateway of the eye and abides [there thinking] 'I am the enjoyer and the agent' — I see him as <s>Brahman</s>, and I meditate on him in this aggregate of body and instruments. Therefore, I declare that <s>puruṣa</s> to be <s>Brahman</s> to you — 'meditate [on him thus].'

children.text:
sa evamuktaḥ pratyuvāca ajātaśatruḥ 'mā mā'iti hastena vinivārayan-etasminbrahmaṇi vijñeye mā saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ;mā metyābādhanārthaṃ dvirvacanam /
evaṃ samāne vijñānaviṣaye āvayorasmānavijñānavata iva darśayatā bādhitāḥ syāma, ato mā saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ-mā saṃvādaṃ kārṣīrasminbrahmaṇi /
anyaccejjānāsi, tadbrahma vaktumarhasi, na tu yanmayā jñāyata eva /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Ajātaśatru</s> replied, waving [him off] with his hand — 'Do not' — regarding this <s>Brahman</s> to be known, 'do not engage in discussion'; the doubling 'do not, with me' is for the purpose of emphasis. [The meaning is:] 'If you engage me in discussion on the same subject of knowledge, then we, whose knowledge is equal, would appear as if we did not know — hence we would be put to shame. Therefore, do not engage in discussion, do not start a debate with me about this <s>Brahman</s>. If you know something else, you may speak of that <s>Brahman</s> — but not what is already known by me.'

children.text: atha cenmanyase-jānīṣe tvaṃ brahmamātraṃ na tu tadviśeṣaṇopāsanaphalānīti-tanna mantavyam, yataḥ sarvametadahaṃ jāne yadbravīṣi /
katham? atiṣṭhāḥ-atītya bhūtāni tiṣṭhātītyatiṣṭhāḥ /
children.translated_text: How? '<s>Atiṣṭhāḥ</s>' — he who stands having surpassed all beings, i.e. the one who surpasses.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā śiro rājeti vai-rājā dīptigumopetatvāt, etairviśeṣaṇairviśiṣṭametadbrahma asminkāryakaraṇasaṅghāte kartṛ bhoktṛ cetyahametamupāsa iti /
children.translated_text: He is the head, the chief of all beings, and the king — endowed with luminous splendor — thus I meditate on this <s>Brahman</s>, qualified by these attributes, as the agent and enjoyer in this aggregate of body and instruments.

children.text: phalamapyevaṃ viśiṣṭopāsakasya-sa ya etamevamupāste 'tiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ mūrdhā rājā bhavati /
children.translated_text: The fruit too for one who meditates with such qualified [meditation] is: one who meditates on him thus becomes the one who surpasses, the head and king of all beings.

children.text: yathāguṇopāsanameva hi phalam;"taṃ yathā yathopāsate tadeva bhavati"iti śruteḥ //2//
children.translated_text: For the fruit corresponds to the quality meditated upon — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Whatever quality one meditates upon, that indeed one becomes.' // 2 //
And if you think, 'You know <s>Brahman</s> merely [as such], but not its qualifying attributes, meditation, and fruits' — that should not be thought, because I know all of this that you are saying.

children.text: saṃvādenādityabrahmaṇi pratyākhyāte 'jātaśatruṇā candramasi brahmāntaraṃ pratipede gārgyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>Ajātaśatru</s> rejected him regarding the <s>Brahman</s> [identified with] the sun through dialogue, <s>Gārgya</s> proposed another <s>Brahman</s> — [identified with] the moon.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.3
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.3

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāsau candre puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasminsaṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
bṛhan pāṇdaravāsāḥ somo rājeti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste 'har-ahar sutaḥ prasuto bhavati |
nāsyānnaṃ kṣīyate || BrhUp_2,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in the moon — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the great one clad in white, <s>Soma</s> the king.' One who meditates on him thus — day after day the <s>Soma</s> is pressed for him. His food does not diminish. // BṛhUp 2.1.3 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.3
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.3:]
