children.text: ya evāsau candre manasi caikaḥ puruṣo bhoktā kartā ceti pūrvavadviśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: The single <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the moon and in the mind — the enjoyer and agent — is to be qualified as before.

children.text: bṛhan mahān pāṇḍaraṃ śuklaṃ vāso yasya so 'yaṃ pāṇḍaravāsāḥ, apśarīratvāccandrābhimāninaḥ prāṇasya, somo rājā candraḥ, yaścānnabhūto 'bhiṣūyate latātmako yajñe, tamekīkṛtyaitamevāhaṃ brahmopāse /
children.translated_text: 'Great' (<s>bṛhat</s>), with a white garment — he whose garment is white is '<s>pāṇḍaravāsāḥ</s>,' because the body of the presiding deity of <s>prāṇa</s> associated with the moon is made of water. '<s>Soma</s> the king' — the moon; and also that which in its plant-form is pressed as food at the sacrifice — combining both, 'I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: yathoktaguṇaṃ ya upāste tasyāharahaḥ sutaḥ somo 'bhiṣuto bhavati yajñe, prasutaḥ prakṛṣṭaṃ sutarāṃ suto bhavati vikāre, ubhayavidhayajñānuṣṭhānasāmarthyaṃ bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who meditates with the qualities described, day after day the <s>Soma</s> is pressed — extracted at the sacrifice; it is abundantly pressed in its transformation — the meaning is: the capacity for performing both types of sacrifice comes about.

children.text: annaṃ cāsya na kṣīyate 'nnātmakopāsakasya //3//
children.translated_text: And his food does not diminish — for one who meditates [on <s>Brahman</s>] whose nature is food. // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.4
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.4

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāsau vidyuti puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasmin saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
tejasvīti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste tejasvī ha bhavati |
tejasvinī hāsya prajā bhavati || BrhUp_2,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in lightning — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the resplendent one.' One who meditates on him thus becomes resplendent. His offspring too becomes resplendent. // BṛhUp 2.1.4 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.4
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.4:]

children.text: tathā vidyuti tvaci hṛdaye caikā devatā /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in lightning, in the skin, and in the heart — [there is] one deity.

children.text: tejasvīti viśeṣaṇam, tasyāstatphalam-tejasvī ha bhavati tejasvinī hāsya prajā bhavati /
children.translated_text: 'Resplendent' (<s>tejasvī</s>) is the qualifying attribute. Its fruit: one becomes resplendent, and one's offspring too becomes resplendent.

children.text: vidyutāṃ bahutvasyāṅgīkaraṇādātmani prajāyāṃ ca phalabāhulyam //4//
children.translated_text: Because the plurality of lightning [flashes] is accepted, there is abundance of fruit in both oneself and one's offspring. // 4 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.5
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.5

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyam ākāśe puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasmin saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
pūrṇam apravartīti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste pūryate prajayā paśubhir nāsyāsmāl lokāt prajodvartate || BrhUp_2,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in space — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the full and non-moving one.' One who meditates on him thus is filled with offspring and cattle. His offspring does not depart from this world. // BṛhUp 2.1.5 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.5
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.5:]

children.text:
tathā ākāśe hṛdyākāśe hṛdaye caikā devatā /
pūrṇamapravarti ceti viśeṣaṇadvayam /
pūrṇatvaviśeṣaṇaphalamidam-pūryate prajayā paśubhiḥ;apravartiviśeṣaṇaphalam-nāsyāsmāllokātprajodvartata iti,
children.translated_text: Similarly, in [outer] space, in the space of the heart, and in the heart — [there is] one deity. 'Full' and 'non-moving' are two qualifying attributes. The fruit of the attribute 'full' is: one is filled with offspring and cattle. The fruit of the attribute 'non-moving' is: one's offspring does not depart from this world —

children.text: prajāsantānāvicchittiḥ //5//
children.translated_text: [meaning] the continuity of one's lineage is not broken. // 5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.6
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.6

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyaṃ vāyau puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasminsaṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
indro vaikuṇṭho 'parājitā seneti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste jiṣṇur hāparājiṣṇur bhavaty anyatastyajāyī || BrhUp_2,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in the wind — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as <s>Indra</s> <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, an unconquered army.' One who meditates on him thus becomes victorious, unconquerable — a conqueror of rivals. // BṛhUp 2.1.6 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.6
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.6:]

children.text: tathā vāyau prāṇe hṛdi caikā devatā /
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the wind, in <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), and in the heart — [there is] one deity.

children.text: tasyā viśeṣaṇam-indraḥ parameśvaraḥ, vaikuṇṭho 'prasahyaḥ, na parairjitapūrvā parājitā senā-marutāṃ gaṇatvaprasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: Its qualifying attributes: <s>Indra</s> — the Supreme Lord; <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — the irresistible one; the army not previously conquered by others is the unconquered army — because the <s>Maruts</s> are well-known as a troop.

children.text: upāsanaphalamapi-jiṣṇurha jayanaśīlo 'parājiṣṇurna ca parairjitasvabhāvo bhavati, anyatastyajāyī anyatastyānāṃ sapatnānāṃ jayanaśīlo bhavati //6//
children.translated_text: The fruit of the meditation too: one becomes victorious — of a conquering nature; unconquerable — not of a nature to be conquered by others; a conqueror of rivals — of a nature to conquer opposing adversaries. // 6 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.7
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.7

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyam agnau puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasminsaṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
viṣāsahir iti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste viṣāsahir ha bhavati |
viṣāsahir hāsya prajā bhavati || BrhUp_2,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in fire — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the forbearing one.' One who meditates on him thus becomes forbearing. His offspring too becomes forbearing. // BṛhUp 2.1.7 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.7
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.7:]

children.text: agnau vācihṛdi caikā devatā /
children.translated_text: In fire, in speech, and in the heart — [there is] one deity.

children.text: tasyā viśeṣaṇam-viṣāsahirmarṣayitā pareṣām /
children.translated_text: Its qualifying attribute: '<s>viṣāsahiḥ</s>' — one who endures, who tolerates [the assaults] of others.

children.text: agnibāhulyāt phalabāhulyaṃ pūrvavat //7//
children.translated_text: Because of the plurality of fires, there is abundance of fruit, as before. // 7 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.8
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.8

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyam apsu puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasminsaṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
pratirūpa iti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste pratirūpaṃ haivainam upagacchati nāpratirūpam |
atho pratirupo 'smāj jāyate || BrhUp_2,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in the waters — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the fitting one (<s>pratirūpa</s>).' One who meditates on him thus — only what is fitting approaches him, not what is unfitting. And one who is fitting is born from him. // BṛhUp 2.1.8 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.8
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.8:]

children.text: apsu retasi hṛdi caikā devatā /
children.translated_text: In the waters, in the semen, and in the heart — [there is] one deity.

children.text: tasyā viśeṣaṇam-pratirūpo 'nurūpaḥ śrutismṛtyapratikūla ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Its qualifying attribute: '<s>pratirūpa</s>' — conforming, not opposed to <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>; this is the meaning.

children.text: phalam-pratirūpaṃ śrutismṛtiśāsanānurūpameva enamupagacchati prāpnoti, na viparītam, anyacca-asmāttathāvidha evopajāyate //8//
children.translated_text: The fruit: only what is fitting — what conforms to the teachings of <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> — approaches, attains him; not the contrary. And further: from him is born one who is likewise [fitting]. // 8 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.9
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.9

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyam ādarśe puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasmin saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
rociṣṇur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste rociṣṇur ha bhavati |
rociṣṇur hāsya prajā bhavati |
atho yaiḥ saṃnigacchati |
sarvāṃs tān atirocate || BrhUp_2,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in the mirror — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the radiant one.' One who meditates on him thus becomes radiant. His offspring too becomes radiant. And he outshines all those he encounters. // BṛhUp 2.1.9 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.9
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.9:]

children.text: ādarśe prasādasvabhāve cānyatra khaḍgādau hārde ca sattvaśuddhisvābhāvye caikā devatā, tasyā viśeṣaṇam-rociṣṇurdīptisvabhāvaḥ, phalaṃ ca tadeva /
children.translated_text: In the mirror — [i.e.,] in what is of a clear nature, including swords and the like [which are reflective] — and in the heart, in the natural purity of <s>sattva</s> — [there is] one deity. Its qualifying attribute: '<s>rociṣṇu</s>' — of a radiant nature. And the fruit is the same [as the attribute].

children.text: rocanādhārabāhulyātphalabāhulyam //9//
children.translated_text: Because of the plurality of the substrata of radiance, there is abundance of fruit. // 9 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.10
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.10

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyaṃ yantaṃ paścāc chabbo 'nūdety etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasmin saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
asur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste sarvaṃ haivāsmiṃl loka āyur eti |
nainaṃ purā kālāt prāṇo jahāti || BrhUp_2,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The sound that follows a person as he walks — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the life-force (<s>asu</s>).' One who meditates on him thus — the full span of life comes to him in this world. Breath does not leave him before his time. // BṛhUp 2.1.10 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.10
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.10:]

children.text: yantaṃ gacchantaṃ ya evāyaṃ śabdaḥ paścātpṛṣṭhato 'nīdetyadhyātmaṃ ca jīvanahetuḥ prāṇaḥ, tamekīkṛtyāha;asuḥ prāṇo jīvanaheturiti guṇastasya;phalam-sarvamāyurasmiṃlloka etīti-yathopāttaṃ karmaṇā āyuḥ;karmaphalaparicchinnakālātpurā pūrvaṃ rogādibhiḥ pīḍyamānamapyenaṃ prāṇo na jahāti //10//
children.translated_text: The sound that follows from behind one who is walking, going — and in the individual self, <s>prāṇa</s> as the cause of life — unifying both, he says: '<s>asu</s>' — the life-force, the cause of living — this is its qualifying attribute. The fruit: the full span of life comes to him in this world — meaning the lifespan as acquired through <s>karma</s>. Before the time delimited by the fruit of <s>karma</s>, even though being afflicted by disease and the like, breath does not leave him. // 10 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.11
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.11

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyaṃ dikṣu puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasmin saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
dvitīyo 'napaga iti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste dvitīyavān ha bhavati |
nāsmād gaṇaś chidyate || BrhUp_2,1.11 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in the directions — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the companion who never departs.' One who meditates on him thus has companions. His group is not severed from him. // BṛhUp 2.1.11 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.11
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.11:]

children.text: dikṣu karṇayorhṛdi caikā devatā aśvinau devāvaviyuktasvabhāvau /
children.translated_text: In the directions, in the ears, and in the heart — [there is] one deity: the two <s>Aśvins</s>, who are of an inseparable nature.

children.text: guṇastasya dvitīyavattvamanapagatvamaviyuktatā cānyonyaṃ diśāmaśvinoścaivandharmitvāt /
children.translated_text: Their qualifying attributes: having a companion, being non-departing, and mutual inseparability — because the directions and the <s>Aśvins</s> share the same property [of being paired].

children.text: tadeva ca phalamupāsakasya-gaṇāvicchedo dvitīyavattvaṃ ca //11//
children.translated_text: And the fruit for the meditator is the same: the non-severance of one's group and having companions. // 11 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.12
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.12

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyaṃ chāyāmayaḥ puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasminsaṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
mṛtyur iti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāste sarvaṃ haivāsmiṃl loka āyur eti |
nainaṃ purā kālān mṛtyur āgacchati || BrhUp_2,1.12 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is made of shadow — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as Death.' One who meditates on him thus — the full span of life comes to him in this world. Death does not come to him before his time. // BṛhUp 2.1.12 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.12
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.12:]

children.text: chāyāyāṃ bāhye tamasyadhyātmaṃ ca āvaraṇātmake 'jñāne hṛdi caikā devatā /
children.translated_text: In the shadow — in external darkness — and in the individual self, in the covering nature of ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), and in the heart — [there is] one deity.

children.text: tasyā viśeṣaṇaṃ mṛtyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Its qualifying attribute is Death.

children.text: phalaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvavat, mṛtyoranāgamanena rogādipīḍābhāvo viśeṣaḥ //12//
children.translated_text: The fruit is the same as before [full lifespan]; the distinction is the absence of affliction from disease and the like, through the non-arrival of death. // 12 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.13
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.13

children.text:
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- ya evāyam ātmani puruṣa etam evāhaṃ brahmopāsa iti |
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- mā maitasmin saṃvadiṣṭhāḥ |
ātmanvīti vā aham etam upāsa iti |
sa ya etam evam upāsta ātmanvī ha bhavati |
ātmanvinī hāsya prajā bhavati |
sa ha tūṣṇīm āsa gārgyaḥ || BrhUp_2,1.13 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> that is in the body (<s>ātman</s>) — I meditate on him as <s>Brahman</s>.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Do not engage me in discussion about this. I meditate on him as the embodied one (<s>ātmanvī</s>).' One who meditates on him thus becomes embodied [i.e., self-possessed]. His offspring too becomes embodied. Then <s>Gārgya</s> fell silent. // BṛhUp 2.1.13 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.13
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.13:]

children.text: ātmani prajāpatau buddhau ca hṛdi caikā devatā /
tasyā ātmanvī-ātmavānīti viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Its qualifying attribute is '<s>ātmanvī</s>' — one who is self-possessed, i.e. <s>ātmavān</s>.

children.text: phalam-ātmanvī ha bhavatyātmavānbhavati, ātmanvinī hāsya prajā bhavati /
children.translated_text: The fruit: one becomes self-possessed — one becomes endowed with a self. His offspring too becomes self-possessed.

children.text: buddhibahulatvātprajāyāṃ sampādanamiti viśeṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: The distinction is: because of the preponderance of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), the accomplishment [of this quality] extends to one's offspring.

children.text: svayaṃ parijñātatvenaivaṃ krameṇa pratyākhyā teṣu brahmasu sa gārgyaḥ kṣīṇabrahmavijñāno 'pratibhāsamānottarastūṣṇīmavākchirā āsa //13//
children.translated_text: Since [each <s>Brahman</s>] was already known by [<s>Ajātaśatru</s>] himself, <s>Gārgya</s>, his knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> exhausted by the successive rejections of those [proposed] <s>Brahmans</s> — unable to think of a further reply — sat silently with his head bowed. // 13 //
In the self — in <s>Prajāpati</s>, in the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), and in the heart — [there is] one deity.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.14
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,1.14

children.text: taṃ tathābhūtamālakṣya gārgyam-
children.translated_text: Perceiving <s>Gārgya</s> in that state —

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- etāvan nū3 iti |
etāvad dhīti |
naitāvatā viditaṃ bhavatīti |
sa hovāca gārgyaḥ -- upa tvāyānīti || BrhUp_2,1.14 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Is that all?' [<s>Gārgya</s> replied:] 'That is all.' [<s>Ajātaśatru</s> said:] 'By that much, it is not known.' <s>Gārgya</s> said: 'Let me come to you [as a student].' // BṛhUp 2.1.14 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.14
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.14:]

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ-etāvannū3iti /
kimetāvadbrahma nirjñātam, āhosvidadhikamapyastīti? itara āhaitāvaddhīti /
naitāvatā viditena brahma viditaṃ bhavatītyāhājātaśatruḥ, kimarthaṃ garvito 'si brahma te bravāṇīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'Is this all?' — meaning: 'Is <s>Brahman</s> fully known by this much, or is there something more?' The other [<s>Gārgya</s>] said: 'This much indeed.' <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: '<s>Brahman</s> is not known by this much' — why then are you proud, saying 'I shall teach you <s>Brahman</s>'?

children.text:
kimetāvadviditaṃ viditameva na bhavati? ityucyate-na, phalavadvijña3naśravaṇāt /
na cārthavādatvameva vākyānāmavagantuṃ śakyam apūrvavidhānaparāṇi hi vākyāni pratyupāsanopadeśaṃ lakṣyante-"atiṣṭhāḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām"ityādīni /
tadanurūpāṇi ca phalāni sarvatra śrūyante vibhaktāni /
arthavādatve etadasamañjasam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But if this much is known, is it truly not known? It is said: no, because fruitful knowledge is heard [in scripture]. Nor can the [Upaniṣadic] sentences be understood as mere <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages), for the sentences are directed at enjoining new [meditations] — they are observed to teach a meditation for each [deity], such as 'You stood firm above all beings' and the like. And corresponding fruits are heard separately everywhere. If they were [mere] <s>arthavāda</s>, this would be inconsistent.

children.text:
kathaṃ tarhi naitāvatā viditaṃ bhavatīti? naiṣa doṣaḥ, adhikṛtāpekṣatvāt /
brahmopādeśārthaṃ hi śuśrūṣave 'jātaśatrave 'mukhyabrahmavidgārgyaḥ pravṛttaḥ, sa yukta eva mukhyabrahmavidājātaśatruṇāmukhya brahmavidgārgyo vaktum- yanmukhyaṃ brahma vaktuṃ pravṛttastvaṃ tanna jānīṣa iti /
yadyamukhyabrahmavijñānamapi pratyākhyāyeta, tadaitāvateti na brūyāt, na kiñcijjñātaṃ tvayetyevaṃ brūyāt, na kiñcijjñātaṃ tvayetyevaṃ brūyāt /
tasmādbhavantyetāvantyavidyāviṣaye brahmāṇi /
etāvadvijñānadvāratvācca parabrahmavijñānasya, yuktameva vaktum-naitāvatāviditaṃbhavatīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And because these [meditations] serve as the doorway to the knowledge of the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, it is entirely proper to say 'by this much it is not known.'

children.text: avidyāviṣaye vijñeyatvaṃ nāmarūpakarmātmakatvaṃ caiṣāṃ tṛtīye 'dhyāye pradarśitam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That these [meditations on deities] have knowability and the nature of name, form, and action within the domain of <s>avidyā</s> has been demonstrated in the third <s>adhyāya</s>.

children.text: tasmāt"naitāvatā viditaṃ bhavati"iti bruvatā adhikaṃ bhrahma jñātavyamastīti darśitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, by saying 'by this much it is not known,' it is shown that there is a higher <s>Brahman</s> to be known.

children.text: taccānupasannāya na vaktavyam ityācāravidhijño gārgyaḥ svayamevāha-upa tvā yānīti-upagacchānīti tvām, yathānyaḥ śiṣyo gurum //14//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And that [higher <s>Brahman</s>] is not to be taught to one who has not approached [as a student] — <s>Gārgya</s>, knowing the rules of conduct, himself says: 'Let me come to you' — 'Let me approach you,' just as any other student [approaches] a teacher. (14)

[Commentary:] How then [is the statement] 'by this much it is not known' [justified]? This is not a fault, because it is relative to the qualified [person]. For <s>Gārgya</s>, who was not a knower of the primary <s>Brahman</s>, had approached <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, who was eager for instruction about <s>Brahman</s>. It is entirely proper for <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, who is a knower of the primary <s>Brahman</s>, to say to <s>Gārgya</s>, who is not a knower of the primary <s>Brahman</s>: 'That primary <s>Brahman</s> which you set out to teach — you do not know it.' If even the non-primary knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> were being rejected, [<s>Ajātaśatru</s>] would not say 'this much'; he would say 'nothing is known by you.' Therefore, these [meditations taught by <s>Gārgya</s>] are valid <s>Brahmans</s> within the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.15
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.1.15]

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- pratilomaṃ caitad yad brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyam upeyād brahma me vakṣyatīti |
vy eva tvā jñapayiṣyāmīti |
taṃ pāṇāv ādāyottasthau |
tau ha puruṣaṃ suptam ājagmatuḥ |
tam etair nāmabhir āmantrayāṃ cakre bṛhan pāṇdaravāsaḥ soma rājann iti |
sa nottasthau |
taṃ pāṇināpeṣaṃ bodhayāṃ cakāra |
sa hottasthau || BrhUp_2,1.15 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'This is contrary to custom — that a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should approach a <s>kṣatriya</s> [thinking] "he will teach me <s>Brahman</s>." Nevertheless, I shall make you know.' Taking him by the hand, he arose. The two came upon a sleeping man. He addressed him with these names: 'O great one, O white-robed one, O King <s>Soma</s>!' He did not rise. He awakened him by pressing with the hand. Then he rose. (BṛUp 2.1.15)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.15
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.15:]

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ pratilomaṃ viparītaṃ caitat /
kiṃ tat? yadbrahmaṇa uttamavarṇa ācāryatve 'dhikṛtaḥ san kṣatriyamanācāryasvabhāvamupeyāt-upagacchecchiṣyavṛttyā brahma me vakṣyatīti /
etadācāravidhiśāsreṣu niṣiddham;tasmāttiṣṭhatvamācārya eva san /
vijñapayiṣyāmyeva tvāmahaṃ yasminvidite brahma viditaṃ bhavati yattanmukhyaṃ brahma vedyam /
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'This is contrary to custom, this is reversed.' What is that? That a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — one of the highest <s>varṇa</s>, qualified for the role of teacher — should approach a <s>kṣatriya</s>, who is not by nature a teacher, in the manner of a student, [thinking] 'he will teach me <s>Brahman</s>.' This is prohibited in the texts on rules of conduct. Therefore, you remain as the teacher. I shall make you know — that primary <s>Brahman</s> which is to be known, knowing which <s>Brahman</s> is [truly] known.

children.text:
taṃ gārgyaṃ salajjamālakṣya viśrambhajananāya pāṇau hasta ādāya gṛhītvottasthāvutthitavān /
tau ha gārgyājātaśatrū puruṣaṃ suptaṃ rājagṛhapradeśe kvacidājagmaturāgatau /
taṃ ca puruṣaṃ suptaṃ pāpya etairnāmabhiḥ"bṛhan pāṇḍaravāsaḥ soma rājan"ityetairāmantrayāñcakre /
evamāmantryamāṇo 'pi sa supto nottasthau, tamapratibudhyamānaṃ pāṇinā āpeṣamāpiṣyāpiṣya bodhayāñcakāra pratibodhitavān; tena sa hottasthau /
tasmādyo gārgyeṇābhipretaḥ nāsāvasmiñcharīre kartā bhoktā brahmeti /
kathaṃ punaridamavagamyate suptapuruṣagamanatatsambodhanānutthānairgārgyābhimatasya brahmaṇo 'brahmatvaṃ jñāpitamiti?
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Perceiving that <s>Gārgya</s> was embarrassed, in order to generate confidence, [<s>Ajātaśatru</s>] took him by the hand — grasped his hand — and arose, stood up. The two — <s>Gārgya</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s> — came upon, arrived at, a sleeping man somewhere in the precincts of the royal palace. Having reached that sleeping man, he addressed him with these names: 'O great one (<s>Bṛhan</s>), O white-robed one (<s>Pāṇḍaravāsas</s>), O King <s>Soma</s>!' Even though thus addressed, that sleeping man did not rise. He then pressed him with the hand — pressing and pressing again — and awakened him; thus he was aroused, and thereupon he rose. Therefore, the one whom <s>Gārgya</s> considered [to be <s>Brahman</s>] — he is not the agent and enjoyer in this body that is <s>Brahman</s>. But how is it understood that, through going to the sleeping man, addressing him, and his not rising, the non-<s>Brahman</s>-ness of <s>Gārgya</s>'s intended <s>Brahman</s> is demonstrated?

children.text:
jāgaritakāle yo gārgyābhipretaḥ puruṣaḥ kartā bhoktā brahma saṃnihitaḥ karaṇeṣu yathā, tathājātaśatrvabhipreto 'pi tatsvāmī bhṛtyeṣviva rājā saṃnihita eva /
kiṃ tu bhṛtyasvāminorgārgyājātaśatrvabhipretayoryadvivekāvadhāraṇa kāraṇaṃ tatsaṅkīrṇatvādanavadhāritaviśeṣam /
yaddraṣṭutvameva bhokturna dṛśyatvam, yaccābhokturdṛśyatvameva na tu draṣṭṛtvam, taccobhayamiha saṅkīrṇatvādvivicya darśayitumaśakyamiti suptapuruṣagamanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the waking state, the person whom <s>Gārgya</s> considers — the agent and enjoyer — is present in the sense-organs, just as [he is during that state]; and likewise, the one intended by <s>Ajātaśatru</s> — its master — is also present, like a king among servants. However, the means of ascertaining the distinction between the servant and the master — [i.e.] between the one intended by <s>Gārgya</s> and the one intended by <s>Ajātaśatru</s> — is difficult [to discern in the waking state] because they are mixed together; the distinction has not been ascertained. That which belongs to the seer is the nature of seeing, not being-seen; and that which belongs to the non-enjoyer is the nature of being-seen, not seeing — both of these, because they are mixed together here [in waking], cannot be shown in a discriminated fashion. Hence [they went] to the sleeping man.

children.text: nanu supte 'pi puruṣe viśiṣṭairnāmabhirāmantrito bhoktaiva pratipatsyate nābhokteti naiva nirṇayaḥ syāditi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] But even in the sleeping man, when addressed with special names, only the enjoyer would respond, not the non-enjoyer — so there would be no determination at all.

children.text:
na, nirdhāritaviśeṣatvādgārgyābhipretasyaḥ yo hi satyenacchannaḥ prāṇa ātmāmṛto vāgādiṣvanastamito nimlocatsu, yasyāpaḥ śarīraṃ pāṇḍaravāsāḥ, yaścāsapatnatvād bṛhan, yaśca somo rājā ṣoḍaśakālaḥ, sa svavyāpārārūḍho yathānirjñāta evānastamitasvabhāva āste /
nacānyasya kasyacidvyāpārastasminkāle gārgyeṇābhipreyate tadvirodhinaḥ /
tasmātsvanāmabhirāmantritena pratiboddhavyam, na ca pratyabudhyata /
tasmātpāriśeṣyādgārgyābhipretasyābhoktṛtvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No — because the [<s>Brahman</s>] intended by <s>Gārgya</s> has been specifically determined. For he who is 'concealed by the real, <s>prāṇa</s>, the <s>ātman</s>, the immortal' — who has not set [like the sun] among speech and the other [organs] even when they set — whose body is the waters, who is white-robed (<s>Pāṇḍaravāsas</s>), who is great (<s>Bṛhan</s>) because of being unopposed, and who is King <s>Soma</s> of sixteen digits — he, even though not engaged in his own activity, continues to exist as though unknowing, with his nature of not-setting intact. And no activity of any other [entity] at that time is intended by <s>Gārgya</s> as contradicting that [<s>prāṇa</s>]. Therefore, being addressed by his own names, he should have responded — yet he did not respond. Therefore, by elimination, the [<s>Brahman</s>] intended by <s>Gārgya</s> — the <s>prāṇa</s> — is a non-enjoyer.

children.text:
bhoktṛsvabhāvaśced bhuñjītaiva svaṃ viṣayaṃ prāptam /
na hi dagdhṛsvabhāvaḥ prakāśayitṛsvabhāvaḥ sanvahnistṛṇolapādi dāhyaṃ svaviṣayaṃ prāptaṃ na dahati, prakāśyaṃ vā na prakāśayati /
na ceddahati prakāśayati vā prāptaṃ svaṃ viṣayam, nāsau vahnirdagdhā prakāśayitā veti niścīyate /
tathāsau prāptaśabdādiviṣayopalabdhṛsvabhāvaśced gārgyābhipretaḥ prāṇo bṛhan pāṇḍaravāsa ityevamādiśabdaṃ svaṃ viṣayamupalabheta, yathā prāptaṃ tṛṇolapādi vahnirdahetprakāśayecca avyabhicāreṇa tadvat /
tasmātprāptānāṃ śabdādīnāmapratibodhādabhoktṛsvabhāva iti niścīyate /
na hi yasya yaḥ svabhāvo niścitaḥ, sa taṃ vyabhicarati kadācidapi /
ataḥ siddhaṃ prāṇasyābhoktṛtvam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] If it were by nature an enjoyer, it would enjoy its own object upon reaching it. For fire, which is by nature a burner and illuminator, does not fail to burn combustible material such as grass and straw that comes within its reach, nor does it fail to illumine what is to be illumined. If it does not burn or illumine its own object upon reaching it, then it is ascertained that it is not fire, not a burner, not an illuminator. Similarly, if <s>Gārgya</s>'s intended [entity] — <s>prāṇa</s>, the great one, the white-robed one — were by nature a perceiver of sound and other sense-objects that come within its reach, it would perceive the sound of its own name 'great one, white-robed one' and the rest, just as fire invariably burns and illumines grass and straw that come within its reach. Therefore, from the non-response to the approaching sounds and the rest, [the conclusion is that <s>prāṇa</s>] is by nature a non-enjoyer. For when the nature of something has been ascertained, it never deviates from it. Thus the non-enjoyership of <s>prāṇa</s> is established.

children.text: sambodhanārthanāmaviśeṣeṇa sambandhāgrahaṇādapratibodha iti cet? syādetat-yathā bahuṣvāsīneṣu svanāmaviśeṣeṇa sambandhāghrahaṇānmāmayaṃ sambodhayatīti, śṛṇvannapi sambodhyamāno viśeṣato na pratipadyate, tathemāni bṛhannityevamādīni mama nāmānītyagṛhītasambandhatvātprāṇo na gṛhṇāti sambodhanārthaṃ śabdam, na tvavijñātṛtvādeveti cet?
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] The non-response is because, when addressed with special names for the purpose of awakening, [<s>prāṇa</s>] does not apprehend the connection [between the names and itself]. It might be that, just as when many are seated, one addressed by a particular name, not apprehending the connection — 'this person is addressing me' — does not specifically respond even though hearing the address; similarly, <s>prāṇa</s> does not apprehend the sound addressed to it for the purpose of awakening because it does not grasp the connection — 'these names such as Bṛhan and the rest are my names' — not because it is a non-knower.

children.text:
na;devatābhyupagame 'ghrahaṇānupapatteḥ /
yasya hi candrādyabhimāninī devatā adhyātmaṃ prāṇo bhoktā abhyupagamyate, tasya tathā saṃvyavahārāya viśeṣanāmnā sambandho 'vaśyaṃ grahītavyaḥ, anyathā āhvānādiviṣaye saṃvyavahāro 'nupapannaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No — because if [<s>prāṇa</s>] is accepted as a deity, non-apprehension is untenable. For one who accepts that a deity presiding over the moon and the rest is the enjoyer, the <s>prāṇa</s> in the individual body — for him, the connection with the special name must necessarily be grasped for the purpose of transactional usage; otherwise, the transactional usage in the context of invocation and the like would be untenable.

children.text:
vyatiriktapakṣe 'pyapratipattera yuktamiti cet? yasya ca prāṇavyatirikto bhoktā, tasyāpi bṛhannityādināmabhiḥ sambodhane bṛhattvādināmnāṃ tadā tadviṣayatvātpratipattiryuktā /
na ca kadācidapi bṛhattvādiśabdaiḥ sambodhitaḥ
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] Even on the alternative view [where the enjoyer is distinct from <s>prāṇa</s>], the non-response would be just as unjustified. For one who [holds that] the enjoyer is distinct from <s>prāṇa</s> — for him too, upon being addressed with names such as 'Bṛhan' and the rest, response would be appropriate, since the meanings of 'greatness' and the rest pertain to that [enjoyer] at that time.

children.text:
pratipadyamāno dṛśyate /
tasmādakāraṇamabhoktṛtve sambodhanāpratipattiriti cet?
children.translated_text: And yet [such a one] is never observed to respond when addressed with the words 'great one' and the like. Therefore, the non-response upon being addressed is irrelevant to [the question of] non-enjoyership.

children.text:
na;tadvatastāvanmātrābhimānānupapatteḥ /
yasya prāṇavyatirikto bhoktā sa prāṇadevatāmātre 'bhimāno yathā haste /
tasmātprāṇanāmasambodhane kṛtsnābhimānino yuktaivāpratipattiḥ;na tu prāṇasyāsādhāraṇanāmasaṃyoge, devatātmatvānabhimānāccātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No — because for one who is merely identified with <s>prāṇa</s> and that alone, such a limited self-identification is untenable. For one who holds the enjoyer to be distinct from <s>prāṇa</s> — that one has self-identification with the <s>prāṇa</s>-deity alone, as with the hand [i.e. as a mere instrument]. Therefore, when addressed by the name '<s>prāṇa</s>,' the non-response of one who identifies with the whole [and not merely a part] is indeed justified. But it is not [justified] in the case of <s>prāṇa</s>'s connection with its own exclusive name — because the self does not identify itself as the <s>prāṇa</s>-deity.

children.text:
svanāmaprayoge 'pyapratipattidarśanādayuktamiti cet? suṣuptasya yallaukikaṃ devadattādi nāma tenāpi sambodhyamānaḥ kadācinna pratipadyate suṣuptaḥ /
tathā bhoktāpi sanprāṇo na pratipadyata iti cet?
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] Since non-response is observed even when one's own name is used, [the argument] is unjustified. When one is in deep sleep and addressed even by one's worldly name '<s>Devadatta</s>' and the like, the deeply sleeping person sometimes does not respond. Similarly, even though <s>prāṇa</s> is an enjoyer, it does not respond [when asleep].

children.text:
na, ātmaprāṇayoḥ suptāsuptatvaviśeṣopapatteḥ /
suṣuptatvātprāṇagrastatayoparatakaṇa ātmā svaṃ nāma prayujyamānamapi na pratipadyate /
na tu tadasuptasya prāṇasya bhoktṛtva uparatakaraṇatvaṃ sambodhanāgrahaṇaṃ vā yuktam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No — because the distinction of being asleep and not-asleep is tenable between the <s>ātman</s> (self) and <s>prāṇa</s>. The <s>ātman</s>, being deeply asleep — having its sense-organs suspended due to being absorbed into <s>prāṇa</s> — does not respond even when its own name is uttered. But for <s>prāṇa</s>, which is not asleep, it is not proper [to ascribe] the suspension of sense-organs as the cause of non-response, if it were an enjoyer.

children.text: aprasiddhanāmabhiḥ sambodhanamayuktamiti cet- santi hi prāṇaviṣayāṇi prasiddhāni prāṇādināmāni;tānyapohya
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] The addressing with unfamiliar names is inappropriate. For there exist well-known names pertaining to <s>prāṇa</s>, such as '<s>prāṇa</s>' and the like. Setting those aside,

children.text:
aprasiddhairbṛhattvādināmabhiḥ sambodhanamayuktam, laukikanyāyāpohāt /
tasmādbhoktureva sataḥ prāṇasyāpratipattiriti cet? na, devatāpratyākhyānārthatvāt /
kevalasambodhanamātrāpratipattyaiva asuptasyādhyātmikasya prāṇasyābhokatṛtve siddhe yaccandradevatāviṣayairnāmabhiḥ sambodhanam, taccandradevatā prāṇo 'smiñcharīre bhokteti gārgyasya viśeṣapratipattinirākaraṇārtham /
na hi tallaukikanāmnā sambodhaneśakyaṃ kartum /
prāṇagrastatvātkaraṇāntarāṇāṃ pravṛttyanupapatterbhoktṛtvāśaṅkānupapattiḥ /
devatāntarābhāvācca /
children.translated_text: to address [it] with unfamiliar names such as 'Bṛhan' and the rest is inappropriate, being contrary to common usage. Therefore, the non-response belongs to <s>prāṇa</s> even though it is an enjoyer. [We say:] No — because [the addressing with deity-specific names] is for the purpose of refuting the deity [theory]. Since the non-enjoyership of the unsleeping, individual <s>prāṇa</s> is already established merely from the non-response to mere address — the additional addressing with names pertaining to the moon-deity is for the purpose of refuting <s>Gārgya</s>'s specific view that 'the moon-deity is the <s>prāṇa</s>, the enjoyer, in this body.' For that [refutation] cannot be accomplished with worldly names. Since the other sense-organs are absorbed into <s>prāṇa</s>, the impossibility of their functioning [makes] the suspicion of enjoyership untenable. And because there is no other deity [present].

children.text: nanvatiṣṭhā ityādyātmanvītyantena granthena guṇavaddevatābhedasya darśitatvāditi cet?
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] But has not the text beginning with '<s>atiṣṭhāḥ</s>' ('you stood firm') and ending with '<s>ātmanvī</s>' ('having a self') demonstrated the distinction of deities possessing qualities?

children.text:
na, tasya prāṇa evaikatvābhyupagamātsarvaśrutiṣvaranābhinidarśanena /
"satyenacchannam prāṇo vā amṛtam"iti ca prāṇabāhyasyānyasyānabhyupagamādbhoktuḥ"eṣa u hyeva sarve devāḥ" "katama eko deva iti prāṇaḥ"iti ca sarvadevānāṃ prāṇa evaikatvopapādanācca /
tathā karaṇabhedeṣvanāśaṅkā, dehabhedeṣviva smṛtijñānecchadipratisandhānānupapatteḥ;na hyanyadṛṣṭamanyaḥ smarati jānātīcchati pratisandadhāti vā /
tasmānna karaṇabhedaviṣayā bhoktṛtvāśaṅkā vijñānamātraviṣayā vā kadācidapyupapadyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No — because the acceptance that all those [deities] are one in <s>prāṇa</s> alone is demonstrated in all the <s>śrutis</s> by the absence of any separate mention. And because of the non-acceptance of any other enjoyer external to <s>prāṇa</s>, [as stated in:] 'Concealed by the real; <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed the immortal.' And because all the gods are shown to be unified in <s>prāṇa</s> alone: 'He indeed is all the gods'; 'Which is the one god? <s>Prāṇa</s>.' Similarly, there is no suspicion [of enjoyership] in the case of the differentiation of sense-organs, just as in the case of the differentiation of bodies — because the continuity of memory, knowledge, desire, and recognition is untenable [across different organs as across different bodies]. For what is seen by one is not remembered, known, desired, or recognized by another. Therefore, the suspicion of enjoyership pertaining to the differentiation of organs, or pertaining to consciousness alone, is never tenable.

children.text:
nanu saṅghāta evāstu bhoktā, kiṃ vyatiriktakalpanayeti? na;āpeṣaṇe viśeṣadarśanāt /
yadi hi prāṇaśarīrasaṅghātamātro bhoktā syātsaṅghātamātrāviśeṣātsadā āpiṣṭasyānāpiṣṭasya ca pratibodhe viśeṣo na syāt /
saṅghātavyatirikte tu punarbhoktari saṅghātasambandhaviśeṣānekatvāt peṣaṇāpeṣaṇakṛtavedanāyāḥ sukhaduḥkhamohamadhyamādhamottamakarmaphalabhedopapatteśca viśeṣo yuktaḥ /
na tu saṅghātamātre sambandhakarmaphalabhedānupapatterviśeṣo yuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] Let the aggregate itself be the enjoyer — why imagine something distinct? [We say:] No — because a distinction is observed upon pressing. For if the enjoyer were merely the aggregate of <s>prāṇa</s> and body, there would be no difference in awakening between one who is pressed and one who is not, since there is no difference in the mere aggregate. But when the enjoyer is distinct from the aggregate, since the variety of connections between [the enjoyer] and the aggregate is manifold, and because the distinction of sensations produced by pressing and not-pressing — and of the fruits of action such as pleasure, pain, and delusion, of inferior, middling, and superior quality — is tenable, the distinction [in awakening] is justified. But in the mere aggregate, since the distinction of connections and fruits of action is untenable, the distinction [in awakening] is not justified.

children.text:
tathā śabdādipaṭumāndyādikṛtaśca /
asti cāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ-yasmātsparśamātreṇāpratibudhyamānaṃ puruṣaṃ suptaṃ pāṇinā āpeṣamāpiṣyāpiṣya bodhayāñcakārājātaśatruḥ /
tasmādya āpeṣaṇena pratibubudhe jvalanniva sphuranniva kutaścidāgata iva piṇḍaṃ ca pūrvaviparītaṃ bodhaceṣṭākāraviśeṣādimattvenāpādayan, so 'nyo 'sti gārgyābhimatabrahmabhyo vyatirikta iti siddham /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, [this distinction is justified] because of the acuteness and dullness of the capacity for [perceiving] sound and the like. And this distinction exists — because <s>Ajātaśatru</s> pressed the sleeping man with the hand — pressing and pressing repeatedly — and awakened him. The person who did not respond to mere touch [i.e. to the address of names]. Therefore, the one who was awakened by pressing — appearing as if blazing, as if flashing, as if having arrived from somewhere, and producing [the appearance of] a body having the opposite condition to the previous [sleep], with the specific characteristics of the gestures of awakening — that one is different, distinct from the <s>Brahman</s> intended by <s>Gārgya</s> — this is established.

children.text:
saṃhatatvācca pārārthyopapattiḥ prāṇasya /
gṛhasya stambhādivaccharīrasya antarupaṣṭambhakaḥ prāṇaḥ śarīrādibhiḥ saṃhata ityavocāma /
aranemivacca, nābhisthānīya etasminsarvamiti ca /
tasmād gṛhādivatsvāvayavasamudāyajātīyavyatiriktārthaṃsaṃhanyataityevamagacchāma /
children.translated_text: And from the fact of being composite, the subservience of <s>prāṇa</s> [to another purpose] is tenable. Just as pillars and the like support a house, <s>prāṇa</s> supports the body from within and is composite — joined with the body and other [elements] — we have said. And like a wheel-hub, this [<s>prāṇa</s>] is in the position of the nave, and in it everything [is fastened]. Therefore, just as a house and the like is put together for the sake of something distinct from its own constituent aggregate — so we have concluded.

children.text: stambhakuḍyatṛṇakāṣṭhādigṛhāvayavānāṃ svātmajanmopacayāpacaya-vināśanāmā-kṛtikārya-dharma- nirapekṣalabdha - sattāditadviṣaya-draṣṭṛ-śrotṛ-mantṛvijñātrarthatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā manyāmahe, tatsaṅghātasya ca - tathā prāṇādyava yavānāṃ tatsaṅghātasya ca svātma -janmopacayā -pacaya -vināśanāmākṛti -kāryadharma -nirapekṣalabdhasattāditadviṣayadraṣṭṛśrotṛmantṛvijñātrarthatvaṃ bhavitumarhatīti /
children.translated_text: Having observed that the components of a house — pillars, walls, grass, wood, and so forth — exist for the sake of a seer, hearer, thinker, and knower whose existence is ascertained independently, without regard to the properties of birth, growth, decay, destruction, name, form, function, and effects pertaining to those components themselves — we consider [that it is the same] for the aggregate of those [components as well]. Similarly, the components such as <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, and their aggregate too, should exist for the sake of a seer, hearer, thinker, and knower whose existence is ascertained independently, without regard to the properties of birth, growth, decay, destruction, name, form, function, and effects pertaining to those components themselves.

children.text:
devatācetanāvattve samatvādguṇabhāvānupagama iti cet-prāṇasya viśiṣṭairnāmabhirāmantraṇadarśanāccetanāvattvamabhyupagatam /
cetanāvattve ca pārārthyopagamaḥ samatvādanupapanna iti cet?
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If the deity [<s>prāṇa</s>] too possesses consciousness, then because of equality [with the Self], the acceptance of a subordinate-principal relationship is untenable. [Response:] The consciousness of <s>prāṇa</s> has been accepted because we see it being addressed with specific names. [Objection:] And if it possesses consciousness, the acceptance of its subservience is untenable because of [its] equality [with the Self]?

children.text:
na;nirupādhikasya kevalasya vijijñāpayiṣitatvāt /
kriyākārakaphalātmakatā hyātmano nāmarūpopādhijanitā avidyādhyāropitā /
tannimitto lokasya kriyākārakaphalābhimānalakṣaṇaḥ saṃsāraḥ /
sa nirupādhikātmasvarūpavidyayā nivartayitavya iti tatsvarūpavijijñāpayiṣayopaniṣadārambhaḥ"brahma te bravāṇi" "naitāvatā viditaṃ bhavati"iti copakramya"etāvadarekhalvamṛtatvam"iti copasaṃhārāt /
na cāto 'nyadantarāle vivakṣitamuktaṃ vāsti /
tasmādanavasaraḥ samatvād guṇabhāvānupagama iti codyasya /
children.translated_text: No — because it is the unconditioned, pure [Self] alone that is intended to be made known. For the nature of the Self as consisting of action, agent, and result is generated by the limiting adjuncts of name and form, superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). <s>Saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), characterized by the self-identification with action, agent, and result, is caused by that [superimposition]. That [<s>saṃsāra</s>] is to be removed through the knowledge of the unconditioned nature of the Self — for this purpose the <s>Upaniṣad</s> is commenced, with the intention of making known that nature. [This is clear] from the opening statement 'I shall tell you <s>Brahman</s>' and 'This much is not known,' and from the conclusion 'This much alone is immortality.' And there is nothing else intended or stated in between. Therefore, there is no occasion for the objection 'because of equality, the subordinate-principal relationship is not accepted.'

children.text: viśeṣavato hi sopādhikasya saṃvyavahārārtho guṇaguṇibhāvaḥ, na viparītasya /
children.translated_text: For the subordinate-principal relationship has a practical, transactional purpose for the conditioned [self] that possesses distinctions — not for its opposite [the unconditioned Self].

children.text: nirūpākhyo hi vijijñāpayiṣitaḥ sarvasyāmupaniṣadi /
children.translated_text: For what is intended to be made known in the entire <s>Upaniṣad</s> is that which is without designation.

children.text: "sa eṣa neti neti"ityupasaṃhārāt /
children.translated_text: Because of the conclusion: 'He is "not this, not this"' (BṛUp 2.3.6).

children.text: tasmādādityādibrahmabhya etebhyo 'vijñānamayebhyo vilakṣaṇo 'nyo 'sti vijñānamaya ityetatsiddham //15//
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that there exists [an entity] consisting of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), different from and distinct from these — from <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) and the rest, from <s>Brahmā</s> — who are not [purely] consisting of consciousness. (15)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.16
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.1.16]

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- yatraiṣa etat supto 'bhūd ya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ kvaiṣa tadābhūt kuta etad āgād iti |
tad u ha na mene gārgyaḥ || BrhUp_2,1.16 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'When this person who consists of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) was thus asleep — where was he then? From where did he come?' <s>Gārgya</s> could not answer this. (BṛUp 2.1.16)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.16
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.16:]

children.text:
sa evamajātaśatrurvyatiriktātmastitvaṃ pratipādya gārgyamuvācayatra yasminkāle eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣa etatsvapanaṃ supto 'bhūtprakpāṇipeṣapratibodhāt; vijñānaṃ vijñāyate 'nenetyantaḥ karaṇaṃ buddhirucyate, tanmayastatprāyo vijñānamayaḥ /
kiṃ punastatprāyatvam? tasminnupalabhyatvaṃ tena copalabhyatvamupalabdhṛtvaṃ ca; kathaṃ punarmayaṭo 'nekārthatve prāyārthataivāvagamyate? "sa vā ayamātmā brahma vijñānamayo manomayaḥ"ityevamādau prāyārtha eva prayogadarśanāt, paravijñānavikāratvasyāprasiddhatvāt,"ya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ"iti ca prasiddhavadanuvādād avayavopamārthayoścātrāsambhavāt pāriśeṣyātprāyārthataiva /
tasmātsaṅgalpavikalpādyātmakamantaḥkaraṇaṃ tanmaya ityetat /
puruṣaḥ puri śayanāt /

kvaiṣa tadābhūditi praśnaḥ svabhāvavijñāpayiṣayā-prākpratibodhātkriyākārakaphalaviparītasvabhāva ātmeti kāryābhāvena didarśayiṣitam;na hi prākpratibodhātkarmādikāryaṃ sukhādi kiñcana gṛhyate;na hi prākpratibodhātkarmādikāryaṃ sukhādi kiñcana gṛhyate;tasmādakarmaprayuktatvāttathāsvābhāvyamevātmano 'vagamyate-yasminsvābhāvye 'bhūt, yataśca svābhāvyātpracyutaḥ saṃsārī svabhāvavilakṣaṇa iti- etadvivakṣayā pṛcchati gārgyaṃ pratibhānarahitaṃ buddhivyutpādanāya /
children.translated_text: The question 'Where was he then?' is asked with the intention of making known his true nature — that before awakening, his nature is the opposite of action, agent, and result, as indicated by the absence of effects. For before awakening, no effect of <s>karma</s> and the like — pleasure and so forth — is apprehended; therefore, from the absence of the effects produced by <s>karma</s>, the natural state of the Self, which is free from action, is understood. [The questions] 'Where was he [during sleep]?' and 'From where did he come [at waking]?' — [<s>Ajātaśatru</s>] asks with the intention of elucidating this, for the instruction of <s>Gārgya</s> who was devoid of insight.

children.text: kvaiṣa tadābhūt? kuta etadāgāt? ityetadubhayaṃ gārgyeṇaiva praṣṭavyamāsīt, tathāpi gārgyeṇa na pṛṣṭamiti nodāste ajātaśatruḥ, bodhayitavya eveti pravartate /
children.translated_text: 'Where was he then? From where did he come?' — both these questions should have been asked by <s>Gārgya</s> himself. Nevertheless, since <s>Gārgya</s> did not ask, <s>Ajātaśatru</s> does not hesitate — [thinking] 'he must be taught,' he proceeds.

children.text: jñapayiṣyāmyeveti pratijñātatvāt /
children.translated_text: Because he had promised: 'I shall make you know.'

children.text: evamasau vyutpādyamāno 'pi gārgyo yatraiṣa ātmābhūtprākpratibodhād yataścaitadāgamanamāgāt tadubhayaṃ na vyutpede vaktuṃ vā praṣṭuṃ vā gārgyo ha na mene na jñātavān //16//
children.translated_text: Thus being instructed, <s>Gārgya</s> could not discern either [answer] — where this Self was before awakening, or from where it came — nor could he speak about it or ask about it. <s>Gārgya</s> could not answer, could not understand. (16)

That <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, having thus demonstrated the existence of a Self distinct [from the conditioned self], said to <s>Gārgya</s>: 'When this person who consists of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) was asleep — before the awakening [signaled by] the slapping of the hand — where was he then?' <s>Vijñāna</s> (consciousness) — that by which one cognizes — refers to the internal organ, the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>). '<s>Vijñānamaya</s>' means predominantly consisting of that. What then is the meaning of 'predominantly'? It means being perceived in it, being perceived by it, and being the perceiver. But how, when the suffix '<s>-maya</s>' has multiple meanings, is the meaning 'predominantly' understood? Because in passages like 'This Self is <s>Brahman</s>, consisting of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), consisting of mind (<s>manomaya</s>)' (BṛUp 2.5.19), the usage in the sense of 'predominantly' is observed; and because a transformation from the supreme consciousness is not well-known; and because in 'this person who consists of consciousness' the reference is to something well-known [the individual self], as if restating [a known fact]; and because the meanings of 'component' and 'comparison' are not possible here — by elimination, the sense of 'predominantly' alone [is intended]. Therefore, the internal organ, consisting of intention (<s>saṃkalpa</s>), deliberation (<s>vikalpa</s>), and the like — that is what '<s>vijñānamaya</s>' means. '<s>Puruṣa</s>' — because [it] rests in the city [of the body] (<s>puri śayanāt</s>).

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.17
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.1.17]

children.text:
sa hovācājātaśatruḥ -- yatraiṣa etat supto 'bhūd ya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣas tad eṣāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānena vijnānam ādāya ya eṣo 'ntar hṛdaya ākāśas tasmiñ chete |
tāni yadā gṛhṇāti |
atha haitat puruṣaḥ svapiti nāma |
tad gṛhīta eva prāṇo bhavati |
gṛhītā vāg |
gṛhītaṃ cakṣur |
gṛhītaṃ śrotram |
gṛhītaṃ manaḥ || BrhUp_2,1.17 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> said: 'When this person who consists of consciousness was asleep — then this consciousness-person, having absorbed the consciousness of these <s>prāṇas</s> (sense-faculties) by means of [his own] consciousness, rests in the space within the heart. When he seizes them, then this person is said to be sleeping (<s>svapiti</s>). Then the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) is seized; speech is seized; the eye is seized; the ear is seized; the mind is seized.' (BṛUp 2.1.17)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.17
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.17:]

children.text: sa hovācājātaśatrurvivakṣitārthasamarpaṇāya-yatraiṣa etatsupto 'bhūdya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ etatsupto 'bhūdya eṣa vijñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ kvaiṣa tadābhūt? kuta etadāgāt? iti yadapṛcchāma, tacchṛṇūcyamānam-yatraiṣa etat supto 'bhūttattadātasminkāle eṣāṃ vāgādīnāṃ prāṇānāṃ vijñānenāntaḥkaraṇagatābhivyaktiviśeṣavijñānena upādhisvabhāvajanitena ādāya vijñānaṃ vāgādīnāṃ svasvaviṣayagatasāmarthyaṃ gṛhītvā, ya eṣo 'ntarmadhye hṛdaye hṛdayasyākāśaḥ, ya ākāśaśabdena para eva sva ātmocyate, tasminsve ātmanyākāśe śete svābhāvike 'sāṃsārike /
children.translated_text: <s>Ajātaśatru</s> spoke, for the purpose of conveying the intended meaning: 'When this person who consists of consciousness was asleep — regarding the question we asked: "Where was he then? From where did he come?" — hear the answer being stated. When this person was asleep, at that time, having absorbed — having taken — the consciousness of these <s>prāṇas</s> of speech and the rest — the specific manifested consciousness belonging to the internal organ, born from the nature of the limiting adjuncts — having seized the capacity of speech and the rest pertaining to their respective objects, [he rests] in the space within the heart — the space that is in the middle of the heart. That which is referred to by the word 'space' is the supreme Self itself, one's own Self. In that, in one's own Self, the space [of the heart], he rests — in the natural, non-transmigrating [state].

children.text:
na kevala ākāśa eva, śrutyantarasāmarthyāt-"satā somya tadā sampanno bhavati"iti /
liṅgopādhisambandhakṛtaṃ viśeṣātmasvarūpamutsṛjya aviśeṣe svābhāvike ātmanyeva kevale vartata ityabhiprāyaḥ
children.translated_text: Not in mere space alone — from the force of another <s>śruti</s>: 'He then becomes merged with Being (<s>Sat</s>), dear one' (ChāUp 6.8.1). The meaning is: having abandoned the specific self-form created by the connection with the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) and its limiting adjuncts, [the self] abides in the natural Self alone, the unconditioned, pure [Self].

children.text:
yadā śarīrendriyādhyakṣatāmutsṛjati, tadāsau svātmani vartata iti kathamavagamyate? nāmaprasiddhyā /
kāsau nāmaprasiddhiḥ? ityāha-tāni vāgādervijñānāni yadā yasminkāle gṛhṇātyādatte atha tadā haitatpuruṣaḥ svapiti
children.translated_text: When he relinquishes the superintendence over the body and sense-organs, how is it known that he then abides in his own Self? Through the well-known designation (<s>nāmaprasiddhi</s>). What is that well-known designation? This is stated: when at whatever time he seizes, takes up, the consciousnesses of speech and the rest — then this person is said to be 'sleeping' (<s>svapiti</s>).

children.text:
nāma-etannāmāsya puruṣasya tadā prasiddhaṃ bhavati /
gauṇamevāsya nāma bhavati /
svamevātmānamapītyapigacchatīti svapitītyucyate /
children.translated_text: This is the well-known designation of this person at that time. It is indeed a secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>) name. He goes to, approaches his own Self (<s>svam apīti</s>) — therefore he is said to 'sleep' (<s>svapiti</s>).

children.text: satyaṃ svapitītināmaprasiddhyā ātmanaḥ saṃsāradharmavilakṣaṇaṃ rūpamavagamyate, na tvatra yuktirastītyāśaṅkyāha-tatttra svāpakāle gṛhīta eva prāṇo bhavati /
prāṇa iti ghrāṇendriyam, vāgādiprakaraṇāt;vāgādisambandhe hi sati sadupādhitvādasya saṃsāradharmitvaṃ lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s>' here refers to the olfactory organ, because of the context of speech and the rest. For when there is connection with speech and the rest, the conditioning makes this [Self] appear to have the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: vāgādayaścopasaṃhṛtā eva tadā tena /
children.translated_text: And speech and the rest are indeed withdrawn at that time by him.

children.text: katham? gṛhītā vāggṛhītaṃ cakṣurgṛhītaṃ śrotraṃ gṛhītaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: How? Speech is seized; the eye is seized; the ear is seized; the mind is seized.

children.text: tasmādupasaṃhṛteṣu vāgādiṣu kriyākārakaphalātmatābhāvātsvātmastha evātmābhavatītyavagamyate //17//
children.translated_text: Therefore, when speech and the rest are withdrawn, because of the absence of the nature of action, agent, and result, it is understood that the Self abides in itself alone. (17)

True, through the well-known designation '<s>svapiti</s>' (he sleeps), the nature of the Self as distinct from the properties of <s>saṃsāra</s> is understood. But lest one suspect there is no reasoning to support this, [the text] says: at the time of falling asleep, the <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed seized.

children.text:
nanu darśanalakṣaṇāyāṃ svapnāvasthāyāṃ kāryakaraṇaviyoge 'pi saṃsāradharmitvamasya dṛśyate /
yathā ca jāgarite sukhī duḥkhī bandhuviyuktaḥ śocati muhyate ta;tasmācchokamohadharmavānevāyam /
nāsya śokamohādāyaḥ sukhaduḥkhādayaśca kāryakaraṇasaṃyogajanitabhrāntyādhyāropitā iti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But in the dream state, characterized by [internal] perception, even when there is separation from the body and organs, the property of being in <s>saṃsāra</s> is observed for this [Self]. Just as in waking, one is happy, miserable, separated from loved ones, and grieves and is deluded — therefore, this [Self] indeed possesses the properties of grief, delusion, and the like. [One should not say] that its grief, delusion, and pleasures and pains are superimposed through the error born of the conjunction with the body and organs.

children.text: na mṛṣātvāt /
children.translated_text: No — because [the dream states] are false.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.18
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.1.18]

children.text:
sa yatraitat svapnyayā carati te hāsya lokāḥ |
tad uteva mahārājo bhavaty uteva mahābrāhmaṇaḥ |
utevoccāvacaṃ nigacchati |
sa yathā mahārājo jānapadān gṛhītvā sve janapade yathākāmaṃ parivartetaivam evaiṣa etat prāṇān gṛhītvā sve śarīre yathākāmaṃ parivartate || BrhUp_2,1.18 ||
children.translated_text: When he moves about in dream by means of dream [perception] — those are his worlds. He becomes, as it were, a great king; he becomes, as it were, a great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; he enters, as it were, into high and low [states]. Just as a great king, having taken his people, moves about as he pleases in his own domain — even so this person, having taken the <s>prāṇas</s> (sense-faculties), moves about as he pleases in his own body. (BṛUp 2.1.18)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.18
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.1.18:]

children.text:
sa prakṛta ātmā yatra yasminkāle darśanalakṣaṇayā svapnyayā svapnavṛttyā carati vartate tadā te hāsya lokāḥ karmaphalāni /
ke te? tattatrotāpi mahārāja iva bhavati /
so 'yaṃ mahārājatvamivāsya lokaḥ, na mahārājatvameva jāgarita iva /
tathā mahābrāhmaṇa iva, utāpyuccāvacamuccaṃ ca devatvādyavacaṃ ca tiryaktvādi, uccamivāvacamiva ca nigacchati /
mṛṣaiva mahārājatvādayo 'sya lokāḥ, ivaśabdaprayogādvyabhicāradarśanācca /
tasmānna bandhuviyogādijanitaśokamohādibhiḥ svapne sambadhyata eva /
children.translated_text: He — the Self under discussion — when (<s>yatra</s>), at whatever time, he moves about, roams, through the dream activity characterized by [internal] perception — then those are his worlds, the fruits of <s>karma</s>. What are they? Then, as it were, he becomes a great king. This great-kingship, as it were, is his world — not actual great-kingship as in waking. Similarly, as it were, a great <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; and he enters, as it were, into high and low — the high being godhood and the like, the low being animal-birth and the like — as if high, as if low, he enters. The great-kingship and the rest are merely false worlds for him — because of the use of the word 'as it were' (<s>iva</s>) and because deviation [from waking reality] is observed. Therefore, he is not truly connected with grief, delusion, and the like that arise from separation from loved ones in dreams.

children.text: nanu ca yathā jāgarite jāgratkālāvyabhicāriṇo lokāḥ, evaṃ svapne 'pi te 'sya mahārājatvādayo lokāḥ svapnakālabhāvinaḥ svapnakālāvyabhicāriṇa ātmabhūtā eva, na tvavidyādhyāropitā iti /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But just as in waking, the worlds are invariable throughout the waking period, so too in dreams, the great-kingship and the like are his worlds — existing during the dream period, invariable during the dream period, being of the nature of the Self — and they are not superimposed through <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text:
nanu ca jāgratkāryakaraṇātmatvaṃ devatātmatvaṃ cāvidyādhyāropitaṃ na paramārthata iti vyatiriktavijñānamayātmapradarśanena pradarśitam /
tatkathaṃ dṛṣṭāntatvena svapnalokasya mṛta ivojjīviṣyanprādurbhaviṣyati? satyam, vijñānamaye vyatirikte kāryakaraṇadevatātmatvapradarśanam avidyādhyāropitam-śuktikāyāmiva rajatatvadarśanam-ityetatsiddhyati vyatiriktātmāstitvapradarśananyāyenaiva, na tu tadviśuddhiparatayaiva nyāya uktaḥ;ityasannapi dṛṣṭānto jāgratkāryakaraṇadevatātmatvadarśanalakṣaṇaḥ punarudbhāvyate /
sarvo hi nyāyaḥ kiñcidviśeṣamapekṣamāṇo 'punaruktibhavati /
children.translated_text: [Response:] But the identity with the body-and-organs and with the deities in the waking state was shown to be superimposed through <s>avidyā</s>, not ultimately real — through the demonstration of the distinct <s>vijñānamaya</s> Self. So how can the dream-world serve as an illustration [for the waking world being real], like a dead man who is about to be revived and will reappear? True — through the demonstration of the distinct <s>vijñānamaya</s>, it is established that the perception of identity with the body-and-organs and deities in waking is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> — like the perception of silver in a mother-of-pearl. This is established by the very reasoning that demonstrates the existence of a distinct Self. But the reasoning was not stated solely for the purpose of [demonstrating] its purity. Therefore, although the illustration [of waking as analogy for dreams] is not [ultimately] valid, the illustration characterized by the perception of identity with the body-and-organs and deities in waking is brought up again. For every line of reasoning, when it serves a different specific purpose, avoids being a mere repetition.

children.text:
na tāvatsvapne 'nubhūtamahārājatvādayo lokā ātmabhūtāḥ;ātmano 'nyasya jāgratprativimbabhūtasya lokasya darśanāt /
mahārāja eva tāvadvyastasuptāsu prakṛtiṣu paryaṅke śayānaḥ svapnānpaśyannupasaṃhṛtakaraṇaḥ punarupagataprakṛtiṃ mabārājamivātmānaṃ jāgarita iva paśyati yātrāgataṃ bhuñjānamiva ca bhogān /
na ca tasya mabārājasya paryaṅke śayanād dvitīyo 'nyaḥ prakṛtyupeto viṣaye paryaṭannahani loke prasiddho 'sti, yamasau suptaḥ paśyati /
na copasaṃhṛtakaraṇasya rūpādimato darśanamupapadyate /
na ca dehe dehāntarasya tattulyasya sambhavo 'sti, dehasthasyaiva hi svapnadarśanam /
children.translated_text: Firstly, the great-kingship and the like experienced in dreams are not of the nature of the Self. Because in dreams, one sees another world — a reflection of the waking [experience]. For example, a great king himself, when his attendants are asleep and his senses are withdrawn, lying on his couch, while seeing dreams — sees himself as if a great king who has recovered his attendants, as if in the waking state, going on a journey and enjoying pleasures. But there is no second person — endowed with attendants, wandering about in the field of sense-objects during the day, well-known in the world — whom the sleeping [king] sees. And for one whose sense-organs have been withdrawn, the seeing of forms and the like is not tenable. Nor is the origination of another body, equivalent [to the waking body], within the [same] body possible — for dream-perception belongs to the one situated in [the same] body.

children.text: nanu paryaṅke śayānaḥ pathi pravṛttamātmānaṃ paśyati-na bahiḥ svapnānpaśyatītyetadāha-sa mahārājo jānapadāñjanapade bhavānrājopakaraṇabhūtānbhṛtyānanyāṃśca gṛhītvopādāya sva ātmīya eva jayādinopārjite janapade yathākāmaṃ yo yaḥ kāmo 'sya yathākāmamicchāto yathā parivartetetyarthaḥ;evamevaiṣa vijñānamayaḥ, etaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇam,
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But lying on his couch, he sees himself on the road — does he not see dreams externally? This is what is stated: that great king, having taken the people — the inhabitants of the kingdom, who serve as royal accessories, servants, and others — and having assembled them, moves about in his own domain — acquired through conquest and the like — as he pleases, at his pleasure, according to his desire — this is the meaning. Even so, this <s>vijñānamaya</s> [person] — the word 'this' (<s>etat</s>) qualifies the action [of moving about],

children.text: prāṇāngṛhītvā jāgaritasthānebhya upasaṃhṛtya sve śarīre sva eva dehe na bahiḥ yathākāmaṃ parivartate;kāmakarmabhyāmudbhāsitāḥ pūrvānubhūtavastusadṛśīrvāsanā anubhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having seized the <s>prāṇas</s> — having withdrawn them from their waking stations — in his own body, in his own body alone and not externally, he moves about as he wishes; the meaning is: he experiences latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) that resemble previously experienced objects, illuminated by desire and <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tasmātsvapne mṛṣādhyāropitā evātmabhūtatvena lokā avidyamānā eva santaḥ, tathā jāgarite 'pi, iti pratyetavyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in dream, the worlds are merely falsely superimposed as being the self — they are indeed non-existent; so too in waking, it should be understood.

children.text: tasmādviśuddho 'kriyākārakaphalātmako vijñānamaya ityetatsiddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that [the self] is pure — not of the nature of action, instruments, and fruit — and is constituted of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>).

children.text: yasmād dṛśyante draṣṭurviṣayabhūtāḥ kriyākārakaphalātmakāḥ kāryakaraṇalakṣaṇā lokāḥ, tathā svapne 'pi, tasmādanyo 'sau dṛśyebhyaḥ svapnajāgaritalokebhyo draṣṭā vijñānamayo viśuddhaḥ //18//
children.translated_text: Because the worlds — characterized by the aggregate of body and organs, of the nature of action, instruments, and fruit — are seen as objects of the seer, and likewise in dream too; therefore, the seer is different from the seen worlds of dream and waking — he is constituted of consciousness and is pure. // 18 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.19
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.1.19]

children.text:
darśanavṛttau svapne vāsanārāśerdṛśyatvādataddharmateti viśuddhatāvagatā ātmanaḥ /
tatra yathākāmaṃ parivartata iti kāmavaśātparivartanamuktam /
draṣṭurdṛśyasambandhaścāsya svābhāvika ityaśuddhatā śaṅkyate;atastadviśuddhyarthamāha-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the activity of seeing in dream, because the mass of latent impressions is [merely] the seen, the self does not have the nature of [what is seen] — thus the purity of the self has been established. But there, 'he moves about as he wishes' was stated — [suggesting] movement at the control of desire. And since the seer's connection with the seen might be considered natural, impurity might be suspected. Therefore, to establish purity, [the text] says:

children.text:
atha yadā suṣupto bhavati |
yadā na kasya cana veda |
hitā nāma nādyo dvāsaptatiḥ sahasrāṇi hṛdayāt purītatam abhipratiṣṭhante |
tābhiḥ pratyavasṛpya purītati śete |
sa yathā kumāro add. vā mahārājo vā mahābrāhmaṇo vātighnīm ānandasya gatvā śayīta |
evam evaiṣa etac chete || BrhUp_2,1.19 ||
children.translated_text: Now when he is in deep sleep — when he does not know of anything whatever — seventy-two thousand channels called <s>Hitā</s> extend from the heart to the pericardium. Through them he slips out and rests in the pericardium. Just as a youth, or a great king, or a great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, having reached the summit of bliss, would rest — just so does this one rest. // BṛhUp 2.1.19 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,1.19
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.1.19:

children.text:
atha yadā suṣupto bhavati-yadā svapnyayā carati, tadāpyayaṃ viśuddha eva /
atha punaryadā hitvā darśanavṛttiṃ svapnaṃ yadā yasminkāle suṣuptaḥ suṣṭhu suptaḥ samprasādaṃ svābhāvyena prasīdati /
kadā suṣupto bhavati? yadā yasminkāle na kasyana na kiñcanetyarthaḥ, veda vijānāti;kasyacana vā śabdādeḥ sambandhi vastvantaraṃ kiñcana na vedetyadhyāhāryam;pūrvaṃ tu nyāyyam, supte tu viśeṣavijñānābhāvasya vivakṣitatvāt /
children.translated_text: 'Now when he is in deep sleep' — when he moves about in the dreaming state, even then he is pure. But again, when — having abandoned the activity of seeing that is dream — at the time when he is deeply asleep, well asleep — he attains <s>samprasāda</s> (perfect serenity) by his own nature. When is he deeply asleep? When — at the time when — 'he does not know of anything whatever' — the meaning is 'nothing at all'; or alternatively, he does not know any other object connected with sound and the like — [this interpretation] requires supplying [additional words]. The former is more appropriate, since what is intended [to be expressed] in deep sleep is the absence of specific cognitions.

children.text:
evaṃ tāvadviśeṣavijñānābhāve suṣupto bhavatītyuktam /
kena punaḥ krameṇa suṣupto bhavati? ityucyate-hitā nāma hitā ityevaṃnāmnyo nāḍyaḥ śirā dehasyānnarasavipariṇāmabhūtāḥ, tāśca dvāsaptatiḥ sahasrāṇi, dve sahasre adhike saptatiśca sahasrāṇi tā dvāsaptatiḥ sahasrāṇi, hṛdayāt-hṛdayaṃ nāma māṃsapiṇḍaḥ-tasmānmāṃsapiṇḍātpuṇḍarīkākārāt, purītataṃ hṛdayapariveṣṭanamācakṣate,
children.translated_text: Thus, it has been stated that one is in deep sleep when there is an absence of specific cognitions. But by what process does one enter deep sleep? This is stated: the channels called <s>Hitā</s> — bearing the name '<s>Hitā</s>' — are the veins of the body, produced from the transformation of the essence of food; and they are seventy-two thousand — two thousand more than seventy thousand, that is seventy-two thousand. From the heart — the heart being a lump of flesh — from that lotus-shaped lump of flesh; [extending] to the <s>purītat</s> — what is called the pericardium, the covering around the heart.

children.text: tadupalakṣitaṃ śarīramiha purītatamabhipratiṣṭhanta iti śarīraṃ kṛtsnaṃ vyāpnuvatyo 'śvatthaparṇarājaya iva bahirmukhyaḥ pravṛttā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That [pericardium] designates the body [as a whole]; the meaning is that [the channels] extend to, i.e. pervade, the entire body, like the veins of an <s>aśvattha</s> (fig) leaf, spreading outward.

children.text:
tatra buddherantaḥkaraṇasya hṛdayaṃ sthānam, tatrasthabuddhitantrāṇi cetarāṇi bāhyāni karaṇāni /
tena buddhiḥ karmavaśācchrotrādīni tābhirnāḍībhirmatsyajālavatkarṇaśaṣkulyādisthānebhyaḥ prasārayati, prasāryacādhitiṣṭhati jāgaritakāle /
tāṃ vijñānamayo 'bhivyaktasvātmacaitanyāvabhāsatayā vyāpnoti /
saṅkocanakāle ca tasyā anusaṅkucita;so 'sya vijñānamayasya svāpaḥ;jāgradvikāsānubhavo bhogaḥ;buddhyupādhisvabhāvānuvidhāyī hi saḥ, candrādipratibimba iva jalādyanuvidhāyī /
tasmāttasyā buddherjāgradviṣayāyāstābhirnāḍībhiḥ pratyavasarpaṇamanu pratyavasṛpya purītati śarīre śete tiṣṭhati, taptamiva lohapiṇḍamaviśeṣeṇa saṃvyāpyāgnivaccharīraṃ saṃvyāpya vartata ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, the heart is the seat of the <s>buddhi</s> (intellect), the internal organ. The other external organs are dependent on the intellect stationed there. Thus, the intellect, under the control of <s>karma</s>, extends the organs of hearing and the rest through those channels, like a fishing net, from the positions of the ear-cavities and the like, and having extended them, presides [over them] during the waking state. The one constituted of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) pervades that [intellect] by manifesting the light of his own consciousness. And when that [intellect] contracts, he contracts correspondingly — that is his sleep; the experience of the expansion during waking is his enjoyment. For he follows the nature of the limiting adjunct (<s>upādhi</s>) that is the intellect, just as the reflection of the moon and the like follows [the movement of] water and the like. Therefore, as the intellect, which pertains to waking objects, creeps back through those channels, [the self] correspondingly creeps back — 'having crept back, he rests in the pericardium, in the body' — the meaning is: like a heated lump of iron, he pervades the body without distinction, abiding like fire pervading [an iron ball].

children.text:
svābhāvika eva svātmani vartamāno 'pi karmānugatabuddhyanuvṛttitvātpurītati śeta ityucyate /
na hi suṣiptikāle śarīrasambandho 'sti /
"tīrṇo hi tadā sarvāñchokānhṛdayasya"iti hi vakṣyati /
children.translated_text: Though abiding in his own essential nature by nature, it is said that he rests in the pericardium because of his following the intellect, which is governed by <s>karma</s>. For in the state of deep sleep, there is no connection with the body. As [the text] will say: 'Then he has crossed beyond all the sorrows of the heart.'

children.text: sarvasaṃsāraduḥkhaviyuktā iyamavasthetyatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ-sa yathā kumāro vā atyantabālo vā, mahārājo vātyantavaśyaprakṛtiryathoktakṛt, mahābrāhmaṇo vā atyantaparipakvavidyāvinayasampannaḥ, atighnīm-atiśayena duḥkhaṃ hantītyatighnī ānandasyāvasthā sukhāvasthā tāṃ prāpya gatvā, śayītāvatiṣṭheta /
children.translated_text: This state is free from all <s>saṃsāric</s> suffering — to illustrate this, an example is given: just as a youth — an extremely young child — or a great king, one whose subjects are fully under his control and who acts as prescribed, or a great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, one endowed with fully ripened knowledge and discipline — having reached <s>atighnī</s> — a state that supremely destroys suffering, i.e., a state of bliss — the state of happiness, having attained it, would rest, would repose.

children.text:
eṣāṃ ca kumārādīnāṃ svabhāvasthānāṃ sukaṃ niratiśyaṃ prasiddhaṃ loke, vikriyamāṇānāṃ hi teṣāṃ duḥkhaṃ na svabhāvataḥ;tena teṣāṃ svābhāvikyavasthā dṛṣṭāntatvenopādīyate prasiddhatvāt /
na teṣāṃ svāpa evābhipretaḥ, svāpasya dārṣṭāntikatvena vivakṣitatvādviśeṣābhāvācca /
viśeṣe hi sati dṛṣṭāntadārṣṭāntikabhedaḥ syāt;tasmānna teṣāṃ svāpo dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
children.translated_text: The unsurpassed happiness of these — youth, king, and the rest — in their natural states is well known in the world. For their suffering occurs when they are disturbed, not by nature. Therefore, their natural state is used as an illustration because of its familiarity. Their sleep itself is not what is intended [as the illustration], since sleep is what is being illustrated, and there would be no distinction [between illustration and illustrated]. For if there were specificity [in their sleep], there would be a difference between example and exemplified; therefore, their sleep is not the example.

children.text: evameva yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ, eṣa vijñānamaya etacchayanaṃ śete iti, etacchabdaḥ kriyāviśeṣaṇārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as this example [of the youth, king, and Brāhmaṇa in their natural happiness] — so this one constituted of consciousness rests in this manner — the word 'this' (<s>etat</s>) qualifies the action.

children.text: evamayaṃ svābhāvike sve ātmani sarvasaṃsāradharmātīto vartate svāpakāla iti //19//
children.translated_text: Thus, this [self] abides in its natural, own self, transcending all the attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>, during the state of sleep. // 19 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,1.20
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.1.20]

children.text:
kvaiṣa tadābhūdityasya praśnasya prativacanamuktam /
anena ca praśnanirṇayena vijñānamayasya svabhāvato viśuddhirasaṃsāritvaṃ coktam /
kuta etadāgāt? ityasya praśnasyāpākaraṇārtha ārambhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The answer to the question 'Where was this one then?' has been given. And by the resolution of this question, the natural purity and non-transmigrating nature of the one constituted of consciousness has been stated. The commencement [of the next section] is for the purpose of resolving the question 'From where did this come?'

children.text:
nanu yasmingrāme nagare vā yo bhavati so 'nyatra gacchaṃstata eva grāmānnagarādvā gacchati nānyataḥ /
tathā sati kvaiṣa tadābhūdityetāvānevāstu praśnaḥ /
yatrābhūttata evāganamaṃ prasiddhaṃ syānnānyata iti kuta etadāgāditi praśno nirarthaka eva /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] When a person is in a certain village or city and goes elsewhere, he goes from that very village or city, not from anywhere else. This being so, 'Where was this one then?' — let the question be just this much. Since it is well known that one comes from where one was, and not from elsewhere — the question 'From where did this come?' would be purposeless.

children.text:
kiṃ śrutirupālabhyate bhavatā? na /
kiṃ tarhi? dvitīyasya praśnasyārthāntaraṃ śrotumicchāmyata ānarthakyaṃ codayāmi /
children.translated_text: Is the <s>śruti</s> being faulted by you? No. Then what? I wish to hear a different meaning for the second question, and therefore I raise the objection of purposelessness.

children.text:
evaṃ tarhi kuta ityapādānārthatā na gṛhyate;apādānārthatve hi punaruktatā, nānyārthatve /
astu tarhi nimittārthaḥ praśnaḥ-kuta etadāgāt-kinnimittamihāgamanam? iti /
children.translated_text: In that case, the word '<s>kuta</s>' (from where) is not taken in the sense of ablative (source); for if taken in the ablative sense, there would be redundancy, but not if taken in a different sense. Let the question then be in the sense of cause: 'From where did this come?' — meaning 'What is the cause of its coming here?'

children.text:
na nimittārthatāpi, prativacanavairūpyāt /
ātmanaśca sarvasya jagato 'gnivisphuliṅgādivadutpattiḥ prativacane śrūyate /
na hi visphuliṅgānāṃ vidravaṇe 'gnirnimittamapādānameva tu saḥ /
tathā paramātmā vijñānamayasyātmano 'pādānatvena śrūyate"asmādātmanaḥ"ityetasminvākye /
tasmātprativacanavailomyātkuta iti praśnasya nimittārthatā na śakyate varṇayitum /
children.translated_text: Nor can it be in the sense of cause, because the answer would then be inconsistent. For in the answer, the origination of the self and the entire world from [<s>Ātman</s>], like sparks from fire, is heard. And sparks do not scatter from fire due to fire being a cause [in the sense of purpose] — rather, fire is [their] material source (<s>upādāna</s>). Similarly, the Supreme Self is heard as the material source of the <s>vijñānamaya</s> self in the sentence 'from this self.' Therefore, because of the inconsistency of the answer, the question '<s>kuta</s>' cannot be interpreted in the sense of cause.
