And from the <s>mantra</s> passages that reveal [<s>Brahman</s>'s] possession of contradictory attributes: 'It moves; it moves not. It is far; it is near' (ĪśUp 5) and the like.

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye dvitīyādhyāye prathamamajātaśatrubrāhmaṇam //1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>Ajātaśatru Brāhmaṇa</s> in the second chapter of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s>. // 1 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,2.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.2.1]

children.text:
'brahma jñapayiṣyāmi'iti prastutam;tatra yato jagajjātaṃ yanmayaṃ yasmiṃśca līyate tadekaṃ brahmeti jñāpitam /
kimātmakaṃ punastajjagajjāyate, līyate ca? pañcabhūtātmakam;bhūtāni ca nāmarūpātmakāni;nāmarūpe satyamiti hyuktam;tasya satyasya pañcabhūtātmakasya satyaṃ brahma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'I shall make you know <s>Brahman</s>' — this was introduced. There, the one <s>Brahman</s> from which the world is born, of which it is constituted, and into which it dissolves — this has been made known. But of what nature is the world that is born and dissolves? It is constituted of the five elements. And the elements have the nature of name and form. Name and form are the true (<s>satya</s>) — as was stated. Of that true [world] constituted of the five elements, <s>Brahman</s> is the truth.

children.text:
kathaṃ punarbhūtāni satyamiti mūrtāmūrtabrāhmaṇam /
mūrtāmūrtabhūtātmakatvātkāryakaraṇātmakāni bhūtāni prāṇā api satyam /
teṣāṃ kāryakaraṇātmakānāṃ bhūtānāṃ satyatvanirdidhārayiṣayā brāhmaṇadvayamārabhyate saivopaniṣadvyākhyā /
kāryakaraṇasatyatvāvadhāraṇadvāreṇa hi satyasya satyaṃ brahmāvadhāryate /
atroktam 'prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣāmeṣa satyam'iti /
tatra ke prāṇāḥ? kiyatyo vā prāṇaviṣayā upaniṣadaḥ? kāḥ? iti ca brahmopaniṣatprasaṅgena karaṇānāṃ prāṇānāṃ svarūpamavadhārayati-pathigatakūpārāmādyavadhāraṇavat /
children.translated_text: But how are the elements 'true'? — this is the topic of the <s>Mūrtāmūrta</s> (formed and formless) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Because the elements consist of formed and formless [aspects], and because the elements, being of the nature of effects and instruments, are also the <s>prāṇas</s> — they too are 'the true.' For the purpose of ascertaining the truth-nature of those elements that are of the nature of effects and instruments, two <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are begun — and that itself is the explanation of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. For through the ascertainment of the truth-nature of effects and instruments, <s>Brahman</s> — the truth of the true — is ascertained. Here it was stated: 'The <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the true; of them, this [self] is the truth.' Now, who are these <s>prāṇas</s>? And how many <s>Upaniṣads</s> pertain to the <s>prāṇas</s>? And what are they? — incidentally, in connection with the <s>Brahman Upaniṣad</s>, the true nature of the <s>prāṇas</s>, the organs, is being ascertained — like ascertaining wells and groves along a path.

children.text:
yo ha vai śiśuṃ sādhānaṃ sapratyādhānaṃ sasthūṇaṃ sadāmaṃ veda sapta ha dviṣato bhrātṛvyān avaruṇaddhi |
ayaṃ vāva śiśur yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ |
tasyedam evādhānam idaṃ pratyādhānaṃ prāṇaḥ sthūṇānnaṃ dāma || BrhUp_2,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: One who knows the child (<s>śiśu</s>) together with its support, its counter-support, its pillar, and its rope — he wards off seven hostile rivals. This indeed is the child — this central <s>prāṇa</s>. This [body] is its support; this [head] is its counter-support; <s>prāṇa</s> [i.e., strength] is its pillar; food is its rope. // BṛhUp 2.2.1 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,2.1
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.2.1:

children.text:
yo ha vai śiśuṃ sādhānaṃ sapratyādhānaṃ sasthūṇaṃ sadāmaṃ veda, tasyedaṃ phalam; kiṃ tat? sapta saptasaṃkhyākān ha dviṣato dveṣakartṝn bhrātṛvyān /
bhrātṛvyā hi dvividhā bhavanti, dviṣanto 'dviṣantaśca, tatra dviṣanto ye bhrātṛvyāstān dviṣato bhrātṛvyānavaruṇaddhi; sapta ye śīrṣaṇyāḥ prāṇā viṣayopalabdhidvārāṇi tatprabhavā viṣayarāgāḥ sahajatvād bhrātṛvyāḥ /
te hyasya svātmasthāṃ dṛṣṭiṃ viṣayaviṣayāṃ kurvanti, tena te dveṣṭāro bhrātṛvyāḥ /
pratyagātmekṣaṇapratiṣedhakaratvāt /
kāṭhake coktam-"parāñci khāni vyatṛṇatsvayambhūstasmātparāṅpaśyati nāntarātman"ityādi /
tatra yaḥ śiśvādīnveda, teṣāṃ yāthātmyamavadhārayati, sa etān bhrātṛvyānavaruṇaddhyapāvṛṇoti vināśayati /
children.translated_text: One who knows the child together with its support, counter-support, pillar, and rope — the fruit of that [knowledge] is this: what is it? He wards off — repels, destroys — seven, i.e. seven in number, hostile, i.e. hate-bearing, rivals (<s>bhrātṛvya</s>). For rivals are of two kinds: those who are hostile and those who are not. Among them, the hostile rivals — he wards off those hostile rivals. The seven are the <s>prāṇas</s> in the head — the doors of perception of sense-objects — and the attachments to sense-objects that arise from them; they are rivals because of being innate. For they make his vision, which is directed toward the inner self, directed toward sense-objects — therefore they are hostile rivals, because they obstruct the vision of the inner self. And in the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> it is stated: 'The self-born pierced the openings outward; therefore one sees outward, not the inner self' and so forth. There, one who knows the child and the rest — who ascertains their true nature — he wards off, removes, destroys these rivals.

children.text:
tasmai phalaśravaṇenābhimukhībhūtāyāha-ayaṃ vāva śiśuḥ /
ko 'sau? yo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇaḥ, śarīramadhye yaḥ prāṇo liṅgātmā, yaḥ pañcadhā śarīramāviṣṭaḥ-bṛhanpāṇḍaravāsaḥ soma rājannityuktaḥ, yasminvāṅmanaḥ prabhṛtīni karaṇāni viṣaktāni-paḍvīśaśaṅkunidarśanāt; sa eṣa śiśuriva, viṣayeṣvitarakaraṇavadapaṭutvāt; śiśuṃ sādhānamityuktam /
kiṃ punastasya śiśorvatsasthānīyasya karaṇātmana ādhānam? tasyedameva śarīramādhānaṃ kāryātmakam-ādhīyate 'sminnityādhānam; tasya hi śiśoḥ prāṇasyedaṃ śarīramadhiṣṭhānam, asminhi karaṇānyadhiṣṭhitāni labdhātmakānyupalabdhidvārāṇi bhavanti, na tu prāṇamātre viṣaktāni /
tathā hi darśitamajātaśatruṇā-upasaṃhṛteṣu karaṇeṣu vijñānamayo nopalabhyate, śarīradeśavyūḍheṣu tu karaṇeṣu vijñānamaya upalabhamāna upalabhyate-tacca darśitaṃ pāṇipeṣapratibodhanena /
idaṃ pratyādhānaṃ śiraḥ; pradeśaviśeṣeṣu-prati pratyādhīyata iti pratyādhānam /
prāṇaḥ sthūṇā annapānajanitāśaktiḥ-prāṇo balamiti paryāyaḥ /
balāvaṣṭambho hi prāṇo 'smiñcharīre-"sa yatrāyamātmābalyaṃ nyetya saṃmohamiva"iti darśanāt /
children.translated_text: To the one who has become attentive upon hearing the fruit, [the text] says: this indeed is the child. Who is that? This central <s>prāṇa</s> — the <s>prāṇa</s> in the middle of the body, the subtle body (<s>liṅgātman</s>), which has entered the body in five ways — described as 'the great, white-robed <s>Soma</s> king' — in which speech, mind, and the other organs are fastened, as demonstrated by the illustration of a tent-peg and rope. This [<s>prāṇa</s>] is like a child, because of its ineptness in [dealing with] sense-objects compared to the other organs. 'The child together with its support' was stated. Now, what is the support of that child, the calf-like entity of the nature of organs? This very body is its support — the body being of the nature of effects — '<s>ādhāna</s>' means that in which [something] is placed; for this body is the abode of that child, <s>prāṇa</s> — in it the organs, having obtained their identity, become the doors of perception — they are not fastened in <s>prāṇa</s> alone. For thus it was demonstrated by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: when the organs are withdrawn, the <s>vijñānamaya</s> [self] is not perceived; but when the organs are deployed in specific bodily locations, the <s>vijñānamaya</s> is perceived as perceiving — and this was demonstrated by the clapping and awakening. The counter-support is the head — [<s>prāṇa</s>] is counter-placed in specific locations. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the pillar — the strength born of food and drink — '<s>prāṇa</s> means strength' is a synonym. For <s>prāṇa</s> is the prop of strength in this body — as seen from [the text]: 'When this self comes to weakness, to a state resembling unconsciousness.'

children.text: yathā vatsaḥ sthūṇāvaṣṭambha evaṃ śarīrapakṣapātī vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ sthūṇeti kecit /
children.translated_text: Just as a calf [is held by] the prop of a pillar, so <s>Vāyu</s>, the <s>prāṇa</s> which tends toward the body, is the pillar — according to some.

children.text: annaṃ dāma-annaṃ hi bhuktaṃ tredhā pariṇamate;ya;sthūlaḥ pariṇāmaḥ, sa etaddvayaṃ bhūtvā imāmapyeti-mūtraṃ ca purīṣaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Food is the rope — for food, when consumed, transforms in three ways: the gross transformation becomes these two — urine and feces — and passes out.

children.text: yo madhyamo rasaḥ sa raso lohitādikrameṇa svakāryaṃ śarīraṃ sāptadhātukamupacinoti;svayonyannāgame hi śarīramupacīyate 'nnamayatvāt;viparyaye 'pakṣīyate patati;yastvaṇiṣṭho rasaḥ-amṛtam ūrkprabhāvaḥ-iti ca kathyate, sa nābherūrdhvaṃ hṛdayadeśamāgatya, hṛdayādviprasṛteṣu dvāsaptatināḍīsahasreṣvanupraviśya yattatkaraṇasaṅghātarūpaṃ liṅgaṃ śiśusañjñakam, tasya śarīre sthitikāraṇaṃ bhavati balamupajanayatsthūṇākhyam;tenānnamubhayataḥ pāśavatsadāmavat prāṇaśarīrayornibandhanaṃ bhavati //1//
children.translated_text: The middle essence — that juice — progressively through the stages of blood and the rest, builds up the body, its own effect, consisting of seven <s>dhātus</s> (tissues). For when food of its own kind arrives, the body is built up, being constituted of food; in its absence, [the body] wastes away and falls. But the subtlest essence — called the immortal, the power of vigor — rising upward from the navel to the region of the heart, entering the seventy-two thousand channels that extend from the heart, reaching the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) in the form of the aggregate of organs called 'the child' — it becomes the cause of its continued existence in the body, generating the strength called 'the pillar.' Thus food serves as a rope binding <s>prāṇa</s> and the body together on both sides. // 1 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,2.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.2.2]

children.text: idānīṃ tasyaiva śiśoḥ pratyādhāna ūḍhasya cakṣuṣi kāścanopaniṣada ucyante-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, certain <s>Upaniṣads</s> (secret doctrines) are stated regarding that very child as placed in the counter-support, i.e., the eye:

children.text:
tam etāḥ saptākṣitaya upatiṣṭhante |
tad yā imā akṣaṃl lohinyo rājayas tābhir enaṃ rudro 'nvāyattaḥ |
atha yā akṣann āpas tābhiḥ parjanyaḥ |
yā kanīnakā tayādityaḥ |
yat kṛṣṇaṃ tenāgnir |
yac chuklaṃ tenendraḥ |
adharayainaṃ vartanyā pṛthivy anvāyattā |
dyaur uttarayā |
nāsyānnaṃ kṣīyate ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_2,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: Seven imperishable [entities] attend upon him. Those red lines in the eye — through them <s>Rudra</s> is connected with him. The water in the eye — through that, <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god). The pupil — through that, <s>Āditya</s> (sun). The dark [part] — through that, <s>Agni</s> (fire). The white [part] — through that, <s>Indra</s>. Through the lower eyelid, the earth is connected with him; through the upper, heaven. One whose food does not diminish — is one who knows this. // BṛhUp 2.2.2 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,2.2
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.2.2:

children.text:
tametāḥ saptākṣitaya upatiṣṭhantetaṃ karaṇātmakaṃ prāmaṃ śarīre 'nnabandhanaṃ cakṣuṣyūḍhametā vakṣyamāṇāḥ sapta saptasaṅkhyākā akṣitayo 'kṣitihetutvādupatiṣṭhante /
yadyapi mantrakaraṇe tiṣṭhatirupapūrva ātmanepadī bhavati, ihāpi sapta devatābhidhānāni mantrasthānīyāni karaṇāni;tiṣṭhaterato 'trāpyātmanepadaṃ na viruddham /
children.translated_text: 'Seven imperishable ones attend upon him' — him, the <s>prāṇa</s> of the nature of the organs, bound to the body by food, placed in the eye — these seven, about to be described, seven in number, imperishable — causes of imperishability — attend upon [him]. Although in the usage of <s>mantras</s>, the verb '<s>tiṣṭhati</s>' with the prefix '<s>upa</s>' takes the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice), here too the seven names of deities serve as [equivalents of] <s>mantras</s> — therefore the <s>ātmanepada</s> is not inconsistent here either.

children.text:
kāstā akṣitayaḥ? ityucyante-tattatra yā imāḥ prasiddhāḥ, akṣannakṣaṇi lohinyo lohitā rājayo rekhāḥ, tābhirdvārabhūtābhirenaṃ madhyamaṃ prāṇaṃ rudro 'nvāyatto 'nugataḥ; atha yā akṣannakṣaṇyāpo dhūmādisaṃyogenābhivyajyamānāḥ, tābhiradbhirdvārabhūtābhiḥ parjanyo devatātmānvāyatto /
ñanugata upatiṣṭhata ityarthaḥ /
sa cānnabhūto 'kṣitiḥ prāṇasya;"parjanye varṣatyānandinaḥ prāṇā bhavanti"iti śrutyantarāt /
children.translated_text: What are those imperishable ones? This is stated: those, the well-known — red lines in the eye — through those, which serve as doors, <s>Rudra</s> is connected with, follows after, the central <s>prāṇa</s>. Then the water in the eye, made manifest through contact with smoke and the like — through that water, which serves as a door, <s>Parjanya</s> as the deity is connected, follows. The meaning is: he attends [upon <s>prāṇa</s>]. And [<s>Parjanya</s>], being in the form of food, is [a cause of] imperishability for <s>prāṇa</s> — from the other <s>śruti</s>: 'When <s>Parjanya</s> rains, the <s>prāṇas</s> rejoice.'

children.text: yā kanīnakā dṛkchaktistayā kanīnakayā dvāreṇādityo madhyamaṃ prāṇamupatiṣṭhate;yatkṛṣṇaṃ cakṣuṣi tenainamagnirupatiṣṭhate;yacchuklaṃ cakṣuṣi tenendraḥ;adharayā vartanyā pakṣmaṇainaṃ pṛthivyanvāyattā, adharatvasāmānyāt;
children.translated_text: The pupil (<s>kanīnakā</s>) — the power of sight — through that pupil, which serves as a door, <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) attends upon the central <s>prāṇa</s>. The dark [part] of the eye — through that, <s>Agni</s> attends upon him. The white [part] of the eye — through that, <s>Indra</s>. Through the lower eyelid, the earth is connected with him — because of the commonality of being lower.

children.text: etāḥ saptānnabhūtāḥ prāṇasya santatamupatiṣṭhante-ityevaṃ yo veda, tasyaitatphalam-nāsyānnaṃ kṣīyate, ya evaṃ veda //2//
children.translated_text: These seven, being in the form of food, constantly attend upon <s>prāṇa</s>. Thus one who knows — for him this is the fruit: his food does not diminish — one who knows this. // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,2.3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.2.3]

children.text:
tad eṣa śloko bhavati --
arvāgbilaś camasa ūrdhvabudhnas tasmin yaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpam |
tasyāsata ṛṣayaḥ sapta tīre vāg aṣṭamī brahmaṇā saṃvidāneti |
arvāgbilaś camasa ūrdhvabudhna iti |
idaṃ tac charīra eṣa hy arvāgbilaś camasa ūrdhvabudhnaḥ |
tasmin yaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpam iti |
prāṇā vai yaśo viśvarūpam |
prāṇān etad āha |
tasyāsata ṛṣayaḥ sapta tīra iti |
prāṇā vā ṛṣayaḥ |
prāṇāṇ etad āha |
vāg aṣṭamī brahmaṇā saṃvidāneti |
vāg ghy aṣṭamī brahmaṇā saṃvitte || BrhUp_2,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: In regard to this, there is this verse: 'A bowl with its opening below, its bottom upward — in it is placed glory of all forms. On its rim sat seven sages; speech, the eighth, is united with <s>Brahman</s>.' 'A bowl with its opening below, its bottom upward' — this [head] is that; for it is the bowl with its opening below and its bottom upward. 'In it is placed glory of all forms' — the <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the glory of all forms; this refers to the <s>prāṇas</s>. 'On its rim sat seven sages' — the <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the sages; this refers to the <s>prāṇas</s>. 'Speech, the eighth, is united with <s>Brahman</s>' — for speech, the eighth, is united with <s>Brahman</s>. // BṛhUp 2.2.3 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,2.3
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.2.3:

children.text:
tattatraitasminnarthe eṣa śloko mantro bhavati-arvāgbilaścamasa ityādiḥ /
tatra mantrārthamācaṣṭe śrutiḥ-arvāgbilaścamasa ityādiḥ /
tatra mantrārthamācaṣṭe śrutiḥ-arvāgbilaścamasa ūrdhvabudhna iti /
kaḥ punarasāvarvāgbilaścamasa ūrdhvabudhnaḥ? idaṃ tat śiraḥ, camasākāraṃ hi tat /
katham? eṣa hyarvāgbilo mukhasya bilarūpatvāt, śiraso budhnākāratvādūrdhvabudhnaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, in this regard, in connection with this meaning, there is this verse, this <s>mantra</s>: 'A bowl with its opening below' and so forth. There, the <s>śruti</s> explains the meaning of the <s>mantra</s>: 'A bowl with its opening below, its bottom upward.' Now, what is this bowl with its opening below and its bottom upward? This is the head — for it is bowl-shaped. How? It has its opening below, because the mouth has the nature of an opening; and its bottom is upward, because the top of the head has the shape of a bottom.

children.text:
tasminyaśo nihitaṃ viśvarūpamiti-yathā somaścamase, evaṃ tasmiñchirasi viśvarūpaṃ nānārūpaṃ nihitaṃ sthitaṃ bhavati /
kiṃ punastad yaśaḥ? prāṇā vai yaśo viśvarūpam-prāṇāḥ śrotrādayo vāyavaśca marutaḥ saptadhā teṣu prasṛtā yaśaḥ-ityetadāha mantraḥ, śabdādijñānahetutvāt /
children.translated_text: 'In it is placed glory of all forms' — just as <s>Soma</s> [is placed] in a cup, so in that head, glory of all forms — of many forms — is placed, established. What then is that glory? 'The <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the glory of all forms' — the <s>prāṇas</s>, the organs such as the ear and the rest, and the <s>Maruts</s> (winds) spread through them in seven ways, are the glory — this is what the <s>mantra</s> says, because they are the cause of the knowledge of sounds and the like.

children.text: tasyāsata ṛṣayaḥ sapta tīra iti-prāṇāḥ parispandātmakāḥ, ta eva ca ṛṣayaḥ, prāṇāvetadāha mantraḥ /
children.translated_text: 'On its rim sat seven sages' — the <s>prāṇas</s>, whose nature is vibration — they are indeed the sages (<s>ṛṣis</s>); this refers to the <s>prāṇas</s>, says the <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: vāgaṣṭamī brahmaṇā saṃvidāneti-brahmaṇā saṃvādaṃ kurvatī aṣṭamī bhavati;taddhetumāha-vāgghyaṣṭamī brahmaṇā saṃvitta iti //3//
children.translated_text: 'Speech, the eighth, is united with <s>Brahman</s>' — being united with, harmonizing with <s>Brahman</s>, [speech] is the eighth. [The text] gives the reason: for speech, the eighth, is united with, conjoined with <s>Brahman</s>. // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,2.4
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.2.4]

children.text: ke punastasya camasasya tīra āsata ṛṣaya iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, who are those sages who sat on the rim of the bowl?

children.text:
imāv eva gotamabharadvājau |
ayam eva gotamo 'yaṃ bharadvājaḥ |
imāv eva viśvāmitrajamadagnī |
ayam eva viśvāmitro 'yaṃ jamadagniḥ |
imāv eva vasiṣṭhakaśyapau |
ayam eva vasiṣṭho 'yaṃ kaśyapaḥ |
vāg evātriḥ |
vācā hy annam adyate |
attir ha vai nāmaitad yad autrir iti |
sarvasyāttā bhavati |
sarvam asyānnaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_2,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: These two are <s>Gotama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s> — this one is <s>Gotama</s>, this one is <s>Bharadvāja</s>. These two are <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s> — this one is <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, this one is <s>Jamadagni</s>. These two are <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> — this one is <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, this one is <s>Kaśyapa</s>. Speech indeed is <s>Atri</s>. For by speech, food is eaten. <s>Atti</s> (eating) indeed is the name of what is called <s>Atri</s>. One who knows this becomes the eater of all; all becomes his food. // BṛhUp 2.2.4 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,2.4
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.2.4:

children.text:
imāveva gotamabharadvājau karṇau-ayameva gotamo 'yaṃ bharadvājo dakṣiṇaścottaraśca, viparyayeṇa vā /
tathā cakṣuṣī upadiśannuvāca-imāveva viśvāmitrajamadagnī dakṣiṇaṃ viśvāmitra uttaraṃ jamadagnirviparyayeṇa vā /
imāveva vasiṣṭhakaśyapau-nāsike upadiśannuvāca;dakṣiṇaḥ puṭo bhavati vasiṣṭhaḥ, uttaraḥ kaśyapaḥ pūrvavat /
vāgevātriḥ, adanakriyāyogātsaptamaḥ;vācā hyannamadyate tasmādattirha vai prasiddhaṃ nāmaitat-attṛtvādattiriti, attireva san yadatrirityucyate parokṣeṇa /
sarvasyaitasyānnajātasya prāṇasyātrinirvacanavijñānādattā bhavati /
attaiva bhavati nāmuṣminnannena punaḥ pratipadyata ityetaduktaṃ bhavati-sarvamasyānnaṃ bhavatīti /
ya evametadyathoktaṃ prāṇayāthātmyaṃ veda, sa evaṃ madhyamaḥ prāṇo bhūtvā
children.translated_text: 'These two are <s>Gotama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>' — the ears. This one is <s>Gotama</s>, this one is <s>Bharadvāja</s> — the right and left, or vice versa. Similarly, indicating the eyes, he said: 'These two are <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>' — the right eye is <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the left is <s>Jamadagni</s>, or vice versa. 'These two are <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s>' — indicating the nostrils, he said: the right nostril is <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the left is <s>Kaśyapa</s>, as before. 'Speech indeed is <s>Atri</s>' — the seventh, because of the connection with the act of eating. For by speech, food is eaten. Therefore '<s>Atti</s>' is indeed the well-known name — from the property of eating, one is called '<s>Atti</s>'; and being <s>Atti</s>, one is called '<s>Atri</s>' indirectly. From the knowledge of the etymology of <s>Atri</s> as related to <s>prāṇa</s>, one becomes the eater of all food of every kind. One becomes the eater alone and is never again reduced to being food — this is what is stated: all becomes his food. One who thus knows this — the true nature of <s>prāṇa</s> as described — he, becoming the central <s>prāṇa</s>,

children.text: ādhānapratyādhānagato bhoktaiva bhavati, na bhojyam, bhojyād vyāvartata ityarthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: situated in the support and counter-support, becomes the enjoyer alone and not the enjoyed — he is distinguished from the enjoyed — this is the meaning. // 4 //

children.text: iti dvitīyam brāhmaṇam //2//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,3.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.3.1]

children.text:
tatra prāṇā vai satyamityuktam /
yāḥ prāṇānāmupaniṣadaḥ, tā brahmopaniṣatprasaṅgena vyākhyātāḥ-ete te prāṇā iti cacha te
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There, it was stated: 'The <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the true.' Those <s>Upaniṣads</s> pertaining to the <s>prāṇas</s> have been explained incidentally in connection with the <s>Brahman Upaniṣad</s> — 'these are those <s>prāṇas</s>.'

children.text: kimātmakāḥ? kathaṃ vā teṣāṃ satyatvam? iti ca vaktavyamiti pañcabhūtānāṃ satyānāṃ kāryakaraṇātmakānāṃ svarūpāvadhāraṇārthamidaṃ brāhmaṇamārabhyate-yadupādhiviśeṣāpanayadvāreṇa 'neti neti'iti brahmaṇaḥ satattvaṃ nirdidhārayiṣitam /
children.translated_text: But of what nature are they? And how is their truth-nature [established]? Since these must still be stated, this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is begun for the purpose of ascertaining the essential nature of the five elements, which are the true, of the nature of effects and instruments — through which, by the removal of specific limiting adjuncts, the real nature of <s>Brahman</s> is to be ascertained as 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>).

children.text:
dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe |
mūrtaṃ caivāmūrtaṃ ca |
martyaṃ cāmṛtaṃ ca |
sthitaṃ ca yac ca |
sac ca tyaṃ ca || BrhUp_2,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s> — the formed (<s>mūrta</s>) and the formless (<s>amūrta</s>); the mortal and the immortal; the stationary and the moving; the existent (<s>sat</s>) and the beyond (<s>tya</s>). (BṛUp 2.3.1)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,3.1
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.3.1:]

children.text:
tatra dvirūpaṃ brahma pañcabhūtajanitakāryakaraṇasambaddhaṃ mūrtāmūrtākhyaṃ martyāmṛtasvabhāvaṃ tajjanitavāsanārūpaṃ ca sarvañjñaṃ sarvaśakti sopākhyaṃ bhavati /
kriyākārakaphalātmakaṃ ca sarvavyavahārāspadam /
tadeva brahma vigatasarvopādhiviśeṣaṃ samyagdarśanaviṣayam ajamajaramamṛtamabhayam, vāṅmanasayorapyaviṣayamadvaitatvāt 'neti neti'iti nirdiśyate /
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>Brahman</s> in its two-formed [aspect] — connected with the body and organs produced from the five elements, designated as formed and formless, having the nature of the mortal and the immortal, together with the latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) generated therefrom — is omniscient, omnipotent, and has designations. It is of the nature of action, agent, and result, and is the ground of all worldly transaction. That very <s>Brahman</s>, devoid of all distinguishing limiting adjuncts, the object of right vision — unborn, undecaying, immortal, fearless, and beyond even the scope of speech and mind because of its non-dual nature — is designated as '<s>neti neti</s>' ('not this, not this').

children.text: tatra yadapohadvāreṇa 'neti neti'iti nirdiśyate brahma, te ete dve vāva-vāvaśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ-dve evetyarthaḥ-brahmaṇaḥ paramātmano rūpe-rūpyate yābhyāmarūpaṃ paraṃ brahma avidyādhyāropyamāṇābhyām /
ke te dve? mūrtaṃ caiva mūrtameva ca /
children.translated_text: What are those two? The formed (<s>mūrta</s>) — indeed the formed.

children.text: tathāmūrtaṃ cāmūrtameva cetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And similarly, the formless (<s>amūrta</s>) — indeed the formless — this is the meaning.

children.text: antarṇītasvātmaviśeṣaṇe mūrtāmūrte dve evetyavadhāryete /
children.translated_text: With their respective qualifiers included, the formed and the formless are determined to be two alone.

children.text: kāni punastāni viśeṣaṇāni mūrtāmūrtayoḥ? ityucyante-martyaṃ ca martyaṃ maraṇadharmi, amṛtaṃ ca tadviparītam, sthitaṃ ca-paricchinnaṃ gatipūrvakaṃ yatsthāsnu, yacca-yātīti yat-vyāpi-aparicchinnaṃ sthitaviparītam, sacca-sadityanyebhyo viśeṣyamāṇāsādhāraṇadharmaviśeṣavat, tyacca-tadviparītam 'tyat'ityeva sarvadā parokṣābhidhānārham //1//
children.translated_text: What then are those qualifiers of the formed and the formless? They are stated: the mortal (<s>martya</s>) — subject to the law of death; and the immortal (<s>amṛta</s>) — the opposite of that; the stationary (<s>sthita</s>) — that which is limited, standing still after movement; and the moving (<s>yat</s>) — that which goes (<s>yāti</s>), i.e., the all-pervading, unlimited, the opposite of the stationary; the existent (<s>sat</s>) — that which possesses distinguishing properties that differentiate it from others; and the beyond (<s>tyat</s>) — the opposite of that, '<s>tyat</s>' being that which is always to be referred to as remote. (1)

Therein, that <s>Brahman</s> which is designated through the process of negation as '<s>neti neti</s>' — those are the two forms of <s>Brahman</s>. The word '<s>vāva</s>' serves for emphasis — the meaning is 'two indeed.' These are the two forms (<s>rūpe</s>) of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Paramātman</s> — [the forms] through which the formless supreme <s>Brahman</s> is given form [as it were], through the superimposition of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,3.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.3.2]

children.text:
tatra catuṣṭayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaṃ mūrtaṃ tathā amūrtaṃ ca /
tatra kāni mūrtaviśeṣaṇāni? kāni cetarāṇi? iti vibhajyate /
children.translated_text: Therein, the formed is qualified by the set of four [attributes]; similarly the formless. Which are the qualifiers of the formed? And which the others? This is now differentiated.

children.text:
tad etan mūrtaṃ yad anyad vāyoś cāntarikṣāc ca |
etan martyam |
etat sthitam |
etat sat |
tasyaitasya mūrtasyaitasya martyasyaitasya sthitasyaitasya sata eṣa raso ya eṣa tapati |
sato hy eṣa rasaḥ || BrhUp_2,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: That which is formed is what is other than wind and space. This is the mortal; this is the stationary; this is the existent. The essence (<s>rasa</s>) of this formed, this mortal, this stationary, this existent — is that which gives heat [the sun]. For this is the essence of the existent. (BṛUp 2.3.2)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,3.2
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.3.2:]

children.text:
tadetanmūrtaṃ mūrcchitāvayavam itaretarānupraviṣṭāvayavaṃ ghanaṃ saṃhatamityarthaḥ /
kiṃ tat? yadanyat;kasmādanyat? vāyoścāntarikṣācca bhūtadvayāt-pariśeṣāt pṛthivyādibhūtatrayam /
etanmartyam-yadetanmūrtākhyaṃ bhūtatrayamidaṃ martyaṃ maraṇadharmi;kasmāt? yasmātsthitametat;paricchinnaṃ hyarthāntareṇa samprayujyamānaṃ virudhyate-yathā ghaṭaḥ stambhakuṇḍyādinā;tathā mūrtaṃ sthitaṃ paricchinnam arthāntarasambandhi tator'thāntaravirodhānmartyam;etatsadviśeṣya māṇāsādhāraṇadharmavat, tasmāddhi paricchinnam, paricchinnatvānmartyam ato mūrtam;mūrtatvādvā martyam, martyatvātsthitam, sthitatvātsat /
ato 'nyonyāvyabhicārāccaturṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ yatheṣṭaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvo hetuhetumadbhāvaśca darśayitavyaḥ /
sarvathāpi tu bhūtatrayaṃ catuṣṭayaviśeṣaṇaviśiṣṭaṃ mūrtaṃ rūpaṃ brahmaṇaḥ /
tatra caturṇāmekasmingṛhīte viśeṣaṇe itaradgṛhītameva viśeṣaṇamityāha-tasyaitasya mūrtasya, etasya martyasya, etasya sthitasya, etasya sataḥ-catuṣṭayaviśeṣaṇasya bhūtatrayasyetyarthaḥ, eṣa rasaḥ sāra ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is formed — meaning having solidified parts, parts interpenetrating one another, dense, compact — what is that? That which is other — other than what? — than wind and space, the two elements. By elimination, it is the triad of elements: earth, water, and fire. This is mortal — this triad of elements called 'formed' is mortal, subject to death. Why? Because it is stationary — being limited, it is obstructed when it comes into contact with something else, just as a pot [is obstructed] by a pillar, a wall, and the like. Thus, the formed is stationary, i.e. limited, and related to other [entities]; because of being obstructed by other things, it is mortal. This is the existent (<s>sat</s>) — possessing distinctive properties that differentiate it from others; from this indeed it is limited; because of being limited, it is mortal; because of being mortal, it is formed; or because of being formed, it is mortal; because of being mortal, it is stationary; because of being stationary, it is existent. Therefore, from the mutual invariable concomitance of these four properties, the relation of qualifier and qualified, and of cause and effect, can be demonstrated in any desired order. In any case, the triad of elements, qualified by the set of four [attributes], is the formed <s>rūpa</s> (form) of <s>Brahman</s>. Therein, when any one of the four qualifiers is grasped, the others are [implicitly] grasped as well — [the text] says: of this very formed, this mortal, this stationary, this existent — of this triad of elements qualified by the four attributes — the essence (<s>rasa</s>), meaning the quintessence, [is stated].

children.text: trayāṇāṃ hi bhūtānāṃ sāriṣṭhaḥ savitā;etatsārāṇi trīṇi bhūtāni, yata etatkṛtavibhajyamānarūpaviśeṣaṇāni bhavanti;ādhidaivikasya kāryasyaitadrūpam-yatsavitā yadetanmaṇḍalaṃ tapati;sato bhūtatrayasya hi yasmādeṣa rasa ityetad gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: For <s>Savitṛ</s> (the sun) is the best representative of the three elements. These three elements have this [sun] as their essence, since they are qualified by the forms being differentiated and assigned to this [sun]. The form of the cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) effect is the sun — that orb which shines. Because this is the essence of the existent — of the triad of elements — this is understood.

children.text: mūrto hyeṣa savitā tapati, sāriṣṭhaśca /
children.translated_text: For this sun that shines is formed, and is the best representative [of the formed].

children.text: yattvādhidaivikaṃ karaṇaṃ maṇḍalasyābhyantaram, tadvakṣyāmaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: As for the cosmic instrument that is within the orb [of the sun] — we shall explain that later. (2)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,3.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.3.3]

children.text:
athāmūrtam |
vāyuś cāntarikṣaś ca |
etad amṛtam |
etad yat |
etat tyam |
tasyaitasyāmūrtasyaitasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasyaiṣa raso ya eṣa etasmin maṇḍale puruṣaḥ |
tyasya hy eṣa rasa |
ity adhidaivatam || BrhUp_2,3.3 ||
children.translated_text: Now the formless: wind and space. This is the immortal; this is the moving; this is the beyond (<s>tya</s>). The essence of this formless, this immortal, this moving, this beyond — is the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) within that orb. For this is the essence of the beyond. This is with reference to the divine (<s>adhidaivatam</s>). (BṛUp 2.3.3)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,3.3
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.3.3:]

children.text:
athāmūrtam-athādhunāmūrtamucyate /
vāyuścāntarikṣaṃ ca yatpariśeṣitaṃ bhūtadvayam-etadamṛtam, amūrtatvāt;asthitam, ato 'virudhyamānaṃ kenacit, amṛtamamaraṇadharmi /
etadyatsthitaviparītam, vyāpi, aparicchinnam, yasmāt 'yat'etad anyebhyo 'pravibhajyamānaviśeṣam, atastyat, 'tyat'iti parokṣābhidhānārhameva-pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: Now the formless — now the formless is stated. Wind and space — the remaining pair of elements — this is the immortal, because of being formless. Not stationary — therefore not obstructed by anything, immortal, not subject to the law of death. This is the moving (<s>yat</s>) — the opposite of the stationary; all-pervading, unlimited. Because [it is designated as] '<s>yat</s>' — having no distinguishing specific properties differentiable from others — therefore '<s>tya</s>' (the beyond), always to be referred to as remote — as before.

children.text: tasyaitasyāmūrtasya tasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasya catuṣṭayaviśeṣaṇasyāmūrtasyaiṣa rasaḥ;ko 'sau? ya
children.translated_text: Of this formless, this immortal, this moving, this beyond — of this, qualified by the set of four [attributes] — the essence is — what is that?

children.text:
eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣaḥ-karaṇātmako hiraṇyagarbhaḥ prāṇa ityabhidhīyate yaḥ, sa eṣo 'mūrtasya bhūtadvayasya rasaḥ pūrvavatsāriṣṭhaḥ /
etatpuruṣasāraṃ cāmūrtaṃ bhūtadvayamhairaṇyagarbhaliṅgārambhāya hi bhūtadvayābhivyaktiravyākṛtāt /
tasmāttadarthyāttatsāraṃ bhūtadvayam /
tyasya hyeṣa rasaḥ-yasmādyo maṇḍalasthaḥ puruṣo maṇḍalavanna gṛhyate sāraśca bhūtadvayasya, tasmādasti maṇḍalasthasya puruṣasya bhūtadvayasya ca sādharmyam, tasmādyuktaṃ prasiddhavadvetūpādānam-tyasya hyeṣa rasa iti /
children.translated_text: The person (<s>puruṣa</s>) within that orb — the <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (Golden Embryo) who has the nature of the [cosmic] instrument, who is called <s>prāṇa</s> — he is the essence of the formless pair of elements, the best representative, as before. This pair of formless elements has this person as its essence — for the manifestation of the pair of elements from the unmanifest is for the purpose of initiating the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. Therefore, because of being for that purpose, the pair of elements has that [<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>] as its essence. 'For this is the essence of the beyond' — since the person within the orb is not perceived like the orb [itself], and is the quintessence of the pair of elements, therefore there is a commonality between the person within the orb and the pair of elements — hence it is proper that a well-known [fact] is taken as the basis: 'for this is the essence of the beyond.'

children.text:
rasaḥ kāraṇaṃ hiraṇyagarbhavijñānātmā cetana iti kecit /
tatra ca kila hiraṇyagarbhavijñānātmanaḥ karma vāyvantarikṣayoḥ prayoktṛ, tatkarma vāyvantarikṣādhāraṃ sadanyeṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ prayoktṛ bhavati;tena svakarmaṇā vāyvantarikṣayoḥ prayokteti tayo rasaḥ kāraṇamucyata iti /
children.translated_text: Some say the essence (<s>rasa</s>) means the cause — the conscious self of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. And in that case, the <s>karma</s> of the conscious self of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> motivates wind and space; that <s>karma</s>, resting in wind and space, becomes the motivator of the other elements. Thus, through his own <s>karma</s>, he motivates wind and space — therefore he is called their essence, i.e. cause.

children.text:
tanna, mūrtarasenātulyatvāt /
mūrtasya tu bhūtatrayasya raso mūrtameva maṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhūtatrayasya raso mūrtameva maṇḍalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhūtatrayasamānajātīyam, na cetanaḥ;tathāmūrtayorapi bhūtayostatsamānajātīyenaivāmūrtasena yuktaṃ bhavitum;vākyapravṛttestulyatvāt;yathā hi mūrtāmūrte catuṣṭayadharmavatī vibhajyete, tathā rasarasavatorapi mūrtāmūrtayostulyenaiva nyāyena yukto vibhāgaḥ, na tvardhavaiśasam /
children.translated_text: This is not so, because of dissimilarity with the essence of the formed. For the essence of the formed triad of elements is seen to be the formed orb itself — of the same class as the triad of elements — not a conscious being. Similarly, for the formless pair of elements too, it is proper to have an essence of the same class — formless. Because the structure of the sentences is the same. For just as the formed and the formless are differentiated with their four attributes, so too the differentiation of the essences — of the formed and the formless — should follow the same principle; there should not be an inconsistent division.

children.text: mūrtarase 'pi maṇḍalopādhiścetano vivakṣyata iti cet? atyalpamidamucyate, sarvatraiva tu mūrtāmūrtayorbrahmarūpeṇa vivakṣitatvāt /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Even in the case of the formed essence, the conscious being conditioned by the orb is intended. [Response:] This says too little, since in all cases, formed and formless alike, it is intended that they are forms of <s>Brahman</s> [and thus connected with consciousness].

children.text: puruṣaśabdo 'cetane 'nupapanna iti cet! na, pakṣapucchādiviśiṣṭasyaiva liṅgasya puruṣaśabdadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The word '<s>puruṣa</s>' (person) is inapplicable to something non-conscious. [Response:] No — because the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' is seen applied to the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) itself, which is qualified by wings, tail, and the like.

children.text: "na vā itthaṃ santaḥ śakṣyāmaḥ prajāḥ prajanayitumimānsapta puruṣānekaṃ puruṣaṃ karavāmeti ta etānsapta puruṣānekaṃ puruṣamakurvan"ityādau annarasamayādiṣu ca śrutyantare puruṣaśabdaprayogāt /
children.translated_text: Because in [the passage] 'We, being thus, will not be able to generate offspring; let us make these seven persons into one person — they made these seven persons into one person' and such, and in other <s>śrutis</s> regarding the food-essence-self and the rest, the word '<s>puruṣa</s>' is used [for non-conscious entities].

children.text: ityadhidaivatamityuktopasaṃhāro 'dhyātmavibhāgoktyarthaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: 'This is with reference to the divine (<s>adhidaivatam</s>)' — the concluding statement that was said is for the purpose of introducing the division with reference to the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>). (3)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,3.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.3.4]

children.text:
athādhyātmam |
idam eva mūrtaṃ yad anyat prāṇāc ca yaś cāyam antar ātmann ākāśaḥ |
etan martyam |
etat sthitam |
etat sat |
tasyaitasya mūrtasyaitasya martyasyaitasya sthitasyaitasya sata eṣa raso yac cakṣuḥ |
sato hy eṣa rasaḥ || BrhUp_2,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: Now with reference to the individual (<s>adhyātmam</s>): the formed and the formless of these — the formed and the formless of <s>Brahman</s>'s conditioning — are divided according to the body-and-organs.

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,3.4
children.translated_text: This indeed is the formed: what is other than <s>prāṇa</s> (breath/wind) and the space within the self. This is the mortal; this is the stationary; this is the existent. The essence of this formed, this mortal, this stationary, this existent — is the eye. For this is the essence of the existent. (BṛUp 2.3.4)

children.text: athādhunādhyātmaṃ mūrtāmūrtayorvibhāga ucyate-kiṃ tanmūrtam? idameva, kiṃ cedam? yadanyatprāṇāccavāyoryaścāyamantarabhyantare ātmannātmanyākāśaḥ khaṃ śarīrasthaśca yaḥ prāṇa etad dvayaṃ varjayitvā yadanyaccharīrārambhakaṃ bhūtatrayam, etanmartyamityādi samānamanyatpūrveṇa /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.3.4:]

children.text: etasya sato hyeṣa rasaḥ-yaccakṣuriti; ādhyātmikasya śarīrārambhakasya kāryasyaiṣa rasaḥ sāraḥ; tena hi sāreṇa sāravadidaṃ śarīraṃ samastaṃ yathādhidaivatamādityamaṇḍalena /
children.translated_text: Now the division of the formed and the formless with reference to the individual (<s>adhyātmam</s>) is stated. What is the formed? This itself — what is this? That which is other than <s>prāṇa</s>, i.e. wind, and the space within the self, within the body. Excluding these two — the space within the body and the <s>prāṇa</s> — whatever other triad of elements constitutes the body — this is the mortal, and so forth — the rest is the same as before.

children.text: prāthamyācca-cakṣuṣī eva prathame sambhavataḥ sambhavata iti /
children.translated_text: The essence of this existent is the eye. The eye is the essence of the body-constituting individual-level effect — the quintessence. By it, as the quintessence, this entire body is substantial — just as the cosmic [body is substantial] through the orb of the sun.

children.text: "tejo raso niranartatāgniḥ"iti liṅgāt; taijasaṃ hi cakṣuḥ; etatsāram; taijasaṃ hi cakṣuḥ; etatsāram ādhyātmikaṃ bhūtatrayam; sato hyeṣa rasa iti mūrtatvasāratve hetvarthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: And because of priority — the two eyes are indeed the first [organs] to come into being, it is said.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,3.5
children.translated_text: From the indicatory mark: 'The essence of fire, restless, is <s>Agni</s>.' For the eye is fiery [in nature]; this is the essence. The fiery eye is the essence of the individual-level triad of elements. 'For this is the essence of the existent' — the word '<s>hi</s>' (for) gives the reason for the essence being of the nature of the formed. (4)

children.text:
athāmūrtaṃ prāṇaś ca yaś cāyam antar ātmann ākāśaḥ |
etad amṛtam |
etad yat |
etat tyat |
tasyaitasyāmūrtasyaitasyāmṛtasyaitasya yata etasya tyasyaiṣa raso yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣaḥ |
tyasya hy eṣa rasaḥ || BrhUp_2,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.3.5]

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,3.5
children.translated_text: Now the formless: <s>prāṇa</s> and the space within the self. This is the immortal; this is the moving; this is the beyond. The essence of this formless, this immortal, this moving, this beyond — is the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) in the right eye. For this is the essence of the beyond. (BṛUp 2.3.5)

children.text:
athādhunāmūrtamucyate /
yatpariśeṣitaṃ bhūtadvayaṃ prāṇaśca yaścāyamantarātmannākāśaḥ, etadamūrtam /
anyatpūrvavat /
etasya tyasyaiṣa rasaḥ sāraḥ, yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣaḥ-dakṣiṇe 'kṣanniti viśeṣagrahaṇam, śāstrapratyakṣatvāt;liṅgasya hi dakṣiṇe 'kṣṇi viśeṣato 'dhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ śāsatrasya pratyakṣaṃ sarvaśrutiṣu tathā prayogadarśanāt /
tyasya hyeṣa rasa iti
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.3.5:]

children.text: pūrvavadviśeṣato 'grahaṇādamūrtatvasāratve eva hetvarthaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: Now the formless is stated. The remaining pair of elements — <s>prāṇa</s> and the space within the self — this is the formless. The rest is as before. The essence of this beyond is the person in the right eye — 'the right eye' is specified because [the self] is known through scripture [to preside there specifically]; for in all <s>śruti</s> passages, the special presiding of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) in the right eye is scripturally evident, since such usage is observed. 'For this is the essence of the beyond' —

children.text: START BrhUp 2,3.6
children.translated_text: As before, because [the person in the right eye] is not perceived as a specific [entity], the word '<s>hi</s>' (for) gives the reason for the essence being of the nature of the formless. (5)

children.text:
brahmaṇaṇa upādhibhūtayormūrtāmūrtayoḥ kāryakaraṇavibhāgena adhyātmādhidaivatayorvibhāgo vyākhyātaḥ satyaśabdavācyayoḥ /
athedānīm-
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.3.6]

children.text:
tasya haitasya puruṣasya rūpam |
yathā māhārajanaṃ vāso yathā pāṇḍvāvikaṃ yathendragopo yathāgnyarcir yathā puṇḍarīkaṃ yathā sakṛdvidyuttam |
sakṛdvidyutteva ha vā asya śrīr bhavati ya evaṃ veda |
athāta ādeśo neti neti |
na hy etasmād iti nety anyat param asti |
atha nāmadheyaṃ satyasya satyam iti |
prāṇā vai satyam |
teṣām eṣa satyam || BrhUp_2,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: The division of the formed and the formless — the two conditioning [forms] of <s>Brahman</s> — in terms of body-and-organs, with reference to both the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) and the divine (<s>adhidaivata</s>), has been explained — [these being] denoted by the word '<s>satya</s>' (true/real). Now then —

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,3.6
children.translated_text: The form of this person is like a saffron-colored garment, like white wool, like an <s>Indragopa</s> insect, like a flame of fire, like a white lotus, like a sudden flash of lightning. One whose glory is like a sudden flash of lightning — [such glory comes to] one who knows this. Now then, the teaching (<s>ādeśa</s>): '<s>neti neti</s>' ('not this, not this'). For there is nothing higher than this — that [one says] 'it is not [this].' Then the designation: 'the truth of the true.' The <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths) are the true; of them, this [self] is the truth. (BṛUp 2.3.6)

children.text: tasya haitasya puruṣasya karaṇātmano liṅgasya rūpaṃ vakṣyāmo vāsanāmayaṃ mūrtāmūrtavāsanāvijñānamayasaṃyogajanitaṃ vicitraṃ paṭabhitticitravanmāyendrajālamṛgatṛṣṇikopamaṃ sarvavyāmohāspadametāvanmātrameva ātmeti vijñānavādino vaināśikā yatra bhrāntāḥ, etadeva vāsanārūpaṃ paṭarūpavadātmano dravyasya guṇa iti naiyāyikā vaiśeṣikāśca sampratipannāḥ, idamātmārthaṃ triguṇaṃ svatantraṃ pradhānāśrayaṃ puruṣārthena hetunā pravartata iti sāṅkhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.3.6:] Of this person — of the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) which has the nature of an instrument — [the text says] we shall state its form. The form is made of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), born from the conjunction of the formed and the formless impressional-consciousness, variegated — like paintings on canvas or walls, comparable to magic, conjuring tricks, and mirages — the ground of all delusion. Those who hold the doctrine of consciousness alone, the <s>Vaināśikas</s> (Buddhist proponents of momentariness), are deluded [in thinking that] this much alone is the Self. Those very impression-forms — like the forms of a painting — are accepted by the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s> as qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) of the Self, which is a substance (<s>dravya</s>). [And] the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> [hold that] 'this — [consisting of the] three <s>guṇas</s>, for the sake of the <s>puruṣa</s> (Self), independent, based on <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) — operates due to the purpose of the <s>puruṣa</s>.'

children.text:
aupaniṣadaṃmanyā api kecitprakriyāṃ racayanti-mūrtāmūrtarāśirekaḥ, paramātmarāśiruttamaḥ, tābhyāmanyo 'yaṃ madhyamaḥ kila tṛtīyaḥ kartrā bhoktrāvijñānamayena ajātaśatrupratibodhitena saha vidyākarmapūrvaprajñāsamudāyaḥ;prayoktā karmarāśiḥ, prayojyaḥ pūrvokto mūrtāmūrtabhūtarāśiḥ sādhanaṃ ceti /
tatra ca tārkikaiḥ saha sandhiṃ kurvanti /
liṅgāśrayaścaiṣa karmarāśirityuktvā punastatasrasyantaḥ sāṅkhyatvabhayāt, sarvaḥ karmarāśiḥ-puṣpāśraya iva gandhaḥ puṣpaviyoge 'pi puṭatailāśrayo bhavati, tadvat-liṅgaviyoge 'pi paramātmaikadeśamāśrayati, sa paramātmaikadeśaḥ kilānyata āgatena guṇena karmaṇā saguṇo bhavati nirguṇo 'pi san, sa kartā bhoktā badhyate mucyate ca vijñānātmā - iti vaiśeṣikacittamapyanusaranti;sa ca karmarāśirbhūtarāśerāgantukaḥ, svato nirguṇa eva paramātmaikadeśatvāt;svata utthitā avidyā anāgantukāpyūṣaravadanātmadharmaḥ-ityanayā kalpanayā sāṅkhyacittamanuvartante /
children.translated_text: Certain persons who fancy themselves [interpreters of] Upaniṣadic [teaching] construct a system of three categories (<s>rāśitraya</s>): one category is that of the formed and formless (<s>mūrtāmūrta</s>); the supreme category — the <s>Paramātman</s> — is the highest; and different from these two is a supposed third, the middle one — the aggregate of knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), and prior cognition (<s>pūrvaprajñā</s>), together with the agent, the enjoyer, the <s>vijñānamaya</s> [self] awakened by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>; the impelling [factor] is the category of action (<s>karmarāśi</s>); the impelled is the aforementioned category of formed and formless elements (<s>mūrtāmūrtabhūtarāśi</s>), which is also the instrument — thus [they say]. And in this [system], they make an alliance with the logicians (<s>tārkikas</s>). Having said that this category of action has the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) as its substratum, then, fearing that it would become <s>Sāṅkhya</s> [doctrine] by having [the subtle body] depart [from the gross body], [they say:] the entire category of action — like fragrance, which resides in a flower and, even when separated from the flower, resides in a casket of oil — similarly, even when separated from the subtle body, takes refuge in a particular location of the <s>Paramātman</s>; that particular location of the <s>Paramātman</s>, though itself quality-less, becomes endowed with qualities due to the quality of action that has come from elsewhere — that [self] is the agent, the enjoyer, is bound and is liberated, and is the <s>vijñānātman</s> — thus they follow even the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> way of thinking. And that category of action is adventitious to the category of elements (<s>bhūtarāśi</s>), [while the self is] intrinsically quality-less owing to being a location of the <s>Paramātman</s>; <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), which arises from itself, though not adventitious, is like saline soil — a non-self property — by this contrivance they follow the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> way of thinking.

children.text: sarvametattārkikaiḥ saha sāmañjasyakalpanayā ramaṇīyaṃ paśyanti, lopaniṣatsiddhāntaṃ sarvanyāyavirodhaṃ ca paśyanti;katham? uktā eva tāvatsāva yavatve paramātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: They regard all this — the harmonization with the logicians — as delightful, and they regard it as the established conclusion of the Upaniṣads and as free from contradiction with all [systems of] reasoning. How [do they see it as free from contradiction]? The very defects already stated regarding the parthood of the <s>Paramātman</s> —

children.text: saṃsāritvasavraṇatvakarmaphaladeśasaṃsāritvasavraṇatvakarmaphaladeśasaṃsaraṇānupapattyādayo doṣāḥ;nityabhede ca vijñānātmanaḥ pareṇaikatvānupapattiḥ /
children.translated_text: the defects of [<s>Brahman</s>'s] being a <s>saṃsārin</s>, being wounded, [its parts] migrating as the fruit of action, and the impossibility of transmigration — [apply here too]; and if the <s>vijñānātman</s> is eternally different [from <s>Brahman</s>], the impossibility of oneness with the Supreme [follows].

children.text:
liṅgameveti cetparamātmana upacaritadeśatvena kalpitaṃ ghaṭakarakabhūchidrākāśādivat, tathā liṅgaviyoge 'pi paramātmadeśāśrayaṇaṃ vāsanāyāḥ /
avidyāyāṣca svata utthānam ūṣaravat-ityādikalpanānupapannaiva /
na ca vāsya deśavyatirekeṇa vāsanāyā vastvantarasañcaraṇaṃ manasāpi kalpayituṃ śakyam /
children.translated_text: If [one says] it is only the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) [that transmigrates] — [then] the attributed spatiality of the <s>Paramātman</s> is a fabrication, like the space [supposedly delimited by] a pot, a water-jug, or a hole; similarly, the taking refuge of the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) in a location of the <s>Paramātman</s> when [the <s>vāsanā</s>] is separated from the subtle body [is also a fabrication]. And the contrivance that <s>avidyā</s> arises from itself like saline soil is itself untenable. Nor can one conceive — even in the mind — of the <s>vāsanā</s> migrating to some other entity apart from the thing [in which] it inheres.

children.text:
na ca śrutayo gacchanti"kāmaḥ saṅkalpo vicikitsā" "hṛdaye hyeva rūpāṇi" "dhyāyatīva lelāyatīva" "kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ""tīrṇo hi tadā sarvāñchokānhṛdayasya"ityādyāḥ /
na cāsāṃ śrutīnāṃ śrutādarthāntarakalpanā nyāyyā, ātmanaḥ parabrahmatvopapādanārthaparatvādāsām, etāvanmātrārthopakṣayatvācca sarvopaniṣadām /
tasmācchrutyarthakalpanākuśalāḥ sarva evopaniṣadarthamanyathā kurvanti /
tathāpi vedārthaścetsyātkāmaṃ bhavatu, na me dveṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor do the <s>śruti</s> texts support [this view] — such as: 'Desire, volition, doubt' (BṛUp 1.5.3); 'For forms are indeed in the heart' (BṛUp 4.4.2); 'It meditates, as it were; it moves, as it were' (BṛUp 4.3.7); 'The desires that are lodged in the heart' (KaUp 2.3.14); 'For then one crosses beyond all the sorrows of the heart' (ChUp 7.1.3) — and so forth. Nor is it proper to fabricate a meaning different from the heard [meaning] of these <s>śruti</s> texts, since they are directed toward establishing the <s>Paramabrahman</s>-hood of the self, and since all Upaniṣads are devoted solely to this much meaning. Therefore, all who are unskilled in the construction of scriptural meaning distort the meaning of the Upaniṣads. Even so, if the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> were [truly] thus, let it be so freely — I have no hostility [toward it].

children.text:
na ca 'dva vāva brahmaṇo rūpe'iti rāśitrayapakṣe samañjasam;yadā tu mūrtāmūrte tajjanitavāsanāśca mūrtāmūrte dve rūpe, brahma ca rūpi tṛtīyam, na cānyaccaturthamantarāletadā etadanukūlamavadhāraṇam, dve eva brahmaṇo rūpe iti;anyathā brahmaikadeśasya vijñānātmano rūpe iti kalpyam, paramātmano vā vijñānātmadvāreṇeti /
tadā ca rūpe eveti dvivacanamasamañjasam, rūpāṇīti vāsanābhiḥ saha bahuvacanaṃ yuktataraṃ syāt- dve ca mūrtāmūrte vāsanāśca tṛtīyamiti /
children.translated_text: Moreover, 'Two indeed are the forms of <s>Brahman</s>' (BṛUp 2.3.1) — this is not consistent on the three-category view. But when the formed and formless [are one pair], and the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) generated by them are [another pair of] formed and formless — these two are the forms [of <s>Brahman</s>], and <s>Brahman</s> itself, the possessor of forms, is the third, and there is no fourth besides these — then this restrictive statement is appropriate: 'Two indeed are the forms of <s>Brahman</s>.' Otherwise, one would have to construe [it as]: 'the forms of the <s>vijñānātman</s>, which is a location of the <s>Paramātman</s>,' or 'the forms of the <s>Paramātman</s> through the medium of the <s>vijñānātman</s>.' And then the dual number in 'two forms' would be inconsistent; the plural 'forms,' together with the <s>vāsanās</s>, would be more appropriate — [namely,] two [sets of] formed and formless, and the <s>vāsanās</s> as a third.

children.text: atha mūrtāmūrte eva paramātmano rūpe, vāsanāstu vijñānātmana iti cet-tadā vijñānātmadvāreṇa vikriyamāṇasya paramātmanaḥ-itīyaṃ vācoyuktiranarthikā syāt, vāsanāyā api vijñānātmadvāratvasya aviśiṣṭatvāt;na ca vastu
children.translated_text: Now, if [one says] the formed and formless are the forms of the <s>Paramātman</s>, while the <s>vāsanās</s> belong to the <s>vijñānātman</s> — then the verbal device '[the <s>Paramātman</s>] is modified through the medium of the <s>vijñānātman</s>' would be purposeless, since the <s>vāsanā</s> too equally has the <s>vijñānātman</s> as its medium. And a real entity

children.text:
vastvantaradvāreṇa vikriyata iti mukhyayā vṛttyā śakyaṃ kalpayitum;na ca vijñānātmā paramātmano vastvantaram, tathā kalpanāyāṃ siddhāntahānāt /
tasmād vedārthamūḍhānāṃ svacittaprabhavā evamādikalpanā akṣarabāhyāḥ;na hyakṣarabāhyo vedārtho vedārthopakārī vā, nirapekṣatvādvedasya prāmāṇyaṃ prati;tasmādrāśitrayakalpanā asamañjasā /
children.translated_text: cannot be conceived as being modified through the medium of another real entity in the primary sense. Nor is the <s>vijñānātman</s> a different entity from the <s>Paramātman</s>, for accepting such a construction would amount to abandoning the established conclusion [of Advaita]. Therefore, fabrications of this sort — such as part-whole, portion-possessor, and modification-modifier [relationships for <s>Brahman</s>] — arising from the minds of those who are confused about the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, are external to the [actual] words [of scripture]. For a meaning external to the words is neither the meaning of the <s>Veda</s> nor helpful to the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>, since the <s>Veda</s>'s authority is independent [of such constructions]. Therefore, the three-category fabrication is inconsistent.

children.text: 'yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣaḥ'iti liṅgātmā prastuto 'dhyātme, adhidaive ca 'ya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣaḥ'
children.translated_text: 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the right eye' (BṛUp 2.3.5) — thus the self associated with the subtle body (<s>liṅgātman</s>) has been introduced in the context of the individual (<s>adhyātma</s>), and in the context of the cosmic (<s>adhidaiva</s>): 'The <s>puruṣa</s> who is in that disc [of the sun]' (BṛUp 2.3.3).

children.text:
iti, 'tasya'iti prakṛtopādānātsa evopādīyate yo 'sau tyasyāmūrtasya raso na tu vijñānamayaḥ /
nanu vijñānamayasyaivaitāni rupāṇi kasmānna bhavanti? vijñānamayasyāpi prakṛtatvāt, 'tasya'iti ca prakṛtopādānāt /
naivam, vijñānamayasyārūpitvena vijijñāpayiṣitatvāt;yadi hi tasyaiva vijñānamayasyaitāni māhārajanādīni rūpāṇi syustasyāva 'neti neti'ityanākhyeyarūpatayādeśo na syāt /
nanvanyasyaivāsādeśo na tu vijñānamayasyeti!
children.translated_text: 'Of that' — since this is a resumptive reference to what was previously introduced, it is that very one who is taken up — the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of that formless [<s>Brahman</s>] — not the <s>vijñānamaya</s> [self]. [Objection:] Why should these not be the forms of the <s>vijñānamaya</s> itself? Since the <s>vijñānamaya</s> too is the topic, and since 'of that' is a resumptive reference to what was previously introduced. [Reply:] Not so — because the intention is to make known the <s>vijñānamaya</s> as formless. For if these forms such as <s>māhārajana</s> (deep saffron) and the like belonged to the <s>vijñānamaya</s> itself, then the designation of it as having an indescribable nature through '<s>neti neti</s>' would not be possible. [Objection:] But perhaps this designation belongs to some other [entity], not to the <s>vijñānamaya</s>!

children.text:
na, ṣaṣṭhānte upasaṃhārāt-"vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāt"iti vijñānamayaṃ prastutya"sa eṣa neti neti"iti"vijñāpayiṣyāmi"iti ca pratijñāyā arthavattvāt /
yadi ca vijñānamayasyaiva asaṃvyavahāryamātmasvarūpaṃ jñāpayitumiṣṭaṃ syātpradhvastasarvopādhiviśeṣam, tata iyaṃ pratijñārthavatī syāt- yenāsau jñāpito jānātyātmānamevāhaṃ brahmāsmīti, śāsraniṣṭhāṃ prāpnoti na bibheti kutaśca /
atha punaranyo vijñānamayaḥ, anyaḥ 'neti neti' iti vyapadiśyate-tadānyadado brahmānyo 'hamasmīti
children.translated_text: [Reply:] No — because of the summing up at the end of the sixth [<s>brāhmaṇa</s>]. Having introduced the <s>vijñānamaya</s> with 'O dear one, by what would one know the knower?' (BṛUp 2.4.14), [the text says] 'That is this — <s>neti neti</s>' (BṛUp 2.3.6); and because the promise 'I shall make [<s>Brahman</s>] known' would [otherwise] be meaningless. For if the intention were to make known the intrinsic nature of the <s>vijñānamaya</s> itself as having a form beyond all limiting adjuncts and free from all conventional designations, then this promise would be meaningful — [namely,] he who is thus made known, knows the self: 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' — and attains the culmination of the teaching, and does not fear from anywhere. But if, on the other hand, the <s>vijñānamaya</s> is one [entity] and the one designated by '<s>neti neti</s>' is another — then the wrong conclusion would be grasped: 'That <s>Brahman</s> is other [than me]; I am other [than <s>Brahman</s>]' —

children.text:
viparyayo gṛhītaḥ syāt, na 'ātmānamevāvedahaṃ brahmāsmi' iti /
tasmāt 'tasya haitasya' iti liṅgapuruśasyai vaitāni rūpāṇi /
children.translated_text: not 'I knew the self: I am <s>Brahman</s>' (BṛUp 1.4.10). Therefore, 'of that' — these are the forms of the <s>puruṣa</s> associated with the subtle body (<s>liṅgapuruṣa</s>).

children.text: satyasya ca satye paramātmasvarūpe vaktavye niravaśeṣaṃ satyaṃ vaktavyam;satyasya ca viśeṣarūpāṇi vāsanāḥ, tāsāmimāni rūpāṇyucyante, etasya puruṣasya prakṛtasya liṅgātmana etāni rūpāṇi;kāni tāni? ityucyante- yathā loke, mahārajanaṃ haridrā tayā raktaṃ māhārajanaṃ yathā vāso loke, evaṃ stryādiviṣayasaṃyoge tādṛśaṃ vāsanārūpaṃ rañjanākāra mutpadyate cittasya, yenāsau puruṣo rakta ityucyate vasrādivat /
children.translated_text: And when the true nature of the <s>Paramātman</s> — the truth of truth (<s>satyasya satya</s>) — is to be stated, the truth must be stated without remainder. Now, the specific forms of truth are the <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions); of these, the following forms are stated — the forms of this <s>puruṣa</s>, the one previously introduced, the self associated with the subtle body. What are they? It is said: just as in the world, <s>mahārajana</s> (turmeric) — [a deep yellow dye] — and cloth dyed with it is called <s>māhārajana</s>, similarly, when there is contact with a sense-object such as a woman and the like, a form of <s>vāsanā</s> of such a kind — in the nature of coloring — arises in the mind, on account of which that <s>puruṣa</s> is called 'colored' (<s>rakta</s>), like a garment and the like.

children.text:
yathā ca loke pāṇḍvāvikam, averidam āvikam ūrṇādi, yathā ca tatpāṇḍuraṃ bhavati, tathānyadvāsanārūpam /
yathā ca loke indragopo 'tyantarakto bhavati, evamasya vāsanārūpam /
kvacidviṣayaviśeṣāpekṣayā rāgasya tāratamyam, kvacitpuruṣacittavṛttyapekṣayā /
yathā ca loke 'gnyarcirbhāsvaraṃ bhavati, tathā kvacitkasyacidvāsanārūpaṃ bhavati /
yathā pumḍarīkaṃ śuklam, tadvadapi ca vāsanārūpaṃ kasyacidbhavati /
yathā sakṛdvidyuktam, yathā loke sakṛdvidyotanaṃ sarvataḥ prakāśakaṃ bhavati, tathā jñānaprakāśavivṛddhyapekṣayā kasyacidvāsanārūpamupajāyate /
naiṣāṃ vāsanārūpāṇāmādiranto madhyaṃ saṅkhyā vā, deśaḥ kālo nimittaṃ
children.translated_text: And just as in the world there is a white woollen [cloth] — this [cloth] made of wool from a sheep — and just as that is white, so too another form of <s>vāsanā</s> [is white]. And just as in the world the <s>indragopa</s> insect is extremely red, so too is a form of <s>vāsanā</s> of this [<s>puruṣa</s>]. In some cases, the gradation of coloring (<s>rāga</s>) depends on the particular sense-object; in other cases, it depends on the particular mental disposition of the person. And just as in the world a flame of fire is luminous, so too for some person, some form of <s>vāsanā</s> is [luminous]. And just as a white lotus is white, so too a form of <s>vāsanā</s> is for someone. Just as [there is] a sudden flash of lightning — just as in the world a single flash of lightning illuminates in all directions — so too, in proportion to the increase of the light of knowledge, a form of <s>vāsanā</s> arises for someone. Of these forms of <s>vāsanā</s>, neither the beginning, end, middle, number, nor the place, time, or cause

children.text:
vāvadhāryate-asaṅkhyeyatvādvāsanāyāḥ, vāsanāhetūnāṃ cānantyāt /
tathā ca vakṣyati ṣaṣṭhe-"idaṃmayo 'domayaḥ"ityādi /
tasmānna svarūpasaṅkhyāvadhāraṇārthā dṛṣṭāntāḥ- 'yathā māhārajanaṃ vāsaḥ'ityādayaḥ, kiṃ tarhi? prakārapradarśanārthāḥ-evamprakārāṇi hi vāsanārūpāṇīti /
yattu vāsanārūpamabhihitamante-sakṛdvidyotanamiveti, tatkila hiraṇyagarbhasya avyākṛtātprādurbhavataḥ taḍidvatsakṛdeva vyaktirbhavatīti;tattadīyaṃ vāsanārūpaṃ hiraṇyagarbhasya yo veda tasya sakṛdvidyutteva, ha vai ityavadhāraṇārthau, evamevāsya śrīḥ khyātirbhavatītyarthaḥ, yathā hiraṇyagarbhasya-evametadyathoktaṃ vāsanārūpamantyaṃ yo veda /
children.translated_text: can be determined — because of the innumerability of <s>vāsanās</s> and because of the infinity of the causes of <s>vāsanās</s>. And thus [the <s>śruti</s>] will say in the sixth [<s>brāhmaṇa</s>]: 'Made of this, made of that' (BṛUp 2.4.7) and so forth. Therefore, the illustrations — 'like a <s>māhārajana</s> garment' and the rest — are not for the purpose of determining the intrinsic nature or the number [of <s>vāsanās</s>]; rather, [they are] for the purpose of showing the kind [of <s>vāsanā</s>] — 'the forms of <s>vāsanā</s> are of such kinds.' As for the form of <s>vāsanā</s> mentioned at the end — 'like a sudden flash of lightning' — that, it is said, belongs to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, who emerges from the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), whose manifestation is a single flash like lightning. That form of <s>vāsanā</s> belonging to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — he who knows it, for him, like a sudden flash of lightning — '<s>ha vai</s>' are emphatic particles — thus indeed does glory and renown become his; that is the meaning — just as for <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, so too for one who knows the form of <s>vāsanā</s> described last.

children.text:
evaṃ niravaśeṣaṃ satyasya svarūpamabhidhāya, yattatsatyasya satyamavocāma tasyaiva svarūpāvadhāraṇārthaṃ brahmaṇa idamārabhyate-athānantaraṃ satyasvarūpanirdeśānantaram, yatsatyasya satyaṃ tadevāvaśiṣyate yasmādatastasmātsatyasya satyaṃ svarūpaṃ nirdekṣyāmaḥ /
ādeśo nirdeśo brahmaṇaḥ /
kaḥ punarasau nirdeśaḥ? ityucyate-neti netītyevaṃ nirdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having thus described the true nature (<s>svarūpa</s>) of truth without remainder, for the purpose of determining the very nature of that which we called 'the truth of truth' — <s>Brahman</s> — this [teaching] is commenced. Then, after the description of the true nature of truth, that which is the truth of truth alone remains; because from that — since [all else derives] from it — [it is called] the truth of truth; [and so] we shall describe [its] true nature. The designation (<s>ādeśa</s>) — the description — of <s>Brahman</s> [follows]. What then is that description? It is said: '<s>neti neti</s>' — 'not this, not this' — such is the description.

children.text:
nanu kathamābhyāṃ 'neti neti'iti śabdābhyāṃ satyasya satyaṃ nirdidikṣitam? ityucyate-sarvopādhiviśeṣāpohena /
yasminna kaścidviśeṣo 'sti-nāma vā rūpaṃ vā karma vā bhedo vā jātirvā guṇo vā;taddvāreṇa hi śabdapravṛttirbhavati /
na caiṣāṃ kaścid viśeṣo brahmaṇyasti;ato na nirdeṣṭuṃ śakyate-idaṃ taditi /
gaurasau spandate śuklo viṣāṇīti yathā loke nirdiśyate, tathā;adhyāropitanāmarūpakarmadvāreṇa brahma nirdiśyate 'vijñānamānandaṃ brahma' 'vijñānaghana eva brahmātmā'ityevamādiśabdaiḥ /
children.translated_text: But how can <s>Brahman</s> — the truth of truth — be designated by these two words '<s>neti neti</s>'? It is said: by the removal of all qualifying attributes (<s>upādhi</s>). Since there is no distinguishing attribute whatsoever in it — neither name, nor form, nor action, nor difference, nor genus, nor quality; for the application of words occurs through these [attributes]. And none of these distinguishing attributes exists in <s>Brahman</s>; therefore it cannot be designated as 'this is that.' [In the world,] one designates thus: 'That is a cow — it moves, is white, has horns.' But in a similar manner, <s>Brahman</s> is designated through superimposed name and form and action — by words such as '<s>Brahman</s> is consciousness and bliss' (BṛUp 3.9.28), '<s>Brahman</s> is a mass of consciousness alone, the self' (BṛUp 2.4.12), and the like.

children.text:
yadā punaḥ svarūpameva nirdidikṣitaṃ bhavati;nirastasarvopādhiviśeṣam, tadā na śakyate kenacidapi prakāreṇa nirdeṣṭum;tadā ayamevābhyupāyaḥ-yaduta prāptanirdeśapratiṣedhadvāreṇa 'neti neti'iti nirdeśaḥ /
idaṃ ca nakāradvayaṃ vīpsāvyāptyartham;yadyatprāptaṃ tattanniṣidhyate /
tathā ca sati anirdiṣṭāśaṅkā brahmaṇaḥ parihṛtā bhavati;anyathā hi nakāradvayena prakṛtadvayapratiṣedhe, yadanyatprakṛtātpratiṣiddhadvayādbrahma tanna nirdiṣṭam, kīdṛśaṃ nu khalu-ityāśaṅkā na nivartiṣyate;tathā cānarthakaśca sa nirdeśaḥ, puruṣasya vividiṣāyā anivartakatvāt;
'brahma jñapayiṣyāmi'iti ca vākyam aparisamāptārthaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: But when it is the intrinsic nature itself that one wishes to designate — free from all qualifying attributes — then it cannot be designated in any manner whatsoever. In that case, the only expedient is this: designation through the negation of [every] designation that presents itself — '<s>neti neti</s>,' 'not this, not this.' And these two negation particles serve the purpose of comprehensive inclusion (<s>vīpsā</s>); whatever [designation] presents itself, that is negated. This being so, the apprehension that <s>Brahman</s> is undesignated is dispelled. For otherwise — if the two negation particles merely negated two [specific] things already introduced — then <s>Brahman</s>, which is different from the introduced [pair] and from the two [things] negated, would remain undesignated, and the doubt 'What kind of thing is it?' would not be removed. And in that case, the designation would be purposeless, because it would fail to remove the person's desire to know. And the statement 'I shall make <s>Brahman</s> known' would remain with its meaning incomplete.

children.text:
yadā tu sarvadikkālādivividiṣā nivartitā syāt sarvopādhinirākaraṇadvāreṇa tadā saindhavaghanavadekarasaṃ prajñānaghanamanantaramabāhyaṃ satyasya satyamahaṃbrahmāsmīti sarvato nivartate vividiṣā, ātmanyevāvasthitā prajñā bhavati /
tasmādvīpsārthaṃ neti netīti nakāradvayam /
nanu mahatā yatnena parikarabandhaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ yuktamevaṃ nirdeśṭuṃ brahma? bāḍham;kasmāt? na hi-yasmāt, 'iti na, iti na'ityetasmāt-itīti vyāptavyaprakārā nakāradvayaviṣayā nirdiśyante, yathā grāmo grāmo ramaṇīya iti, anyatparaṃ nirdeśanaṃ nāsti;tasmādayameva nirdeśo brahmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when the desire to know in every direction — [regarding] place, time, and so forth — has been removed through the negation of all limiting adjuncts, then, like a lump of salt of one taste, [<s>Brahman</s>] is a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>) of one taste, without an inside, without an outside, the truth of truth — 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' — and the desire to know ceases in every direction, [and] cognition remains established in the self alone. Therefore, the two negation particles in '<s>neti neti</s>' serve the purpose of comprehensive inclusion (<s>vīpsā</s>). [Objection:] But is it proper to designate <s>Brahman</s> in this way, after making such elaborate preparations? [Reply:] Indeed it is — why? Because — since — 'not this, not this' — the two negation particles, whose scope is the totality of what is to be negated, designate [by negation] in the manner of comprehensiveness; just as [one says] 'every village is delightful' — there is no other, higher designation. Therefore, this alone is the description of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: yaduktam- 'tasyopaniṣatsatyasya satyam'iti, evaṃprakāreṇa satyasya satyaṃ tatparaṃ brahma;ato yuktamuktaṃ nāmadheyaṃ brahmaṇaḥ, nāmaiva nāmadheyam;kiṃ tat? satyasya satyaṃ prāṇā vai satyaṃ teṣāmeṣa satyamiti //6//
children.translated_text: What was said — 'its <s>Upaniṣad</s> [secret name] is the truth of truth' — in that manner, the truth of truth is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, the designation (<s>nāmadheya</s>) of <s>Brahman</s> is fittingly stated — a designation that is a name indeed. What is that? 'The truth of truth — the <s>prāṇas</s> (life-breaths) are indeed truth; of them, this [<s>Brahman</s>] is the truth.' (BṛUp 2.3.6)

children.text: iti tṛtīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //3//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. (3)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.1
children.translated_text: START BrhUp 2,4.1

children.text:
ātmetyevopāsīta;tadeva tasminsarvasminpadanīyamātmatattvam, yasmātpreyaḥ putrādeḥ-ityupanyastasya vākyasya vyākhyānaviṣaye sambandhaprayojane abhihite- 'tadātmānamevāvedahaṃ brahmāsmīti tasmāttatsarvamabhavat'iti;evaṃ pratyagātmā brahmavidyāyā viṣaya ityetadupanyastam /
avidyāyāśca viṣayaḥ- 'anyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmīti na sa veda'ityārabhya cāturvarṇyapravibhāgādinimittapāṅktakarmasādhyasādhanalakṣaṇo bījāṅkuravadvyākṛtāvyākṛtasvabhāvo nāmarūpakarmātmakaḥ saṃsāraḥ 'trayaṃ vā idaṃ nāma rūpaṃ karma'ityupasaṃhṛtaḥ /
śāsrīya utkarṣalakṣaṇo brahmalokānto 'dhobhāvaśca sthāvarānto 'śāsrīyaḥ pūrvameva pradarśitaḥ- 'dvayā ha'ityādinā /
etasmādavidyāviṣayādviraktasya pratyagātmaviṣayabrahmavidyāyāmadhikāraḥ kathaṃ nāma syāditi-tṛtīye 'dhyāye upasaṃhṛtaḥ samasto 'vidyāviṣayaḥ /
caturthe tu brahmavidyāviṣayaṃ pratyagātmānam 'brahma te bravāṇi'iti 'brahma jñapayiṣyāmi'iti ca prastutya, tadbrahmaikamadvayaṃ sarvaviśeṣaśūnyaṃ kriyākārakaphalasvabhāvasatyaśabdavācyāśeṣabhūtadharmapratiṣedhadvāreṇa 'neti neti'iti jñāpitam /
children.translated_text:
One should meditate as the self alone' — in that very sentence, the reality of the self (<s>ātmatattva</s>) is what is to be ascertained throughout all of this. Because [it is] 'dearer than a son' and so forth — the exposition of the meaning of this sentence that was introduced [earlier] has been given with its connection and purpose. 'He knew the self: I am <s>Brahman</s>; therefore he became all' — thus the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) has been introduced as the subject of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavidyā</s>).
And the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — beginning from 'another is he, another am I — he does not know' — <s>saṃsāra</s>, whose nature consists of name, form, and action (<s>nāmarūpakarma</s>), characterized by the means and ends of the fivefold ritual action arising from the divisions of the four <s>varṇas</s> and the like, whose nature is alternately manifest and unmanifest like seed and sprout, has been concluded with 'this indeed is the triad: name, form, and action.'
The scriptural elevation up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s> and the non-scriptural downward course extending to immovable beings have been previously shown by 'the two indeed' and so forth.
From this domain of <s>avidyā</s>, for one who is disenchanted, how could qualification for the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> pertaining to the inner self arise? — the entire domain of <s>avidyā</s> has been concluded in the third <s>adhyāya</s>.
In the fourth [<s>adhyāya</s>], having introduced the inner self as the subject of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> with 'I shall tell you about <s>Brahman</s>' and 'I shall make <s>Brahman</s> known,' that <s>Brahman</s> — one, non-dual, devoid of all distinctions, empty of the nature of action, agent, and fruit, expressible by the word 'truth' — was made known through the negation of all attributes of existing things by '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this).

children.text:
asyā brahmavidyāyā aṅgatvena saṃnyāso vidhitsitaḥ, jāyāputravittādilakṣaṇaṃ pāṅktaṃ karmāvidyāviṣayaṃ yasmānnātmaprāptisādhanam; anyasādhanaṃ hyanyasmai phalasādhanāya prayujyamānaṃ pratikūlaṃ bhavati /
na hi bubhukṣāpipāsānivṛttyarthaṃ dhāvanaṃ gamanaṃ vā sādhanam; manuṣyalokapitṛlokadevalokasādhanatvena hi putrādisādhanāni śrutāni, nātmaprāptisādhanatvena /
viśeṣitatvācca; na ca brahmavido vihitāni, kāmyatvaśravaṇāt- 'etāvānvai kāmaḥ' iti /
brahmavidaścāptakāmatvādāptakāmasya kāmānupapatteḥ /
"yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ lokaḥ"iti ca śruteḥ /
children.translated_text:
Renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) is intended to be enjoined as an auxiliary (<s>aṅga</s>) of this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, since the fivefold ritual action characterized by the domain of <s>avidyā</s> — having wives, sons, wealth, and the like as its [instruments] — is not the means for the attainment of the self; for a means suited to one [goal], when applied to a different result, becomes counterproductive.
For running or walking is not the means for the removal of hunger and thirst; for sons and the like have been heard in scripture as means for the attainment of the worlds of men, ancestors, and gods — not as means for the attainment of the self.
And because [such actions] are specified [as for those with desires]; and they are not enjoined for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, because [scripture] is heard to [describe them as] objects of desire — 'this much indeed is desire.'
And because for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, who has attained all desires, desires are impossible — since one whose desires are fulfilled cannot have [further] desires.
And from the <s>śruti</s>: 'For whom this self is [their] world.'

children.text: kecittu brahmavido 'pyeṣaṇāsambandhaṃ varṇayanti, tairbṛhadāraṇyakaṃ na śrutam; putrādyeṣaṇānāmavidvadviṣayatvam; vidyāviṣaye ca-"yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ lokaḥ"ityataḥ"kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmaḥ"ityeṣa vibhāgastairna śrutaḥ śrutyā kṛtaḥ; sarvakriyākārakaphalopamardasvarūpāyāṃ ca vidyāyāṃ satyām, saha kāryeṇāvidyāyā anupapattilakṣaṇaśca virodhastairna vijñātaḥ /
vyāsavākyaṃ ca tairna śrutam; karmavidyāsvarūpayorvidyāvidyātmakayoḥ pratikūlavartanaṃ virodhaḥ;
children.translated_text: And the statement of <s>Vyāsa</s> has not been heard by them: the opposition between <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), which are of the nature of <s>avidyā</s> and <s>vidyā</s> respectively, is a counterproductive antagonism;

children.text: "yadidaṃ vedavacanaṃ kuru karma tyajeti ca /
children.translated_text: "This Vedic utterance says both 'perform action' and 'renounce it' —

children.text: kāṃ gatiṃ vidyayā yānti kāṃ ca gacchanti karmaṇā //
children.translated_text: to what destination do they go by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), and where do they go by <s>karma</s> (action)?

But some describe a connection between the desires (<s>eṣaṇās</s>) and the knower of <s>Brahman</s> as well — they have not [properly] heard the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>; the desires for sons and the rest pertain to the domain of the ignorant; and in the domain of knowledge — 'for whom this self is [their] world' — from this [passage], 'what shall we do with offspring?' — this division made by the <s>śruti</s> has not been heard by them. And when <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), whose nature is the destruction of all action, agency, and results, is [established as] real, the impossibility of <s>avidyā</s> together with its effects — this contradiction in the form of impossibility has not been understood by them.

children.text: etadvai śrotumicchāmi tadbhavānprabravītu me /
children.translated_text: This indeed I wish to hear; may you, venerable sir, tell me this.

children.text: etāvanyonyavairūpye vartete pratikūlataḥ /
children.translated_text: These two, being of contrary natures, operate in opposition to each other."

children.text: "ityevaṃ pṛṣṭasya prativacanena - "karmaṇā badhyate janturvidyayā ca vimucyate /
children.translated_text: Thus, having been questioned, [<s>Vyāsa</s>] demonstrated the opposition through his reply — "A creature is bound by <s>karma</s> (action), and is liberated by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge);

children.text: tasmātkarma na kurvanti yatayaḥ pāradarśinaḥḥ //
children.translated_text: therefore the ascetics (<s>yatis</s>), who see the farther shore, do not perform action."

children.text:
ityevamādivirodhaḥ pradarśitaḥ /
tasmānna sādhanāntarasahitā brahmavidyā puruṣārthasādhanam, sarvavirodhāt, sādhananirapekṣaiva puruṣārthasādhanamiti pārivrājyaṃ sarvasādhanasaṃnyāsalakṣaṇamaṅgatvena vidhitsyate /
etāvadeva amṛtatvasādhanam ityavadhāraṇāt, ṣaṣṭhasamāptau, liṅgācca-karmī sanyājñavalkyaḥ pravavrājeti /
maitreyyai ca karmasādhanarahitāyai sādhanatvenāmṛtatvasya brahmavidyopadeśād vittanindāvacanācca /
yadi hyamṛtatvasādhanaṃ karma syād vittasādhyaṃ pāṅktaṃ karma, iti tannindāvacanamaniṣṭaṃ syāt /
yadi tu paritityājayiṣitaṃ karma, tato yuktā tatsādhananindā /
children.translated_text:
Thus and in other ways the opposition has been demonstrated.
Therefore, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> combined with other means is not the means to the highest human goal, because of contradiction with everything; rather, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, being independent of [all other] means, is itself the means to the highest human goal — thus <s>pārivrājya</s> (the mendicant life), characterized by the renunciation of all means, is intended to be enjoined as an auxiliary.
Because of the definitive statement 'this much alone is the means to immortality' at the conclusion of the sixth [<s>adhyāya</s>]; and from the indicative sign (<s>liṅga</s>) — <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, who was a performer of rituals, renounced [the world] and became a wandering monk.
