And because the teaching of the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> was given to <s>Maitreyī</s>, who was free from the means of ritual action, as the means to immortality; and from the statement disparaging wealth.
For if <s>karma</s> (action) — the fivefold ritual accomplished through wealth — were the means to immortality, then the statement disparaging it would be undesirable.
But if [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] intended to make [<s>Maitreyī</s>] abandon <s>karma</s>, then the disparagement of its means [i.e., wealth] is fitting.

children.text:
karmādhikāranimittavarṇāśramādipratyayopamardācca-"brahma taṃ parā dāt" "kṣatraṃ taṃ parādāt"ityādeḥ /
na hi brahmakṣatrādyātmapratyayopamarde, brāhmaṇenedaṃ kartavyaṃ kṣatriyeṇedaṃ kartavyamiti viṣayābhāvādātmānaṃ labhate vidhiḥ /
yasyaiva puruṣasyopamarditaḥ pratyayo brahmakṣatrādyātmaviṣayaḥ, tasya tatpratyayasaṃnyāsāt tatkāryāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ karmasādhanānāṃ ca arthaprāptaśca sanyāsaḥ /
tasmādātmajñānāṅgatvena saṃnyāsavidhitsayaiva ākhyāyikeyamārabhyate-
children.translated_text:
And because the notions of <s>varṇa</s>, <s>āśrama</s>, and the like — which are the basis for qualification for ritual action — are destroyed [by <s>brahmavidyā</s>]; from [passages such as] '<s>Brahman</s> delivered him beyond' and 'the ruling power delivered him beyond.'
For when the notion of the self as <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, and the like is destroyed, injunctions such as 'a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should do this' and 'a <s>kṣatriya</s> should do this' — in the absence of a subject — cannot find a locus for the injunction.
For that very person whose notion of the self as <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s>, and the like has been destroyed — through the renunciation of that notion, the renunciation of the actions [associated with it] and of the means of those actions follows as a natural consequence.
Therefore, with the intention of enjoining renunciation as an auxiliary of the knowledge of the self, this narrative (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>) is commenced —

children.text:
maitreyīti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ -- udyāsyan vā are 'ham asmāt sthānād asmi |
hanta te 'nayā kātyāyanyāntaṃ karavāṇīti || BrhUp_2,4.1 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Maitreyī</s>!' said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, 'I am about to depart from this station.
Come, let me make a settlement between you and this <s>Kātyāyanī</s>.' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.1 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.1
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.1:]

children.text:
maitreyīti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ-maitreyīṃ svabhāryāmāmantritavānyājñavalkyo nāma ṛṣiḥ;udyāsyannūrdhvaṃ yāsyanpārivrājyākhyamāśramāntaraṃ vai /
are iti sambodhanam /
aham, asmādgārhasthyāt, sthānādāśramāt, ūrdhvaṃ gantumicchannasmi
children.translated_text:
'<s>Maitreyī</s>!' said <s>Yājñavalkya</s> — <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, the <s>ṛṣi</s> by name, addressed his own wife <s>Maitreyī</s>. 'I am about to go forth (<s>udyāsyan</s>)' — I am about to go upward, that is, to the other stage of life (<s>āśrama</s>) called <s>pārivrājya</s> (the mendiciant order). Indeed!
'Are' is a term of address.
'I, from this household (<s>gārhasthya</s>), from this station (<s>āśrama</s>), am about to go forth' —

children.text: bhavāmi;ato hantānumatiṃ prārthayāmi te tava;kiñcānyatte tavānayā dvitīyayā bhāryayā kātyāyanyāntaṃ vicchedaṃ karavāṇi;patidvāreṇa yuvayormayā sambandhasya vicchedaṃ karavāṇi dravyavibhāgaṃ kṛtvā;vittena saṃvibhajya yuvāṃ gamiṣyāmi //1//
children.translated_text: 'I am [about to become a renunciant]; therefore, come (<s>hanta</s>), I seek your consent. Moreover, let me make a settlement (<s>antam</s>), a separation, between you and this other wife, <s>Kātyāyanī</s>. Through the medium of the husband, let me make a separation of the connection between you two and myself by dividing the property. Having distributed the wealth between you two, I shall depart.' || 1 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 2.4.2]

children.text:
sā hovāca maitreyī -- yan nu ma iyaṃ bhagoḥ sarvā pṛthivī vittena pūrṇā syāt kathaṃ tenāmṛtā syām iti |
neti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
yathaivopakaraṇavatāṃ jīvitaṃ tathaiva te jīvitaṃ syāt |
amṛtatvasya tu nāśāsti vitteneti || BrhUp_2,4.2 ||
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Maitreyī</s> said: 'If, venerable sir, this entire earth filled with wealth were mine, would I be immortal through it?'
'No,' said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
'Your life would be just like that of those who have [abundant] means.
But there is no hope of immortality through wealth.' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.2 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.2
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.2:]

children.text: sā evamuktā hovāca-yadyadi 'nu'iti vitarke, me mama iyaṃ pṛthivī, bhagoḥ-bhagavan, sarvā sāgaraparikṣiptā vittena dhanena pūrṇā syāt;katham? na kathañcanetyākṣepārthaḥ, praśnārtho vā, tena pṛthivīpūrṇavittasādhyena karmaṇāgnihotrādinā amṛtā kiṃ syāmiti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: She, having been thus addressed, said — 'if indeed (<s>yadi</s>)' — '<s>nu</s>' is used in the sense of deliberation — 'mine (<s>me</s>), this earth, venerable sir (<s>bhagoḥ</s>), all of it, surrounded by the ocean, were full (<s>pūrṇā</s>) of wealth (<s>vittena</s>)'; 'how?' — this is used in the sense of denial, meaning 'in no way'; or it is used in the sense of a question — 'would I be immortal through that, through the ritual action such as <s>Agnihotra</s> accomplished by wealth sufficient to fill the earth?' — thus the connection with the distant [part of the sentence].

children.text: pratyuvāca yājñavalkyaḥ-kathamiti yadyākṣepārtham, anumodanaṃ neti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ-kathamiti yadyākṣepārtham, anumodanaṃ neti hovāca yājñavalkya iti;praśnaścetprativacanārtham;naiva syā amṛtā, kiṃ tarhi? yathaiva loke upakaraṇavatāṃ sādhanavatāṃ jīvitaṃ sukhopāyabhogasampannam;tathaiva tadvadeva tava jīvitaṃ syāt;amṛtatvasya tu nāśā manasāpyasti vittena vittasādhyena karmaṇeti //2//
children.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied: if 'how' (<s>katham</s>) is meant in the sense of denial, then 'no' (<s>neti</s>) said <s>Yājñavalkya</s> is an endorsement; if it is a question, then it is a response. You would never be immortal. Rather, what then? Just as in the world the life of those who possess means (<s>upakaraṇavat</s>), who have [abundant] resources, is endowed with the enjoyment of comfortable means — just so, exactly like that, would your life be. But of immortality there is no hope (<s>āśā</s>) — not even mentally — through wealth or through ritual action accomplished by wealth. || 2 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 2.4.3]

children.text:
sā hovāca maitreyī -- yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syāṃ kim ahaṃ tena kuryām |
yad eva bhagavān veda tad eva me brūhīti || BrhUp_2,4.3 ||
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Maitreyī</s> said: 'That by which I would not become immortal — what shall I do with that?
Tell me, venerable sir, just that which you know [to be the means to immortality].' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.3 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.3
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.3:]

children.text: sā hovāca maitreyī;evamuktā pratyuvāca maitreyī-yadyevaṃ yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syām, kimahaṃ tena vittena kuryām? yadeva bhagavānkevalamamṛtatvasādhanaṃ veda, tadevāmṛtatvasādhanaṃ me mahyaṃ brūhi //3//
children.translated_text: She, <s>Maitreyī</s>, said — having been thus addressed, <s>Maitreyī</s> replied: 'If this is so, then that by which I would not become immortal — what shall I do with that wealth? That which you, venerable sir, know as solely the means to immortality — tell that, the means to immortality, to me.' || 3 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 2.4.4]

children.text:
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ -- priyā batāre naḥ satī priyaṃ bhāṣase |
ehy āssva |
vyākhyāsyāmi te |
vyācakṣāṇasya tu me nididhyāsasveti || BrhUp_2,4.4 ||
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'Dear indeed you are to us, and dear is what you speak.
Come, sit down.
I shall explain it to you.
But as I expound, do meditate upon it.' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.4 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.4
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.4:]

children.text:
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ /
evaṃ vittasādhye 'mṛtatvasādhane pratyākhyāte, yājñavalkyaḥ svābhiprāyasampattau tuṣṭa āha;sa hovāca-priyeṣāṭā, batetyanukampyāha, are maitreyi no 'smākaṃ pūrvamapi priyā satī bhavantī idānīṃ priyameva cittānukūlaṃ bhāṣase;ata ehyāḥsvopaviśa vyākhyāsyāmi-yatte tava iṣṭam amṛtatvasādhanam ātmajñānaṃ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said — when the means to immortality through the [ritual actions] accomplished by wealth had been rejected, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, pleased at the agreement with his own intention, said: 'Dear one (<s>priyā</s>), <s>iṣāṭā</s>!' He says '<s>bata</s>' out of compassion. 'O <s>Maitreyī</s>, being dear to us already before, you now speak what is truly dear, what is agreeable to the mind. Therefore, come (<s>ehi</s>), sit down (<s>āssva</s>), I shall explain — that which is desired by you, the means to immortality, the knowledge of the self (<s>ātmajñāna</s>) —

children.text: kathayiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: I shall tell you.'

children.text: vyācakṣāṇasya tu me mama vyākhyānaṃ kurvato nididhyāsasva vākyānyarthato niścayena dhyātumiccheti //4//
children.translated_text: 'But as I expound — while I am giving the explanation — meditate upon (<s>nididhyāsasva</s>) it; that is, desire to contemplate the sentences with certainty as to their meaning.' || 4 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 2.4.5]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- na vā are patyuḥ kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavati |
na vā are jāyāyai kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavati |
na vā are putrāṇāṃ kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are vittasya kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are brahmaṇaḥ kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are kṣatrasya kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are lokānāṃ kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are devānāṃ kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are bhūtānāṃ kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanti |
na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati |
ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyo maitreyi |
ātmano vā are darśanena śravaṇena matyā vijñānenedaṃ sarvaṃ viditam || BrhUp_2,4.5 ||
children.translated_text:
He said: 'Verily, a husband is dear not for the sake of the husband, but for the sake of the self is the husband dear.
Verily, a wife is dear not for the sake of the wife, but for the sake of the self is the wife dear.
Verily, sons are dear not for the sake of the sons, but for the sake of the self are sons dear.
Verily, wealth is dear not for the sake of the wealth, but for the sake of the self is wealth dear.
Verily, the <s>brahmin</s> class is dear not for the sake of the <s>brahmin</s> class, but for the sake of the self is the <s>brahmin</s> class dear.
Verily, the <s>kṣatriya</s> class is dear not for the sake of the <s>kṣatriya</s> class, but for the sake of the self is the <s>kṣatriya</s> class dear.
Verily, the worlds are dear not for the sake of the worlds, but for the sake of the self are the worlds dear.
Verily, the gods are dear not for the sake of the gods, but for the sake of the self are the gods dear.
Verily, beings are dear not for the sake of the beings, but for the sake of the self are beings dear.
Verily, everything is dear not for the sake of everything, but for the sake of the self is everything dear.
Verily, the self should be seen, should be heard, should be reflected upon, should be meditated upon, O <s>Maitreyī</s>.
Verily, by the seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing of the self, all this is known.' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.5 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.5
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.5:]

children.text:
sa hovāca-amṛtatvasādhanaṃ vairāgyamupadidikṣurjāyāpatiputrādibhyo virāgamutpādayati tatsaṃnyāsāya /
na vai-vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhasmaraṇārthaḥ;prasiddhamevaitalloke;patyurbhartuḥ kāmāya prayojanāya jāyāyāḥ patiḥ priyo na bhavati, kiṃ tarhyātmanastu kāmāya prayojanāyaiva bhāryāyāḥ patiḥ priyo bhavati /
tathā na vā are jāyāyā ityādi samānamanyat, na vā are putrāṇām, na vā are vittasya, na vā are brahmaṇaḥ, na vā are kṣatrasya, na vā are devānām, na vā are bhūtānām, na vā are sarvasya, pūrvaṃ pūrvaṃ yathāsanne prītisādhane vacanam;tatra tatreṣṭataratvādvairāgyasya;sarvagrahaṇamuktānuktārtham /
children.translated_text:
He said — wishing to teach the means to immortality, namely dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] generates disenchantment with wives, husbands, sons, and the like, for the purpose of their renunciation.
'Verily (<s>vai</s>)' — the word <s>vai</s> is used for recalling what is well-known; this is indeed well-known in the world. Not for the sake of the husband (<s>pati</s>), for the purpose of the husband, is the husband dear to the wife; rather, for the sake of the self alone, for the purpose of the self, is the husband dear to the wife.
Likewise 'verily, not for the sake of the wife' and so forth — the rest is the same; 'verily, not for the sake of sons,' 'verily, not for the sake of wealth,' 'verily, not for the sake of the <s>brahmin</s> class,' 'verily, not for the sake of the <s>kṣatriya</s> class,' 'verily, not for the sake of the gods,' 'verily, not for the sake of beings,' 'verily, not for the sake of everything' — the statement proceeds from what is nearest to what is progressively more remote as the instrument of affection; in each case, dispassion is [generated] because of the greater desirability [of the self]. The word 'everything' (<s>sarva</s>) covers both what has been mentioned and what has not.

children.text:
tasmāllokaprasiddhametat-ātmaiva priyaḥ, nānyat /
'tadetatpreyaḥ putrāt'ityupanyastam, tasyaitad vṛttisthānīyaṃ prapañcitam /
tasmādātmaprītisādhanatvādgauṇī anyatra prītiḥ, ātmanyeva mukhyā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, because [other things] serve as instruments of the self's affection, the affection for other things is secondary (<s>gauṇī</s>); [only] the affection for the self is primary (<s>mukhyā</s>).

children.text: tasmādātmā vai are draṣṭavyo darśanārhaḥ, darśanaviṣayamāpādayitavyaḥ;śrotavyaḥ pūrvamācāryata āgamataśca;paścānmantavyastarkataḥ;tato nididhyāsitavyo niścayena dhyātavyaḥ;evaṃ hyasau dṛṣṭo bhavati śravaṇamanananididhyāsanasādhanairnirvartitaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the self (<s>ātman</s>) is verily to be seen (<s>draṣṭavya</s>), worthy of being seen, to be brought within the range of vision; [it is] to be heard (<s>śrotavya</s>), first from the teacher and from scripture; thereafter to be reflected upon (<s>mantavya</s>), through reasoning; and then to be meditated upon (<s>nididhyāsitavya</s>), to be contemplated with certainty. For thus is it [truly] seen — when the means of hearing, reflection, and meditation (<s>śravaṇa</s>, <s>manana</s>, <s>nididhyāsana</s>) have been accomplished.

children.text: yadaikatvamatānyupagatāni, tadā samyagdarśanaṃ brahmaikatvaviṣayaṃ prasidati, nānyathā śravaṇamātreṇa /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When the views of oneness have been accepted, then right vision pertaining to the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> becomes clear — not otherwise, by mere hearing alone.

children.text: yadbrahmakṣatrādi karmanimittaṃ varṇāśramādilakṣaṇam ātmavidyādhyāropitapratyayaviṣayaṃ kriyākārakaphalātmakamavidyāpratyayaviṣayam-rajjavāmva sarpapratyayaḥ, tadupamardanārtham āha-ātmani khalvare maitreyi dṛṣṭe śrute mate vijñāte idaṃ sarvaṃ viditaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is in the domain of action — characterized by <s>varṇa</s> (social order), <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), and the like, having <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>kṣatriya</s> and the like as its characteristic, the object of a cognition superimposed upon the knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>, consisting of action, agents, and results, the object of the cognition of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — like the cognition of a snake on a rope — for the purpose of destroying that, [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] says: 'When indeed, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, the <s>Ātman</s> has been seen, heard, reflected upon, and known — all this is known.' (5)

Therefore, this is well-known in the world: the self alone is dear, nothing else.
'This is dearer than a son' — this was introduced [earlier], and this [present passage] is its detailed exposition.

children.text:
nanu kathamanyasminvidite 'nyadviditaṃ bhavati? naiṣa doṣaḥ;na hi ātmavyatirekeṇānyatkiñcidasti ;yadyasti na tadviditaṃ syāt;na tvanyadasti;ātmaiva tu sarvam;tasmātsarvamātmani vidite viditaṃ syāt /
kathaṃ punarātmaiva sarvamityetacchrāvayati-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But how, when one thing is known, is another known? This is not a fault; for apart from the <s>Ātman</s>, nothing else exists. If something else existed, it would not be known [merely by knowing the <s>Ātman</s>]. But there is nothing else — the <s>Ātman</s> alone is everything. Therefore, when the <s>Ātman</s> is known, everything would be known. But how is the <s>Ātman</s> everything? He explains this:

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.4.6]

children.text:
brahma taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmano brahma veda |
kṣatraṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ kṣatraṃ veda |
lokās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano lokān veda |
devās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano devān veda |
bhūtāni taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano bhūtāni veda |
sarvaṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ sarvaṃ veda |
idaṃ brahmedaṃ kṣatram ime lokā ime devā imāni bhūtānīdaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātmā || BrhUp_2,4.6 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class) forsakes him who knows <s>Brahman</s> as other than the <s>Ātman</s>. The <s>kṣatra</s> (warrior class) forsakes him who knows the <s>kṣatra</s> as other than the <s>Ātman</s>. The worlds forsake him who knows the worlds as other than the <s>Ātman</s>. The gods forsake him who knows the gods as other than the <s>Ātman</s>. The beings forsake him who knows the beings as other than the <s>Ātman</s>. Everything forsakes him who knows everything as other than the <s>Ātman</s>. This <s>Brahman</s>, this <s>kṣatra</s>, these worlds, these gods, these beings, this everything — is this <s>Ātman</s>. (BṛUp 2.4.6)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.6
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.4.6:]

children.text: brahma brāhmaṇajātistaṃ puruṣaṃ parādātparādadhyātparākuryāt;kam? yo 'nyatrātmana ātmasvarūpavyatirekeṇa-ātmaiva na bhavatīyaṃ brāhmaṇajātiriti-tāṃ yo veda, taṃ parādadhyātsā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Brahma</s>' — the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class — forsakes, abandons, rejects that person. Whom? One who knows <s>Brahman</s> as other than the <s>Ātman</s> — as distinct from the essential nature of the <s>Ātman</s>, [thinking] 'This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class is not the <s>Ātman</s> itself' — one who knows it thus, him that

children.text: brāhmaṇajātiranātmasvarūpeṇa māṃ paśyatīti;paramātmāhi sarveṣāmātmā /
children.translated_text: <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class [forsakes, thinking:] 'He sees me as having a nature other than the <s>Ātman</s>.' For the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) is the <s>Ātman</s> of all.

children.text: tathā kṣatraṃ kṣatriyajātiḥ, tathā lokāḥ, devāḥ, bhūtāni, sarvam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, the <s>kṣatra</s> — the <s>kṣatriya</s> class; similarly, the worlds, the gods, the beings, everything.

children.text: idaṃ brahmeti-yānyanukrāntāni tāni sarvāṇi, ātmaiva, yadayamātmā-yo 'yamātmā draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavya iti prakṛtaḥ;yasmādātmano jāyata ātmanyeva līyata ātmamayaṃ ca sthitikāle, ātmavyatirekeṇāgrahaṇāt, ātmaiva sarvam //6//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This is <s>Brahman</s>' — all those that have been enumerated, all of them are the <s>Ātman</s> alone. 'That which is this <s>Ātman</s>' — this <s>Ātman</s> which has been introduced as 'to be seen, to be heard,' and which is the topic under discussion. Since [everything] is born from the <s>Ātman</s>, dissolves into the <s>Ātman</s> alone, and during the period of subsistence is constituted by the <s>Ātman</s>, and because it is not apprehended apart from the <s>Ātman</s> — the <s>Ātman</s> alone is everything. (6)

children.text:
kathaṃ punaridānīmidaṃ sarvamātmaiveti grahītuṃ śakyate? cinmātrānugamātsarvatra citsvarūpataiveti gamyate /
tatra dṛṣṭānta ucyate /
tatra dṛṣṭānta ucyate-yatsvarūpavyatirekeṇāgrahaṇaṃ yasya, tasya tadātmatvameva loke dṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But how can all this be grasped as being the <s>Ātman</s> alone? Because consciousness (<s>cit</s>) alone pervades everywhere, it follows that everything has the nature of consciousness. In that regard, an example is stated. And the principle observed in the world is: that which cannot be apprehended apart from something else is of the nature of that [other thing].

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.4.7]

children.text:
sa yathā dundubher hanyamānasya na bāhyāñ chabdāñ chaknuyād grahaṇāya |
dundubhes tu grahaṇena dundubhyāghātasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ || BrhUp_2,4.7 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, when a drum (<s>dundubhi</s>) is being struck, one would not be able to grasp the external sounds [separately]; but by grasping the drum, or the one who strikes the drum, the sound is grasped. (BṛUp 2.4.7)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.7
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.4.7:]

children.text: sa yathā-sa iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ, loke yathā dundubherbheryādeḥ, hanyamānasya tāḍyamānasya daṇḍādinā, na, bāhyāñchabdān bahirbhūtāñchabdaviśeṣān dundubhiśabdasāmānyānniṣkṛṣṭān dundubhiśabdaviśeṣān na śaknuyād grahaṇāya grahītum;dundubhestu grahaṇena, dundubhiśabdā eta iti, śabdaviśeṣā gṛhītā bhavanti, dundubhiśabdasāmānyavyatirekeṇābhāvātteṣām /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Sa yathā</s>' — '<s>sa</s>' introduces the example. In the world, just as — of a drum, a <s>bherī</s> (kettledrum) and the like, being struck, being beaten with a stick and the like — one would not be able to grasp the external sounds, the specific sounds that exist outside, extracted as particular sounds of the drum from the general sound of the drum — one cannot grasp them separately. But by grasping the drum — [understanding] 'these are the sounds of the drum' — the specific sounds are grasped, because of their non-existence apart from the general sound of the drum.

children.text: dundubhyāghātasya vā, dunduberāhananam āghātaḥ, dundubhyāghātaviśiṣṭasya śabdasāmānyasya grahaṇena tadgatā viśeṣā gṛhītā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Or, by grasping the striking of the drum — the beating of the drum, the striking — by grasping the general sound as qualified by the striking of the drum, the specific sounds therein are grasped —

children.text: bhavanti, na tu ta eva nirbhidya grahītuṃ śakyante, viśeṣarūpeṇābhāvātteṣām /
children.translated_text: but they cannot be grasped by extracting [them] independently, because of their non-existence in a distinct form.

children.text: tathā prajñānavyatirekeṇa svapnajāgaritayorna kaścidvastuviśeṣo gṛhyate;tasmātprajñānavyatirekeṇa abhāvo yuktasteṣām //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, apart from consciousness (<s>prajñāna</s>), no particular object in the dream or waking states is apprehended. Therefore, the non-existence of those [objects] apart from consciousness is justified. (7)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.4.8]

children.text: sa yathā śaṅkhasya dhmāyamānasya na bāhyāñ chabdāñ chaknuyād grahaṇāya śaṅkhasya tu grahaṇena śaṅkhadhmasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ || BrhUp_2,4.8 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, when a conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>) is being blown, one would not be able to grasp the external sounds [separately]; but by grasping the conch, or the one who blows the conch, the sound is grasped. (BṛUp 2.4.8)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.8
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.4.8:]

children.text: tathā sa yathā śaṅkhasya dhmāyamānasya śabdena saṃyojyamānasya āpūryamāṇasya na bāhyāñchabdāñchaknuyādityevamādi pūrvavat //8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, just as of a conch being blown — being filled with breath, being sounded — one would not be able to grasp the external sounds and so forth — as before. (8)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.9
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.4.9]

children.text: sa yathā vīṇāyai vādyamānāyai na bāhyāñ chabdāñ chaknuyād grahaṇāya vīṇāyai tu grahaṇena vīṇāvādasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ || BrhUp_2,4.9 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, when a <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) is being played, one would not be able to grasp the external sounds [separately]; but by grasping the <s>vīṇā</s>, or the playing of the <s>vīṇā</s>, the sound is grasped. (BṛUp 2.4.9)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.9
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.4.9:]

children.text: tathā vīṇāyai vādyamānāyai-vīmāyā vādyamānāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, of a <s>vīṇā</s> being played —

children.text: anekadṛṣṭāntopādānamiha sāmānyabahutvakhyāpanārtham-aneke hi vilakṣaṇāścetanācetanarūpāḥ sāmānyaviśeṣāḥ-teṣāṃ pāramparyagatyā yathaikasminmahāsāmānye 'ntarbhāvaḥ prajñānaghane, kathaṃ nāma pradarśayitavya iti;dundubhiśaṅkhavīṇāśabdasāmānyaviśeṣāṇāṃ yathā śabdatve 'ntarbhāvaḥ, evaṃ sthitikāle tāvatsāmānyaviśeṣāvyatirekād brahmaikatvaṃ śakyamavagantum //9//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The adduction of multiple examples here is for the purpose of demonstrating the multiplicity of the general [categories]. For the general and particular [categories] are many and diverse, consisting of sentient and insentient forms. How to demonstrate their subsumption, through successive stages, into one great general [category] — the mass of pure consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>)? Just as the specific drum-sounds, conch-sounds, and <s>vīṇā</s>-sounds are subsumed under the general [category] of sound — so too, during the period of subsistence, the oneness of <s>Brahman</s> can be understood through the non-separability of the general and the particular. (9)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.10
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.4.10]

children.text:
evamutpattikāle prāgutpatterbrahmaiveti śakyamavagantum /
yathāgnervisphuliṅgadhūmāṅgārārciṣāṃ prāgvibhāgādagnireveti bhavatyagnyekatvam, evaṃ jagannāmarūpavikṛtaṃ pragutpatteḥ prajñānaghana eveti yuktaṃ grahītumityetaducyate-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, at the time of origination, prior to origination, it can be understood that [everything] is <s>Brahman</s> alone. Just as sparks, smoke, embers, and flames — prior to their separation from fire — are fire alone, and there is oneness of fire; so too, the world — modified into name and form — prior to its origination, is properly grasped as the mass of pure consciousness alone. This is what is said. As an example for demonstrating [the state at the time of] origination:

children.text:
sa yathārdraidhāgner abhyāhitāt pṛthag dhūmā viniścaranty eva vā are 'sya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitam etad yad ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇy anuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānani |
asyaivaitāni niśvasitāni || BrhUp_2,4.10 ||
children.translated_text: Just as from a fire kindled with damp fuel, various kinds of smoke issue forth — even so, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, the breath of this great Being is that which is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>, the <s>Itihāsa</s> (history), the <s>Purāṇa</s> (ancient lore), <s>Vidyā</s> (sciences), the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, the <s>ślokas</s> (verses), the <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms), the <s>anuvyākhyānas</s> (explanations), and the <s>vyākhyānas</s> (commentaries). From this [great Being] alone are all these breathed forth. (BṛUp 2.4.10)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.10
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.4.10:]

children.text:
sa yathā-ārdraidhāgneḥ, ārdrairedhobhiriddho 'gnirārdraidhāgniḥ, tasmāt, abhyāhitātpṛthagdhūmāḥ, pṛthagnānāprakāram, dhūmagrahaṇaṃ visphulihgādipradarśanārtham, dhūmavisphuliṅgādayo viniścaranti vinirgacchanti /
evam-yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ, are maitreyyasya paramātmanaḥ prakṛtasya mahato bhūtasya niśvasitametat, niśvasitamiva niśvasitam;yathā aprayatnenaiva puruṣaniśvāso bhavatyevaṃ vā are /
kiṃ tanniśvasitamiva tato jātamityucyate-yadṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasaḥ-caturvidhaṃ mantrajātam, itihāsa ityurvaśīpurūravasoḥ saṃvādādiḥ-"urvaśīhāpsarāḥ"ityādibrāhmaṇameva, purāṇam"asadvā idamagra āsīt"ityādi, vidyā devajanavidyā vedaḥ so 'yamityādyā, upaniṣadaḥ"priyamityetadupāsīta"ityādyāḥ, ślokā brāhmaṇaprabhavā mantrāḥ"tadete ślokāḥ"ityādayaḥ; sūtrāṇi vastusaṅgraha vākyāni vede yathā-"ātmetyevopāsīta"ityādīni, anuvyākhyānāni mantravivaraṇāni, vyākhyānānyarthavādāḥ, athavā vastusaṅgrahavākyavivaraṇānyanuvyākhyānāni, yathā caturthādhyāye 'ātmetyevopāsīta' ityasya, yathā vā 'anyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmīti na sa veda yathā paśurevam' ityasyāyamevādhyāyaśeṣaḥ, mantravivaraṇāni vyākhyānāni, evamaṣṭavidhaṃ brāhmaṇam /
evaṃ mantrabrāhmaṇayoreva grahaṇam, niyataracanāvato vidyamānasyaiva vedasyābhivyaktiḥ puruṣaniśvāsavat, na ca puruṣabuddhiprayatnapūrvakaḥ; ataḥ pramāṇaṃ nirapekṣa eva svārthe; tasmādyattenoktaṃ tattathaiva pratipattavyam, ātmanaḥ śreya icchadbhiḥ jñānaṃ vā karma veti /
nāmaprakāśavaśā hi rūpasya vikriyāvyavasthā /

nāmarūpayoreva hi paramātmopādhibhūtayorvyākriyamāṇayoḥ salilaphenavattattvānyatvenānirvaktavyayoḥ sarvāvasthayoḥ saṃsāratvam-ityato nāmna eva niśvasitatvamuktam, tadvacanenaivetarasya niśvasitatvasiddheḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For it is name and form alone — the limiting adjuncts of the <s>Paramātman</s> — which, as they are being manifested, like the foam of water, are indefinable as either identical with or different from [<s>Brahman</s>] in all states — that constitute <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, [the text] states only the breathed-forth nature of name, since by stating that, the breathed-forth nature of the other [form] is also established.

children.text: athavā sarvasya dvaitajātasya avidyāviṣayatvamuktam-"brahma taṃ parādāt.....idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā"iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Alternatively, the statement '<s>Brahman</s> forsakes him... this everything is this <s>Ātman</s>' has declared that the entire domain of duality is within the sphere of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: tena vedasyāprāmāṇyamāśaṅkyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From that, the suspicion of the <s>Veda</s>'s lack of authority is raised.

children.text: tadāśaṅkānivṛttyarthamidamuktam? puruṣaniśvāsavadaprayatnotthitatvātpramāṇaṃ vedaḥ, na yathā anyo grantha iti //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Is this [passage about breathing forth] stated for the purpose of dispelling that suspicion? [Yes:] because the <s>Veda</s> arose without effort, like a person's breath, it is a means of valid knowledge — unlike other [human-composed] texts. (10)

[Commentary:] '<s>Sa yathā</s>' — '<s>ārdraidhāgneḥ</s>' means a fire kindled with damp fuel; from that fire, which has been heaped upon, various kinds of smoke issue forth — '<s>pṛthak</s>' means in diverse ways; the mention of smoke is for the purpose of indicating sparks and the like too; they issue forth, they emerge. 'Even so' — as in this example — O <s>Maitreyī</s>, of this supreme <s>Ātman</s> under discussion, the great Being, this is the breath — the breath, as it were. Just as a person's breath occurs without effort, even so. What is that which is breathed forth, as it were, born from it? The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, and the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s> — the fourfold collection of <s>mantras</s>. <s>Itihāsa</s> — the dialogue of <s>Urvaśī</s> and <s>Purūravas</s> and the like — which is itself part of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, beginning with '<s>Urvaśī</s>, the <s>Apsaras</s>...' <s>Purāṇa</s> — 'In the beginning, this was non-being' and the like. <s>Vidyā</s> — the <s>Devajanavdyā</s> and others: 'This <s>Veda</s> is this' and the like. <s>Upaniṣads</s> — 'One should meditate upon this as dear' and the like. <s>Ślokas</s> — the <s>mantra</s> verses originating from the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, such as 'These are the verses' and the like. <s>Sūtras</s> — concise aphoristic sentences within the <s>Veda</s>, such as '<s>ātmety evopāsīta</s>' ('one should meditate on it as the <s>Ātman</s> alone') and the like. <s>Anuvyākhyānas</s> — expositions of <s>mantras</s>. <s>Vyākhyānas</s> — the <s>arthavāda</s> passages. Or alternatively, <s>anuvyākhyānas</s> are expositions of the aphoristic sentences, as in the fourth chapter for '<s>ātmety evopāsīta</s>,' or as this very remainder of the chapter [serves as exposition for] '<s>anyo 'sāv anyo 'ham asmīti na sa veda yathā paśur evam</s>' ('He who thinks "that is one, I am another" does not know; he is like an animal'). <s>Vyākhyānas</s> are explanations of <s>mantras</s>. Thus the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is eightfold. Thus only the <s>mantras</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are referred to. The manifestation of the already existing <s>Veda</s>, which has a fixed composition, is like a person's breath — not preceded by the person's intellect and effort. Therefore, [the <s>Veda</s>] is a means of valid knowledge, independent with respect to its own subject matter. Therefore, whatever it states should be accepted accordingly by those who desire their own highest good — whether it be knowledge or action. For the arrangement of modifications of form is dependent on name, which reveals them.

children.text:
kiñcānyat, na kevalaṃ sthityutpattikālayoreva prajñānavyatirekeṇābhāvājjagato brahmatvam, pralayakāle ca /
jalabudbudaphenādīnāmiva salilavyatirekeṇābhāvaḥ, evaṃ prajñānavyatirekeṇa tatkāryāṇāṃ nāmarūpakarmaṇāṃ tasminneva līyamānānāmabhāvaḥ /
tasmādekameva brahma prajñānaghanamekarasaṃ pratipattavyamityata āha /
pralayapradarśanāya dṛṣṭāntaḥ-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of the world [follows] not only from its non-existence apart from consciousness during the periods of subsistence and origination, but also at the time of dissolution. Just as bubbles, foam, and the like have no existence apart from water — so too, name, form, and action, which are the effects of that [<s>Brahman</s>], dissolving into it, have no existence apart from consciousness. Therefore, <s>Brahman</s> alone — the mass of consciousness, of one taste — is to be realized. Thus [the text] says. As an example for demonstrating dissolution:

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.11
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.4.11]

children.text:
sa yathā sarvāsām apāṃ samudra ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ sparśānāṃ tvag ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ gandhānāṃ nāsike ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ rasānāṃ jihvaikāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ rūpāṇāṃ cakṣur ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣaṃ śabdānāṃ śrotram ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃkalpānāṃ mana ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarvāsāṃ vidyānāṃ hṛdayam ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ hastāv ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣām ānandānām upastha ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ visargāṇāṃ pāyur ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣām adhvanāṃ pādāv ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ vedānāṃ vāg ekāyanam || BrhUp_2,4.11 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the ocean is the one destination of all waters — so the skin is the one destination of all touches; the nostrils are the one destination of all smells; the tongue is the one destination of all tastes; the eye is the one destination of all forms; the ear is the one destination of all sounds; the mind is the one destination of all intentions; the heart is the one destination of all knowledge; the hands are the one destination of all actions; the reproductive organ is the one destination of all pleasures; the excretory organ is the one destination of all discharges; the feet are the one destination of all travels; speech is the one destination of all <s>Vedas</s>. (BṛUp 2.4.11)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.11
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.4.11:]

children.text:
sa iti dṛṣṭāntaḥ;yathā yena prakāreṇa, sarvāsāṃ nadīvāpītaḍāgādigatānāmapām, samudro 'bdhirekāyanam, ekagamanamekapralayo 'vibhāgaprāptirityarthaḥ;yathāyāṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ, evaṃ sarveṣāṃ sparśānāṃ mṛdukarkaśakaṭhinapicchilādīnāṃ vāyorātmabhūtānāṃ tvagekāyanam, tvagiti tvagviṣayaṃ sparśasāmānyamātram, tasminpraviṣṭāḥ sparśaviśeṣāḥ-āpa iva samudram-tadvyatirekeṇābhāvabhūtā bhavanti;tasyaiva hi te saṃsthānamātrā āsan /
tathā tadapi sparśasāmānyamātraṃ tvakchabdavācyaṃ manaḥsaṅkalpe manoviṣayasāmānyamātre, tvagviṣaya ivasparśaviśeṣāḥ, praviṣṭaṃ tadvyatirekeṇābhāvabhūtaṃ bhavati;evaṃ manoviṣayo 'pi buddhiviṣayasāmānyamātre praviṣṭastadvyatirekeṇābhāvabhūto bhavati;vijñānamātrameva bhūtvā prajñānaghane pare brahmaṇyāpa iva samudre pralīyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Sa</s>' introduces the example. Just as — in the manner that — of all waters in rivers, ponds, lakes, and the like, the ocean is the one destination (<s>ekāyana</s>) — the one destination, the one going, the one dissolution, the attainment of non-differentiation — this is the meaning. As in this example, so too — of all touches such as soft, rough, hard, slimy, and the like — which are of the nature of air — the skin is the one destination. 'Skin' here means merely the general [category of] touch that is the object of skin. In that, the specific touches — like waters in the ocean — having entered, become non-existent apart from it, for they were merely configurations of that [general category] alone. Similarly, that general [category of] touch itself, denoted by the word 'skin,' [enters into] the mental intention (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), the general [category of] the mind's object — just as specific touches [enter] their general domain — having entered, becomes non-existent apart from it. Similarly, the mental object too, having entered the general [category of] the intellectual object, becomes non-existent apart from it. Having become mere consciousness (<s>vijñānamātra</s>), it dissolves in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the mass of consciousness — like waters in the ocean.

children.text:
evaṃ paramparākrameṇa śabdādau saha grāhakeṇa karaṇena pralīne prajñānaghane upādhyabhāvātsaindhavaghanavat prajñānaghanamekarasamanantamapāraṃ nirantaraṃ brahma vyavatiṣṭhate /
tasmādātmaiva ekamadvayamiti pratipattavyam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, through successive stages, when sound and the rest, together with the apprehending organ, have dissolved into the mass of consciousness — in the absence of limiting adjuncts, like a solid mass of salt, the mass of consciousness — of one taste, infinite, boundless, without interior division — <s>Brahman</s> alone remains. Therefore, the <s>Ātman</s> alone — one, non-dual — is to be realized.

children.text:
tathā sarveṣāṃ gandhānāṃ pṛthivīviśeṣāṇāṃ nāsike ghrāṇaviṣayasāmānyam, tathā sarveṣāṃ rasānāmabviśeṣāṇāṃ cakṣuścakṣurviṣayasāmānyam, tathā śabdānāṃ śrotraviṣayasāmānyaṃ pūrvavat /
tathā śrotrādiviṣayasāmānyānāṃ manoviṣayasāmānye saṅkalpe;manoviṣayasāmānyasyāpi buddhiviṣayasāmānye vijñānamātre;vijñānamātraṃ bhūtvā parasminprajñānaghane pralīyate /
tathā karmendriyāṇāṃ viṣayā vadanādānagamanavisargānandaviśeṣāḥ tattatkriyāsāmānyeṣveva praviṣṭā na vibhāgayogyā bhavanti, samudra ivābviśeṣāḥ; tāni ca sāmānyāni prāṇamātram, prāṇaśca prajñānamātrameva /
"yo vai prāṇaḥ sā prajñā yā vai prajñā sa prāṇaḥ"iti kauṣītakino 'dhīyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>Kauṣītakins</s> recite: 'That which is <s>prāṇa</s> is <s>prajñā</s> (consciousness); that which is <s>prajñā</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>.'

children.text: nanu sarvatra viṣayasyaiva pralayo 'bhihitaḥ, na tu karaṇasya;tatra ko 'bhiprāya iti? bāḍham;kintu viṣayasamānajātīyaṃ karaṇaṃ manyate śrutiḥ, na tu jātyantaram;viṣayasyaiva svātmagrāhakatvena saṃsthānāntaraṃ karaṇaṃ nāma-yathā rūpaviśeṣasyaiva saṃsthānaṃ pradīpaḥ karaṇaṃ sarvarūpaprakāśane, evaṃ sarvaviṣayaviśeṣāṇāmeva svātmaviśeṣaprakāśakatvena saṃsthānāntarāṇi karaṇāni pradīpavat /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But everywhere only the dissolution of sense-objects has been stated, not of the sense-organs; what then is the intent? [Reply:] Granted; however, the <s>śruti</s> considers the sense-organ to be of the same class as its sense-object, not of a different class. Rather, the sense-organ is merely a different configuration of the sense-object itself functioning as the apprehender of its own nature — just as a lamp, which is itself a specific form, serves as the instrument for illuminating all forms. In the same way, the sense-organs are different configurations of those very sense-object specificities, functioning as illuminators of their own specific natures, like lamps.

children.text: tasmānna karaṇānāṃ pṛthakpralaye yatnaḥ kāryaḥ,
children.translated_text: Therefore, no separate effort is needed for the dissolution of the sense-organs,

children.text: viṣayasāmānyātmakatvādviṣayapralayenaiva pralayaḥ siddho bhavati karaṇānāmiti //11//
children.translated_text: because, being of the nature of the generic sense-objects, the dissolution of the sense-organs is accomplished through the dissolution of the sense-objects themselves. // 11 //

Similarly, of all odors — which are specificities of earth — the nose [is their locus, and they merge into] the generic sense-object of the organ of smell. Similarly, of all flavors — which are specificities of water — the eye [is their locus, and they merge into] the generic sense-object of the eye. Similarly, of sounds — [they merge into] the generic sense-object of hearing, as before.
Similarly, the generic sense-objects of hearing and the rest [merge] into the generic mental sense-object, i.e., conceptual thought (<s>saṅkalpa</s>); the generic mental sense-object too [merges] into the generic object of the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), i.e., into mere consciousness (<s>vijñānamātra</s>); having become mere consciousness, it dissolves into the supreme mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>).
Similarly, the objects of the motor organs — the specific activities of speaking, grasping, moving, excretion, and pleasure — having entered into the generic forms of their respective activities, become incapable of differentiation, like water-specificities [dissolved] in the ocean. And those generic forms are nothing but <s>prāṇa</s> alone, and <s>prāṇa</s> is nothing but consciousness (<s>prajñāna</s>) alone.

children.text:
tatra 'idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmā' iti pratijñātam, tatra heturabhihitaḥ-ātmasāmānyatvam, ātmajatvam, ātmapralayatvaṃ ca /
tasmādutpattisthitipralayakāleṣu prajñānavyatirekeṇābhāvāt"prajñānaṃ brahma" "ātmaivedaṃ sarvam"iti pratijñātaṃ yat, tattarkataḥ sādhitam /
svābhāviko 'yaṃ pralaya iti paurāṇikā vadanti /
yastu buddhipūrvakaḥ pralayo brahmavidāṃ brahmavidyānimittaḥ, ayamātyantika ityācakṣate-avidyānirodhadvāreṇa yo bhavati; tadartho 'yaṃ viśeṣārambhaḥ-
children.translated_text:
There, it was asserted: 'All this is this self.' The reason stated for that is: [the world's] commonality with the self, its origination from the self, and its dissolution into the self.
Therefore, since apart from consciousness (<s>prajñāna</s>) there is no existence at the times of origination, continuance, and dissolution, what was asserted — '<s>prajñāna</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' and 'the self alone is all this' — that has been established through reasoning.
The <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (followers of the Purāṇas) say: this dissolution is natural (<s>svābhāvika</s>).
But the dissolution that is deliberate (<s>buddhipūrvaka</s>), occurring through <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) for the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — they declare this to be absolute (<s>ātyantika</s>), being that which occurs through the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). For that purpose, this special [section] is commenced —

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.12
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.12]

children.text:
sa yathā saindhavakhilya udake prāsta udakam evānuvilīyeta na hāsyodgrahaṇāyeva syāt |
yato-yatas tv ādadīta lavaṇam |
evaṃ vā ara idaṃ mahad bhūtam anantam apāraṃ vijñānaghana eva |
etebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tāny evānuvinaśyati |
na pretya saṃjñāstīty are bravīmi |
iti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ || BrhUp_2,4.12 ||
children.translated_text: Just as a lump of salt thrown into water would dissolve into the water itself, and there would be no possibility of picking it up — yet from wherever one might take [the water], it would be salty — even so, indeed, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, this great being, infinite, boundless, is a mass of consciousness alone (<s>vijñānaghana</s>). Having arisen from these elements, it perishes along with them. After departing, there is no [specific] consciousness — thus I say, O dear one. So said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. // BṛhUp 2.4.12 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.12
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.4.12:

children.text:
tatra dṛṣṭānta upādīyate-sa yatheti /
saindhavakhilyaḥ- sindhorvikāraḥ saindhavaḥ, sindhuśabdenodakamabhidhīyate, syandanātsindhurudakam, tadvikārastatra bhavo vā saindhavaḥ saindhavaścāsau khilyaśceti saindhavakhilyaḥ, khila eva khilyaḥ svārthe yatpratyayaḥ, udeka sindhau svayonauprastaḥ prakṣiptaḥ, udakameva vilīyamānamanuvilīyeta;yattadbhaumataijasasamparkātkāṭhinyaprāptiḥ /
khilyasya svayonisamparkādapagacchati tadudakasya vilayanam, tadanu saindhavakhilyo vilīyata ityucyate /
tadetadāha udakamevānuvilīyeteti /
children.translated_text: There, an illustration is adduced: 'Just as' and so forth. A salt-lump (<s>saindhavakhilya</s>) — <s>saindhava</s> is a transformation of <s>sindhu</s>; by the word <s>sindhu</s>, water is denoted — water is <s>sindhu</s> because of flowing — and its transformation, or what occurs in it, is <s>saindhava</s>; and being both <s>saindhava</s> and <s>khilya</s> (a lump), it is <s>saindhavakhilya</s>; <s>khilya</s> is just <s>khila</s> (a lump) with the <s>yat</s>-suffix in the sense of the word itself. [This lump,] thrown, cast into the <s>sindhu</s> (water), its own source, would dissolve into the water itself. That [hardness] which was the attainment of solidity through contact with earthly and fiery [elements] — when the lump comes into contact with its own source, that [hardness] is removed, which is the dissolution of the water; following that, the salt-lump is said to dissolve. This is what [the text] says: 'it would dissolve into the water itself.'

children.text:
na ha naiva asya khilyasyodgrahaṇāyoddhṛtya pūrvavadgrahaṇāya grahītuṃ naiva samarthaḥ kaścitsyātsunipuṇo 'pi /
ivaśabdo 'narthakaḥ /
grahaṇāya naiva samarthaḥ;kasmāt? yato yato yasmādyasmāddeśātadudakamādadīta gṛhītvā svādayet, lavaṇāsvādameva tadudakaṃ na tu khilyamāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Indeed, there would be no possibility at all — not even someone extremely skilled would be capable — of picking it up, i.e., of extracting and grasping the lump as before. The word '<s>iva</s>' is meaningless [here]. Not capable of grasping [it] — why? Because from wherever, from whatever location, one might take that water and taste it, it would taste of salt alone — but not [yield] the lump itself.

children.text:
yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ, evameva vā are maitreyidaṃ paramātmākhyaṃ mahadbhūtam-yasmānmahato bhūtādavidyayā paricchinnā satī kāryakaraṇopādhisambandhātkhilyamāvamāpannāsi, martyā janmamaraṇāśanāyāpipāsādisaṃsāradharmavatyasi, nāmarūpakāryātmikā-amuṣyānva yāhamiti, sa khilyabhāvastava kāryakaraṇabhūnopādhisamparkabhrāntijanito mahati bhūte svayonau mahāsamudrasyānīye paramātmani ajare 'mare 'bhaye śudve saindhavavanavadekarase prajñānaghane 'nante 'pāre nirantare 'vidyājanitabhrāntimedavarjite praveśitaḥ /
tasminpraviṣṭe svayonigraste khilyabhāve 'vidyākṛte bhedabhāve praṇāśite-idamekamadvaitaṃ mahadbhūtam mahacca tad bhūtaṃ ca mahadbhūtaṃ sarvamahattaratvādākāśādikāraṇatvācca /
bhūtaṃ viṣvapi kālepu svarūpādhyabhicārātsarvadaiva pariniṣpannamiti vaikāliko niṣṭhāpratyayaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Just as this illustration [shows] — even so indeed, O dear <s>Maitreyī</s>, this — called the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) — great being. Since you, from that great being, through <s>avidyā</s>, being delimited, through association with the limiting adjuncts of the aggregate of effects and instruments, have attained a lump-like state — you are mortal, afflicted with the <s>saṃsāric</s> attributes of birth, death, hunger, thirst, and the like, constituted of name and form — 'I am so-and-so's [wife/descendant].' That lump-like state of yours, produced by the delusion born of contact with the limiting adjuncts consisting of the elements that are effects and instruments, [is to be dissolved] in the great being, your own source — in the supreme self that is like a great ocean, unaging, immortal, fearless, pure — like a salt-lump, of one taste, a mass of consciousness, infinite, boundless, unbroken, free from the delusion born of <s>avidyā</s>. [Your lump-like state] is to be dissolved into it. When that [lump-like state], swallowed by its own source, when the differentiated state created by <s>avidyā</s> has been destroyed — this one, non-dual great being, great and real (or: a great <s>bhūta</s>), greater than all, being the cause of space and the rest.
<s>Bhūta</s> [also means]: at all times, because of the unfailing nature of its own essential nature — it is always fully accomplished; thus the past-tense suffix denotes timelessness.

children.text:
athavā bhūtaśabdaḥ paramārthavācī, mahacca pāramārthikaṃ cetyarthaḥ;laukikaṃ tu yadyapi mahadbhavati, svapnamāyākṛtaṃ himavadādiparvatopamaṃ na paramārthavastu;ato viśinaṣṭi--idaṃ tu mahacca tadabhūtaṃ ceti /
anantaṃ nāsyānto vidyata ityanantam;kadācidāpekṣikaṃ syādityato viśinaṣṭayapāramitivijñaptirvijñānam, vijñānama ca tadghanaśceti vijñānaghanaḥ, ghanaśabdojātyantarapratiṣedhārthaḥ-yathā suvarṇaghano 'yoghana iti;
children.translated_text: Alternatively, the word <s>bhūta</s> means 'ultimately real' (<s>paramārthavācī</s>) — meaning it is great and ultimately real. But the mundane, even though it may be great — like something created in dream or by illusion, resembling a <s>Himālaya</s> or other mountain — is not an ultimately real thing. Therefore, [the text] distinguishes: but this is both great and real. Infinite — it has no end, hence infinite. Lest it might sometimes be relatively [infinite, the text] further distinguishes: boundless. A mass of consciousness (<s>vijñānaghana</s>) — <s>vijñapti</s> (cognition) is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness), and that which is dense with it is <s>vijñānaghana</s>. The word <s>ghana</s> (mass, dense) is for the purpose of negating any other class [of substance] — just as [one says] 'a mass of gold' or 'a mass of iron.'

children.text: evaśabdo 'vadhāraṇārthaḥ-nānyañjātyantaramantarāle vidyata ityarthaḥ /
yadīdamekamadvaitaṃ paramārthataḥ svacchaṃ saṃsāraduḥkhāsampṛttkam, kinnimito 'yaṃ khilyabhāva ātmano jāto mṛtaḥ sukhī duḥkhyahaṃ mametyevamādilakṣaṇo 'nekasaṃsāradharmopadrutaḥ? ityucyate--
children.translated_text: If this is truly one, non-dual, essentially pure, and untouched by the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, then why has this lump-like state of the self arisen — characterized by 'I am born,' 'I have died,' 'I am happy,' 'I am miserable,' 'I [am],' 'mine,' and so forth — afflicted by the manifold attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>? To this, [the text] says:

children.text: etebhyo bhūtebhyo yānyetāni kāryakaraṇavipayākārapariṇatāni nāmarūpātmakāni salliphenavudvudopamānisvacchasya paramātmanaḥ salilopamasya, yepāṃ viṣayaparyantānāṃ prajñānaghane brahmaṇi paramārthavivekajñānena pravilāpanamuttakaṃ nadīsamudravata--etabhyo hetubhūtebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ satyaśabdavācyebhyaḥ samutthāya saindhavakhilyavat-yathā adbhayaḥ sūryacandrādipratibimbaḥ, yathā vā svacchasya sphaṭikasya alattakādyupādhibhyo rattkādibhāvaḥ, evaṃ kāryakaraṇabhūtabhūtopādhibhyo viśepātmakhilyabhāvena samutthāya samyagutthāya--yebhyo bhūtebhya utthitaḥ tāni yadākāryakaraṇaviṣayākārapariṇatāni bhūtānyātmano viśepātmakhilyahetubhūtāni śāstrācāryopadeśena brahmavidyāyā nadīsamudravatpravilāpitāni vinaśyanti, salilaphenabudbudādivatteṣu vinaśyatsu anvevaiṣa viśeṣātmakhilyabhāvo vinaśyati;yathā udakālattphakādihetvapanaye sāryacandrasphaṭikādipratibimbo vinaśyati, candrādi svarūpameva paramārthato vyavatiṣṭhate, tadvatprajñānaghanamanantamapāraṃ svacchaṃ vyavatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: From these elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) — which have been transformed into the forms of effects, instruments, and objects constituted of name and form, comparable to the froth, bubbles, [and foam] of the pure supreme self that is like water — whose dissolution, up to the range of sense-objects, into the mass of consciousness that is <s>Brahman</s>, through the knowledge of ultimate discrimination, like rivers into the ocean — from these elements that are causal, denoted by the word 'true' (<s>satya</s>), having arisen like a salt-lump — just as a reflection of the sun, moon, and the like [arises] from water, or just as the redness and the like of a clear crystal [arises] from limiting adjuncts such as red lac — so, having arisen, having fully arisen from the elemental limiting adjuncts of effects, instruments, and objects in the form of a differentiated lump-like self — when those elements, which have been transformed into the forms of effects, instruments, and objects and which are the causes of the differentiated lump-like state of the self, are dissolved through the instruction of scripture and teacher by means of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> like rivers into the ocean, when they perish like the froth and bubbles of water — this differentiated lump-like state correspondingly perishes along with them. Just as upon the removal of the causal factors — water, red lac, and the like — the reflections in the sun, moon, crystal, and the like perish, while the essential nature of the moon and the like alone remains in ultimate reality — so too the mass of consciousness, infinite, boundless, pure, alone remains.

children.text: na tatra pretya viśepasaṃjñāsti kāryakaraṇasaṅghātebhyovimuttkasya-ityevamare maitreyi bravīmi nāsti viśeṣasaṃjñeti--ahamasāvamuṣya putro mamedaṃ kṣetraṃ dhanaṃ sukhī duḥkhītyevamādilakṣaṇā, avidyākṛtatvāttasyāḥ;avidyāyāścabrahmavidyayā niranvayato nāśitatvātkuto viśeṣasaṃjñāsambhavo brahmavidaścaitanyasvabhāvāvasthitasya? śarīrāvasthitasyāpi viśeṣasaṃjñā nopapadyate kimuta kāryakaraṇavimuttkasya sarvataḥ? iti hovācottkavānkila paramārthadarśanaṃ maitreyyai bhāryāyai yājñavalkyaḥ //12 //
children.translated_text: There is no specific consciousness (<s>saṃjñā</s>) after departing — for one who has been freed from the aggregate of effects and instruments — 'thus, O dear <s>Maitreyī</s>, I say,' says [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>]: there is no specific consciousness — [such as] 'I am so-and-so, this is so-and-so's son,' 'this is my field, my wealth, I am happy, I am miserable' — and so forth, characterized by [individual identification]. This is because it is produced by <s>avidyā</s>, and because <s>avidyā</s> has been completely destroyed without remainder by <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. Whence could specific consciousness possibly arise for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> who abides in the nature of consciousness? Even while situated in the body, specific consciousness is not possible — how much less for one freed from the aggregate of effects and instruments in every respect? Thus spoke, with full conviction regarding the vision of ultimate reality, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> to <s>Maitreyī</s>, his wife. // 12 //
The word '<s>eva</s>' (alone, only) is for emphasis — the meaning is: no other class [of substance] exists in between.

children.text: evaṃ pratibodhitā--
children.translated_text: Thus instructed [she said] —

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.13
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.13]

children.text:
sā hovāca maitreyī -- atraiva mā bhagavān amūmuhan na pretya saṃjñāstīti |
sa hovāca -- na vā are 'haṃ mohaṃ bravīmi |
alaṃ vā ara idaṃ vijñānāya || BrhUp_2,4.13 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s> said: 'Here indeed, Revered One, you have caused me bewilderment — [by saying] that after departing, there is no consciousness.' He said: 'Indeed, I do not speak bewilderment. This is sufficient for understanding.' // BṛhUp 2.4.13 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.13
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.4.13:

children.text:
sā ha kilovācottkavatī maitreyī--atraiva etasmitreva ekasminvastuni brahmaṇi virudvadharmavattavamācakṣaṇena bhagavatā mama moha kṛtaḥ;tadāha--atraiva mā bhagavānpūjāvānamūmuhanmohaṃ kṛtacān /
kathaṃ tena virudvadharmavattvam utkamityucyate--pūrva vijñānaghana eveti pratiśāya punarna pretya saṃśāstīti;kathaṃ vijñānaghana eva? kathaṃ vā na pretya saṃjñāstīti? na hyuṣṇaḥ śītaścāgnirevaiko bhavati /
ato mūḍhāsmyatra /
children.translated_text:
She, <s>Maitreyī</s>, spoke with conviction: 'Here indeed, in this very single entity, <s>Brahman</s>, you have created bewilderment for me by declaring it to possess contradictory attributes.' She says: 'Here indeed, Revered One' — [using the] honorific — 'you have caused me bewilderment, you have produced confusion.'
How has [he stated] contradictory attributes? This is explained: first, [<s>Brahman</s> was described as] 'a mass of consciousness alone' — and then [he said] 'after departing, there is no consciousness.' How can it be a mass of consciousness alone? And how can there be no consciousness after departing? For one and the same fire cannot be both hot and cold.
Therefore, I am confused about this.

children.text:
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ-na vā are maitreyyahaṃ mohaṃ bravīmi mohanaṃ vākyaṃ na bravīmityarthaḥ /
nanu kathaṃ virudvadharmatvamavocaḥ-vijñāna ghanaṃ saṃjñābhāvaṃ ca ? na mayedamekasminvamiṃṇyamihitam, tvayaivedaṃ virudvadharmatvenaikaṃ vastu parigṛhītaṃ bhrāntyā, na tu mayottkam /
mayā tvidamuttkam--yastvavidyāpratyupasyāpitaḥkāryakaraṇasambandhī ātmanaḥ khilyabhāvaḥ, yasminvidyayā nāśite, tannimittā yā viśeṣasaṃjñā śarīrādisambandhinī anyatvadarśanalakṣaṇā, sā kāryakaraṇasaṅghātopādhau pravilāpite naśyati hetvabhāvād udakādyādhāranāśādiva candrādipratibimba stannimittaśca prakāśādiḥ; na punaḥ paramārthacandrādityasvarūpānāśavadasaṃsāribrahmasvarūpasya vijñānaghanasya nāśaḥ; tadvijñāghana ityuttkam; sa ātmā sarvasya jagataḥ, paramārthato bhūtanāśānna vināśī /
vināśī tvavidyakṛtaḥ khilyabhāvaḥ,"vācārambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyam"(chā0 u0 6 /1 /4) iti śrutyantarāt /
ayaṃ tu pāramārthikaḥ-avināśī vā are 'yamātmā, ato 'laṃ paryāptaṃ vai are idaṃ mahadbhūtamanantamapāraṃ ya yāvyākhyātaṃ vijñānāya vijñātum /
children.translated_text:
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'Indeed, O dear <s>Maitreyī</s>, I do not speak bewilderment' — meaning: I do not speak a bewildering statement.
[<s>Maitreyī</s> asks:] 'But how then did you state contradictory attributes — a mass of consciousness and the absence of consciousness?' [<s>Yājñavalkya</s> replies:] I did not attribute these to one and the same entity. Rather, it is you who, through error, have grasped this single entity as having contradictory attributes — it was not stated by me.
What I stated was this: that lump-like state of the self, associated with the connection to the aggregate of effects and instruments, which is superimposed through <s>avidyā</s> — when that is destroyed by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), the specific consciousness that is conditioned by the body and the like, characterized by the perception of otherness — that is what ceases, since the limiting adjuncts of the aggregate of effects and instruments have been dissolved, just as a reflection of the moon and the like [ceases] upon the destruction of the supporting medium of water and the like, along with the illumination and the like caused by it. But the essential nature of the moon, sun, and the like — like the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, the non-transmigratory self, which is a mass of consciousness — is not destroyed. That is what was said by 'mass of consciousness.' That self is the [self] of the entire universe; from the standpoint of ultimate reality, because of the destruction of the elements, [it is] not destructible.
What is destructible is the lump-like state created by <s>avidyā</s> — [as stated] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Modification is merely a name, a verbal handle' (ChUp 6.1.4).
But this is ultimately real: 'This self is imperishable' — therefore, 'this is sufficient, fitting indeed, O dear one, this great being, infinite, boundless' — as was explained — 'for understanding, for knowing.'

children.text: START BrhUp 2,4.14
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 2.4.14]

children.text:
yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ jighrati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati tad itara itaraṃ śṛṇoti tad itara itaraṃ jighrati tad itara itaram abhivadati tad itara itaraṃ manute tad itara itaraṃ vijānāti |
yatra vāsya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ jighret tat kena kaṃ jighret tat kena kaṃ paśyet tat kena kaṃ śṛṇuyāt tat kena kam abhivadet tat kena kaṃ manvīta tat kena kaṃ vijānīyāt |
yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijānāti taṃ kena vijānīyāt |
vijñātāram are kena vijānīyād iti || BrhUp_2,4.14 ||
children.translated_text:
For where there is, as it were, duality, there one smells another, there one sees another, there one hears another, there one speaks to another, there one thinks of another, there one knows another.
But where everything has become one's own self alone, then by what and whom would one smell? By what and whom would one see? By what and whom would one hear? By what and whom would one speak? By what and whom would one think? By what and whom would one know?
By what would one know that by which all this is known?
The knower — O dear one, by what would one know him? // BṛhUp 2.4.14 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,4.14
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 2.4.14:

children.text:
kathaṃ tarhi pretya saṃjñā nāstītyucyate /
śṛṇu /
yatra yasminnavidyākalpite kāryakaraṇasaṃghātopādhijanite viśeṣātmani khilyabhāve hi yasmādaddvaitamiva pāramārthato 'dvaite brahmaṇi dvaitamiva bhinnamiva vastvantaramātmana upalakṣyate /
nanu dvaitenopamīyamānatvāddvaitasya pāramārthikatvamiti /
na /
'vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyami'ti śrutyantarā 'dekamevā'dvitīyamātmaivedaṃ sarvāmiti ca /
tattatra yasmāddvaitamiva tasmādevetaro 'sau paramātmanaḥ khilyabhūta ātmāparamārthaścandroderivodakacandrādipratibimba itaro ghrātetareṇa dhrāṇenetaraṃ ghrātavyaṃ jighrati /
itara itaramiti kārakapradarśanārthaṃ jighratīti kriyāphalayorabhidhānam /
yathā chinttīti yathodyamyodyamya nipātanaṃ chedasya ca dvaidhībhāva ubhayaṃ chinattītyekenaiva śabdenābhidhīyate kriyāvasānatvātkriyāvyatirekeṇa ca tatphalasyānupalambhāt /
itaro ghrāṇetareṇa ghrāṇenetaraṃ ghratavyaṃ jighrati tathā sarvaṃ pūrvavadvijānāti /
iyamavidyāvadavasthā /
children.translated_text: How then is it said 'after departing, there is no consciousness'? Listen: where — in the particular self produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), generated by the limiting adjuncts of the aggregate of body and organs — in its dissolution (<s>khilya</s>), since indeed in [what is] ultimately non-dual <s>Brahman</s>, [there appears] as it were a duality, as if a separate entity other than the Self is perceived. [Objection:] Since duality is compared [to something], duality is ultimately real. [Response:] No — because of the other <s>śruti</s>: 'It is a mere name, a modification, a verbal designation' (ChāUp 6.1.4) and 'the Self alone is all this' and 'One only, without a second.' Therefore, since there [appears] as it were a duality, the other — that self which is subordinate (<s>khilyabhūta</s>) to the supreme Self, not ultimately [real], like a reflected moon in water and similar reflections — that other [self] smells with the other, [i.e.] smells the other object of smell with the other instrument of smell. '[The] other [smells] the other' — this is to indicate the factors of action (<s>kāraka</s>). '[He] smells' — this denotes both the action and its result. Just as '[he] cuts' — just as the act of raising [the axe] repeatedly and striking, and the splitting into two halves — both are denoted by the single word 'cuts,' because the action terminates [in its result] and because the result is not apprehended apart from the action. [Similarly,] the other smells the other object of smell with the other instrument of smell; likewise he cognizes everything, as before. This is the state under <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

children.text:
yatra tu brahmavidyayāvidyā nāśamupagamitā tatrā'tmavyatirekeṇānyasyābhāvaḥ /
yatra vā asya brahmavidaḥ sarvaṃ nāmarūpādyātmanyeva pravilāpitamātmaiva saṃvṛttaṃ yatraivamātmaivābhūttatra kena karaṇena kaṃ dhrātavyaṃ ko jighrettathā paśyodvijānīyāt /
sarvatra hi kārakasādhyā kriyā /
ataḥ kārakābhāve 'nupapattiḥ kriyāyāḥ kriyābhāve ca phalābhāvaḥ /
tasmādavidyāyāmeva satyāṃ kriyākārakaphalavyavahāro na brahmavidaḥ /
ātmatvādeva sarvasya nā'tmavyatirekeṇa kārakaṃ kriyāphalaṃ vāsti /
nacānātmā sansarvamātmaiva bhavati kasyacit /
tasmādavidyayaivānāttmatvaṃ parikalpitaṃ na tu paramārthata ātmavyatirekeṇāsti kiñcit /
tasmātparamārthātmaikatvapratyaye kriyākārakaphalapratyayānupapattiḥ /
ato virodhādbrahmavidaḥ kriyāṇāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ cāntyantameva nivṛttiḥ /
kena kimiti kṣepārthaṃ vacanaṃ prakārāntarānupapattidarśanārtham /
kenacidapi prakāreṇa kriyākaraṇādikārakānupapatteḥ /
kenatcitkañcitkāścitkathaṃ cinna jivredevetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: But where, through the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>avidyā</s> has been brought to destruction — there, there is no existence of anything other than the Self. Or where, for this knower of <s>Brahman</s>, all name and form and the rest have been dissolved into the Self alone, [and] the Self alone has come to be — where thus the Self alone has become [everything] — there, by what instrument could one smell what object of smell, or see, or cognize? For everywhere, action is accomplished through factors of action (<s>kāraka</s>). Therefore, in the absence of factors of action, action is impossible; and in the absence of action, there is no result. Therefore, the transaction of action, agent, and result exists only so long as <s>avidyā</s> obtains — not for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>. Since everything is the Self, there is no factor of action or result of action apart from the Self. And it is never the case that what is non-Self becomes wholly the Self for anyone. Therefore, non-Selfhood is imagined through <s>avidyā</s> alone; ultimately, there is nothing apart from the Self. Therefore, when the conviction of the ultimate oneness of the Self arises, the notions of action, factors of action, and result are impossible. Hence, because of contradiction, for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, there is absolute cessation of actions and their means. 'By what instrument — what [object]?' — this is a dismissive statement, to show the impossibility of any other way. Because by no means whatsoever are the factors of action such as instrument and the like possible — [therefore] by nothing could anyone smell anything in any manner — this is the meaning.

children.text:
yatrāpyavidyāvasthāyāmanyo 'nyaṃ paśyati tatrāpi yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijānāti taṃ kena vijānīyādyena vijānāti tasya karaṇasya
vijñeye viniyuktatvāt /
jñātuśva jñeya eva hi jijñāsā nā'tmani /
children.translated_text: the desire to know (<s>jijñāsā</s>) pertains only to the object to be known, not to the Self itself.

children.text: na cāgnerivā'tmā'tmano viṣayo na cāviṣaye jñāturjñānamupapadyate /
children.translated_text: And the Self is not its own object, just as fire [does not burn itself]; and knowledge of the knower does not arise when there is no object.

children.text: tasmādyenedaṃ vijānāti taṃ vijñātāraṃ kena karaṇena ko vānyo vijānīyāt /
children.translated_text: Therefore, that by which one knows all this — that knower — by what instrument, or what other person, could know it?

children.text: yadā tu punaḥ paramārthavivekino brahmavido vijñātaiva kevalo 'dvayo vartate taṃ vijñātāramare kena vijānīyāditi //4//
children.translated_text: But when the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the discriminator of ultimate reality, exists as the knower alone — solitary, non-dual — that knower, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, by what could one know? // 4 //

Even in the state of <s>avidyā</s>, where one sees another, there too — by what could one know that by which one knows all this? For the instrument of cognition, being engaged in the object to be cognized,

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye dvitīyādhyāyasya caturthaṃ brāhmaṇam //4//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the commentary on the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>, second chapter. // 4 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.1]

children.text:
yatkevalaṃ karmanirapekṣamamṛtavasādhanaṃ tadvaktavyamiti maitreyībrāhmaṇamārabdham /
taccā'tmajñānaṃ savaṃsanyāsāṅgaviśiṣṭam /
ātmani ca vijñāte sarvamidaṃ vijñātaṃ bhavati /
ātmā ca priyaḥ sarvasmāt /
tasmādātmā draṣṭavyaḥ sa ca śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāstavya iti ca darśanaprakārā uktāḥ /
tatra śrotavya ācāryāgamābhyām /
mantavyastarkataḥ /
tatra ca tarka ukta ātmaivedaṃ sarvamiti pratijñātasya hetuvacanamātmaikasāmānyatvamātmaikodbhavatvamātmaikapralayatvaṃ ca /
tatrāyaṃ heturasiddha ityāśaṅkyata ātmaikasāmānyodbhavapralayākhyastadāśaṅkānivṛtyarthametadbrāhmaṇamārabhyate /
children.translated_text: That which is independent of <s>karma</s> (action) alone and is the means to immortality — that is to be stated; hence the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s> was begun. And that is the knowledge of the Self, qualified by the subsidiary element of complete renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>). And when the Self is known, all this becomes known. And the Self is dearer than everything. Therefore, the Self is to be seen — and it is to be heard about, reflected upon, and meditated upon — thus the modes of realization have been stated. Therein, it is to be heard from the teacher and scripture. It is to be reflected upon through reasoning. And reasoning was stated — the supporting arguments for the thesis 'the Self alone is all this' are: the commonality of all in the Self, the origination of all from the Self, and the dissolution of all into the Self. Therein, this supporting argument — called 'the commonality of origination and dissolution in the one Self' — might be suspected to be unestablished; for the removal of that suspicion, this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is commenced.

children.text:
yasmātparasparopakāryopakārakabhūtaṃ jagatsarvaṃ pṛthivyādi /
yacca loke parasparakāryopakārakabhūtaṃ tadekakāraṇapūrvakamekasāmānyātmakamekapralayaṃ ca dṛṣṭam /
tasmādidamapi pṛthivyādilakṣaṇaṃ jagatparasparopakāryopakārakatvāttathābhūtaṃ bhavitumarhati /
eṣa hyartho 'sminbrāhmaṇeprakāśyate /
athavā'tmaivedaṃ sarvamiti pratijñātasyā'tmotpattisthitilayatvaṃ kriyate /
tathā hi naiyāyikairuktaṃ hetvapadeśātpratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ nigamanamiti /
anyairvyākhyātamā dundubhidṛṣṭāntācchrotavyārthamāgamavacanaṃ prāṅbhadhuvrahmaṇānmantavyārthamupapattipradarśanena madhubrāhmaṇena tu nididhyāsanavidhirucyata iti /
sarvathāpi tu yathā'gamenāvadhāritaṃ tarkatastathaiva mantavyam /
yathā tarkato matasya tarkāgamābhyāṃ niścitasya tathaiva nididhyāsanaṃ kriyata iti pṛthaṅnididhyāsanavidhiranarthaka eva /
tasmātpṛthakprakaraṇavibhāgo 'narthaka ityasmadabhiprāyaḥ śravaṇamanananididhyāsanānāmiti /
sarvathāpi tvadhyāyadvayasyārtho 'sminbrāhmaṇa upasaṃhriyate /
children.translated_text: Because the entire world, beginning with earth, is mutually in the relation of benefited and benefactor. And what is observed in the world to be mutually in the relation of effect and benefactor is seen to have a single prior cause, a single common essence, and a single dissolution. Therefore, this world too, characterized by earth and the rest, being mutually in the relation of benefited and benefactor, is fit to be of that nature. For this is the meaning that is elucidated in this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Alternatively, for the thesis 'the Self alone is all this,' the origination, sustenance, and dissolution [of all] from the Self is demonstrated. As indeed the <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) have said: 'The restatement of the thesis after the presentation of reasons is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>).' Others have explained: from the illustration of the drum, the teaching to be heard through scriptural statement [is given]; before the Honey-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the aspect to be reflected upon through the demonstration of reasoning [is given]; and through the Honey-<s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the injunction of meditation (<s>nididhyāsana</s>) is stated. In any case, however, what has been ascertained through scripture is to be reflected upon through reasoning in exactly that way. Since the meditation upon what has been ascertained through reasoning and scripture is to be done in exactly that way, a separate injunction of meditation is purposeless. Therefore, a separate division of sections is purposeless — this is our view — regarding hearing, reflection, and meditation. In any case, however, the meaning of the two chapters is summarized in this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text:
iyaṃ pṛthivī sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asyai pṛthivyai sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yas cāyam adhyātmaṃ śārīras tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: This earth is the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of this earth. And this person made of light (<s>tejomaya</s>), made of immortality (<s>amṛtamaya</s>), who is in this earth — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), the bodily one, made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.1)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.1
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.1:]

children.text:
iyaṃ pṛthivī prasiddhā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu sarveṣāṃ brahmādistambaparyantānāṃ bhūtānāṃ prāṇināṃ madhu kāryaṃ madhviva madhu yathaiko madhvapūpo 'nekairmadhukarairnirvartita evamiyaṃ pṛthivī sarvabhūtanirvartitā /
tathā sarvāṇi bhūtāni pṛthivyai pṛthivyā asyā madhu kāryam /
kiñca yaśvāyaṃ puruṣo 'syāṃ pṛthivyāṃ tejomayaśvinmātraprakāśamayo 'mṛtamayo 'maraṇadharmā puruṣo yaścāyamadhyātmaṃ śārīraḥ śarīre bhavaḥ pūrvavattejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣaḥ /
sa ca liṅgābhimānī /
sa ca sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmupakārakaraṇatvena madhu /
sarvāṇi ca bhūtānyasya madhu /
caśabdasāmarthyāt /
evametaccatuṣṭayaṃ tāvadekaṃ sarvabhūtakāryaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtānyasya kāryam ato 'syaikakāraṇapūrvakatā /
yasmādekasmātkāraṇādetajjātaṃ tadevaikaṃ paramārthato brahmetaratkāryaṃ vācā'rambhaṇaṃ vikāro nāmadheyamātramityeṣamadhuparyāyāṇāṃ sarveṣāmarthaḥ saṃkṣepataḥ /
children.translated_text: From whatever single cause this [fourfold set] is born — that one alone is ultimately <s>Brahman</s>; the rest, being effects, are mere verbal designations, modifications, names alone — 'It is a mere name, a modification, a verbal designation' (ChāUp 6.1.4) — this is the meaning of all the honey-passages in summary.

children.text: ayameva sa yo 'yaṃ pratijñāta idaṃ sarvaṃ yadayamātmeti /
children.translated_text: This indeed is that [Self] which was stated in the thesis: 'all this is the Self.'

children.text: idamamṛtaṃ yanmaitreyyā amṛtatvasādhanamuktamātmavijñānamidaṃ tadamṛtam /
children.translated_text: This is the immortal — what was told to <s>Maitreyī</s> as the means to immortality, namely the knowledge of the Self — this is that immortal [means].

children.text: idaṃ brahma yadbrahmā te bravāṇi jñapayiṣyāmītyadhyāyādau prakṛtaṃ yadviṣayā ca vidyā brahmavidyetyucyata idaṃ sarvaṃ yasmādbrahmaṇo vijñānātsarvaṃ bhavati //1//
children.translated_text: This is <s>Brahman</s> — what was introduced at the beginning of the chapter as 'I shall tell you about <s>Brahman</s>, I shall make you know,' and the knowledge concerning which is called '<s>Brahmavidyā</s>' (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) — this is all, because from the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, everything becomes [known]. // 1 //

This well-known earth is the honey of all beings — of all living creatures from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — the honey, meaning the effect, honey-like honey. Just as a single honey-cake is produced by many bees, so this earth is produced by all beings. Similarly, all beings are the honey, the effect, of this earth — honey of the earth. Moreover, the person (<s>puruṣa</s>) who is in this earth, made of light (<s>tejomaya</s>), of the nature of pure luminous radiance, made of immortality (<s>amṛtamaya</s>), of immortal nature — and the person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), the bodily one — existing in the body — likewise made of light, made of immortality. And he is the one identified with the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>). And he is the honey of all beings, because of being their benefactor through providing instruments [of experience]. And all beings are his honey. By the force of the word 'and' (<s>ca</s>). Thus this fourfold [set] — first, the effect of all beings, and all beings being its effect — therefore this [earth] has a single prior cause.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.2]

children.text:
imā āpaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
āsām apāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam āsv apsu tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ raitasas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: These waters are the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of these waters. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in these waters — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), pertaining to semen, made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.2)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.2
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.2:]

children.text: tathā'paḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the waters.

children.text: adhyātmaṃ retasyapāṃ viśeṣato 'vasthānam //2//
children.translated_text: With reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), [the person] pertaining to semen — this is the specific abode of water. // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.3]

children.text:
ayam agniḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asyāgneḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asminn agnau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ vāṅmayas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: This fire is the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of this fire. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this fire — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), consisting of speech (<s>vāṅmaya</s>), made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.3)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.3
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.3:]

children.text: tathāgniḥ vācyagnerviśeṣato 'vasthānam //3//
children.translated_text: Similarly, fire. Speech is the specific abode of fire [at the individual level]. // 3 //
