children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.4]

children.text:
ayaṃ vāyuḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asya vāyoḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asmin vāyau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ prāṇas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idaṃ amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: This wind is the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of this wind. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this wind — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), who is <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.4)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.4
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.4:]

children.text: tathā vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, wind.

children.text: adhyātmaṃ prāṇo bhūtānāṃ śarīrārambhakatvenopakārānmadhutvaṃ tadantargatānāṃ tejomayādīnāṃ karaṇatvenopakārānmadhutvam /
children.translated_text: With reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) [is the correlate]. The honey-nature of the beings [i.e., the elements] is because of being beneficial in initiating the body; the honey-nature of the [persons] made of light and the rest contained within them is because of being beneficial as instruments [of experience].

children.text: tathā coktaṃ"tasyaiva vācaḥ pṛthivī śarīraṃ jyotīrūpamayamagniḥ"iti //4//
children.translated_text: And thus it has been stated: 'Of that very speech, earth is the body; and the luminous form is fire' (BṛUp 2.5.1). // 4 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.5]

children.text:
ayam ādityaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asyādityasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asminn āditye tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ cākṣuṣas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.5 ||
children.translated_text: This sun is the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of this sun. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this sun — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), pertaining to the eye (<s>cākṣuṣa</s>), made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.5)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.5
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.5:]

children.text: tathā'dityo madhu /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the sun is the honey.

children.text: cākṣuṣo 'dhyātmam //5//
children.translated_text: The one pertaining to the eye (<s>cākṣuṣa</s>) [is the correlate] with reference to the individual self. // 5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.6]

children.text:
imā diśaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
āsāṃ diśāṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam āsu dikṣu tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ śrautraḥ prātiśrutkas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.6 ||
children.translated_text: These quarters are the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of these quarters. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in these quarters — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), pertaining to the ear, the echo-person (<s>prātiśrutka</s>), made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.6)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.6
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.6:]

children.text: tathā diśo madhu /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the quarters are the honey.

children.text: diśāṃ yadyapi śrotramadhyātmaṃ śabdapratiśravaṇavelāyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ saṃnihito bhavatītyadhyātmaṃ prātiśrutkaḥ pratiśrutkāyāṃ pratiśravaṇavelāyāṃ bhavaḥ prātiśrutkaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: Although the ear is the individual-level [correlate] of the quarters, specifically at the time of hearing echoes it becomes particularly connected — therefore, with reference to the individual self, [the person is called] '<s>prātiśrutka</s>' — the one present at the time of echo (<s>pratiśrutkā</s>), i.e. at the moment of hearing reverberations. // 6 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.7]

children.text:
ayaṃ candraḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhv |
asya candrasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asmin candre tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ mānasas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmedam amṛtam |
idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.7 ||
children.translated_text: This moon is the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of this moon. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this moon — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), pertaining to the mind (<s>mānasa</s>), made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.7)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.7
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.7:]

children.text: tathā candraḥ /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the moon.

children.text: adhyātmaṃ mānasaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: The one pertaining to the mind (<s>mānasa</s>) [is the correlate] with reference to the individual self. // 7 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.8]

children.text:
iyaṃ vidyut sarveṣāṃ bhūtānaṃ madhu |
asyai vidyutaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asyāṃ vidyuti tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ taijasas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.8 ||
children.translated_text: This lightning is the honey of all beings; all beings are the honey of this lightning. And this person made of light, made of immortality, who is in this lightning — and this person with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>), the lustrous one (<s>taijasa</s>), made of light, made of immortality — this is indeed that which is this Self. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is all. (BṛUp 2.5.8)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.8
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.8:]

children.text: tathā vidyut /
children.translated_text: Similarly, lightning.

children.text: tvaktejasi bhavastaijaso 'dhyātmam //8//
children.translated_text: The lustrous one (<s>taijasa</s>) — existing in the skin's luminosity — [is the correlate] with reference to the individual self. // 8 //

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.9
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.9]

children.text:
ayaṃ stanayitnuḥ sarveṣāṃ bhutānāṃ madhu |
asya stanayitnoḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asminstanayitnau tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ śābdaḥ sauvaras tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.9 ||
children.translated_text: This thunder is the honey of all beings. Of this thunder, all beings are the honey. And the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this thunder, and the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who, in the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), is of the nature of sound (<s>śābda</s>) and of voice (<s>sauvara</s>) — he is indeed this, he who is this <s>Ātman</s>. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is everything. (BṛUp 2.5.9)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.9
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.9:]

children.text: tathā stanayitnaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, thunder —

children.text: śabde bhavaḥ śābdo 'dhyātmaṃ yadyapi tathāpi svare viśeṣato bhavatīti sauvaro 'dhyātmam //9//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Śābda</s>' means 'existing in sound'; in the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), although [it is of the nature of sound], it specially pertains to voice — hence '<s>sauvara</s>' ('pertaining to the voice') in the individual self. (9)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.10
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.10]

children.text:
ayam ākāśaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asyākāśasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asminn ākāśe tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ hṛdy ākāśas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.10 ||
children.translated_text: This space (<s>ākāśa</s>) is the honey of all beings. Of this space, all beings are the honey. And the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this space, and the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who, in the individual self, is the space in the heart — he is indeed this, he who is this <s>Ātman</s>. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is everything. (BṛUp 2.5.10)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.10
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.10:]

children.text: tathā'kāśaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, space —

children.text: adhyātmaṃ hyadyākāśaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the individual self, it is the space in the heart. (10)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.11
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.11]

children.text:
ayaṃ dharmaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asya dharmasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asmin dharme tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ dhārmas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.11 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>dharma</s> (law) is the honey of all beings. Of this <s>dharma</s>, all beings are the honey. And the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this <s>dharma</s>, and the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who, in the individual self, is <s>dhārma</s> (pertaining to <s>dharma</s>) — he is indeed this, he who is this <s>Ātman</s>. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is everything. (BṛUp 2.5.11)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.11
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.11:]

children.text:
ayaṃ dharmo 'yamityapratyakṣo 'pi dharmaḥ kāryeṇa tatprayuktena pratyakṣeṇa vyapadiśyate 'yaṃ dharma iti pratyakṣavat /
dharmaśca vyākhyātaḥ śrutismṛtilakṣaṇaḥ kṣatrādīnāmapi niyantā jagato vaicitryakṛtpṛthivyādīnāṃ pariṇāmahetutvātprāṇibhiranuṣṭhīyamānarūpaśca /
tena cāyaṃ dharma iti pratyakṣeṇa vyapadeśaḥ /
satyadharmayoścābhedena nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ śāsrācāralakṣaṇayoridda(? ) tu bhedena vyapadeśa ekatve satyapi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And <s>satya</s> (truth) and <s>dharma</s> have been indicated without distinction — the two being characterized as scriptural and traditional conduct. But here [in this section], there is a designation with distinction, even though they are one,

children.text: dṛṣṭādṛṣṭabhedarūpeṇa kāryārambhakatvāt /
children.translated_text: because [<s>dharma</s>] initiates effects in the form of both seen and unseen [results].

children.text: yastvadṛṣṭo 'pūrvākhyo dharmaḥ sa sāmānyaviśeṣātmanādṛṣṭena rūpeṇa kāryamārabhate sāmānyarūpeṇa pṛthivyādīnāṃ prayoktā bhavati viśeṣarūpeṇa cādhyātmaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That <s>dharma</s> which is unseen, called <s>apūrva</s>, by its general and particular nature, initiates effects through its unseen form; in its general form, it is the impeller of earth and the other [elements]; in its particular form, it [impels] the individual aggregate of body and organs (<s>kāryakaraṇasaṃghāta</s>).

children.text: tatra pṛthivyādīnāṃ prayoktari yaścāyamasmindharme tejomayastathādhyātmaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātakartari dharme bhavo dhārmaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, in the <s>dharma</s> that impels earth and the like, is the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s>; and similarly, in the individual self, in the <s>dharma</s> that is the agent of the aggregate of body and organs — '<s>dhārma</s>' means 'born of <s>dharma</s>' — [is the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s>]. (11)

[Commentary:] 'This <s>dharma</s>' — although <s>dharma</s> is imperceptible, indicated by 'this' (<s>ayam</s>), it is designated through its effects, which are perceptible and produced by it, as 'this <s>dharma</s>' — as if it were perceptible. And <s>dharma</s> has been explained as having the character of <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and <s>smṛti</s> (tradition); it is the governor even of the <s>kṣatriya</s> and other [classes]; it is the cause of the world's diversity and the cause of the transformation of earth and the like; and it has the form of being practiced by living beings. Hence the designation 'this <s>dharma</s>' by means of the perceptible [effects].

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.12
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.12]

children.text:
idaṃ satyaṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asya satyasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asmin satye tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ sātyas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.12 ||
children.translated_text: This truth (<s>satya</s>) is the honey of all beings. Of this truth, all beings are the honey. And the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this truth, and the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who, in the individual self, is <s>sātya</s> (pertaining to truth) — he is indeed this, he who is this <s>Ātman</s>. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is everything. (BṛUp 2.5.12)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.12
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.12:]

children.text: tathā dṛṣṭenānuṣṭhīyamānenā'cārarūpeṇa satyākhyo bhavati sa eva dharmaḥ so 'pi dviprakāra eva sāmānyaviśeṣātmarūpeṇa /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, [<s>dharma</s>] in its visible form, being practiced as conduct, is called <s>satya</s> (truth); that very <s>dharma</s> is also of two kinds — having a general and particular nature.

children.text: sāmānyarūpaḥ pṛthivyādisamaveto viśeṣarūpaḥ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasamaveta /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In its general form, it inheres in earth and the like; in its particular form, it inheres in the aggregate of body and organs.

children.text: tatra pṛthivyādisamavete vartamānakriyārūpe satye tathādhyātmaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasa mavete satye bhavaḥ satyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, in <s>satya</s> which has the form of present activity inhering in earth and the like, and similarly in the individual self, in <s>satya</s> inhering in the aggregate of body and organs — '<s>sātya</s>' means 'born of <s>satya</s>.'

children.text: satyena vāyurāvātīti śrutyantarāt //12//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [This is supported] by another <s>śruti</s>: 'By truth the wind blows' (and the like). (12)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.13
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.13]

children.text:
idaṃ mānuṣaṃ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asya mānuṣasya sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asmin mānuṣe tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam adhyātmaṃ mānuṣas tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.13 ||
children.translated_text: This human race (<s>mānuṣa</s>) is the honey of all beings. Of this human race, all beings are the honey. And the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this human race, and the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who, in the individual self, is human (<s>mānuṣa</s>) — he is indeed this, he who is this <s>Ātman</s>. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is everything. (BṛUp 2.5.13)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.13
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.13:]

children.text: dharmasatyābhyāṃ prayukto 'yaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātaviśeṣaḥ sa yena jātiviśeṣeṣa saṃyukto bhavati /
sa jātiviśeṣo mānuṣādiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That specific class is the human (<s>mānuṣa</s>) and the like.

children.text: tatra mānuṣādijātiviśiṣṭā eva sarve prāṇinikāyāḥ parasparopakāryopakārakabhāvena vartamānā dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, all groups of living beings, distinguished by the specific classes of human and the like, are seen as existing in a mutual relationship of benefactor and beneficiary.

children.text: ato mānuṣādijātirapi sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the human and other classes too are the honey of all beings.

children.text: tatra mānuṣādijātirapi bāhyā'dhyātmikī cetyubhayathā nirdeśabhāgbhavati //13//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, the human and other classes are to be referred to in both ways — as external (<s>bāhya</s>) and as pertaining to the individual self (<s>ādhyātmika</s>). (13)
[Commentary:] Impelled by <s>dharma</s> and <s>satya</s>, this particular aggregate of body and organs is conjoined with a specific class (<s>jāti</s>).

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.14
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.14]

children.text:
ayam ātmā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu |
asyātmanaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni madhu |
yaś cāyam asminn ātmani tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo yaś cāyam ātmā tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yam eva sa yo 'yam ātmā |
idam amṛtam idaṃ brahmedaṃ sarvam || BrhUp_2,5.14 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s> is the honey of all beings. Of this <s>Ātman</s>, all beings are the honey. And the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is in this <s>Ātman</s>, and the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> who is this <s>Ātman</s> — he is indeed this, he who is this <s>Ātman</s>. This is the immortal, this is <s>Brahman</s>, this is everything. (BṛUp 2.5.14)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.14
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.14:]

children.text:
yastu kāryakaraṇasaṃghāto mānuṣādijātiviśiṣṭaḥ so 'yamātmā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ madhu /
nanvayaṃ śārīraśabdena nirdiṣṭaḥ pṛthivīparyāya eva /
na /
pārthivāṃśasyaiva tatra grahaṇāt /
idaṃ tu sarvātmā pratyastamitādhyātmādhibhūtādisarvaviśeṣaḥ sarvabhūtadevatāgaṇaviśiṣṭaḥ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātaḥ so 'yamātmetyucyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But here, [it is] the <s>Ātman</s> of everything (<s>sarvātman</s>), in which all distinctions of <s>adhyātma</s> (individual self), <s>adhibhūta</s> (external beings), and the like have subsided, and which is qualified by all beings and groups of deities — this aggregate of body and organs is called '<s>Ātman</s>.'

children.text: tasminnasminnātmani tejomayo 'mṛtamayaḥ puruṣo 'yamūrtarasaḥ sarvātmako nirdiśyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In this <s>Ātman</s>, the luminous, immortal <s>Puruṣa</s> — the embodied essence (<s>ūrtarasa</s>) who is the <s>Ātman</s> of everything — is indicated.

children.text: ekadeśena tu pṛthivyādiṣu nirdiṣṭo 'trādhyātmaviśeṣābhāvātsa na nirdiśyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] However, having been indicated partially in earth and the like, here, due to the absence of a specific individual (<s>adhyātma</s>) distinction, he is not separately indicated.

children.text: yastu pariśiṣṭo vijñānamayo yadartho 'yaṃ dehaliṅgasaṃghāta ātmā sa yaścāyamātmetyucyate //14//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But the remaining one — the one made of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), for whose sake this aggregate of body and indicators (<s>dehaliṅgasaṃghāta</s>) exists — that <s>Ātman</s> is what is referred to as 'this <s>Ātman</s>.' (14)

[Commentary:] Now, the aggregate of body and organs, distinguished by the specific class of human and the like — this <s>Ātman</s> is the honey of all beings. [Objection:] But was not this [<s>Ātman</s>] designated by the word '<s>śārīra</s>' (embodied) as belonging to the same series as earth and the like? [Answer:] No — because only the earthy portion was included there.

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.15
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.15]

children.text:
sa vā ayam ātmā sarveṣāṃ adhipatiḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ rājā |
tad yathā rathanābhau ca rathanemau cārāḥ sarve samarpitāḥ |
evam evāsminn ātmani sarvāṇi bhūtāni sarve devāḥ sarve lokāḥ sarve prāṇāḥ sarva eta ātmānaḥ samarpitāḥ || BrhUp_2,5.15 ||
children.translated_text: Verily, this <s>Ātman</s> is the lord of all beings, the king of all beings. Just as all spokes are fixed in the hub and the rim of a wheel — even so, in this <s>Ātman</s>, all beings, all gods, all worlds, all vital breaths, all these selves are fixed. (BṛUp 2.5.15)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.15
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.15:]

children.text:
yasminnātmani pariśiṣṭo vijñānamayo 'mātmā /
tasminnavidyākṛtakāryakaraṇasaṅghātopadhiviśiṣṭe brahmavidyāyā paramārthātmani praveśite, sa evamuttko 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtastraḥ prajñānaghanabhūtaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmayamātmā sarvairūpāsyaḥ sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāmadhipatiḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ svatantro na kumāramātyavat, kiṃ tarhi? sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ rājā /
rājatvaviśeṣaṇamadhipatiriti;bhavati kaścidrājocitaṣṭattimāśritya rājā, na tvadhipatiḥ, ato viśinaṣṭyadhipatiriti /
evaṃ sarvabhūtātmā vidvān brahmavinmuttko bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In that <s>Ātman</s>, the remaining one made of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) is the <s>Ātman</s>. When, through <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>), the aggregate of body and organs — the limiting adjunct created by <s>avidyā</s> — has been resolved into the ultimate <s>Ātman</s> (<s>paramārthātman</s>), that very [<s>Ātman</s>], being thus elevated, without interior, without exterior, entire, a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>) — is the <s>Ātman</s> of all beings, to be meditated upon by all, the lord of all beings, sovereign over all beings — not like a prince or minister, but rather the king of all beings. The qualification 'lord' (<s>adhipati</s>) [specifies further]: for someone may be a king by virtue of royal lineage, yet not a lord; hence the distinction 'lord.' Thus, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, being the <s>Ātman</s> of all beings, becomes liberated.

children.text:
yaduttkam 'brahmavidyayā sarvaṃ bhaviṣyanto manuṣyā manyante kimu tadbrahmāvedyasmāttatsarvamabhavat'itīdaṃ tad vyākhyātam /
evamātmānabheva sarvātmatvena ācāryagamābhyāṃ śrutvā, matvā tarkato vijñāya sākṣādevaṃ yathā madhubrāhmaṇe darśitaṃ tathā, tasmādbrahmavijñānādevaṃlakṣaṇāt pūrvamapibrahemaiva sadavidyayā abrahmāsīt, sarvabheva ca sadasarvamāsīt tāntvavidyāmasmādvijñanāttiraskṛtya brahmavidbrahmaiva san brahmābhavat sarvaḥ sa sarvamabhavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What was stated — 'Those who know <s>brahmavidyā</s>, thinking "we shall become everything" — what indeed did that <s>Brahman</s> know, from which it became all?' — this has now been explained. Having thus heard from the teacher and from scripture that the <s>Ātman</s> alone is the <s>Ātman</s> of all, having reflected upon it through reasoning, having directly realized it just as it has been shown in the <s>Madhubrāhmaṇa</s> — therefore, from such <s>brahmavidyā</s> having this character, even before [realization], [the self] was indeed <s>Brahman</s> alone, but through <s>avidyā</s> it was [as if] not <s>Brahman</s>; and though it was everything, it was [as if] not everything. Having dispelled that <s>avidyā</s> through this knowledge, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, being <s>Brahman</s> itself, becomes <s>Brahman</s>, becomes everything.

children.text:
parisamāptaḥ śāstrārtho yadarthaḥ prastutaḥ /
tasminnetasmin sarvātmabhūte brahmavidi sarvātmani sarvaṃ jagat samarpitamityetasminnarthe dṛṣṭānta upādīyate-tadyathā rathanābhau ca rathenemau cārāḥ sarve samarpitā iti prasidvor'thaḥ, evamevāsminnātmani paramātmabhūte brahmavidi sarvāṇi bhūtāni brahmādistambaryantāni, sarve devā agnyādayaḥ, sarve lokā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The purpose of the scripture that was undertaken has been concluded. In that — in this knower of <s>Brahman</s> who has become the <s>Ātman</s> of all — the entire world is fixed. For this meaning, an illustration is adduced: 'Just as in the hub and the rim of a wheel, all spokes are fixed' — this is well-known. Even so, in this <s>Ātman</s> that has become the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, in the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, all gods such as <s>Agni</s> and the rest, all worlds

children.text: bhūrādayaḥ, sarve praṇā vāgādayaḥ, sarva eta ātmāno jalacandravat pratiśarīrānupraveśino 'vidyākalpitāḥ, sarvaṃ jagadasmin samarpitam /
children.translated_text: such as <s>Bhūḥ</s> and the rest, all vital breaths such as speech and the rest, all these selves — like reflections of the moon in water, entering into each body, projected by <s>avidyā</s> — the entire world is fixed in this [<s>Ātman</s>].

children.text:
yaduttkaṃ brahmavidvāmadevaḥ pratipede-'ahaṃ manurabhavaṃ sūryaśca'iti, sa eṣa sarvātmabhāvo vyākhyātaḥ /
sa eṣa vidvān brahmavit sarvopādhiḥ sarvātmā sarvo bhavati /
nirupādhirnirupākhyaḥ anantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghano 'jājaro 'mṛtobhayo 'calo neti netyasthūlo 'naṇurityevaṃviśeṣaṇo bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As was stated, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, realized: 'I was <s>Manu</s> and <s>Sūrya</s>' — this state of being the <s>Ātman</s> of all has been explained. This very knower, the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, possessing all limiting adjuncts, being the <s>Ātman</s> of all, becomes everything. Without limiting adjuncts, without designation, without interior, without exterior, entire, a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), unaging, immortal, fearless, immovable — he is characterized as '<s>neti neti</s>' ('not this, not this'), 'not gross, not subtle,' and the like.

children.text:
tametamarthamajānantastārkikāḥ kecit paṇḍitaṃmanyāścāgamavidaḥ śāstrārtha virudvaṃ manyamānā vikalpayanto mohamagādhamupayānti /
tametamarthametau manetrāvanuvadataḥ--"anejadekaṃ manaso javīyaḥ" "tadejati tannaijati"iti /
tathā ca taittirīyake--"yasmātparaṃ nāpāramasti kiñcat""etatsāma gāyannāste" "ahamannamahamannamahamannam"ityādi /
tathā ca cchāndogye"jakṣat krīḍanramamāṇaḥ" "sayadi pitṛlokakāmaḥ" "sarvagandhaḥ sarvarasaḥ"ityādi /
āyarvaṇe ca"sarvajñaḥ sarvavit""dūrāta sudūre tadihāntike ca /
"kaṭhavallīṣvapi"aṇoraṇīyān mahato mahīyān" "kastaṃ madāmadaṃ devam" "tadvāvato 'nyānatyeti tiṣṭhat"iti ca /
tathā gītāsu"ahaṃ kraturahaṃ yajñaḥ" "pitāhamasya jagataḥ" "nādatte kasyacit pāpam" "samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu" "avimattkaṃ vibhattkepu" "grasiṣṇu prabhaviṣṇu ca"ityevamādyāgamārtha virudvamiva
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Not knowing this meaning, certain logicians (<s>tārkikas</s>) and certain scholars who fancy themselves learned but who regard themselves as knowledgeable of scripture, thinking it to be contrary to the meaning of scripture, engage in various speculations and fall into deep delusion. This very meaning is restated by these two <s>mantras</s>: 'Unmoving, it is one, swifter than the mind' (<s>ĪśUp</s>); 'It moves; it moves not' (<s>ĪśUp</s>). And likewise in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s>: 'Than which there is nothing higher' (<s>TaiUp</s>); 'He sits singing this <s>Sāman</s>'; 'I am food, I am food, I am food,' and so forth. And likewise in the <s>Chāndogya</s>: 'Eating, playing, rejoicing'; 'If he desires the world of the fathers'; 'All fragrances, all tastes,' and so forth. And in the <s>Ātharvana</s>: 'Omniscient, all-knowing'; 'Far away, yet very near.' And in the <s>Kaṭhavallī</s>: 'Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great'; 'Who knows that blissful <s>Brahman</s> which is intoxication?'; 'Standing, it outpaces all others who run.' And likewise in the <s>Gītā</s>: 'I am the ritual, I am the sacrifice'; 'I am the father of this world'; 'He accepts no one's sin'; 'Equal in all beings'; 'Undivided among the divided'; 'Devouring and generating' — thinking that the meaning of such scriptural passages appears

children.text: pratibhāntaṃ manyamānāḥ svacittasāmarthyādarthanirṇayāya vikalpayantaḥ, astyātmā nāstyātmā kartākartā muttko badvaḥ kṣaṇiko vijñānamātraṃ śūnyaṃ cetyevaṃ vikalpayanto na pāramadhigacchantyavidyāyāḥ, virudvarrmadarśitvāt sarvatra /
children.translated_text: to be contradictory, and speculating from the strength of their own intellect to determine the meaning — [thinking] 'the self exists,' 'the self does not exist,' 'it is an agent,' 'it is not an agent,' 'it is liberated,' 'it is bound,' 'it is momentary,' 'it is mere consciousness,' 'it is void' — speculating thus, they do not reach the far shore of <s>avidyā</s>, because they see contradictions everywhere.

children.text: tasmāttatra ya eva śrutyācāryadarśitamārgānusāriṇaḥ, ta evāvidyāyāḥ pāramadhigacchanti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, only those who follow the path shown by <s>śruti</s> and the teacher reach the far shore of <s>avidyā</s>.

children.text: ta eva vāsmānmohasamudrādagādhāduttariṣyanti, netare svavudvikauśalānusāriṇaḥ //15 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] They alone will cross over this fathomless ocean of delusion — not others, who follow the [supposed] skill of their own intellect. (15)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.16
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.16]

children.text:
parisamāptā brahmavidyāmṛtatvasādhanābhūtā, yāṃ maitreyī pṛṣṭavatī bhartāram 'yadeva bhagavānamṛtatvasādhanaṃ veda tadeva me brūhi'iti /
etasyā brahmavidyāyāḥ stutyartheyamākhyāyikāyāḥ saṅkṣepator'thaprakāśanārthāvetau mantrau bhavataḥ /
evaṃ hi mantrabrāhmaṇābhyāṃ stutatvāt amṛtatvasarvaprāptisādhanatvaṃ brahmavidyāyāḥ prakaṭīkṛtaṃ rājamārga mupanītaṃ bhavati--yathāditya udyañchalārvaraṃ tamo 'panayatīti tadvat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>brahmavidyā</s> that is the means to immortality is now concluded — that which <s>Maitreyī</s> asked of her husband: 'Whatever, O venerable one, you know to be the means to immortality, tell me that alone.' For the purpose of praising this <s>brahmavidyā</s>, two <s>mantras</s> are provided here as a condensed exposition of the meaning of this narrative. For when thus praised by both <s>mantra</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the nature of <s>brahmavidyā</s> as the means to immortality and the attainment of everything is made manifest, led onto the royal highway — just as the sun, rising, removes all darkness.

children.text:
api caivaṃ stutā brahmavidyāyā indrarakṣitā sā duṣprāpyā devairapi;.smādaścibhyāmapidevabhipagbhyāmindrarakṣitā vidyā mahatāyāsena prāptā /
brāhmaṇasya śiraśchittvāśvayaṃ śiraḥ pratisandhāya tasminnindreṇacchinne punaḥ svaśira eva pratisandhāya tena brāhmaṇasya svaśirasaivottkāśeṣā brahmavidyā śrutā /
tasmāttataḥ parataraṃ kiñcit puruṣārthasādhanaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhāvi vā, kuta eva vartamānam, iti nātaḥ parāstutirasti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, <s>brahmavidyā</s> thus praised is guarded by <s>Indra</s> and is difficult to obtain even by the gods. The <s>Aśvins</s> too, who are gods, obtained this <s>Indra</s>-guarded knowledge only with great effort — having cut off the head of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [<s>Dadhyañc</s>], attaching a horse's head, and when <s>Indra</s> cut that off, reattaching his own head; and thus, through the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s own head, the rest of the <s>brahmavidyā</s> was heard. Therefore, nothing higher than this exists as a means to the highest human goal — neither in the past nor in the future, let alone in the present. Hence there is no praise higher than this.

children.text:
api caivaṃ stūyate brahmavidyāsarvapuruṣārthānāṃ karma hi sādhanamiti loke prasidvam /
tacca karma vittasādhyam,
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is thus praised — for in the world it is well known that action (<s>karma</s>) is the means to all human goals (<s>puruṣārthas</s>). And that action is accomplished through wealth,

children.text:
tenāśāpināstyamṛtatvasya /
tadidamamṛtatvaṃ kevalayātmavidyayā karmanirapekṣayā prāpyate;yasmāt karmaprakaraṇe vaktuṃ prāptapi kevalaprakaraṇe, karmaprakaraṇāduttīrta karmaṇā virudvatvāt kevalasaṃnyāsasahitā abhihitā amṛtatvasādhanāya /
tasmānnātaḥ paraṃ puruṣārthasādhanamasti /
children.translated_text: therefore, even hope does not exist for immortality [through action]. This immortality is attained solely through the knowledge of the self (<s>ātmavidyā</s>), independent of action; because even though [the teaching of <s>ātmavidyā</s>] could be stated in the context of action (<s>karmaprakaraṇa</s>), it was stated in the context of [pure] knowledge alone — since it contradicts action, having transcended the context of action — it was taught together with complete renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) as the means to immortality. Therefore, there is no higher means to the human goal than this.

children.text:
api caivaṃ stutā brahmavidyā sarvo hi loko dvandvārāmaḥ"sa vai naiva reme tasmādekākī na ramate"iti śruteḥ /
yājñavalkyo lokasādhāraṇo 'pi sannātmajñānabaladbhāryāputravittādisaṃsāraratiṃ parityajya prajñānatṛpta ātmaratirbabhūva /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is thus praised — for the entire world delights in pairs of opposites (<s>dvandva</s>), as the <s>śruti</s> says: 'He indeed did not rejoice; therefore, one who is alone does not rejoice' (BṛUp 1.4.3). Yet <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, though being like ordinary people, by the power of self-knowledge, abandoned the delight in <s>saṃsāra</s> — in wives, sons, wealth, and the like — and, satisfied with wisdom (<s>prajñāna</s>), became one who delights in the self alone.

children.text: api caivaṃ stutā brahmavidyā yasmādyājñavalkyenasaṃsāramārgad vyuttiṣṭhatāpi priyāyai bhāryāyai protyarthameṃvāmihitā,"priyaṃ bhāpasa ehyāḥsva"iti liṅgāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is thus praised — because <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, even while departing from the path of <s>saṃsāra</s>, taught it to his dear wife for her own benefit, as indicated by the words 'Dear one, come, sit here' (BṛUp 2.4.1).

children.text:
tatreyaṃ stutyarthākhyāyiketyavocāma /
kā punaḥ sā ākhyāyikā? ityucyate---
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In that context, we have said that this is a narrative (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>) for the purpose of praise. What then is that narrative? It is said:

children.text:
idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca |
tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat -- tad vāṃ narā sanaye daṃsa ugram āviṣ kṛṇomi tanyatur na vṛṣṭim |
dadhyaṅ ha yan madhv ātharvaṇo vām aśvasya śīrṣṇā pra yad īm uvāceti || BrhUp_2,5.16 ||
children.translated_text: 'This is verily that honey which <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> told to the two <s>Aśvins</s>. Seeing this, the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) said: "O you two heroes, I make manifest that fierce deed of yours, done for the sake of gain, like rain [accompanied by] thunder. <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> declared to you two that honey through the head of a horse."' (BṛUp 2.5.16)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.16
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.16:]

children.text:
idamityanantaranirdiṣṭaṃ vyapadiśati, budvau sannihitatvāt /
vaiśabdaḥ smaraṇārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This' (<s>idam</s>) — he designates what has been described immediately after [the <s>madhu-brāhmaṇa</s>], because it is proximate in the mind. The word '<s>vai</s>' is for the purpose of recalling [what is well-known].

children.text:
tadityākhyāyikānirvṛttaṃprakaraṇāntarābhihitaṃ parokṣaṃ vaiśabdena smārayanniha vyapadiśati /
yattat pravargyaprakaraṇe mūcitam, nāviṣkṛtaṃ madhu, tadidaṃ madhvihānantaraṃ nirdiṣṭam-'iyaṃ pṛthivī'ityādinā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'That' (<s>tat</s>) — by the word '<s>vai</s>,' [the text] recalls what was accomplished through the narrative and stated in another context — something not directly present — and designates it here. That which was indicated in the context of the <s>Pravargya</s> ritual — the honey (<s>madhu</s>) that was not made manifest [there] — this very honey has been described here immediately after [the <s>madhu-brāhmaṇa</s>], beginning with 'This earth' and so forth.

children.text:
kathaṃ tatra prakaraṇānte sūcitam-dadhyaṅ ha vā ābhyāmātharvaṇo madhu nāma brāhmaṇamuvāca /
tadenayoḥ priyaṃ dhāma tadevainayoretenopagacchati /
sa hovācendreṇa vā uttko 'smayetaccedanyasmā anuvrūyāstata eva te śiraśchindyāmiti /
tasmādvai bibhemi, yadvai me sa śiro na chindyāt tadvāmupaneṣya iti /
tau hocaturāvāṃ tvā tasmāt trāsyāvahe iti kathaṃ mā trāsyethe? iti /
yadā nāvupaneṣyase;atha te śiraśchittvā anyatrāhratyopanidhāsyāvaḥ;athāśvasya śira āhratya tatte pratidhāsyāvaḥ;tena nāvanuvakṣyasi /
yadā nāvanuvakṣyasi, atha te tadindraḥ śiraśchetsyati;atha te svaṃ śira āhratya tatte pratidhāsyāva iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How was it indicated at the end of that [<s>Pravargya</s>] context? — '<s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> told the two [<s>Aśvins</s>] the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> called "honey" (<s>madhu</s>). That is their beloved abode; they approach it by this very [knowledge]. He [<s>Dadhyañc</s>] said: "<s>Indra</s> has made a pact with me — if you should recite this to anyone else, I shall cut off your head for that very reason." Therefore I am afraid — lest he cut off my head. Therefore I shall teach you.' They said: 'We two shall protect you from that.' 'How will you protect me?' [he asked]. 'When you are about to teach us, we shall cut off your head and place it elsewhere; then, bringing the head of a horse, we shall attach it to you. With that [head] you shall teach us. When you have finished teaching us, then <s>Indra</s> will cut off that [horse's] head; then, bringing your own head, we shall re-attach it to you.'

children.text:
tatheti tau hopaninye /
tau yadopaninye, athāsya śiracchittvānyatropanidadhutuḥ;athāśvasya śira āhratya tadvāsya pratidadhatuḥ /
tena hābhyāmanuvāca /
sa yadā ābhyāmanuvācāthāsya tadindraḥ śiraściccheda /
athāsya svaṃ śira āhratya tadvāsya pratidadhaturiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'So be it' — and he taught them. When he had taught them, they cut off his head and placed it elsewhere; then, bringing the head of a horse, they attached it to him. With that [head], he taught them. And when he had taught them, <s>Indra</s> cut off that [horse's] head. Then, bringing his own head, they re-attached it to him.

children.text:
yāvattu pravargyakarmāṅgabhūtaṃ madhu tāvadeva tatrābhihitam, na tu kakṣyamātmājñānākhyam /
tatra yā ākhyāyikābhihitā seha stutyarthā pradarśyate /
idaṃ vai tanmadhu dadhyaṅṅātharvaṇo 'nena prapañcenāśvibhyāmuvāca /
tadetadṛpiḥ-tadetat karma, śṛpirmantraḥ, paśyannupalabhamānaḥ, avocat-uttkavān /
katham? taddaṃsa iti vyavahitena sambandhaḥ /
daṃsa iti karmaṇo nāmadheyam /
tacca daṃsaḥ kiviśiṣṭam? ugraṃ krūram /
vāṃ yuvayoḥ /
he narā narākārāvaśvinau /
tacca karma kinnimitam? sanaye lābhāya !lāmalubdho hi loke 'pi krūraṃ karmācarati, tathaivaitāvupalabhyete yathā soke /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] However, only the honey that forms part of the <s>Pravargya</s> ritual was stated there — not the inner [meaning], which is characterized by self-knowledge (<s>ātmajñāna</s>). The narrative that was related there is presented here for the purpose of praise. 'This is verily that honey' — <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> told the two <s>Aśvins</s> through this elaborate [teaching]. 'Seeing this, the <s>ṛṣi</s>' — 'this' refers to this deed (<s>karma</s>); '<s>ṛṣi</s>' means the <s>mantra</s> [seer]; 'seeing' means perceiving; 'said' means declared. How? '<s>Tat daṃsa</s>' — the connection is with the separated [word]. '<s>Daṃsa</s>' is the name of the deed. And what kind of deed is it? '<s>Ugra</s>' — fierce, cruel. '<s>Vām</s>' — of you two. 'O <s>Narā</s>' (heroes) — the two <s>Aśvins</s>, having the form of men. And for what purpose was this deed done? '<s>Sanaye</s>' — for gain. For even in the world, one who is greedy for gain performs cruel deeds — so too these two are observed [to act] just as [people do] in the world.

children.text:
tadāviḥ prakāśaṃ kṛṇomi karomi yadrahasi bhavadbhayāṃ kṛtam, kimiva? ityucyate--tanyatuḥ parjanyaḥ, na iva /
nakārastūpariṣṭādupacāra upamārthīyo vede, na pratipedhārthaḥ;yathāśvaṃ na /
aśvamiveti yadvat /
tanyaturiva vṛrṣṭi yathā parjanyo vṛrṣṭi prakāśayati stanayitnvādiśabdaiḥ, tadvadahaṃ yuvayoḥ krūraṃ karma āviṣkṛṇomīti sambandhaḥ /
nanvaśvinoḥ stutyarthau kathamimau mantrau syātāṃ nindāvacanau hīmau /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'That I make manifest (<s>āviḥ</s>)' — I reveal, make public, what was done by you in secret. Like what? It is said: '<s>tanyatuḥ</s>' means <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god); '<s>na</s>' [here functions] not as a negation. The particle '<s>na</s>' here, placed before [the noun], is used figuratively in the <s>Veda</s> for the purpose of comparison, not for negation — just as '<s>aśvam na</s>' means 'like a horse.' Like rain [accompanied by] thunder — just as <s>Parjanya</s> makes rain manifest through the sounds of thunder and the like, similarly, I make manifest the cruel deed of you two — this is the syntactical connection. [Objection:] But how can these <s>mantras</s> be for the praise of the <s>Aśvins</s>, when they seem to be words of censure?

children.text:
naipa doṣaḥ;stutirevaiṣā, na nindāvacanau /
yasmādīdṛśamapyatikrūraṃ karma kurvatoryuvayorna loma ca mīyata iti /
na cānyatkiñcidvīyata eveti /
stutāvetau bhavataḥ /
nindāṃ praśaṃsāṃ hi laukikāḥ smaranti /
tathā praśaṃsārūpā ca nindā loke prasidvā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There is no fault in this — for this is indeed praise, not words of censure. Because even while performing such an extremely cruel deed, not even a hair of yours was harmed — nor was anything else at all lost. Thus you two are [being] praised. For worldly [usage] recognizes censure [used as] praise. And likewise, praise in the form of censure is well known in the world.

children.text: dadhyaṅnāma ātharvaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Dadhyañc</s>' by name, son of <s>Atharvan</s> (<s>Ātharvaṇa</s>).

children.text: hetyanarthako nipātaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Ha</s>' is a meaningless particle.

children.text: yanmadhukakṣyamātmajñānalakṣaṇamāthavaṇo vāṃ yukābhyāmaśvasya śīrṣṇā śirasā prayat īm uvāca yat provāca madhu /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'That which is the honey — the inner [meaning] characterized by self-knowledge — <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> told you two (<s>vām</s>) through the head (<s>śīrṣṇā</s>) of a horse — '<s>pra yat īm uvāca</s>' means 'that which he declared, the honey.'

children.text: īmityanarthako nipātaḥ //16//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Īm</s>' is a meaningless particle. (16)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.17
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.17]

children.text:
idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca |
tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat -- ātharvaṇāyāśvinau dadhīce 'śvyaṃ śiraḥ praty airayatam |
sa vāṃ madhu pra vocad ṛtāyan tvāṣṭraṃ yad dasrāv apikakṣyaṃ vām iti || BrhUp_2,5.17 ||
children.translated_text: 'This is verily that honey which <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> told to the two <s>Aśvins</s>. Seeing this, the <s>ṛṣi</s> said: "For <s>Dadhīci Ātharvaṇa</s>, O <s>Aśvins</s>, you two provided the head of a horse. Keeping his vow, O <s>Dasras</s>, he told you two the honey of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> — that which is your secret."' (BṛUp 2.5.17)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.17
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.17:]

children.text:
idaṃ vai tanmadhvityādi pūrvavanmantrāntaradarśanārtham /
tathānyo mantrastāmeva ākhyāyikāmanusaratisma /
ātharvaṇo dadhyaṅnāma, ātharvaṇo 'nyo vidyata ityato viśinaṣṭi dadhyaṅnāmātharvaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This is verily that honey' and so forth — as before; the purpose is to introduce another <s>mantra</s>. Thus another <s>mantra</s> follows the very same narrative. '<s>Ātharvaṇa</s>' — [here] the name is <s>Dadhyañc</s>; since there could be another <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>, [the text] specifies: '<s>Dadhyañc</s> by name, the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>.'

children.text:
tasmai dadhīca ātharvaṇāya he 'śvināviti mantradṛśo vacanam, aśvyama śvasya svabhūtaṃ śiraḥ, brāhmaṇasya śirasicchinne 'śvasya śiraśchittvedṛśamatikrūraṃ karma kṛtvā aśvayaṃ śiro brāhmaṇaṃ prati erayataṃ gamitavantau yuvām /
sa cātharvaṇo vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ tanmadhu pravocad yat pūrvaṃ pratijñātaṃ vakṣyāmīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'For that <s>Dadhīci Ātharvaṇa</s>' — this is the speech of the seer of the <s>mantra</s>; O two <s>Aśvins</s> — '<s>aśvyam</s>' means a head belonging to a horse, [its] own; having cut off the head of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and cut off the head of a horse — having performed such an extremely cruel deed — '<s>airayatam</s>' means you two conveyed, made go, the horse's head onto the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. And that <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> told you two (<s>vām</s>) that honey — that which was previously promised: 'I shall tell [it].'

children.text:
sa kimarthamevaṃ jīvitasandehamāruhya pravocat? ityucyate /
śṛtāyan yata pūrvaṃ pratijñātaṃ satyaṃ tat paripālayitumicchan /
jīvitādapi hi satyadharmaparipālanā gurutaretyesya liṅgametat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For what purpose did he speak thus, risking his life? It is said: '<s>ṛtāyan</s>' — because, wishing to uphold the truth (<s>satya</s>) that had been previously promised. For the preservation of the <s>dharma</s> of truth is weightier even than life — this is the indication of this [passage].

children.text: ki tanmadhu pravocat? ityucyate-tvāṣṭram, tvaṣṭā ādityastasya sambandhi, yajñasya śiraśchinnaṃ tvaṣṭābhavat,
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What was the honey that he told? It is said: '<s>Tvāṣṭram</s>' — related to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> is the sun (<s>Āditya</s>); it was <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> whose sacrifice's head was severed,

children.text:
tatpratisandhānārtha pravargya karma /
tatra pravargyakarmāṅgabhūtaṃ yad vijñānaṃ tattvāṣṭraṃ madhu-yajñasya śiraśchedanapratisandhānādiviṣayaṃ darśanaṃ tattvāṣṭraṃ yanmadhu he dastro, dastrāviti parabalānāmupakṣapayitārau śatrūṇāṃ vā
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] and the <s>Pravargya</s> ritual serves the purpose of re-attaching it. The knowledge that forms part of the <s>Pravargya</s> ritual — the vision (<s>darśana</s>) pertaining to the severing and re-attachment of the sacrifice's head — that is the '<s>Tvāṣṭra</s>' honey. O <s>Dasras</s> — '<s>Dasra</s>' means those who consume the strength of others, or those who harm enemies,

children.text: hiṃsitārau, api ca na kevalaṃ tvāṣṭrameva madhu karmasambandhiyuvābhyāmavocat, api ca kakṣyaṃ gopyaṃ rahasyaṃ paramātmasambandhi yad vijñānaṃ madhu madhubrāhmaṇenottkamadhyāyadvayaprakāśitam, tacca vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ pravocadityanuvartate //17//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] and moreover — <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> told you two not merely the <s>Tvāṣṭra</s> honey related to ritual, but also the '<s>kakṣya</s>' — the secret, the hidden, the esoteric — that which is the knowledge (<s>vijñāna</s>) related to the <s>Paramātman</s>, the honey illuminated through the two chapters culminating in the <s>madhu-brāhmaṇa</s> — that too he told you two (<s>vām</s>); this is to be supplied. (17)

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.18
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.18]

children.text:
idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca |
tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat -- puraś cakre dvipadaḥ puraś cakre catuṣpadaḥ |
puraḥ sa pakṣī bhutvā puraḥ puruṣa āviśad iti |
sa vā ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvāsu pūrṣu puriśayaḥ |
nainena kiṃ canānāvṛtam |
nainena kiṃ canāsaṃvṛtam || BrhUp_2,5.18 ||
children.translated_text: 'This is verily that honey which <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> told to the two <s>Aśvins</s>. Seeing this, the <s>ṛṣi</s> said: "He made cities for the two-footed; he made cities for the four-footed. Having become a bird, he entered the cities as a <s>puruṣa</s>." This <s>puruṣa</s> indeed, lying in all cities, is the <s>puriśaya</s> (city-dweller). There is nothing that is not covered by him. There is nothing that is not pervaded by him.' (BṛUp 2.5.18)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.18
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.18:]

children.text:
idaṃ vai tanmadhviti pūrvavat /
uttkau dvau mantrau pravargyasambandhyākhyāyikopasaṃhartārau /
dvayoḥ pravargyakarmārthayoradhyāyayorartha ākhyāyikābhūtābhyāṃ mantrābhyāṃ prakāśitaḥ /
brahmavidyārthayostvadhyāyayorarthauttarābhyāmṛgbhyāṃ prakāśayitavyaḥ, ityataḥ pravartate /
yat kakṣyaṃ ca madhuttkavānātharvaṇo yuvābhyāmityuttkam /
kiṃ punasdanmadhu? ityucyate-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This is verily that honey' — as before. The first two <s>mantras</s> serve to conclude the narrative related to the <s>Pravargya</s>. The meaning of the two chapters relating to the <s>Pravargya</s> ritual has been illuminated by the two <s>mantras</s> that formed part of the narrative. But the meaning of the two chapters relating to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is to be illuminated by the subsequent <s>ṛk</s> verses — and therefore [this section] commences. That which is the secret honey — declared by <s>Ātharvaṇa</s> to you two — was previously stated. What then is that honey? It is said:

children.text:
puraścakre puraḥ purāṇi śarīrāṇi yata iyamacyākṛtavyākaraṇaprakriyā sa parameśvaro nāmarūpe avyākrate vyākurvāṇaḥ prathamaṃ bhūrādīṃ llokān sṛṣṭvā cakre kṛtavāna dvipado dvipādapalakṣitāni manuṣyaśarīrāṇi pakṣiśarīrāṇi /
tavā puraḥ śarīrāṇi cakre catuṣpadaścatuṣpādupalakṣitāni paśuśarīrāṇi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'He made cities (<s>puras</s>)' — '<s>puras</s>' means bodies; that supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) — through this process of manifesting the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — first having created the worlds such as <s>bhūḥ</s> and the rest, evolving name and form from the unmanifest, made (<s>cakre</s>) 'two-footed' [cities] — bodies characterized by two feet, namely human bodies and bird bodies. Likewise, he made 'four-footed' [cities] — bodies characterized by four feet, namely animal bodies.

children.text: puraḥ purastān sa īśvaraḥ pakṣī liṅgaśarīraṃ bhūtvā puraḥ śarīrāṇipuruṣa āviśadityasyārthamācaṣṭe śrutiḥ-sa vā ayaṃ puruṣaḥ sarvāsuyūrṣu sarvaśarīreṣu puriśayaḥ, puriśeta iti puriśayaḥ san puruṣa ityucyate /
nainenānena kiñacana kiñcidapyanāvṛtamanācchaditam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'By him, nothing whatsoever is uncovered' — nothing at all is left unpermeated.

children.text: tathā nainena kiñcanāsaṃvṛtamantarananupraveśitaṃ bāhyabhūtenāntarbhūtena ca na anāvṛtam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Likewise, 'by him, nothing whatsoever is unenveloped' — nothing is left unentered; [he pervades] both as external and internal — nothing is uncovered.

children.text: evaṃ sa eva nāmakhyātmanā antarvahirbhāvena kāryakaraṇarūpeṇa vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, he alone — in the form of name and the like, as the inner self (<s>ātman</s>) — is established [in everything] through being both internal and external, in the form of cause and effect.

children.text: puraścakre ityādimantraḥ saṅkṣepata ātmaikatvamācaṣṭaityarthaḥ //18//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>mantra</s> 'He made cities' and so forth briefly declares the oneness of the self — this is the meaning. (18)

[Commentary:] 'Having become a bird (<s>pakṣin</s>)' — that is, having first [assumed] a subtle body (<s>liṅgaśarīra</s>), the Lord entered [all] bodies as a <s>puruṣa</s> — and the <s>śruti</s> states the meaning of this: 'This <s>puruṣa</s> indeed, in all cities — in all bodies — is the <s>puriśaya</s>,' one who lies in the city; being one who lies in the city (<s>puriśaya</s>), he is called '<s>puruṣa</s>.'

children.text: START BrhUp 2,5.19
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 2.5.19]

children.text:
idaṃ vai tan madhu dadhyaṅṅ ātharvaṇo 'śvibhyām uvāca |
tad etad ṛṣiḥ paśyann avocat -- rūpaṃrūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva tad asya rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya |
indro māyābhiḥ pururūpa īyate yuktā hy asya harayaḥ śatā daśeti |
ayaṃ vai harayo 'yaṃ vai daśa ca sahasraṇi bahūni cānantāni ca |
tad etad brahmāpūrvam anaparam anantaram abāhyam |
ayam ātmā brahma sarvānubhūḥ |
ity anuśāsanam || BrhUp_2,5.19 ||
children.translated_text: 'This is verily that honey which <s>Dadhyañc Ātharvaṇa</s> told to the two <s>Aśvins</s>. Seeing this, the <s>ṛṣi</s> said: "He became the counterpart of every form — this was his form, for the purpose of making him known. <s>Indra</s>, through his <s>māyās</s> (powers), goes about in many forms; for yoked are his steeds, ten hundreds." He indeed is the steeds; he indeed is tens and thousands, many and infinite. This is <s>Brahman</s> — without a prior, without a posterior, without an interior, without an exterior. This self is <s>Brahman</s>, the all-experiencing. Such is the teaching.' (BṛUp 2.5.19)

children.text: BrhUpBh_2,5.19
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 2.5.19:]

children.text:
idaṃ vai tanmadhvityādi pūrvavat /
rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo rūpāntaraṃ babhūvetyarthaḥ /
pratirūpo 'nurūpo vā yādṛksaṃmathānau mātāpitarau tatsaṃsthānastadanurūpa eva putro jāyate /
na hi catuṣpado dvipājjāyate dvipado vā catuṣpāt /
sa eva hi parameśvaro nāmarūpe vyākurvāṇo rūpaṃ rūpaṃ pratirūpo babhūva /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This is verily that honey' and so forth — as before. 'He became the counterpart of every form' — the meaning is: he became a form corresponding to [each] different form. '<s>Pratirūpa</s>' means 'of corresponding form' — just as parents of a certain appearance [produce] a son who conforms to that appearance, of that very corresponding form. For a four-footed being is not born from a two-footed one, nor a two-footed being from a four-footed one. That very supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), evolving name and form, 'became the counterpart of every form.'

children.text:
kimartha punaḥ pratirūpamāgamanaṃ tasya? ityucyate--tadasyātmano rūpaṃ praticakṣaṇāya pratikhyāpanāya /
yadi hi nāmarūpe na vyākriyete, tadā asyātmano nirūpādhikaṃ rūpaṃ prajñānaghanākhyaṃ na pratikhyāyeta /
yadā punaḥ kāryakaraṇātmanā nāmarūpe vyāka-te bhavataḥ, tadāsya rūpaṃ pratikhyāyeta /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But for what purpose was his coming as a counterpart? It is said: 'That is his — the self's — form, for the purpose of making known (<s>praticakṣaṇāya</s>), for the purpose of revelation.' For if name and form were not evolved, then his — the self's — form, free from all limiting adjuncts, known as a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), would not be revealed. But when name and form become evolved — in the form of cause and effect — then his form is revealed.

children.text:
indraḥ parameśvaro māyābhiḥ prajñābhiḥ nāmarūpabhūtakṛtamithyābhimānairvā, na tu paramārthataḥ; pururūpo bahurūpa īyate gabhyate, ekarūpa eva prajñānaghanaḥ sannavidyāprajñābhiḥ /
kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt? yuttkā ratha iva vājinaḥ svavipayaprakāśanāya, hi yasmāndasya harayo haraṇādindriyāṇi, śatā śatāni, daśa ca prāṇibhedabāhulyācchatāna daśa ca bhavanti /
tasmādindriyavipayabāhulyāttatprakāśanāyeva ca yuttkāna tāni na ātmaprakāśanāya /
"parāñci khāni vyatṛṇat svayambhūḥ"iti hi kāṭhake /
tasmātaireva vipayasvarūpairīyate na prajñānaghanaikarasena svarūpeṇa /
children.translated_text:
[Commentary:] <s>Indra</s>, the supreme Lord, through <s>māyās</s> — through cognitions, or through false self-identifications produced by name, form, and elements — not in ultimate reality; appears as multiform (<s>pururūpa</s>), of many forms — he is apprehended [thus], though being of one form alone, a mass of pure consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), through the cognitions of <s>avidyā</s>.
For what reason? Like horses yoked to a chariot, for the purpose of illuminating their own objects — because his steeds (<s>harayas</s>), the sense organs (<s>indriyas</s>) that carry [sense-data], are hundreds upon hundreds, and ten as well, owing to the multiplicity of living beings — they are hundreds and ten.
Therefore, due to the multiplicity of sense-objects, and because [the senses] are yoked solely for illuminating those [objects] — not for illuminating the self.
'The self-born one pierced the openings outward' — thus says the <s>Kāṭhaka</s> (<s>Kaṭha Upaniṣad</s>).
Therefore, [the self] is apprehended only through the forms of those sense-objects — not through its own nature as the mass of pure consciousness of one taste.

children.text:
evaṃ tahi ayamanyaḥ parameśvaro 'nye haraya ityevaṃ prāpte ucyate-ayaṃ vai harayo 'yaṃ vai daśa ca sahasrāṇi bahūni cānantāni ca prāṇibhedasyānantyāt /
kiṃ bahunā, tadetadbrahma ya ātmā /
apūrvaṃ nāsya kāraṇaṃ pūrva vidyata ityapūrvam /
nāsyāparaṃ kāryaṃ vidyata ityanaparam /
nāsya jātyantaramantarāle vidyata ityanaltaram /
tathā bahirasya na vidyata ityavāhyam /
kiṃ punastannirantaraṃ brahma? ayamātmanā /
ko 'sau? yaḥ pratyagātmā draṣṭā śrotā mantā bodvā vijñātā sarvānubhūḥ, sarvātmanā sarvamanubhavatīti sarvamanubhūḥ /
ityetadanuśāsanaṃ sarvavedāntopadeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the instruction, the teaching of all <s>Vedānta</s>.

children.text: eṣa sarvavedāntānāmupasaṃhrator'thaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is the concluding purport of all the <s>Vedāntas</s>.

children.text: etadamṛtamabhayam /
children.translated_text: This is the immortal, the fearless.

children.text: parisamāptaśca śāstrārthaḥ //19 //
children.translated_text: And the meaning of the scripture is fully concluded. || 19 ||

[Commentary:] If this is so — 'this one [the self] is different, and the supreme Lord is different, and the steeds are different' — when such a [conclusion] is arrived at, [the text] says: this one indeed is the steeds, this one indeed is ten and thousands, many and infinite — owing to the infinity of the varieties of living beings.
What need of more words? That is this <s>Brahman</s>, which is the self.
It is without prior (<s>apūrva</s>) — no cause prior to it exists, hence without prior.
No subsequent effect of it exists, hence without posterior (<s>anapara</s>).
No other species exists in between, hence without interior (<s>anantara</s>).
Likewise, nothing external to it exists, hence without exterior (<s>abāhya</s>).
What then is this <s>Brahman</s> that is without interval? It is this self (<s>ātman</s>).
Who is that? The inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) — the seer, the hearer, the thinker, the knower, the cognizer, the all-experiencer — one who experiences everything through the totality of selves, hence the all-experiencer (<s>sarvānubhū</s>).

children.text: // iti pañcamaṃ brāhmaṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
