children.text: ADHYAYA 3
children.translated_text: ADHYĀYA 3

children.text:
janako ha vaideha ityādi yājñavalkoyaṃ kāṇḍamārabhyate /
upapattipradhānatvādatikrāntena madhukāṇḍena samānārthatve 'pi sati na punaruktatā /
madhukāṇḍaṃ hyāgemapradhānam /
āgamopapattī hyātmaikatvaprakāśanāya pravṛtte śaknutaḥ karatalagatabilvamiva darśayitum /
śrotavyo mantavya iti hyuktam /
tasmādāgamārthasyaiva parīkṣāpūrvakaṃ nirdhāraṇāya yājñavalkīyaṃ kāṇḍamupapattipradhānamārabhyate /
ākhyāyikā tu vijñānastutyarthopāyavidhiparā vā /
prasiddho hyupāyo vidvadbhiḥ śāstreṣu ca dṛṣṭo dānam /
dānena hṛyupanamante prāṇinaḥ /
prabhūtaṃ hiraṇyaṃ gosahasradānaṃ cehopalabhyate /
tasmādanyapareṇāpi śāstreṇa vidyāprāptyupāyadānapradarśanārthā'khyāyikā'rabdhā /
api ca tadvidyasaṃyogastaiśva saha vādakaraṇaṃ vidyāprāptyupāyo nyāyavidyāyāṃ dṛṣṭaḥ /
taccāsminnadyāye prābalyena pradarśyate /
pratyakṣā ca vidvatsaṃyoge prajñāvṛddhiḥ /
tasmādvidyāprāptyupāyapradarśanārthaivākhyāyikā /
children.translated_text:
[Commentary:] '<s>Janaka</s>, [king] of <s>Videha</s>' — thus begins the <s>Yājñavalkya</s> section (<s>Yājñavalkīya Kāṇḍa</s>).
Because it is predominantly reasoning-based, even though it has the same meaning as the preceding <s>Madhukāṇḍa</s> (honey doctrine), there is no repetition.
For the <s>Madhukāṇḍa</s> is predominantly based on scripture (<s>āgama</s>).
Scripture and reasoning, being engaged in illuminating the oneness of the self, are capable of showing it like a <s>bilva</s> fruit in the palm of one's hand.
'It should be heard, it should be reflected upon' — thus it was said.
Therefore, for the purpose of ascertaining the meaning of scripture through prior examination, the <s>Yājñavalkya</s> section, predominantly based on reasoning, is commenced.
The narrative (<s>ākhyāyikā</s>) is either for the purpose of glorifying knowledge, or has as its object the injunction of the means [to knowledge].
For donation (<s>dāna</s>) is a well-known means [to knowledge], recognized by the learned and seen in the treatises.
By gifts, living beings are won over in their hearts.
And here we find an abundant [gift of] gold and a thousand cows.
Therefore, the narrative is commenced even by another scripture for the purpose of demonstrating donation as a means of attaining knowledge.
Moreover, association with the learned and engaging in debate with them is seen as a means to attaining knowledge in the science of logic (<s>nyāyavidyā</s>).
And that is prominently demonstrated in this <s>adhyāya</s>.
And the increase of wisdom through association with the learned is directly perceived.
Therefore, the narrative is solely for the purpose of demonstrating the means of attaining knowledge.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.1.1]

children.text:
janako ha vaideho bahudakṣiṇena yajñeneje |
tatra ha kurupañcālānāṃ brāhmaṇā abhisametā babhūvuḥ |
tasya ha janakasya vaidehasya vijijñāsā babhūva -- kaḥ svid eṣāṃ brāhmaṇānām anūcānatama iti |
sa ha gavāṃ sahasram avarurodha |
daśadaśa pādā ekaikasyāḥ śṛṅgayor ābaddhā babhūvuḥ || BrhUp_3,1.1 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Janaka</s>, [king] of <s>Videha</s>, performed a sacrifice with abundant fees (<s>dakṣiṇās</s>).
There, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Kuru</s>-<s>Pañcāla</s> [countries] had assembled.
<s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> had a desire to know: 'Which of these <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is the most learned?'
He penned up a thousand cows.
To the horns of each, ten <s>pādas</s> [of gold] were fastened. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.1 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.1 janako nāma ha kila samrāḍrājā babhūva videhānāṃ tatra bhavo vaidehaḥ /
sa ca bahudakṣiṇena yajñena śākhāntaraprasiddho vā bahudakṣiṇo nāma yajño 'śvamedho vā dakṣiṇābāhulyādbahudakṣiṇa ihocyate teneje 'yajat /
tatra tasminyajñe nimantritā darśanakāmā vā kurūṇāṃ deśānāṃ pañcālānāṃ ca brāhmaṇāsteṣu hi viduṣāṃ bāhulyaṃ prasiddhamabhisametā abhisaṃgatā babhūvuḥ /
tatra mahāntaṃ vidvatsamudāyaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya ha kila janakasya vaidehasya yajamānasya ko nu khalvatra brahmiṣṭha iti viśeṣeṇa jñātumicchā vijijñāsā babhūva /
kathaṃ, kaḥsvitko nu khalveṣāṃ brāhmaṇānāmanūcānatamaḥ sarva ime 'nūcānāḥ kaḥsvideṣāmatiśayenānūcāna iti /
sa hānūcānatamaviṣayotpannijijñāsaḥ saṃstadvijñānopāyārthaṃ gavāṃ sahasraṃ prathamavayasāmavarurodha goṣṭhe 'varodhaṃ kārayāmāsa /
kiṃviśiṣṭāstā gāvo 'varuddhā ityucyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What kind of cows were those that were penned up? This is stated:

children.text: palacaturthabhāgaḥ pādaḥ suvarṇasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] A <s>pāda</s> is a quarter [<s>pala</s>] measure of gold.

children.text: daśa daśa pādā ekaikasyā goḥ śṛṅgayorābaddhā babhūvuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Ten <s>pādas</s> [of gold] were fastened to the horns of each cow.

children.text: pañca pañca pādā ekaikasmiñśṛṅge //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Five <s>pādas</s> on each horn. || 1 ||

[Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.1:] <s>Janaka</s> by name was indeed an emperor (<s>samrāj</s>), a king of the <s>Videhas</s>; born there, he is [called] <s>Vaideha</s>.
He performed a sacrifice with abundant fees (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) — or the sacrifice known as 'bahudakṣiṇa,' well-known in another <s>Veda</s> branch, or the horse-sacrifice (<s>aśvamedha</s>), which is called 'bahudakṣiṇa' (having abundant fees) here because of the abundance of sacrificial fees.
There, at that sacrifice, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Kuru</s> and <s>Pañcāla</s> countries — in which countries the abundance of the learned is well-known — having been invited, or having come out of a desire to see, had assembled, had gathered together.
There, having seen the great assembly of the learned, <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s>, the sacrificer, had a desire to know — a wish to know specifically — 'Who indeed among them is the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmiṣṭha</s>)?'
How [did he determine this]? 'Which one indeed (<s>kaḥsvit</s>) — who indeed — among these <s>brāhmaṇas</s> is the most learned (<s>anūcānatama</s>)? All of these are learned — who among them is preeminent in learning?'
He, with the desire to know who was the most learned having arisen, and for the purpose of a means of ascertaining that — penned up in a cow-pen (<s>goṣṭha</s>) a thousand cows of prime age.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.1.2]

children.text:
tān hovāca -- brāhmaṇā bhagavanto yo vo brahmiṣṭhaḥ sa etā gā udajatām iti |
te ha brāhmaṇā na dadhṛṣuḥ |
atha ha yājñavalkyaḥ svam eva brahmacāriṇam uvāca -- etāḥ saumyodaja sāmaśravā3 iti |
tā hodācakāra |
te ha brāhmaṇāś cukrudhuḥ: -- kathaṃ nu no brahmiṣṭho bruvīteti |
atha ha janakasya vaidehasya hotāśvalo babhūva |
sa hainaṃ papraccha -- tvaṃ nu khalu no yājñavalkya brahmiṣṭho 'sī3 iti |
sa hovāca -- namo vayaṃ brahmiṣṭhāya kurmo gokāmā eva vayaṃ sma iti |
taṃ ha tata eva praṣṭuṃ dadhre hotāśvalaḥ || BrhUp_3,1.2 ||
children.translated_text:
To them he said: 'Venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, whoever among you is the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmiṣṭha</s>), let him drive away these cows.'
Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> did not dare.
Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> addressed his own pupil: 'Drive these [cows] away, dear <s>Sāmaśravas</s>.'
He drove them away.
The <s>brāhmaṇas</s> were angered: 'How dare he claim to be the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> among us!'
Now <s>Aśvala</s> was the <s>hotṛ</s> priest of <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s>.
He asked [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>]: 'Are you indeed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> among us?'
[<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] said: 'We bow to the most learned in <s>Brahman</s>. We were merely desirous of cows.'
Thereupon, <s>Aśvala</s> the <s>hotṛ</s> priest resolved to question him further. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.2 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.2 gā evamavarudhya brāhmaṇāṃstānhovāca /
he brāhmaṇā bhagavanta ityāmantratha yo vo yuṣmākaṃ brahmiṣṭhaḥ sarve yūyaṃ brahmāṇo 'tiśayena yuṣmākaṃ brahmā yaḥ sa etā gā udajatāmutkālayatu svagṛhaṃ prati /
te ha brāhmaṇā na dadhṛṣuḥ ha kilaivamuktā brāhmaṇā brahmiṣṭhatāmātmanaḥ pratijñātuṃ na dadhṛpurna pragalbhāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ /
apragalbhabhūteṣu brāhmaṇeṣvatha ha yājñavalkyaḥ svamātmīyameva brahmacāriṇamantevāsinamuvāca- etā gā he somyodajodgamayāsmadgṛhān prati, he sāmaśravaḥ- sāmavidhiṃ hi śṛṇotyator'yāccaturvedo yājñavalkyaḥ /
tā gā hodācakārotkālitavānācāryagṛhaṃ prati /
yājñavalkyena brahmiṣṭhapaṇasvīkaraṇena ātmano brahmiṣṭhatā pratijñātā, iti te ha cukrudhuḥ kruddhavanto brāhmaṇāḥ /
teṣāṃ krodhābhiprāyamācaṣṭe- kathaṃ no 'smākaṃ ekaikapradhānānāṃ brahmiṣṭho 'smīti bruvīteti /
atha haivaṃ kruddheṣu brāhmaṇeṣu janakasya yajamānasya hotā ṛtvigaśvalo nāma babhūva āsīt /
sa enaṃ yājñavalkyam, brahmiṣṭhābhimānī rājāśrayatvāccadhṛṣṭaḥ, yājñavalkyaṃ papraccha pṛṣṭavān /
katham? tvaṃ nu khalu no yājñavalkya brahmiṣṭho 'sī 3 iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How [did he ask]? 'Are you indeed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> among us?'

children.text: plutirbhartsanārthā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The prolonged accent (<s>pluti</s>) is used for the purpose of reproach.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ- namaskarmo vayaṃ brahmiṣṭhāya, idānīṃ gokāmāḥ smo vayamiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'We bow to the most learned in <s>Brahman</s>; we were merely desirous of cows' —

children.text: taṃ brahmiṣṭhapratijñaṃ santaṃ tata eva brahmiṣṭhapaṇasvīkaraṇāt praṣṭuṃ dadhre dhṛtavān mano hotā aśvalaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Aśvala</s>, the <s>hotṛ</s> priest, having resolved to question him — who had made the claim of being the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> — precisely because of his acceptance of the wager, set his mind to questioning him. || 2 ||

[Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.2:] Having penned up the cows thus, he said to those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>:
'O venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' — thus addressing them — 'whoever among you is the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmiṣṭha</s>) — all of you are knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, but whoever among you is preeminent — let him drive away these cows, let him send them to his own house.'
Those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> did not dare — having been thus told, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> did not dare, did not have the boldness to claim for themselves the status of being the most learned in <s>Brahman</s>.
When the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> lacked boldness, then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> addressed his own pupil, his resident student: 'Drive these cows away, O dear <s>Sāmaśravas</s> — [so named because] he hears (<s>śṛṇoti</s>) the <s>Sāma</s>-ritual procedure, and accordingly <s>Yājñavalkya</s> was a master of all four <s>Vedas</s>.
He drove the cows away — he sent them toward the teacher's house.
By <s>Yājñavalkya</s>'s acceptance of the wager for the most learned in <s>Brahman</s>, his own claim to being the most learned was declared; therefore those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> were angered, became wrathful.
The purport of their anger is stated: 'How can he declare himself the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> among us, each of whom is preeminent?'
Then, when the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> were thus angered, <s>Aśvala</s> by name was the <s>hotṛ</s> priest, the <s>ṛtvik</s>, of <s>Janaka</s> the sacrificer.
He — bold because of his status as the most learned in <s>Brahman</s> and because of [his position under] royal patronage — questioned <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.1.3]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yad idaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyunāptaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyunābhipannaṃ kena yajamāno mṛtyor āptim atimucyata iti |
hotrartvijāgninā vācā |
vāg vai yajñasya hotā |
tad yeyaṃ vāk so 'yam agniḥ sa hotā sā muktiḥ sātimuktiḥ || BrhUp_3,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'since all this is pervaded by death, since all this is overcome by death — by what means does the sacrificer free himself from the reach of death?' By the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest, by fire, by speech. Speech indeed is the <s>Hotṛ</s> of the sacrifice. This speech is this fire; that is the <s>Hotṛ</s>; that is liberation (<s>mukti</s>); that is complete liberation (<s>atimukti</s>). (BṛUp 3.1.3)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.3 yājñavalkyeti hovāca /
tatra madhukāṇḍe pāḍaktena karmaṇā darśanasaptuccitena yajamānasya mṛtyoratyayo vyākhyāta udgīthaprakaraṇe saṅkṣepataḥ /
tasyaiva parīkṣāviṣayo 'yamititadgatadarśanaviśeṣārtho 'yaṃ vistara ārabhyate /
yadidaṃ sādhanajātam asya karmaṇa ṛtvigagnyādi mṛtyunā karmalakṣaṇena svābhāvikāsaṅgasahitena āptaṃ jyāptam, na kevalaṃ vyāptamabhiṣannaṃ ca mṛtyunā baśīkṛtaṃ ca /
kena darśanalakṣaṇena sādhanena yajamāno mṛtyorāptimati mṛtyugacaratvam atikramya mucyate svatantro mṛtyoravaśo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
nanūdgītha evābhihitaṃ yenātimucyatemukhyaprāṇātmadarśaneneti /
bāḍhamuktam, yo 'nukto viśeṣastatra, tadartho 'yamārambha ityadoṣaḥ /
hotrartvijāgninā vācetyāha yājñavalkyaḥ /
etasyārthaṃvyācaṣṭe /
kaḥ punarhetā yena mṛtyumatikāmati? ityucyate-vāgvai yajñasya yajamānasya"yajño vai yajamānaḥ"iti śruteḥ /
yajñasya yajamānasya yāvāksaiva hotādhiyajñe /
katham? tatatrayeyaṃvanga yajñasyayajamānasya so 'yaṃ prasiddho 'gniradhidaivatam /
tadetatvyannaprakaraṇevyākhyātam /
sa cāgnirhetā"agnirvai hotā"iti śruteḥ /
yadetad yajñasya sādhanadvayamhotā catviṅg adhiyajñam, adhyātmaṃ ca vāk etadubhayaṃ sādhanadvayaṃ paricchinnaṃ mṛtyunā āptaṃ svābhāvikājñānāsaṅgaprayuktena karmaṇā mṛtyunā pratikṣaṇamanyathātvamāpadyamānaṃ vaśīkṛtam /
tad anenādhidaivatarūpeṇāgninā'dṛśyamānaṃ'yajamānasya yajñasya sṛtyoratimuktaye bhavati /
tadetadāha-sa muktiḥ sa hotā agnirmuktiḥ, agnisvarūpadarśanameva muktiḥ /
yadaiva sādhanadvayamagnirūpeṇa gaśyati, tadānīmeva hi svābhāvikādāsaṅgānmṛtyorvimucyate ādhyātmikāt paricchinnarūpādādhibhautikācca /
tasmāt sa hotā agnirūpeṇa dṛṣṭo muktirmuktisādhanaṃ yajamānasya /
sā atimuktiḥ-yaiva ca muktiḥ sātimuktiḥ, atimuktisādhanamityarthaḥ /
sādhanadvayasya paricchinnasya yā adhidevatārūpeṇāparicchinnenāgnirūpeṇa dṛṣṭiḥ, sā muktiḥ /
yāsau muktiradhidevatādṛṣṭiḥ saiva, adhyātmādhibhūtaparicchedaviṣayāsaṅgāspadaṃ mṛtyumatikramya adhidevatātvasyāgnibhāvasya prāptiryā phalabhūtā, sā atimuktirityucyate /
tasyā atimuktermuktireva sādhanamiti kṛtvā sā atimuktirityāha /
yajamānasya hyatimuktirvāgādīnāmagnyādibhāva ityudgīthaprakaraṇe vyākhyātam /
tatra sāmānyena mukhyaprāṇadarśanamātraṃ muktisādhanamuktam, na tadviśeṣaḥ /
vāgādīnām agnyādidarśanamiha viśeṣo varṇyate /
mṛtyuprāptyatimuktistu saiva phalabhūtā, yodgīthabrāhmaṇena vyākhyātā -'mṛtyupratikrānto dīpyate'(1 / 3 / 12) ityādyā //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.1.3:] '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said. Therein, in the Honey-section (<s>Madhukāṇḍa</s>), the sacrificer's transcendence of death through action enriched with [meditative] vision was explained in the <s>Udgītha</s> section in summary. The present [discussion] has that very [topic] as its subject of examination — this elaboration is commenced for the purpose of the specific vision contained in it. 'All this' — the entire set of means of this ritual action — the priests, fires, and the rest — [is] pervaded, permeated, by death characterized by <s>karma</s> (action) together with the natural attachment [born of ignorance]; not merely pervaded but also overcome by death, i.e. brought under its control. By what means — characterized by [meditative] vision — does the sacrificer, transcending the reach of death, i.e. the state of being within death's domain, become liberated, become free, become independent of death — this is the meaning. [Objection:] But it was already stated in the <s>Udgītha</s> [section] that by which one is liberated — namely, through the vision of the essential <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath). [Response:] True, it was stated; but the specific detail that was not stated there — this commencement is for that purpose; hence there is no fault. '<s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied: by the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest, by fire, by speech.' He explains the meaning of this. But who is the <s>Hotṛ</s> by whom one transcends death? It is said: speech indeed is the <s>Hotṛ</s> of the sacrifice, i.e. of the sacrificer — because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'the sacrifice is indeed the sacrificer.' Speech alone is the <s>Hotṛ</s> of the sacrificer in the context of the sacrifice (<s>adhiyajña</s>). How? That very speech of the sacrificer — this well-known fire is its cosmic correlate (<s>adhidaivata</s>). This was explained in the food section. And that fire is the <s>Hotṛ</s> — because of the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Agni</s> indeed is the <s>Hotṛ</s>.' This pair of means of the sacrifice — the <s>Hotṛ</s> and fire in the context of the sacrifice (<s>adhiyajña</s>), and speech at the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>) — this pair of means, being limited, is pervaded by death — by <s>karma</s> impelled by natural ignorance and attachment — being subjected to constant transformation and brought under its control. When seen in its cosmic form (<s>adhidaivata</s>) as fire — [when] the unseen [nature is perceived] — it serves for the liberation of the sacrificer from death in the sacrifice. This is what [the text] says: 'that is liberation, that is the <s>Hotṛ</s>' — fire is liberation; the vision of the true nature of fire is itself liberation. When the pair of means is seen in the form of fire, at that very moment one is freed from the natural attachment — from death at the individual level (<s>ādhyātmika</s>), from the limited form, and from the physical (<s>ādhibhautika</s>) [level]. Therefore, the <s>Hotṛ</s> seen in the form of fire is liberation, the means of liberation for the sacrificer. 'That is complete liberation (<s>atimukti</s>)' — that which is liberation is itself complete liberation, meaning it is the means of complete liberation. The vision of the limited pair of means in the form of the unlimited cosmic deity (<s>adhidevatā</s>) as fire — that is liberation. That liberation — that vision of the cosmic deity — which, transcending death that is the ground of attachment regarding the limitation at the individual and physical levels, results in the attainment of the state of fire as cosmic deity — that result is called complete liberation. Liberation itself is the means of that complete liberation — therefore [the text] says 'that is complete liberation.' For the sacrificer's complete liberation is the transformation of speech and the rest into fire and the rest — as was explained in the <s>Udgītha</s> section. There, only the general vision of the essential <s>prāṇa</s> was stated as the means of liberation, not its specific details. The specific vision of speech and the rest as fire and the rest is described here. But the transcendence of death and its complete liberation is that very result — as explained by the <s>Udgītha Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'having crossed over death, he shines' (BṛUp 1.3.12) and so forth. // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.1.4]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yad idaṃ sarvam ahorātrābhyām āptaṃ sarvam ahorātrābhyām abhipannaṃ kena yajamāno 'horātrayor āptim atimucyata iti |
adhvaryuṇartvijā cakṣuṣādityena |
cakṣur vai yajñasyādhvaryuḥ |
tad yad idaṃ cakṣuḥ so 'sāv ādityaḥ |
so 'dhvaryuḥ sā muktiḥ sātimuktiḥ || BrhUp_3,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'since all this is pervaded by day and night, since all this is overcome by day and night — by what means does the sacrificer free himself from the reach of day and night?' By the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priest, by the eye, by the sun. The eye indeed is the <s>Adhvaryu</s> of the sacrifice. This eye is that sun; that is the <s>Adhvaryu</s>; that is liberation; that is complete liberation. (BṛUp 3.1.4)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.4 yājñavalkyeti hovāca /
svābhāvikādajñānāsaṅgaprayuktāt karmalakṣaṇānmṛtyoratimuktirvyākhyātā /
tasya karmaṇaḥ sāsaṅgasya mṛtyorāśrayabhūtānāṃ darśapūrṇamāsādikarmasādhanānāṃ yo vipariṇāmahetuḥ kālaḥ, tasmāt kālāt pṛthagatinuṣṭhānavyatirekeṇāpi prāgūrdhvaṃ ca kriyāyāḥ sādhanavipariṇāmahetutvena vyāpāradarśanāt kālasya /
tasmāt pṛthakkālādatimuktirvaktavyetyata āha- yadidaṃ sarvamahorātrābhyāmāptam, sa ca kālo dvirūpaḥ - ahorātrādilakṣaṇāḥ, tithyādilakṣaṇaśca /
tatrāhorātrādilakṣaṇāttāvadatimuktimāha - ahorātrābhyāṃ hi sarvaṃ jāyate vardhate vinaśyati ca, tathā yajñasādhanaṃ ca /
yajñasya yajamānasya cakṣuradhvaryuśca /
śiṣṭānyakṣarāṇi pūrvavanneyāni /
children.translated_text: The remaining words are to be construed as before.

children.text: yajamānasya cakṣuradhvaryuśca sādhanadvayamadhyātmādhibhūtaparicchedaṃ hitvā adhidaivatātmanā dṛṣṭaṃ yat sa muktiḥ so 'dhvaryurādityabhāvena dṛṣṭo muktiḥ /
children.translated_text: The pair of means of the sacrificer — the eye and the <s>Adhvaryu</s> — having abandoned the limitation at the individual and physical levels, when seen in the cosmic form (<s>adhidaivata</s>) — that is liberation. The <s>Adhvaryu</s> seen in the form of the sun is liberation.

children.text: saiva muktirevātimuktiriti /
children.translated_text: That liberation itself is complete liberation.

children.text: pūrvavat ādityātmabhāvamāpannasya hi nāhorātre sambhavataḥ //4//
children.translated_text: As before, for one who has attained the nature of the sun, day and night are not possible. // 4 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.1.4:] '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said. The complete liberation from death — characterized by <s>karma</s> impelled by natural ignorance and attachment — has been explained. Of that <s>karma</s>, together with its attachment, which is death — the cause of transformation of its means, the instruments of rituals like the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the rest — is time. From that time, even apart from the performance of a particular action, since time is observed to be operative as the cause of transformation of the means both before and after the action — therefore, liberation from time separately must be stated. Hence [the text] says: 'all this is pervaded by day and night.' And time has two aspects — characterized by day-and-night and the like, and characterized by lunar days (<s>tithi</s>) and the like. Therein, first, liberation from [time] characterized by day and night is stated: for by day and night, everything is born, grows, and perishes; likewise the means of sacrifice. [The correlate:] the eye and <s>Adhvaryu</s> of the sacrificer.

children.text: idānīṃ tithyādilakṣaṇādatimuktirucyate-
children.translated_text: Now liberation from [time] characterized by lunar days (<s>tithi</s>) and the like is stated:

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.1.5]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yad idaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvapakṣāparapakṣābhyām āptaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvapakṣāparapakṣābhyām abhipannaṃ kena yajamānaḥ pūrvapakṣāparapakṣayor āptim atimucyata iti |
udgātrartvijā vayunā prāṇena |
prāṇo vai yajñasyodgātā |
tad yo 'yaṃ prāṇaḥ sa vāyuḥ sa udgātā |
sa muktiḥ sātimuktiḥ || BrhUp_3,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'since all this is pervaded by the bright and dark fortnights, since all this is overcome by the bright and dark fortnights — by what means does the sacrificer free himself from the reach of the bright and dark fortnights?' By the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest, by the wind, by <s>prāṇa</s> (breath). <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Udgātṛ</s> of the sacrifice. This <s>prāṇa</s> is that wind; that is the <s>Udgātṛ</s>; that is liberation; that is complete liberation. (BṛUp 3.1.5)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.5 idānīṃ tithyādilakṣaṇādatimuktirūcyate-yadidaṃ sarvam - ahorātrayoraviśiṣṭayorādityaḥ kartā, na prati padādīnāṃ tithīnām;tāsāṃ tu vṛddhikṣayopagamanenapratipatprabhṛtīnāṃ candramāḥ kartā /
atastadāpācyā pūrvapakṣāparapakṣātyayaḥ, ādityāpacyā ahorātrātyayavat /
tatra yajamānasya prāṇo vāyuḥ, sa evaudgātā - ityudgīthabrāhmaṇe 'vagatam'vācā ca hyeva sa prāṇena codagāyat'iti ca nirdhāritam /
'athaitasya prāṇasyāpaḥ śarīraṃ jyotīrūpamasau candraḥ'iti ca /
prāṇāvāyucandramasāmekatvāccandramasā vāyunā copasaṃhāre na kaścid viśeṣaḥ /
evaṃ manyamānā śrutirvāyunā adhidaivatarūpeṇopasaṃharati /
api ca vāyunimittau hi vṛddhikṣayau candramasaḥ /
tena tithyādilakṣaṇasya kālasya karturapi kārayitā vāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, wind is the mover even of the agent of [time] characterized by lunar days and the like.

children.text: ato vāyurūpāpannastithyādikālādatīto bhavatītyupapannataraṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: Hence, one who has attained the form of wind transcends the time characterized by lunar days and the like — this is more fitting.

children.text: tena śrutyantare candrarūpeṇa dṛṣṭirmuktiratimuktiśca /
children.translated_text: Therefore, in another <s>śruti</s>, the vision in the form of the moon is liberation and complete liberation.

children.text: iha tu kāṇvānāṃ sādhanadvayasya tatkāraṇarūpeṇa vāyvātmanā dṛṣṭirmuktiratimuktiśceti na śrutyorvirodhaḥ //5//
children.translated_text: But here, for the <s>Kāṇvas</s>, the vision of the pair of means in the form of their cause — wind — is liberation and complete liberation. Thus there is no contradiction between the two <s>śrutis</s>. // 5 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.1.5:] Now liberation from [time] characterized by lunar days and the like is stated. 'All this' — day and night being undifferentiated, the sun is the agent [of day-night]; but it is not the agent of the individual lunar days (<s>tithi</s>) such as <s>pratipad</s> and the rest; rather, the moon is the agent of these, since it undergoes waxing and waning from <s>pratipad</s> onwards. Therefore, the transcendence of the bright and dark fortnights [should be taught] as brought about by the moon — just as the transcendence of day and night is brought about by the sun. Therein, the <s>prāṇa</s> and wind [are the correlates] of the sacrificer; [<s>prāṇa</s>] is indeed the <s>Udgātṛ</s> — this was understood in the <s>Udgītha Brāhmaṇa</s>: 'by speech and by <s>prāṇa</s> he sang the <s>Udgītha</s>,' and it was established. And [it was stated]: 'of this <s>prāṇa</s>, water is the body, and the luminous form is that moon.' Since <s>prāṇa</s>, wind, and moon are one, there is no difference whether the summary is made with the moon or with wind. The <s>śruti</s>, considering this, summarizes with wind in its cosmic form. Moreover, the waxing and waning of the moon are indeed caused by wind.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.1.6]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yad idam antarikṣam anārambaṇam iva kenākrameṇa yajamānaḥ svargaṃ lokam ākramata iti |
brahmaṇartvijā manasā candreṇa |
mano vai yajñasya brahmā |
tad yad idaṃ manaḥ so 'sau candraḥ sa brahmā sa muktiḥ sātimuktir ity atimokṣā |
atha saṃpadaḥ || BrhUp_3,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'since this space is, as it were, without support — by what means of ascent does the sacrificer ascend to the heavenly world?' By the <s>Brahman</s> priest, by the mind, by the moon. The mind indeed is the <s>Brahman</s> of the sacrifice. This mind is that moon; that is the <s>Brahman</s>; that is liberation; that is complete liberation. Thus far [the teachings] regarding complete liberation. Now, the correspondences (<s>saṃpat</s>). (BṛUp 3.1.6)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.6 mṛtyoḥ kālādatimuktirvyākhyātā yajamānasya /
so 'timucyamānaḥ kenāvaṣṭambhena paricchedaviṣayaṃ mṛtyumatotya phalaṃ prāpnotyatimucyata ityucyate /
yadidaṃ prasiddhamantarikṣamākāśo 'nārambaṇamanālambanamivaśabdādastyeva tatrā'lambanaṃ tattu na jñāyata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
yattu tadajñāyamānamālambanaṃ tatsarvanāmnā keneti pṛcchyate /
anyathā phalaprāpterasaṃbhavāt /
yenāvaṣṭambhenā'krameṇa yajamānaḥ karmaphalaṃ pratipadyamāno 'timucyate kiṃ taditi praśnaviṣaya /
kenā'krameṇa yajamānaḥ svargaṃ lokamākramata iti svargaṃ lokaṃ phalaṃ prāpnotyatimucyata ityarthaḥ /
brahmaṇartvijā manasā candreṇetyakṣaranyāsaḥ pūrvavat /
tatrādhyātmaṃ yajñasya yajamānasya yadidaṃ prasiddhaṃ manaḥ so 'sau candro 'dhidaivatam /
mano 'dhyātmaṃ candramā adhidaivatamiti hi prasiddham /
sa eva candramā brahmartviktenādhibhūtaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ paricchinnaṃ rūpamadhyātmaṃ ca manasa etaddvayamaparicchinnena candramaso rūpeṇa paśyati /
tena candramasā manasāvalambanena karmaphalaṃ svargaṃ lokaṃ prāpnotyatimucyata ityabhiprāyaḥ /
itītyupasaṃhārāthaṃ vacanam /
ityevaṃprakārā mṛtyoratimokṣāḥ /
sarvāṃṇi hi darśanaprakārāṇi yajñāṅgaviṣayāṇyasminnavasara uktānīti kṛtvopasaṃhāra ityatimokṣāḥ /
evaṃprakārā atimokṣā ityarthaḥ /
atha saṃpadaḥ /
athādhunā saṃpada ucyante /
saṃpannāma kenacitsāmānyenāgnihotrādīnāṃ karmaṇāṃ mahatāṃ phalavatāṃ tatphalāya saṃpādanaṃ saṃpat /
phalasyaiva vā sarvotsāhena phalasādhanānuṣṭhāne prayatatāṃ kenacidvaiguṇyenāsaṃbhavaḥ /
tadidānīmāhitāgniḥ sanyatkiñcitkarmāgnihotrādīnāṃ yathāsaṃbhavamādāyā'lambanīkṛtya karmaphalavidvattāyāṃ satyāṃ yatkarmaphalakāmo bhavati tadeva saṃpādayati /
children.translated_text: Now, one who has established the [sacrificial] fires, taking up whatever <s>karma</s> — from the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the rest as applicable — and making it a support, when the knowledge of the fruit of <s>karma</s> is present, whatever fruit of <s>karma</s> he desires — that alone he achieves.

children.text: anyathā rājasūyāśvamedhapuruṣamedhasarvamedhalakṣaṇānāmadhikṛtānāṃ traivarṇikānāmapyasaṃbhavasteṣāṃ tatpāṭhaḥ svādhyāyārtha eva kevalaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Otherwise, even for the three <s>varṇas</s> (classes) who are qualified for [rituals] characterized by the <s>Rājasūya</s>, <s>Aśvamedha</s>, <s>Puruṣamedha</s>, and <s>Sarvamedha</s>, since those [rituals] are impossible [to perform in practice], their recitation would serve the purpose of self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>) alone.

children.text: yadi tatphalaprāptyupāyaḥ kaścana na syāt /
children.translated_text: If there were no means of attaining their fruits.

children.text: tasmātteṣāṃ sepadaiva tatphalaprāptistasmātsaṃpadāmapi phalavattvamataḥ saṃpada ārabhyante //6//
children.translated_text: Therefore, for them, the attainment of those fruits is through correspondence (<s>saṃpat</s>) alone; therefore, correspondences too are productive of results — hence the correspondences are commenced. // 6 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.1.6:] The sacrificer's complete liberation from death and from time has been explained. He who is thus being liberated — by what support, transcending the domain of limitation which is death, does he attain the result? It is said that he attains complete liberation. 'This well-known space is, as it were, without support' — the word 'as it were' (<s>iva</s>) [indicates that] there is indeed a support there, but it is not known — this is the intent. That unknown support — it is asked about with the general word 'by what' (<s>kena</s>). Otherwise, the attainment of the result would be impossible. By what support and by what means of ascent the sacrificer, obtaining the fruit of <s>karma</s>, is liberated — what is that? — this is the subject of the question. 'By what means of ascent does the sacrificer ascend to the heavenly world?' — meaning, [by what means] does the sacrificer attain the heavenly world as the fruit, and become liberated? 'By the <s>Brahman</s> priest, by the mind, by the moon' — the arrangement of words is as before. Therein, at the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>), the well-known mind of the sacrificer — that moon is its cosmic correlate (<s>adhidaivata</s>). That mind is the individual correlate; the moon is the cosmic correlate — this is well known. That very moon, the <s>Brahman</s> priest — through it, the physical (<s>adhibhūta</s>), the limited form of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [priest], and the individual form of the mind — this pair [is seen] in the unlimited form of the moon. Through that moon, through the mind as support, one attains the fruit of <s>karma</s> — the heavenly world — and is liberated — this is the intent. 'Thus' — this is a summarizing statement. Thus are the modes of complete liberation from death. For all the specific forms of vision regarding the limbs of the sacrifice have been stated on this occasion — hence the summary: 'thus [the teachings regarding] complete liberation.' The meaning is: thus are the modes of complete liberation. 'Now, the correspondences (<s>saṃpat</s>)' — now the correspondences are stated. A correspondence (<s>saṃpat</s>) means: by some common feature, the achievement (<s>saṃpādana</s>) [of the fruit] of great fruit-bearing rituals like the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the rest for the purpose of their fruit. Or [alternatively:] the impossibility of the fruit for those who exert all effort in performing the means to the fruit, due to some deficiency.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.1.7]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- katibhir ayam adyargbhir hotāsmin yajñe kariṣyatīti |
tisṛbhir iti |
katamās tās tisra iti |
puronuvākyā ca yājyā ca śasyaiva tṛtīyā |
kiṃ tābhir jayatīti |
yat kiñcedaṃ prāṇabhṛd iti || BrhUp_3,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'with how many <s>ṛcs</s> (verses) will the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest perform in this sacrifice today?' 'With three.' 'Which are those three?' 'The <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), and the <s>śasyā</s> (laudatory verse) as the third.' 'What does one win by these?' 'Whatever here has breath.' (BṛUp 3.1.7)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.7 yājñavalkyeti hovāca abhimukhīkaraṇāya /
katibhirayamadyargbhirhetāsmin yajñe katibhiḥ katisaṅkhyābhirṛgbhirṛgjātibhiḥ ayaṃhotartvigasmin yajñe kariṣyati śastraṃ śaṃsati /
āhetaraḥ-tisṛbhirṛgjātibhiḥ /
ityukkavantaṃ pratyā hetaraḥ-katamāstāstistra iti /
saṅkhyeyaviṣayo 'yaṃ praśnaḥ, pūrvastu saṅkhyāviṣayaḥ /
puronuvākyāca-prāgyāgaphālād yāḥ prayujyante ṛcaḥ, sā ṛgjātiḥ puronuvākyetyucyate /
yāgārthaṃ yāḥ prayujyante ṛcaḥ, sā ṛgjātiryājyā /
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛcs</s> (verses) that are employed for the purpose of the sacrifice — that class of <s>ṛcs</s> is called <s>yājyā</s> (offering-verse).

children.text: śastrārthaṃ yāḥ prayujyante ṛcaḥ, sā ṛgjātiḥ śasyā /
children.translated_text: The <s>ṛcs</s> that are employed for the purpose of the recitation (<s>śastra</s>) — that class of <s>ṛcs</s> is called <s>śasyā</s> (recitation-verse).

children.text: sarvāstu yāḥ kāścana ṛcaḥ;tāḥ stotriyā vā anyā vā sarvā etāsveva tisṛṣu ṛgjātiṣvantarbhavanti /
children.translated_text: But all the <s>ṛcs</s> of whatever kind — whether they are <s>stotriya</s> (laudatory) or otherwise — all of them fall within these three classes of <s>ṛcs</s> alone.

children.text: kiṃ tābhirjayatīti yatkiñcedaṃ prāṇabhṛditi-ataścasaṅkhyāsāmānyād yatkiñcitprāṇabhṛjjātama, tat sarvaṃ jayati tat sarvaṃ phalajātaṃ sampādayati saṅkhyādisāmānyena //7//
children.translated_text: What does one win by means of them? 'Whatever here has breath' — and thus, by the commonality of number, whatever living being has been born, all that one wins; one accomplishes all that class of fruits by the commonality of number and the rest. // 7 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.1.7:] '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said — to get his attention. 'With how many <s>ṛcs</s> will the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest perform in this sacrifice today?' — with how many, meaning of what number, <s>ṛcs</s>, meaning types of <s>ṛc</s>-verses, will this <s>Hotṛ</s> priest perform — recite the <s>śastra</s> (liturgical recitation) — in this sacrifice? The answerer [replied]: 'With three types of <s>ṛc</s>-verses.' The questioner [asked] the answerer: 'Which are those three?' This question concerns what is to be enumerated; the previous question concerned the enumeration [itself]. '<s>Puronuvākyā</s>' — the <s>ṛc</s>-verses that are employed before the offering call (<s>yāgaphāla</s>); that class of <s>ṛc</s> is called <s>puronuvākyā</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.8
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.8]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- katy ayam adyādhvaryur asmin yajña āhutīr hoṣyatīti |
tisra iti |
katamās tās tisra iti |
yā hutā ujjvalanti yā hutā atinedanti yā hutā adhiśerate |
kiṃ tābhir jayatīti |
yā hutā ujjvalanti devalokam eva tābhir jayati |
dīpyata iva hi devaloko |
yā hutā atinedante pitṛlokam eva tābhir jayati |
atīva hi pitṛlokaḥ |
yā hutā adhiśerate manuṣyalokam eva tābhir jayatyi |
adha iva hi manuṣyalokaḥ || BrhUp_3,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'how many oblations will the <s>Adhvaryu</s> priest offer today in this sacrifice?' 'Three,' he replied. 'Which are those three?' 'Those which, when offered, blaze up; those which, when offered, make a thundering noise; those which, when offered, sink down. What does one win by means of them? By those which blaze up when offered, one wins the world of the gods — for the world of the gods shines, as it were. By those which make a thundering noise when offered, one wins the world of the fathers — for the world of the fathers is excessive, as it were. By those which sink down when offered, one wins the world of men — for the world of men is below, as it were.' // BṛhUp 3.1.8 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.8 yājñavalkyeti hovāveti pūrvavat /
katyayamadyādhvaryurasmin yajña āhutīrheṣyatīti, katyāhutiprakārāḥ? tastra iti, katamāstāstistra iti pūrvavat /
itara āha-yā hūtā ujjvalanti samidājyāhutayaḥ yā hutā atinedante 'tīva śabdaṃ kuvanti māsādyāhutayaḥ, yā hutā adhiśerate 'dhyādho gatvā bhūmeradhiśerate payaḥsomāhutayaḥ /
kiṃ tābhirjayatīti, tābhirevaṃ nirvartitābhirāhutibhiḥ kiṃ jayatīti /
yā āhutayo hutā ujjvalantyujjvalanayuktā āhutayo nirvartitāḥ, phalaṃ ca devalokākhyamujjvalameva, tena sāmānyena yā mayatā ujjvalantya āhutayo nirvartyamānāstā etāḥ sākṣāddevalokasya karmaphalasyarūpaṃ devalokākhyaṃ phalameva mayā nirvartyata ityevaṃ sampādayati /
yā hutā atinedante āhutayaḥ pitṛlokameva tābhirjayati kutsitaśabdakartṛtvasāmānyena /
pitṛlokameva tābhirjayati kutsitaśabdakartṛtvasāmānyena /
pitṛlokasambaddhāyāṃ hi saṃyamanyāṃ puryāṃ vaivasvatena yātyamānānāṃ'hā hatāḥ sma muñca muñca'iti śabdobhavati /
tathāvadānāhutayaḥ tena pitṛlokasāmānyāt pitṛloka eva mayā nirvartyata iti sampādayati /
yā hutā adhiśerate manuṣyalokameva tāmijayati bhūmyupari sambandhasāmānyāt /
adha iva hyagha eva hi manuṣyalokaḥ uparitanān sādhyāṃllokānapekṣya, athavādhogamanamapekṣya /
ato manuṣyaloka eva mayā nirvartyata iti sampādayati /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [one thinks:] 'the world of men is being produced by me' — thus one accomplishes.

children.text: yā hutā adhiśerate manuṣyalokameva tābhijayati bhūmyupari sambandhasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Those which, when offered, sink down — by them one wins the world of men, through the commonality of connection with the ground above.

children.text: adha iva hyadha eva hi manuṣyalokaḥ uparitanān sādhyāṃllokānapekṣya, athavādhogamanamapekṣya /
children.translated_text: 'Below, as it were' — indeed, the world of men is below, relative to the upper worlds of the <s>Sādhyas</s> and the like; or, [below] relative to the downward course.

children.text: ato manuṣyaloka eva mayā nirvartyata iti sampādayati payaḥsomāhutinirvartanakāle //8//
children.translated_text: Therefore, [one thinks:] 'the world of men is being produced by me' — thus one accomplishes at the time of performing the oblations of milk and <s>soma</s>. // 8 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.1.8: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said — as before. 'How many oblations will the <s>Adhvaryu</s> offer today in this sacrifice?' — meaning: how many types of oblations? 'Three.' 'Which are those three?' — as before.
The other said: 'Those which, when offered, blaze up' — these are the oblations of firewood and ghee. 'Those which, when offered, make a thundering noise' — those which produce excessive sound — these are oblations [offered] from month to month and the like. 'Those which, when offered, sink down' — those which, having gone downward, settle on the ground — these are the oblations of milk and <s>soma</s>.
'What does one win by them?' — by those oblations that have been thus performed, what does one win?
Those oblations which, when offered, blaze up — oblations performed in conjunction with blazing — and the fruit, called the world of the gods, also blazes; by that commonality, the blazing oblations being performed — [it is as if] 'by me these oblations, which are directly the form of the ritual-fruit called the world of the gods, that fruit called the world of the gods, are being produced' — thus one accomplishes [the result].
Those oblations which, when offered, make a thundering noise — by them one wins the world of the fathers, through the commonality of producing disagreeable sound.
One wins the world of the fathers through the commonality of producing disagreeable sound. For in the city of <s>Saṃyamanī</s>, connected with the world of the fathers, when [beings] are being judged by <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>), the sound arises: 'Alas! We are killed! Release us, release us!'
Similarly, the oblations at the <s>avadāna</s> (cutting of portions) — through that commonality with the world of the fathers, [one thinks:] 'the world of the fathers is being produced by me' — thus one accomplishes.
Those which, when offered, sink down — by them one wins the world of men, through the commonality of connection with the ground above.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.9
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.9]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- katibhir ayam adya brahmā yajñaṃ dakṣiṇato devatābhir gopāyatīti |
ekayeti |
katamā saiketi |
mana eveti |
anantaṃ vai mano 'nantā viśve devāḥ |
anantam eva sa tena lokaṃ jayati || BrhUp_3,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'with how many deities does the <s>Brahman</s> priest today protect this sacrifice from the south?' 'With one,' he replied. 'Which is that one?' 'The mind alone.' The mind indeed is infinite; the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) are infinite. An infinite world one wins thereby. // BṛhUp 3.1.9 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.9 yājñavalkyeti hovāceti pūrvavat /
ayamṛtvigbrahmā dakṣiṇato brahmāsane sthitvā yajñaṃ gopāyati /
katibhirdevatābhirgopāyatīti prāsaṅgikametadvahuvacanam /
ekayā hi devatayā gopāyatyasau /
evaṃ jñāte bahuvacanena praśno nopapadyate svayaṃ jānatastasmātpūrvayoḥ kaṇḍikayoḥ praśnaprativacaneṣu katibhiḥ kati tisṛbhististra iti prasaṅgaṃ dṛṣṭvehāpi bahuvacanenaiva praśnopakramaḥ kriyate /
athavā prativādivyāmohārtha bahuvacanam /
itara āhaikayetyekā sā devatā yayā dakṣiṇataḥ sthitvā brahmā'sane yajñaṃ gopāyati /
katamā saiketi /
mana eveti manaḥ sā devatā /
manasā hi brahmā vyāpriyate dhyānenaiva /
"tasya yajñasya manaśca vākca vartanī tayoranyatarāṃ manasā saṃskaroti brahmā"(cha.u.4 / 16 / 1) iti śrutyantarāt /
tena mana eva devatā tayā manasā hi gopāyati brahmā yajñam /
tacca mano vṛttibhedenānantam /
vaiśabdaḥ prasiddhāvadyotanārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The particle '<s>vai</s>' is for indicating something well known.

children.text: prasiddhaṃ manasa ānantyma /
children.translated_text: The infinitude of mind is well known.

children.text: tadānantyābhimānino devāḥ,"sarve devā yatraikaṃ bhavanti"ityādiśrutyantarāt /
children.translated_text: The gods who identify with that infinitude — [are the <s>Viśvedevas</s>], from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Where all the gods become one' and so forth.

children.text: tenānantyasāmānyādanantameva sa tena lokaṃ jayati //9//
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the commonality of infinitude, one wins an infinite world thereby. // 9 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.1.9: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said — as before. This officiating priest, the <s>Brahman</s>, seated in the <s>Brahman</s>'s seat to the south, protects the sacrifice. 'With how many deities does he protect?' — this plural form is incidental. For he protects with a single deity. When this is known, a question in the plural is inappropriate for one who himself knows. Therefore, having seen the pattern of question and answer in the preceding two sections — with 'how many' and 'three' — here too the commencement of the question is made with the plural form.
Alternatively, the plural is for the purpose of confusing the opponent.
The other said: 'With one' — that is the one deity by which the <s>Brahman</s> priest, seated in the <s>Brahman</s>'s seat to the south, protects the sacrifice. 'Which is that one?' 'The mind alone' — the mind is that deity. For the <s>Brahman</s> priest functions through the mind alone, through meditation.
[This is known] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Of that sacrifice, mind and speech are the two tracks; with one of them, the <s>Brahman</s> priest refines [the sacrifice] through the mind' (ChUp 4.16.1).
Therefore, the mind alone is the deity; by that mind, the <s>Brahman</s> priest protects the sacrifice. And that mind, through the diversity of its modifications, is infinite.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,1.10
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.1.10]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- katy ayam adyodgātāsmin yajñe stotriyāḥ stoṣyatīti |
tisra iti |
katamās tās tisra iti |
puronuvākyā ca yājyā ca śasyaiva tṛtīyā |
katamās tāḥ |
yā adhyātmam iti |
prāṇa eva puronuvākyāpāno yājyā vyānaḥ śasyā |
kiṃ tābhir jayatīti |
pṛthivīlokam eva puronuvākyayā jayaty antarikṣalokaṃ yājyayā dyulokaṃ śasyayā |
tato ha hotāśvala upararāma || BrhUp_3,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'how many <s>stotriya</s> (laudatory hymns) will the <s>Udgātṛ</s> priest chant today in this sacrifice?' 'Three.' 'Which are those three?' 'The <s>puronuvākyā</s> (invitatory verse), the <s>yājyā</s> (offering verse), and the <s>śasyā</s> (recitation verse) as the third.' 'Which are those?' 'Those which relate to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>).' <s>Prāṇa</s> (outward breath) is the <s>puronuvākyā</s>; <s>apāna</s> (inward breath) is the <s>yājyā</s>; <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath) is the <s>śasyā</s>. 'What does one win by them?' One wins the earth-world by the <s>puronuvākyā</s>; the atmospheric world by the <s>yājyā</s>; the heavenly world by the <s>śasyā</s>.' Thereupon the <s>Hotṛ</s> priest <s>Aśvala</s> fell silent. // BṛhUp 3.1.10 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,1.10 yājñavalkyeti hovāceti pūrvavat /
kati stotriyāḥ stopyatītyayamudgātā /
stotriyā nāma ṛksāmasamudāyaḥ katipayānāmṛcām /
stotriyāvāśamyāvāyāḥ kāścana ṛcaḥ, tā sarvāstistra evetyāha /
tāśca vyākhyātāḥ- muronuvākyā ca yājyā ca śasyaiva tṛtīyeti /
tatra pūrvamuktam - yatkiñcedaṃ prāṇabhṛta sarve jayatīti tat kena sāmānyena? ityucyate - katamāstāstistra ṛco yā adhyātmaṃ bhavantīti /
prāṇa eva puronuvākyā, paśabdasāmānyāt /
avāno yājyā, ānantaryāt /
apānena hi prattaṃ havirdevatā grasanti, yāgaśca pradānam /
vyānaḥśasyā -"aprāṇannanapānannṛcamabhivyāharati"(cha. u. 1 / 3 / 4) / iti śratyantarāt /
kiṃ tābhirjayatīti vyākhyātam /
tatra viśeṣasambandhasāmānyamanuktamihocyate, sarvamanyad vyākhyātam /
children.translated_text: Therein, the specific commonality of connection — which was not stated — is stated here; everything else has been explained.

children.text: lokasambandhasāmānyena pṛthivīlokamevapuronuvākyayā jayati, antarikṣalokaṃ yājyayā, madhyamatvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: Through the commonality of connection with the world, one wins the earth-world by the <s>puronuvākyā</s>; the atmospheric world by the <s>yājyā</s>, through the commonality of being in the middle.

children.text: dyulokaṃśasyayordhvatvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: The heavenly world by the <s>śasyā</s>, through the commonality of being above.

children.text: tato ha tasmādātmanaḥ praśnanirṇayādasau hotā aśvala upararāma nāyamasmadgecara iti //10//
children.translated_text: Thereupon — after the resolution of his questions — that <s>Hotṛ</s> priest <s>Aśvala</s> fell silent, [thinking:] 'this one is beyond my reach.' // 10 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.1.10: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said — as before. 'How many <s>stotriya</s> hymns will this <s>Udgātṛ</s> chant?' A <s>stotriya</s> is a collection of <s>ṛcs</s> and <s>sāmans</s>, consisting of a certain number of verses. <s>Stotriyā</s> and <s>āśamsyā</s> — whatever <s>ṛcs</s> there are — all of them are just three, he says. And those have been explained: the <s>puronuvākyā</s>, the <s>yājyā</s>, and the <s>śasyā</s> as the third.
Therein, it was previously stated: 'whatever here has breath, one wins all of that' — by what commonality? This is stated: 'Which are those three <s>ṛcs</s> that relate to the individual self (<s>adhyātmam</s>)?'
<s>Prāṇa</s> (outward breath) is the <s>puronuvākyā</s>, because of the commonality of the prefix '<s>pra</s>-.' <s>Apāna</s> (inward breath) is the <s>yājyā</s>, because of proximity. For by <s>apāna</s>, the received oblation is consumed by the deities; and sacrifice (<s>yāga</s>) is an act of giving.
<s>Vyāna</s> (diffused breath) is the <s>śasyā</s> — [as known] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Without breathing out or breathing in, he utters the <s>ṛc</s>' (ChUp 1.3.4).
'What does one win by them?' — this has been explained.

children.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāye prathamamaśvalabrāhmaṇam //1//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>Aśvala Brāhmaṇa</s> in the third chapter. // 1 //

children.text:
ākhyāyikāsambandhaḥ prasiddha eva /
mṛtyoratimuktirvyākhyātā kālalakṣaṇāt karmalakṣaṇācca /
kaḥ punarasau mṛtyuryasmādatimuktirvyākhyātā? sa ca svābhāvikājñānāsaṅgāspado 'dhyātmādhibhūtāviṣayaparicchinno grahātigrahalakṣaṇo mṛtyuḥ /
tasmāt paricchinnarūpānmṛtyoratimuktasya rūpāṇyaganyādityādīnyudgīthaprakaraṇe vyākhyātāni /
aśvalapraśnecatadgato viśeṣaḥ kaścit /
taccaitat karmaṇāṃ jñānasahitānāṃ phalam /
etasmāt sādhyasādhanarūpāt saṃsārānmokṣaḥ kartavya ityatobandhanarūpasyamṛtyoḥ svarūpamucyate /
baddhasya hi mokṣaḥ kartavyaḥ /
yadapyatimuktasya svarūpamuktaṃ tatrāpi grahātigrahābhyāmavinirmukta eva mṛtyurūpābhyām /
tathā coktaṃ"aśanāyāhimṛtyuḥ"(bṛ.u.1 / 2 / 1) "eṣa eva mṛtyuḥ"iti /
ādityasthaṃ puruṣamaṅgīkṛtyāha"eko mṛtyurvahavā"iti ca /
tadātmabhāvāpanno hi mṛtyorāptimatimucyata ityucyate /
na ca tatra grahātigrahau mṛtyurūpau nastaḥ /
"athaitasya manaso dyauḥ śarīraṃ jyotīrūpamasāvādityaḥ"(bṛ. u. 1 / 5 / 12) 'manaśva'grahaḥ sa kāmenātigrāheṇa gṛhītaḥ"(3 / 2 / 7) iti, vakṣyati"prāṇo vai grahaḥ so 'pānenātigrāheṇa"(3 / 2 / 2) iti,"vāgvai grahaḥ sa nāmnātigrāheṇa"(3 / 2 / 3) iti ca /
tathā vyannavibhāge vyākhyātamasmābhiḥ /
suvicāritaṃ caitad yadeva pravṛttikāraṇaṃ tadeva nivṛttikāraṇaṃ na bhavatīti /
kecittu sarvameva nivṛttikāraṇaṃ manyante /
ataḥ kāgṇāt pūrvasmātpūrvasmānmṛtyormucyate uttaramuttaraṃ pratipadyamāno vyāvṛttyarthameva prati padyate na tu tādarthyam, ityata ā dvaitakṣayāta sarvaṃ mṛtyuḥ, dvainakṣaye tu paramārthatā mṛtyorāptimatimucyate /
ataśca āpekṣikī gauṇī muktirantarāle /
sarvametad evat abārhadāraṇyakam /
nanu sarvaikatvaṃ mokṣaḥ"tasmāttatsarvamabhavat"(bṛ. u. 1 / 4 / 10) iti śruteḥ /
bāḍhaṃ bhavatyetadapi, natu"grāmakāmo yajeta, paśukāmo yajeta"ityādiśrutīnāṃ tādarthyam /
yadi hyadvaitārthatvameva āsāṃ grāmapaśusvargādyarthatvaṃ nāstīti grāmapaśusvargādayo na gṛhyeran, gṛhyante tu karmaphalavaicitryaviśeṣāḥ /
yadi ca vaidikānāṃ karmaṇāṃ tādarthyameva, saṃsāra eva nābhaviṣyat /
atha tādarthye 'pi anuniṣpāditapadārthasvabhāvaḥ saṃsāra iti cet /
yathā ca rūpadarśanārtha āloke sarvo 'pi tatrasthaḥ prakāśyata eva /
na;pramāṇānupapatteḥ /
advaitārthatve vaidikānāṃ karmaṇāṃ vidyāsahitānām anyaspānuniṣpāditatve pramāṇānupapattiḥ /
na pratyakṣaṃ nānumānamata eva ca nāgamaḥ /
ubhayam ekena vākyena pradarśyata iti cet kulyāpraṇayanālokādivat /
tannevam;vākyadharmānupapatteḥ /
na ca ekavākyagatasyārthasya pravṛttinivṛttisādhanatvamavagantuṃ śakyate /
kulyāpraṇayanālokādāvarthasya pratyakṣatvādadoṣaḥ /
yadapyucyate mantrā asminnartheḥ dṛṣṭā iti /
ayameva tu tāvadarthaḥ pramāṇāgamyaḥ /
mantrāḥ punaḥ kim asminnartha āhosvidanyasminnartha iti mṛgyametat /
tasmād grahātiprahalakṣaṇo mṛtyurbandhaḥ, tasmānbhokṣo vaktavya ityata idamārabhyate na ca jānīmo viṣayasandhāvivāntarāle 'vasthānamardhajaratīyaṃ kauśalam /
yattu mṛtyoratimucyata ityukatvā grahātigrahāvucyete, tacvarthasambandhāt /
sarvo 'yaṃ sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇo bandhaḥ, grahātigrahāvinirmokāt /
nigaḍe hi nirjñāte nigaḍitasya mokṣāya yatnaḥ kartavyo bhavati;tasmātādarthyenārambhaḥ /
children.translated_text:
[Commentary:] The connection with the narrative is well known. Liberation from death through [what is] characterized by time and characterized by <s>karma</s> has been explained. But who is that death from which liberation has been explained? That death, whose basis is the natural <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance) and attachment, delimited by the <s>adhyātma</s> (individual self) and <s>adhibhūta</s> (elemental) domains, characterized by <s>graha</s> (seizer) and <s>atigraha</s> (over-seizer) — that is death. Therefore, the forms of one liberated from that death, which is delimited in nature — the forms such as the sun and the rest, innumerable — have been explained in the <s>Udgītha</s> section. In the <s>Aśvala</s> questions, some specific detail pertaining to that [was given]. And this is the fruit of actions conjoined with knowledge. From this <s>saṃsāra</s> characterized by ends and means, liberation is to be sought — therefore the essential nature of death, which is bondage, is stated. For it is the bound one who is to be liberated. Even when the essential nature of the liberated one was stated, there too one is indeed not freed from death in the form of <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s>. And thus it was stated: 'Hunger is death' (BṛUp 1.2.1), 'This alone is death' (BṛUp 1.2.7). Taking the person stationed in the sun as accepted, [the text] says: 'There is one death; there are many.' And indeed, one who has attained that state [of identity with the person in the sun] is said to be liberated from death. And there, the <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s> of the nature of death are not destroyed.
'And of this mind, heaven is the body; the luminous form is the sun' (BṛUp 1.5.12); 'Mind is the <s>graha</s>; it is seized by desire, the <s>atigraha</s>' (BṛUp 3.2.7) — thus it will be said; '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>graha</s>; it [is seized] by <s>apāna</s>, the <s>atigraha</s>' (BṛUp 3.2.2); 'Speech indeed is the <s>graha</s>; it [is seized] by name, the <s>atigraha</s>' (BṛUp 3.2.3) — thus too.
Similarly, in the section on the division of food, this was explained by us. And this is well-considered: that which is the cause of engagement [in the world] cannot itself be the cause of withdrawal — there is no [such case]. But some think that everything is a cause of withdrawal. Therefore, from each successive [level of] death, one is liberated — attaining each successive [higher level], one attains it for the purpose of withdrawal alone, not for the purpose of [identifying with] it. Hence, up to the dissolution of duality, everything is death; but upon the dissolution of duality, the ultimate reality, the attainment of death [i.e., identity with the cosmic person], is transcended.
Therefore, the liberation in between is relative, secondary. All this is indeed the teaching of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>.
[Objection:] But oneness with all is liberation — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'Therefore, he became all' (BṛUp 1.4.10). [Reply:] Certainly, this too holds. But this does not serve the purpose of <s>śruti</s> statements like 'One who desires a village should sacrifice; one who desires cattle should sacrifice.' For if [those texts] were solely for the purpose of non-duality, then villages, cattle, heaven, and the like — being purposeless — would not be grasped [as real goals]; but they are grasped, [since] the specific varieties of <s>karmaphala</s> (fruits of action) [are real]. And if the Vedic <s>karmas</s> had oneness as their sole purpose, <s>saṃsāra</s> would not have existed at all. If [one says:] even when [<s>karma</s>] is for the purpose of oneness, <s>saṃsāra</s> has a nature whose constituents have not [yet] been fully realized — [we reply:] just as everything in a lamp meant for seeing forms is illuminated — [objection:] no, because there is no valid basis [for that]. If Vedic <s>karmas</s> conjoined with <s>vidyā</s> are solely for the purpose of non-duality, [and you claim] they leave other things unrealized — there is no valid basis [for this claim]. Neither perception, nor inference, and for that very reason, nor scripture [supports it]. [If one says:] both [engagement and withdrawal] are shown by a single sentence, as in the case of digging a canal and light [entering together] — [we reply:] that is not so, because the properties of a [single] sentence do not support it. For it is not possible to understand the meaning contained in a single sentence as being both a means to engagement and a means to withdrawal. In the case of digging a canal and lamp-light, there is no fault because the result is directly perceptible. As for the claim that <s>mantras</s> are seen [to serve] in this meaning — this very meaning, to begin with, is not accessible through any means of valid knowledge. And whether <s>mantras</s> [serve] in this meaning or in another — this needs to be investigated.
Therefore, death in the form of <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s> is bondage; liberation from that is to be stated — hence this [section] is commenced. And we do not know — in the intermediary realm of the objects of sense-pursuit — the skill of the <s>Ardhajaratīya</s> (the 'half-decrepit' doctrine). As for [the text] first stating liberation from death and then stating <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s> — that is because of the connection in meaning. All this bondage, characterized by ends and means, [exists] because of non-liberation from <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s>. For when the fetters are known, effort must be made for the liberation of the fettered one; therefore, the commencement [of this section] is for that purpose.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.1

atha hainaṃ jāratkārava ārtabhāgaḥ papraccha |
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- kati grahāḥ katy atigrahā iti |
aṣṭau grahā aṣṭāv atigrahā iti |
ye te 'ṣṭau grahā aṣṭāv atigrahāḥ katame ta iti || BrhUp_3,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga</s> questioned him. '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'how many <s>grahas</s> (seizers) are there, and how many <s>atigrahas</s> (over-seizers)?' 'Eight <s>grahas</s> and eight <s>atigrahas</s>.' 'Which are those eight <s>grahas</s> and eight <s>atigrahas</s>?' (BṛUp 3.2.1)
[Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.2.1]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.1 atha hainaṃ haśabda aitihyārthaḥ /
athānantaramaśvala uparate prakṛtaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ jaratkārugotro jāratkārava ṛtabhāgasyāpatyamārtabhāgaḥ papraccha yājñavalkyeti hovācetyabhimukhokaraṇāya /
pūrvavatpraśnaḥ kati grahāḥ katyatigrahā iti /
itiśabdo vākyaparisamāptyarthaḥ /
tatra nirjñāteṣu vā grahātigraheṣu praśnaḥ syādanirjñāteṣu vā /
