athanirjñātāstadā saṃkhyeyaviṣayapraśna iti ke grahāḥ ke 'tigrahā iti praṣṭavyaṃ na tu kati grahāḥ katyatigrahā iti praśnaḥ /
api ca nirjñātasāmānyakeśu viśeṣavijñānāya praśno bhavati yathā katame 'tra kaṭhāḥ katame 'tra kālāpā iti /
na cātra grahātigrahā nāma padārthāḥ kecana loke prasiddhāḥ /
yena viśeṣārthaḥ praśnaḥ syāt /
nanu cātimucyata ityuktaṃ grahagṛhotasya hi mokṣaḥ sa muktiḥ sātimuktiriti hi dviruktam /
tasmātprāptā grahā atigrahāśca /
nanu tatrāpi catvāro grahā atigrahāśca nirjñātā vākcakṣuḥ prāṇamanāṃsi tatra katīti praśno nopapadyate nirjñātatvāt /
na /
anavadhāraṇārthatvāt /
na hi catuṣṭvaṃ tatra vivakṣitamiha tu grahātigrahādarśane 'ṣṭhatvaguṇavivakṣayā katoti praśna upapadyata eva /
tasmātsa muktiḥ sātimuktiriti muktyatiktī dvirukte grahātigrahā api siddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, since liberation (<s>mukti</s>) and <s>atimukti</s> were stated twice, the <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> too are established.

children.text: ataḥ katisaṃkhyākā grahāḥ kati vātigrahā iti pṛcchati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Hence, he asks: how many in number are the <s>grahas</s>, and how many are the <s>atigrahas</s>?

children.text: itara āha-aṣṭau grahā aṣṭāvatigrahā iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The other [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] replied: 'Eight <s>grahas</s> and eight <s>atigrahas</s>.'

children.text: ye te 'ṣṭau grahā abhihitāḥ katame te niyamena grahītavyā iti //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Which are those eight <s>grahas</s> that you have stated — which of them are to be specifically ascertained?' (1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.1:] 'Then indeed him' — the word '<s>ha</s>' conveys the sense of tradition. 'Then' — immediately after <s>Aśvala</s> desisted, <s>Jāratkārava</s> — of the <s>Jaratkāru</s> lineage — <s>Ārtabhāga</s>, the offspring of <s>Ṛtabhāga</s>, questioned the aforesaid <s>Yājñavalkya</s>; '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said — for the purpose of making him face him. The question is as before: 'How many <s>grahas</s>, how many <s>atigrahas</s>?' The word '<s>iti</s>' serves to conclude the sentence. Now, the question could be about <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> that are either already known or unknown. If the <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> are already known, then since their qualities and number would also be known, the question 'how many <s>grahas</s>, how many <s>atigrahas</s>?' — being about number — would be inappropriate. On the other hand, if they are unknown, the question should be about the things to be enumerated — 'what are the <s>grahas</s>, what are the <s>atigrahas</s>?' — not 'how many <s>grahas</s>, how many <s>atigrahas</s>?' Moreover, when the general [category] is known, the question arises for the knowledge of particulars — as in 'which among these are <s>Kaṭhas</s>, which are <s>Kālāpas</s>?' But here, '<s>grahas</s>' and '<s>atigrahas</s>' are not well-known entities in the world, on the basis of which a question about particulars could arise. [Objection:] But was it not said [earlier] that '[the vital breath] was released' — for the release of one seized by a <s>graha</s> is liberation (<s>mukti</s>), and that is <s>atimukti</s> — thus it was stated twice. Therefore, <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> are established. [Reply:] But even there, four <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> — namely speech, sight, breath, and mind — are already known; so the question 'how many?' would be inappropriate, since they are known. [Answer:] No — because the [earlier passage] did not intend to make a definitive determination. For the number four was not intended there; but here, in the context of establishing <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s>, with the intention of [teaching] the quality of eightness, the question 'how many?' is indeed appropriate.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.2.2]

children.text:
prāṇo vai grahaḥ |
so 'pānenātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
prāṇena hi gandhāñ jighrati || BrhUp_3,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: The breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) indeed is a <s>graha</s> (seizer). It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> (over-seizer) that is <s>apāna</s>. For by the breath one smells odors. (BṛUp 3.2.2)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.2 tatrā'ha /
prāṇo vai grahaḥ prāṇa iti ghrāṇamucyate /
prakaraṇāt /
vāyusahitaḥ saḥ /
apāneneti gandhenetyetat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Apāna</s>' here means odor (<s>gandha</s>) — this is what is meant.

children.text: apānasacivatvādapāno gandha ucyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Odor is called '<s>apāna</s>' because it accompanies the <s>apāna</s> (downward breath).

children.text: apānopahṛtaṃ hi gandhaṃ ghrāṇena sarvo loko jighrati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For everyone in the world smells odor — which has been brought [to the nose] by the <s>apāna</s> — through the organ of smell.

children.text: tadetaducyate 'pānena hi gandhāñjighratīti //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This very meaning is stated: 'For by the breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) one smells odors.' (2)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.2:] Therein, he says: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is a <s>graha</s>' — here '<s>prāṇa</s>' refers to the organ of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>), from the context. It is accompanied by the vital air (<s>vāyu</s>).

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.3-9
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.2.3–9]

children.text:
vāg vai grahaḥ |
sa nāmnātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
vācā hi nāmāny abhivadati || BrhUp_3,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: Speech indeed is a <s>graha</s>. It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is name. For by speech one utters names. (BṛUp 3.2.3)

children.text:
jihvā vai grahaḥ |
sa rasenātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
jihvayā hi rasān vijānāti || BrhUp_3,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: The tongue indeed is a <s>graha</s>. It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is taste. For by the tongue one discerns tastes. (BṛUp 3.2.4)

children.text:
cakṣur vai grahaḥ |
sa rūpeṇātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
cakṣuṣā hi rūpāṇi paśyati || BrhUp_3,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: The eye indeed is a <s>graha</s>. It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is form. For by the eye one sees forms. (BṛUp 3.2.5)

children.text:
śrotraṃ vai grahaḥ |
sa śabdenātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
śrotreṇa hi śabdāñ śṛṇoti || BrhUp_3,2.6 ||
children.translated_text: The ear indeed is a <s>graha</s>. It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is sound. For by the ear one hears sounds. (BṛUp 3.2.6)

children.text:
mano vai grahaḥ |
sa kāmenātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
manasā hi kāmān kāmayate || BrhUp_3,2.7 ||
children.translated_text: The mind indeed is a <s>graha</s>. It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is desire. For by the mind one desires desires. (BṛUp 3.2.7)

children.text:
hastau vai grahaḥ |
sa karmaṇātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
hastābhyāṃ hi karma karoti || BrhUp_3,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: The hands indeed are a <s>graha</s>. They are seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is action. For by the hands one performs action. (BṛUp 3.2.8)

children.text:
tvag vai grahaḥ |
sa sparśenātigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ |
tvacā hi sparśān vedayata |
ity aṣṭau grahā aṣṭāv atigrahāḥ || BrhUp_3,2.9 ||
children.translated_text: The skin indeed is a <s>graha</s>. It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is touch. For by the skin one feels touches. These are the eight <s>grahas</s> and eight <s>atigrahas</s>. (BṛUp 3.2.9)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.3-9 vāgvai grahaḥ /
vācā hyadhyātmaparicchinnayā'saṅgaviṣayāspadayāsatyānṛtāsabhyabībhatsād ivacaneṣu vyāpṛtayā gṛhīto loko 'pahṛtastena /
vāggrahaḥ sa nāmnātigrāreṇa gṛhītaḥ sa vāgākhyo graho nāmnā vaktavyena viṣayeṇātigraheṇa atigrāheṇeti daighyaṃ chāndasaṃ nāma vaktavyārthā hi vāktena vaktavyenārthena tādarthyena prayuktā vāktena vaśīkṛtā tena tatkāryamakṛtvā naiva tasyā mokṣaḥ /
ato nāmnātigrāheṇa gṛhītā vāgityucyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, speech is said to be seized by name, the <s>atigraha</s>.

children.text: vaktavyāsaṅgena hi pravṛttā sarvānarthairyujyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For [speech], when engaged through attachment to what is to be spoken, becomes involved in all misfortunes.

children.text: samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The rest is the same [as the pattern established above].

children.text: ityete tvakparyantā aṣṭau grahāḥ sparśaparyantāścaite 'ṣṭāvatigrahā iti // 3-9 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus these eight <s>grahas</s> ending with skin, and these eight <s>atigrahas</s> ending with touch. (3–9)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.3–9:] 'Speech indeed is a <s>graha</s>' — for by speech, delimited in the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), providing a locus for attachment, engaged in [speaking] truth, falsehood, propriety, impropriety, and the like — the world is seized, carried away; thereby speech is a <s>graha</s>. 'It is seized by the <s>atigraha</s> that is name' — that <s>graha</s> called speech is seized by name, that is, by the object to be spoken. '<s>Atigrāheṇa</s>' — the lengthening [of the vowel] is Vedic. For name is the object to be spoken by speech; speech, being employed for the purpose of the object to be spoken, is controlled by it; and without performing its function for that [object], there is no release for speech.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.10
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.2.10]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yad idaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyor annaṃ kā svit sā devatā yasyā mṛtyur annam iti |
agnir vai mṛtyuḥ so 'pām annam |
apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati || BrhUp_3,2.10 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'since everything here is the food of death, which is that deity for whom death is food?' 'Fire indeed is death; it is the food of water. [One who knows this] conquers re-death (<s>punarmṛtyu</s>).' (BṛUp 3.2.10)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.10 upasaṃhṛteṣu grahātigraheṣvāha punaḥ - yājñavalkyeti hovāca /
yadidaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyorannaṃ yadidaṃ vyākṛtaṃ sarvaṃ mṛtyorannaṃ sarvaṃ jāyate vipadyate ca grahātigrahalakṣaṇena mṛtyunā grastam /
kāsvitkā nu syātsā devatā yasyā devatāyā mṛtyurapyannaṃ bhavet /
"mṛtyuryasyopasecanam"iti śrutyantarāt /
ayamabhiprāyaḥ praṣṭuḥ /
yadi mṛtyormṛtyuṃ vakṣyatyanavasthā syāt /
atha na vakṣyatyasmādgrahātigrahalakṣaṇānmṛtyormokṣo nopapadyate /
grahātigrahamṛtyuvināśe hi mokṣaḥ yāt /
sa yadi mṛtyorapi mṛtyuḥ syādbhavedgrahātigrahalakṣaṇasya mṛtyorvināśaḥ ato durvacanaṃ praśnaṃ manvānaḥ pṛcchati kāsvitsā devateti /
asti tāvanmṛtyormṛtyuḥ /
nanvanavasthā syāttasyāpyanyo mṛtyuriti /
nānavasthā /
sarvamṛtyormṛtyvantarānupapatteḥ /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate 'sti mṛtyormṛtyuriti /
dṛṣṭatvāt /
agnistāvatsarvasya dṛṣṭo mṛtyurvināśakatvāt /
so 'dbhirbhakṣyate so 'gnirapāmannam /
gṛhāṇa tarhyasti mṛtyormṛtyuriti /
tena sarvaṃ grahātigrahajātaṃ bhakṣyate mṛtyormṛtyunā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By that [death of death], everything that is of the nature of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> is consumed by death's death.

children.text: tasminbandhane nāśite mṛtyunā bhakṣite saṃsārānmokṣa upapanno bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When that bondage is destroyed — when death is consumed — liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> becomes possible.

children.text: bandhanaṃ hi grahātigrahalakṣaṇamuktaṃ tasmācca mokṣa upapadyata ityetatprasādhitam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For bondage in the form of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> has been stated, and liberation from that [bondage] is possible — this has been established.

children.text: ato bandhamokṣāya puruṣaprayāsaḥ saphalo bhavatyato 'pajayati punarmṛtyum //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, a person's effort for [attaining] freedom from bondage is fruitful; therefore, one conquers re-death. (10)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.10:] When the <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> have been concluded, he says again: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said. 'Since everything here is the food of death' — since everything that is differentiated is the food of death, the entire [world] is born and perishes, being devoured by death in the form of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> — 'which then — which indeed might be — that deity, for whom even death would become food?' [This echoes] the <s>śruti</s> from another context: 'Death is its condiment.' The intention of the questioner is this: if [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] speaks of death's death, there would be an infinite regress. But if he does not speak [of it], then liberation from this death in the form of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> would be impossible. For liberation consists in the destruction of death in the form of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s>. If there were a death of death, then the destruction of death in the form of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> would be possible. Therefore, thinking this to be a difficult question, he asks: 'Which is that deity?' Now, there is indeed a death of death. [Objection:] Would there not be an infinite regress — that there would be yet another death of that [death]? [Answer:] No infinite regress — because of the impossibility of another death beyond the death of everything. But how is it known that there is a death of death? Because it is observed: fire is indeed observed to be the death of everything, since it destroys everything. And that [fire] is consumed by water — that fire is the food of water. Therefore, accept that there is a death of death.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.11
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.2.11]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yatrāyaṃ puruṣo mriyata ud asmāt prāṇāḥ krāmanty āho neti |
neti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
atraiva samavanīyante |
sa ucchvayati |
ādhmāyati |
ādhmāto mṛtaḥ śete || BrhUp_3,2.11 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'when this person dies, do the vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>) depart upward from him, or not?' '<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: No. They merge right here. He swells up; he becomes inflated; the dead [body] lies inflated.' (BṛUp 3.2.11)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.11 pareṇa mṛtyunā mṛtyau bhakṣite paramātmadarśanena yo 'sau mukto vidvānso 'yaṃ puruṣo yatra yasminkāle mriyata udūrdhvamasmādbrahmavido mriyamāṇātprāṇā vāgadayo grahā nāmādayaścātigrahā vāsanārūpā antasthāḥ prayojakāḥ kāmatnyūrdhvamutkrāmantyāhosvinneti /
neti hovāca yājñavalkyo notkrāmantyatraivāsminneva pareṇā'tmanāvibhāgaṃ gacchanti viduṣi kāryāṇi karaṇāni ca svayonau parabrahmasatattave samavanīyanta ekībhāvena samavasṛjyante pralīyanta ityarthaḥ /
ūrmaya ida samudre /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Like waves in the ocean.

children.text: tathā ca śrutyantaraṃ kalāśabdavācyānāṃ prāṇānāṃ parasminnātmani pralayaṃ darśayati -"evamevāsya paridraṣṭurimāḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ puruṣāyaṇāḥ puruṣaṃ prāpyāstaṃ gacchantī"ti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And likewise, another <s>śruti</s> demonstrates the dissolution of the <s>prāṇas</s> — denoted by the word '<s>kalā</s>' (parts) — into the supreme <s>Ātman</s>: 'Thus indeed, these sixteen parts of this seer, whose goal is the <s>Puruṣa</s>, reach the <s>Puruṣa</s> and dissolve' (<s>PraśUp</s>).

children.text: iti pareṇā'tmanāvibhāgaṃ gacchantīti darśitam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, it has been shown that they merge into non-differentiation with the supreme <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: na tarhi mṛto, nahi, mṛtaścāyaṃ yasmātsa ucchvayatyucchūnatāṃ pratipadyata ādhmāyati bāhyena vāyunā pūryate dṛtivadādhmāto mṛtaḥ śete niśceṣṭaḥ bandhananāśe muktasya na kvacidgamanamiti vākyārthaḥ //11//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, he has not [truly] died — no indeed; and yet this one is dead, because he swells up — becomes distended — and becomes inflated, being filled with external air like a bellows; the dead [body] lies inflated, motionless. The meaning of the sentence is: when bondage is destroyed, there is no going anywhere for the liberated one. (11)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.11:] When death — the higher death — has consumed [ordinary] death through the vision of the supreme <s>Ātman</s>, that liberated knower — this person — when he dies, at what time, do the <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the other <s>grahas</s>, and names and the other <s>atigrahas</s>, in the form of residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), the inner impelling forces — depart upward from this dying knower of <s>Brahman</s>, or not? <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: No — they do not depart. Right here, in this very [self], they merge into non-differentiation with the supreme <s>Ātman</s>. For the knower, the effects and instruments [of action], [dissolving into] their source — the supreme <s>Brahman</s>-reality — are merged (<s>samavanīyante</s>), unified, dissolved — this is the meaning.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.12
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.2.12]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yatrāyaṃ puruṣo mriyate |
kim enaṃ na jahātīti |
nāmeti |
anantaṃ vai nāmānantā viśve devāḥ |
anantam eva sa tena lokaṃ jayati || BrhUp_3,2.12 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'when this person dies, what does not leave him?' 'Name (<s>nāma</s>),' [he replied]. 'Name indeed is infinite; infinite are the <s>Viśvedevas</s>. By it, he conquers an infinite world.' (BṛUp 3.2.12)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.12 muktasya kiṃ prāṇā eva samavanoyanta āhosvittatprayojakamapi sarvam /
atha prāṇā eva na tatprayojakaṃ sarva, prayojake vidyamāne punaḥ prāṇānāṃ prasaṅgaḥ /
atha sarvameva kāmakarmādi, tato mokṣa upapadyata ityevamartha uttaraḥ praśnaḥ /
yājñavalkyeti hovāca yatrāyaṃ puruṣo mriyate kimenaṃ na jahātīti /
āhetaro nāmeti sarvaṃ samavanīyata ityarthaḥ /
nāmamātraṃ tu na līyata ākṛtisambandhāt /
nityaṃ hi nāma /
anantaṃ vai nāma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Infinite indeed is name.

children.text: nityatvamevā'nantyaṃ nāmnaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The infinity of name is its very eternity.

children.text: tadānantyādhikṛtā anantā bai viśve devā anantameva sa tena lokaṃ jayati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Presiding over that infinity [of name] are the infinite <s>Viśvedevas</s>; by that [name], he indeed conquers an infinite world.

children.text: tannāmānantyādhikṛtānviśvāndevānātmatvenopetya tenā'nantyadarśanenānantameva lokaṃ jayati //12//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having attained the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, who preside over the infinity of name, as his own <s>Ātman</s>, by that vision of infinity, he conquers an infinite world indeed. (12)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.12:] [Question:] For the liberated one, do only the <s>prāṇas</s> merge [into <s>Brahman</s>], or does everything that impels them also [merge]? If only the <s>prāṇas</s> [merge] but not everything that impels them, then while the impelling [forces] remain, there would again be the contingency of [new] <s>prāṇas</s>. But if everything — desire, <s>karma</s>, and the like — [merges], then liberation is possible. With this purport, the next question [is asked]. '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'when this person dies, what does not leave him?' The other [replied]: 'Name' — everything merges, this is the meaning. But name alone does not dissolve, because of its connection with the universal form (<s>ākṛti</s>). For name is eternal.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,2.13
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.2.13]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yatrāsya puruṣasya mṛtasyāgniṃ vāg apyeti vātaṃ prāṇaś cakṣur ādityaṃ manaś candraṃ diśaḥ śrotraṃ pṛthivīṃ śarīram ākāśam ātmauṣadhīr lomāni vanaspatīn keśā apsu lohitaṃ ca retaś ca nidhīyate kvāyaṃ tadā puruṣo bhavatīti |
āhara saumya hastam ārtabhāga |
āvām evaitasya vediṣyāvo na nāv etat sajana iti |
tau hotkramya mantrayāṃ cakrāte |
tau ha yad ūcatuḥ karma haiva tad ūcatuḥ |
atha ha yat praśaṃsatuḥ karma haiva tat praśaśaṃsatuḥ |
puṇyo vai puṇyena karmaṇā bhavati pāpaḥ pāpeneti |
tato ha jāratkārava ārtabhāga upararāma || BrhUp_3,2.13 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'when this person dies — his speech enters fire, his breath enters the wind, his eye enters the sun, his mind enters the moon, his ear enters the directions, his body enters the earth, his self enters space, the hairs of his body enter the plants, the hairs of his head enter the trees, his blood and semen are deposited in water — where then is this person?' 'Take my hand, dear <s>Ārtabhāga</s>. We two alone shall know of this; this is not for us [to discuss] among people.' They two went out and deliberated. What they spoke of was <s>karma</s> (action) alone. What they praised was <s>karma</s> alone. One becomes good by good <s>karma</s>; one becomes evil by evil <s>karma</s>. Thereupon <s>Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga</s> held his peace. (BṛUp 3.2.13)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,2.13 grahātigraharūpaṃ bandhanamuktaṃ mṛtyurūpaṃ tasya ca mṛtyormṛtyusadbhāvānmokṣaścopapadyate /
sa ca mokṣo grahātigraharūpāṇāmihaiva pralayaḥ pradīpanirvāṇavat /
yadvadgrahātigrahākhyaṃ bandhanaṃ mṛtyurūpaṃ tasya yatprayojakaṃ tatsvarūpanirdhāraṇārthamidamārabhyate /
yājñavalkyeti hovāca /
atra kecidvarṇayanti grahātigrahasya saprayojakasya vināśe 'pi kila na mucyate /
nāmāvaśiṣṭo 'vidyayoṣarasthānīyayā svātmaprabhavayā pa mātmanaḥ paricchinno bhojyācca jagato vyāvṛtta ucchinna kāmakarmāntarāle vyavatiṣṭhate /
tasya paramātmaikatvadarśane dvaitadarśanamapanetavyamityataḥ paraṃ paramātmadarśanamārabdhavyamityevamapavargākhyāmantarālāvasthāṃ parikalyottaragranthasaṃbandhaṃ kurvanti /
tatra vaktavyaṃ viśīrṇeṣu karaṇeṣu videhasya paramātmadarśanaśravaṇamanananididhyāsanāni kathamiti /
samavanītaprāṇasya hi nāmamātrāvaśiṣṭasyeti tairucyate /
mṛtaḥ śeta iti hayuktam /
na manorathenāpyetadupapādayituṃ śakyate /
atha jīvannevāvidyāmātrāvaśiṣṭo bhojyādapāvṛtta iti parikalpyate tattu kiṃnimittamiti vaktavyam /
samastadvaitaikatvātmaprāptinimittamiti yadyucyate tatpūrvameva nirākṛtam /
karmasahitena dvaitaikatvātmadarśanena sampanno vidvānmṛtaḥ samavanītaprāṇo jagadātmatvaṃ hiraṇyagarbhasvarūpaṃ vā prāpnuyādasamavanītaprāṇo bhojyājjīvanneva vyāvṛtto viraktaḥ paramātmadarśanābhimukhaḥ syāt /
na cobhayamekaprayatnaniṣpādyena sādhanena labhyam /
hiraṇyagarbhaprāptisādhanaṃ cenna tato vyāvṛttisādhanam /
paramātmābhimukhīkaraṇasya bhojyādvayāvṛtteḥ sādhanaṃ cenna hiraṇyagarbhaprāptisādhanam /
na hi yadgatisādhanaṃ tadgatinivṛtterapi /
atha mṛtvā hiraṇyagarbhaṃ prāpya tataḥ samavanītaprāṇo nāmāvaśiṣṭaḥ paramātmajñāne 'dhikriyate /
tato 'smadādyarthaṃ paramātmajñānopadeśo 'narthakaḥ syāt /
sarveṣāṃ hi brahmavidyā puruṣārthāyopadiśyate"tadyo yo devānām"ityādyayā śrutyā /
tasmādatyantanikṛṣṭā śāstrabāhyaiveyaṃ kalpanā /
prakṛtaṃ tu vartayiṣyāma /
tatra kena prayuktaṃ grahātigrahalakṣaṇaṃ bandhanamityetannirdidhārayiṣayā'ha-yatrāsya puruṣasyāsamyagdarśinaḥ śiraḥpāṇyādimato mṛtasya vāgagnimapyeti vātaṃ prāṇo 'pyeti cakṣurādityamapyetīti sarvatra sambadhyate /
manaścandraṃ diśaḥ śrotraṃ pṛthivīṃ śarīramākāśamātmetyatrā'tmādhiṣṭhānaṃ hṛdayākāśamucyate /
sa ākāśamapyeti /
oṣadhīrapiyati lomāni /
vanaspatīnapiyanti keśāḥ /
apsu lohitaṃ ca retaśca nidhīyata iti punarādānaliṅgam /
sarvatra hi vāgādiśabdena devatāḥ parigṛhyante na tu karaṇānyevāpakrāmanti prāṅmokṣāt /
tatra devatābhiranadhiṣṭhitāni karaṇāni nyastadātrādyupamānāni videhaśca kartā puruṣo 'svatantraḥ kimāśrito bhavatīti pṛcchayate-kvāyaṃ tadā puruṣo bhavatīti /
kimāśritastadā puruṣo bhavatīti /
yamāśrayamāśritya punaḥ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātamupādatte yena grahātigrahalakṣaṇaṃ bandhanaṃ prayujyate tatkimiti praśnaḥ /
atrocyate-svabhāvayadṛcchākālakarmadaivavijñānamātraśūnyāni vādibhiḥ parikalpitāni /
ato 'nekavipratipattisthānatvānnaiva jalpanyāyena vastunirṇayaḥ /
atra vastunirṇayaṃ cedicchasyāhara sobhya hastasārtabhāga ha āvāmevaitasya tvatpṛṣṭasya veditavyaṃ yattadvediṣyāvo nirūpayiṣyāvaḥ /
kasmāt /
na nāvāvayoretadvastu sajane janasamudāye nirṇetuṃ śakyate /
ata ekānta gamiṣyāvo vicāraṇāya /
tau hetyādi śrutivacanam /
tau yājñavalkyārtabhāgāvekāntaṃ gatvā kiṃ cakraturityucyate-tau hotkramya sajanāddeśānmantrayāñcakrāte /
ādau laukikavādipakṣāṇāmekaikaṃ parugṛhya vicāritavantau /
tau ha vicārya yadūcaturapohya pūrvapakṣānsarvāneva tacchṛṇu /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having deliberated, what those two said — having refuted all the opponent's positions — listen to that:

children.text: karma haivā'śrayaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kāryakaraṇopādānahetuṃ tattatrocaturuktavantau /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Action (<s>karma</s>) alone is the substrate — the cause of repeatedly taking up the aggregate of body and senses — this is what those two said, what they declared.

children.text: na kevalaṃ kālakarmadaiveśvareṣvabhyupagateṣu hetuṣu yatpraśaśaṃsatustau karma haiva tatpraśaśaṃsatuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Not merely among the [proposed causes of] time, action, fate, and God — among those accepted as causes — that which those two praised, that is, those two praised action alone.

children.text: yasmānnirdhāritametatkarmaprayuktaṃ grahātigrahādikāryakaraṇopādānaṃ punaḥ punastasmātpuṇyo vai śāstravihitena puṇyena karmaṇā bhavati tadviparotena viparīto bhavati pāpaḥ pāpenetyevaṃ yājñavalkyena praśneṣu nirṇīteṣu tato 'śakyaprakampyatvādyājñavalkyasya ha jaratkārava ārtabhāga upararāma //13//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since it has been determined that the taking up of the aggregate of body and senses — [involving] <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s> and the rest — is impelled by action, repeatedly — therefore, by meritorious (<s>puṇya</s>) action prescribed by scripture, one becomes meritorious; by the opposite — by sinful (<s>pāpa</s>) action — one becomes the opposite, sinful. Thus, when the questions were settled by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, thereupon <s>Jaratkārava Ārtabhāga</s>, because <s>Yājñavalkya</s> could not be shaken, desisted [from further questioning]. (13)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.2.13:] The bondage characterized by the <s>grahas</s> (seizers) and <s>atigrahas</s> (over-seizers) has been stated, and it is in the form of death; and since there is the real existence of a death of that death, liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) too is established. And that liberation is the dissolution, right here [in this life], of the [bondage] in the form of <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s> — like the extinguishing of a lamp. Now, in order to determine the nature of that which impels the bondage called <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s>, which is in the form of death, this [section] is commenced. '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said. Here, some explain: even upon the destruction of the <s>graha-atigraha</s> together with its impelling cause, [the self] is allegedly not liberated. With only name remaining, [the self,] through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — which is like barren land, self-originated — delimited from the <s>Paramātman</s> and turned away from the world of enjoyment, with desire and action cut off, stands in an intermediate state. For the vision of oneness with the <s>Paramātman</s>, the vision of duality must be removed — and therefore the vision of the <s>Paramātman</s> must be commenced — thus they contrive an intermediate state called <s>apavarga</s> (release) and establish the connection with the subsequent text. Regarding that, the following must be said: when the organs have disintegrated, how can the disembodied one engage in hearing, reflecting, and meditating upon the vision of the <s>Paramātman</s>? 'For one whose vital breaths have been withdrawn, only name remains' — thus they say. But [the assertion that] 'one who is dead lies [in an intermediate state]' is improper. This cannot be established even by wishful thinking. Now, if one construes [the view that] while still living, with only <s>avidyā</s> remaining, [the self] is turned away from the object of enjoyment — then the cause of that must be stated. If it is said that the cause is the attainment of the self of the oneness of all duality — that has already been refuted earlier. A wise person who has accomplished the vision of the oneness of duality together with action — upon dying, with vital breaths withdrawn, would attain the universal selfhood or the nature of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>; or, without withdrawing the vital breaths, while still living, turned away from the objects of enjoyment, dispassionate, he would be inclined toward the vision of the <s>Paramātman</s>. And both [results] cannot be obtained by a single means accomplished through a single effort. If the means is for attaining <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, it is not the means for turning away from that [world]. If the means is for inclining toward the <s>Paramātman</s> — for turning away from the objects of enjoyment — it is not the means for attaining <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. For that which is a means to [a particular] destination is not also [a means] for the cessation of that destination. Now, if [one says that] after dying and attaining <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, then, with vital breaths withdrawn and only name remaining, one becomes qualified for the knowledge of the <s>Paramātman</s> — in that case, the teaching of <s>Paramātman</s>-knowledge for us and the like would be purposeless. For the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is taught for the benefit of all persons — as [indicated by] the <s>śruti</s>: 'Whoever among the gods' (BṛUp 1.4.10) and the like. Therefore, this contrivance — utterly debased and outside scripture — [should be rejected]. We shall continue with the topic at hand. Therein, with the desire to determine what impels the bondage characterized by <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s> — that is, the repeated taking up of the aggregate of body and senses — [the text] says: 'Where then does this person go?' — where this person (<s>puruṣa</s>) who lacks right vision, whose head, hands, and the like [have perished in death] — where does his speech go? It enters fire. Where does his <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) go? It enters wind. Where does his eye go? It enters the sun — and so forth, applying everywhere. The mind [enters] the moon; the ear [enters] the directions; the body [enters] the earth; the self [enters] space — and here, 'self' refers to the space within the heart, the substrate of the self. That [self] enters space. The body-hairs enter plants. The head-hairs enter trees. The blood and semen are deposited in water — this is the sign of being taken up again. For everywhere, by the words 'speech' and the rest, the presiding deities are included — not merely the organs themselves, for they do not depart prior to liberation. Therein, the organs, no longer presided over by the deities, are like a sickle and other instruments that have been laid down — and the disembodied agent, the <s>puruṣa</s>, being dependent, on what does he rest? — this is asked: 'Where then does this person go?' On what does the <s>puruṣa</s> then rest? — the substrate on which, resting, he takes up again the aggregate of body and senses, and by which the bondage characterized by <s>graha</s> and <s>atigraha</s> is impelled — what is that? — this is the question. Here it is said: [various schools] have contrived [the cause to be] inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), chance (<s>yadṛcchā</s>), time (<s>kāla</s>), action (<s>karma</s>), fate (<s>daiva</s>), consciousness-only (<s>vijñānamātra</s>), or the void (<s>śūnya</s>). Therefore, since this is a point of many conflicting views, the determination of reality cannot be achieved by the method of disputation (<s>jalpa</s>). Here, if you desire the determination of reality — 'Come, O <s>Somya</s>,' <s>Ārtabhāga</s> — '<s>hasta</s>' means 'take my hand' — let us two alone know that which is to be known regarding this question of yours. Why? Because this matter (<s>vastu</s>) cannot be determined by us in a public gathering (<s>sajana</s>). Therefore, let us go to a private place for deliberation. 'They went out' and so forth is the statement of <s>śruti</s>. Those two — <s>Yājñavalkya</s> and <s>Ārtabhāga</s> — having gone to a private place away from the gathering, what did they do? It is said: they went out and deliberated. They first took up, one by one, the positions of the worldly disputants and examined them.

children.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāye dvitīyamārtabhāgabrāhmaṇam //2//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>Ārtabhāga Brāhmaṇa</s> of the third <s>Adhyāya</s>. (2)

atha hainaṃ bhujyur lāhyāyaniḥ papraccha -- yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- madreṣu carakāḥ paryavrajāma |
te patañcalasya kāpyasya gṛhān aima |
tasyāsīd duhitā gandharvagṛhītā |
tam apṛcchāma ko 'sīti |
so 'bravīt sudhanvāṅgirasa iti |
taṃ yadā lokānām antān apṛcchāma |
athainam abrūma -- kva pārikṣitā abhavann iti |
kva pārikṣitā abhavan |
sa tvā pṛcchāmi yājñavalkya |
kva pārikṣitā abhavann iti || BrhUp_3,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Bhujyu Lāhyāyani</s> questioned him: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'we wandered about as traveling students among the <s>Madras</s>. We came to the house of <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s>. He had a daughter who was possessed by a <s>Gandharva</s>. We asked him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am <s>Sudhanvan Āṅgirasa</s>." When we asked him about the ends of the worlds, we said to him: "What became of the <s>Pārikṣitas</s>?" What became of the <s>Pārikṣitas</s>? I ask you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>: what became of the <s>Pārikṣitas</s>?' (BṛUp 3.3.1)

na /

puruṣapravṛttijananāyāvaśyaṃ cetkarmaphalaṃ kalpayitavyam karmāviruddhaviṣaya eva śrutārthāpatteḥ kṣīṇatvānnityo mokṣaḥ phalaṃ kalpayituṃ na śakyastadvyavadhānājñānanivṛttirvā /
aviruddhatvāddṛṣṭasāmarthyaviṣayatvācceti /
pāriśeṣyanyāyānmokṣa eva kalpayitavya iti cet /
sarveṣāṃ hi karmaṇāṃ sarvaṃ phalam na cānyaditarakarmaphalavyatirekeṇa phalaṃ kalpanāyogyamasti /
pariśiṣṭaśca mokṣaḥ /
sa ceṣṭo vedavidāṃ phalam /
tasmātsa eva kalpayitavya iti cet /
na /
karmaphalavyaktonāmānantyātpāriśeṣyanyāyānupapatteḥ /
nahi puruṣecchāviṣayāṇāṃ karmaphalānāmetāvattvaṃ nāma kenacidasarvajñenāvadhṛtaṃ tatsādhanānāṃ vā puruṣecchānāṃ vāniyatadeśakālanimittatvātpuruṣecchāviṣayasādhanānāṃ ca puruṣeṣṭaphalaprayuktatvāt /
pratiprāṇi cecchāvaicitryātphalānāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ cā'nantyasiddhiḥ /
tadānantyāccāśakyametāvattvaṃ puruṣairjñātum /
ajñāte ca sādhanaphalaitāvattve kathaṃ mokṣasya pariśeṣasiddhiriti /
karmaphalajātipāriśeṣyamiti cet /
satyapīcchāviṣayāṇāṃ tatsādhanānāṃ cā'nantye karmaphalajātitvaṃ nāma sarveṣāṃ tulyam /
mokṣasatvakarmaphalatvātpariśiṣṭaḥ syāt /
tasmātpariśeṣātsa eva yuktaḥ kalpayitumiti cet /
na /
tasyāpi nityakarmaphalatvābhyupagame karmaphalasamānajātīyatvopapatteḥ pariśeṣānupapattiḥ /
tasmādanyathāpyupapatteḥ kṣīṇā śrutārthāpattiḥ /
utpattayāptivikārasaṃskārāṇāmanyatamapi nityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalamupapadyata iti kṣīṇā śrutārthāpattiḥ /
caturṇāmanyatama eva mokṣa iti cet /
na tāvadutpādyo nityatvāt /
ata evāvikāryo 'saṃskāryaścāta eva, asādhanadravyātmakatvācca /
sādhanātmakaṃ hi dravyaṃ saṃskriyate /
yathā pātrājyādi prokṣaṇādinā /
na ca saṃskriyamāṇaḥ saṃskāranirvartyo vā yūpādivat /
pāriśeṣyādāpyaḥ syāt /
nā'pyo 'pyātmasvabhāvatvādekatvācca /
itaraiḥ karmabhirvailakṣaṇyānnityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ tatphalenāpi vilakṣaṇena bhavitavyamiti cet /
na /
karmatvasālakṣaṇyātsalakṣaṇaṃ kasmātphalaṃ na bhavatītarakarmaphalaiḥ /
nimittavailakṣaṇyāditi cet /
na /
kṣāmavatyādibhiḥ samānatvāt /
yathā hi gṛhadāhādau nimitte kṣāmavatyādīṣṭiryathā bhinne juhoti skanne juhotītyevamādau naimittikeṣu karmasu na mokṣaḥ phalaṃ kalpyate /
taiścāviśeṣānnaimittikatvena jīvanādinimitte ca śravaṇāt /
tathā nityānāmapi na mokṣaḥ phalam /
ālokasya sarveṣāṃ rūpadarśanasādhanatva ulūkādaya ālokena rūpaṃ na paśyantītyulukādicakṣuṣo vailakṣaṇyāditaralokacakṣurbhirna rasādiviṣayatvaṃ parikalpyate rasādiviṣaye sāmarthyasyādṛṣṭatvāt /
sudūramapi gatvā yadviṣaye dṛṣṭaṃ sāmarthyaṃ tatraiva kaścidviśeṣaḥ kalpayitavyaḥ /
yatpunaruktaṃ vidyāmantraśarkarādisaṃyuktaviṣadadadhyādivannityāni kāryāntaramārabhanta iti /
ārabhyatāṃ viśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ tadiṣṭatvādavirodhaḥ /
nirabhisaṃdheḥ karmaṇo vidyāsaṃyuktasya viśiṣṭakāryāntarārambhe na kaścidvirodhaḥ /
devayājyātmayājinorātmayājino viśeṣaśravaṇāddevayājinaḥ'śreyānātmayājī'tyādau'yadeva vidyayā karotī'tyādau ca /
yastu paramātmadarśanaviṣaye manunokta ātmayājiśabdaḥ'samaṃ paśyannātmayājī'tyatra samaṃ paśyannātmayājī bhavatītyarthaḥ /
athavā bhūtapūrvagatyā /
ātmayājyātmasaṃskārārthaṃ nityāni karmāṇi karoti"idaṃ me 'nenāṅga saṃskriyate"iti śruteḥ /
tathā gārbhairhemairityādiprakaraṇe kāryakaraṇasaṃskārārthatvaṃ nityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ darśayati /
saṃskṛtaśca ya ātmayājī taiḥ karmabhiḥ samaṃ draṣṭuṃ samartho bhavati /
tasyeha vā janmāntare vā samamātmadarśanamutpadyate samaṃ paśyansvārājyamadhigacchatītyeṣor'thaḥ /
ātmayājiśabdastu bhūtapūrvagatyā prayujyate /
children.translated_text: The word 'self-sacrificer' (<s>ātmayājin</s>) is used in the sense of a past [practice that has been] transcended.

children.text: jñānayuktānāṃ nityānāṃ karmaṇāṃ jñānotpattisādhanatvapradarśanārtham /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of demonstrating that the obligatory rituals (<s>nitya karman</s>), when conjoined with knowledge, are the means for the arising of knowledge.

children.text: kiñcānyat- brahmā viśvasṛjo dharmo mahānavyaktameva ca /
children.translated_text: Moreover: '<s>Brahmā</s>, the creators of the world, <s>dharma</s>, and the great unmanifest —

children.text: uttamāṃ sāttvikīmetāṃ gatimāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: the wise declare this to be the supreme <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) destination.'

[Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.3.1:] Then <s>Bhujyu Lāhyāyani</s> questioned him.
The bondage characterized by the graspers and over-graspers has been explained.
That from which, being released from [the graspers] together with their impellers, one is liberated — or that by which, being bound, one transmigrates — that is death.
And from that, liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) is possible.
Because there is a death of death.
And the liberated one has no going anywhere.
Total annihilation with only a name remaining, like the extinction of a lamp — this too has been ascertained.
Therein, for the transmigrating [beings] and for those being liberated, while the conjunction of the effects and instruments with their own causes remains the same — for the liberated, there is absolutely no further taking up [of effects and instruments].
But for the transmigrating, the repeated taking up [of bodies and instruments] is impelled by that which is called <s>karma</s> (action) — this has been ascertained through investigation.
And upon the exhaustion of that [<s>karma</s>], total annihilation with only a name remaining is liberation.
And that <s>karma</s> is known as merit (<s>puṇya</s>) and demerit (<s>pāpa</s>).
Because it has been ascertained [by the <s>śruti</s>]: 'One becomes meritorious by meritorious action, sinful by sinful [action].'
This <s>saṃsāra</s> is caused by that [<s>karma</s>].
Therein, through demerit, one experiences suffering among the stationary and moving beings — which are by nature predominantly painful — and in hells, animal births, ghostly states, and the like, being repeatedly born and dying — this is well-known to all the world, like the royal highway.
But that which is scriptural — 'One becomes meritorious by meritorious action' — it is precisely to that that regard is given here by the <s>śruti</s>.
And meritorious action alone is the means to all human goals (<s>puruṣārthas</s>) — thus declare all <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s> statements.
Since liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) too is a human goal, its being achievable [through merit] follows.
The greater the excellence of merit, the greater the excellence of the fruit attained.
Therefore, the suspicion might arise that liberation will come about through the supreme excellence of merit.
That [suspicion] must be dispelled. Even for <s>karma</s> combined with knowledge, this much is [the extent of] the destination.
Because <s>karma</s> and its fruit pertain to the domain of differentiated name and form.
But in what is non-produced, eternal, possessing the characteristics of the undifferentiated, not of the nature of name and form, and devoid of the nature of action, agent, and fruit — <s>karma</s> has no operation.
And where there is [such] operation, that is <s>saṃsāra</s> alone — for the purpose of demonstrating this meaning, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [section on <s>Brahman</s>] is commenced.
But what some say — that <s>karma</s> combined with <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), being without selfish motive (<s>nirabhisaṃdhi</s>), produces a different result, like clear curds mixed with mantras and sugar and the like — that is not so.
Because <s>mokṣa</s> is not something to be produced.
For liberation is merely the destruction of bondage, not something produced as an effect; and bondage is <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — this we have stated.
And the destruction of <s>avidyā</s> by <s>karma</s> is impossible.
Because the capacity of <s>karma</s> pertains only to things within the range of perception.
For production, attainment, modification, and purification (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are the domains of the capacity of <s>karma</s>.
<s>Karma</s> has the capacity to produce, to cause attainment, to modify, and [to purify] — beyond these, the capacity of <s>karma</s> has no other domain.
Because this is not known in the world.
And <s>mokṣa</s> is not any one of these categories.
We have stated that it is merely veiled by <s>avidyā</s>.
[Objection:] Granted. Let this be the nature of <s>karma</s> by itself alone. But <s>karma</s> combined with <s>vidyā</s>, being without selfish motive, has a different nature.
For it is seen that even things whose capacity has been ascertained in one domain — like clear curds and the like — when combined with <s>vidyā</s>, mantras, sugar, and the like, have capacity in another domain.
Likewise, let <s>karma</s> too [have such capacity].
[Reply:] No. Because there is no means of valid knowledge [to establish this].
For regarding the capacity of <s>karma</s> in a domain other than the stated domain — neither perception, nor inference, nor analogy, nor presumption (<s>arthāpatti</s>), nor verbal testimony is available as a means of valid knowledge.
[Objection:] But the impossibility of the injunction being otherwise [explained] in the absence of another fruit — that is the means of valid knowledge.
For the fruit of obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) rituals is not postulated through the <s>Viśvajit</s> analogy.
Nor is there a fruit stated [for them] in <s>śruti</s>.
And they are enjoined.
By the method of residue, <s>mokṣa</s> is understood to be their fruit.
For otherwise, people would not engage [in them].
[Reply:] But is this not the very <s>Viśvajit</s> analogy — since the fruit of <s>mokṣa</s> is being postulated?
If <s>mokṣa</s> or some other fruit were not postulated, people would not engage [in obligatory rituals] — therefore <s>mokṣa</s> is postulated as the fruit through the presumption derived from <s>śruti</s>, just as in the <s>Viśvajit</s> [sacrifice].
[Objection:] If so, how can it be said that the <s>Viśvajit</s> analogy does not apply? That the fruit is postulated and yet the <s>Viśvajit</s> analogy does not apply — this is a contradiction.
[Reply:] If [you say] <s>mokṣa</s> is simply not a fruit at all — [we say:] no, because that would involve abandoning [your own] thesis.
For it was asserted that <s>karma</s> produces a different result (<s>kāryāntara</s>), like clear curds and the like. If <s>mokṣa</s> is a product (<s>kārya</s>), a fruit of <s>karma</s>, then that thesis would be abandoned [since you said it's not a fruit].
And if <s>mokṣa</s> is an effect of <s>karma</s>, a distinction must be stated between it and fruits like heaven and the like.
If it is not an effect of <s>karma</s>, then the meaning of the statement 'obligatory rituals have <s>mokṣa</s> as their fruit' must be explained.
And it is not possible to postulate a distinction merely by the difference between the words 'effect' (<s>kārya</s>) and 'fruit' (<s>phala</s>).
'<s>Mokṣa</s> is not a fruit, and yet it is accomplished by obligatory rituals; obligatory rituals have no fruit and no product' — this meaning stated [by you] is contradictory, like saying 'fire is cold.'
[Objection:] It is like knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>). Just as <s>mokṣa</s> is the product of knowledge — though not actively produced by knowledge, it is still said to be so — similarly, let it be a product of <s>karma</s>.
[Reply:] No. Because knowledge removes ignorance.
Because knowledge removes the veil of ignorance, <s>mokṣa</s> is figuratively called a product of knowledge.
But <s>avidyā</s> is not to be removed by <s>karma</s>.
Nor is it possible to postulate any obstacle other than <s>avidyā</s> as the veil [preventing] <s>mokṣa</s>.
Because <s>mokṣa</s> is eternal, and because it is not different from the nature of the one who accomplishes [it] — [there is nothing] that <s>karma</s> could remove.
[Objection:] <s>Karma</s> too removes ignorance.
[Reply:] No. Because [<s>karma</s>] is of a different character [from knowledge].
Non-manifestation is <s>ajñāna</s> (ignorance), and it is contradicted by knowledge, which has the character of manifestation.
But <s>karma</s> is not contradicted by that <s>ajñāna</s>; therefore <s>karma</s> is of a different character from knowledge.
Whether <s>ajñāna</s> is called the absence of knowledge, or doubtful knowledge, or wrong knowledge — all of it is removed by knowledge alone.
But it is not removed by <s>karma</s> of any kind whatsoever, because there is no contradiction [between <s>karma</s> and <s>ajñāna</s>].
[Objection:] But let it be postulated that the capacity of <s>karma</s> to remove ignorance is unseen (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>).
[Reply:] No. Because when the removal of ignorance by knowledge is [already] understood, the postulation of an unseen removal is impossible.
Just as, when the removal of husks from rice-grains by threshing is understood, an unseen [capacity] — produced by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit) of obligatory rituals like the <s>Agnihotra</s> — is not postulated for the removal of husks.
Similarly, the removal of ignorance is not postulated as an unseen [result] produced by the <s>adṛṣṭa</s> of obligatory rituals.
And we have stated that rituals performed repeatedly are contradictory to knowledge.
That knowledge which is not contradicted by rituals — that has been said to be the cause of attaining the world of the gods: 'by <s>vidyā</s>, the world of the gods' — thus the <s>śruti</s>.
Moreover, if another fruit of obligatory rituals — which are heard [in <s>śruti</s>] — is to be postulated, and if that which is contradicted by rituals in the domain of substances, qualities, and actions is simply not a product [of <s>karma</s>] at all — then what should be postulated? That in which the capacity of <s>karma</s> has not been seen at all? Or rather, that in which [its] capacity has been seen and which is a fruit not contradicted by rituals — let that be postulated.
And if a fruit of rituals must be postulated [in order to explain] why people engage [in them], then through the presumption from <s>śruti</s>, it should be postulated only in a domain that is not contradicted by <s>karma</s>. <s>Mokṣa</s>, being eternal, cannot be postulated as a fruit — nor can the removal of the <s>ajñāna</s> that veils it [be so postulated].
Because [<s>mokṣa</s>] is not contradicted [by <s>karma</s>], and because [<s>karma</s>'s] capacity has been seen [only] in its own domain.
[Objection:] By the method of residue, <s>mokṣa</s> alone should be postulated. For all rituals have all [possible] fruits; and there is no other fruit, beyond the fruits of other rituals, that is fit to be postulated. And <s>mokṣa</s> is the residue. And it is the desired fruit for the knowers of the <s>Veda</s>. Therefore, it alone should be postulated.
[Reply:] No. Because the infinity of the particular fruits of rituals makes the method of residue impossible.
For the totality of the particular fruits of rituals, which are objects of human desire, has not been ascertained by anyone who is not omniscient — nor [has the totality] of the means to them, nor of the human desires [themselves], because human desires have no fixed limitation of place, time, or cause. And because the means to the objects of human desire are impelled by the desired fruits of humans.
And because of the diversity of desires in each living being, the infinity of fruits and their means is established.
And because of that infinity, it is impossible for humans to know their totality.
And when the totality of means and fruits is not known, how can the establishment of <s>mokṣa</s> by the method of residue [work]?
[Objection:] The method of residue applies to the class (<s>jāti</s>) of fruits of <s>karma</s>. Even though the objects of desire and their means are infinite, the class-nature of 'fruit of <s>karma</s>' is the same for all. <s>Mokṣa</s>, not being a fruit of <s>karma</s>, would be the residue. Therefore, by the method of residue, it alone is fit to be postulated.
[Reply:] No. Because if <s>mokṣa</s> too is accepted as a fruit of obligatory rituals, it would be of the same class as fruits of <s>karma</s>, and the method of residue would not apply.
Therefore, because [the matter] can be explained otherwise too, the presumption from <s>śruti</s> is exhausted [i.e., loses force].
Any one of production, attainment, modification, or purification can be a fruit of obligatory rituals — thus the presumption from <s>śruti</s> is exhausted.
[Objection:] <s>Mokṣa</s> is precisely one of these four.
[Reply:] It is not, to begin with, something to be produced, because of [its] eternality.
For this very reason, it is not something to be modified, nor to be purified — and also because it is not of the nature of a substance that serves as a means [to something else].
For a substance that serves as a means is what gets purified.
As for instance, a vessel, clarified butter, and the like are purified by sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and the like.
And [<s>mokṣa</s>] is not something being purified, nor something to be produced by purification, like a sacrificial post (<s>yūpa</s>) and the like.
By the method of residue, it would be something to be attained (<s>āpya</s>).
[Reply:] It is not attainable either, because it is of the nature of the self and because it is one [with the self].
[Objection:] Because obligatory rituals are dissimilar from other rituals, their fruit too must be dissimilar.
[Reply:] No. Because of the similarity in being <s>karma</s> — why should the fruit not be similar to the fruits of other rituals?
[Objection:] Because of the dissimilarity of the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>).
[Reply:] No. Because of the similarity with [rituals like] the <s>Kṣāmavatī</s> and the like.
Just as in occasional (<s>naimitta</s>) rituals — such as the <s>Kṣāmavatī</s> and other <s>iṣṭis</s>, [performed] when the house is burned and so forth, or [rituals performed] 'when [the oblation] is split,' 'when [it] is spilled,' and so forth — <s>mokṣa</s> is not postulated as the fruit.
And because there is no difference [between obligatory and occasional rituals]; and because [obligatory rituals] are heard [in <s>śruti</s>] as occasioned by [conditions such as] being alive and the like.
Similarly, for obligatory rituals too, <s>mokṣa</s> is not the fruit.
Just as light is the means of seeing forms for everyone — yet owls and the like do not see forms by light — the dissimilarity of the owl's eye and the like from the eyes of other beings does not lead one to postulate that those other eyes perceive tastes and the like, because the capacity [of eyes] in the domain of tastes and the like has not been seen.
Even going very far afield, whatever capacity has been seen in a particular domain — only some specific [variation] within that [same domain] should be postulated.
As for what was said — that obligatory rituals, like clear curds combined with mantras, sugar, and the like, produce a different result — let them produce a distinguished result, since that is what is desired — there is no contradiction.
For the desireless (<s>nirabhisaṃdhi</s>) <s>karma</s> combined with <s>vidyā</s> producing a distinguished different result — there is no contradiction in this.
[This follows] from the <s>śruti</s>'s statement of a distinction between one who sacrifices to the gods and one who sacrifices to the self — the self-sacrificer being superior — in [passages like] 'the self-sacrificer is superior' and 'whatever one does with knowledge' and the like.
But the word '<s>ātmayājin</s>' (self-sacrificer) as used by <s>Manu</s> in the context of the vision of the supreme self — in '<s>samaṃ paśyann ātmayājī</s>' ('seeing equally, the self-sacrificer') — the meaning is: one who sees equally becomes a self-sacrificer.
Alternatively, by way of what has already been accomplished:
The self-sacrificer performs obligatory rituals for the purpose of self-purification (<s>ātmasaṃskāra</s>) — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'This limb of mine is being purified by this [ritual].'
Likewise, in the section [beginning with] 'by the embryonic [rituals], by the golden [rites]' and so forth, [the text] shows that obligatory rituals serve the purpose of purifying the effects and instruments [i.e., body and senses].
And one who is thus purified — the self-sacrificer — by those rituals becomes capable of seeing equally.
For such a one, the equal vision of the self arises either in this life or in another birth — 'seeing equally, one attains sovereignty (<s>svārājya</s>)' — this is the meaning.

iti ca devasārṣṭivyatirekeṇa bhūtāpyayaṃ darśayati bhūtānyapyeti pañca vai /
bhūtānyatyetīti pāṭhaṃ ye kurvanti teṣāṃ vedaviṣaye paricchinnabuddhitvādadoṣaḥ /
na cārthavādatvamadhyāyasya brahmāntakarmavipākārthasya tadvayatiriktātmajñānārthasya ca karmakāṇḍopaniṣadbhayāṃ tulyārthatvadarśanāt /
vihitākaraṇapratiṣiddhakarmaṇāṃ ca sthāvaraśvasūkarādiphaladarśanāt /
vāntāśyādipretadarśanācca /
na ca śrutismṛtivīrītapratiṣiddhavyatirekeṇa vihitāni vā pratiṣiddhānivā karmāṇi kenacidavagantuṃ śakyante /
yeṣāmakaraṇādanuṣṭhānācca pretaśvasūkarasthāvarādīni karmaphalāni pratyakṣānumānābhyāmupalabhyante /
na caiṣāmakarmaphalatvaṃ kenacidabhyupagamyate /

tasmāt"sa ātmano vapāmudakhidat" "so 'rodīdi"tyādivannābhūtārthavādatvam /
tatrāpyabhūtārthavadatvaṃ mā bhūditi cet /
bhavatvevam /
na caitāvatāsya nyāyasya bādho bhavati /
na cāsmatpakṣo vā duṣyati /
na ca"brahmā viśvasṛja"ityādīnāṃ kāmyakarmaphalatvaṃ śakyaṃ vaktum /
teṣāṃ devasārṣṭitāyāḥ phalasyoktatvāt /

yeṣāṃ punarnityāni nirabhisaṃdhīnyātmasaṃskārārthāni teṣāṃ jñānotpattyarthāni tāni /
"brāhmīyaṃ kriyate tanuḥ"iti smaraṇāt /
teṣāmārādupakārakatvānmokṣasādhanānyapi karmāṇi bhavantīti na virudhyate /

na ca pramāṇāntaraviruddhārthaviṣaye śruteḥ prāmāṇyaṃ kalpyate yathā śīto 'gniḥ kledayatīti /
śrute tu tādarthye vākyasya pramāṇāntarasyā'bhāsatvama /
yathā khadyoto 'gniriti talamalinamantarikṣamiti bālānāṃ yatpratyakṣamapi tadviṣayapramāṇāntarasya yathārthatve niścite niścitārthamapi bālapratyakṣamābhāsībhavati /
tasmādvedaprāmāṇyasyāvyabhicārāttādarthye sati vākyasya tathātvaṃ syāt /
na tu puruṣamatikauśalam /
nahi puruṣamatikauśalātsavitā rūpaṃ na prakāśayati /
tathā vedavākyānyapi nānyārthāni bhavanti /
tasmānna mokṣārthāni karmāṇīti siddham /
ataḥ karmaphalānāṃ saṃsāratvapradarśanāyaiva brāhmaṇamārabhyate /
athānantaram uparate jāratkārave, bhujyuriti nāmato lahyasyāpatyaṃ lāhyastadapatyaṃ lāhyāyaniḥ papraccha /
yājñavalkyeti hovāca /
ādābuktamaśvamedhadarśanam;samaṣṭivyaṣṭiphalaścāśvamedhakratuḥ, jñānasamuccito vā kevalajñānasampādito vā, sarvakarmaṇāṃ parā kāṣṭhā;bhraṇahatyāśvamedhābhyāṃ na paraṃ puṇyapāpayoriti hi smaranti;tena hi samaṣṭiṃ vyaṣṭīśca prāpnoti;tatra vyaṣṭayo nirjñātā antaraṇḍaviṣayā aśvamedhayāgaphalabhūtāḥ;'mṛtyurasyātmā bhavatyetāsāṃ devatānāmekā bhavati'(1 / 2 / 7) ityuktam /
mṛtyuścāśanāyālakṣaṇo buddhayātmā samaṣṭiḥ prathamajo vāyuḥ sūtraṃ satyaṃ hiraṇyagarbhaḥ;tasya vyākṛto viṣayaḥ-yadātmakaṃ sarvaṃ dvaitaikatvam /
yaḥ sarvabhūtāntarātmā liṅgam amūrtaraso yadāśritāni sarvabhūtakarmāṇi, yaḥ karmaṇāṃ karmasambaddhānāṃ ca vijñānānāṃ parā gatiḥ paraṃ phalam, tasya kiyān gocaraḥ kiyati vyāptiḥ sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalībhūtā, sā vaktavyā;tasyām uktāyāṃ sarvaḥ saṃsāro bandhagocara ukto bhavati /
tasya ca samaṣṭivyaṣṭyātmadarśanasya alaukikatvapradarśanārthamākhyāyikāmātmano vṛttāṃ prakurute;tena ca prativādibuddhiṃvyāmohayiṣyāmīti manyate /
madreṣu madrā nāma janapadāsteṣu, carakā adhyayanārthavratacaraṇāccarakā adhvaryavo vā, paryavrajāma paryaṭitavantaḥ;te patañcalasya nāmataḥ, kāpyasya kapigotrasya, gṛhān aima gatavantaḥ /
tasyāsīd duhitā gandharvagṛhītā-gandharveṇa amānuṣeṇa sacvena kenacidāviṣṭā;gandharvo vā dhiṣṇyo 'gnirṛtvigadevatā viśiṣṭavijñānatvādavasīyate;na hi sacvamātrasyedṛśaṃ vijñānamupapadyate /
taṃ sarve vayaṃ parivāritāḥ santo 'pṛcchāma-ko 'sīti, kastvamasi kinnāmā kiṃsatacvaḥ /
so 'bravīd gandharvaḥ sudhanvā nāmataḥ, āṅgiraso gotrataḥ /

taṃ yadā yasmin kāle lokānāmantān paryavasānāni apṛcchāma athainaṃ gandharvamabrūma-bhūvanakośaparimāṇajñānāya pravṛtteṣu sarveṣvātmānaṃ ślāghayantaḥ pṛṣṭavanto vayam;katham? kva pārikṣitā abhavanniti /
children.translated_text: When at that time we asked him about the ends of the worlds, their ultimate limits — then we said to that <s>gandharva</s>, all of us, praising ourselves as being engaged in knowing the extent of the cosmic sphere: 'How [did we ask]? Where did the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> go?'

children.text: sa ca gandharvaḥ sarvamasmabhyabravīt /
children.translated_text: And that <s>gandharva</s> told us everything.

children.text: tena divyebhyo mayā labdhaṃ jñānam, tattava nāsti, ato nigṛhīto 'si, ityabhiprāyaḥ /
children.translated_text: The purport is: 'I have obtained knowledge from divine [sources]; you do not have that; therefore you are defeated.'

children.text: so 'haṃ vidyāsampanno labdhāgamo gandharvāt tvā tvāṃ pṛcchāmi yājñavalkya-kva pārikṣitā abhavantat tvaṃ kiṃ jānāsi? he yājñavalkya'kathaya pṛcchāmi kva pārikṣitā abhavanniti //1//
children.translated_text: I, thus endowed with knowledge, having received the teaching from the <s>gandharva</s>, ask you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> — where did the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> go? Do you know this? O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, tell me — I ask: where did the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> go? // 1 //

And thus, distinct from equality with the gods (<s>devasārṣṭi</s>), [the text] shows the dissolution into the elements (<s>bhūtāpyaya</s>): 'he enters the five elements.' Those who read '<s>bhūtānyatyeti</s>' ('he transcends the elements') — there is no fault [in our position] because of their limited understanding regarding the scope of the <s>Veda</s>. Nor is this chapter mere laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>), since the chapter is intended to teach the maturation of <s>karma</s> up to [the level of] <s>Brahmā</s>, as well as Self-knowledge that transcends that — because the same purport is seen in both the ritual portion (<s>karmakāṇḍa</s>) and the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. And because [birth as] stationary beings, dogs, pigs, and the like is observed as the result of non-performance of enjoined acts and performance of prohibited acts. And because the state of a ghost (<s>preta</s>) is observed [as the result] of eating one's own vomit and the like. And no one can know what acts are enjoined or prohibited except through <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, which are distinguished from what is prohibited. The results of <s>karma</s> — such as becoming a ghost, dog, pig, stationary being, and the like — are apprehended through perception and inference for those who fail to perform what is enjoined and who engage in what is prohibited. And no one holds that these are not results of <s>karma</s>. Therefore, just as these maturation-results of <s>karma</s> — ghosts, animals, stationary beings, and the like — [result] from non-performance of the enjoined and engagement in the prohibited, so too the states up to and including <s>Brahmā</s> should be understood as results of <s>karma</s>-maturation among the elevated [states]. Therefore, [passages like] 'He cut out the omentum from himself' and 'He wept' are not mere fictitious laudatory passages (<s>abhūtārthavāda</s>). [Objection:] Let it be that even those [creation passages] are not fictitious laudatory passages. [Response:] Let it be so. This does not invalidate our reasoning. Nor is our position thereby vitiated. Nor can [passages like] '<s>Brahmā</s>, the creators of the world' and the rest be said to describe the results of desire-motivated rituals (<s>kāmya karma</s>), since equality with the gods has already been stated as their result. Therefore, the results of obligatory rituals performed with intention (<s>sābhisaṃdhi</s>), as well as [those of] the <s>Sarvamedha</s>, <s>Aśvamedha</s>, and the like, are [attaining] the state of <s>Brahmā</s> and so forth. But for those whose obligatory rituals are performed without intention, for the purpose of self-purification — for those, [the rituals] are for the purpose of the arising of knowledge. Because of the <s>smṛti</s>: 'This body of <s>Brahman</s> is being fashioned.' Because of their being immediately beneficial [for knowledge], the rituals also serve as means to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation) — this is not contradictory. And we shall explain this meaning in the sixth [chapter], at the conclusion of the <s>Janaka</s> narrative. As for the objection 'like poison in curd and the like' — there is no contradiction there, because it is within the scope of perception and inference. But that meaning which is accessible only through scripture — there, in the absence of a [contradicting] statement conveying that meaning, similarity with 'poison in curd' and the like cannot be postulated. Nor is the authoritativeness of <s>śruti</s> postulated in matters contradicted by other means of knowledge — just as [one would not accept] 'fire is cold and moistens.' But when the purpose of the <s>śruti</s> [is established], the other means of knowledge become apparent [rather than the reverse]. Just as 'a firefly is fire' or 'the sky is dirty' — the perception even of children regarding these — when the correctness of another means of knowledge regarding that [same] subject is ascertained, even the ascertained perception of children becomes apparent [i.e. illusory]. Therefore, since the authoritativeness of the <s>Veda</s> is unfailing, when the purpose of a passage [is established], the passage is [understood] accordingly. It is not [a matter of] the cleverness of human intellect. For the sun does not fail to illuminate form because of the cleverness of human intellect. Similarly, Vedic passages do not take on a different meaning [due to human ingenuity]. Therefore, it is established that rituals are not [directly] the means to <s>mokṣa</s>. Hence, this <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> is commenced solely for the purpose of demonstrating that the fruits of <s>karma</s> belong to <s>saṃsāra</s>. Now, next, when <s>Jāratkārava</s> had ceased [questioning], <s>Bhujyu</s> by name, the son of <s>Lahya</s> — <s>Lāhya</s> is his descendant, [hence] <s>Lāhyāyani</s> — questioned. '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said. It has already been stated that the realization of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> [is the topic]; and the <s>Aśvamedha</s> ritual has both the collective (<s>samaṣṭi</s>) and individual (<s>vyaṣṭi</s>) [dimensions] as its fruit, or it may be combined with knowledge, or its [fruit] may be obtained through knowledge alone — it is the highest limit of all rituals. For they remember: 'There is no merit or demerit higher than the <s>Aśvamedha</s> and killing a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' By it, one attains both the collective and individual [dimensions]. Therein, the individual [dimensions] were ascertained as pertaining to the intra-cosmic sphere, being the fruits of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> ritual: 'Death becomes his self, he becomes one of these deities' (BṛUp 1.2.7) — this was stated. And death, characterized by hunger and thirst, the intellectual self — the collective is the first-born <s>Vāyu</s>, the thread (<s>sūtra</s>), truth, <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>. His domain is elaborated — that which constitutes the Self of all, the unity underlying all duality. The inner Self of all beings is the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>), the formless essence on which all the <s>karmas</s> of all beings depend; he who is the ultimate destination, the supreme fruit, of all <s>karmas</s> and of the cognitions connected with <s>karma</s> — how extensive is his domain, how far does his pervasion extend in every direction, completely encompassing [all]? That is to be stated. When that is stated, the entire <s>saṃsāra</s>, the domain of bondage, will have been stated. And for the purpose of demonstrating the extraordinary nature of that vision of the Self in its collective and individual forms, [<s>Bhujyu</s>] narrates a story about himself. And he thinks: 'By this, I shall bewilder the intellect of my opponent.' Among the <s>Madras</s> — <s>Madra</s> being the name of a country — wandering students (<s>carakas</s>), either because of the practice of wandering for the sake of study, or <s>Adhvaryu</s> priests [of the <s>Caraka</s> school] — we wandered about. We came to the house of <s>Patañcala</s> by name, of the <s>Kāpya</s> [family], of the <s>Kapi</s> <s>gotra</s>. He had a daughter who was possessed by a <s>gandharva</s> — seized by some non-human being, a <s>gandharva</s>. Or the <s>gandharva</s> may be determined to be <s>Dhiṣṇya</s> fire, a presiding deity of the ritual, because of possessing distinctive knowledge — for such knowledge is not possible for a mere [non-human] being. We all, surrounding him, asked: 'Who are you?' — 'What is your name? What is your lineage?' He said: 'I am a <s>gandharva</s>, <s>Sudhanvan</s> by name, <s>Āṅgirasa</s> by <s>gotra</s>.'

children.text: START BrhUp 3,3.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.3.2]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- uvāca vai saḥ |
agacchan vai te tad yatrāśvamedhayājino gacchantīti |
kva nv aśvamedhayājino gacchantīti |
dvātriṃśataṃ vai devarathāhnyāny ayaṃ lokaḥ |
taṃ samantaṃ pṛthivī dvistāvat paryeti |
tāṃ samantaṃ pṛthivīṃ dvistāvat samudraḥ paryeti |
tad yāvatī kṣurasya dhārā yāvad vā makṣikāyāḥ pattraṃ tāvān antareṇākāśaḥ tān aindraḥ suparṇo bhūtvā vāyave prāyacchat |
tān vāyur ātmani dhitvā tatrāgamayad yatrāśvamedhayājino 'bhavann iti |
evam iva vai sa vāyum eva praśaśaṃsa tasmād vāyur eva vyaṣṭir vāyuḥ samaṣṭiḥ |
apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda |
tato ha bhujyur lāhyāyanir upararāma || BrhUp_3,3.2 ||
children.translated_text: He [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] said: 'He [the <s>gandharva</s>] indeed said: they went to where the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> go.' 'Where do the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> go?' 'This world extends thirty-two journeys of the sun-god's chariot. The earth surrounds it on all sides, twice as far. The ocean surrounds that earth on all sides, twice as far. Then, between [the two halves of the cosmic egg], there is a space as thin as the edge of a razor or as the wing of a fly. <s>Indra</s>, having become a bird (<s>suparṇa</s>), delivered them to <s>Vāyu</s>. <s>Vāyu</s>, placing them in himself, took them there — to where the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> were.' Thus indeed he praised <s>Vāyu</s>. Therefore, <s>Vāyu</s> alone is the individual (<s>vyaṣṭi</s>); <s>Vāyu</s> is the collective (<s>samaṣṭi</s>). He who knows this conquers repeated death. Thereupon, <s>Bhujyu Lāhyāyani</s> desisted. (BṛUp 3.3.2)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,3.2 sa hovāca yājñavalkya uvāca vai saḥ /
vaiśbdaḥ smaraṇārthaḥ /
uvāca vai sa gandharvastubhyam /
agacchanvai te pārikṣitāstattatra kva? yatra yasminnaśvamedhayājino gacchantīti /
nirṇote praśna āha-kva nu kasminnaśvamedhayājino gacchantīti /
teṣāṃ gativivakṣayā bhuvanakośaparimāṇamāha-dvātriṃśataṃ vai dve adhike triṃśaddvātriṃśataṃ vai devarathāhrayāni deva ādityastasya ratho devarathastasya rathasya gatyāhrā yāvatparicchidyate deśaparimāṇa taddevarathāhrayaṃ taddvātriṃśadguṇitaṃ devarathāhrayāni tāvatparimāṇo 'yaṃ loko lokālokagiriṇā parikṣiptaḥ /
yatra vairājaṃ śarīraṃ yatra ca karmaphalopabhogaḥ prāṇināṃ sa eṣa loka etāvāṃlloko 'taḥ paramalokastaṃ lokaṃ samantaṃ samantato lokavistārāddviguṇaparimāṇavistāreṇa parimāṇena taṃ lokaṃ parikṣiptā paryeti pṛthivī /
tāṃ pṛthivīṃ tathaiva samantaṃ dvistāvaddviguṇena parimāṇena samudraḥ paryeti yaṃ ghanodamācakṣate paurāṇikāḥ /
tatraṇḍakapālayorvivaraparimāṇamucyate /
yena vivareṇa mārgeṇa vahirnirgacchanto vyāpnuvantyaśvamedhayājinaḥ /
tatra yāvatī yāvatparimāṇa kṣurasya dhārāgraṃ yāvadvā saukṣmyeṇa yuktaṃ makṣikāyāḥ patraṃ tāvāṃstāvatparimāṇo 'ntareṇa madhye 'ṇḍakapālayorākāśchidraṃ tenā'kāśenetyetat /
tānpārikṣitānaśvamedhayājinaḥ prāptānidraḥ parameśvaro yo 'śvameve 'gniścitaḥ suparṇo yadviṣayaṃ darśanamuktaṃ tasya prāci diviśara ityādinā suparṇaḥ pakṣī bhūtvā pakṣapucchādyātmakaḥ suparṇo bhūtvā vāyave prāyacchanmūrtatvānnāstyātmano gatistatreti /
tānpārikṣitānvāyurātmani dhitvā sthāpayitvā svātmabhūtānkṛtvā tatra tasminnagamayat /
kva /
yatra pūrve 'tikrāntāḥ pārikṣitā aśvamedhayājino 'bhavanniti /
evamiva vā evameva sa gandharvo vāyumeva praśaśaṃsa pārikṣitānāṃ gatim /
samāptā'khyāyikā /
ākhyāyikānirvṛttaṃ tvarthamākhyāyikāto 'pasutya śrutiḥ svamukhenaivā'caṣṭe 'smabhyam /
yasmādvāyuḥ sthāvarajaṅgamānāṃ bhūtānāmantarātmā bahiśca sa eva tasmādadhyātmādhibhūtādhidaivabhāvena vividhā yāṣṭirvyāptiḥ sa vāyureva /
tathā samaṣṭiḥ kevalena sūtrātmanā vāyureva /
children.translated_text: Similarly, the collective (<s>samaṣṭi</s>), in the form of the thread-self (<s>sūtrātman</s>) alone, is <s>Vāyu</s>.

children.text: evaṃ vāyumātmānaṃ samaṣṭivyaṣṭirūpātmakatvenopagacchati ya evaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: Thus, one who knows <s>Vāyu</s> as the Self, having the nature of both the collective and individual forms — he who knows thus.

children.text: tasya kiṃ phalamityāhi-apa punarmṛtyuṃ jayati sakṛtmṛtvā punanaṃ mriyate /
children.translated_text: What is his fruit? This is stated: he conquers repeated death — having died once, he does not die again.

children.text: tata ātmanaḥ praśnanirṇayādbhujyurlāhyāyanirupararāma //2//
children.translated_text: Thereupon, from the resolution of his own question, <s>Bhujyu Lāhyāyani</s> desisted. // 2 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.3.2:] He, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, said: 'He indeed said' — the word 'indeed' (<s>vai</s>) is for recollection — 'that <s>gandharva</s> said to you: the <s>Pārikṣitas</s> went there — where? — to where the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> go.' The question [being] resolved, he says: 'Where do the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> go?' With the intention of describing their destination, he states the extent of the cosmic sphere: 'Thirty-two' — two more than thirty makes thirty-two — 'journeys of the divine chariot' — the divine one is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), his chariot is the divine chariot; a day's journey (<s>āhnya</s>) is the extent of space measured by the travel of that chariot; thirty-two of those [day-journeys] is the measure of this world, enclosed by the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain. Where the <s>Vairāja</s> body [exists], where beings experience the fruits of <s>karma</s> — that is this world, this much is the world; beyond this is the non-world. That world, on all sides, the earth — with a circumference twice as large as the extent of the world — the earth encircles that world. That earth, similarly, on all sides, the ocean surrounds it with twice the circumference — what the <s>Paurāṇikas</s> (Purāṇic authorities) call the 'dense water' (<s>ghanoda</s>). There, the measurement of the gap between the two halves of the cosmic egg is stated — by which gap, by which path, the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> emerge and pervade [the beyond]. There, 'as much as' — as much in measure as — 'the edge of a razor,' or as is fitting in subtlety, 'the wing of a fly' — that much in measure, between — in the middle of the two halves of the cosmic egg — is the space, the opening. Through that space — those <s>Pārikṣitas</s>, the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, having arrived — <s>Indra</s>, the supreme Lord, who is the fire-altar constructed in the form of a horse — the <s>suparṇa</s> (bird), the vision concerning which was stated [in] 'eastward [facing], the bird of heaven' and so forth — having become a <s>suparṇa</s>, a bird possessing wings, tail, and the rest — delivered them to <s>Vāyu</s>, since being of corporeal form, the Self cannot travel there on its own. <s>Vāyu</s>, placing them in himself, establishing them, making them his own — took them there. Where? To where the earlier <s>Pārikṣitas</s>, who had passed on before, the performers of the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, were. 'Thus indeed' — just so — that <s>gandharva</s> praised <s>Vāyu</s> alone in describing the destination of the <s>Pārikṣitas</s>. The narrative is concluded. But the meaning derived from the narrative — the <s>śruti</s>, withdrawing from the narrative, tells us in its own voice. Since <s>Vāyu</s> is the inner self of all beings, both stationary and moving, and also external — therefore the manifold individual pervasion (<s>vyaṣṭi</s>) in the form of the individual, physical, and cosmic aspects — that is <s>Vāyu</s> alone.

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye tṛtīyādhyāyasya tṛtīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //3//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the commentary on the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>, third chapter. // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,4.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.4.1]

children.text:
atha hainam uṣastaś cākrāyaṇaḥ papraccha |
yājñavalkyeti hovāca -- yat sākṣād aparokṣād brahma ya ātmā sarvāntaras taṃ me vyācakṣveti |
eṣa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ |
yaḥ prāṇena prāṇiti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ |
yo 'pānenāpāniti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ |
yo vyānena vyaniti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ |
ya udānenodaniti sa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ |
eṣa ta ātmā sarvāntaraḥ || BrhUp_3,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> questioned him: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'that <s>Brahman</s> which is directly perceived, not hidden — the Self that is within all — explain that to me.' 'This is your Self that is within all.' 'Which one is within all, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'That which breathes through <s>prāṇa</s> — that is your Self which is within all. That which breathes downward through <s>apāna</s> — that is your Self which is within all. That which pervades through <s>vyāna</s> — that is your Self which is within all. That which rises upward through <s>udāna</s> — that is your Self which is within all. This is your Self which is within all.' (BṛUp 3.4.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,4.1 atha hainamuṣastaścākrāyaṇaḥ papraccha /
puṇyapāpaprayuktairgrahātigrahairgṛhītaḥ punaḥ punargrahātigrahāṃstyajannupādadatsaṃsaratītyuktam /

children.translated_text: All the activities such as breathing and the rest, belonging to the aggregate of effects and instruments, are performed by [that self] — just as [activities are performed] in a wooden puppet.

children.text: nahi cetanāvadanadhiṣṭhatasya dāruyantrasyeva prāṇanādiceṣṭā vidyante /
children.translated_text: For in a wooden puppet not presided over by a conscious [being], activities such as breathing and the rest do not exist.

children.text: tasmādvijñānamayenādhiṣṭhitaṃ vilakṣaṇena dāruyantravatprāṇanādiceṣṭāṃ pratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, [the aggregate], being presided over by the <s>vijñānamaya</s> (the one constituted of consciousness), which is of a different nature [from the aggregate], engages in the activities of breathing and the rest — just like a wooden puppet.

children.text: tasmātso 'sti kāryakaraṇasaṃghātavilakṣaṇo yaściṣṭayati //1//
children.translated_text: Therefore, that [self] exists — distinct from the aggregate of effects and instruments — which causes [the aggregate] to act. // 1 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.4.1: Then <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> questioned him.
[Commentary:] It was stated that one who is seized by the <s>grahas</s> (seizers) and <s>atigrahas</s> (over-seizers) impelled by merit and demerit transmigrates, repeatedly abandoning and taking up [new] <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s>. And the supreme excellence of merit has been explained — having as its domain the differentiated [world], in the form of the aggregate and the individual, [culminating in] the attainment of the self of duality-and-oneness. But does the one who, seized by <s>grahas</s> and <s>atigrahas</s>, transmigrates — does he exist or not? And if he exists, what are his characteristics? — for the discriminative knowledge of the self itself, the <s>Uṣasta</s>-questioning is commenced.
And from the attainment of his essential nature, which is free from limiting adjuncts and whose nature is free from action and agency, one is liberated from the bondage described above, together with its impelling cause.
The connection with the narrative is well known. Then <s>Uṣasta</s> by name, the offspring of <s>Cakra</s>, hence <s>Cākrāyaṇa</s>, questioned him — the previously introduced <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
[<s>Uṣasta</s> asked:] 'That which is <s>Brahman</s> — directly, without intermediary, not mediated by anything, immediate to the seer, non-figurative — not like "hearing is <s>Brahman</s>" and the like — what is that? It is the self (<s>ātman</s>).' By the word 'self,' the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>) is denoted, because the word 'self' is well known [in that sense]. The innermost of all (<s>sarvāntara</s>) — that which, through the words 'which' and 'who,' is the well-known self, is <s>Brahman</s>. 'Explain that self to me' — the meaning is: 'clearly, as one shows a cow by grasping its horns, so point it out — tell me "this is that."'
Thus addressed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied: 'This is your self, the innermost of all (<s>sarvāntara</s>), the innermost of everything.' The phrase 'innermost of all' is for apprehending all qualifications. That which is <s>Brahman</s> — directly, without intermediary, immediate, non-figurative, the greatest, the self, the innermost of everything — qualified by all these attributes together, this is it.
'Who is that, your self?' That which is this aggregate of effects and instruments that is yours — by which self you are a possessor of a self — this is your self. The meaning is: of your aggregate of effects and instruments.
Therein — within the gross body, the subtle body (<s>liṅgātman</s>), and thirdly the aggregate of instruments — and that about which there is doubt — among these, 'which is my self, the innermost, that you intend to speak of?' — when thus asked, the other said: 'That which, by means of <s>prāṇa</s> — the breath moving through the mouth and nostrils — breathes, performs the activity of breathing — by which <s>prāṇa</s> is impelled, that is the meaning.' That is the self of your aggregate of effects and instruments, constituted of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>). The rest is the same [as before]. 'That which breathes downward by <s>apāna</s>.' 'That which pervades by <s>vyāna</s>' — the lengthened [vowel] form is Vedic.

children.translated_text: <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> said: 'Just as one might say "that is a cow, that is a horse" — in the same way, what you have indicated [is merely an indication]. That which is <s>Brahman</s> directly, without intermediary — which is the self, the innermost of all — explain that to me.' 'This is your self, the innermost of all.' 'Which one, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, is the innermost of all?' 'You cannot see the seer of seeing. You cannot hear the hearer of hearing. You cannot think the thinker of thinking. You cannot know the knower of knowing. This is your self, the innermost of all. Everything other than this is afflicted.' Thereupon <s>Uṣasta Cākrāyaṇa</s> fell silent. // BṛhUp 3.4.2 //
