children.text:
athainam uddālaka āruṇiḥ papraccha -- yājñavalkyeti hovāca |
madreṣv avasāma patañcalasya kāpyasya gṛheṣu yajñam adhīyānāḥ |
tasyāsīd bhāryā gandharvagṛhītā |
tam apṛcchāma -- ko 'sīti |
so 'bravīt kabandha ātharvaṇa iti |
so 'bravīt patañcalaṃ kāpyaṃ yājñikāṃś ca -- vettha nu tvaṃ kāpya tat sūtraṃ yasminn ayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavantīti |
so 'bravīt patañcalaḥ kāpyo nāhaṃ tad bhagavan vedeti |
so 'bravīt patañcalaṃ kāpyaṃ yājñikāṃś ca |
vettha nu tvaṃ kāpya tam antaryāmiṇaṃ ya imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāny antaro yamayati |
so 'bravīt patañcalaḥ kāpyo nāhaṃ taṃ bhagavan vedeti |
so 'bravīt patañcalaṃ kāpyaṃ yājñikāṃś ca |
yo vai tat kāpya sūtraṃ vidyāt taṃ cāntaryāmiṇam iti sa brahmavit sa lokavit sa devavit sa vedavit sa ātmavit sa sarvavit |
iti tebhyo 'bravīt |
tad ahaṃ veda |
tac cet tvaṃ yājñavalkya sūtram avidvāṃs taṃ cāntaryāmiṇaṃ brahmagavīr udajase mūrdhā te vipatiṣyati |
veda vā ahaṃ gautama tat sūtraṃ taṃ cāntaryāmiṇam iti |
yo vā idaṃ kaśca brūyād veda vedeti yathā vettha tathā brūhīti || BrhUp_3,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> questioned him: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said, 'we dwelt among the <s>Madras</s>, in the house of <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s>, studying the sacrifice. His wife was possessed by a <s>Gandharva</s>. We asked him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am <s>Kabandha Ātharvaṇa</s>." He said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and the ritualists: "Do you know, <s>Kāpya</s>, that thread by which this world and the other world and all beings are strung together?" <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> said: "I do not know that, sir." He said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and the ritualists: "Do you know, <s>Kāpya</s>, that inner controller who controls this world and the other world and all beings from within?" <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> said: "I do not know him, sir." He said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and the ritualists: "He who, <s>Kāpya</s>, knows that thread and that inner controller — he is a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, a knower of the worlds, a knower of the gods, a knower of the <s>Vedas</s>, a knower of the Self, a knower of all." Thus he told them. 'I know that. If you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, drive away the cows of [those who know] <s>Brahman</s> without knowing that thread and that inner controller, your head will fall off.' '<s>Gautama</s>, I know that thread and that inner controller.' 'Anyone might say "I know, I know." Tell us what you know.' (BṛUp 3.7.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,7.1 atha hainamuddālako nāmataḥ, aruṇasyāpatyamāruṇiḥ papraccha;yājñavalkyeti hovāca;madreṣu deśeṣvavasāmoṣitavantaḥ, patañcalasya-patañcalo nāmatastasyaiva kapigotrasya kāpyasya gṛheṣu yajñamadhīyānā yaśaśāstrādhyayanaṃ kurvāṇāḥ /
tasyāsīd bhāryā gandharvagṛhītā;tamapṛcchāma-ko 'sīti;so 'bravīt kabandho nāmataḥ, atharvaṇo 'patyamātharvaṇa iti /
so 'bravīd gāndharvaḥ patañcalaṃ kāpyaṃ yājñikāṃśca tacchipyān-vettha nu tvaṃ he kāpya jānīṣe tat sūtram? kiṃ tat? yena sūtreṇāyaṃ ca leka idaṃ ca janma, paraśca lokaḥ paraṃ ca pratipattavyaṃ janma, sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni brahmādistambaparyantāni, sandṛbdhāni saṅgrathitāni sragiva sūtreṇa viṣṭabdhāni bhavanti yena-tat kiṃ sūtraṃ vettha? so 'bravīdevaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ kāpyaḥ-nāhaṃ tad bhagavan vedeti, tat sūtraṃ nāhaṃ jāne he bhagavanniti sampūjayannāha /
so 'bravīt punargandharva upādhyāyamasmāṃśca-vettha na tvaṃ kāpya tamantaryāmiṇam? antaryāmīti viśeṣyate-ya imaṃ ca lokaṃ paraṃ ca lokaṃ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni yo 'ntarābhyantaraḥ san yamayati niyamayati, dāruyantramiva brāmayati, svaṃ svamucitavyāpāraṃ kārayatīti /
so 'bravīdevamuktaḥ patañcalaḥ kāpyaḥ-nāhaṃ taṃ jāne bhagavanniti sampūjayannāha /
so 'bravīt punargandharvaḥ;sūtratadantargatāntaryāmiṇorvijñānaṃ stūyate-yaḥ kaścid vai tat sūtraṃ he kāpya bavidyād vijānīyāt taṃ cāntaryāmiṇaṃ sūtrāntargataṃ tasyaiva sūtrasya niyantāraṃ vidyāt yaḥ-ityevamuktena prakāreṇa, sa hi brahmavita paramātmavit sa lokāṃśca bhūrādīnantaryāmiṇā niyamyamānāṃllokān vetti, sa devāṃścāgnyādīṃllokino jānāti, vedāṃśca sarvapramāṇabhūtān vetti, bhūtāni ca brahmādīni sūtreṇa dhiyamāṇāni tadantargatenāntaryāmiṇā niyamyamānāni vetti, sa ātmānaṃ ca kartṛtvabhoktṛtvaviśiṣṭaṃ tenaivāntaryāmiṇā niyamyamānaṃ vetti, sarvaṃ ca jagata tathābhūtaṃ vettīti /

evaṃ stute sūtrāntaryāmivijñāne pralubdhaḥ kāpyo 'bhimukhībhūtaḥ, vayaṃ ca;tebhyaścāsmabhyamabhimukhībhūtebhyobravīd gandharvaḥ sūtramantaryāmiṇaṃ ca;tadahaṃ sūtrānitaryāmivijñānaṃ veda gandharvāllabdhāgamaḥ san /
children.translated_text: When the knowledge of the thread and inner controller was thus praised, <s>Kāpya</s>, being enticed, became attentive — and so did we. And to us who had become attentive, the <s>Gandharva</s> told [about] the thread and the inner controller. 'I, thus endowed with the knowledge obtained from the <s>Gandharva</s>, having received the teaching from the <s>Gandharva</s>, know [about] the thread and inner controller.'

children.text: tacced yājñavalkya sūtraṃ taṃ cāntaryāmiṇamavidvāṃścebrahmavit san yadi brahmagavīrudajatase brahmavidāṃ svabhūtā gā udajase unnayasi tvam anyāyena, tato macchāpadagdhasya mūrdhā śiraste tava vispaṣṭaṃ ṣatiṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'If, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, without knowing that thread and that inner controller — if, being a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, you drive away the cows that belong to the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, you drive them away wrongfully — then your head, cursed by me, will surely fall off.'

children.text: evamukto yājñavalkya āhaveda jānāmyahaṃ he gautameti gotrataḥ, tat sūtraṃ yad gandharvastubhyamuktavān yaṃ cāntaryāmiṇaṃ gandharvād viditavanto yūyam, taṃ cāntaryāmiṇaṃ vedāhamiti /
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'I know — I understand, O <s>Gautama</s>' — addressing him by his <s>gotra</s> — 'that thread which the <s>Gandharva</s> told you about, and that inner controller which you learned about from the <s>Gandharva</s> — I know that inner controller.'

children.text: evamukto pratyāha gautamaḥ-yaḥ kaścit prākṛta idaṃ yattavayoktaṃ brūyāt-katham? veda vedeti-ātmānaṃ ślāghayan, kiṃ tena garjitena kāryeṇa darśaya;yathā vetya tathā brūhīti //1//
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, <s>Gautama</s> replied: 'Any ordinary person might say what you have said — "I know, I know" — boasting about himself. What is the point of mere thundering? Demonstrate it! Tell us as you know it.' // 1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.7.1:] Then <s>Uddālaka</s> by name, the son of <s>Aruṇa</s>, hence <s>Āruṇi</s>, questioned him. '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' he said. 'Among the <s>Madras</s>' — in those countries — 'we dwelt,' meaning we resided — 'in the house of <s>Patañcala</s>' — <s>Patañcala</s> by name, of the <s>Kapi</s> <s>gotra</s>, hence <s>Kāpya</s> — 'studying the sacrifice' — engaged in the study of ritual texts. 'His wife was possessed by a <s>Gandharva</s>. We asked him: "Who are you?" He said: "<s>Kabandha</s> by name, the descendant of <s>Atharvan</s>, hence <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>."' The <s>Gandharva</s> said to <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s> and the ritualists, his students: 'Do you know, O <s>Kāpya</s> — do you understand — that thread (<s>sūtra</s>)? What is that? That thread by which this world — this present birth — and the other world — the birth yet to be attained — and all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — are strung together, tied together, supported like a garland by a thread — do you know that thread?' He, <s>Kāpya</s>, thus asked, said: 'I do not know that, sir' — 'I do not know that thread, O venerable one' — he said, honoring [the <s>Gandharva</s>]. He said again — the <s>Gandharva</s> [said] to the teacher and to us: 'Do you know, <s>Kāpya</s>, that inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>)?' The inner controller is further specified: 'who, being within, internal, controls — regulates — this world and the other world and all beings; who makes them revolve like a wooden machine, causing each to perform its proper function.' He, <s>Patañcala Kāpya</s>, thus addressed, said: 'I do not know him, sir' — he said, honoring [the <s>Gandharva</s>]. He said again — the <s>Gandharva</s> [said]; the knowledge of the thread and of the inner controller contained within it is praised: 'Whoever indeed, O <s>Kāpya</s>, knows — understands — that thread, and knows that inner controller contained within that very thread, its ruler' — in the manner thus stated — 'he is a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, a knower of the supreme Self; he knows the worlds — <s>Bhūḥ</s> and the rest — controlled by the inner controller; he knows the gods — <s>Agni</s> and the rest, the lords of the worlds; he knows the <s>Vedas</s>, the source of all valid knowledge; he knows the beings from <s>Brahmā</s> onwards, held by the thread, regulated by the inner controller contained within it; he knows the Self — [the individual self] characterized by being an agent and enjoyer, itself also regulated by that very inner controller; and he knows everything, the entire world as being thus constituted.'

children.text: START BrhUp 3,7.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.7.2]

children.text:
sa hovaca -- vāyur vai gautama tat sūtram |
vāyunā vai gautama sūtreṇāyaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni saṃdṛbdhāni bhavanti |
tasmād vai gautama puruṣaṃ pretam āhur vyasraṃsiṣatāsyāṅgānīti |
vāyunā hi gautama sūtreṇa samdṛbdhāni bhavantīti |
evam evaitad yājñavalkya |
antaryāmiṇaṃ brūhīti || BrhUp_3,7.2 ||
children.translated_text: He [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] said: 'Wind (<s>Vāyu</s>), <s>Gautama</s>, is that thread. By wind as thread, <s>Gautama</s>, this world and the other world and all beings are strung together. Therefore, <s>Gautama</s>, they say of a dead person that his limbs have become unstrung. For by wind as thread, <s>Gautama</s>, they are strung together.' 'Just so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. Now tell of the inner controller.' (BṛUp 3.7.2)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,7.2 sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ /

brahmalokā yasminnotāśca protāśca vartamānekāle, yathā pṛthivyapsu, tat sūtram āgamagamyaṃ vattavyamiti tadarthaṃ praśnāntaramutthāpitam;atastannirṇayāyāha-vāyurvai gautama tat sūtram, nānyat;vāyuriti sūkṣmamākāśavadviṣṭambhakaṃ pṛthivyādīnām, yadātmakaṃ saptadaśavidhaṃ liṅgaṃ karmavāsanāsamavāyi prāṇinām, yattat samaṣṭivyaṣṭyātmakam, yasya bāhyā medāḥ saptasapta marudraṇāḥ samudrasyevormayaḥ, tadetad vāyavyaṃ tattvaṃ sūtrāmityabhidhīyate /
children.translated_text: The worlds of <s>Brahman</s> — that in which they are woven, warp and woof, at the present time — just as the earth [is woven] in water — that thread, accessible through scripture, is to be stated. For that purpose, a different question was raised. Hence, for its resolution, he says: '<s>Vāyu</s> (wind), <s>Gautama</s>, is that thread' — and nothing else. '<s>Vāyu</s>' — the subtle [entity], which supports [all things] like space, the earth and the rest — whose nature constitutes the seventeen-fold subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) conjoined with the residual impressions of <s>karma</s> (<s>karmavāsanā</s>) belonging to living beings — which is of the nature of both the collective (<s>samaṣṭi</s>) and the individual (<s>vyaṣṭi</s>) — whose external [manifestations] are the seven times seven winds, like waves of the ocean — this <s>Vāyu</s>-principle is called the thread (<s>sūtrātman</s>).

children.text: vāyunā vai gautama sūtreṇāyaṃ ca lokaḥ paraśca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni sandṛbdhāni bhavanti saṅprathitāni bhavantīti prasiddhametat /
children.translated_text: 'By wind as thread, <s>Gautama</s>, this world and the other world and all beings are strung together, are tied together' — this is well-known.

children.text: asti ca loke prasiddhiḥ, katham? yasmād vāyuḥ sūtram, vāyunā vidhṛtaṃ sarvam, tasmād vai gautama puruṣaṃ pretamāhuḥ kathayanti - vyasraṃsipata visrastānyasyapuruṣasyāṅgānīti;sūtrāpagame hi maṇyādīnāṃ protāni yad yasyāṅgāni syustato yuktametad vāyvapagame 'vasraṃsanamaṅgānām ato vāyunā hi gautama sūtreṇa sandṛbdhāni bhavantīti nigamayati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And there is a well-known [illustration] in the world. How? Since <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is the thread (<s>sūtra</s>), and everything is held together by <s>Vāyu</s> — therefore, O <s>Gautama</s>, they say, they narrate, of a dead person: 'His limbs have fallen apart, the limbs of this person have become disjoined.' For just as, when the thread is removed, the beads and the like that were strung [on it] — whichever limbs belong to whichever [person] — from that, it is appropriate that when <s>Vāyu</s> departs, the limbs fall apart. Therefore, he concludes: 'It is by <s>Vāyu</s> indeed, O <s>Gautama</s>, as the thread, that they are strung together.'

children.text: evamevaitad yājñavalkya samyaguktaṃ sūtram;tadantargataṃ tvidānīṃ tasyaiva sūtrasya niyantāramantaryāmiṇaṃ brūhītyukta āha //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, you have rightly explained the thread (<s>sūtra</s>). But now tell me of the controller, the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), who is within that very thread' — thus asked, he [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] replied. || 2 ||
[Commentary on BṛUp 3.7.2:] He, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, said.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,7.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.7.3]

children.text: yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan pṛthivyā antaro yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yasya pṛthivī śarīraṃ yaḥ pṛthivīm antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.3 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the earth, is within the earth, whom the earth does not know, whose body is the earth, who controls the earth from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.3 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,7.3 yaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhan bhavati, so 'ntaryāmī, sarvaḥ pṛthivyāṃ tiṣṭhatīti sarvatra prasaṅgo mā bhūditi viśinaṣṭi - pṛthivyā antaro 'bhyantaraḥ /
tatraitat syāt pṛthivīdevataiva antaryāmītyata āha - yamantaryāmiṇaṃ pṛthivī devatāpi na veda mayyanyaḥ kaścidvartata iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here the [objection] might arise: it is the deity of the earth itself that is the inner controller. Therefore [the text] says: 'whom the inner controller — even the deity of the earth does not know' — [thinking] 'there is someone else within me.'

children.text: yasya pṛthivī śarīram-yasya ca pṛthivyeva śarīram, nānyat-pṛthivīdevatāyā yaccharīram, tadeva śarīraṃ yasya, śarīragrahaṇaṃ copalakṣaṇārtham, karaṇaṃ ca pṛthivyāḥ, tasya svakarmaprayuktaṃ hi kāryaṃ ca pṛthivīdevatāyāḥ, tadasya svakarmābhāvādantaryāmiṇo nityamuktatvāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Whose body is the earth' — for whom the earth itself is the body, and nothing else. That which is the body of the deity of the earth — that very [body] is the body of this [inner controller]. And the mention of 'body' is by way of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>) — [it includes] the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of the earth as well. For the effect and instrument of the earth-deity are impelled by that [deity's] own <s>karma</s>; but for this inner controller, [there is] no <s>karma</s> of his own, because the inner controller is eternally liberated.

children.text: parārthakartavyatāsvabhāvatvāt parasya yat kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca tadevāsya, na svataḥ, tadāha-yasya pṛthivī śarīramiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the nature [of effects and instruments] is to serve the purpose of another — the effect and instrument of the other [deity] are his [the inner controller's] [as well], not inherently his own. This is what [the text] says: 'whose body is the earth.'

children.text: devatākāryakaraṇasyeśvarasākṣimātrasānnidhyena hi niyamenapravṛttinivṛttī syātām;ya īdṛgīśvaro nārāyaṇākhyaḥ, pṛthirvī pṛthivīdevatām, yamayati niyamayati svavyāpāre, antaro 'bhyantarastiṣṭhan, eṣa ta ātmā, te tava, mama ca sarvabhūtānāṃ cetyupalakṣaṇārthametat;antaryāmī yastvayāpṛṣṭaḥ, amṛtaḥ sarvasaṃsāradharmavarjita ityetat //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For by the mere witnessing presence of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), the effects and instruments of the deity would operate or cease to operate in a regulated manner. He who is such a Lord, called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, controls, regulates the earth — [that is,] the earth-deity — in her own activity, dwelling within her, as an interior [presence]. 'He is your self' — 'your' means yours, and mine, and of all beings — this is by way of indication. [He is] the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) about whom you asked; [he is] immortal (<s>amṛta</s>) — devoid of all the attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>. || 3 ||

[Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.3:] He who dwells in the earth — he is the inner controller. [But] since everyone dwells in the earth, lest there be the contingency [of applying this] to all, [the text] distinguishes: '[He who is] within the earth' — interior to it.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,7.4-14
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.7.4-14]

children.text: yo 'psu tiṣṭhann adbhyo 'ntaro yam āpo na vidur yasyāpaḥ śarīraṃ yo 'po 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.4 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the waters, is within the waters, whom the waters do not know, whose body is the waters, who controls the waters from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.4 ||

children.text: yo 'gnau tiṣṭhann agner antaro yam agnir na veda yasyāgniḥ śarīraṃ yo 'gnim antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.5 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in fire, is within fire, whom fire does not know, whose body is fire, who controls fire from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.5 ||

children.text: yo 'ntarikṣe tiṣṭhann antarikṣād antaro yam antarikṣaṃ na veda yasyāntarikṣaṃ śarīraṃ yo 'ntarikṣam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.6 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the atmosphere, is within the atmosphere, whom the atmosphere does not know, whose body is the atmosphere, who controls the atmosphere from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.6 ||

children.text: yo vāyau tiṣṭhan vāyor antaro yaṃ vāyur na veda yasya vāyuḥ śarīraṃ yo vāyum antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.7 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the wind, is within the wind, whom the wind does not know, whose body is the wind, who controls the wind from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.7 ||

children.text: yo divi tiṣṭhan divo 'ntaro yaṃ dyaur na veda yasya dyauḥ śarīraṃ yo divam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.8 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in heaven, is within heaven, whom heaven does not know, whose body is heaven, who controls heaven from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.8 ||

children.text: ya āditye tiṣṭhann ādityād antaro yam ādityo na veda yasyādityaḥ śarīraṃ ya ādityam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.9 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the sun, is within the sun, whom the sun does not know, whose body is the sun, who controls the sun from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.9 ||

children.text: yo dikṣu tiṣṭhan digbhyo 'ntaro yaṃ diśo na vidur yasya diśaḥ śarīraṃ yo diśo 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.10 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the directions, is within the directions, whom the directions do not know, whose body is the directions, who controls the directions from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.10 ||

children.text: yaś candratārake tiṣṭhañ candratārakād antaro yaṃ candratārakaṃ na veda yasya candratārakaṃ śarīraṃ yaś candratārakam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.11 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the moon and stars, is within the moon and stars, whom the moon and stars do not know, whose body is the moon and stars, who controls the moon and stars from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.11 ||

children.text: ya ākāśe tiṣṭhann ākāśād antaro yam ākāśo na veda yasyākāśaḥ śarīraṃ ya ākāśam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.12 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in space (<s>ākāśa</s>), is within space, whom space does not know, whose body is space, who controls space from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.12 ||

children.text: yas tamasi tiṣṭhaṃs tamaso 'ntaro yaṃ tamo na veda yasya tamaḥ śarīraṃ yas tamo 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.13 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in darkness, is within darkness, whom darkness does not know, whose body is darkness, who controls darkness from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.13 ||

children.text: yas tejasi tiṣṭhaṃs tejaso 'ntaro yaṃ tejo na veda yasya tejaḥ śarīraṃ yas tejo 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.14 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in light, is within light, whom light does not know, whose body is light, who controls light from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.14 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,7.4-14 samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.4-14:] The rest is the same [as the commentary on 3.7.3].

children.text: yo 'psu tiṣṭhan-agnau, antarikṣe, vāyau, divi, āditye, yastamasyāvaraṇātmake bāhye tamasi, tejasi tadviparīte prakāśasāmānye ityevamadhidaivatam antaryāmiviṣayaṃ darśanaṃ devatāsu /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'He who dwells in the waters' — in fire, in the atmosphere, in the wind, in heaven, in the sun; 'he who [dwells] in darkness' — in external darkness that has the nature of covering; 'in light' — in its opposite, the general [category of] luminosity. Thus, the vision (<s>darśana</s>) pertaining to the cosmic level (<s>adhidaivata</s>) — the inner controller with respect to the deities — [has been stated].

children.text: athādhibhūtaṃ bhūteṣu brahmadistambaparyanteṣu antaryāmidaśanamadhibhūtam // 4 -14 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now the physical level (<s>adhibhūta</s>) — the vision of the inner controller with respect to beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — [this is] the physical [level]. || 4-14 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,7.15-23
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.7.15-23]

children.text:
athādhibhūtam |
yaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhan sarvebhyo bhūtebhyo 'ntaro yaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni na vidur yasya sarvāṇi bhutāni śarīraṃ yaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāny antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ |
ity adhibhūtam || BrhUp_3,7.15 ||
children.translated_text:
Now the physical level (<s>adhibhūta</s>):
He who, dwelling in all beings, is within all beings, whom all beings do not know, whose body is all beings, who controls all beings from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal.
Thus the physical level. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.15 ||

children.text: athādhyātmam | yaḥ prāṇe tiṣṭhan prāṇād antaro yaṃ prāṇo na veda yasya prāṇaḥ śarīraṃ yaḥ prāṇam antaro yamayati eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.16 ||
children.translated_text:
Now the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>):
He who, dwelling in <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), is within <s>prāṇa</s>, whom <s>prāṇa</s> does not know, whose body is <s>prāṇa</s>, who controls <s>prāṇa</s> from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.16 ||

children.text: yo vāci tiṣṭhan vāco 'ntaro yaṃ vāṅ na veda yasya vāk śarīraṃ yo vācam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.17 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in speech, is within speech, whom speech does not know, whose body is speech, who controls speech from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.17 ||

children.text: yaś cakṣuṣi tiṣṭhañ cakṣuṣo 'ntaro yaṃ cakṣur na veda yasya cakṣuḥ śarīraṃ yaś cakṣur antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.18 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the eye, is within the eye, whom the eye does not know, whose body is the eye, who controls the eye from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.18 ||

children.text: yaḥ śrotre tiṣṭhañ chrotrād antaro yaṃ śrotraṃ na veda yasya śrotraṃ śarīraṃ yaḥ śrotram antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.19 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the ear, is within the ear, whom the ear does not know, whose body is the ear, who controls the ear from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.19 ||

children.text: yo manasi tiṣṭhan manaso 'ntaro yaṃ mano na veda yasya manaḥ śarīraṃ yo mano 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.20 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the mind, is within the mind, whom the mind does not know, whose body is the mind, who controls the mind from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.20 ||

children.text: yas tvaci tiṣṭhaṃs tvaco 'ntaro yaṃ tvaṅ na veda yasya tvak śarīraṃ yas tvacam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.21 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the skin, is within the skin, whom the skin does not know, whose body is the skin, who controls the skin from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.21 ||

children.text: yo vijñāne tiṣṭhan vijñānād antaro yaṃ vijñānaṃ na veda yasya vijñānaṃ śarīraṃ yo vijñānam antaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ || BrhUp_3,7.22 ||
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in <s>vijñāna</s> (understanding), is within <s>vijñāna</s>, whom <s>vijñāna</s> does not know, whose body is <s>vijñāna</s>, who controls <s>vijñāna</s> from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.22 ||

children.text:
yo retasi tiṣṭhaṃ retaso 'ntaro yaṃ reto na veda yasya retaḥ śarīraṃ yo reto 'ntaro yamayaty eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ |
adṛṣṭo draṣṭāśrutaḥ śrotāmato mantāvijñato vijñātā |
nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā nānyo 'to 'sti śrotā nānyo 'to 'sti mantā nānyo 'to 'sti vijñātā |
eṣa ta ātmāntaryāmy amṛtaḥ |
ato 'nyad ārtam |
tato hoddālaka āruṇir upararāma || BrhUp_3,7.23 ||
children.translated_text:
He who, dwelling in semen, is within semen, whom semen does not know, whose body is semen, who controls semen from within — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal.
Unseen, he is the seer; unheard, he is the hearer; unthought, he is the thinker; unknown, he is the knower.
There is no other seer than he; there is no other hearer than he; there is no other thinker than he; there is no other knower than he.
He is your self, the inner controller, the immortal.
What is other than him is afflicted.
Thereupon, <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> desisted. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.23 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,7,15-23 athādhyātmam-yaḥ prāṇe prāṇavāyusahite ghrāṇe, yo vāci, cakṣuṣi, śrotre, manasi, tvaci, vijñāne, budvau, retasi prajanane /
kasmāt punaḥ kāraṇāt pṛthivyādidevatā mahābhāgāḥ satyo manuṣyādivadātamani tiṣṭhantamātmano niyantāramantaryāmiṇaṃ na vidurityata āha-adṛṣṭenad daṣṭo na viṣayībhūtaḥ cakṣurdarśanasya kasyacit, svayaṃ tu cakṣuṣi sannihitatvādd daśisvarūpa iti draṣṭā /
tathāśrutaḥ śrotragocaratvamanāpannaḥ kasyacit, svayaṃ tvaluptaśravaṇaśaktiḥ sarvaśrotreṣu sannihitatvāchracotā /
tathāmato manaḥsaṅkalpaviṣayatāmanāpannaḥ;dṛṣṭaśrute eva hi sarvaḥ saṅkalpayati;uddṛṣṭatvādakṣutatvādevāmataḥ;allaptamananaśaktitvāt sarvamanaḥsu sannihitatvācca mantā /
tathāvijñāto niścayagocaratāmanāpannorūpādivat lasukhādivadvā, svayaṃ tvaluptavijñānaśaktitvāttatsannidhānācca vijñātā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, 'unknown' — not having come within the range of determinate cognition, like form and the like, or like pleasure and the like — yet he himself, because his power of knowing is undiminished and because of his presence [in all <s>vijñāna</s>], is the knower.

children.text: tatra yaṃ pṛthivī na veda yaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni na viduriti cānye niyantavyā vijñātāro 'nyo niyantā antaryāmīti prāptam, tadanyatvāśaṅkānivṛttyarthamucyate - nānyo 'taḥ, nānyaḥ ato 'smādantaryāmiṇo nānyo 'sti draṣṭā, tathā nānyo 'to 'sti mantā, nānyo 'to 'sti śrotā, nānyo 'to 'sti mantā, nānyo 'to 'sti vijñātā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein — since [the text] says 'whom the earth does not know' and 'whom all beings do not know' — the [conclusion] might be arrived at that those to be controlled, the knowers, are different [from the controller], and the controller, the inner controller, is a different [entity]. To dispel that suspicion of difference, [the text] says: 'There is no other than he (<s>nānyo 'taḥ</s>)' — there is no other than this inner controller who is a seer; similarly, 'there is no other than he who is a thinker,' 'there is no other than he who is a hearer,' 'there is no other than he who is a thinker,' 'there is no other than he who is a knower.'

children.text: yasmāt paro nāsti draṣṭā śrotā mantā vijñātā, yo 'dṛṣṭo draṣṭā, aśrutaḥ śrotā, amato mantā, avijñāto vijñātā, amṛtaḥ sarvasaṃsāradharmavarjitaḥ sarvasaṃsāriṇāṃ karmaphalavibhāgakartā - eṣa te ātmāntaryāmyamṛtaḥ asmādīśvarādātmano 'nyadārtam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since there is no seer, hearer, thinker, or knower other [than him] — he who is the unseen seer, the unheard hearer, the unthought thinker, the unknown knower — the immortal (<s>amṛta</s>), devoid of all the attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the apportioner of the fruits of <s>karma</s> for all transmigrating beings — he is your self, the inner controller, the immortal. What is other than this Lord, this self — that is afflicted (<s>ārta</s>).

children.text: tato hi uddālaka āruṇirupararāma //15//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thereupon <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> desisted [from further questioning]. || 15 ||

[Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.7.15-23:] Now the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>) — 'he who [dwells] in <s>prāṇa</s>' — in the organ of smell together with the <s>prāṇa</s> breath; 'in speech,' 'in the eye,' 'in the ear,' 'in the mind,' 'in the skin,' 'in <s>vijñāna</s>' — in the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>); 'in semen' — in the reproductive organ.
But for what reason do the earth and other deities, being great and exalted, not know the inner controller who dwells within them, as [even] humans and the like [do not]? To this he says: 'Unseen' — not having become the object of anyone's visual perception — he is himself the seer, because of his nature as seeing, since he is present in every eye.
Similarly, 'unheard' — not having come within the range of anyone's auditory perception — he is himself the hearer, because his power of hearing is undiminished and because he is present in every ear.
Similarly, 'unthought' — not having come within the range of mental conception; for everyone conceives only what has been seen and heard; being unseen and unheard, he is necessarily unthought; yet because his power of thinking is undiminished and because he is present in every mind, he is the thinker.

children.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāye saptamamantaryāmibrāhmaṇam //7//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh, the Inner Controller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of the third <s>Adhyāya</s>. || 7 ||

children.text: ataḥ paramaśanāyādivinirmuktaṃ nirupādhikaṃ sākṣādaparokṣāt sarvāntaraṃ brahma vaktavyamityata ārambhaḥ -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Henceforth, <s>Brahman</s> itself — free from hunger and the like, without limiting adjuncts (<s>nirupādhika</s>), directly and immediately perceived, innermost of all — must be stated. Therefore, [the next section] is commenced —

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.8.1]

children.text:
atha ha vācaknavy uvāca -- brāhmaṇā bhagavanto hantāham imaṃ dvau praśnau prakṣyāmi |
tau cen me vivakṣyati |
na vai jātu yuṣmākam imaṃ kaścid brahmodyaṃ jeteti |
pṛccha gārgīti || BrhUp_3,8.1 ||
children.translated_text:
Then <s>Vācaknavī</s> (<s>Gārgī</s>) said: 'Venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, I shall now ask this one two questions.
If he answers them for me,
then none of you will ever defeat him in the <s>brahmodya</s> (theological debate).'
'Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>.' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.1 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.1 atha ha vācaknavyuvāca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.1:] Then <s>Vācaknavī</s> said.

children.text: sarvaṃ yājñavalkyena niṣiddhā mūrdhapātabhayāduparatā satī punaḥ praṣṭuṃ brāhmaṇānujñāṃ prārthayate - he brāhmaṇā bhagavantaḥ pūjāvantaḥ śṛṇuta mama vacaḥ;hantāhamimaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ punardvai praśnau prakṣyāmi, yadyanumatirbhavatāmasti;tau praśnau cedyadi vakṣyati kathayiṣyati me, kathañcinna vai jātu kadācid yuṣmākaṃ madhye imaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ kaścid brahmodyaṃ brahmavadanaṃ prati jetā na vai kaścid bhavediti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having been completely silenced by <s>Yājñavalkya</s> [previously, with the threat of] her head falling off, having desisted, she now, seeking the permission of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> to question again, says: 'O venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, worthy of respect, hear my words. I shall now question this <s>Yājñavalkya</s> again with two questions, if your permission is given. If he answers those two questions — if he will tell, will explain them to me — then certainly no one among you will ever defeat this <s>Yājñavalkya</s> in the <s>brahmodya</s> (theological debate), in speaking about <s>Brahman</s> — no one would be a victor.'

children.text: evamuktā brāhmaṇā anujñāṃ pradaduḥ - pṛccha gārgīti //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus addressed, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> gave their permission: 'Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>.' || 1 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 3.8.2]

children.text:
sā hovāca -- ahaṃ vai tvā yājñavalkya yathā kāśyo vā vaideho vograputra ujjyaṃ dhanur adhijyaṃ kṛtvā dvau bāṇavantau sapatnātivyādhinau haste kṛtvopottiṣṭhed evam evāhaṃ tvā dvābhyāṃ praśnābhyām upodasthām |
tau me brūhīti |
pṛccha gārgīti || BrhUp_3,8.2 ||
children.translated_text:
She said: 'I rise against you, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, with two questions, as a warrior of <s>Kāśī</s> or <s>Videha</s>, son of a hero, would rise, having strung his unstrung bow and taken in hand two piercing arrows aimed at the enemy. Answer them for me.'
'Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>.' || <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.2 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.2 labdhānujñā ha yājñavalkyaṃ sā hovāca - ahaṃ vai tvā tvāṃ dvau praśnau prakṣyāmītyanuṣajyate;kau tāviti jijñāsāyāṃ tayorduruttaratvadyotayituṃ dṛṣṭāntapūrvakaṃ tāvāha - he yājñavalkya yathā loke kāśyaḥ kāśiṣu bhavaḥ kāśyaḥ, prasiddhaṃ śauryaṃ kāśye, vaideho vā videhānāṃ vā rājā, ugraputraḥ śūrānvaya ityarthaḥ, ujjyam avatāritajyākaṃ dhanuḥ punaradhijyam āropitalyākaṃ kṛtvā dvau bāṇavantau bāṇaśabdena śarāgre yo vaṃśakhaṇḍaḥ saṃdhīyate, tena vināpi śaro bhavatītyato viśinaṣṭi bāṇavantāviti - dvau bāṇavantau śarau, tayoreva viśeṣaṇaṃ sapatnātivyādhinau śatroḥ pīḍākarāvatiśayena, haste kṛtvopottiṣṭhet samīpata ātmānaṃ darśayet evamevāhaṃ tvā tvāṃ śarasthānīyābhyāṃ praśnābhyāṃ dvābhyāmupodasthāṃ utthitavatyasmi tvatsamīpe /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.2: Having obtained permission, she said to <s>Yājñavalkya</s>: 'I shall ask you two questions' — this is connected. Wishing to know what those two [questions] are, and in order to indicate their difficulty of answer, she first speaks with an illustration: 'O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, just as in the world, a <s>Kāśya</s> — one born in <s>Kāśī</s> — the valor of a <s>Kāśya</s> being well-known — or a <s>Vaideha</s>, the king of the <s>Videhas</s>, <s>ugraputra</s>, meaning one of heroic lineage — having strung a bow that was unstrung, i.e., whose bowstring had been removed, making it re-strung, i.e., with the bowstring re-fitted, with two arrows fitted with bamboo tips' — by the word '<s>bāṇa</s>' is meant the bamboo fragment attached to the tip of the arrow; since an arrow can exist even without it, [the text] specifies '<s>bāṇavantau</s>' (fitted with tips) — 'two arrows fitted with bamboo tips, which are <s>sapatnātivyādhin</s>' (capable of excessively piercing the enemy), causing pain to the foe in an extraordinary manner — 'having taken them in hand, would rise up and present himself nearby — even so, I have confronted you with two questions that serve as arrows.'

children.text: tau me brūhīti - brahmaviccet /
children.translated_text: 'Answer those two for me' — [this is said] if [you are] a knower of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: āhetaraḥ - pṛccha gārgīti //2//
children.translated_text: The other said: 'Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>.' // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.3]

children.text: sā hovāca -- yad ūrdhvaṃ yājñavalkya divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yad antarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣate kasmiṃs tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti || BrhUp_3,8.3 ||
children.translated_text: She said: 'That which is above heaven, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, that which is below the earth, that which is between heaven and earth — these [heaven and earth] — that which they call past, present, and future — in what is that woven, warp and woof?' // BṛhUp 3.8.3 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.3 sā hovāca - yadūrdhvamupari divaḥaṇḍakapālād yaccāvāgadhaḥ pṛthivyā adho 'ṇḍakapālāt, yaccāntarā madhye dyāvāpṛthivī dyāvāpṛthivyoḥ aṇḍakapālayoḥ, ime ca dyāvāpṛthivī, yad bhūtaṃ yaccātītam, bhavacca vartamānaṃ svavyāpārastham, bhaviṣyacca vartamānādūrdhvakālabhāviliṅgagamyam - yat sarvametadācakṣate kathayantyāgamataḥ - tat sarvaṃ dvaitajātaṃ yasminnekībhavatītyarthaḥ - tat sūtrasaṃjñaṃ pūrvoktaṃ kasminnotaṃ ca protaṃ ca pṛthivīdhāturivāpsu //3//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.3: She said: 'That which is above (<s>ūrdhvam</s>), i.e., higher than heaven — above the upper shell of the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍakapāla</s>) — and that which is below, i.e., lower than the earth — below the lower shell of the cosmic egg — and that which is in between, i.e., in the middle of heaven and earth, i.e., between the two shells of the cosmic egg — and these heaven and earth [themselves] — and that which is past, i.e., what has elapsed — and the present, that which is engaged in its own activity — and the future, that which is to come, accessible through the marks of future-tense forms from what is present — all this that they speak of, that they declare on the basis of scripture — the meaning is: all this aggregate of duality, that in which it becomes one — that previously mentioned [entity] called <s>sūtra</s> (thread) — in what is it woven, warp and woof? — just as the substance of earth [is woven] in water.' // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.4
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.4]

children.text: sa hovāca -- yad ūrdhvaṃ gārgi divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yad antarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣata ākāśe tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti || BrhUp_3,8.4 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'That which is above heaven, O <s>Gārgī</s>, that which is below the earth, that which is between heaven and earth — these [heaven and earth] — that which they call past, present, and future — that is woven, warp and woof, in space (<s>ākāśa</s>).' // BṛhUp 3.8.4 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.4 sa hovācetaraḥ - he gārgi yat tvayoktam'ūrdhvaṃ divaḥ'ityādi, tat sarvaṃ yat sūtramācakṣate tat sūtram, ākāśe tadotaṃ protaṃ ca, yadetad vyākṛtaṃ sūtrātmakaṃ jagadavyākṛtākāśe, apsviva pṛthivīdhātuḥ, triṣvapi kāleṣu vartate utpattau sthitau laye ca //4//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.4: He, the other [i.e., <s>Yājñavalkya</s>], said: 'O <s>Gārgī</s>, that which you have stated — "above heaven" and so forth — all of that, which is what they call <s>sūtra</s> (the thread) — that <s>sūtra</s> is woven, warp and woof, in space (<s>ākāśa</s>).' This differentiated world, which is of the nature of the <s>sūtrātman</s> (thread-self), [exists] in the undifferentiated space — like the substance of earth in water — in all three times: at origination, continuance, and dissolution. // 4 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.5
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.5]

children.text: sā hovaca -- namas te 'stu yājñavalkya yo ma etaṃ vyavoco 'parasmai dhārayasveti pṛccha gārgīti || BrhUp_3,8.5 ||
children.translated_text: She said: 'Salutations to you, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, you who have answered this for me. Prepare yourself for the other [question].' 'Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>.' // BṛhUp 3.8.5 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.5 punaḥ sā hovāca;namaste 'stvityādi praśnasya durvacatvapradarśanārtham;yo me mamaitaṃ praśnaṃ vyavoco viśeṣaṇāpākṛtavānasi;etasya durvacatve kāraṇam - sūtrameva tāvadagamyamitarairdurvācyam, kimuta tat, yasminnotaṃ ca protaṃ ceti;ato namo 'stu te tubhyam /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.5: Again she said: 'Salutations to you' and so forth — for the purpose of showing the difficulty of the question. 'You who have answered (<s>vyavocaḥ</s>) this question of mine — you have resolved it.' The reason for its difficulty [is this]: even the <s>sūtra</s> (thread-self) itself is inaccessible, difficult for others to express — how much more difficult then is that in which it is woven, warp and woof! Therefore, salutations to you.

children.text: aparasmai dvitīyāya praśnāya dhārayasva dṛḍhīkurvātmānamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Prepare yourself for the second question' — meaning: strengthen yourself, make yourself firm.

children.text: pṛccha gārgītītara āha //5//
children.translated_text: 'Ask, <s>Gārgī</s>' — said the other. // 5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.6
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.6]

children.text: sā hovāca -- yad ūrdhvaṃ yājñavalkya divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yad antarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣate kasmiṃs tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti || BrhUp_3,8.6 ||
children.translated_text: She said: 'That which is above heaven, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, that which is below the earth, that which is between heaven and earth — these [heaven and earth] — that which they call past, present, and future — in what is that woven, warp and woof?' // BṛhUp 3.8.6 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.6 vyākhyātamanyat;sā hovāca yadurdhvaṃ yājñavalkyaityādipraśnaḥ prativacanaṃ ca uktasyaivārthasyāvadhāraṇārthaṃ punarucyate;na kiñcidapūrvamarthāntaramucyate //6//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.6: The rest has been explained. She said: 'That which is above heaven, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>' and so forth — the question and answer, of the very same meaning already stated, are repeated for the purpose of establishing [the teaching]. Nothing new or different in meaning is stated. // 6 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.7
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.7]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- yad ūrdhvaṃ gārgi divo yad avāk pṛthivyā yad antarā dyāvāpṛthivī ime yad bhūtaṃ ca bhavac ca bhaviṣyac cety ācakṣata ākāśa eva tad otaṃ ca protaṃ ceti |
kasmin nu khalv ākāśa otaś ca protaś ceti || BrhUp_3,8.7 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'That which is above heaven, O <s>Gārgī</s>, that which is below the earth, that which is between heaven and earth — these [heaven and earth] — that which they call past, present, and future — that is woven, warp and woof, in space alone.' 'In what then is space woven, warp and woof?' // BṛhUp 3.8.7 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,8.7 sarvaṃ yathoktaṃ gārgyā pratyuccārya tameva pūrvoktamarthamavadhāritavānākāśa eveti yājñavalkyaḥ /
gārgyāha-kasminnu khalvākāśa otaśca protaśceti /
ākāśameva tāvat kālatrayātītatvād durvācyam, tato 'pi kaṣṭataramakṣaram yasminnākāśamotaṃ ca protaṃ ca, ato 'vācyamitikṛtvā, na pratipadyate sā apratipattirnāma nigrahasthānaṃ tārkikasamaye;athāvācyamapi vakṣyati, tathāpi vipratipattirnāma nigrahasthānam;virudvā pratipattirhi sā, yadavācyasya vadanam;ato durvacanaṃ praśnaṃ manyate gārgī // 7 // tad doṣadvayamapi parijihīrpannāha-
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.7: Having repeated <s>Gārgī</s>'s statement exactly as stated, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> confirmed the very same previously stated meaning: 'In space alone.' <s>Gārgī</s> said: 'In what then is space woven, warp and woof?' Space itself, to begin with, is difficult to express because it transcends the three times — how much more arduous then is the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) in which space is woven, warp and woof! Therefore it is inexpressible. Thinking thus, she does not assent — and that non-assent is a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) in the logicians' convention. But even though it is inexpressible, [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] will express it; even so, there is a contradictory assent (<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>), which is also a point of defeat — for it is a contradictory position, namely the expressing of the inexpressible. Therefore, <s>Gārgī</s> considers the question difficult to answer. // 7 // Wishing to avoid both these defects, he said:

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.8
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.8.8]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- etad vai tad akṣaraṃ gārgi brāhmaṇā abhivadanty asthūlam anaṇv ahrasvam adīrgham alohitam asneham acchāyam atamo 'vāyv anākāśam asaṅgam arasam agandham acakṣuṣkam aśrotram avāg amano 'tejaskam aprāṇam amukham agātram anantaram abāhyam (VAR for agātram: amātram) |
na tad aśnāti kiṃ cana |
na tad aśnāti kaś cana || BrhUp_3,8.8 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'That, O <s>Gārgī</s>, which the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> call the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) — it is neither gross nor subtle, neither short nor long, neither red nor moist, neither shadow nor darkness, neither wind nor space, unattached, without taste, without smell, without eyes, without ears, without speech, without mind, without radiance, without breath, without mouth, without measure, without interior and without exterior. It does not consume anything, nor does anyone consume it.' // BṛhUp 3.8.8 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,8.8 sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ-etad vai tad yat pṛṣṭavatyasi kasminnu khalvākāśa otaśca protaśceti, kiṃ tat? akṣaram-yanna kṣīyate na kṣaratīti vākṣaram-tadakṣaraṃ he gārgi brāhmaṇā brahmavido 'bhivadanti /
brahmaṇābhivadanakathanena-nāhamavācyaṃ vakṣyāmi na cana pratipadyeyam-ityevaṃ dopadrayaṃ pariharati /
evamapākute praśne punargārgyāḥ prativacanaṃ draṣṭavyam-brūhi kiṃ tadakṣaram? yad brāhmaṇā abhivadanti, ityukta āha-prasthūlaṃ tat sthūlādanyat, evaṃ tarhyaṇu? anaṇu, astu tarhi hasvam, ahasvam;evaṃ tarhi dīrgham, nāpi dīrghamadīrgham;evametaiścaturbhiḥ parimāṇapratiṣedhairdravyadharmaḥ pratiṣidvaḥ, na dravyaṃ tadakṣaramityarthaḥ /
astu tarhi lohito guṇaḥ, tato 'pyanyadalohitam;āgneyo guṇo lohitaḥ;bhavatu tarhyapyāṃ snehanam, na, asnehanam;astu tarhicchāyā, sarvathāpyanirdeśyatvāt, chāyāyā apyanyadacchāyam;astu tarhi tamaḥ, atamaḥ;bhavatu vāyustarhi, avāyuḥ;bhavettarhyākāśam, anākāśam;bhavatu tarhi saṅgātmakaṃ jatuvat, asaṅgam'raso 'stu tarhi, arasam';tathā gandho 'stvagandham;astu tarhi cakṣuḥ, acakṣuṣkam-na hi cakṣurasya karaṇaṃ vidyate 'to 'cakṣuṣkam;"paśyatyacakṣuḥ"iti mantravarṇāt /
tathāśrotram;"sa śṛṇotyakarṇaḥ"iti;bhavatu tarhi vāgavāk;tathāmanaḥ;tathātejaskam-avidyamānaṃ tejo 'sya tadatejaskam;na hi tejo 'gnyādiprakāśavadasya vidyate;aprāṇam-ādhyātmiko vāyuḥpratiṣidhyate 'prāṇamiti;mukhaṃ tarhi dvāraṃ tadamukham;amānnam-mīyate yena tanmātram amātraṃ mātrārūpaṃ tanna bhavati, na tena kiñcinmīyate;astu tarhicchidravat, anantaram-nāsyāntaramasti;sambhavet tarhi bahistasya, abāhyam;astu tarhi bhakṣayitṛ tat na tadaśnāti kñcina;bhavettarhi bhakṣyaṃ kasyacit, na tadaśnāti kaścana;sarvaviśeṣaṇarahitamityarthaḥ;ekamevādvitīyaṃ hi tat kena kiṃ viśiṣyate // 8 // anekaviśeṣaṇapratiṣedhaprayāsādastitvaṃ tāvadakṣarasyopagamitaṃ śrutyā;tathāpi lokabudvimapekṣyā śaṅkyate yataḥ, ato 'stitvāyānumānaṃ pramāṇamupanyasyati-
children.translated_text:
<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.8.8: He, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, said: 'That indeed is what you have asked about — "In what then is space woven, warp and woof?" — what is that? The Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) — that which is not diminished, does not decay — that Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, declare.' By stating that the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> declare it — 'I shall not speak the inexpressible, nor shall I fail to assent' — thus he avoids both defects.
With the question thus dealt with, the further response to <s>Gārgī</s> is to be seen: 'Tell me, what is that Imperishable that the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> declare?' — thus asked, he says: 'It is not gross' — it is other than the gross; 'then is it subtle?' — not subtle either; 'then let it be short' — not short; 'then long?' — not long either. Thus, by these four negations of dimension, the property of being a substance is negated — the meaning is: the Imperishable is not a substance.
'Then let it be a quality, such as red' — it is other than that too, not red. The quality of redness belongs to fire. 'Then let it be moist (<s>sneha</s>)' — no, without moisture. 'Then let it have shadow' — since it is in every way indescribable, it is other even than shadow, without shadow. 'Then let it be darkness' — without darkness. 'Then let it be wind' — without wind. 'Then let it be space' — without space. 'Then let it be something attached, like resin' — unattached. 'Then let it be taste' — without taste. 'Then smell' — without smell. 'Then let it have eyes' — without eyes; for no sense-organ of sight exists for it — hence without eyes. From the <s>mantra</s>: 'It sees without eyes' (ŚvetUp). Similarly, without ears. From: 'It hears without ears' (ŚvetUp). 'Then let it be speech' — without speech. Similarly, without mind. Without radiance — its radiance is non-existent, meaning it has no radiance; for it does not have radiance like the light of fire and the like. Without <s>prāṇa</s> — the breath belonging to the individual level is negated by 'without <s>prāṇa</s>.' 'Then let it have a mouth' — the opening, the door — without mouth. 'Without measure (<s>amātra</s>)' — that by which something is measured is a measure; this is not of the nature of a measure — nothing is measured by it. 'Then let it be like a hole, having an interior' — without interior: it has no interior. 'Then let it have an exterior' — without exterior. 'Then let it be something that consumes' — it does not consume anything. 'Then let it be something consumed by another' — no one consumes it. Free from all qualifications — this is the meaning. For being one alone, without a second, by what would it be qualified? // 8 // Through the effort of negating multiple qualifications, the existence of the Imperishable has been accepted by the <s>śruti</s>. Even so, because common understanding might raise doubts, [the text] presents inferential evidence for its existence:

children.translated_text: Under the mighty rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, sun and moon stand held apart. Under the mighty rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, heaven and earth stand held apart. Under the mighty rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, moments, hours, days and nights, fortnights, months, seasons, and years stand held apart. Under the mighty rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, some rivers flow eastward from the white mountains, others westward — each in whatever direction it flows. Under the mighty rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, men praise the giver, gods are dependent on the sacrificer, and the fathers are dependent on the offering-ladle. // BṛhUp 3.8.9 //

BrhUpBh_3,8.9 etasya vā akṣarasya;yadetadadhigatamakṣaraṃ sarvāntaraṃ sākṣādaparokṣādbrahma, ya ātmā aśanāyādidharmātītaḥ, etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane-yathā rājñaḥ praśāsane rājyamasphuṭitaṃ niyataṃ vartate, evamatasyākṣarasya praśāsane he gārgi sūryācandramaso ahorātrayorlokapradīpau, tādarthyena praśāsitrā tābhyāṃ nirvatyamānalokaprayojanavijñānavatā nirmitau ca, syātāṃ sādhāraṇasarvaprāṇiprakāśopakārakatvāllaukikapradīpavat /
tasmādasti tad yena vidhṛtāvīśvarau svatantrau sastau nirmitau tiṣṭhato niyatadeśakālanimittodayāstamayavṛddhikṣayābhyāṃ vartete;tadastyevametayoḥ praśāsitrakṣaram, pradīpakartṛvidhārayitṛvat /
etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgī dyāvāpṛthivī ca sāvayavatvāt sphuṭanasvabhāve api satyau gurutvāt patanasvabhāve saṃyuktatvād viyogasvabhāve cetanāvadabhimānidevatādhiṣṭhitatvāt svatantre api etasyākṣarasya praśāsane vartete vidhṛte tiṣṭhataḥ;etaddhyakṣaraṃ sarvavyavasthāsetuḥ sarvamaryādāvidharaṇam, ato nāsyākṣarasya praśāsanaṃ dyāvāpṛthivyāvatikrāmataḥ;tasmāt siddhamasyāstitvamakṣarasya avyabhicāri hi talliṅgam, yad dyāvāpṛthivyau niyate vartete;cetanāvantaṃ praśāsitāramasaṃsāriṇamantareṇa naitad yuktam /
"yena dyaurugrā pṛthivī ca dṛṣṭā"iti mantravarṇāt /
etasya vā akṣarasya praśāsane gārgi, nimeṣā muhūrtā ityete kālāvayavāḥ sarvasya atītānāgatavartamānasya janimataḥ kalayitāraḥ - yathā loke prabhuṇā niyato gaṇakaḥ sarvamāyaṃ vyayaṃ cāpramatto gaṇayati, tathā prabhusthānīya eṣāṃ kālāvayavānāṃ niyantā /
tathā prācayaḥ prāgañcanāḥ pūrvadiggamanā nadyaḥ syandante sravanti śvetebhyo himavadādibhyaḥ parvatebhyo giribhyo gaṅgādyā nadyastāśca yathā pravartitā eva niyatāḥ pravartante 'nyathāpi pravartitumutsahantyaḥ, tadetalliṅgaṃ praśāstuḥ /
pratīcyo 'nyāḥ pratīcīṃ diśamañcanti sindhvādyā nadyaḥ, anyāśca yāṃ yāṃ diśamanupravṛttāstāṃ tāṃ na vyabhicaranti;tacca siṅgam /
kiñca dadato hiraṇyādīn prayacchata ātmapīḍāṃ kurvato 'pi pramāṇajñā api manuṣyāḥ praśaṃsanti;tatra yacca dīyate, ye ca dadati, ye ca pratigṛhmanti, teṣāmihaiva samāgamo vilayaścānvakṣo dṛśyate;adṛṣṭastu paraḥ samāgamaḥ, tathāpi manuṣyā dadatāṃ dānaphalena saṃyogaṃ paśyantaḥ pramāṇajñatayā praśaṃsanti; tacca, karmaphalena saṃyojayitari kartuḥ karmaphalavibhāgajñe praśāstaryasati na syāt;dānakriyāyāḥ pratyakṣavināśitvāt;tasmādasti dānakartṛṇāṃ phalena saṃyojayitā /
apūrvamiti cet? tatsadbhāve pramāṇānupapatteḥ praśasturapīti cet /
na, āgamatātparyasya siddhatvāt;avocāma dyāgamasya vastuparatvāt /
kiñcānyat, apūrvakalpanāyāṃ cārthāpatteḥ, kṣayo 'nyathaivopapatteḥ /
sevāphalasya sevyāt prāptidarśanāt /
sevāyāśca kriyātvāt, tatsāmānyācca vāgadānahomādīnāṃ sevyād īśvarādeḥ phalaprāptirupapadyate dṛṣṭakriyādharmasāmarthyamaparityajyaiva phalaprāptikalpanopapattau dṛṣṭakriyādharmasāmarthyaparityāgo na nyāyyaḥ /

iha tu īśvarasya sevyasya sadbhāvamātraṃ kalpyam, na tu phaladānasāmarthyaṃ dātṛtvaṃ ca, sevyāt phalaprāptidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But here, for the Lord who is the one served, only the bare existence needs to be postulated — not the power to bestow fruit or the status of giver — since the attainment of fruit from the one served is observed.

children.text: anumānaṃ ca darśitam -'dyāvāpṛthivyau vidhṛte tiṣṭhataḥ'ityādi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And the inference has been shown — 'heaven and earth stand held in place' and the like.

children.text: tathā ca yajamānaṃ devā īśvarāḥ santo jīvanārthe 'nugatāḥ, carapuroḍāśādyupajīvanaprayojanena, anyathāpi jīvitumutsahantaḥ kṛpaṇāṃ dīnāṃ vṛttimāśritya sthitāḥ, tacca praśāstuḥ praśāsanāt syāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And thus, the gods — being lords — have followed the sacrificer for the sake of their livelihood, for the purpose of subsisting on the <s>carupuroḍāśa</s> (rice-cake offerings) and the like; though capable of living otherwise, they have remained established in a lowly, wretched mode of living — and this would be due to the governance of the ruler.

children.text: tathā pitaro 'pi tadarthaṃ darvī darvīhomamanvāyattā anugatā ityarthaḥ, samānaṃ sarvamanyat //9//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, the ancestors (<s>pitṛs</s>) too, for that [same] purpose, have followed [the sacrificers], dependent on the ladle-oblations (<s>darvīhoma</s>) — this is the meaning. Everything else is the same. (9)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.8.9:] Under the rule of this very Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) — that which has been ascertained as the Imperishable, the innermost of all, the directly present and non-remote <s>Brahman</s>, the self that transcends the properties of hunger and the like — under the rule of this very Imperishable: just as under the rule of a king, the kingdom continues unbroken and regulated, so too, under the rule of this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, the sun and moon — the lamps of the world for the sake of day and night — being created by the ruler for the purpose of accomplishing the worldly functions carried out through them, stand held in place, like worldly lamps, because of their common usefulness in illuminating all living beings. Therefore, there exists that by which these two — the sun and moon — who are lords, independent, and created, are held in place, functioning through their risings and settings, waxings and wanings, which are regulated in place, time, and cause. That ruler — the Imperishable — does indeed exist, like the maker and sustainer of a lamp. Under the rule of this very Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, heaven and earth too — though by their nature as composite entities they are subject to splitting, though by their heaviness they are subject to falling, though by their being conjoined they are subject to separation, and though they are independent being presided over by the identifying deities who possess consciousness — even so, under the rule of this Imperishable, they stand held in place. For this Imperishable is the bridge of all cosmic order, the upholder of all boundaries; therefore, heaven and earth do not transgress the governance of this Imperishable. Therefore, the existence of this Imperishable is established, for the sign [of its existence] is unfailing — namely, that heaven and earth function in a regulated manner. Without a conscious, non-<s>saṃsāric</s> ruler, this would not be possible — from the <s>mantra</s>: 'By whom the mighty heaven and earth are beheld.' Under the rule of this very Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, moments (<s>nimeṣa</s>), <s>muhūrtas</s> — these divisions of time are the reckoners of everything that has been born, past, future, and present — just as in the world, an accountant appointed by the ruler diligently reckons all income and expenditure, so too [the Imperishable] stands in the place of the ruler as the controller of these temporal divisions. Likewise, the eastward-flowing rivers — flowing eastward, moving toward the eastern direction, the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and others — flow from the white [mountains], from <s>Himavat</s> and other mountains and peaks; and they flow in their appointed courses as if directed, though capable of flowing otherwise — this is the sign of the ruler. Other [rivers] flow westward — the <s>Sindhu</s> and other rivers move toward the western direction; and all the others, whichever direction they follow, do not deviate from it — that too is a sign. Moreover, even people who know the means of valid knowledge praise those who give gold and the like, who bestow [gifts], even at the cost of self-affliction. Therein, what is given, and those who give, and those who receive — their meeting and dissolution are observed directly here [in this world]. But the further meeting [i.e., the reuniting of the giver with the fruit] is unseen. Even so, people, seeing the connection of givers with the fruit of their giving, praise [them] because of their knowledge of valid means. And this [praise] would not be possible in the absence of a ruler who connects the doer with the fruit of action, who knows the apportionment of the fruit of action to the doer — since the act of giving is observed to perish directly. Therefore, there exists one who connects givers with their fruit. [Objection:] Let it be <s>apūrva</s> (unseen merit). [Reply:] No, because there is no means of valid knowledge for the real existence of that [<s>apūrva</s>]. [Objection:] But even a ruler is [merely] postulated! [Reply:] No, because the purport of scripture is already established; we have said that scripture is directed toward [establishing] a real entity. Moreover, even in postulating <s>apūrva</s>, there is the [need for an] inference from circumstantial evidence (<s>arthāpatti</s>), and the destruction [of results] can be explained otherwise. Because the fruit of service is seen to come from the one served. And because service is an action, and because of the analogy with [other types of service], the attainment of fruit from the one served — the Lord — for speech, donations, oblations, and the like is established. When the postulation of the attainment of fruit is possible without abandoning the observed power of the property of action, it is not proper to abandon the observed power of the property of action. And because of the excess of postulation [involved in <s>apūrva</s>]: should one postulate a Lord, or <s>apūrva</s>? Therein, the natural [property] of action — the attainment of fruit from the one served — is observed; but not from <s>apūrva</s>. Nor is <s>apūrva</s> observed. In that case, the unseen <s>apūrva</s> must be postulated, and its power to bestow fruit [must also be postulated], and given that power, the gift [of additional postulation] is excessive.

itaścāsti tadakṣaraṃ smāttadajñāne niyatā saṃsāropapattiḥ /
bhavitavyaṃ tu tena, yadvijñānāt tadvicchedaḥ, nyāyopapatteḥ /
nanu kriyāta eva tadvicchittiḥ syāditi cet? na -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, that Imperishable exists — because from ignorance of it, the invariable occurrence of <s>saṃsāra</s> is established. And that [Imperishable] must indeed exist, from the knowledge of which comes the cessation [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] — because this is established by reasoning. [Objection:] But let the cessation [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] come about through action alone! [Reply:] No —

children.text:
yo vā etad akṣaram gārgy aviditvāsmiṃl loke juhoti yajate tapas tapyate bahūni varṣasahasrāṇy antavad evāsya tad bhavati
yo vā etad akṣaram aviditvā gārgy aviditvāsmāl lokāt praiti sa kṛpaṇaḥ |
atha ya etad akṣaraṃ gārgi viditvāsmāl lokāt praiti sa brāhmaṇaḥ || BrhUp_3,8.10 ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Gārgī</s>, whoever, without knowing this Imperishable, makes offerings in this world, performs sacrifices, and practices austerities — even for many thousands of years — that [fruit] of his is finite. O <s>Gārgī</s>, whoever departs from this world without knowing this Imperishable — he is pitiable (<s>kṛpaṇa</s>). But whoever, O <s>Gārgī</s>, departs from this world knowing this Imperishable — he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (BṛUp 3.8.10)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,8.10 yo vā etadakṣaraṃ he gārgi aviditvāvijñāya asmiṃlloke juhoti yajata tapastapyate yadyapi bahūni varṣasahasrāṇi, antavad evāsya tat phalaṃ bhavati, tatphalopabhogānte kṣīyanta evāsya karmāṇi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.8.10:] O <s>Gārgī</s>, whoever, without knowing this Imperishable — without understanding it — makes offerings in this world, performs sacrifices, and practices austerities — even for many thousands of years — that fruit of his is finite; at the end of the enjoyment of that fruit, his actions are indeed exhausted.

children.text: api ca yadvijñānāt kārpaṇyātyayaḥ saṃsāravicchedaḥ, yadvijñānābhāvācca karmakṛt kṛpaṇaḥ kṛtaphalasyaivopabhoktājananamaraṇaprabandhārūḍhaḥ saṃsarati, tadastyakṣaraṃ praśāsitṛ;tadetaducyate - yo vā etadakṣaraṃ gārgyaviditvā asmāllokāt praiti sa kṛpaṇaḥ, paṇakrīta iva dāsādiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, that from the knowledge of which comes the transcendence of wretchedness (<s>kārpaṇya</s>) — the cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s> — and from the absence of knowledge of which the performer of actions, being wretched, merely enjoying the fruit of what he has done, mounted on the stream of birth and death, transmigrates — that Imperishable, the ruler, exists. This is what is said: O <s>Gārgī</s>, whoever departs from this world without knowing this Imperishable — he is wretched (<s>kṛpaṇa</s>), like a slave purchased for a price.

children.text: atha ya etadakṣaraṃ gārgi viditvā asmāllokāt praiti sa brāhmaṇaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But whoever, O <s>Gārgī</s>, departs from this world knowing this Imperishable — he is a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. (10)

children.text: agnerdahanaprakāśakatvāt svābhāvikasya praśāstṛtvamacetanasyaivetyata āha -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] Since fire possesses the natural properties of burning and illuminating, the rulership [of the universe] belongs to the non-conscious [<s>pradhāna</s>] alone. To this [the text] says:

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.11
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.8.11]

children.text:
tad vā etad akṣaraṃ gārgy adṛṣṭaṃ draṣṭraśrutaṃ śrotramataṃ mantravijñātaṃ vijñātṛ |
nānyad ato 'sti draṣṭṛ |
nānyad ato 'sti śrotṛ |
nānyad ato 'sti mantṛ |
nānyad ato 'sti vijñātṛ |
etasmin nu khalv akṣare gārgy ākāśa otaś ca protaś ca || BrhUp_3,8.11 ||
children.translated_text: That Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, is unseen but is the seer; unheard but is the hearer; unthought but is the thinker; unknown but is the knower. There is no other seer than this. There is no other hearer than this. There is no other thinker than this. There is no other knower than this. In this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, space is woven, warp and weft. (BṛUp 3.8.11)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,8.11 tad vā etadakṣaraṃ gārgi adṛṣṭaṃ na kenacid dṛṣṭam, aviṣayatvāt svayaṃ tu draṣṭṛ dṛṣṭisvarūpatvāt /
tathā śrutaṃ śrotrāviṣayatvāt, svayaṃ śrotṛ śrutisvarūpatvāt /
tathāmataṃ manaso 'viṣayatvāt, svayaṃ mantṛmatisvarūpatvāt /
tathāvijñātaṃ buddheraviṣayatvāt, svayaṃ vijñātṛ vijñānasvarūpatvāt /
kiñca nānyadato 'smādakṣarādasti - nāsti kiñcid draṣṭṛ darśanakriyākartṛ;etadevākṣaraṃ darśanakriyākartṛ sarvatra /
tathā nānyadato 'sti śrotṛ;tadevākṣaraṃ śrotṛ sarvatra /
nānyadato 'sti mantṛ;tadevākṣaraṃ mantṛ sarvatra sarvamanodvāreṇa /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There is no other thinker than this; this Imperishable alone is the thinker everywhere, through every mind as doorway.

children.text: nānyadato 'sti vijñātṛ vijñānakriyākartṛ, tadevākṣaraṃ sarvabuddhidvāreṇa vijñānakriyākartṛ, nācetanaṃ pradhānamanyad vā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] There is no other knower — no other agent of the act of knowing; this Imperishable alone, through every intellect as doorway, is the agent of knowing — not the non-conscious <s>pradhāna</s> (primal matter) or anything else.

children.text: etasminnu khalvakṣare gārgyākāśa otaśca protaśceti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'In this Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, space is woven, warp and weft.'

children.text: yadeva sākṣādaparokṣādbraṅma, ya ātmā sarvāntaro 'śanāyādi saṃsāradharmātītaḥ, yasminnākāśa otaśca protaśca, eṣā parā kāṣṭhā, eṣā parā gatiḥ, etat paraṃ brahma, etat pṛthivyāderākāśāntasya satyasya satyam //11//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is the directly present, non-remote <s>Brahman</s>, the self, the innermost of all, transcending the <s>saṃsāric</s> properties of hunger and the like, in which space is woven, warp and weft — this is the supreme limit (<s>parā kāṣṭhā</s>), this is the supreme goal (<s>parā gati</s>), this is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, this is the truth of truth — from earth up to and including space. (11)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.8.11:] That Imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, is unseen — not seen by anyone, because it is not an object [of perception]; but it is itself the seer, because its nature is seeing itself. Likewise, it is unheard — because it is not an object of the ear; but it is itself the hearer, because its nature is hearing itself. Likewise, it is unthought — because it is not an object of the mind; but it is itself the thinker, because its nature is thinking itself. Likewise, it is unknown — because it is not an object of the intellect; but it is itself the knower, because its nature is knowing itself. Moreover, there is nothing other than this Imperishable — there exists nothing that is a seer, an agent of the act of seeing; this Imperishable alone is the agent of seeing everywhere. Likewise, there is no other hearer than this; this Imperishable alone is the hearer everywhere.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,8.12
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.8.12]

children.text:
sā hovāca -- brāhmaṇā bhagavantas tad eva bahu manyadhvaṃ yad asmān namaskāreṇa mucyedhvam |
na vai jātu yuṣmākam imaṃ kaścid brahmodyaṃ jeteti |
tato ha vācaknavy upararāma || BrhUp_3,8.12 ||
children.translated_text: She said: 'Venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, you may consider it a great thing if you escape from him with a mere salutation. None of you will ever defeat him in a debate about <s>Brahman</s>.' Thereupon <s>Vācaknavī</s> (<s>Gārgī</s>) desisted. (BṛUp 3.8.12)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,8.12 sā hovāca - he brāhmaṇā bhagavantaḥ śṛṇuta madīyaṃ vacaḥ;tadeva bahu manyedhvam;kiṃ tat? yadasmād yājñavalkyānnamaskāreṇa mucyedhvam - asmai namaskāraṃ kṛtvā tadeva bahu manyadhvamityarthaḥ;jayastvasya manasāpi na āśaṃsanīyaḥ, kimuta kāryataḥ;kasmāt? na vai yuṣmākaṃ madhye jātu kadācidapīmaṃ yājñavalkyaṃ brahmodyaṃ prati jetā /
praśnau cenamahyaṃ vakṣyati, na jetā bhaviteti pūrvameva mayā pratijñātam;adyāpi mamāyameva niścayaḥ - brahmodyaṃ pratyetattulyo na kaścid vidyata iti /
tato ha vācaknavyupararāma /
atra antaryāmibrāhmaṇe etad uktam - yaṃ pṛthivī na veda, yaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni na vidiriti ca /
yamantaryāmiṇaṃ na vidurye ca na viduryacca tadakṣaraṃ darśanādakriyākartṛtvena sarveṣāṃ cetanādidhāturityuktam-kastveṣāṃ viśeṣaḥ kiṃ vā sāmānyamiti /
tatra kecidācakṣate-parasya mahāsamudrasthānāyasya brahmaṇo 'kṣarasya apracalitatvarūpasyeṣatpracalitāvasthāntaryāmī;atyantapracalitāvasthā kṣetrajñaḥ, yastaṃ na vedāntaryāmiṇam;tathānyāḥ pañcāvasthāḥ parikalpayanti, tathā aṣṭāvasthā brahmaṇo bhavantīti vadanti /
anye 'kṣarasya śaktaya etā iti vadanti, anantaśaktimadakṣaramiti ca /
anye tvakṣarasya vikārā iti vadanti /
avasthāśaktī tāvannopapadyeto akṣarasya, aśanāyādisaṃsāradharmātītatvaśruteḥ /
na hyaśanāyādyatītatvamaśanāyādidharmavadavasthāvattvaṃ caikasya yugapadupapadyate;tathā śaktimattvaṃ ca /
vikārāvayavatve ca doṣāḥ pradarśitāścaturthe /
tasmādetā asatyāḥ sarvāḥ kalpanāḥ /
kastarhi meda eṣām? upādhikṛta iti brūmaḥ;na svata eṣāṃ medo 'medo vā, saindhavaghanavat prajñānadhanaikarasasvāmāvyāt,"apūrvamanaparamanantaramabāhyam""ayamātmā brahma"iti ca śruteḥ /
"savāhyābhyāntaro hyajaḥ"iti cātharvaṇe /
tasmānnirūpādhikasyātmano nirūpākhyātvānnirviśeṣatvādekatvācca"neti neti"iti vyapadeśo bhavati /
avidyākāmakarmaviśiṣṭakāryakaraṇopādhirātmā saṃsārī jiva ucyate /
nityaniratiśayajñāna śaktyupādhirātmāntaryāmīśvara ucyate, sa eva nirūpādhiḥ kevalaḥ śudvaḥ svena svabhāvenākṣaraṃ para ucyate, tathā hiraṇyagarmāvyākṛtadevatājātipiṇḍamanuṣyatiryakpretādikāryakaraṇopādh ibhirviśiṣṭastadākhyastadarūpo bhavati /
tathā"tadejati tannaijati"iti vyākhyātam /
tathā"eṣa ta ātmā" "eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā" "eṣa sarveṣu bhūteṣu gūḍhaḥ" "tattavamasi" "ahamevedaṃ sarvam" "ātmaivedaṃ sarvam" "nānyo 'to 'sti draṣṭā"ityādiśrutayo na virudhyante /
children.translated_text: Similarly, [<s>śrutis</s> such as] 'This is your Self,' 'This is the inner Self of all beings,' 'This is hidden in all beings,' 'You are that' (<s>tat tvam asi</s>), 'I am indeed all this,' 'The Self alone is all this,' 'There is no other seer than this' — and other such <s>śrutis</s> are not contradicted [by the limiting-adjunct doctrine].

children.text: kalpanāntareṣvetāḥ śrutayo na gacchanti /
children.translated_text: These <s>śrutis</s> do not apply to any other postulated [theories of multiple states, powers, or transformations].

children.text: tasmādupādhimedenaila eṣāṃ medo nānyathā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the distinction among these is due to limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>) alone, and not otherwise.

children.text: 'ekamevādvitīyam'ityavadhāraṇāt sarveṣaniṣatsu //12//
children.translated_text: Because of the definitive statement: 'One only, without a second' (ChāUp 6.2.1) — all [apparent] differences are negated. // 12 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.8.12:] She said: 'O venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, hear my words. Consider this much to be a great [achievement]: that you should be freed from this <s>Yājñavalkya</s> with a mere salutation' — the meaning is: having bowed to him, consider that alone a great [thing]. His victory should not be hoped for even mentally, let alone in reality. Why? 'For never, at any time, among you, will anyone ever defeat this <s>Yājñavalkya</s> in the <s>brahmodya</s> (theological debate).' And my questions I shall ask him — 'he will not be a victor' — this was my previous declaration. Even now, this is my firm conviction: that in the <s>brahmodya</s>, there is no one equal to him. Thereupon <s>Vācaknavī</s> held her peace. Here, in the Inner Controller <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, it was stated: 'whom the earth does not know,' and 'whom all beings do not know.' [The question arises:] what is the distinction between the inner controller whom they do not know and the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), which — being stated through the absence of action and through being the controller of all conscious beings and the rest — [appears similar]? And what is their commonality? Therein, some declare: the imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, which has the status of a great ocean, in its state of complete motionlessness — the inner controller is its state of slight motion; the state of extreme motion is the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (individual knower), who does not know that inner controller. Similarly, they postulate five [further] states, and thus say there are eight states of <s>Brahman</s>. Others say these are powers (<s>śakti</s>) of the imperishable, and that the imperishable has infinite powers. Yet others say these are transformations (<s>vikāra</s>) of the imperishable. [Reply:] States and powers are not possible for the imperishable, because of the <s>śruti</s> that it transcends hunger, thirst, and all attributes of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For transcendence of hunger and the like, and having states like those having hunger and the like, cannot both be possible for one and the same [entity] simultaneously. Similarly with having powers. And the defects of having transformations and parts have been shown in the fourth [section]. Therefore, all these postulations are unreal. What then is the distinction among them? We say: it is caused by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhi</s>). There is no real distinction or non-distinction of these [from the Self], because — like a solid mass of salt — [the Self] is of the nature of pure consciousness alone, of a single taste, of its own nature. Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'Without prior, without posterior, without interior, without exterior — this Self is <s>Brahman</s>.' And in the <s>Ātharvana</s> [Upaniṣad]: 'For the unborn is both external and internal.' Therefore, for the Self without limiting adjuncts, because of having no designation, because of having no distinguishing features, and because of oneness — the designation 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>) applies. The Self conditioned by the limiting adjuncts of effects and instruments consisting of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), desire, and <s>karma</s> — the transmigrating [self] — is called the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul). The Self conditioned by the limiting adjunct of the eternal, unsurpassed power of knowledge is called the inner controller, <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord). That very [Self], without limiting adjuncts, pure, alone, of its own nature, is called the imperishable (<s>akṣara</s>), the supreme. Similarly, being qualified by the limiting adjuncts of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>), deities, species, embodied beings, humans, animals, ghosts, and the like — [the Self] bears those names and assumes those forms. This is how 'It moves; it does not move' (ĪśUp 5) has been explained.

children.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāyeṣṭamamakṣarabrāhmaṇam //8//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth, the Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>) <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of the third chapter. // 8 //

children.text:
atha hainaṃ vidagdhaḥ śākalyaḥ papraccha /
pṛthivyādīnāṃ sūkṣmatāratamyakrameṇa pūrvasya pūrvasya uttarasminnuttarasminnotaprotabhāvaṃ kathayan sarvāntaraṃ brahma prakāśitavān tasya ca brahmaṇo vyākṛtaviṣaye sūtramedeṣu niyantṛtvamuktam-vyākṛtaviṣaye vyaktaraṃ liṅgamiti /
tasyaiva brahmaṇaḥ sākṣādaparokṣatve niyantavyadevatāmedasaṃkocavikā sadvāreṇādhigantavye iti tadarya śākalyabrāhmaṇamāramyate--
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vidagdha Śākalya</s> questioned him. [Commentary:] Through the graduated sequence of subtlety — from earth and the rest — the warp-and-woof status of each preceding [level] in each succeeding [level] being stated, the innermost <s>Brahman</s> was illuminated. And of that <s>Brahman</s>, in its differentiated domain, the controlling nature as the thread was stated — [and] in the differentiated domain, the <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) is more manifest. Of that very <s>Brahman</s> — [in order to teach its] direct and immediate [nature] — through the doorway of the contraction and expansion of the deities that are to be controlled — [this is] to be understood. For that purpose, the <s>Śākalya Brāhmaṇa</s> is commenced.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.1]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ vidagdhaḥ śākalyaḥ papraccha -- kati devā yājñavalkyeti |
sa haitayaiva nividā pratipede yāvanto vaiśvadevasya nividy ucyante |
trayaś ca trī ca śatā trayaś ca trī ca sahasreti |
om iti hovāca |
katy eva devā yājñavalkyeti |
trayastriṃśad iti |
om iti hovāca |
katy eva devā yājñavalkyeti |
ṣaḍ iti |
om iti hovāca |
katy eva devā yājñavalkyeti |
traya iti |
om iti hovāca |
katy eva devā yājñavalkyeti |
dvāv iti |
om iti hovāca |
katy eva devā yājñavalkyeti |
adhyardha iti |
om iti hovāca |
katy eva devā yājñavalkyeti |
eka iti |
om iti hovāca |
katame te trayaś ca trī ca śatā trayaś ca trī ca sahasreti || BrhUp_3,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Vidagdha Śākalya</s> questioned him: 'How many gods are there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' He answered according to that very <s>nivid</s> (invocatory formula) which is recited in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> [liturgy]: 'Three hundred and three, and three thousand and three.' 'Yes,' he said. 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'Thirty-three.' 'Yes,' he said. 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'Six.' 'Yes,' he said. 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'Three.' 'Yes,' he said. 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'Two.' 'Yes,' he said. 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'One and a half.' 'Yes,' he said. 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'One.' 'Yes,' he said. 'Which are those three hundred and three and three thousand and three?' (BṛUp 3.9.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.1 atha hainaṃ vidagdha iti nāmataḥ śakalasyāpatyaṃ śākalyaḥ papraccha--katisaṃkhyākā devā he yājñavalkyeti /
sa yājñavalkyaḥ, ha kila, etayaiva vakṣyamāṇayā nividā pratipede saṃkhyām, yāṃ saṃkhyāṃ pṛṣṭavāñśākalyaḥ /

yāvanto yāvatsaṃkhyākā devā vaiśvadevasya śastrasya nividi-nivinnāma devatāsaṃkhyāvācakāni mantrapadāni, kānicid vaiśvadeve śastre śasyante tāni nivitsaṃjñakāni;tasyāṃ nividi yāvanto devāḥ śrūyante tāvanto devā iti /
