children.translated_text: As many gods as are [mentioned] in the <s>nivid</s> of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> <s>śastra</s> (liturgical recitation) — the <s>nivid</s> being the mantra-words that express the number of deities; certain [words] recited in the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> <s>śastra</s> are called <s>nivid</s>; as many gods as are heard in that <s>nivid</s>, that many are the gods.

children.text: kā punaḥ sā nividiti tāni nivitpadāni pradarśyante-trayaśca trī ca śatā-trayaśca devāḥ, devānāṃ trī ca trīṇi ca śatāni;punarapyevaṃ trayaśca, trī ca sahasrā sahasrāṇ-etāvanto devā iti śākalyo 'pyomiti hovāca /
children.translated_text: What then is that <s>nivid</s>? Those <s>nivid</s>-words are demonstrated: 'three and three hundred' — three gods, and three hundred of those gods; and again likewise, three, and three thousand — this many are the gods. And <s>Śākalya</s> too said 'Yes.'

children.text: evameṣāṃ madhyamā saṃkhyā samyaktayā jñātā, punastepāmeva devānāṃ saṃkocaviṣayāṃ saṃkhyāṃ pṛcchati-katyeva devā yājñavalkyeti;trayastriśata;pada, trayaḥ, dvau, adhyardhaḥ, eka iti /
children.translated_text: Thus, the median number of these [gods] having been properly ascertained, he then asks about the contracted number of those very gods: 'How many gods are there really, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' — [the answers being:] thirty-three, six, three, two, one-and-a-half, one.

children.text: devatāsaṃkocavikāsaviṣayāṃ saṃkhyāṃ pṛṣṭvā punaḥ saṃkhyeyasvarūpaṃ pṛcchati-katame te trayaśca trī ca śatā trayaśca trī ca sahasreti //1//
children.translated_text: Having asked about the contracted and expanded numbers of the deities, he then asks about the nature of what is being enumerated: 'Which are those three hundred and three and three thousand and three?' // 1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.1:] Then <s>Vidagdha</s> by name, the son of <s>Śakala</s>, hence <s>Śākalya</s>, questioned: 'How many in number are the gods, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' He, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, answered with that very <s>nivid</s> about to be stated — [giving] the number that <s>Śākalya</s> had asked about.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.2]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- mahimāna evaiṣām ete |
trayastriṃśat tv eva devā iti |
katame te trayastriṃśad iti |
aṣṭau vasava ekādaśa rudrā dvādaśādityāḥ ta ekatriṃśad aindraś caiva prajāpatiś ca trayastriṃśāv iti || BrhUp_3,9.2 ||
children.translated_text: He said: 'These are but their glories (<s>mahimānas</s>). The gods are indeed thirty-three.' 'Which are those thirty-three?' 'Eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, twelve <s>Ādityas</s> — these make thirty-one; and <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> make thirty-three.' (BṛUp 3.9.2)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.2 sa hovācetaraḥ - mahimāno vibhūtayaḥ, eṣāṃ trayastriṃśataḥ devānām ete trayaśca trī ca śatetyādayaḥ;paramārthatastu trayastriṃśattveva devā iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.2:] He [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] said: 'Glories' — manifestations of power — of these thirty-three gods; these — 'three and three hundred' and so forth — are [their manifestations]. But in reality, the gods are indeed thirty-three.

children.text: katame te trayastriṃśadityucyate - aṣṭau vasavaḥ ekādaśa rudrāḥ, dvādaśa ādityāste ekatriṃśat, indraścaiva prajāpatiśca trayastriṃśāviti trayastriṃśataḥ pūraṇau //2//
children.translated_text: 'Which are those thirty-three?' is answered: eight <s>Vasus</s>, eleven <s>Rudras</s>, twelve <s>Ādityas</s> — these make thirty-one; and <s>Indra</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s> complete the thirty-three. // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.3]

children.text:
katame vasava iti |
agniś ca pṛthivī ca vāyuś cāntarikṣaṃ cādityaś ca dyauḥ ca candramāś ca nakṣatrāṇi caite vasavaḥ |
eteṣu hīdaṃ sarvaṃ vasu hitaṃ iti tasmād vasava iti || BrhUp_3,9.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Which are the <s>Vasus</s>?' 'Fire, earth, wind, atmosphere, sun, heaven, moon, and stars — these are the <s>Vasus</s>. For in these, all this wealth (<s>vasu</s>) is deposited. Therefore they are <s>Vasus</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.3)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.3 katame vasava iti teṣāṃ svarūpaṃ pratyekaṃ pṛchcyate;agniśca pṛthivī ceti - agnyādyā nakṣatrāntarā ete vasavaḥ - prāṇināṃ karmaphalāśrayatvena kāryakaraṇasaṃghātarūpeṇa tannivāsatvena ca vipariṇamanto jagadidaṃ sarvaṃ vāsayanti vasanti ca;te yasmād vāsanti tasmāde vasava iti //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.3:] 'Which are the <s>Vasus</s>?' — the nature of each [group] is asked individually. 'Fire, earth' and so forth — fire and the rest, up to the stars — these are the <s>Vasus</s>. Because, by serving as substrates for the fruits of <s>karma</s> of living beings, by transforming into the form of aggregates of effects and instruments, and by being the abodes [of living beings] — they cause all this world to dwell (<s>vāsayanti</s>) [in them], and they themselves dwell [therein]. Because they cause [beings] to dwell, therefore they are <s>Vasus</s>. // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.4]

children.text:
katame rudrā iti |
daśeme puruṣe prāṇā ātmaikādaśaḥ |
te yadāsmāc charīrān martyād utkrāmanty atha rodayanti |
tad yad rodayanti tasmād rudrā iti || BrhUp_3,9.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Which are the <s>Rudras</s>?' 'These ten <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths/organs) in a person, with the self (<s>ātman</s>) as the eleventh. When they depart from this mortal body, they make [the relatives] weep (<s>rodayanti</s>). Because they make [them] weep, they are <s>Rudras</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.4)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.4 katame rudrā iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.4:] 'Which are the <s>Rudras</s>?'

children.text: daśeme puruṣe karmabuddhīndriyāṇi prāṇāḥ, ātmā mana ekādaśaḥ - ekādaśānāṃ pūraṇaḥ te ete prāṇā yadā asmāccharīrānmartyāt prāṇināṃ karmaphalapabhogakṣaye utkrāmanti - atha tadā rodayanti tatsambandhinaḥ /
children.translated_text: These ten — the five action-organs and five knowledge-organs — are the <s>prāṇas</s> in a person; the self, meaning the mind, is the eleventh — completing the count of eleven. When these <s>prāṇas</s> depart, at the exhaustion of the fruits of <s>karma</s> for enjoyment, from this mortal body of living beings — then, at that time, they cause weeping in the relatives [of the deceased].

children.text: tattatra yasmādrodayanti te sambandhinaḥ, tasmād rudrā iti //4//
children.translated_text: Because they cause the relatives to weep — therefore they are <s>Rudras</s>. // 4 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.5]

children.text:
katama ādityā iti |
dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsarasyaita ādityāḥ |
ete hīdaṃ sarvam ādadānā yanti |
te yad idaṃ sarvam ādadānā yanti tasmād ādityā iti || BrhUp_3,9.5 ||
children.translated_text: 'Which are the <s>Ādityas</s>?' 'The twelve months of the year are the <s>Ādityas</s>. For they go, taking (<s>ādadānāḥ</s>) all this. Because they go taking all this, they are <s>Ādityas</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.5)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.5 katama ādityā iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.5:] 'Which are the <s>Ādityas</s>?'

children.text: dvādaśa vai māsāḥ saṃvatsarasya kālasyāvayavāḥ prasiddhāḥ, ete ādityāḥ;katham? ete hi yasmāt punaḥ punaḥ parivartamānāḥ prāṇināmāyūṃṣi karmaphalaṃ ca ādadānā gṛhyanta upādadato yanti gacchanti te yad yasmādevamidaṃ sarvamādadānā yanti tasmādādityā iti //5//
children.translated_text: The twelve well-known months are the divisions of the year, of time. These are the <s>Ādityas</s>. How? Because, revolving again and again, taking (<s>ādadānāḥ</s>) — seizing, appropriating — the lifespans and the fruits of <s>karma</s> of living beings, they go. Because they thus go taking all this — therefore they are <s>Ādityas</s>. // 5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.6]

children.text:
katama indraḥ katamaḥ prajāpatir iti |
stanayitnur evendro yajñaḥ prajāpatir iti |
katamaḥ stanayitnur iti |
aśanir iti |
katamo yajña iti |
paśava iti || BrhUp_3,9.6 ||
children.translated_text: 'Which is <s>Indra</s>? Which is <s>Prajāpati</s>?' 'Thunder is <s>Indra</s>. The sacrifice is <s>Prajāpati</s>.' 'What is thunder?' 'The thunderbolt.' 'What is the sacrifice?' 'The animals.' (BṛUp 3.9.6)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.6 katama indraḥ katamaḥ prajāpatiriti, stanayityurevendro yajñaḥ prajāpatiriti, katamaḥ stanayitnurityaśaniriti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.6:] 'Which is <s>Indra</s>? Which is <s>Prajāpati</s>?' Thunder is <s>Indra</s>; the sacrifice is <s>Prajāpati</s>. 'What is thunder?' The thunderbolt.

children.text: aśanirvajraṃ vīryaṃ balam, yat prāṇinaḥ pramāpayati, sa indraḥ;indrasya hi tat karma /
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt is the vajra — power, strength — which destroys living beings. That is <s>Indra</s>, for that is the work of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: katamo yajña iti paśava iti - yajñasya hi sādhanāni paśavaḥ;yajñasyārūpatvāt paśusādhanāśrayatvācca paśavo yajña ityucyate //6//
children.translated_text: 'What is the sacrifice?' 'The animals' — for the animals are the means of the sacrifice. Because the sacrifice has no [visible] form of its own, and because it rests on the animals as its means, the animals are called the sacrifice. // 6 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.7]

children.text:
katame ṣaḍ iti |
agniś ca pṛthivī ca vāyuś cāntarikṣaś cādityaś ca dyauś caite ṣaṭ |
ete hīdaṃ sarvaṃ ṣaḍ iti || BrhUp_3,9.7 ||
children.translated_text: 'Which are the six?' 'Fire, earth, wind, atmosphere, sun, and heaven — these are the six. For all this is [comprised in] these six.' (BṛUp 3.9.7)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.7 katame ṣaḍiti;ta evāgnyādayo vasutvena paṭhitāścandramasaṃ nakṣatrāṇi ca varjayitvā ṣaḍ bhavanti - ṣaṭasaṃkhyāviśiṣṭāḥ, trayastriṃśadādi yaduktamidaṃ sarvam, eta eva ṣaḍ bhavanti sarvo hi vasvādivistara eteṣveva ṣaṭasvantarbhavatītyarthaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.7:] 'Which are the six?' The very same — fire and the rest listed as <s>Vasus</s>, excluding the moon and stars — become six. Distinguished by the number six, all this that was stated as thirty-three and so forth — these very six comprise it all; for the entire expansion of <s>Vasus</s> and the rest is subsumed in these six alone — this is the meaning. // 7 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.8]

children.text:
katame te trayo devā iti |
ima eva trayo lokāḥ |
eṣu hīme sarve devā iti |
katamau tau dvau devā iti |
annaṃ caiva prāṇaś ceti |
katamo 'dhyardha iti |
yo 'yaṃ pavata iti || BrhUp_3,9.8 ||
children.translated_text: 'Which are those three gods?' 'These three worlds alone. For in these, all these gods [are comprised].' 'Which are those two gods?' 'Food and <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) indeed.' 'Which is the one-and-a-half?' 'The one that blows [i.e. the wind].' (BṛUp 3.9.8)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.8 katame te trayo devā iti;ima eva trayo lokā iti - pṛthivīmagniṃ caikokṛtyaiko devaḥ, antarikṣaṃ vāyuṃ caikīkṛtya tṛtīyaḥ - te eva trayo devā iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.8:] 'Which are those three gods?' 'These three worlds alone' — combining earth and fire into one god, and atmosphere and wind into [another] — the third [being heaven and sun] — these are the three gods.

children.text: eṣu. hi yasmāt, triṣu deveṣu sarve devā antarbhavanti tena ta eva devāstrayaḥ - ityeṣa nairuktānāṃ keṣāñcit pakṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because all the gods are subsumed in these three gods — therefore they are the three gods. This is the view of certain etymologists (<s>Nairuktas</s>).

children.text: katamau tau dvau devāviti - annaṃ caiva prāṇaścaitau dvau devau, anayoḥ sarveṣāmuktānāmantarbhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Which are those two gods?' 'Food and <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) indeed — these are the two gods.' All those mentioned [above] are subsumed in these two.

children.text: katamo 'dhyargha iti - yo 'yaṃ pavate vāyuḥ //8//
children.translated_text: "Which is the one-and-a-half god?" — It is this <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) that blows. ||8||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.9
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.9]

children.text:
tad āhur yad ayam eka ivaiva pavate |
atha katham adhyardha iti |
yad asminn idaṃ sarvam adhyārdhnot tenādhyardha iti |
katama eko deva iti |
prāṇa iti |
sa brahma tyad ity ācakṣate || BrhUp_3,9.9 ||
children.translated_text: Then they said: "Since this one alone blows, how is he one-and-a-half?" "Because in him all this has prospered (<s>adhyārdhnot</s>), therefore he is the one-and-a-half (<s>adhyardha</s>)." "Which is the one god?" "<s>Prāṇa</s> (the vital breath)," he said. "He is <s>Brahman</s>, which they call <s>tyat</s> (that)." || BṛhUp 3.9.9 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.9 tattatrāhuścodayanti - yadayaṃ vāyureka ivaiva eka eva pavate ;atha kathamadhyardha iti? yadasminnidaṃ sarvamadhyārdhnot-asmin vāyau satīdaṃ sarvamadhyārdhnodadhi ṛddhiṃ prāpnoti, tenādhyardha iti /
katama eko deva iti? prāṇa iti sa prāṇo brahma-sarvadevātmakatvānmahad brahma, tena sa brahma tyadityācakṣate-tyaditi tad brahmācakṣate parokṣāmidhāyakena śabdena /
devānāmetadekatvaṃ nānātvaṃ ca /
anantānāṃ devānāṃ nivitsaṃkhyāviśaṣṭeṣvantarbhāvaḥ, teṣāmapi trayāstriśadādipūttarottareṣu yāvadekasmin prāṇe /
children.translated_text: The innumerable gods are subsumed within those distinguished by the numbers of the <s>nivit</s>-series, and those in turn within the successively higher groupings of thirty-three and so on, down to the one <s>Prāṇa</s>.

children.text: prāṇasyaiva caikasya sarvo 'nantasaṅkhyāto vistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: And the entire innumerable expansion is of <s>Prāṇa</s> alone.

children.text: evamekaścānantaśca avāntarasaṃkhyāviśiṣṭaśca prāṇa eva /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Prāṇa</s> alone is one, innumerable, and distinguished by intermediate numbers.

children.text: tatra ca devasyaikasya nāmarūpakarnaguṇaśaktimedaḥ, adhikāramedāt //9//
children.translated_text: And the distinction of names, forms, actions, qualities, and powers of that one god is due to the distinction of functions. ||9||

[Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.9:] Thereupon they raise the objection: since this <s>Vāyu</s> alone blows as one, how then is he the one-and-a-half? Because in him — in this <s>Vāyu</s> — all this has prospered, that is, has attained abundance (<s>ṛddhi</s>), therefore he is the one-and-a-half. "Which is the one god?" "<s>Prāṇa</s>," he said. That <s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s> — being the Self of all the gods, it is the great <s>Brahman</s>; therefore it is <s>Brahman</s>, which they designate as <s>tyat</s> — they designate that <s>Brahman</s> by the indirect word <s>tyat</s> (that). This is the oneness and the multiplicity of the gods.

children.text: idānīṃ tasyaiva prāṇasya brahmaṇaḥ punaraṣṭadhā meda upadiśyate-
children.translated_text: Now the eightfold distinction of that very <s>Prāṇa</s>, which is <s>Brahman</s>, is being taught —

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.10]

children.text:
pṛthivy eva yasyāyatanam agnir loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyaṃ śārīraḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
amṛtam iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.10 ||
children.translated_text: "Earth alone is his abode, fire is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He is indeed this <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the body. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "The immortal (<s>amṛta</s>)," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.10 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.10 pṛthivyeva yasya devasyāyatanamāśrayaḥ, agnirloko yasya - lokayatyaneneti lokaḥ, paśyatīti - agninā paśyatītyarthaḥ /
manojyotiḥ manasā jyotiṣā saṃkalpavikalpādikāryaṃ karoti yaḥ, so 'yaṃ manojyotiḥ /
pṛthivīśarīro 'gnidarśano manasā saṃkalpayitā pṛthivyabhimānī kāryakaraṇasaṃghātavān deva ityarthaḥ /
ya evaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyād vijānīyāt sarvasyātmana ādhyātmikasya kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasya ātmanaḥ paramayanaṃ para āśrayastaṃ parāyaṇam /
mātṛjena tvaṅmāṃsarudhirarūpeṇa kṣetrasthānīyena bījasthānīyasya pitṛjasya asthimajjāśukrarūpasya paramayanam, karaṇātmanaśca, sa vai veditā syāt /
ya etadevaṃ vetti sa vai veditā paṇḍitaḥ syādityābhiprāyaḥ /
yājñavalkya tvaṃ tamajānanneva paṇḍitābhimānītyamiprāyaḥ /
yadi tadvijñāne pāṇḍityaṃ labhyate, veda vai ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yamāttha yaṃ kathayasi tamahaṃ veda /
tatra śākalyasya vacanaṃ draṣṭyam-yadi tvaṃ vettha taṃ puruṣam, brūhikiṃviśeṣaṇo 'sau? saḥ-ya evāyaṃ śārīraḥ- pārdhivāṃśe śarīre bhavaḥ śārīro mātṛjakośatrayarūpa ityarthaḥ, sa e, devaḥ, yastvayā pṛṣṭaḥ, he śākalya /
kintvasti tatra vaktavyaṃ viśeṣaṇāntaram, tad vadaiva pṛcchaivetyarthaḥ, he śākalya /
sa evaṃ prakṣobhito 'marpavaśaga āha-tottrādinta iva gajaḥ- tasya devasya śarīrasya kā devatā? yasmānniṣpadyate yaḥ sā tasya devatetyasmin prakaraṇe vivakṣitaḥ;amṛtamiti hovāca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus provoked, under the sway of misfortune, he spoke — like an elephant goaded by the prod — "What is the deity of that bodily god?" The deity is that from which it is produced — this is the intended meaning in this context. "The immortal (<s>amṛta</s>)," he said.

children.text: amṛtamiti yo bhuktasyānnasya raso mātṛjasya lohitasya niṣpattihetuḥ /
children.translated_text: "The immortal" refers to that which is the essence (<s>rasa</s>) of consumed food, which is the cause of the production of blood derived from the mother.

children.text: tasmādvayannarasāllohitaṃ niṣpadyate striyāṃ śritam, tataśca lohitamayaṃ śarīraṃ bījāśrayam /
children.translated_text: From that food-essence, blood is produced, which resides in the woman, and from that blood the body is formed, which serves as the receptacle for the seed.

children.text: samānamanyat //10//
children.translated_text: The rest is the same as before. ||10||

[Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.10:] Earth alone is the abode, the support, of this god. Fire is his world — 'world' means that by which one perceives (<s>lokayati</s>); he sees through fire, that is the meaning. Mind is his light — with the light that is the mind, he performs the function of willing and deliberating; thus he is one whose light is the mind. The meaning is: this god has earth as his body, fire as his means of seeing, and the mind as his instrument of willing; he is the presiding deity of earth, possessing the aggregate of body and organs. Whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> thus qualified — the ultimate resort (<s>parāyaṇa</s>), the supreme support of every self, that is, of the individual aggregate of body and organs — the ultimate resort of the maternal portion, consisting of skin, flesh, and blood, which is like the field, for the paternal portion consisting of bone, marrow, and semen, which is like the seed, and also of the self consisting of the organs — he indeed would be a knower. He who knows this would indeed be a learned person (<s>paṇḍita</s>) — that is the purport. "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, you do not know it and yet presume to be learned" — that is the implied meaning. "If learning is attained through knowledge of that, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak, whom you describe — him I know." Thereupon, regarding <s>Śākalya</s>'s words — "If you know that <s>puruṣa</s>, tell me, what are his distinguishing marks?" — "He is indeed this bodily <s>puruṣa</s>" — the one dwelling in the body made of the earthly portion, meaning one who consists of the three sheaths derived from the mother — "he is that god about whom you asked, O <s>Śākalya</s>. But there is yet another distinguishing characteristic to be stated about him; do speak, that is, do ask, O <s>Śākalya</s>."

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.11
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.11]

children.text:
kāma eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyaṃ kāmamayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
striya iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.11 ||
children.translated_text: "Desire (<s>kāma</s>) alone is his abode, the heart is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He is indeed this <s>puruṣa</s> who is made of desire (<s>kāmamaya</s>). Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "Women," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.11 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.11 kāma eva yasyāyatanam /
strīvyatikārābhilāṣaḥ kāmaḥ kāmaśarīra ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Desire (<s>kāma</s>) means the longing for union with a woman; the meaning is that desire is his body.

children.text: hradayaṃ lokohradayena budvayā paśyati /
children.translated_text: The heart is his world — through the heart, that is, through the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), he perceives.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ kāmamayaḥ puruṣo 'dhyātmamapi kāmamaya eva /
children.translated_text: He who is this <s>puruṣa</s> made of desire (<s>kāmamaya</s>) — at the individual level too, he is indeed made of desire.

children.text: tasya kā devateti striya iti hovāca;strīto hi kāmasya dīptirjīyate //11//
children.translated_text: "What is his deity?" "Women," he said; for from women the flame of desire is kindled. ||11||
[Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.11:] Desire alone is his abode.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.12
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.12]

children.text:
rūpāṇy eva yasyāyatanaṃ cakṣur loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāsāv āditye puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
satyam iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.12 ||
children.translated_text: "Forms (<s>rūpa</s>) alone are his abode, the eye is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He who is that <s>puruṣa</s> in the sun — he is that one. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "Truth (<s>satya</s>)," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.12 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.12 rūpāṇyeva yasyāyatanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.12:] Forms alone are his abode.

children.text: rūpāṇi śuklakṛṣṇādīni /
children.translated_text: Forms means white, black, and other colors.

children.text: ya evāsāvāditye puruṣaḥ- sarveṣāṃ hi rūpāṇāṃ viśiṣṭaṃ kāryamāditye puruṣaḥ tasya kā devateti? satyāmiti hovāca /
children.translated_text: "He who is that <s>puruṣa</s> in the sun" — for the <s>puruṣa</s> in the sun is the most distinguished product of all forms. "What is his deity?" "Truth (<s>satya</s>)," he said.

children.text: satyāmiti cakṣurucyate, cakṣuṣo hyavyātmataḥ ādityasyādhidaivatasya niṣpatti //12//
children.translated_text: "Truth" here refers to the eye, for from the eye at the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>), the sun at the cosmic level (<s>adhidaivata</s>) is produced. ||12||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.13]

children.text:
ākaśa eva yasyāyatanaṃ śrotraṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyam śrautaḥ prātiśrutkaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣa |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
diśa iti hovaca || BrhUp_3,9.13 ||
children.translated_text: "Space (<s>ākāśa</s>) alone is his abode, the ear is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He who is this auditory <s>puruṣa</s>, the echo-being — he is that one. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "The directions (<s>diśaḥ</s>)," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.13 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.13 ākāśa eva yasyāyatanam ya evāyaṃ śrotro bhavaḥ śrotraḥ, tatrāpi pratiśravaṇavelāyāṃ viśeṣato bhavatīti prātiśrutkaḥ, tasya kādevateti? diśa iti hovāca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.13:] Space alone is his abode. He who is born of the ear is the auditory one (<s>śrautra</s>), and he becomes especially manifest at the time of echo — hence he is the echo-being (<s>prātiśrutka</s>). "What is his deity?" "The directions," he said.

children.text: digbhyo hyasāvādhyātmiko niṣpadyate //13//
children.translated_text: For from the directions this individual-level being is produced. ||13||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.14
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.14]

children.text:
tama eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyaṃ chāyāmayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
mṛtyur iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.14 ||
children.translated_text: "Darkness (<s>tamas</s>) alone is his abode, the heart is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He who is this <s>puruṣa</s> made of shadow (<s>chāyāmaya</s>) — he is that one. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "Death (<s>mṛtyu</s>)," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.14 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.14 tama eva yasyāyatanam /
tama iti śārvadyandhakāraḥ parigṛhyate /
children.translated_text: By 'darkness' is meant the darkness that pervades everywhere.

children.text: adhyātmaṃ chāyāmayo 'jñānamayaḥ puruṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: At the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>), the <s>puruṣa</s> made of shadow is the one made of ignorance (<s>ajñānamaya</s>).

children.text: tasya kā devateti? mṛtyuriti hovāca /
children.translated_text: "What is his deity?" "Death," he said.

children.text: mṛtyurapidaivataṃ tasya niṣpattikāraṇam //14//
children.translated_text: Death is also the cosmic deity that is the cause of his production. ||14||
[Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.14:] Darkness alone is his abode.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.15
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.15]

children.text:
rūpāṇy eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyam ādarśe puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
satyam iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.15 ||
children.translated_text: "Forms (<s>rūpa</s>) alone are his abode, the heart is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He who is this <s>puruṣa</s> in the mirror — he is that one. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "Truth (<s>satya</s>)," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.15 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.15 rūpāṇyeva yasyāyatanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.15:] Forms alone are his abode.

children.text: pūrva sādhārāni rūpāṇyuktāni, iha tu prakāśakāni viśiṣṭāni rūpāṇi gṛhyante /
children.translated_text: Previously, forms in general were mentioned; here, however, specifically luminous forms are taken.

children.text: rūpāyatanasya devasya viśeṣāyatanaṃ pratibimbādhāramādarśādi tasya kā devateti? asuriti hovāca /
children.translated_text: For the god whose abode is form, the specific abode is a mirror and the like, which is the substrate of a reflection. "What is his deity?" "The vital force (<s>asu</s>)," he said.

children.text: tasya pratibimbākhyasya puruṣasya niṣpattirasoḥ prāṇāt //15//
children.translated_text: The production of that <s>puruṣa</s> known as the reflection is from the vital force (<s>asu</s>), that is, from <s>Prāṇa</s>. ||15||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.16
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.16]

children.text:
āpa eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyaṃ apsu puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
varuṇa iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.16 ||
children.translated_text: "Water (<s>āpas</s>) alone is his abode, the heart is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He who is this <s>puruṣa</s> in the waters — he is that one. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "<s>Varuṇa</s>," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.16 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.16 āpa eva yasya āyatanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.16:] Water alone is his abode.

children.text: sādhāraṇāḥ sarvā āpa āyatanaṃ vāpīkūpataḍāgādyāśrayāsvapsu viśeṣāvasthānam /
children.translated_text: All waters in general are the abode, while the specific dwelling is in the waters contained in wells, ponds, tanks, and such reservoirs.

children.text: tasya kā devateti? varuṇa iti;varuṇāt saṅghātakarñyodhyātmamāpa eva vāpyādyapaṃ niṣpattikāraṇam //16//
children.translated_text: "What is his deity?" "<s>Varuṇa</s>," he said; for from <s>Varuṇa</s>, the binding agent, at the individual level (<s>adhyātma</s>), the waters in wells and such are the cause of the production of the waters. ||16||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.17
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.17]

children.text:
reta eva yasyāyatanaṃ hṛdayaṃ loko mano jyotir yo vai taṃ puruṣaṃ vidyāt sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ sa vai veditā syāt |
yājñavalkya veda vā ahaṃ taṃ puruṣaṃ sarvasyātmanaḥ parāyaṇaṃ yam āttha |
ya evāyaṃ putramayaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
vadaiva śākalya tasya kā devateti |
prajāpatir iti hovāca || BrhUp_3,9.17 ||
children.translated_text: "Semen (<s>retas</s>) alone is his abode, the heart is his world, mind is his light — whoever truly knows that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, he indeed would be a knower." "<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I do know that <s>puruṣa</s> who is the ultimate resort of every self, of whom you speak. He who is this <s>puruṣa</s> made of offspring (<s>putramaya</s>) — he is that one. Speak on, <s>Śākalya</s> — what is his deity?" "<s>Prajāpati</s> (the Lord of Creatures)," he said. || BṛhUp 3.9.17 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.17 reta eva yasyāyatanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.17:] Semen alone is his abode.

children.text: ya evāyaṃ putramayo viśeṇāyatanaṃ reta āyatanasya, putrasya iti ca asthimañjāśukāṇi piturjātāni /
children.translated_text: He who is this one made of offspring — the specific abode of the one whose abode is semen is the son, and his bones, marrow, and semen are born from the father.

children.text: tasya kā devateti? prajāpatiriti hovāca /
children.translated_text: "What is his deity?" "<s>Prajāpati</s>," he said.

children.text: prajñāpatiḥ pitocyate, pitṛto hi putrasyotpattiḥ //17//
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> here refers to the father, for from the father is the birth of the son. ||17||

children.text:
aṣṭakā devalokapuruṣabhedena tridhā tridhā ātmānaṃ pravibhajyāvasthita ekaiko devaḥ prāṇabheda evopāsanārtha vyapadiṣṭaḥ /
adhunā digvibhāgena pañcadhā pravibhaktasya ātmānayupasaṃhārārthamāha /
tūṣṇīmbhūtaṃ śākalyaṃ yājñavalkyo graheṇevāveśayannāha -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Each of the eight gods, having divided himself in three ways — as the cosmic deity, the world, and the <s>puruṣa</s> — abides thus; each one is taught as a modification of <s>Prāṇa</s> for the purpose of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>). Now, in order to gather back the Self that has been divided fivefold by the directions, he speaks. Addressing the silent <s>Śākalya</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> speaks as if seizing him with a counter-question —

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.18
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.18]

children.text:
śākalyeti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
tvāṃ svid ime brāhmaṇā aṅgārāvakṣayaṇam akratā3 iti || BrhUp_3,9.18 ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Śākalya</s>," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, "did these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> make you their coal-remover?" || BṛhUp 3.9.18 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.18 śākalyeti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.18:] "O <s>Śākalya</s>," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: tvāṃ sviditi vitarke, ime nūnaṃ brāhmaṇāḥ, aṅgārāvakṣaṇam - aṅgārā avakṣīyante yasmin sandaṃśādau tadaṅgārāvakṣaṇam - tadā nūnaṃ tvāmakrata kṛtavanto brāhmaṇāḥ, tvaṃ tu tanna budhyase ātmānaṃ mayā dahyamānam ityabhiprāyaḥ //18//
children.translated_text: The word <s>svit</s> indicates conjecture. "These <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> surely made you the coal-remover (<s>aṅgārāvakṣaṇa</s>)" — the instrument for removing hot coals, such as tongs, is called <s>aṅgārāvakṣaṇa</s> — "they surely made you that, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, but you do not realize that you yourself are being burnt by me" — that is the purport. ||18||

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.19
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 3.9.19]

children.text:
yājñavalkyeti hovāca śākalyaḥ |
yad idaṃ kurupañcālānāṃ brāhmanān atyavādīḥ kiṃ brahma vidvān iti |
diśo veda sadevāḥ sapratiṣṭhā iti |
yad diśo vettha sadevāḥ sapratiṣṭhāḥ || BrhUp_3,9.19 ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>," said <s>Śākalya</s>, "since you have talked down the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Kuru</s>-<s>Pañcāla</s> region, what <s>Brahman</s> do you know?" "I know the directions along with their deities and their supports." "Since you know the directions along with their deities and their supports —" || BṛhUp 3.9.19 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.19 yājñavalkyeti hovāca śākalyaḥ - yadidaṃ kuruṣañcalānāṃ brāhmaṇānatyavādīḥ - atyuktavānasi - svayaṃ bhītāstvāmaṅgārāvakṣayaṇaṃ kṛtavanta iti - kiṃ brahma vidvān sannevamadhikṣipasi brāhmaṇān? yājñavalkya āha - brahma vijñānaṃ tāvadidaṃ mama, kiṃ tat? diśo veda digviṣayaṃ vijñānaṃ jāne /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 3.9.19:] "O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>," said <s>Śākalya</s>: "Since you have talked down the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Kuru</s>-<s>Pañcāla</s> region" — you have spoken them down, that is, you have outspoken them — "they, being afraid themselves, made you the coal-remover" — "Do you thus look down upon the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> because you know <s>Brahman</s>?" <s>Yājñavalkya</s> replied: "This much knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> is mine — what is it? I know the directions — I possess knowledge concerning the directions."

children.text: tacca na kvalaṃ diśa, eva, sadevā devaiḥ saha digadhiṣṭhātṛbhiḥ, kiñca sapratiṣṭhitāḥ pratiṣṭhābhiśca saha /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And not merely the directions alone, but 'with deities' — together with the presiding deities of the directions; and moreover, 'with supports' — together with their foundations.

children.text: itara āha - yad yadi diśo vettha sadevāḥ, sapratiṣṭhā iti, saphalaṃ yadi vijñānaṃ tvayā pratijñātam //19//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The other [<s>Śākalya</s>] said: 'If you know the directions — with deities, with supports — [then] if the knowledge you claim bears fruit' — [proceed]. (19)

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.20
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.20]

children.text:
kiṃdevato 'syāṃ prācyāṃ diśy asīti |
ādityadevata iti |
sa ādityaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti |
cakṣuṣīti |
kasmin nu cakṣuḥ pratiṣṭhitam iti |
rūpeṣv iti |
cakṣuṣā hi rūpāṇi paśyati |
kasmin nu rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitānīti |
hṛdaya iti hovāca |
hṛdayena hi rūpāṇi jānāti |
hṛdaye hy eva rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitāni bhavantīti |
evam evaitad yājñavalkya || BrhUp_3,9.20 ||
children.translated_text: 'What is your deity in this eastern direction?' 'The <s>Āditya</s> (sun) deity.' 'In what is that <s>Āditya</s> established?' 'In the eye.' 'In what is the eye established?' 'In forms — for by the eye one sees forms.' 'In what are forms established?' 'In the heart,' he said, 'for by the heart one knows forms; forms are indeed established in the heart.' 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.20)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.20 kindevataḥ kā devatāsya tava digbhṛtasya /
asau hi yājñavalkyo hṛdayamātmānaṃ dikṣu pañcadhā vibhaktaṃ digātmabhūtam, taddvāreṇa sarvaṃ jagadātmatvenopagamya, ahamasmi digātmeti vyavasthitaḥ pūrvābhimukhaḥ - sapratiṣṭhāvacanād, yathā yājñavalkyasya pratijñā tathaiva pṛcchati - kindevatastvamasyāṃ diśyasīti /
sarvatra hi vede yāṃ yāṃ devatādvapāste, ihaiva tadbhūtastāṃ tāṃ pratipadyata iti;tathā ca vakṣyati -'devo bhūtvā devānapyeti'(bṛ.u.4 / 1 / 2) iti /
asyāṃ prācyāṃ kā devatā digātmanastavādhiṣṭhātrī, kayā devatayā tvaṃ prāpīdigrūpeṇa sampanna ityarthaḥ /
itara āha - ādityadevata iti /
prācyāṃ diśi mama ādityo devatā, so 'hamādityadevataḥ /
sadevā ityetaduktam, sapratiṣṭhā iti tu vaktavyamityāha - sa ādityaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti? cakṣuṣīti /
adhyātmataścakṣuṣa ādityo niṣpanna iti hi mantrabrāhmaṇavādāḥ -"cakṣoḥ sūryo ajāyata" (yaju.31 / 12) "cakṣuṣa ādityaḥ"(ai.u.1 / 4) ityādayaḥ /
kāryaṃ hi kāraṇe pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati /
kasminnu cakṣuḥ pratiṣṭhitamiti? rūpeṣviti;rūpagrahaṇāya hi rūpātmakaṃ cakṣu rūpeṇa prayuktam;yairhi rūpaiḥ prayuktaṃ tairātmagrahaṇāyārabdhaṃ cakṣuḥ saha prācyā diśā saha tatsthaiḥ sarvai rūpeṣu pratiṣṭhitam /
cakṣuṣā saha prācī dik sarve rūpabhūtā, tāni ca kasminnu rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitānīti? hṛdaya iti hovāca /
hṛdayārabdhāni rūpāṇi /
rūpākāreṇa hi hṛdayaṃ pariṇatam /
yasmād hṛdayena hi rūpāṇi sarvo loko jānāti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the entire world knows forms by the heart.

children.text: hṛdayamiti buddhimanaso ekīkṛtya nirdeśaḥ, tasmād hṛdaye hyeva rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitāni /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Heart' is a designation combining the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) and mind (<s>manas</s>) as one; therefore, forms are indeed established in the heart.

children.text: hṛdayena hi smaraṇaṃ bhavati rūpāṇāṃ vāsanātmanām;tasmād hṛdaye rūpāṇi pratiṣṭhitāni ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For remembrance of forms — which exist in the nature of residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) — occurs through the heart; therefore, forms are established in the heart — this is the meaning.

children.text: evamevaitad yājñavalkya //20//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (20)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.20:] 'What is the deity' — what deity of yours, you who bear the directions? For <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, taking the heart as the <s>Ātman</s>, having divided himself fivefold among the directions, having become one whose nature is the directions, through that [identification] having attained the entire universe as his own self, is established as 'I am the self of the directions,' facing the east. Because of the statement 'with supports,' [<s>Śākalya</s>] asks just as <s>Yājñavalkya</s> has claimed: 'What deity are you in this direction?' For everywhere in the <s>Veda</s>, whatever deity one meditates upon, having become that very [deity] right here, one attains it; and thus [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] himself will say: 'Having become a god, he goes to the gods' (BṛUp 4.1.2). 'In this eastern [direction], what deity presides over you as the self of the directions? By what deity have you become accomplished in the form of the direction?' — this is the meaning. The other replied: '<s>Āditya</s> (sun) deity.' 'In the eastern direction, <s>Āditya</s> is my deity; I am one whose deity is <s>Āditya</s>.' 'With deities' — this has been stated. 'With supports' remains to be stated — hence he asks: 'In what is that <s>Āditya</s> established?' 'In the eye.' From the standpoint of the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>), the sun is produced from the eye — for the <s>mantra</s> and <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> passages say: 'From the eye the sun was born' (YajuVe 31.12); 'From the eye, the <s>Āditya</s>' (AiUp 1.4) and the like. For the effect is established in the cause. 'In what is the eye established?' 'In forms' — for the eye, being of the nature of form, is employed by form for the purpose of grasping form. Those forms by which the eye is employed — the eye, having been engaged for the purpose of self-apprehension by them, together with the eastern direction and all [forms] situated therein, is established in forms. The eastern direction together with the eye — all have the nature of forms. 'In what then are forms established?' 'In the heart,' he said. Forms originate from the heart. For the heart has transformed itself in the shape of forms.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.21
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.21]

children.text:
kiṃdevato 'syāṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśy asīti |
yamadevata iti |
sa yamaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti |
yajña iti |
kasmin nu yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti |
dakṣiṇāyām iti |
kasmin nu dakṣiṇā pratiṣṭhiteti |
śraddhāyām iti |
yadā hy eva śraddhatte 'tha dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti |
śraddhāyāṃ hy eva dakṣiṇā pratiṣṭhiteti |
kasmin nu śraddhā pratiṣṭhiteti |
hṛdaya iti hovāca |
hṛdayena hi śraddhām |
hṛdaye hy eva śraddhā pratiṣṭhitā bhavatīti |
evam evaitad yājñavalkya || BrhUp_3,9.21 ||
children.translated_text: 'What is your deity in this southern direction?' '<s>Yama</s> deity.' 'In what is that <s>Yama</s> established?' 'In the sacrifice.' 'In what is the sacrifice established?' 'In the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).' 'In what is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> established?' 'In faith (<s>śraddhā</s>)' — for when one has faith, then one gives the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is indeed established in faith. 'In what is faith established?' 'In the heart,' he said, 'for by the heart one knows faith; faith is indeed established in the heart.' 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.21)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.21 kindevato 'syāṃ dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśyasīti pūrvavat /
dakṣiṇāyāṃ diśi kā devatā tatra? yamadevata iti, yamo devatā mama dakṣiṇādigbhūtasya /
sa yamaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti? yajña iti - yajñe kāraṇe pratiṣṭhito yamaḥ saha diśā /
kathaṃ punaryajñasya kāryaṃ yamaḥ? ityucyate - ṛtvigbhirniṣpādito yajño dakṣiṇayā yajamānastebhyo yajñaṃ niṣkrīya tena yajñena dakṣiṇāṃ diśaṃ saha yamenābhijayati /
tena yajñe yamaḥ kāryatvāt pratiṣṭhitaḥ saha dakṣiṇayā diśā /
kasminnu yajñaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti? dakṣiṇāyāmiti - dakṣiṇayā sa na ṣkrīyate, tena dakṣiṇākāryaṃ yajñaḥ /
kasminnu dakṣiṇā pratiṣṭhiteti? śraddhāyāmiti - śraddhā nāma ditsutvam āstikyabuddhibhaktisahitā /
kathaṃ tasyāṃ pratiṣṭhitā dakṣiṇā? yasmād yadā hyeva śraddhatte 'tha dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti;nāśraddadhad dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti;tasmācchraddhāyāṃ hyeva dakṣiṇā pratiṣṭhiteti /
kasminnu śraddhā pratiṣṭhiteti? hṛdaya iti hovāca - hṛdayasya hi vṛttiḥ śraddhā yasmāt, hṛdayena hi śraddhāṃ jānāti, vṛttiśca vṛttimati pratiṣṭhitā bhavati /
tasmād hṛdaye hyeva śraddhā pratiṣṭhitā bhavatīti /
evamevaitad yājñavalkya //21 // //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (21)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.21:] 'What is your deity in this southern direction?' — as before. 'In the southern direction, what is the deity there?' '<s>Yama</s> deity' — <s>Yama</s> is the deity of mine who has become the self of the southern direction. 'In what is that <s>Yama</s> established?' 'In the sacrifice' — <s>Yama</s>, together with the direction, is established in the sacrifice, which is its cause. But how is <s>Yama</s> the effect of sacrifice? It is explained thus: the sacrifice is accomplished by the priests (<s>ṛtvijs</s>); the patron of the sacrifice (<s>yajamāna</s>) pays for the sacrifice from the priests by means of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; by that sacrifice he conquers the southern direction together with <s>Yama</s>. Therefore, <s>Yama</s>, being the effect of sacrifice, is established in it, together with the southern direction. 'In what is the sacrifice established?' 'In the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>' — the sacrifice is paid for by the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; therefore the sacrifice is the effect of the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. 'In what is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> established?' 'In faith (<s>śraddhā</s>)' — <s>śraddhā</s> is the disposition of willingness to give, combined with belief in the existence [of the other world] and devotion. How is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> established in it? Because 'when one has faith, then one gives the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>' — one who lacks faith does not give the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>; therefore, the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> is indeed established in faith. 'In what is faith established?' 'In the heart,' he said — for faith is a function of the heart; 'for by the heart one knows faith'; and a function is established in that which possesses the function. Therefore, 'faith is indeed established in the heart.'

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.22
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.22]

children.text:
kiṃdevato 'syāṃ pratīcyāṃ diśy asīti |
varuṇadevata iti |
sa varuṇaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti |
apsv iti |
kasmin nv āpaḥ pratiṣṭhitā iti |
retasīti |
kasmin nu retaḥ pratiṣṭhitam iti |
hṛdaya iti |
tasmād api pratirūpaṃ jātam āhur hṛdayād iva sṛpto hṛdayād iva nirmita iti |
hṛdaye hy eva retaḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavatīti |
evam evaitad yājñavalkya || BrhUp_3,9.22 ||
children.translated_text: 'What is your deity in this western direction?' '<s>Varuṇa</s> deity.' 'In what is that <s>Varuṇa</s> established?' 'In the waters.' 'In what are the waters established?' 'In semen.' 'In what is semen established?' 'In the heart.' 'Therefore, even of one born resembling [the father], they say: he has slipped from the heart, he is fashioned from the heart. For semen is indeed established in the heart.' 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.22)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.22 kingadevato 'syāṃ pratīcyāṃ diśyasīti? tasyāṃ varuṇo 'dhidevatā mama /
sa varuṇaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti? apsviti - apāṃ hi varuṇaḥ kāryam,"śraddhā vā āpaḥ" "śraddhāto varuṇamasṛjata"iti śruteḥ /
kasminnvāpaḥ pratiṣṭhitā iti? retasīti -"retaso hyāpaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ"iti śruteḥ /
kasminni retaḥ pratiṣṭhitamiti? hṛdaya iti - yasmād hṛdayasya kāryaṃ retaḥ /
kāmo hṛdayasya vṛttiḥ kāmino hi hṛdayādreto 'dhiskandati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Desire is a function of the heart; for from the heart of one who has desire, semen leaps forth.

children.text: tasmādapi pratirūpamanurūpaṃ putraṃ jātamāhurlokikāḥ - asya piturhṛdayādivāyaṃ putraḥ supto viniḥsṛtaḥ, hṛdayādiva nirmito yathā suvarṇena nirmitaḥ kuṇḍalaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, even of a son born resembling [the father] — a son who conforms [to the parent's appearance] — people in the world say: 'This son has, as it were, slipped forth from this father's heart; he is, as it were, fashioned from the heart' — just as an earring is fashioned from gold.

children.text: tasmāt hṛdaye hyeva retaḥ pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, semen is indeed established in the heart.

children.text: evamevaitat yājñavalkya //22..//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (22)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.22:] 'What is your deity in this western direction?' '<s>Varuṇa</s> is the presiding deity of mine [in that direction].' 'In what is that <s>Varuṇa</s> established?' 'In the waters' — for <s>Varuṇa</s> is the effect of the waters; [as the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'Faith is the waters'; 'From faith he created <s>Varuṇa</s>.' 'In what are the waters established?' 'In semen' — [as the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'From semen the waters were created.' 'In what is semen established?' 'In the heart' — because semen is the effect of the heart.

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.23
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.23]

children.text:
kiṃdevato 'syām udīcyāṃ diśy asīti |
somadevata iti |
sa somaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti |
dīkṣāyām iti |
kasmin nu dikṣā pratiṣṭhiteti |
satya iti |
tasmād api dīkṣitam āhuḥ satyaṃ vadeti |
satye hy eva dīkṣā pratiṣṭhiteti |
kasmin nu satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitam iti |
hṛdaya iti hovāca |
hṛdayena hi satyaṃ jānāti |
hṛdaye hy eva satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavatīti |
evam evaitad yājñavalkya || BrhUp_3,9.23 ||
children.translated_text: 'What is your deity in this northern direction?' '<s>Soma</s> deity.' 'In what is that <s>Soma</s> established?' 'In <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration).' 'In what is <s>dīkṣā</s> established?' 'In truth (<s>satya</s>).' 'Therefore, they say to one who has been consecrated: speak the truth. For <s>dīkṣā</s> is indeed established in truth.' 'In what is truth established?' 'In the heart,' he said. 'For by the heart one knows truth. Truth is indeed established in the heart.' 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (BṛUp 3.9.23)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.23 kindevato 'syāmudīcyāṃ diśyasīti? somadevata iti - soma iti latāṃ somaṃ devatāṃ caikīkṛtya nirdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.23:] 'What is your deity in this northern direction?' '<s>Soma</s> deity' — <s>Soma</s> here is a designation combining the <s>Soma</s> plant and the <s>Soma</s> deity as one.

children.text: sa somaḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti? dīkṣāyāmiti - dīkṣito hi yajamānaḥ somaṃ krīṇāti, krītena someneṣṭvā jñānavānuttarāṃ diśaṃ pratipadyate somadevatādhiṣṭhitāṃ saumyām /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'In what is that <s>Soma</s> established?' 'In <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration)' — for the consecrated patron purchases the <s>Soma</s>; having sacrificed with the purchased <s>Soma</s>, and having acquired knowledge, he attains the northern direction, which is presided over by the <s>Soma</s> deity, which is auspicious (<s>saumya</s>).

children.text: kasminnu dīkṣā pratiṣṭhiteti!satya iti;katham? yasmāt satye dīkṣā pratiṣṭhitā, tasmādapi dīkṣitamāhuḥ - satyaṃ vadeti;kāraṇabhreṣo kāryabhreṣo mā bhūditi;satye hyeva dīkṣā pratiṣṭhitamiti? hṛdaya iti hovāca;hṛdayena hi satyaṃ jānāti;tasmād hṛdaye hyeva satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'In what is <s>dīkṣā</s> established?' 'In truth (<s>satya</s>)' — how so? Because <s>dīkṣā</s> is established in truth; therefore, they say to one who has been consecrated: 'Speak the truth' — lest a deviation from the cause lead to a deviation from the effect. '<s>Dīkṣā</s> is indeed established in truth.' 'In what is truth established?' 'In the heart,' he said. 'For by the heart one knows truth.' Therefore, 'truth is indeed established in the heart.'

children.text: evamevaitad yājñavalkya //23//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even so it is, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' (23)

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.24
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.24]

children.text:
kiṃdevato 'syāṃ dhruvāyāṃ diśy asīti |
agnidevata iti |
so 'gniḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti |
vācīti |
kasmin nu vāk pratiṣṭhiteti |
hṛdaya iti |
kasmin nu hṛdayaṃ pratiṣṭhitam iti || BrhUp_3,9.24 ||
children.translated_text: 'What is your deity in this upward (<s>dhruvā</s>) direction?' '<s>Agni</s> (fire) deity.' 'In what is that <s>Agni</s> established?' 'In speech.' 'In what is speech established?' 'In the heart.' 'In what is the heart established?' (BṛUp 3.9.24)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.24 kindevato 'syāṃ diśyasīti /
meroḥ samantato vasatāmavyabhicārādūrdhvā dig dhruvetyucyate /
agnidevata iti - ūrdhvāyāṃ hi prakāśabhūyastvam, prakāśaścāgniḥ /
so 'gniḥ kasmin pratiṣṭhita iti? vācīti /
kasminni vāk pratiṣṭhiteti? hṛdaya iti /
tatra yājñavalkyaḥ sarvāsu dikṣu vipasṛtena hṛdayena sarvāṃ diśa ātmatvenābhisampannaḥ;sadevāḥ sapratiṣṭhitā diśa ātmabhūtāstasya nāmarūpakarmātmabhūtasya yājñavalkyasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, by means of the heart that has spread out into all directions, is accomplished as the self of all directions. The directions, with deities and with supports, are of the nature of the self of <s>Yājñavalkya</s> — who has the nature of name, form, and action.

children.text: yad rūpaṃ tat prācyā diśā saha hṛdayabhūtaṃ yājñavalkyasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is form — that, together with the eastern direction, has become of the nature of the heart of <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: yat kevalaṃ karma putrotpādanalakṣaṇaṃ ca yānasahitaṃ ca sahaphenādhiṣṭhātrībhiśca devatābhirdakṣiṇāpratīcyudīcyaḥ karmaphalātmikā hṛdayameva āpannāstasya, dhruvayā diśā saha nāma sarvaṃ vāgdvāreṇa hṛdayameva āpannam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is mere action — including the activity of procreation and the means of [ritual] journey — together with the presiding deities — the southern, western, and northern [directions], having the nature of the fruits of action, have entered the heart itself; and together with the fixed direction (<s>dhruvā</s>), all name, through the medium of speech, has entered the heart itself.

children.text: etāvaddhīdaṃ sarvam, yaduta rūpaṃ vā karma vā nāma veti tat sarvaṃ hṛdayameva, tat sarvātmakaṃ hṛdayaṃ pṛcchyate - kasminnu hṛdayaṃ pratiṣṭhitamiti //24//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This much alone constitutes everything — namely, form, action, and name. All of that is the heart itself. That heart, which is the self of all, is now questioned: 'In what is the heart established?' (24)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.24:] 'What is your deity in this direction?' Since [the upward direction] is invariable for all who dwell around <s>Meru</s>, the upward direction is called '<s>dhruvā</s>' (fixed). '<s>Agni</s> deity' — for in the upward direction, luminosity predominates, and luminosity is <s>Agni</s>. 'In what is that <s>Agni</s> established?' 'In speech.' 'In what is speech established?' 'In the heart.'

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.25
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.25]

children.text:
ahalliketi hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
yatraitad anyatrāsman manyāsai |
yad dhy etad anyatrāsmat syāc chvāno vainad adyur vayāṃsi vainad vimathnīrann iti || BrhUp_3,9.25 ||
children.translated_text: 'You are a fool (<s>ahallika</s>),' said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, 'if you think it is anywhere other than in ourselves. For if it were anywhere other than in us, dogs would eat it, or birds would tear it apart.' (BṛUp 3.9.25)

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.25 ahalliketi hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ, nāmāntareṇa sambodhanaṃ kṛtavān /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.25:] '<s>Ahallika</s>' — said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, addressing [<s>Śākalya</s>] by another name.

children.text: yatra yasminkāle, etad hṛdayamātmāsya asmadasmatto vartata iti manyāsai manyase - yaddhi yadi hyetad hṛdayamanyatrāsmat syād bhavet, śvānau vainaccharīraṃ tadā adyuḥ, vayāṃsi vā pakṣiṇo vainad vimathnīran viloḍayeyuḥ vikarperanniti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'At the time when (<s>yatra</s>) — if you think that this heart, this self of ours, exists apart from us (<s>asmat</s>), outside us — if indeed (<s>yad dhi</s>) this heart were anywhere other than us, then dogs would eat this body, or birds would tear it apart, would rend it, would scatter it.'

children.text: tasmānmayi śarīre hṛdayaṃ pratiṣṭhitamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the heart is established in me, in the body — this is the meaning.

children.text: śarīrasyāpi nāmarūpakarmātmakatvāt hṛdaye pratiṣṭhitatvam //25//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since even the body has the nature of name, form, and action, it too is established in the heart. (25)

children.text: hṛdayaśarīrasyorevamanyenyapratiṣṭhoktā kāryakaraṇayoḥ atastvāṃ pṛcchāmi -
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, the mutual establishment of the heart and the body has been stated — of the effect and the instrument. 'Therefore, I ask you' —

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.26
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 3.9.26]

children.text:
kasmin nu tvaṃ cātmā ca pratiṣṭhitau stha iti |
prāṇa iti |
kasmin nu prāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti |
apāna iti |
kasmin nv apānaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti |
vyāna iti |
kasmin nu vyānaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti |
udāna iti |
kasmin nūdānaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti |
samāna iti |
sa eṣa neti nety ātmā |
agṛhyo na hi gṛhyate |
aśīryo na hi śīryate |
asaṅgo na sajyate |
asito na vyathate |
na riṣyati |
etāny aṣṭāv āyatanāny aṣṭau lokā add. aṣṭau devā aṣṭau puruṣāḥ |
sa yas tān puruṣān niruhya pratyuhyātyakrāmat taṃ tvaupaniṣadaṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchāmi |
taṃ cen me na vivakṣyasi mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatīti |
taṃ ha na mene śākalyas |
tasya ha mūrdhā vipapāta |
api hāsya parimoṣiṇo 'sthīny apajahrur anyan manyamānāḥ || BrhUp_3,9.26 ||
children.translated_text:
'In what are you and the self established?' 'In <s>prāṇa</s> (outbreath).' 'In what is <s>prāṇa</s> established?' 'In <s>apāna</s> (inbreath).' 'In what is <s>apāna</s> established?' 'In <s>vyāna</s> (diffused breath).' 'In what is <s>vyāna</s> established?' 'In <s>udāna</s> (upward breath).' 'In what is <s>udāna</s> established?' 'In <s>samāna</s> (equalizing breath).'
This is that self [described as] 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>). Ungraspable — for it is not grasped. Indestructible — for it is not destroyed. Unattached — for it does not become attached. Unfettered — it does not suffer. It is not injured.
These are the eight abodes, eight worlds, eight gods, eight persons. He who, having separated and re-assembled those persons, transcended them — that <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person I ask you about. If you will not explain him to me, your head will fall off.' <s>Śākalya</s> did not know him. His head fell off. And robbers carried away his bones, thinking them to be something else. // BṛhUp 3.9.26 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.26 kasminnu tvaṃ ca śarīramātmā ca tava hṛdayaṃ pratiṣṭhitau stha iti? prāṇa iti;dehātmānau prāṇe pratiṣṭhitau syātāṃ prāṇavṛttau /
kasminnu prāṇāḥ pratiṣṭhita iti apāna iti - sāpi prāṇavṛttiḥ prāgeva preyāt apānavṛttyā cenna nigṛhyeta /
kasminnvapānaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti? vyāna iti - sāpyapānavṛttiradha eva yāyāt prāṇavṛttiśca prāgeva, madhyasthayā cedvyānavṛttyā na nigṛhyeta /
kasminnu vyānaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti? udāna iti - sarvāstisro 'pi vṛttaya udāne kīlasthānīye cenna niruddhā, viṣvageveyuḥ /
kasminnūdānaḥ pratiṣṭhita iti? samāna iti - samānapratiṣṭhā hyetāḥ sarvā vṛttayaḥ /
etaduktaṃ bhavati - śarīrahṛdayavāyavo 'nyonyapratiṣṭhāḥ, saṅghātena niṣatā vartante vijñānamayārthaprayuktā iti /
sarvametad yena niyataṃ yasmin pratiṣṭhitamākāśāntamotaṃ ca protaṃ ca, tasya nirupādhikasya sākṣādaparokṣād brahmaṇo nirdeśaḥ katavya ityayamārambhaḥ /
sa eṣaḥ - sayo netinetīti nirdiṣṭo madhukāṇḍe, eṣa saḥ /
so 'yamātmāgṛhyo na gṛhyaḥ /
katham? yasmāt sarvakāryadharmātītaḥ, tasmādagṛhyaḥ /
kutaḥ? yasmānna hi gṛhyate /
yaddhi karaṇagocaraṃ vyākṛtaṃ vastu, tad grahaṇagocaram. idaṃ tu tadviparītamātmatattvam /
tathāśīryaḥ;yaddhi mūrtaṃ saṃhataṃ śarīrādi tacchīryate;ayaṃ tu tadviparīto 'to na hi śīryate /
tathāsaṅgo mūrto mūrtāntareṇa sambadhyamānaḥ sajyate 'yaṃ ca tadviparīto 'to na hi sajyate /
tathāsito 'baddhaḥ, yaddhi mūrta tad vadhyate;ayaṃ tu tadviparītatvādabaddhatvānna vyathate, ato na riṣyati - grahaṇaviśaraṇasambandhakāryadharmarahitatvānna riṣyati na hiṃsāmāpadyate na vinaśyatītyarthaḥ /
kramamatikramya aupaniṣadasya puruṣasya ākhyāyikāto 'pasṛtya śrutyā svena rūpeṇa tvarayā nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ, tataḥ punarākhyāyikāmevāśrityāha - etāni yānyuktānyaṣṭāvāyatanāni'pṛthivyeva yasyāyatanam'ityevamādīni, aṣṭau lokā agnilokādayaḥ, aṣṭau devāḥ amṛtamiti hovāca ityevamādayaḥ, aṣṭau puruṣāḥ śarīraḥ puruṣaḥ, ityādayaḥ, sa yaḥ kaścit tān puruṣāñśārīraprabhṛtīn niruhya niścayenohya garmayitvāṣṭacatuṣkabhedena lokasthitimupapādyaḥ, punaḥ prācīdigādidvāreṇa pratyuhya upasaṃhṛtya svātmani hṛdaye 'tyakrāmadatikrāntavānupādhidharma hṛdayādyātmatvam;svenaivātmanā vyavasthito ya aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣo 'śanāyādivarjitaḥ upaniṣatsveva vijñeyo nānyapramāṇagamyaḥ, taṃ tvā tvāṃ vidyābhimāninaṃ puruṣaṃ pṛcchāmi /
taṃ ced yadi me na vivakṣyasi vispaṣṭaṃ na kathayiṣyasi, mūrdhā te vipatiṣyatītyāha yājñavalkyaḥ /
taṃ tvaupaniṣadaṃ puruṣaṃ śākalyo na mene ha na vijñātavān kila tasya ha mūrdhā vipapāta vipatitaḥ /
samāptākhyāyakā /
śrutevacanaṃ taṃ ha na mena ityādi /
kiṃ cāpi hāsya parimoṣiṇastaskarā asthīnyapi saṃskārārtha śiṣyenīyamānāni gṛhān pratyapajahaḥ-apahratavantaḥ kinnimittam? anyad dhanaṃ nīyamānaṃ manyamānāḥ /
pūrvavṛttā hyākhyāyikeha sūcitā /
aṣṭādhyāya kila śākalyena yājñavalkyasya samānānta eva kila saṃvādo nivṛttaḥ;tatra yājñavalkyena śāpo dattaḥ-pure 'tithye mariṣyasi na te 'sthīni ca na gṛhān prāpsyantīti /
children.translated_text: It is said that in the eighth chapter, <s>Śākalya</s>'s dialogue with <s>Yājñavalkya</s> ended in an impasse; there, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> pronounced a curse: 'You shall die in a hostile city, and your bones shall not reach home.'

children.text: sa ha tathaiva mamāra /
children.translated_text: And he indeed died in that very manner.

children.text: tasya hāpyanvaḥ manyamānāḥ parimoṣiṇo 'thīnyapajahaḥ;tasmānnopavādī syāduta hyevaṃvit paro bhavatīti /
children.translated_text: And his [bones], thinking [them to be valuables], robbers carried away, thinking otherwise. Therefore, one should not speak ill [of a knower of <s>Brahman</s>]; for such a knower is indeed supreme.

children.text: saipā ākhyāyikā ācārārtha sūcitā vidyāstutaye ceha //26//
children.translated_text: This narrative has been alluded to for the purpose of [teaching] proper conduct and for the praise of knowledge. // 26 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.26: 'In what are you — the body — and the self — your heart — established?' 'In <s>prāṇa</s>' — the body and self are established in the activity of <s>prāṇa</s>.
'In what is <s>prāṇa</s> established?' 'In <s>apāna</s>' — that <s>prāṇa</s>-activity too would depart forward if it were not restrained by the <s>apāna</s>-activity.
'In what is <s>apāna</s> established?' 'In <s>vyāna</s>' — that <s>apāna</s>-activity too would go only downward, and the <s>prāṇa</s>-activity only forward, if they were not restrained by the <s>vyāna</s>-activity situated in the middle.
'In what is <s>vyāna</s> established?' 'In <s>udāna</s>' — all three activities, if not checked by <s>udāna</s> which serves as a pillar, would scatter in all directions.
'In what is <s>udāna</s> established?' 'In <s>samāna</s>' — for all these activities have <s>samāna</s> as their support.
What is stated [here] amounts to this: the body, heart, and vital airs are mutually established in one another; joined together in a composite, they function, impelled by the <s>vijñānamaya</s> (the one constituted of consciousness).
All this which is governed by him, in whom it is established, up to and including space, woven warp and woof — of that unconditioned, directly perceived, non-mediate <s>Brahman</s>, a description must be given — this is the commencement [of what follows].
'This is that' — that which was described as '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) in the Honey Chapter (<s>Madhukāṇḍa</s>) — this is that same [self].
This self is ungraspable (<s>agṛhya</s>) — not to be grasped. How so? Because it transcends all the properties of effects — therefore it is ungraspable. Why? Because it is indeed not grasped. For that which is a differentiated thing within the range of the sense-organs — that is within the range of grasping. But this self-nature is the opposite of that.
Similarly, indestructible (<s>aśīrya</s>) — for that which is material, composite, such as the body and the like, is destroyed; but this is the opposite — therefore it is indeed not destroyed.
Similarly, unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>) — a material thing, being in contact with another material thing, becomes attached; but this is the opposite — therefore it is indeed not attached.
Similarly, unfettered (<s>asita</s>), i.e., unbound — for that which is material is injured; but this, being the opposite and being unbound, does not suffer; therefore it is not injured — being devoid of the properties of grasping, destruction, attachment, and causal effect, it is not injured, does not suffer harm, does not perish — this is the meaning.
Having transcended the sequence [of questions], leaving the narrative aside, the <s>śruti</s> in its own voice hastily describes the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person. Then, reverting to the narrative again, [the text] says: 'These' — those that were stated — 'are the eight abodes,' [beginning with] 'earth indeed is its abode' and so forth; 'eight worlds' — the world of fire and the rest; 'eight gods' — [beginning with] 'the immortal, he said' and so forth; 'eight persons' — the embodied person and the rest. He who, having separated (<s>niruhya</s>) those persons beginning with the embodied one — having ascertained them by definite reasoning, having warmed up [the inquiry] through the eight groups of four — and having re-assembled (<s>pratyuhya</s>), i.e., withdrawn them through the gateway of the eastern direction and the rest, gathering them back into his own self in the heart — transcended (<s>atyakrāmat</s>) the properties of the limiting adjuncts such as the heart; the <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person — free from hunger and the like, to be known only through the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, not accessible through any other means of valid knowledge — 'I ask you about that person, you who pride yourself on your knowledge. If you do not explain him to me clearly, your head will fall off' — thus said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
<s>Śākalya</s> did not know (<s>na mene</s>) that <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person. His head fell off.
The narrative is concluded. The words of the <s>śruti</s> are: 'He did not know him' and so forth. And furthermore — 'robbers carried away his bones' — even the bones, which [his disciples] were carrying home for funeral rites, were stolen by robbers. Why? 'Thinking them to be something else' — thinking that what was being carried was wealth. For the previous [incident regarding] the narrative is alluded to here.

children.text:
yasya neti, netītyanyapratiṣedhadvāreṇa brahmaṇo nirdeśaḥ kṛtaḥ, tasya vidhimukhena kathaṃ nirdeśaḥ kartavyaḥ, iti punarākhyāyikāmeva āśrityāha mūlaṃ ca jagato vaktavyamiti /
ākhyāyikāsambandhastvavrahyavido brāhmaṇāñjitvā godhanaṃ irtavyamiti /
nyāyaṃ matvāha--
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Of that [self] whose description was given through the negation of other [attributes] by '<s>neti neti</s>' — how is its description to be given in a positive manner? — reverting again to the narrative, and [since] the root of the world must also be stated, [the text continues]. The connection with the narrative is [as follows]: thinking it proper that, having defeated the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> who are knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, the cattle-wealth should be distributed — he said:

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.27
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.27]

children.text:
atha hovāca -- brāhmaṇā bhagavanto yo vaḥ kāmayate sa mā pṛcchatu |
sarve vā mā pṛcchata |
yo vaḥ kāmayate taṃ vaḥ pṛcchāmi sarvān vā vaḥ pṛcchāmīti |
te ha brāhmaṇā na dadhṛṣuḥ || BrhUp_3,9.27 ||
children.translated_text: Then he said: 'Venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, whoever among you wishes, let him question me — or all of you question me. Whoever among you wishes — I shall question him; or I shall question all of you.' But those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> did not dare. // BṛhUp 3.9.27 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.27 atha hovāca /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.27: Then he said.

children.text: athānantaraṃ tūṣṇīmbhūteṣu brāhmaṇeṣu hovāca, he brāhemaṇā bhagavanta ityevaṃ sambodhya-yo vo yuṣmākaṃ madhye kāmayate icchati-yājñavalkyaṃ pṛcchāmīti, sa mā māmāgatya pṛcchat;sarve vā mā pṛcchata- sarve vā yūyaṃ mā māṃ pṛcchata /
children.translated_text: Then, when the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> had become silent, he said, addressing them: 'O venerable <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' — thus addressing them — 'whoever among you wishes, desires — [thinking] "I shall question <s>Yājñavalkya</s>" — let him come and question me; or let all of you question me — all of you question me.'

children.text: yo vaḥ kāmayate yājñavalkyo māṃ pṛcchatviti, taṃ vaḥ pṛcchami;sarvān vā vo yuṣmānahaṃ pṛcchāmi /
children.translated_text: 'Whoever among you wishes [thinking] "Let <s>Yājñavalkya</s> question me" — I shall question him; or I shall question all of you.'

children.text: te ha brāhmaṇā na dadhṛṣuḥ-te brāhmaṇā evamuktā api na pragalbhāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ kiñcidapi pratyuttaraṃ vaktum //27//
children.translated_text: But those <s>brāhmaṇas</s> did not dare — those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, thus addressed, did not become bold enough to say anything whatsoever in reply. // 27 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.28:1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.28, verse 1]

children.text:
tān haitaiḥ ślokaiḥ papraccha --
yathā vṛkṣo vanaspatis tathaiva puruṣo 'mṛṣā |
tasya lomāni parṇāni tvag asyotpāṭikā bahiḥ || BrhUp_3,9.28:1 ||
children.translated_text:
He questioned them with these verses:
Just as a tree, a lord of the forest, even so truly is man.
His hairs are its leaves; his skin is its outer bark. // BṛhUp 3.9.28:1 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.28:1 teṣu apragalbhabhūteṣu brāhmaṇeṣu tān haitairvakṣyamāṇaiḥ ślokaiḥ papraccha pṛṣṭavān /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.28:1: When the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> had become unable to speak boldly, he questioned them — asked them — with these verses that are about to be stated.

children.text: yathā loke vṛkṣo vanaspatiḥ, vṛkṣasya viśeṣaṇaṃ vanaspatiriti, tathaiva puruṣo 'mṛpā-amṛpā satyametat-tasya lomāni;tasya puruṣasya lomānītarasya vanaspateḥ parṇāni;tvagasyotpāṭikā vahiḥ-tvagasya puruṣasya itarasyotpāṭikā vanaspateḥ //1//
children.translated_text: Just as in the world a tree, a lord of the forest (<s>vanaspati</s>) — 'lord of the forest' being a qualifier of 'tree' — even so truly (<s>amṛṣā</s>) is man. His hairs — the hairs of this man are the leaves of the other, the tree. His skin is its outer bark (<s>utpāṭikā</s>) — the skin of this man is the outer bark of the other, the tree. // 1 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.28:2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.28, verse 2]

children.text:
tvaca evāsya rudhiraṃ prasyandi tvaca utpaṭaḥ |
tasmāt tad ātṛṇṇāt praiti raso vṛkṣād ivāhatāt || BrhUp_3,9.28:2 ||
children.translated_text: From his skin indeed, blood flows forth; [from] the bark, sap [oozes] when cut. Therefore, when wounded, [blood] flows from [a man] just as sap from a tree that has been struck. // BṛhUp 3.9.28:2 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.28:2 tvaca eva sakāśādasya puruṣasya rudhiraṃ prasyandi, vanaspateratvaca utpaṭaḥ-tvaca evotsphuṭati yasmāt;evaṃ sarvaṃ samānameva vanaspateḥ puruṣasya ca;tasmād ātṛṇṇāt hisitāt prati tad rudhiraṃ nirgacchati vṛkṣādivāhatācchinnād rasaḥ //2//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.28:2: From his skin indeed — from the skin of this man — blood flows forth; from the bark of the tree, sap bursts forth — because it oozes from the bark itself. Thus everything is the same between tree and man. Therefore, from one who is wounded (<s>ātṛṇṇa</s>), injured, that blood flows out — just as sap from a tree that has been struck, i.e., cut. // 2 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.28:3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.28, verse 3]

children.text:
māṃsāny asya śakarāṇi kināṭaṃ snāva tat sthiram |
asthīny antarato dāruṇi majjā majjopamā kṛtā || BrhUp_3,9.28:3 ||
children.translated_text: His flesh is the [tree's] wood-chips; the inner bark is the sinew — it is firm. The bones are the inner wood; the marrow is made in the likeness of marrow. // BṛhUp 3.9.28:3 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.28:3 evaṃ māṃsānyasya puruṣasya, vanaspatesyāni śakarāṇi śakalānītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.28:3: Thus, the flesh of this man [corresponds to] the wood-chips (<s>śakarāṇi</s>), meaning the splinters, of the tree.

children.text: kināṭaṃ vṛkṣasya, kināṭaṃ nāma śakalebhyo 'bhyantaraṃ valkalarūpaṃ kāṣṭhasaṃlagnam, tat snāva puruṣasya;tat sthiram-tacca kināṭaṃ snāvavad dṛḍhaṃ hi tat;asthīni puruṣasya, snāvno 'ntarato 'sthīni bhavanti;tathā kināṭasyābhyantarato dāruṇi kāṣṭhāni;majjā, majjeva vanaspateḥ puruṣasya ca majjopamā kṛtā, majjāyā upamāmajjopamā, nānyo viśeṣo 'stītyarthaḥ;yathā vanaspatermajjā tathā puruṣasya, yathā puruṣasya tathā vanaspateḥ //3//
children.translated_text: The inner bark (<s>kināṭa</s>) of the tree — <s>kināṭa</s> being the bark-like layer beneath the splinters, adhering to the wood — that corresponds to the sinew (<s>snāva</s>) of the man. It is firm — that inner bark is as firm as sinew. The bones of the man — [just as] within the sinew come the bones, so within the inner bark come the pieces of wood (<s>dāru</s>). The marrow — the marrow of the tree and of the man is made in the likeness of marrow (<s>majjopamā</s>); 'likeness of marrow' means 'having the semblance of marrow' — there is no other difference; just as the marrow of the tree, so of the man; just as the marrow of the man, so of the tree. // 3 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.28:4
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.28, verse 4]

children.text:
yad vṛkṣo vṛkṇo rohati mūlān navataraḥ punaḥ |
martyaḥ svin mṛtyunā vṛkṇaḥ kasmān mūlāt prarohati || BrhUp_3,9.28:4 ||
children.translated_text: If a tree, when felled, grows again from the root, newer than before — from what root does a mortal, felled by death, grow again? // BṛhUp 3.9.28:4 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.28:4 yad yadi vṛkṣo vṛkṇaśchinno rohati punaḥ punaḥ prarohatiprādurbhavati mūlāt punarnavataraḥ pūrvasmādabhinavataraḥ;yadetasmād viśeṇāt prāg vanaspateḥ puruṣasya ca, sarvaṃ sāmānyamavagatam;ayaṃ tu vanaspatau viśeṣo dṛśyate yacchinnasyaprarohaṇam;na tu puruṣe mṛtyunā vṛkṇe punaḥ prarohaṇaṃ dṛśyate;bhavitavyaṃ ca kutaścitprarohaṇena;tasmāda vaḥ pṛcchāmi-martyo manuṣyaḥ svinmṛtyunā vṛkṇaḥ kasmānmūlāt prarohati? mṛtasya puruṣasya kutaḥ prarohaṇamityarthaḥ //4//
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.28:4: If a tree, when felled, i.e., cut down, grows again — again sprouts, comes forth — from the root, again, newer than before, i.e., fresher than it was before. Before this particular [verse], the complete similarity between tree and man had been understood. But this particular difference is seen in the tree — namely, the sprouting again of what was cut. In man, however, when one is felled by death, no sprouting again is seen. Yet there must be some sprouting forth from somewhere. Therefore, I ask you: a mortal, a human being — felled by death — from what root does he sprout again? The meaning is: from what [source] is the regeneration of a dead person? // 4 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.28:5
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.28, verse 5]

children.text:
retasa iti mā vocata jīvatas tat prajāyate |
dhānāruha iva vai vṛkṣo 'ñjasā pretya sambhavaḥ || BrhUp_3,9.28:5 ||
children.translated_text: Do not say 'from semen' — for that is produced from one who is alive. A tree [can grow] from seed, like a sprout from grain. [But a man's] rebirth after dying is straightforward. // BṛhUp 3.9.28:5 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.28:5 yadi cedevaṃ vadatha-retamaḥ prarohatīti, mā vocata maivaṃ vaṣatumarhatha;kasmāt? yasmājjīvataḥ puruṣāttad retaḥ prajāyate, na mṛtāt /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.28:5: And if you say this — 'he sprouts again from semen' — do not say so, you ought not to say this. Why? Because that semen is produced from a living person, not from a dead one.

children.text: api ca dhānāruhaḥ, dhānā bījam, bījaruho /
children.translated_text: Moreover, <s>dhānāruha</s> — <s>dhānā</s> means seed; a <s>dhānāruha</s> is one that grows from seed.

children.text: pi vṛkṣo bhavati, na kevalaṃ kāṇḍaraha eva;ivaśabdo 'narthakaḥ, vai vṛkṣo 'jjasā sākṣāt pretya mṛtvāsambhavo dhānāto 'pi pretya sambhavo bhavedajjasā punarvanaspateḥ //5//
children.translated_text: The tree indeed grows [thus] — not merely from a trunk-sprout alone. The word '<s>iva</s>' is meaningless [here]. Indeed, a tree straightforwardly, having died, can be reborn even from a grain-seed. Thus the tree can be reborn after dying, straightforwardly. // 5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 3,9.28:6
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 3.9.28, verse 6]

children.text:
yat samūlam āvṛheyur vṛkṣaṃ na punar ābhavet |
martyaḥ svin mṛtyunā vṛkṇaḥ kasmān mūlāt prarohati || BrhUp_3,9.28:6 ||
children.translated_text: If they were to pull up a tree together with its root, it would not come into being again. From what root does a mortal, felled by death, grow again? // BṛhUp 3.9.28:6 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_3,9.28:6 yad yadi saha mūlena dhānyā vā āvṛheyurudyaccheparuyeyurvṛkṣam, na punarābhavet punarāgatya na bhavet /
children.translated_text: <s>BṛhUpBh</s> 3.9.28:6: If they were to pull up, uproot together with its roots and seed, a tree — it would not come into being again, would not return to existence.

children.text: tasmād vaḥ pṛcchāmi sarvasyaiva jagato mūlam sartyaḥ svinmṛtyunā vṛkṇaḥ kasmānmūlāt prarohati //6//
children.translated_text: Therefore, I ask you about the root of the entire world: a mortal, felled by death — from what root does he sprout again? // 6 //
