children.text:
BrhUpBh_3,9.28:7-8. jāta eveti manyadhvaṃ yadi kimanna praṣṭavyamiti-aniṣyamāṇasya hi sambhavaḥ praṣṭavyaḥ, na jātasya, ayaṃ tu jāta evātopasmin viṣaye praśna eva nopa'dyata iti cet-na, kiṃ tarhi? mṛtaḥ punarapi jāyata evānyathākṛtābhyāgamakṛtanāśaprasaṅgāt;ato vaḥ pṛcchāmi-ko nvenaṃ mṛtaṃ punarjanayet? tatra vijajñurbrāhmaṇāḥ-yato mṛtaḥ punaḥ prarohati jagato mūlaṃ na vijñātaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ;ato brahmiṣṭhatvād hratā gāvaḥ;yājñavalkyena jitābrāhmaṇāḥ /
samāptā ākhyāyikā /
yajjagato mūlam, yena ca śabdena sākṣād vyapadiśyate brahma, yad yājñavalkyo brāhmaṇān pṛṣṭavāṃstat svena rūpeṇa śrutirasyabhyamāha-vijñānaṃ vijñaptirvijñānam, tacca ānandam, na viṣayavijñānavad duḥkhānuvidvam, kiṃ tarhi? prasannaṃ śivamatulamanāyāsaṃnityatṛptame karasamityarthaḥ. kiṃ tad brahma umayaviśeṇavad rātiḥ-rāteḥ paṣṭhayatha prathamā, dhanasyetyarthaḥ, dhanasya dātuḥ karmakṛto yajamānasya parāyaṇaṃ parā gatiḥ karmaphalasya pradātṛ /
kiñca vyutthāyaiṣaṇābhyasyasminneva brahmāṇi tiṣṭhatyakarmakṛt, tad brahma vettīti tadvicca;tasya-tiṣṭhamānasya ca tadvidaḥ, brahmavida ityarthaḥ, parāyaṇamiti /
atredaṃ vicāryate-ānandaśabdo loke sukhavācī prasidvaḥ, atra ca brahmaṇo viśeṣaṇatvena ānandaśabdaḥ śrūyate-ānandaṃ brahmeti /
śrutyantare ca-"ānando brahmeti vyajānāt""ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān" "yadeṣa ākāśa ānando na syāta" "yo vai bhūmā tat sukham"iti ca;"eṣa parama ānandaḥ"ityevamādyāḥ /
saṃvedye ca sukhe ānandaśabdaḥ prasidvaḥ brahmānandaśca yadi saṃvedyaḥ syād yuktā ete brahmaṇyānandaśabdāḥ /
nanu ca śrutiprāmāṇyāt saṃvedyānandasvarūpameva brahma, kiṃ tatra vicāryam? iti na, virudvaśrutivākyadarśanāt--satyam, ānandaśabdo brahmaṇi śrūyate, vijñānapratiṣedhaścaikatve--"yatra tvasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyettatkena kaṃ vijānīyāt" "yatra nānyat paśyati nānyacchṛṇoti nānyadvijānāti sa bhūmā" "prājñenātmanā sampariṣvakto na bāhyaṃ kiñcana veda"ityādi;virudvaśrutivākyadarśanāt tena kartavyo vicāraḥ;tasmād yuktaṃ vedavākyarthanirṇayāya vicārayitum /
mokṣavādivipratipatteśca-sāṃkhyā vaiśeṣikāśca mokṣavādino nāsti mokṣe sukhaṃ saṃvedyamityevaṃ vipratipannāḥ;anye nigtiśayaṃ sukhaṃ svasaṃvadyamiti;kiṃ tāvad yuktam? ānandādiśravaṇāt"jakṣatakrīḍan ramamāṇaḥ"'sayāda pitṛlokakāmo bhavata' "yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit""sarvān kāmān samaśnute"ityādiśrutibhyo mokṣe sukhaṃ saṃvedyamiti /
nanvekatve kārakavimāgamāvād vijñānānupapattiḥ, kriyāyāścāne kakārakrasādhyātvād vijñānasya ca kriyātvāt /
naiṣa doṣaḥ;śabdaprāmāṇyād bhaved vijñānamānandaviṣaye;"vijñānamānandam"ityādīni ānandasvarūpasyāsaṃvedyatve 'nupapannāni vacanānītyavocāma /
nanu vacanenāpyagneḥ śaityamudakasya cauṣbhyaṃ na kriyate eva, jñāpakatvād vacanānām /
na ca deśāntare 'gniḥ śīta iti śakyate jñāpayitum;agamye vā deśāntare uṣṇamudakamiti /
na, pratyagātmanyānandavijñānadarśanāt;na'vijñānamānandam'itvevamādīnāṃ vacanānāṃ śīto 'gnirityādivākyavat pratyakṣādivirudvārthapratipādakatvām /
anubhūyate tvavirudvārthatā;sukhyahamiti sukhātmakamātmānaṃ svayameva vedayate;tasmāt sutarāṃ pratyakṣāvirudvārthatā;tasmādānandaṃ brahma vijñānātmakaṃ sat svayameva vedayate /
tathā ānandapratipādikāḥ śrutayaḥ samañjasāḥ syuḥ'jakṣat krīḍan ramamāṇaḥ' ityevamādyāḥ pūrvoktāḥ /
na, kāryakaraṇābhāve 'nupapattervijñānasya-śarīraviyogo hi mokṣa ātyantikaḥ;śarīrabhāve ca karaṇānupapattiḥ, āśrayābhāvāt;tataśca vijñānānupattiḥ, ākāryakaraṇatvāt;dehadyabhāve ca vijñānotpattau sarveṣāṃ kāryakaraṇopādānānarthakyaprasaṅgaḥ /
ekatvavirodhācca-paraṃ ced brahma ānandātmakamātmānaṃ nityavijñānatvānnityameva vijānīyāt, tanna, saṃsāryapi saṃsāravinirmuktaḥ svābhāvyaṃ pratipadyeta;jalāśaya ivodakāñjaliḥ kṣipto na pṛthaktvena vyavatiṣṭhate ānandātmakabrahmavijñānāya, tadā mukta ānandātmakamātmānaṃ vedayate ityetadanarthakaṃ vākyam /
atha brahmānandamanyāḥ san mukto vedayate, pratyagātmānaṃ ca, ahamasmyānandasvarūpa iti, tadaikatvavirodhaḥ, tathā ca sati sarvaśrutivirodhaḥ, tṛtīyā ca kalpanā nopapadyate /
kiñcānyat, brahmaṇaśca nirantarātmānandavijñāne vijñānāvijñānakalpanānarthakyam;nirantaraṃ cedātmānandaviṣayaṃ brahmaṇo vijñānam, tadeva tasya svabhāva ityātmānandaṃ vijānātīti kalpanānupapannā;atadvijñānaprasaṅge hi kalpanāyā arthavattvam, yathā ātmānaṃ paraṃ ca vettīti, na hīṣvādyāsaktamanaso nairantaryeṇoṣujñānājñānakalpanāyā arthavattvam /
atha vicchinnamātmānandaṃ vijānāti-vijñānasya ātmavijñānacchidre anyaviṣayatvaprasaṅgaḥ;ātmanaśya vikriyāvattvaṃ tataścānityatvaprasaṅgaḥ;tasmād vijñānamānandamiti svarūpānvākhyānaparaiva śrutiḥ, nātmānandasaṃvedyatvārtha /

'jakṣat krīḍan'ityādiśrutivirodho 'saṃvedyatva iti cet! na;sarvātmaikatve yathāprāptānuvāditvāt-muktasya sarvātmabhāve sati yatra kvacid yogiṣu deveṣu vā jakṣaṇādi prāptam, tad yathāprāptamevānūdyate-tattasyaiva sarvātmabhāvāditi sarvātmabhāvamokṣastutaye /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] If [<s>Brahman</s>'s bliss] is non-experiential, there would be a contradiction with <s>śrutis</s> like 'eating, playing, rejoicing' and the like! [Reply:] No — because, in the oneness of all selves, [these statements] merely restate what is already obtained: for the liberated one who has become the self of all, whatever eating, playing, and the like is found anywhere — in <s>yogins</s> or in gods — that is merely restated as already obtained, because that [eating and the like] belongs to him by virtue of his being the self of all — this is for the glorification of liberation as the state of being the self of all.

children.text: yathāprāptānuvaditve duḥkhitvamapīti cet-yogyādiṣu yathāprāptajakṣaṇādivat sthāvarādiṣu yathāprāptaduḥkhitvamapīti cet! na, nāmarūpakṛtakāryakaraṇopādhisamparkajanitabhrāntyadhyāropitatvāt sukhitvaduḥkhitvādiviśeṣasyeti parihratametat sarvam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] If [the text] merely restates what is already obtained, then suffering too would [have to be restated] — just as eating and the like are restated as already obtained in <s>yogins</s> and others, so too the suffering already obtained in plants and the like [should be restated]! [Reply:] No — because the attribution of the specific properties of happiness and suffering and the like is falsely superimposed through the delusion born from the contact with the limiting adjuncts of body and senses constituted by name and form — all this has been resolved.

children.text: virudvaśrutīnāṃ ca viṣayamavocāma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And we have stated the domains of the contradictory <s>śruti</s> texts.

children.text: tasmāt"eṣo 'sya parama ānandaḥ"itivat sarvāṣyānandavākyāni draṣṭavyāni //28//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, all the sentences about bliss should be understood in the same way as 'This is his supreme bliss' (BṛUp 4.3.32). (28)

[Commentary on BṛUp 3.9.28, continued:] If you think '[the world] is simply born [and that settles it]' — then what is there to ask? — for the origination of what does not yet exist is worth inquiring about, not [the origination] of what is already born; and since this [world] is indeed already born, no question arises on this subject. [Reply:] No — for what [is the case]? Having died, [the world] is born again — otherwise there would be the absurd consequence of the arrival of what was not made and the destruction of what was made. Therefore I ask you: who indeed causes this dead [being] to be born again? Thereupon the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> were silenced — because they did not know the root of the world, from which the dead sprouts forth again. Therefore, because of his being the most learned in <s>Brahman</s>, the cows were rightfully taken; the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> were defeated by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
The narrative is concluded.
That which is the root of the world, and the word by which <s>Brahman</s> is directly designated — that which <s>Yājñavalkya</s> had asked the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — the <s>śruti</s> now declares in its own voice: '<s>Vijñāna</s>' (consciousness) — cognition is consciousness, and that is <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) — not mixed with suffering like object-directed cognition; rather, it is serene, auspicious, incomparable, effortless, eternally satisfied, of one form — this is the meaning. What is that <s>Brahman</s>? — characterized like the ornament of <s>Umā</s>: '<s>rātiḥ</s>' — from the root '<s>rā</s>' (to give), sixth or first [declension], meaning: 'of wealth'; of the giver of wealth, the performer of rituals, the sacrificer — [<s>Brahman</s> is] the supreme goal (<s>parāyaṇa</s>), the highest destination, the bestower of the fruits of <s>karma</s>.
Moreover, one who, having risen up from desires, stands in this very <s>Brahman</s> without performing action — he knows that <s>Brahman</s> and is a knower of it (<s>tadvit</s>); and [<s>Brahman</s>] is the supreme goal of that one who stands [thus], the knower of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.
Here the following is to be investigated: the word '<s>ānanda</s>' (bliss) is well known in the world as denoting pleasure (<s>sukha</s>), and here too the word '<s>ānanda</s>' is heard as a qualifier of <s>Brahman</s> — '<s>Brahman</s> is bliss.' And in other <s>śruti</s> texts: 'He understood bliss as <s>Brahman</s>' (TaiUp 3.6); 'The knower of <s>Brahman</s>'s bliss' (TaiUp 2.9); 'If this space were not bliss' (TaiUp 2.7); 'That which is the infinite — that is happiness' (ChUp 7.23); 'This is the supreme bliss' (BṛUp 4.3.32) — and so forth.
Now, the word '<s>ānanda</s>' is well known [as referring to] experiential pleasure, and if <s>Brahman</s>'s bliss too were experiential, then these uses of the word '<s>ānanda</s>' for <s>Brahman</s> would be fitting. [Objection:] Since the authority of <s>śruti</s> [establishes that] <s>Brahman</s> is of the nature of experiential bliss, what is there to investigate? [Reply:] No — because contradictory <s>śruti</s> statements are observed. True, the word '<s>ānanda</s>' is heard [applied to] <s>Brahman</s>, but the negation of cognition is also [heard] in the context of oneness: 'But when everything has become the self alone, then by what would one see whom? By what would one know whom?' (BṛUp 2.4.14); 'Where one does not see another, does not hear another, does not know another — that is the Infinite' (ChUp 7.24.1); 'Embraced by the all-knowing self, one knows nothing external' (BṛUp 4.3.21) — and so forth. Because contradictory <s>śruti</s> statements are observed, investigation must be undertaken. Therefore, it is proper to investigate in order to determine the meaning of the Vedic sentences.
And because of the conflicting views among the teachers of <s>mokṣa</s>: the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s> and <s>Vaiśeṣikas</s>, who teach <s>mokṣa</s>, hold the conflicting view that 'there is no experiential pleasure in <s>mokṣa</s>'; others [hold] that 'there is unsurpassed self-experienced pleasure.' What then is correct? Because of the hearing [of terms like] '<s>ānanda</s>' and the like, [and from <s>śrutis</s> such as:] 'Eating, playing, rejoicing' (TaiUp 2.5); 'His desire is for the world of the fathers' (ChUp 8.2.1); 'Who is all-knowing, all-perceiving' (MuṇḍUp 1.1.9); 'He obtains all desires' (TaiUp 2.1) — from such <s>śrutis</s>, [one might conclude that] there is experiential pleasure in <s>mokṣa</s>.
[Objection:] But in oneness, because of the absence of the differentiation of agents, cognition is impossible — since action is accomplished through multiple agents, and cognition too is an action. [Reply:] This is not a fault — on the authority of scripture, cognition could exist regarding the object of bliss; [but] we have said that the statements '<s>vijñānam ānandam</s>' (consciousness is bliss) and the like are impossible if the nature of bliss is non-experiential. [Objection:] But even by [scriptural] statement, one cannot make fire cold or water hot, since statements are informative [not creative]. Nor can one inform [someone] that fire is cold in some other place; or that in some inaccessible place water is hot. [Reply:] No — because bliss-consciousness is observed in the inner self. The statements '<s>vijñānam ānandam</s>' and the like are not like the statement 'fire is cold,' conveying a meaning contradicted by perception and other [means of knowledge]. Rather, the non-contradicted meaning is experienced: 'I am happy' — one knows the self as of the nature of happiness by oneself. Therefore, all the more so, the meaning is not contradicted by perception. Therefore, <s>Brahman</s>, which is bliss and of the nature of consciousness, knows itself by itself.
Thus, the <s>śruti</s> statements that teach bliss — 'eating, playing, rejoicing' and the rest cited above — would be consistent.
[Reply:] No — because in the absence of body and senses, cognition is impossible. For <s>mokṣa</s> is the absolute separation from the body; and in the absence of the body, the senses are impossible, due to the absence of their substratum; and from that, cognition is impossible, because it is [produced] through body and senses; and if cognition were to arise in the absence of body and the rest, the absurd consequence would follow that the taking up of all bodies and senses would be purposeless.
And because of the contradiction with oneness: if the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, being of the nature of bliss, were to eternally know itself — because of its being eternally conscious — then even the <s>saṃsārin</s>, being released from <s>saṃsāra</s>, would revert to its natural state; just as a handful of water thrown into a reservoir does not persist as separate — [so too] for the purpose of <s>Brahman</s>'s knowing itself as of the nature of bliss. In that case, [the statement] 'then the liberated one experiences the self as of the nature of bliss' would be a meaningless sentence.
Alternatively, if the liberated one experiences the bliss of <s>Brahman</s> as another [entity], and also experiences the inner self — 'I am of the nature of bliss' — then there would be a contradiction with oneness; and in that case, all <s>śrutis</s> would be contradicted; and a third construction is not possible.
Moreover, if <s>Brahman</s> has an uninterrupted cognition of its own bliss, then the construction of 'knowing' and 'not-knowing' would be pointless; for if <s>Brahman</s>'s cognition regarding its own bliss is uninterrupted, that alone is its nature — and the construction 'it knows its own bliss' is untenable. Only in the case of the possibility of non-cognition would such a construction be meaningful — as in 'it knows itself and the other.' For one whose mind is continuously attached to sugar, the construction of continuously knowing or not knowing sugar is not meaningful.
Alternatively, if [<s>Brahman</s>] knows its own bliss intermittently, then in the gap between self-cognitions, there would be the possibility of cognition directed toward something other [than the self]; and the self would be subject to modification, and from that the consequence of non-eternality would follow. Therefore, the <s>śruti</s> '<s>vijñānam ānandam</s>' (consciousness is bliss) is solely directed at describing [<s>Brahman</s>'s] essential nature — not at [establishing] the experiential nature of its own bliss.

children.text: iti tṛtīyādhyāye navamaṃ śākalyabrāhmaṇam //1 //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth <s>Śākalya Brāhmaṇa</s> in the third chapter. (1)

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ //3//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter in the commentary on the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s>. (3)

children.text: ADHYAYA 4
children.translated_text: CHAPTER 4

children.text:
janako ha vaideha āsāñcakre /
asya sambandhaḥ- śarīrādyānaṣṭau puruṣānniruhya, pratyuhya punarhṛdaye, digbhedanena ca punaḥ pañcadhā vyāhya, hṛdaye pratyūhya, hṛdayaṃ śarīraṃ ca punaranyonyapratiṣṭhaṃ prāṇādipaḍhtavṛtyātmake samānākhye jagadātmanu sūtra upasaṃhṛtya, jagadātmani sūtra upasaṃhṛtya, jagadātmānaṃśarīrahṛdayasūtrāvasthamatikrāntavān ya aupaniṣadaḥ puruṣo neti netīti vyapadiṣṭaḥ, sa sākṣāñcopādānakāraṇasvarūpeṇa ca nirdiṣṭaḥ 'vijñānamānandam' iti /
tasyaiva vāgādidevatādvāreṇa punaradhigamaḥ kartavya ityadhigamanopāyāntarārtho 'yamārambho brāhmaṇadvayasya /
ākhyāyikā tvācārapradarśanārthā-
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> held court. Its connection [with the preceding is as follows]: having identified the eight <s>puruṣas</s> (persons) in the body and the like, having drawn them back into the heart, and again having distributed [them] fivefold through the differentiation of the directions, and having drawn [them back] into the heart, and having subsumed the heart, the body, and [everything] into the thread-self (<s>sūtrātman</s>) called <s>Samāna</s>, whose nature is the fivefold activity of <s>prāṇa</s> and the like, [which is] the self of the world — and having subsumed [all] into the self of the world — the <s>Aupaniṣada Puruṣa</s> (the person of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>) who has transcended the states of body, heart, and thread, designated by '<s>neti neti</s>' — he has been directly described, and also described through his nature as the material cause, by '<s>vijñānam ānandam</s>' (consciousness is bliss). The re-ascertainment of that very [<s>Brahman</s>] through the doorway of the deities of speech and the like is to be undertaken — this commencement of the two <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> [sections] is for the purpose of another means of ascertainment. The narrative, however, is for the purpose of demonstrating conduct.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,1.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.1.1]

children.text:
janako ha vaideha āsāṃ cakre |
atha ha yājñavalkya āvavrāja |
taṃ hovāca -- yājñavalkya kim artham acārīḥ paśūn icchan aṇvantānīti |
ubhayam eva saṃrāḍ iti hovāca || BrhUp_4,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> held court. Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s> came. [<s>Janaka</s>] said to him: '<s>Yājñavalkya</s>, for what purpose have you come? Desiring cattle, or [desiring to hear] the subtle conclusions [of philosophical questions]?' He said: 'For both indeed, O Emperor (<s>Samrāj</s>).' (BṛUp 4.1.1)

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,1.1 janako ha vaideha āsāñcakre āsanaṃ kṛtavānāsthāyikāṃ dattavānityarthaḥ, darśanakāmebhyo rājñaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 4.1.1:] <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> held court — <s>āsāṃ cakre</s> means he made a seat [available], i.e., he had granted an [open] audience — of the king, for those desiring to see [him].

children.text: atha ha tasminnavasare yājñavalkyaḥ āvavrāja-āgatavānātmano yogakṣemārtham, rājño vā vivadiṣāṃ dṛṣṭvānugrahārtham /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then, at that occasion, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> came — he had arrived either for the purpose of his own welfare, or having seen the desire for debate on the part of the king, for the purpose of granting him favor.

children.text: tamāgataṃ yajñavalkyaṃ yathāvat pūjāṃ kṛtvovāca hoktavāñjanakaḥ he yājñavalkya kimartham acārīḥ-āgato 'si? kiṃ paśūnicchan punarapi, āhosvidaṇvantān sūkṣmāntān sūkṣmavastunirṇayāntān praśnān mattaḥ śrotumicchanniti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having duly honored <s>Yājñavalkya</s> who had come, <s>Janaka</s> spoke — said: 'O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, for what purpose have you come? Desiring cattle again? Or [desiring to hear] the subtle — the fine, having as their conclusion the determination of subtle matters — questions from me?'

children.text: ubhayameva paśūn praśnāṃśca he samrāṭ-samrāḍiti vājapeyayājino liṅgam ; yaśca ājñayā rājyaṃ praśāsti, samrāṭ ; tasyā mantraṇaṃ he samrāḍiti ; samastasya vā bhāratasya varṣasya rājā //4,1.1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'For both indeed — cattle and questions — O <s>Samrāj</s> (Emperor).' The [title] '<s>Samrāj</s>' is the mark of one who has performed the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice; or, one who rules the kingdom by his command is a <s>samrāj</s>; addressing him [thus]: 'O <s>Samrāj</s>'; or, [he is] the king of the entire <s>Bhārata</s> land. (4.1.1)

children.text: START BrhUp 4,1.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.1.2]

children.text:
yat te kaścid abravīt tac chṛṇavāmeti |
abravīn me jitvā śailiniḥ -- vāg vai brahmeti |
yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tac chailinir abravīd vāg vai brahmeti |
avadato hi kiṃ syād iti |
abravīt tu te tasyāyatanaṃ pratiṣṭhām |
na me 'bravīd iti |
ekapād vā etat samrāḍ iti |
sa vai no brūhi yājñavalkya |
vāg evāyatanam ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhā prajñety enad upāsīta |
kā prajñatā yājñavalkya |
vāg eva samrāḍ iti hovāca |
vācā vai samrāḍ bandhuḥ prajñāyate |
ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇy anuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānānīṣṭaṃ hutam āśitaṃ pāyitam ayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni vācaiva saṃrāṭ prajñāyante |
vāg vai samrāṭ paramaṃ brahma |
nainaṃ vāg jahāti |
sarvāṇy enaṃ bhūtāny abhikṣaranti |
devo bhūtvā devān apyeti |
ya evaṃ vidvān etad upāste |
hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ |
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ -- pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti || BrhUp_4,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: 'Let us hear what anyone has told you.' '<s>Jitvā Śailini</s> told me: "Speech indeed is <s>Brahman</s>." Just as one who has a mother, a father, and a teacher would speak — so did <s>Śailini</s> declare: "Speech indeed is <s>Brahman</s>." For what would a speechless person have?' 'But did he tell you its abode (<s>āyatana</s>) and support (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>)?' 'He did not tell me.' 'This is only one-footed, O <s>Samrāj</s>.' 'Then tell us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' 'Speech alone is the abode; space is the support. One should meditate upon it as wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>).' 'What is the nature of wisdom (<s>prajñatā</s>), <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'Speech itself, O <s>Samrāj</s>,' he said. 'For by speech, O <s>Samrāj</s>, a kinsman is known. The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>, history (<s>itihāsa</s>), ancient lore (<s>purāṇa</s>), sciences (<s>vidyā</s>), <s>Upaniṣads</s>, verses (<s>ślokas</s>), aphorisms (<s>sūtras</s>), explanations (<s>anuvyākhyānas</s>), commentaries (<s>vyākhyānas</s>), what is offered, what is poured, what is eaten, what is drunk, this world and the other world, and all beings — by speech alone, O <s>Samrāj</s>, are they known. Speech indeed, O <s>Samrāj</s>, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Speech does not forsake him. All beings flow toward him. Having become a god, he goes to the gods — whoever, knowing thus, meditates upon this.' <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> said: 'I give you a thousand [cows] with a bull as large as an elephant.' <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'My father was of the opinion that one should not accept [a gift] without having fully instructed [the giver].' (BṛUp 4.1.2)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,1.2 kintu yatte tubhyaṃ kaścidabravīdācāryo 'nekācāryo 'nekācāryasevī hi bhavāṃstacchṛṇavāmeti /
itara āha - abravadīduktavānme mamā'cāryo jitvā nāmataḥ śilinasyāpatyaṃ śailinirvāgvai brahmeti vāgdevatā brahmeti /
āhetapo yathā mātṛmānmātā yasya vidyate putrasya samyaganuśāstryanuśāsanakartrī sa mātṛmān /
ata ūrdhvaṃ pitā yasyānuśāstā sa pitṛmān /
upanayanādūrdhvamā samāvartanādācāryo yasyānuśāstā sa ācāryavān /
evaṃ śuddhitrayahetusaṃyuktaḥ sa sādhādācāryaḥ svayaṃ na kadācidapu prāmāṇādvyabhicarati sa yathā brūyācchiṣyāya tathāsau jitvā śailiniruktavānvāgvai brahmeti /
avadato hi kiṃ syāditi /
na hi mūkasyehārthamamutrārthaṃ vā kiñcana syāt /
kintvabravīduktavāste tubhyaṃ tasya brahmaṇa āyatanaṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ ca /
āyatanaṃ nāma śarīram /
pratiṣṭhā triṣvapi kāleṣu ya āśrayaḥ /
āhetaro na me 'bravīditi /
itara āha-yadyevamekapādvā etadekaḥ pādo yasya brahmaṇastadidamekapādbrahma tribhiḥ pādaiḥ śūnyamupāsyamānamapi na phalāya bhavatītyarthaḥ /
yadyevaṃ sa tvaṃ vidvānsanno 'smabhyaṃ brūhi he yājñavalkyeti /
sa cā'ha-vāgevā'yatanaṃ vāgdevasya brahmaṇo vāgeva karaṇamāyatanaṃ śarīramākāśo 'vyākṛtākhyaḥ pratiṣṭhotpattisthitilayakāleṣu /
prajñetyenadupāsīta prajñetīyamupaniṣadbrahmaṇaścaturthaḥ pādaḥ prajñeti kṛtvainadbrahmopāsīta /
kā prajñatā yājñavalkya ki svayameva prajñota prajñānimittam /
yathā'yatanapratiṣṭhe brahmaṇo vyatirikte tadvatkim /
na, katha tarhi, vāgeva samrāḍiti hovāca vāgeva prajñeti hovācoktavānna vyatiriktā prajñāti /
kathaṃ punarvāgeva prajñeti, ucyate-vācā vai samrāḍbandhuḥ prajñāyate 'smākaṃ bandhurityukte prajñāyakate bandhustathargvaidādi /
iṣṭaṃ yāganimitta dharmajātaṃ hutaṃ homanimittaṃ ca /
āśitamannadānimittaṃ pāyitaṃ pānadānanimittamayaṃ ca loka idaṃ ca janma paraśca lokaḥ pratipattavyaṃ ca janma sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni vācaiva samrāṭprajñāyante 'to vāgvaisamrāṭparamaṃ brahma nānaṃ yathoktabrahmavidaṃ vāgjahāti /
sarvāṇyenaṃ bhūtānyabhikṣaranti balidānādibhiriha /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'All beings flow toward him' — through offerings of tribute and the like in this world.

children.text: devo bhūtvā punaḥ śarīrapātottarakālaṃ devānapyetyapigacchati ya evaṃ vidvānetadupāste vidyāniṣkriyārthaṃ hastitulya ṛṣabho hastyṛṣabho yasmingosahasretaddhastṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Having become a god' — again, after the fall of the body, 'he goes to the gods.' One who, knowing thus, meditates upon this — for the purpose of the dispensation of knowledge — [<s>Janaka</s> gives <s>Yājñavalkya</s>] a bull-elephant (<s>hastyṛṣabha</s>) — 'a thousand with a bull-elephant' — 'I give,' said <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s>.

children.text: sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:

children.text: ananuśiṣya śiṣyaṃ kṛtārthamakṛtvā śiṣyāddhanaṃ na hareteti me mama pitāmanyata mamāpyayamevābhiprāyaḥ //4,1.2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Without having instructed the student, without having fulfilled his purpose, one should not take wealth from the student' — my father thought thus; and this is my intention too. (4.1.2)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.1.2:] 'But what someone told you — a teacher; for you are one who has served many teachers — listen to that.' The other said: '<s>Jitvan</s> by name — <s>Jitvan</s>, offspring of <s>Śilina</s>, hence <s>Śailini</s> — told me: "Speech indeed is <s>Brahman</s>" — speech is the deity that is <s>Brahman</s>.' He said: 'Like one who has a mother (<s>mātṛmān</s>)' — whose mother is a proper instructor, providing right instruction — 'who has a father (<s>pitṛmān</s>)' — whose father is an instructor; from beyond that, after investiture (<s>upanayana</s>) up to the completion of study (<s>samāvartana</s>), the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) — 'who has a teacher (<s>ācāryavān</s>).' Thus endowed with the three causes of purification, that good teacher — one who himself never deviates from authoritative sources — as he would say to his student, just so did <s>Jitvan Śailini</s> say: 'Speech indeed is <s>Brahman</s>.' 'For what would there be for one who cannot speak?' — for a mute person would have no purpose either in this world or the next. 'But did he tell you the abode (<s>āyatana</s>) and support (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) of that <s>Brahman</s>?' The abode means the body; the support means that which serves as the basis in all three times. The other said: 'He did not tell me.' The other [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] said: 'Then it is only one-footed (<s>ekapāt</s>)' — this <s>Brahman</s> has only one foot; a <s>Brahman</s> that lacks three of its four feet, even when meditated upon, does not yield fruit — this is the meaning. 'If so, then you, being learned, tell us, O <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' And he said: 'Speech alone is the abode' — speech is the instrument of the deity-<s>Brahman</s>; speech is the instrument-abode, and the body is space — the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>) — as the support during origination, subsistence, and dissolution. '<s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom) — one should meditate upon it as <s>prajñā</s>' — this is the <s>upaniṣad</s>, the fourth foot of <s>Brahman</s>: one should meditate upon it as <s>Brahman</s>, qualifying it as <s>prajñā</s>. 'What is that <s>prajñatā</s> (wisdom-character), <s>Yājñavalkya</s>? Is it self-luminous, or is there a cause of <s>prajñā</s>? Is it something separate, like the abode and support of <s>Brahman</s>?' 'No — then how? Speech alone is <s>prajñā</s>, O sovereign' — he said; <s>prajñā</s> is not something separate. But how is speech itself <s>prajñā</s>? It is explained: 'By speech, O sovereign, a kinsman (<s>bandhu</s>) is recognized' — when someone says 'he is our kinsman,' the kinsman becomes known; likewise the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the rest. That which is accomplished through sacrifice (<s>iṣṭa</s>) — the <s>dharma</s> produced through sacrificial rites — that which is accomplished through oblation (<s>huta</s>) — through the offering rite — that which is given through food (<s>āśita</s>) — through the giving of food — that which is given through drink (<s>pāyita</s>) — through the giving of drink — this world, this birth, the next world, the birth to come, and all beings — by speech alone, O sovereign, are [all these] recognized.' Therefore, 'speech, O sovereign, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; it does not forsake him who knows <s>Brahman</s> thus described in the manner of speech.'

children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.1.3]

children.text:
yad eva te kaścid abravīt tac chṛṇavāmeti |
abravīn ma udaṅkaḥ śaulbāyanaḥ |
prāṇo vai brahmeti |
yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tac chaulbāyano 'bravīt prāṇo vai brahmeti |
aprāṇato hi kiṃ syād iti |
abravīt tu te tasyāyatanaṃ pratiṣṭhām |
na me 'bravīd iti |
ekapād vā etat samrāḍ iti |
sa vai no brūhi yājñavalkya |
prāṇa evāyatanam ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhā |
priyam ity enad upāsīta |
kā priyatā yājñavalkya |
prāṇa eva samrāḍ iti hovāca |
prāṇasya vai samrāṭ kāmāyāyājyaṃ yājayati |
apratigṛhyasya pratigṛhṇāti |
api tatra vadhāśaṅkā bhavati yāṃ diśam eti prāṇasyaiva samrāṭ kāmāya |
prāṇo vai samrāṭ paramaṃ brahma |
nainaṃ prāṇo jahāti |
sarvāṇy enaṃ bhūtāny abhikṣaranti |
devo bhūtvā devān apyeti |
ya evaṃ vidvān etad upāste |
hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehah |
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ -- pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti || BrhUp_4,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever someone told you, let us hear that.' '<s>Udaṅka Śaulbāyana</s> told me: "Breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) indeed is <s>Brahman</s>." As one who has a mother, a father, and a teacher would say, so did <s>Śaulbāyana</s> say: "Breath indeed is <s>Brahman</s>." For what would there be for one without breath?' 'But did he tell you its abode and support?' 'He did not tell me.' 'Then it is only one-footed, O sovereign.' 'Do tell us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' 'Breath itself is the abode; space is the support. One should meditate upon it as the dear (<s>priya</s>).' 'What is that dearness, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'Breath itself, O sovereign,' he said. 'For the sake of breath alone, O sovereign, one performs sacrifice for one for whom sacrifice should not be performed; one accepts [gifts] from one from whom [gifts] should not be accepted; one even goes in a direction where there is fear of being killed — all for the sake of breath alone, O sovereign. Breath indeed, O sovereign, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. Breath does not forsake him; all beings flow toward him. Having become a god, he goes to the gods — he who, knowing thus, meditates upon this.' 'I give a thousand [cows] with a bull-elephant,' said <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s>. <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'My father thought that one should not take [gifts] without having instructed.' (BṛUp 4.1.3)

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,1.3 yadeva te kaścidabravīdudaṅko nāmataḥ śulbasyāpatyaṃ śaulbasyāpatyaṃ śaulbāyano 'bravītprāṇo vai brahmeti prāṇo vāyurdevatā pūrvavat /
prāṇa evā'yanamākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhopaniṣatpriyamityenadupāsīta /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Breath itself is the abode; space is the support. The <s>upaniṣad</s> is: one should meditate upon it as the dear (<s>priya</s>).'

children.text: kathaṃ punaḥ priyatvaṃ, prāṇasya vai he samrāṭkāmāya prāṇasyārthāyāyājyaṃ yājayati patitādikamapyapratigṛhyasyāpyugrādeḥ pratigṛhṇātyapi tatra tasyāṃ diśi vadhanimittamāśaṅkaṃ vadhāśaṅketyartho yāṃ diśameti taskarādyākīrṇāṃ ca tasyāṃ diśi ba dhāśahkā taccaitatsarvaṃ prāṇasya priyatve bhavati prāṇasyaiva samrāṭkāmāya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But how is it characterized by dearness? 'For the sake of breath alone, O sovereign, one performs sacrifice for one for whom sacrifice should not be performed' — [even for] an outcast and the like; 'one accepts [gifts] from one from whom [gifts] should not be accepted' — even from a fierce person and the like; 'moreover, there is the apprehension of killing in that direction' — the fear of killing is the meaning — 'in whatever direction one goes' — even [a direction] infested with thieves and the like — 'in that direction there is the apprehension of killing' — yet all this happens because of the dearness of breath, 'for the sake of breath alone, O sovereign.'

children.text: tasmātprāṇo vai samrāṭparamaṃ brahma nainaṃ prāṇo jahāti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, 'breath indeed, O sovereign, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>; breath does not forsake him.'

children.text: samānamanyat //4,1.3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The rest is the same. (4.1.3)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.1.3:] 'Whatever someone told you' — <s>Udaṅka</s> by name, offspring of <s>Śulba</s>, hence <s>Śaulbāyana</s>, said 'breath indeed is <s>Brahman</s>' — breath (<s>Vāyu</s>) is the deity; as before.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,1.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.1.4]

children.text:
yad eva te kaścid abravīt tac chṛṇavāmeti |
abravīn me barkur vārṣṇaḥ |
cakṣur vai brahmeti |
yathā mātṛmān pitṛmān ācāryavān brūyāt tathā tad vārṣṇo 'bravīc cakṣur vai brahmeti |
apaśyato hi kiṃ syād iti |
abravīt tu te tasyāyatanaṃ pratiṣṭhām |
na me 'bravīd iti |
ekapād vā etat samrāḍ iti |
sa vai no brūhi yājñavalkya |
cakṣur evāyatanam ākāśaḥ pratiṣṭhā |
satyam ity etad upāsīta |
kā satyatā yājñavalkya |
cakṣur eva samrāḍ iti hovāca |
cakṣuṣā vai samrāṭ paśyantam āhur adrākṣīr iti |
sa āhādrākṣam iti tat satyaṃ bhavati |
cakṣur vai samrāṭ paramaṃ brahma |
nainam cakṣur jahāti |
sarvāṇy enaṃ bhūtāny abhikṣaranti |
devo bhūtvā devān apyeti |
ya evaṃ vidvān etad upāste |
hastyṛṣabhaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ |
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ -- pitā me 'manyata nānanuśiṣya hareteti || BrhUp_4,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever someone told you, let us hear that.' '<s>Barku Vārṣṇa</s> told me: "The eye indeed is <s>Brahman</s>." As one who has a mother, a father, and a teacher would say, so did <s>Vārṣṇa</s> say: "The eye indeed is <s>Brahman</s>." For what would there be for one who cannot see?' 'But did he tell you its abode and support?' 'He did not tell me.' 'Then it is only one-footed, O sovereign.' 'Do tell us, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.' 'The eye itself is the abode; space is the support. One should meditate upon it as truth (<s>satya</s>).' 'What is that truth-character, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>?' 'The eye itself, O sovereign,' he said. 'For, O sovereign, when they say to one who sees with the eye: "Did you see [it]?" and he says "I saw [it]" — that is truth. The eye indeed, O sovereign, is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. The eye does not forsake him; all beings flow toward him. Having become a god, he goes to the gods — he who, knowing thus, meditates upon this.' 'I give a thousand [cows] with a bull-elephant,' said <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s>. <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: 'My father thought that one should not take [gifts] without having instructed.' (BṛUp 4.1.4)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,1.4 yadeva te kaścidbarkuriti nāmato vṛṣṇasyāpatyaṃ vārṣṇaścakṣurvai brahmetyādityo devatā cakṣuṣyupaniṣatsatyam /
yasmācchrotreṇa śrutamanṛtamapi syānna tu cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭam /
tasmādvai samrāṭpaśyantamāhuradrākṣīstvaṃ hastinamiti sa cedadrākṣamityāhatatsatyameva bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, O sovereign, when they say to one who sees: 'Did you see the elephant?' — if he says 'I saw [it],' that is truth indeed.

children.text: yastvanyau brūyadahamaśrauṣamiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But if another were to say 'I heard [it]' —

children.text: tadvyabhicarati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] that is subject to deviation [from truth].

children.text: yattu cakṣuṣā dṛṣṭaṃ tadavyabhicāritvātsatyameva bhavati //4,1.4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But what is seen by the eye — that, because of its non-deviating character, is truth indeed. (4.1.4)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.1.4:] 'Whatever someone told you' — <s>Barku</s> by name, offspring of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, hence <s>Vārṣṇa</s> — 'the eye indeed is <s>Brahman</s>' — <s>Āditya</s> (sun) is the deity. The <s>upaniṣad</s> pertaining to the eye is: truth (<s>satya</s>). Because what is heard by the ear may even be false, but what is seen by the eye [is not].

children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.1.5]
