so 'haṃ bhagavate sahasraṃ dadāmi |
ata ūrdhvaṃ vimokṣāyaiva brūhīti |
atra ha yājñavalkyo bibhayāṃ cakāra -- medhāvī rājā sarvebhyo māntebhya udarautsīd iti || BrhUp_4,3.33 ||
children.translated_text: He who among human beings is prosperous and wealthy, lord over others, most abundantly endowed with all human enjoyments — that is the highest bliss of human beings. Now, a hundred-fold the bliss of human beings is one bliss of the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors) who have won their world. A hundred-fold the bliss of the <s>Pitṛs</s> who have won their world is one bliss of the <s>Gandharva</s>-world. A hundred-fold the bliss of the <s>Gandharva</s>-world is one bliss of the <s>Karmadevāḥ</s> (gods by action), those who attain divinity through <s>karma</s>. A hundred-fold the bliss of the <s>Karmadevāḥ</s> is one bliss of the <s>Ājānadevāḥ</s> (gods by birth), and also of a <s>śrotriya</s> (one learned in the Vedas) who is free from crookedness and unsmited by desire. A hundred-fold the bliss of the <s>Ājānadevāḥ</s> [continues the ascending scale of bliss up to <s>Brahman</s>]. (BṛUp 4.3.33)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,3.33 yasya paramāndasya mātrā avayavā brahmādibhirmanuṣyaparyantairbhūtairupajīvyante tadānandamātrādvāreṇa mātriṇaṃ paramānandamadhijigamiyiṣannāha saindhavalavaṇaśakalairiva lavaṇaśailam /
sa yaḥ kasminmanuṣyāṇāṃ madhye rāddhaḥ saṃsiddho 'vikalaḥ samagrāvayava ityarthaḥ /
samṛddha upabhogopakaraṇasaṃpanno bhavati /
kiñcānyeṣāṃ samānajātīyānāmadhipatiḥ svatantra patirna māṇḍalikaḥ sarvaiḥ samastairmānuṣyakairiti divyabhogopakaraṇanivṛtyarthaṃ manuṣyāṇāmeva yāni bhogopakaraṇāni taiḥ saṃpannānāmapyatiṣayena saṃpannaḥ saṃpannatamaḥ sa manuṣyāṇāṃ parama ānandaḥ /
tatrā'nandānditorabhedanirdeśānnārthāntarabhūtatvamityetat /
paramānandarasyaiveyaṃ viṣayāviṣayyākareṇa mātrā prasṛteti hayuktaṃ yatra vā anyadiva syādityādivākyena /
tasmādyukto 'yaṃ parama ānanda ityabhedanirdeśaḥ /
yudhiṣṭhirāditulyo rājātrodāharaṇam /
dṛṣṭaṃ manuṣyānandaramādiṃ kṛtvā śataguṇottarakrameṇonnīya paramānandaṃ yatra bhedo nivartate tamadhigamayati /
atrāyamānandaḥ śataguṇottarottarakrameṇa vardhamāno yatra vṛddhikāṣṭāmanubhavati /
yatra gaṇitabhedo nivartate 'nyadarśanaśravaṇamananābhāvāttaṃ paramānandaṃ vivakṣannāha /
atha ye manuṣyāṇāmevaṃprakārāḥ śatamānandabhedāḥ sa ekaḥ pitṝṇām /
teṣāṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ jitalokānāmiti /
śrāddhādikarmabhiḥpitṝṃstoṣayitvā tena karmaṇā jito loko yeṣāṃ te jitalokāḥ pitarasteṣāṃ pitṛṇāṃ jitalokānāṃ manuṣyānandaśataguṇīkṛtaparimāṇa eka ānando bhavati /
so 'pi śataguṇīkṛto gandharvaloka eka ānando bhavati /
sa ca śataguṇīkṛtaḥ karmadevānāmeka ānandaḥ /
agnihotrādiśrautakarmaṇā ye devatvaṃ prāpnuvanti te karmadevaiḥ /
tathaivai''jānadevānāmeka ānandaḥ /
ājānata evotpattita eva ye devāsta ājānadevāḥ /
yaśca śrotriyo 'dhītavedo 'vaḍajino vṛjinaṃ pāpaṃ tadrahito yathoktakārityarthaḥ /
akāmahato vītatṛṣṇa ājānadevo 'bhyor'vāgyāvanto viṣayāsteṣu /
tasya caivaṃbhūtasyā'jānadevaiḥ samāna ānanda ityetadanvākṛṣyate ca śabdāttacchataguṇīkṛtaparimāṇaḥ prajāpatiloka eka ānando virāṭśarīre /
tathā tadvijñānavāñśrotriyo 'dhītavedaścāvṛjina ityādi pūrvavat /
tacchataguṇīkṛtaparimāṇa eka ānando brahmaloke hiraṇyagarbhātmani /
yaścetyādi pūrvavadeva /
ataḥ paraṃ gaṇitanivṛttaḥ /
eṣa parama ānanda prayuktaḥ /
yasya ca paramānandajasya brahmalokādyānandā mātrā udadheriva vipruṣaḥ /
evaṃ śataguṇottarottaravṛddhyupetā ānandā yatraikatā yānti yaśca śrotriyapratyakṣo 'thaiṣa eva saṃprasādalakṣaṇaḥ parama ānandastatra hi nānyatpaśyati nānyacchṛṇoti /
atho bhūmā bhūmatvādamṛtaḥ /
itare tadviparītāḥ /
atra ca śrotrayitvādvṛjinatve tulye /
akāmahatatvakṛto viśeṣa ānandaśataguṇavṛddhihetuḥ /
atraitāni sādhanāni śrotriyatvāvṛjinatvākāmahatatvāni tasya tasyā'nandasya prāptāvarthādibhihitānu yathā karmāṇgnihotrādīni devānāṃ devatvaprāptau /
tatra ca śrotriyatvāvṛjinatvalakṣaṇe karmaṇī adharabhūmiṣvapi samāne iti nottarānandaprāptisādhane abhyupeyete /
akāmahatatvaṃ tu vairāgyatāratamyopapatteruttarottarabhūmyānandaprāptisādhanamityavagamyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Freedom from being smitten by desire, i.e. <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), is understood to be the means of attaining the bliss of each successively higher level, because of the gradation of dispassion.

children.text: sa eṣa parama ānando vitṛṣṇaśrotriyapratyakṣo 'dhigataḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This supreme bliss is directly realized by the desireless <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar).

children.text: tathā ca vedavyāsaḥ-"yacca kāmasukhaṃ loke yacca divyaṃ mahatsukham /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And thus <s>Vedavyāsa</s> [says]: 'Whatever sensual happiness there is in this world, and whatever great divine happiness there is —

children.text: tṛṣṇākṣayasukhasyaite nārhataḥ ṣoḍaśīṃ kalām" //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] These do not equal a sixteenth part of the happiness of the destruction of craving.'

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.3.33:] In order to lead one to the supreme bliss — whose fractions, whose parts, are enjoyed by beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to humans — through the gateway of those portions of bliss, just as one [would approach] a mountain of salt through small crystals of salt, [the text] says: He who, among human beings, is <s>rāddha</s> — accomplished, complete, having all limbs intact — that is the meaning. <s>Samṛddha</s> — endowed with the means of enjoyment. Moreover, lord over others of the same class — an independent ruler, not a subordinate chief. Endowed with all, with the totality of human enjoyments — the word 'human' is used to exclude divine means of enjoyment; with those means of enjoyment that belong to humans, he is most abundantly endowed.

children.text:
iti /
eṣa brahmaloko he samrāḍiti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ so 'hamevanuśiṣṭo bhagavate tubhyaṃ sahasraṃ dadāmi gavām /
ata ūdhvaṃ vimokṣāyaiva brūhīti vyākhyātametat /
atra ha vimokṣāyetyasminvākye yājñavalkyo bibhayāñcakāra bhītavān /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here, at [the words] 'for the sake of liberation' in this sentence, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> became afraid.

children.text: yājñavalkyasya bhayakāraṇamāha śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>śruti</s> states the reason for <s>Yājñavalkya</s>'s fear.

children.text: na yājñavalkyo vaktṛtvasāmarthyābhāvādbhītavānajñānādvā kiṃ tarhi medhāvī rājā sarvebhyo mā māmantebhyaḥ praśnanirṇayavasānebhya udarautsīdāvṛṇodavarodhaṃ kṛtavānityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Yājñavalkya</s> was not afraid due to lack of ability to teach, nor due to ignorance. Rather, [he feared that] the intelligent king would extract him from all the conclusions of questions — would confine him, would block him — that is the meaning.

children.text: yadyānmayā nirṇītaṃ praśnarūpaṃ vimokṣārthaṃ tattadekadeśatvenaiva kāmapraśnasya gṛhītvā punaḥ punarmāṃ paryanuyuṅktta eva medhāvitvādityetadbhayakāraṇaṃ sarvaṃ madīyaṃ vijñānaṃ kāmapraśnavyājenopāditsatīti //4,3.33//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [He feared:] 'Whatever I have determined regarding the questions about liberation, the intelligent [king], grasping each of those as merely a part of the question about desire, will press me again and again due to his intelligence' — this was the cause of his fear — '[the king] wants to obtain all my knowledge under the pretext of questions about desire.' (4.3.33)

[Commentary:] 'This is the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, O Emperor,' said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. [<s>Janaka</s> replied:] 'I, thus instructed, give to you, O Venerable One, a thousand cows. From here onwards, please teach for the sake of liberation.' This has been explained.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,3.34
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.3.34]

children.text: sa vā eṣa etasmin svapnānte ratvā caritvā dṛṣṭvaiva puṇyaṃ ca pāpaṃ ca punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati buddhāntāyaiva || BrhUp_4,3.34 ||
children.translated_text: This very being, having enjoyed and wandered about in this state of dream, and having seen merit and sin, returns again in the reverse order, running back to the state of waking. (BṛUp 4.3.34)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,3.34 atra vijñānamayaḥ svayañjyotirātmā svapne pradarśitaḥ /
svapnāntabudvāntasaṃcāreṇa kāryakaraṇavyatirittkatā /
kāmakarmapravivekaścāsaṅgatayā mahāmatsyadṛṣṭāntena pradarśitaḥ /
punaścāvidyākāryaṃ svapna eva dhnantovetyādinā pradarśitam /
arthādavidyāyāḥ satattvaṃnirdhīritamatadvarmādhyāropaṇarūpatvamanātmadharmatvaṃ ca /
tathā vidyāyāśca kāryaṃ pradarśitaṃ sarvatmabhāvaḥ svapna eva pratyakṣataḥ sarvo 'smīti manyate so 'sya paramo loka iti /
tatra ca sarvātmabhāvaḥ svabhāvo 'syaivamavidyākāmakarmādisarvasaṃsāradharmasaṃbandhātītaṃ rūpamasya sākṣātsuṣupte gṛhyata ityenadvijñāpitaṃ svayañjyotirātmaiṣa parama ānandaḥ /
eṣa vidyāyā viṣayaḥ /
sa eṣa paramaḥ saṃprasādaḥ sukhasya ca parā kāṣṭhetyetadevamantena granthena vyākhyātam /
taccaitsarvaṃ vimokṣapadārthasarvaṃ vimokṣapadārthasya dṛṣṭāntabhūtaṃ bandhanasya ca /
te caite mokṣabandhane sahetuke saprapañce nirdiṣṭe vidyāvidyākārye tatsarvaṃ dṛṣṭāntabhūtameveti taddārṣṭāntikasthānīye mokṣahandhane sahetuke kāmapraśnārthabhūte tvayā vattkavye iti punaḥ parthanuyuṅttke janako 'ta ūrdhvaṃ vimokṣāyaiva brūhīti /
tatra mahāmatsyavatsvabuddhāntāvasaṅgaḥ saṃcaratyeka ātmā svayañjyotirityuktam /
yathā cāsau kāryakaraṇānu mṛtyurūpāṇi parityajannupādadānaśca mahāmatsyavatsvapnabuddhāntāvanusaṃcarati tathā jāyamāno mriyamāṇaśca taireva mṛtyurūpaiḥ saṃyujyate viyujyate ca /
ubhau lokānusaṃcaratīti saṃcaraṇaṃ svapnabuddhantānusaṃcārasya dārṣṭāntikatvena sūcitam /
tadiha vistareṇa sanimittaṃ saṃcaraṇaṃ varṇayitavyamiti tadartho 'yamārambhaḥ tatra ca buddhāntātsvapnāntamayamātmānupraveśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, this traversal, together with its cause, is to be described here in detail — for that purpose, this section is commenced. And therein, the self has been progressively introduced from the waking state to the dream state.

children.text: tasmātsaṃprāsādasthānaṃ mokṣadṛṣṭanāntabhūtam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the state of deep serenity (<s>saṃprasāda</s>) serves as an illustration for <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: tataḥ pracyāvya buddhānte saṃsāravyavahāraḥ pradariśyitavya iti tenāsya saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having displaced [the self] from that [deep sleep], the transactional activity of <s>saṃsāra</s> in the waking state is to be demonstrated — thus is its connection [with the preceding section].

children.text: sa vai buddhāntātspnāntakrameṇa saṃprasanna eṣa etasminsaṃprasāde sthitvā tataḥ punarīṣatpracyutaḥ svapnānte ratvā caritvetyādi pūrvavadbundāyaivā'dravati //4,3.34//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That self, from the waking state, sequentially through the dream state, has become serene in this deep serenity (<s>saṃprasāda</s>). Having been established in this <s>saṃprasāda</s>, then having slightly descended from it to the dream state, having sported and moved about — and so forth, as before — it runs back to the waking state itself. (4.3.34)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.3.34:] Here, the self-luminous self constituted of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>) has been demonstrated in dream. Through the traversal of the dream and waking states, its distinction from the aggregate of effects and instruments [has been shown]. The discrimination of desire and action [from the self], and [its] non-attachment, have been demonstrated through the great-fish illustration. Furthermore, that the effect of <s>avidyā</s> is [seen] in dream itself has been demonstrated by [the passage beginning with] 'he destroys' and so forth. By implication, the real existence of <s>avidyā</s> has been established, as well as its nature of being the superimposition of non-self properties, and its being a non-self property. Likewise, the effect of <s>vidyā</s> has been demonstrated — the state of being the self of all (<s>sarvātmabhāva</s>) — directly perceived in dream itself: 'I am this all' — [thus] he thinks; 'that is his supreme world.' And therein, the state of being the self of all is its very own nature; thus it has been made known that the form of this [self] — which is beyond all connection with <s>saṃsāric</s> properties such as <s>avidyā</s>, desire, <s>karma</s>, and the like — is directly apprehended in deep sleep. This self-luminous self is the supreme <s>ānanda</s> (bliss). This is the object of <s>vidyā</s>. 'This is the supreme <s>saṃprasāda</s> (serenity)' and 'the ultimate limit of bliss' — this has been explained by this entire textual section. And all of this serves as an illustration for the meaning of the term '<s>vimokṣa</s>' (liberation) and for bondage. These two — <s>mokṣa</s> and bondage — together with their causes and elaborations, have been indicated as the effects of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>avidyā</s>. All of this is merely illustrative. Therefore, with respect to the illustrated counterparts — <s>mokṣa</s> and bondage together with their causes, which constitute the subject matter of [<s>Janaka's</s>] question about desire — [<s>Janaka</s>] presses [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>] again: 'From here onward, please speak only for liberation.' Therein, it was said that the one self, self-luminous, traverses [the states] unattached, like a great fish, between waking and dream. And just as it abandons and takes up the effects and instruments — which are the forms of death — and like a great fish traverses the dream and waking states, so too, being born and dying, it is conjoined with and separated from those very forms of death. 'It traverses both worlds' — this traversal has been indicated as the illustrated counterpart (<s>dārṣṭāntika</s>) of the traversal between dream and waking.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,3.35
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.3.35]

children.text:
tad yathānaḥ susamāhitam utsarjaṃ yāyād evam evāyaṃ śārīra ātmā prājñenātmanānvārūḍha utsarjaṃ yāti |
yatraitad ūrdhvocchvāsī bhavati || BrhUp_4,3.35 ||
children.translated_text: Just as a heavily loaded cart goes creaking along, even so this embodied self (<s>śārīra ātmā</s>), mounted upon by the all-knowing self (<s>prājña ātman</s>), goes creaking along — when [the dying person] becomes one who breathes upward. (BṛUp 4.3.35)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,3.35 ita ārabhyāsya saṃsāro varṇyate /
yathāyamātmā svapnāntādbuddhāntamāgata evamayamasmāddehaddehāntaraṃ pratipatsyata ityāhātra dṛṣṭāntam /
tattatra yathā loke 'naḥ śakaṭaṃ susamāhitaṃ suṣṭhu bhṛśaṃ vā samāhitaṃ bhāṇḍopaskaraṇenolūkhalamusalaśūrpapiṭharādinānnādyena ca saṃpannaṃ saṃbhāreṇā'kranāntamityarthaḥ /
tathā bhārākrāntaṃ sadutsarjacchabdaṃ kurvadyathā yayādgacchecchākaṭikenādhiṣṭhitaṃ sat /
evameva yathokto dṛṣṭānto 'yaṃ śarīraḥ śārīre bhavaḥ /
ko 'sau /
ātmā liṅgopādhiḥ /
yaḥ svapnabuddhāntāvivi janmamaraṇābhyāṃ pāpmasaṃsargaviyogalakṣaṇābhyāmihalokaparalokāvanusaṃcarati /
yasyotkramaṇamanu prāṇādyutkramaṇaṃ sa prājñena pareṇā'tmanā svayañjyotiḥsvabhāvenānvārūṭho 'dhiṣṭhito 'vabhāsyamānaḥ /
tathā coktamāttamanaivāyaṃ jyotiṣā'ste palyayata iti /
utsarjanyāti /
tatra caitanyātmajyotiṣā bhāsye liṅge prāṇapradhāne gacchati tadupādhirapyātmā gacchatīva /
tathā śrutyantaram-"kasminnvaham"ityādi"dhyāyatīva"iti ca /
ata evoktaṃ prājñenā'tmanānvārūṭha iti /
anyathā prājñenaikībhūtaḥ śakaṭavatkathamutsarjanyāti /
tena liṅgopādhirātmotsarjanmarmasu nikṛtyamāneṣu duḥkhavedanayār''taḥ śabdaṃ kurvanyāti gacchati tatkasminkāla iti /
ucyate-yatraitadbhavati /
etaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Etad</s>' (this) is an adverbial modifier of the action.

children.text: ūrdhvocchvāsī yatrordhvocchāsitatvamasya bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Ūrdhvocchvāsī</s>' — when the condition of breathing upward occurs for this [dying person] — this is the meaning.

children.text: dṛśyamānasyāpyanuvadanaṃ vairāgyagahetoḥ īdṛśaḥ kaṣṭaḥ khalvayaṃ saṃsāraḥ yenotkrāntikāle marmasūtkṛtyamāneṣu smṛtilopo duḥkhavedanārtasya puruṣārthasādhanapratipattau cāsāmarthyaṃ paravaśīkṛtacittasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The description of what is directly perceived [at the time of death] is for the purpose of generating dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>): such indeed is this terrible <s>saṃsāra</s>, wherein at the time of departure, when the vital points are being pierced, there is loss of memory, affliction from the sensation of pain, and incapacity for the pursuit of the means to the highest good (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) — for one whose mind has become subject to another's control.

children.text: tasmādyāvadiyamavasthā nā'gamiṣyati tāvadeva puruṣārthasādhanakarvyatāyāmapramatto bhavedityāha kāruṇyācchrutiḥ //4,3.35//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, as long as this condition has not yet come upon one, one should be diligent in the pursuit of the means to the highest good — thus the <s>śruti</s> speaks out of compassion. (4.3.35)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.3.35:] From here onward, the <s>saṃsāra</s> of this [self] is described. Just as this self comes from the dream state to the waking state, even so this [self] will proceed from this body to another body — for this purpose, an illustration is stated here. There — just as in the world, a cart (<s>anaḥ</s>) — a wagon — <s>susamāhita</s> — well loaded, or excessively loaded — with goods and equipment such as mortars, pestles, winnowing baskets, pots, and the like, as well as provisions of food — filled with supplies, meaning weighed down with a heavy load — in that condition, <s>utsarjan</s> — making a creaking sound — just as it would go, would move, when mounted by a driver. Even so — as is this illustration — this <s>śārīra</s> — 'pertaining to the body' (<s>śārīre bhavaḥ</s>). Who is that? The self (<s>ātmā</s>) — conditioned by the limiting adjunct of the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>). The one who, between dream and waking, through birth and death — characterized by the connection and separation from sin — traverses this world and the next. The one whose departure is followed by the departure of the <s>prāṇas</s> and the rest — he is mounted upon (<s>anvārūḍha</s>), presided over, illuminated by the <s>prājña</s> — the supreme self, whose nature is self-luminosity. And thus it was said: 'By the self alone does this one sit, by its light does it go about and perform actions' (BṛUp 4.3.6). It goes creaking (<s>utsarjan</s>). Therein, when the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) — which is the primary component of the <s>prāṇa</s> — illuminated by the light of consciousness that is the self, moves, then the self too, conditioned by that limiting adjunct, appears to move. So too, another <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'In whom I' and so forth, and 'it thinks, as it were' (BṛUp 4.3.7). Therefore it is said 'mounted upon by the <s>prājña</s> self.' Otherwise, having merged with the <s>prājña</s>, how would it go creaking like a cart? Therefore, the self conditioned by the limiting adjunct of the subtle body, when the vital points (<s>marmans</s>) are being pierced, afflicted by the sensation of pain, goes creaking — goes forth, making sounds. At what time? This is stated: 'when this occurs' (<s>yatraitad</s>).

children.text: START BrhUp 4,3.36
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.3.36]

children.text:
sa yatrāyam aṇimānaṃ nyeti jarayā vopatapatā vāṇimānaṃ nigacchati |
tad yathāmraṃ vodumbaraṃ vā pippalaṃ vā bandhanāt pramucyate |
evam evāyaṃ puruṣa ebhyo 'ṅgebhyaḥ saṃpramucya punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratiyony ādravati prāṇāyaiva || BrhUp_4,3.36 ||
children.translated_text: When this [person] becomes emaciated — whether through old age or through disease — he reaches emaciation. Just as a mango, or a fig, or a fruit of the <s>Pippala</s> tree is released from its stalk, even so this <s>puruṣa</s>, freeing himself from these limbs, runs back again by the same path, by the same origin, to <s>prāṇa</s> (life-breath) alone. (BṛUp 4.3.36)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,3.36 tadasyordhvocchvāsitvaṃ kasminkāle kiṃnimittaṃ kathaṃ kimarthaṃ vā syādityetaducyate-so 'yaṃ prākṛtaḥ śiraḥ pāṇyādimānpiṇḍo yatra yasminkāle 'yamaṇimānamaṇorbhāvamaṇutvaṃ kārśyamityarthaḥ /
nyeti nigacchati /
kiṃnimittaṃ jarayā vā svayameva kālapakvaphalavajjīrṇaḥ kārśyaṃ gacchati /
upatapatītyupatapañjvarādirogastenopatapatā vā /
upatapyamāno hirogeṇa viṣamāgnitayānnaṃ bhuktaṃ na jarayati tato 'nnarasenānupacīyamānaḥ piṇḍaḥ kārśyamāpapadyate taducyata upatapatā veti /
aṇimānaṃ nigacchati /
yadātyantakārśyaṃ pratipanno jarādinimittaistadordhvocchavāsī bhavati /
yadordhvocchvāsī tadā bhṛśāhitasaṃbhāraśakaṭavadutsarjanyāti /
jaribhābhavo rogādipīḍanaṃ kārśyāpattiśca śarīravato 'vaśyaṃbhāvina ete 'narthā iti vairāgyāyedamucyate /
yadāsāvutsarjanyāti tadā kathaṃ śarīraṃ vimuñcatīti dṛṣṭānta ucyate-tattatra yatāmraṃ vā phalamudumbaraṃ vā pippalaṃ vāphalam /
viṣamānekadṛṣṭāntopādānaṃ maraṇasyāniyatanimittatvakhyāpanārtham /
aniyatāni hi maraṇasya nimittānyasaṃkhyātāni ca /
etadapi vairāgyārthameva /
yasmādayamanekamaraṇanimittavāṃstasmātsarvadā mṛtyorāsye vartata iti /
bandhanādbadhyate yena vṛntena saha sa bandhanakāraṇo raso yasminvā badhyata iti vṛntamevocyate bandhana tasmādrasādvṛntādvā bandhanātpramucyate vātādyanekanimitamevamevāyaṃ puruṣo liṅgātmā liṅgopādhirebhyo 'ṅgebhyaścakṣurādidehāvayavebhyaḥ saṃpramucya samyaṅnirlepena pramucya /
na suṣuptagamanakāla iva prāṇena rakṣan /
kiṃ tarhi saha vāyunopasaṃhṛtya /
punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ punaḥśabandātpūrvamapyayaṃ dedāddehāntaramasakṛdgatavānyathā svapnabuddhāntau punaḥ purgacchati tathā punaḥ pratinyāyaṃ pratigamanaṃ yathāgatamityarthaḥ /
pratiyoni yoniṃ yoni prati karmaśrutādivaśādādravati /
kimartham /
prāṇāyaiva prāṇavyūhāyaivetyarthaḥ /
saprāṇa eva hi gacchati tataḥ prāṇayaiveti viśeṣaṇamanarthakam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For it goes with the <s>prāṇa</s> indeed; therefore '<s>prāṇāyaiva</s>' (for <s>prāṇa</s> alone) — this qualifier would be meaningless [if taken literally].

children.text: prāṇavyūhāya hi gamanaṃ dehāddehāntaraṃ prati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the journey from body to another body is for the deployment of the <s>prāṇas</s> (<s>prāṇavyūha</s>).

children.text: tena hyasya karmaphalopabhogārthasiddhirna prāṇasattāmātreṇa /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For through that [deployment] is accomplished his fruition of the results of <s>karma</s> — not through the mere existence of <s>prāṇa</s>.

children.text: tasmāttādarthāyarthaṃ yuktaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ prāṇavyūhāyeti //4,3.36//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the qualifier '<s>prāṇavyūhāya</s>' (for the deployment of <s>prāṇas</s>) is fitting and purposeful. (4.3.36)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.3.36:] That condition of breathing upward — at what time, from what cause, in what manner, and for what purpose does it occur? — this is stated. This (<s>saḥ</s>) — the natural physical body consisting of head, hands, and the like — <s>yatra</s> — at whatever time — this [body] reaches emaciation (<s>aṇimāna</s>) — the state of being minute, meaning thinness, leanness — it reaches, it attains. From what cause? Either through old age — by itself alone, like a naturally ripened fruit, having grown old, it reaches emaciation. Or '<s>upatapatā</s>' — afflicted — [meaning] by disease such as fever and the like. Being afflicted by disease, through the imbalance of the digestive fire, the eaten food is not digested; consequently, the body, not being nourished by the essence of food, falls into emaciation — this is what is stated by '<s>upatapatā</s>.' It reaches emaciation. When extreme emaciation is attained due to causes such as old age and the like, then [the person] becomes one who breathes upward. When breathing upward, then like a heavily loaded cart, [the self] goes creaking. Old age, affliction by disease and the like, and the onset of emaciation — these misfortunes are inevitably [experienced] by one who possesses a body — this is stated for the purpose of [generating] dispassion. When this [self] goes creaking, then how does it leave the body? An illustration is stated: there — just as a mango (<s>āmra</s>) fruit, or a fig (<s>udumbara</s>), or a fruit of the sacred fig (<s>pippala</s>). The use of multiple dissimilar illustrations is for the purpose of indicating that the causes of death are undetermined. For the causes of death are undetermined and innumerable. This too is for the purpose of dispassion alone — since this [person] has innumerable causes of death, therefore he always stands in the jaws of death. From the bond (<s>bandhana</s>) — that by which it is bound, namely the stalk, or the sap by which it is bound — the stalk itself is called the bond; from that sap or stalk, the bond, it is released. [This occurs] through wind and numerous other causes. Even so, this <s>puruṣa</s> — the self conditioned by the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) — from these limbs — from the parts of the body such as eyes and the rest — frees himself completely (<s>saṃpramucya</s>), releases himself entirely and without residue. Not as at the time of going to deep sleep, [when] the <s>prāṇa</s> protects [the body]. Rather, withdrawing together with the vital air (<s>vāyu</s>). Again (<s>punaḥ</s>) — by the word 'again,' [it is indicated that] even previously, this [self] has gone from body to body not just once; just as it returns again and again from dream to waking and from waking to dream, so too again, <s>pratinyāya</s> — according to the established path, meaning 'the way it came.' <s>Pratiyoni</s> — toward the womb; toward the womb, in accordance with its <s>karma</s>, <s>śruta</s> (learning), and the like, it runs. For what purpose? For <s>prāṇa</s> alone — meaning: for the deployment of the <s>prāṇas</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,3.37
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.3.37]

children.text:
tad yathā rājānam āyantam ugrāḥ pratyenasaḥ sūtagrāmaṇyo 'nnaiḥ pānair avasathaiḥ pratikalpante 'yam āyāty ayam āgacchatīti |
evaṃ haivaṃvidaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni pratikalpanta idaṃ brahmāyātīdam āgacchatīti || BrhUp_4,3.37 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, when a king is arriving, the <s>ugras</s> (village officers), <s>pratyenasas</s> (police officers), chariot-drivers, and village headmen wait for him with food, drink, and lodgings, [saying] 'Here he comes! Here he approaches!' — even so, all beings wait for one who knows thus, [saying] 'Here <s>Brahman</s> comes! Here it approaches!' (BṛUp 4.3.37)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,3.37 tatrāsyedaṃ śarīraṃ parityajya gacchato nānyasya dehāntarasyopādāne sāmarthyamasti /
dehendriyaviyogāt /
na cānye 'sya bhṛtyasthānīyā gṛhamiva rājñe śarīrāntaraṃ kṛtvā pratīkṣamāṇā vidyante /
athaivaṃ sati kathamasya śarīrāntaropādānamiti /
ucyate-sarvaṃ hyasya jagatsvakarmaphalopabhogasādhanatvāyopāttaṃ svakarmaphalopabhogāya cāyaṃ pravṛtto dehāddehāntaraṃ pratipitsustasmātsarvameva jagatsvakarmaṇā prayuktaṃ tatkarmaphalopabhogāyogyaṃ sādhanaṃ kṛtvā pratīkṣata eva /
"kṛtaṃ lokaṃ puruṣo 'bhijāyate"iti śruteḥ /
yathā svapnājjāgaritaṃ pratipitsoḥ /
tatkathamiti lokaprasiddho dṛṣṭānta ucyate-tattatra yathā rājānaṃ rājyābhiṣiktamāyāntaṃ svarāṣṭra ugrā jātiviśeṣāḥ krūrakarmaṇo vā pratyenasaḥ prati pratenasi pāpakarmaṇi niyuktāḥ pratyenasastaskarādidaṇḍanādau niyuktāḥ sūtāśca grāmaṇyo grāmanetāraste pūrvameva rājña āgamanaṃ buddhvānnairbhojyabhakṣyādiprakāraiḥ pānairmadirādibhirāvasathaiśca prāsādādibhiḥ pratikalpante niṣpannaireva pritīkṣante 'yaṃ rājā'yātyayamāgacchatītyevaṃ vadantaḥ /
yathāyaṃ dṛṣṭānta evaṃ haivaṃvidaṃ karmaphalasya veditāraṃ saṃsāriṇamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As is this illustration, even so, for one who knows thus — meaning one who knows the fruit of <s>karma</s>, the <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being) — this is the meaning.

children.text: karmaphalaṃ hi prastutaṃ tadevaṃśabdena parāmṛśyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the fruit of <s>karma</s> is the topic at hand; that is referred to by the word '<s>evam</s>' (thus).

children.text: sarvāṇi bhūtāni śarīrakartṝṇi karaṇānugrahītṝṇi cā'dityādīni tatkarmaprayuktāni kṛtaireva karmaphalobabhogasādhanaiḥ pratīkṣante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] All beings — those that create the body, and those that assist the senses, such as <s>Āditya</s> (sun) and the like — impelled by his <s>karma</s>, with the already-prepared means for the fruition of <s>karma</s>, they wait.

children.text: idaṃ brahma bhoktṛkartṛ cāsmākamāyāti tathedamāgacchatītyevameva ca kṛtvā pratīkṣanta ityarthaḥ //4,3.37//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This <s>Brahman</s> — the experiencer and agent — of ours is coming; thus this one approaches!' — having done so in this very way, they wait — this is the meaning. (4.3.37)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.3.37:] Therein, for this [self] who abandons this body and goes forth, there is no capacity of another to prepare a different body [for it] — because of separation from the body and senses. Nor are there other servants, like those of a king, who stand waiting, having prepared another body as a house [is prepared] for a king. If this is so, how does it take up another body? It is said: for the entire world has been taken up for the purpose of serving as the means for the fruition of its own <s>karma</s>, and this [self] has set forth for the fruition of its own <s>karma</s>, wishing to proceed from one body to another; therefore, the entire world, impelled by its <s>karma</s>, having prepared the means suitable for the fruition of that <s>karma</s>, indeed waits. [As the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'A person is born into a world that has been made [for him]' (BṛUp 4.4.6). Just as [one proceeds] from dream to waking. An illustration well-known in the world is stated for this: there — just as a king — an anointed sovereign — who is arriving, coming to his own kingdom, the <s>ugras</s> — a particular caste, or those performing cruel deeds — the <s>pratyenasas</s> — those appointed to [punish] sins, meaning those appointed for the punishment of thieves and the like — chariot-drivers (<s>sūtas</s>) and village headmen (<s>grāmaṇyas</s>), leaders of villages — they, having learned beforehand of the king's arrival, with foods — various kinds of edible and consumable provisions — with drinks such as liquors and the like — with lodgings such as palaces and the like — <s>pratikalpante</s> — they wait with everything prepared, saying 'This king is coming! This one approaches!'

children.text: START BrhUp 4,3.38
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.3.38]

children.text:
tad yathā rājānaṃ prayiyāsantam ugrāḥ pratyenasaḥ sūtagrāmaṇyo 'bhisamāyanti |
evam evemam ātmānam antakāle sarve prāṇā abhisamāyanti |
yatraitad ūrdhvocchvāsī bhavati || BrhUp_4,3.38 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, when a king is about to depart, the <s>ugras</s>, <s>pratyenasas</s>, chariot-drivers, and village headmen gather around him — even so, at the time of death, all the <s>prāṇas</s> gather around this self, when [the dying person] becomes one who breathes upward. (BṛUp 4.3.38)

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,3.38 tameva jigamiṣuṃ ke saha gacchante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 4.3.38:] That [self] which wishes to depart — who goes along with it?

children.text: ye vā gacchanti te kiṃ tatkriyāpraṇunnā āhosvittatkarmavaśātsvayameva gacchanti paralokaśarīrakartṝṇi ca bhūtānīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And those who go — are they impelled by its action, or do they go of their own accord? [And are they] the beings that create the next body?

children.text: atrocyate dṛṣṭāntaḥ - tatadyathā rājānaṃ prayiyāsantaṃ prakarṣeṇa yātumicchantamugrāḥ pratyenasaḥ sūtagrāmaṇyastaṃ yathābhisamāyantyābhumikhyena samāyantyekībhāvena tamabhimukhā āyantyanājñaptā eva rājñā kevalaṃ tajjigamiṣābhijñāḥ, evamevemamātmānaṃ bhoktāramantakāle maraṇakāle sarve prāṇā vāgādayo 'bhisamāyanti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here an illustration is stated: just as, when a king is about to depart, wishing to travel far, the <s>Ugrāḥ</s> (fierce guards), the <s>Pratyenasaḥ</s> (border-officials), the <s>Sūtagrāmaṇīs</s> (chariot-chieftains) assemble around him — approaching face to face, coming to unite — they come toward him, not even commanded by the king, merely knowing his wish to go. Even so, all the <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the rest — assemble around this self, the experiencer, at the time of death.

children.text: yatrātadūrdhvocchvāsī bhavatīti vyākhyātam //4,3.38//
children.translated_text: 'Where he then becomes one who breathes upward' — this has been explained. // 4.3.38 //

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye caturthādhyāyasya tṛtīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the fourth chapter of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s>. //

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.1]

children.text:
sa yatrāyam ātmābalyaṃ nyetya saṃmoham iva nyeti |
athainam ete prāṇā abhisamāyanti |
sa etās tejomātrāḥ samabhyādadāno hṛdayam evānvavakrāmati |
sa yatraiṣa cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣaḥ parāṅ paryāvartate |
athārūpajño bhavati || BrhUp_4,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: When this self comes to weakness and, as it were, comes to a state of bewilderment, then these <s>prāṇas</s> assemble around it. It gathers up these particles of light (<s>tejomātrās</s>) and descends into the heart. When this person of the eye (<s>cākṣuṣa puruṣa</s>) turns away, then one becomes unable to perceive forms. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.1 sa yatrāyamamātmā /
saṃsāropavarṇanaṃ prastutam /
tatrāyaṃ puruṣa ebhyo 'ṅgebhyaḥ saṃpramucyetyuktam /
tatsaṃpramokṣaṇaṃ kasminkāle kathe veti savistaraṃ saṃsaraṇaṃ varṇayitavyamityāpabhyate-so 'yamātmā prastuto yatra yasminkāle 'balyamabalabhāvaṃ ni etya gatvā /
yaddehasya daurbalyaṃ tadātmana eva daurbalyamityuparyate 'balyaṃ nyetyeti /
na hyasau svato 'mūrtatvādabalabhāvaṃ gacchati /
tathā saṃmohamiva saṃmūṭhatā saṃmoho vivekābhāvaḥ saṃmūḍhatāmiva nyeti nigacchati /
na cāsya svataḥ saṃmoho 'saṃmoho vāsti /
nityacaitanyajyotiḥsvabhāvatvāt /
tenevaśabdaḥ saṃmohamiva nyetīti /
utkrāntikālaṃ hi karaṇopasaṃhāranimitto vyākulībhāva ātmana iva lakṣyate laikikaiḥ /
tathā ca vaktāro bhavanti saṃmūḍhaḥ saṃmūḍho 'yamiti /
atha vobhayatrevaśabdaprayogo yojyaḥ /
abalyamiva nyet saṃmohamiva nyetīti /
ubhayas paropādhinimittatvāviśeṣāt /
samānakartṛkanirdeśācca /
athāsminkāla ete prāṇā vāgādaya enamātmanamabhisamāyanti tadāsya śārīrasyā'tmano 'ṅgebhyaḥ saṃpramo7ṇam /
kathaṃ punaḥ saṃpramokṣaṇaṃ kena vā prakāreṇā'tmānamabhisamāyantīti /
ucyate-sa ātmaitāstejomātrāstejaso mātrāstejomātrāstejovayavā rūpādiprakāśakatvāccakṣurādīni karaṇānītyarthaḥ /
tā etāḥ samabhyādadānaḥ samyaṅnirlepenābhyādadāna ābhimukhyenā /
ña'dadānaḥ saṃharamāṇastatsvapnāpekṣayā viśeṣaṇaṃ samiti /
na tu svapne nirlepena samyāgādānam /
asti tvādānamātram /
'gṛhītā vāggṛhītaṃ cakṣuḥ' 'asya lokasya sarvāvato mātrāmapādāya' 'śukramādāye'tyādivākyebhyaḥ /
hṛdayameva puṇḍarīkākāramanvakrāmatyanvāgacchati /
hṛdaye 'bhivyaktavijñāno bhavatītyarthaḥ /
buddhyādivikṣepopasaṃhāpe sati /
na hi tasya svataścalanaṃ vikṣepopasaṃhārādivikriyā vā /
dhyāyatīva lelāyatīvetyuktvāt /
buddhyādyupādhidvāraiva hi sarvavikriyā'dhyāropyatetasmin /
kadā punastasya tejomātrābhyādāmiti /
uc.te-sa yatraiṣa cakṣuṣi bhavaścākṣuṣa- puruṣa jādityāṃśo bhoktuḥ karmaṇā prayukto yādavaddehadhāraṇaṃ tāvaccakṣuṣo 'nugrahaṃ kurvanvartate /
maraṇakāle tvasya cakṣuranugrahaṃ parityajati svamādityātmānaṃ pratipadyate /
tadetaduktaṃ"yatrāsya puruṣasya mṛtasyāgniṃ vāgapyeti vātaṃ prāṇaścakṣurādityāmi"tyādi /
punardehagrahaṇakāle saṃśrayiṣyanti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] At the time of assuming a new body, they will rejoin [the self].

children.text: tathā svapsyataḥ prabudhyataśca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And likewise when falling asleep and when waking up.

children.text: tadetadāhi-cākṣuṣaḥ puruṣo yatra yasminkāle parāṅparyāvartate parisamantātparāṅvyāvartata iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is what [the text] says: the <s>cākṣuṣa puruṣa</s> (person of the eye) — when, at which time, he turns completely away (<s>parāṅ paryāvartate</s>) — turns away in all directions.

children.text: athātrāsminkāle 'rūpajño bhavati mumūrṣū rūpaṃ na jānāti tadāyamātmā cakṣurāditejomātrāḥ samabhyādadāno bhavati svapnkāla iva //4,4.1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then, at this time — one who is about to die (<s>mumūrṣu</s>) — becomes unable to perceive forms (<s>arūpajña</s>); then this self is gathering up the <s>tejomātrās</s> (particles of light) — the sense-organs such as the eye and the rest — just as in the dream state. // 4.4.1 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 4.4.1: 'When this self' — the description of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) is the topic under discussion.
Therein, it was stated: 'This person is released from these limbs.'
The detailed description of transmigration is to be presented — [explaining] at what time and in what manner that release [occurs] — so it is commenced. This self under discussion — 'when,' at which time — 'comes to weakness' (<s>abalya</s>), reaches a state of powerlessness.
The weakness of the body is spoken of as the weakness of the self itself — thus it is said: 'comes to weakness.'
For it does not of itself reach a state of powerlessness, being formless by nature.
Likewise, 'as it were, to bewilderment' — bewilderment is the absence of discrimination — it arrives at, as it were, a state of bewilderment.
Nor does it inherently possess bewilderment or non-bewilderment,
because its nature is the eternal light of consciousness.
Therefore the word 'as it were' (<s>iva</s>) [is used]: 'as it were, comes to bewilderment.'
For at the time of departure, the disturbance caused by the withdrawal of the sense-organs appears to ordinary people as if belonging to the self.
And thus speakers say: 'He is bewildered, he is bewildered.'
Alternatively, the word 'as it were' should be construed with both: 'comes to weakness, as it were' and 'comes to bewilderment, as it were,'
because there is no difference in both being caused by external limiting adjuncts,
and because of the indication of the same agent [for both].
Then, at this time, these <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the rest — assemble around this self. Then occurs the release of this embodied self from the limbs.
But how does the release happen, and in what manner do they assemble around the self?
It is said: this self gathers up these <s>tejomātrās</s> (particles of light) — <s>tejas</s> means luminosity, <s>mātrā</s> means particle — '<s>tejomātrās</s>' means the particles of luminous energy, i.e., the sense-organs such as the eye and the rest, since they illuminate forms and other [objects] — this is the meaning.
These [particles of light] he gathers up completely (<s>samabhyādadāna</s>) — taking them back toward himself without residue, withdrawing them.
The prefix <s>sam</s> qualifies [the action] in contrast to [the partial withdrawal in] dream.
For in dream there is no complete, residue-free gathering up;
rather, there is only a partial gathering up —
as [known] from such passages as 'Speech is taken up, the eye is taken up,' 'Having taken a portion of this entire world,' and 'Having taken up the shining [faculties].'
He descends into the heart — the lotus-shaped [organ] — meaning: consciousness becomes manifest in the heart.
This [occurs] when there is the expansion and withdrawal of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the like.
For there is no movement of its own, nor modification such as expansion and withdrawal.
Because it was stated: 'It thinks, as it were; it moves, as it were.'
For all modification is superimposed upon it only through the limiting adjuncts of <s>buddhi</s> and the like.
But when does it gather up the <s>tejomātrās</s>?
It is said: when this person who is in the eye (<s>cākṣuṣa puruṣa</s>) — the portion of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) — [who,] impelled by the <s>karma</s> of the experiencer, serves to support the eye as long as the body is maintained —
at the time of death, he relinquishes his support of the eye and returns to his own solar nature.
This is what was stated: 'When this person dies, speech enters fire, <s>prāṇa</s> enters the wind, the eye enters the sun' and so forth.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.2]

children.text:
ekībhavati na paśyatīty āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na jighratīty āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na rasayatīty āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na vadatīty āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na śṛṇotīty āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na manuta ity āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na spṛśatīty āhuḥ |
ekībhavati na vijānātīty āhuḥ |
tasya haitasya hṛdayasyāgraṃ pradyotate |
tena pradyotenaiṣa ātmā niṣkrāmati |
cakṣuṣṭo vā mūrdhno vānyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhyaḥ |
tam utkrāmantaṃ prāṇo 'nūtkrāmati |
prāṇam anūtkrāmantaṃ sarve prāṇā anūtkrāmanti |
savijñano bhavati |
saṃjānam evānvavakrāmati |
taṃ vidyākarmaṇī samanvārabhete pūrvaprajñā ca || BrhUp_4,4.2 ||
children.translated_text:
'He becomes one' (<s>ekībhavati</s>) — they say, 'he does not see.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not smell.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not taste.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not speak.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not hear.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not think.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not touch.' 'He becomes one' — they say, 'he does not know.'
The tip of his heart lights up. By that illumination, the self departs — either through the eye, or through the crown of the head, or through other parts of the body.
When it departs, <s>prāṇa</s> follows after it. When <s>prāṇa</s> departs, all the <s>prāṇas</s> follow after it.
It becomes endowed with particular consciousness (<s>savijñāna</s>). It follows after that which has consciousness. Knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and <s>karma</s> attend upon it, as does the experience of former lives (<s>pūrvaprajñā</s>). // <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.2 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.2 ekībhavati karaṇajātaṃ svena liṅgātmanā /
tadaivana pārśvasthā āhurna paśyatīti /
tathā ghrāṇadevatānivṛttau ghrāṇamekībhavati liṅgātmanā tadā na jighratītyāhuḥ /
samānamanyat /
jihvāyāṃ somo varuṇo vā devatā tannivṛtyapekṣayā na rasayata ityāhuḥ /
tathā na vadati na śṛṇoti na manute na spṛśati na vijānātītyāhuḥ /
tadopalakṣyate devatānivṛttiḥ karaṇānāṃ ca hṛdaya ekībhāvaḥ /
tatra hṛdaya upasaṃhṛteṣu karaṇeṣu yo 'ntarvāyapāraḥ sa kathyate-tasya haitasya prakṛtasya hṛdayasya hṛdayacchidrasyetyetat /
agraṃ nāḍīmukhaṃ nirgamadvāraṃ pradyotate svapnakāla iva svena bhāsātejomātrādānakṛtena svonāva jyotiṣā'tmanaiva ca /
tenā'tmajyotiṣā pradyotena hṛdayāgreṇaiṣa ātmā vijñānamayo liṅgopādhirnigracchati niṣkramāti /
tathā'tharvaṇe"kasminnvahamutkrānta utkrānto bhaviṣyāmi kasminvā pratiṣṭhate pratiṣṭhāsyāmīti sa prāṇamasṛjata"iti /
tatra cā'tmacaitanyajyotiḥ sarvadābhivyaktataram /
tadupādhidvārā hyātmani janmamaraṇagamanāgamanādisarvavikriyālakṣaṇaḥ saṃvyavahāraḥ /
tadātmakaṃ hi dvādaśavidhaṃ karaṇaṃ buddhyādi tatsūtraṃ tajjīvanaṃ so 'ntarātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca /
tena pradyotena hṛdayāgraprakāśena niṣkramamāṇaḥ kena mārgeṇa niṣkrāmatīti /
ucyate-cakṣuṣṭo vā /
ādityalokaprāptinimittaṃ jñānaṃ karma vā yadi syāt /
mūrdhno vā brahmalokaprāptinimittaṃ cet /
anyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhyaḥ śarīrāvayavebhyo yathākarma yathāśrutam /
taṃ vijñānātmānamutkrāmantaṃ paralokasya prasthitaṃ paralokāyodbhūtākūtamityartha- /
prāṇaḥ sarvādhikāristhānīyo rājña ivānūtkrāmati /
taṃ ca prāṇamanūtkrāmantaṃ vāgādayaḥ sarve prāṇāṃ anūtkrāmanti /
yathāpradhānānvācikhyāseyaṃ na tu krameṇa sārthavadgmanamiha vivakṣitam /
tadaiṣa ātmā savijñāno bhavati svapn iva viśeṣavijñānavānbhavati karmavaśānn svatantraḥ svātantryeṇa hi savijñānatve sarvaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ syāt /
naiva tu tallabhyate /
ata evā'ha vyāsaḥ"sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ"iti /
karmaṇā tūdbhāvyamānenāntaḥkaraṇavṛttiviśeṣāśritavāsanātmakaviśeṣavijñānena sarvo loka etasminkāle savijñāno bhavati /
savijñānameva ca gantavyamanvavakrāmatyagacchati viśeṣavijñānodbhāsitamevetyarthaḥ /
tasmāttatkāle svātantryārthaṃ yogadharmānusevanaṃ parisaṃkhyānābhyāsaśca viśiṣṭapuṇyopayaśca śraddhadhānaiḥ paralokārthibhirapramattaiḥ kartavya iti /
sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ yatnato vidheyor'tho duścaritāccoparamaṇam /
na hi tatkāle śakyate kiñcitsampādayitum /
karmaṇā nīyamānasya svātantryābhāvāt /
'puṇyo vai puṇyena karmaṇā bhavati pāpaḥ pāpena'tyuktam /
etasya hyanarthasyopaśamopāyavidhānāyā sarvaśākhopaniṣadaḥ pravṛttāḥ /
na hi tadvihitopāyānusevanaṃ muktvā'tyantiko 'syānarthasyopaśamopāyo 'sti /
tasmādatraivopaniṣadvihitopāye yatnaparairbhavitavyamityeṣa prakaraṇārthaḥ /
śakaṭavastaṃbhṛsaṃbhāraṃ utsarjanyātītyuktaṃ, kiṃ punastasya paralokāya pravṛttasya pathdanaṃ śākaṭikasaṃbhārasthānīyaṃ gatvā vā paralokaṃ yadbhuṅkte śarīrādyārambhakaṃ ca yattatkimiti /
ucyate-taṃ paralokāya gacchantamātmānaṃ vidyākarmaṇī vidyā ca karma ca vidyākarmaṇī vidyā sravaprakārā vihitā pratiṣiddhā cāvihitāpratiṣiddhā ca /
tathā karma vihitaṃ pratiṣiddhaṃ cāvihitapratiṣiddhaṃ ca samanvārabhete samyaganvārabhete anvālabhete anugacchataḥ pūrvaprajñā ca pūrvānubhūtaviṣayā prajñāpūrvaprajñātītakarmaphalānubhavavāsanetyarthaḥ /
sā ca vāsanāpūrvakarmarambhe karmavipāke cāṅgaṃ bhavati /
tenāsāvapyanvāpabhate /
na hi tayā vāsanayā vinā karma kartuṃ phalaṃ copabhoktuṃ śakyate /
na hyanabhyaste viṣaye kauśalamindrayāṇāṃ bhavati /
pūrvānubhavavāsanāpravṛttānāṃ tvindriyāṇāmihābhyāsamanantareṇa kauśalamupapadyate /
dṛśyate ca keṣāñcitkāsucitkriyāsu citrakarmādilakṣaṇāsu vinaivehābhyāsena janmata eva kauśalaṃ kāsucidatyantasaukaryayuktāsvapyakauśalaṃ koṣāñcit /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And it is observed that some people possess skill from birth itself in certain artistic activities such as painting and the like, without any practice in this [life], while some people lack skill even in [activities] that are accompanied by extreme ease.

children.text: tathā pūrvaprajñayā vinā karmaṇi vā phalopabhoge vā na kasyacitpravṛttirupapadyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Likewise, without <s>pūrvaprajñā</s> (experience of former lives), no one's engagement in either action or the enjoyment of its fruit is tenable.

children.text: tasmādetattrayaṃ śākaṭikasambhārasthānīyaṃ paralokapathyadana vidyākarmapūrvaprajñākhyam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, this triad — called <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>karma</s> (action), and <s>pūrvaprajñā</s> (former experience) — constitutes the provisions for the journey, analogous to the supplies of a carter.

children.text: yasmādvidyākramaṇī pūrvapjñā ca dehāntarapratipatyupabhogasādhanaṃ tasmadvidyākarmādi śubhameva samātaredyatheṣṭadehasambhogopabhogau syātāmiti prakaraṇārthaḥ //4,4.2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Since <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s>, together with <s>pūrvaprajñā</s>, are the means for obtaining a new body and experiencing [its fruits] — therefore one should accumulate only auspicious <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s>, so that the desired body and the desired experience may be obtained — this is the import of the passage. // 4.4.2 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 4.4.2: 'He becomes one' (<s>ekībhavati</s>) — the aggregate of sense-organs [becomes unified] with its own subtle body (<s>liṅgātman</s>).
Then, those standing nearby say: 'He does not see.'
Likewise, when the deity of the organ of smell withdraws — smell becomes one with the subtle body — then they say: 'He does not smell.'
The rest is similar.
In the tongue, <s>Soma</s> or <s>Varuṇa</s> is the deity — with reference to the withdrawal of that [deity], they say: 'He does not taste.'
Likewise: 'He does not speak,' 'He does not hear,' 'He does not think,' 'He does not touch,' 'He does not know' — thus they say.
Thereby the withdrawal of the deities and the unification of the sense-organs in the heart is indicated.
There, when the sense-organs have been withdrawn into the heart, the intervening [process] is described: of this — the one under discussion — heart, i.e., of the aperture of the heart — this is the meaning —
the tip (<s>agra</s>), the opening of the <s>nāḍī</s>, the exit-door, lights up — as in the dream state, by its own radiance — the illumination produced by the gathering up of the <s>tejomātrās</s> — by its own light, and by the light of the self itself.
By that illumination of the tip of the heart, this self — the <s>vijñānamaya</s> (made of consciousness), conditioned by the subtle body — departs, exits.
As the <s>Atharvaveda</s> also [says]: 'In what [capacity], having departed, shall I be departed? In what [capacity], being established, shall I be established? — Thus it created <s>prāṇa</s>.'
And there, the consciousness-light of the self is always most fully manifest.
For through the limiting adjunct, all transactional activity characterized by birth, death, coming, going, and the like is [superimposed] upon the self.
For the twelve-fold instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) — <s>buddhi</s> and the rest — is of that [self's] nature; that is its thread (<s>sūtra</s>), that is its life; it is the inner self (<s>antarātman</s>) of both the moving and the stationary [creation].
By that illumination — the light at the tip of the heart — through which path does it depart when departing?
It is said: either through the eye,
if there is knowledge or <s>karma</s> that is the cause of attaining the world of <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun);
or through the crown of the head, if [the cause is] for attaining the world of <s>Brahmā</s>;
or through other parts of the body — other limbs — according to one's <s>karma</s>, according to one's knowledge.
That <s>vijñānātman</s> (consciousness-self) departing — set forth toward the other world, meaning: having arisen with the intention directed toward the other world —
<s>Prāṇa</s>, holding the position of chief superintendent — like a king — follows after it.
And when <s>prāṇa</s> follows after it, all the <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the rest — follow after it.
This description of sequential following is not meant [to indicate] an actual procession with purpose, like that of a caravan;
rather, [it is described] in the manner of following the chief.
Then this self becomes <s>savijñāna</s> (endowed with particular consciousness) — as in dream, it possesses specific cognition due to the force of <s>karma</s>, not independently. For if it were independently endowed with consciousness, everyone would be fully accomplished.
But that [independence] is never obtained.
Therefore <s>Vyāsa</s> also says: 'Always absorbed in the contemplation of That' (BhG 12.8).
Rather, through the specific cognition whose nature consists of <s>vāsanās</s> (latent impressions) residing in particular modifications of the internal organ, produced by <s>karma</s> that is being activated — everyone at this time becomes endowed with [particular] consciousness.
And being endowed with consciousness, it follows after that which is to be attained — the destination illuminated by specific cognition — this is the meaning.
Therefore, at that time, for the purpose of independence [over one's destiny], the practice of the disciplines of <s>yoga</s>, the cultivation of discrimination (<s>parisaṃkhyāna</s>), and the accumulation of distinguished merit should be undertaken by those who have faith, who seek the other world, and who are vigilant.
The meaning that is to be strived for from all <s>śāstras</s> [is to be practiced], and there should be cessation from misconduct.
For at that time [of death], nothing can be accomplished,
because of the absence of independence for one who is being carried along by <s>karma</s>.
'One becomes meritorious by meritorious action, sinful by sinful [action]' — thus it was stated.
For the purpose of prescribing the means of cessation of this calamity, all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> of all the [Vedic] branches have been set forth.
For apart from the practice of the means prescribed therein, there is no means whatsoever for the complete cessation of this calamity.
Therefore, one should be intent upon effort in the means prescribed by the <s>Upaniṣads</s> alone — this is the import of the passage.
It was stated: 'Leaving behind the provisions of the cart, he departs.' But what then is the provision for the journey to the other world — analogous to the supplies of a carter — and what does he enjoy upon reaching the other world, and what initiates the [new] body and the rest?
It is answered: that self, going to the other world — knowledge and <s>karma</s> — <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>karma</s> (action) — <s>vidyā</s> of every kind, whether enjoined or prohibited, as well as that which is neither enjoined nor prohibited;
likewise <s>karma</s> — enjoined, prohibited, and that which is neither enjoined nor prohibited — attend upon it (<s>samanvārabhete</s>), follow after it, accompany it. And <s>pūrvaprajñā</s> — the cognition pertaining to objects previously experienced — meaning: the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of the experience of the fruits of past <s>karma</s>.
And that <s>vāsanā</s> serves as an auxiliary both in the commencement of [new] <s>karma</s> and in the ripening of [its] fruits.
Therefore, it too attends upon [the departing self].
For without that <s>vāsanā</s>, it is not possible to perform action or to experience its fruit.
For the sense-organs do not possess skill in a subject that has not been previously practiced.
But the sense-organs that are activated by the <s>vāsanās</s> of previous experience — for them, skill arises here even without [fresh] practice.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.3

tad yathā tṛṇajalāyukā tṛṇasyāntaṃ gatvānyam ākramam ākramyātmānam upasaṃharati |
evam evāyam ātmedaṃ śarīraṃ nihatyāvidyāṃ gamayitvānyam ākramam ākramyātmānam upasaṃharati || BrhUp_4,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: Just as a grass-leech (<s>tṛṇajalāyukā</s>), having reached the tip of a blade of grass, takes hold of another support and draws itself together — even so, this self, having cast aside this body and having dispelled ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>), takes hold of another support and draws itself together. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.3 //
[Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.3]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.3 evaṃ vidyādisambārasamphṛto dehāntaraṃ pratipadyamāno muktvā pūrvaṃ dehaṃ pakṣīva vṛkṣāntaraṃ dehāntaraṃ pratipadyate /
athavā'tivāhikena śarīrāntareṇa karmaphalajanmadeśaṃ nīyate /
kiñcātrasthasyaiva sarvagatānāṃ karaṇānāṃ vṛttilābho bhavatyāhosviccharīraḥsya saṃkucitāni karaṇāni mṛtasya bhinnaghaṭapradīpaprakāśavatsarvato vyapya punardehāntarārambhe saṅkocamupagacchanti /
kiñca manomātraṃ vaiśeṣikasamaya iva dehāntarārambhadeśaṃ prati gacchati kiṃvā kalpanānāntarameva vedāntasamaya iti /
ucyate-"ta ete sarva eva samāḥ sarve 'nantāḥ"iti śruteḥ sarvātmakāni tāvatkaraṇāni /
sarvātmakaprāṇasaṃśrayācca /
teṣāmādhyāmikādhibhautikaparicchedaḥ prāṇikarmajñānabhāvanānimittaḥ /
atastadvaśātsvabhāvataḥ sargatānāmanantānāmapi prāṇānāṃ karjñānavāsanānurūpeṇaiva dehānnarārambhavaśātprāṇānāṃ vṛttiḥ saṃkucati vikasati ca /
tathā coktam-"samaḥ pluṣiṇā samo maśakena samo nāgena sama ebhistribhirlokaiḥ samo 'nena sarveṇa"iti /
tathā cedaṃ vacanamanukūlam-",sa yo haitānanantānupāste"ityādi /
"taṃ yathā yathopāsate"iti ca /
tatra vāsanā pūrvaprajñākhyā vidyākarmatantrā jalūkavatsaṃtataiva svapnakāla iva karmakṛtaṃ dehāddehāntaramārabhate hṛdayasyaiva punardehāntarārambhe dehāntaraṃ pūrvāśrayaṃ vimuñcatītyetasminnarthe dṛṣṭānta upādīyate-tattatra dehāntarasañcāra idaṃ nidarśanam /
yathā yena prakāreṇa tṛṇajalāyukā tṛṇajalūkā tṛṇasyāntamavasānaṃ gatvā prāpyānyaṃ tṛṇāntaramākramamākramyata ityākramastamākramamākramyā'ścityā'tmānamātmanaḥ pūrvavayavamupasaṃharatyantyāvayavasthāne /
evamevāyamātmā yaḥ prakṛtaḥ saṃsārīdaṃ śarīraṃ pūrvopāttaṃ nihatya svapnaṃ pratipitsuriva pātayitvāvidyāṃ gamayitvācetanaṃ kṛtvā svātmosaṃhāreṇānyamākramaṃ tṛṇāntaramiva tṛṇajalūkā śarīrāntaraṃ gṛhītvā prasārityā vāsanayā'mānamupasaṃharati /
tatrā'tmabhāvamārabhate yathā svapne dehāntaramārabhate svapnadehāntarasya śarīrāmbhadeśa ārabhyamāṇe dehe jaṅgame sthāvare vā /
tatra ca karmavaśātkaraṇāni labdhavṛttīni saṃhanyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And there, the instruments, having acquired their functioning through the force of <s>karma</s>, are assembled together.

children.text: bāhyaṃ ca kuśamṛttikāsthānīyaṃ śarīramārabhyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And the external body — corresponding to the grass and clay [in the analogy] — is commenced.

children.text: tatra ca karaṇavyūhamapekṣya vāgādyanugrahāyāgnyādidevatāḥ saṃścayante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And there, with a view to the arrangement of the instruments, and for the benefit of speech and the like, the deities such as <s>Agni</s> and the rest are assembled.

children.text: eṣa dehāntarārambhavidhiḥ //4,4.3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is the method of the commencement of another body. (4.4.3)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.3:] Thus, equipped with the provisions of knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>) and the like, proceeding to obtain another body, having abandoned the former body, like a bird [moving] to another tree, it obtains another body.
Alternatively, by means of an <s>ātivāhika</s> (subtle transmigrating) body, it is carried to the place of birth determined by the fruits of <s>karma</s>.
Furthermore, do the instruments (<s>karaṇas</s>), being all-pervading, acquire their functioning while [the self] remains right here, or do the instruments, contracted within the body, upon the death [of the person], pervade everywhere — like the light of a lamp [spreading] from a broken pot — and then contract again at the commencement of another body?
Moreover, does the mind alone go to the place where another body is to commence, as in the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> system, or does [the transition happen] without any intervening construction at all, according to the <s>Vedānta</s> system?
It is replied: From the <s>śruti</s> — 'These are all equal, all infinite' — the instruments are, to begin with, of the nature of the totality of the self.
And because they depend on <s>prāṇa</s>, which is of the nature of the totality.
Their delimitation as subjective (<s>ādhyātmika</s>) and objective (<s>ādhibhautika</s>) is caused by the <s>karma</s>, knowledge, and mental impressions (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of the living being.
Therefore, by the force of that, even though the <s>prāṇas</s> are by nature all-pervading and infinite, the functioning of the <s>prāṇas</s> contracts and expands in accordance with the impressions of <s>karma</s> and knowledge, due to the commencement of different bodies.
Thus it has been said: 'Equal to a flea, equal to a mosquito, equal to an elephant, equal to these three worlds, equal to this entire [universe].'
Likewise, this statement is supportive: 'He who meditates upon these infinite [ones]' and so forth.
And: 'As one meditates upon him, so one becomes.'
Therein, the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression), called 'prior cognition' (<s>pūrvaprajñā</s>), which is governed by knowledge and <s>karma</s>, continuously — like a leech — commences another body from the body fashioned by <s>karma</s>, as in the dream state; and at the commencement of another body, it abandons the former body as its previous support — for this purpose, an illustration is given: 'This is the illustration for the passage to another body' — just as, in the manner in which, a caterpillar (<s>tṛṇajalūkā</s>) — a leech of grass — having reached the end of a blade of grass, having grasped another blade of grass — that grasping is its 'step' (<s>ākrama</s>) — having made that step, it draws itself up, draws back its former parts to the position of the last part.
Even so does this self — the one under discussion, the transmigrating self — having struck down this previously assumed body — as one wishing to enter a dream, as it were — having cast it down, having caused <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) to depart, having rendered it unconscious, by withdrawing itself, having grasped another step — like the leech [grasping] another blade of grass — having taken hold of another body, it extends itself by means of <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), and draws itself back.
There it commences its self-existence — just as in dream it commences another body — the body being commenced at the place where the dream-body is to begin, whether mobile or immobile.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.4]

children.text:
tad yathā peśaskārī peśaso mātrām apādāyānyan navataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ tanute |
evam evāyam ātmedaṃ śarīraṃ nihatyāvidyāṃ gamayitvānyan navataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ kurute |
pitryaṃ vā gāndharvaṃ vā daivaṃ vā prājāpatyaṃ vā brāhmaṃ vānyeṣāṃ vā bhūtānām || BrhUp_4,4.4 ||
children.translated_text:
Just as a goldsmith, taking a portion of gold, fashions another, newer, more beautiful form,
even so does this self, having struck down this body and having caused <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) to depart, fashion another, newer, more beautiful form —
whether that of the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), or of the <s>Gandharvas</s>, or of the <s>Devas</s> (gods), or of <s>Prajāpati</s>, or of <s>Brahmā</s>, or of any other beings. (BṛUp 4.4.4)

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,4.4 tatra dehāntarārambhe nitthopāttamevopādānamupamṛdyopamṛdya dehāntaramārabhata āhostidapūrvameva punaḥ punarādatta iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.4:] Therein, regarding the commencement of another body — does it take as its material only what was previously assumed, refashioning it again and again, or does it take something entirely new each time?

children.text: atrocyate dṛṣṭāntaḥ-tattatretasminnarthe--yathā peśaskārī peśaḥ suvarṇa tat karotīti peśaskārī suvarṇakāraḥ, peśasaḥ suvarṇasya mātrāmapādāyāpicchidya gṛhītvā anyat pūrvasmād racanāviśeṣānnavataramabhinavataraṃ kalyāṇāt kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ tanute nirminoti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] To this, an illustration is stated — in this matter: just as a goldsmith — one who works with gold (<s>peśas</s>), hence a <s>peśaskārī</s> (goldsmith) — taking a portion of gold, having cut off and taken a piece, fashions another [ornament], newer than the previous one by virtue of a distinctive design, and more beautiful than [the already] beautiful — he creates, he produces [that] form.

children.text: evamevāyamātmetyādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even so does this self' — and so forth, as before.

children.text: nityopāttānyeva pṛthivyādīnyākāśāntāni pañca bhūtāni yāni 'dve vāva brahmaṇo rūpe' iti caturthe vyākhyātāni peśaḥsthānāyāni,tānyevopamṛdyopamṛdya, anyadanyacca dehāntaraṃ navataraṃ kalyāṇataraṃ rūpaṃ saṃsthānaveśeṣaṃ vā pitṛbhyo hitaṃ pitṛlokopabhogayogyamityarthaḥ, gāndharvaṃ gandharvāṇāmupabhogayogyam, tathā devānāṃ daivam, prajāpateḥ prajāpatyam, brahmaṇa idaṃ brāhmaṃ vā; yathākarma yathāśrutamanyeṣāṃvā bhūtānāṃ sambandhi śarīrāntaraṃ kuruta ityabhisambanyate //4,4.4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The five elements — from earth to space — which are eternally assumed, which have been explained in the fourth [chapter] as 'There are indeed two forms of <s>Brahman</s>' and which correspond to the gold [in the analogy] — those very [elements], refashioning them again and again, [the self] makes another, newer, more beautiful form — that is, a bodily configuration — suitable for the <s>Pitṛs</s>, fit for enjoyment in the world of the ancestors — that is the meaning; or the <s>Gandharva</s> [form], fit for the enjoyment of the <s>Gandharvas</s>; likewise the divine [form] for the gods; that of <s>Prajāpati</s> for <s>Prajāpati</s>; or that of <s>Brahmā</s>, belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>; according to one's <s>karma</s> and learning, or belonging to any other beings — the connection is: [the self] fashions another body — this is to be supplied. (4.4.4)

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.5]

children.text:
sa vā ayam ātmā brahma vijñānamayo manomayo prāṇamayaś cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaḥ pṛthivīmaya āpomayo vāyumaya ākāśamayas tejomayo 'tejomayaḥ kāmamayo 'kāmamayaḥ krodhamayo 'krodhamayo dharmamayo 'dharmamayaḥ sarvamayaḥ |
tad yad etad idaṃmayo 'domaya iti |
yathākārī yathācārī tathā bhavati |
sādhukārī sādhur bhavati |
pāpakārī pāpo bhavati |
puṇyaḥ puṇyena karmaṇā pāpaḥ pāpena |
atho khalv āhuḥ |
kāmamaya evāyaṃ puruṣa iti |
sa yathākāmo bhavati tatkratur bhavati |
yatkratur bhavati tat karma kurute |
yat karma kurute tad abhisaṃpadyate || BrhUp_4,4.5 ||
children.translated_text:
This self is indeed <s>Brahman</s> — consisting of knowledge (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), consisting of mind (<s>manomaya</s>), consisting of <s>prāṇa</s> (<s>prāṇamaya</s>), consisting of sight (<s>cakṣurmaya</s>), consisting of hearing (<s>śrotramaya</s>), consisting of earth (<s>pṛthivīmaya</s>), consisting of water (<s>āpomaya</s>), consisting of wind (<s>vāyumaya</s>), consisting of space (<s>ākāśamaya</s>), consisting of light (<s>tejomaya</s>), consisting of non-light (<s>atejomaya</s>), consisting of desire (<s>kāmamaya</s>), consisting of non-desire (<s>akāmamaya</s>), consisting of anger (<s>krodhamaya</s>), consisting of non-anger (<s>akrodhamaya</s>), consisting of <s>dharma</s> (<s>dharmamaya</s>), consisting of non-<s>dharma</s> (<s>adharmamaya</s>), consisting of everything (<s>sarvamaya</s>).
This is what is meant by 'consisting of this, consisting of that.'
As one acts, as one conducts oneself, so one becomes.
One who does good becomes good;
one who does evil becomes evil.
One becomes meritorious by meritorious action, sinful by sinful action.
But they also say:
This person is indeed made of desire.
As is his desire, so is his resolve (<s>kratu</s>).
As is his resolve, so is the action he performs.
As is the action he performs, so is what he attains. (BṛUp 4.4.5)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.5 yo 'sya bandhanasaṃjñakā upādhibhūtāḥ, yaiḥ saṃyuttkastanmaye 'yamiti vibhāvyate, te padārthāḥ puñjīkṛtyehaikatra pratinirdiśyante-sa vā ayaṃ ya evaṃ saṃsaratyātmā brahmaiva para eva yo 'śanāyādyatīto, vijñānamayo vijñānaṃ budvistenopalaṅyamāṇastanmayaḥ /
katama ātmeti yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣviti hayuktam /
vijñānamayo vījñānaprāyo yasmāttadvarmatvamasya vibhāvyate dhyāyatīva lelāyatīveti /
tathā manomayo manaḥ saṃnikarṣānmanomayaḥ /
tathā prāṇamayaḥ prāṇaḥ pañcavṛttistanmayo yena cetanaścalatīva lakṣyate /
tathā cakṣurmayo rūpadarśanakāle /
evaṃ śrotramayaḥ śabdaśravaṇakāle /
evaṃ tasya tasyendriyasya vyāpārodbhave tattanmayo bhavati /
evaṃ budviprāṇadvāreṇa cakṣurādikaraṇamayaḥ sañśarīrārambhakapṛthivyādibhūtamayo bhavati /
tatra pārthivaśarīrārambhe pṛthivīmayo bhavati /
tathā varuṇādilokeṣvāpyaśarīrārambha āpomayo bhavati /
tathā vāyavyaśarīrārambhe vāyumayo bhavati /
tathā'kāśaśarīrārambha ākāśamayo bhavati /
evametāni taijasāni devaśarīrāṇi /
teṣvārabhyamāṇeṣu tanmayastejomayo bhavati /
ato vyatiriktāni paśvādiśarīrāṇi narakapretādiśarīrāṇi cātejomayāni tānyapekṣyā'hātejomaya iti /
evaṃ kāryakaraṇasaṃghātamayaḥ sannātmā prāptavyaṃ vastvantaraṃ paśyannidaṃ mayā prāptamado mayā prāptavyamityevaṃ viparītapratyayastadabhilāṣaḥ kāmamayo bhavati /
tasminkāme doṣaṃ paśyatastadviṣayābhilāṣapraśāme citaṃ prasannamakaluṣaṃ śāntaṃ bhavati /
tanmayo 'kāmamayaḥ /
evaṃ tasminvihate kāmekenācitsa kāmaḥ krodhatvena pariṇamate tena tanmayo bhavankrodhamayaḥ /
sa krodhaḥ kenacidupāyena nivartito yadā bhavati tadā prasannamanākulaṃ citaṃ sadakrodha ucyate tena tanmayaḥ /
evaṃ kāmakrodhābhyāmakāmākrodhābhyāṃ ca tanmayo bhūtvā dharmamayo 'dharmamayaśca bhavati /
na hi kāmakrodhādibhirvinā dharmādipravṛttirūpapadyate /
"yadyadvi kurute karma tattatkāmasya ceṣṭitam" /
iti smaraṇāt /
dharmamayo 'dharmayaśca bhūtvā sarvamayo bhavati /
samastaṃ dharmādharmayoḥ kāryaṃ yāvartkicidvyākṛtaṃ tatsarvaṃ dharmādharmayoḥ phalaṃ tatpratipadyāmānastanmayo bhavati /
kiṃ bahunā tadetatsidvamasya yadayamidaṃmayo gṛhyamāṇaviṣayādidaṃmayastasmādayamadomayaḥ /
ada iti parokṣaṃ kāryeṇa gṛhyamāṇena nirdiśyate /
anantā hyantaḥkaraṇe bhāvanāviśeṣāḥ /
naiva te viśeṣato nirdeṣṭuṃ śakyante /
tasmistasminkṣaṇe kāryato 'vagamyanta idamasya hradi vartate 'dosyate tena gṛhyamāṇakāryeṇedaṃmayatayā nirdiśyate parokṣo 'ntaḥstho vyavahāro 'yamidānīmadomaya iti /
saṃkṣepatastu yathā kartuṃ yathā vā carituṃ śīlamasya so 'yaṃ yathākārī yathā cārī sa tathā bhavati /
karaṇaṃ nāma niyatā kriyā vidhipratiṣedhādigamyā caraṇaṃ nāmāniyatamiti viśeṣaḥ /
sādhukārī sādhurbhavatīti yathākārītyasya viśeṣaṇaṃ pāpakārī pāpo bhavatīti ca yathācārītyasya /
tācchīlyapratyayopādānādatyantatātparyataiva tanmayatvaṃ na tu tatkarmamātreṇotyāśaṅkayā'ha-puṇyaḥ puṇyena karmaṇā bhavati pāpaḥ pāpeneti /
puṇyapāpakarmamātreṇaiva tanmayatā syānna tu tācchīlyamapekṣate /
tācchīlye tu tanmayatvātiśaya ityayaṃ viśeṣaḥ /
tatra kāmakrodhādipūrvakapuṇyakāritā sarvamayatve hetuḥ saṃsārasya kāraṇaṃ dehāddehāntarasaṃcārasya ca /
etatprayukto hyanyadanyaddehāntaramupādatte /
tasmātpuṇyāpuṇye saṃsārasya kāraṇam /
etadviṣayau hi vidhipratiṣedhau /
atra śāstrasya sāphalyamiti /
atho apyanye bandhamokṣakuśalāḥ khalvāhuḥ-satyaṃ kāmādipūrvake puṇyāpuṇye śarīragrahaṇakāraṇaṃ tathāpi kāmaprayukto hi puruṣaḥ puṇyapuṇye karmaṇī upacinoti kāmaprahāṇe tu karma vidyāmānamapi puṇyapuṇyepacayakaraṃ na bhavati /
upacite api puṇyapuṇye karmaṇī kāmaśūnye phalārambhake na bhavataḥ /
tasmātkāma eva saṃsārasya mūlam /
tathā cektamātharvaṇe-kāmānyaḥ kāmayate manyamānaḥ sa kāmabhirjāyate tatra tatra iti /
tasmātkāmamaya evāyaṃ puruṣo yadanyamayatvaṃ tadakāraṇaṃ vidyānamapītyapto 'vadhārayati kāmamaya eveti /
yasmātsa ca kāmamayaḥ sanyādṛśena kāmena yathākāmo bhavati tatkraturbavati sa kāma īṣadabhilāṣamātreṇābhivyakto yasminviṣaye bhavati so 'vihanyamānaḥ sphuṭībhavankratutvāmāpadyate /
kraturnādhyavasāyo niścayo yadanantarā kriyā pravartate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Kratu</s> means firm determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>), the resolve (<s>niścaya</s>) immediately after which action proceeds.

children.text: yatkraturbhavati yādṛkkāmakāryeṇa kratunā yathārūpaḥ kraturasya so 'yaṃ yatkraturbhavati tatkarma kuruteyadviṣayaḥ kratustatphalanirvṛttaye yadyogyaṃ karma tatkurute nirvartayati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As is his resolve — with whatever kind of desire-produced resolve, of whatever form his resolve is — so, being of that resolve, he performs that action — whatever action is suitable for the accomplishment of the fruit pertaining to the object of that resolve, that [action] he performs, he carries out.

children.text: yatkarma kurute tadabhisaṃpadyate, tadīyaṃ phalamabhisaṃpadyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Whatever <s>karma</s> (action) he performs, he attains that; he attains the fruit belonging to that [<s>karma</s>].

children.text: tasmātsarvamayatve 'sya saṃsāritve ca kāma heturiti //4,4.5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, since [the self] is constituted of everything and is subject to <s>saṃsāra</s>, desire is the cause [of both]. || 4.4.5 ||

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.5:] Those limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) that constitute what is called [the self's] bondage, through association with which this [self] is perceived as 'consisting of that' — those categories are gathered together and indicated here in one place: This self is indeed <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme — the one who thus transmigrates — who has transcended hunger and the rest. It is <s>vijñānamaya</s> — consisting of <s>vijñāna</s> (cognition), i.e. <s>buddhi</s> (intellect); being apprehended through that, it is perceived as consisting of that.
Which self? That which was stated: 'The one consisting of <s>vijñāna</s> among the <s>prāṇas</s>.' It is <s>vijñānamaya</s> — predominantly consisting of <s>vijñāna</s>, because its nature is perceived as that: 'it thinks, as it were; it moves, as it were.'
Likewise, it is <s>manomaya</s> — consisting of mind, because of the proximity of mind.
Likewise, <s>prāṇamaya</s> — consisting of <s>prāṇa</s>, the fivefold vital breath; because of that, the conscious [self] appears as if moving.
Likewise, <s>cakṣurmaya</s> — consisting of sight, at the time of seeing forms.
Similarly, <s>śrotramaya</s> — consisting of hearing, at the time of hearing sounds.
Thus, at the arising of the activity of each sense organ, it becomes as if consisting of that.
In this way, through the gateway of <s>buddhi</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>, it becomes as if consisting of the sense organs such as the eye and the like, and also as if consisting of the gross elements such as earth and the like, which are the material cause of the body.
Therein, at the commencement of an earthly body, it becomes <s>pṛthivīmaya</s> (consisting of earth).
Likewise, at the commencement of a body in the world of <s>Varuṇa</s> and the like, it becomes <s>āpomaya</s> (consisting of water).
Likewise, at the commencement of an airy body, it becomes <s>vāyumaya</s> (consisting of wind).
Likewise, at the commencement of a body of space, it becomes <s>ākāśamaya</s> (consisting of space).
Thus, these are the luminous divine bodies;
when these are commenced, being as if consisting of that, it becomes <s>tejomaya</s> (consisting of light).
Bodies distinct from those — [such as those of] animals and the like, and bodies of hell-dwellers and ghosts — are non-luminous; with reference to those, it is called <s>atejomaya</s> (consisting of non-light).
Thus, being as if consisting of the aggregate of effects and instruments, the self, seeing some other thing to be attained — 'This I have obtained, that I must obtain' — with such erroneous cognition and desire for that, it becomes <s>kāmamaya</s> (consisting of desire).
When, seeing a fault in that desire, the longing for that object subsides, the mind becomes clear, unpolluted, serene.
Being as if consisting of that, it is <s>akāmamaya</s> (consisting of non-desire).
Thus, when that desire is obstructed by something, that very desire transforms into anger; through that, being as if consisting of it, it becomes <s>krodhamaya</s> (consisting of anger).
When that anger is dispelled by some means, the mind being calm and untroubled is called free from anger; being as if consisting of that, [it is <s>akrodhamaya</s>].
Thus, through desire and anger, and through non-desire and non-anger, being as if consisting of those, it becomes <s>dharmamaya</s> (consisting of <s>dharma</s>) and <s>adharmamaya</s> (consisting of <s>adharma</s>).
For without desire, anger, and the like, the engagement in <s>dharma</s> and the like is not possible.
Because of the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Whatever action one performs, that is the activity of desire.'
Having become consisting of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, it becomes <s>sarvamaya</s> (consisting of everything).
The entire effect of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, whatever is differentiated — all that is the fruit of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; experiencing it, being as if consisting of that, [it becomes consisting of everything].
In short, this is established: that it is <s>idaṃmaya</s> — consisting of 'this,' of the object being apprehended — from that, it is <s>adomaya</s> — consisting of 'that.'
'That' (<s>adas</s>) refers to what is indicated indirectly by the effect being apprehended.
For the mental impressions (<s>bhāvanā</s>) in the inner organ are infinite.
They cannot be specified in detail.
At each moment, they are understood through their effects — 'this is in his heart now, that will be' — thus, through the effect being apprehended, it is indicated as <s>idaṃmaya</s>, and the internal, hidden activity — now it is <s>adomaya</s>.
But in brief, as one is accustomed to act, as one is accustomed to conduct oneself — that one, acting thus and conducting himself thus, so becomes.
'Action' (<s>karaṇa</s>) means a specific, determined act, known through injunction and prohibition; 'conduct' (<s>caraṇa</s>) means what is not [so] determined — this is the distinction.
'One who does good becomes good' — this is a specification of 'as one acts'; 'one who does evil becomes evil' — this is a specification of 'as one conducts oneself.'
Since the suffix denoting habitual disposition is used, the 'consisting-of' nature is absolute — lest one suspect it arises from a single action alone, it is said: one becomes meritorious through meritorious action, sinful through sinful [action].
Through meritorious and sinful actions alone does the 'consisting-of' nature arise, though habitual disposition is not required;
but when there is habitual disposition, there is an excess of the 'consisting-of' nature — this is the distinction.
Therein, the doing of meritorious [and sinful] acts, preceded by desire and anger, is the cause of 'consisting of everything,' the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and the cause of passage from body to body.
For impelled by this, one assumes one body after another.
Therefore, merit and demerit are the cause of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
Injunctions and prohibitions pertain to these;
therein lies the efficacy of scripture.
But others, skilled in the knowledge of bondage and liberation, say: True, merit and demerit preceded by desire and the like are the cause of assuming a body; yet, since a person impelled by desire accumulates meritorious and sinful actions, upon the abandonment of desire, even actions that exist as accumulated merit and demerit do not lead to further accumulation.
Even accumulated meritorious and sinful actions, when devoid of desire, do not become productive of results.
Therefore, desire alone is the root of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
And thus it has been stated in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>: 'He who desires something, thinking [himself to be someone], is born here and there through those desires.'
Therefore, this person is indeed made of desire. Whatever other 'consisting-of' nature there is — that is not a [primary] cause; even if knowledge is present — thus one should ascertain with certainty: [he is] consisting of desire alone.
Since he is consisting of desire, with whatever kind of desire — as is his desire, so is his resolve (<s>kratu</s>). That desire, once manifested in the slightest form of longing toward some object, unobstructed, becoming clear, attains the state of resolve (<s>kratu</s>).

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> 4.4.6]

children.text:
tad eṣa śloko bhavati --
tad eva saktaḥ saha karmaṇaiti liṅgaṃ mano yatra niṣaktam asya |
prāpyāntaṃ karmaṇas tasya yat kiñceha karoty ayam |
tasmāl lokāt punar aity asmai lokāya karmaṇe |
iti nu kāmayamānaḥ |
athākāmayamāno yo 'kāmo niṣkāma āptakāma ātmakāmo na tasya prāṇā utkrāmanti |
brahmaiva san brahmāpyeti || BrhUp_4,4.6 ||
children.translated_text:
Regarding this, there is this verse:
Being attached to that [object of desire], together with <s>karma</s> it goes — the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) to which the mind is attached.
Having reached the end of that <s>karma</s>, whatever [<s>karma</s>] this one performs here,
from that world he comes again to this world for [further] action.
Thus [it is for] the one who has desire.
But as for the one who is without desire — who is desireless (<s>akāma</s>), freed from desire (<s>niṣkāma</s>), whose desires have been fulfilled (<s>āptakāma</s>), whose desire is the self alone (<s>ātmakāma</s>) — his vital breaths (<s>prāṇas</s>) do not depart.
Being <s>Brahman</s> itself, he merges in <s>Brahman</s>. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.6 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.6 tattasminnartha eṣa śloko mantropi bhavati /
tadevaiti tadeva gacchati sakta āsaktastatrodbhūtābhilāṣaḥ sannityarthaḥ /
kathameti /
saha karmaṇā yatkarmaphalāsaktaḥ sannakarottena karmaṇā sahaiva tadeti tatphalameti /
kiṃ talliṅgamanaḥ /
manaḥ pradhānatvālliṅgasya mano liṅgamityucyate /
athavā liṅgayate 'vagamyate 'vagacchati yena talliṅgaṃ tanmano yatra yasminniṣaktaṃ niścayena saktamudbhūtābhilāṣamasya saṃsāriṇaḥ /
tadabhilāṣo hi tatkarma kṛtavān /
tasmāttanmano 'bhiṣaṅgavaśādevāsya tena karmaṇā tatphalaprāptiḥ /
tenaitasidvaṃ bhavati kāmo mūlaṃ saṃsārasyeti /
ata ucchinnakāmasya vidyamānānyapi karmāṇi brahmavido vandhyaprasavāni bhavanti /
"paryāptakāmasaya kṛtātmanaśca ihaiva sarve pravilītanti kāmāḥ"iti śruteḥ /
