kiñca prāpyāntaṃ karmaṇaḥ prāpya bhuktvāntamavasānaṃ tasya karmaṇaḥ phalaṃ bhuktvāntaṃ prāpya tasmāllokātpunaraityāgacchatyasmai lokāya karmaṇe 'yaṃ hi lokaḥ karmapradhānastenā'ha karmaṇa iti /
punaḥ karmakaraṇāya punaḥ karma kṛtvā phalāsaṅgavaśātpunaramuṃ lokaṃ yātītyevam /
iti nvevaṃ nu kāmayamānaḥ saṃsarati /
ya mātkāmayamāna evaivaṃ saṃsaratyatha tasmādakāmayamāno na kvacitsaṃsarati /
phalāsaktasya hi gatiruktā /
akāmasya hi kriyānupapatterakāmayamāno mucyata eva /
kathaṃ punakāmayamāno bhavati /
yo 'kāmo bhavatyasāvakāmayamānaḥ kathamakāmatetyucyate--yo niṣṭakāmo yasmānnirgatāḥ kāmāḥ so 'yaṃ niṣkāmaḥ /
kathaṃ kāmā nirgacchanti /
ya āptakāmo bhavatyāptāḥ kāmā yena sa āptakāmaḥ /
kathamāpyante kāmā ātmakāmatvena yasyā'maiva nānyaḥ kāmayitavyo vastvantarabhūtaḥ padārtho bhavati /
ātmaivānantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana ekaraso nordhva na tiryaṅnādha ātmano 'nyatkāmayitavyaṃ vastvantaram /
yasya sarvamātmaivābhūttatkena kaṃ paśyecchṛṇuyānmanvīta vijānīyādvaivaṃ vijānankaṃ kāmayeta /
jñāyamāno hyanyatvena padārthaḥ kāmayitavyo bhavati /
na cāsāvanyo brahmavida āptakāmasyāsti /
ya evā'tmakāmatayā'ptakāmaḥ sa niṣkāmo 'kāmo 'kāmayamānaśceti mucyate /
na hi yasyā'tmaiva sarvaṃ bhavati tasyānātmā kāmayitavyo 'sti /
anātmā cānyaḥ kāmayitavyaḥ sarvaṃ cā'tmaivābhūditi vipratiṣidvam /
sarvātmadarśinaḥ kāmayitavyābhāvātkarmānupapattiḥ /
ye tu pratyavāyaparihārārthaṃ karma kalpayanti brahmavido 'pi teṣāṃ sarva bhavati /
pratyavāyasya jihāsitavyasyā'tmano 'nyasyābhipretatvāt /
yena cāśanāyādyatīto nityaṃ pratyavāyasaṃbadvo vidita ātmā taṃ vayaṃ brahmavidaṃ brūmaḥ /
nityamevāśanāyādyatītamātmanaṃ paśyati /
yasmācca jihāsitavyamanyamupādeyaṃ vā yo na paśyati tasya karma na śakyata eva saṃbaddhu m /
yastvabrahmavitasya bhavatyeva pratyavāyaparihārārthaṃ karmeti na virodhaḥ /
ataḥ kāmābhāvādakāmayamāno na jāyate mucyata eva /
tasyaivamakāmayamānasya karmābhāve gamanakāraṇābhāvātprāṇā vāgādayo notkrāmanti nordhva krāmanti dehāt /
sa ca vidvānāptakāma ātmakāmatayehaiva brahmabhūtaḥ /
sarvātmano hi brahmaṇo dṛṣṭāntatvena pradarśitametadrūpaṃ tadvā asyaitadāptakāmamātmakāmamakāmaṃ rūpamiti /
tasya hi dārṣṭāntikabhūto 'yamartha upasaṃhriyate 'thākāmayamāna ityādinā /
sa kathamevaṃbhūto mucyata ityucyate-yo hi suṣuptāvasthamiva nirviśeṣamadvaitamaluptacidrūpajyotiḥ svabhāvamātmānaṃ paśyati tasyaivākāmayamānasya karmabhāve gamanakāraṇabhāvatprāṇā vāgādayo notkrāmanti /
kintu vidvānsaihaiva brahma, yadyapi dehāvāniva lakṣyate sa brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti /
yasmānna hi tasyābrahmatvaparicchedahetavaḥ kāmāḥ santi tasmādihaiva brahmaiva sanbrahmāpyeti na śarīrapātettarakālam /
na hi viduṣo mṛtasya bhāvāntarāpattirjīvato 'nyabhāvo dehāntarapratisaṃdhānābhāvamātreṇova tu brahmāpyetītyucyate /
bhāvāntarārāpattau hi mokṣasya sarvopaniṣanidvivakṣitor'tha ātmaikatvākhyaḥ sa bādhito bhavet /
karmahetukaśca mokṣaḥ prāpnoti na jñānanimitta iti /
sa cāniṣṭo 'nityatvaṃ ca mokṣasya prāpnoti /
na hi kriyānirvṛttor'tho nityo dṛṣṭaḥ /
nityaśca mokṣo 'bhyupagamyate /
"eṣa nityo mahimā"iti mantravarṇāt /
na ca svābhāvikātsvabhāvādanyannityaṃ kalpayituṃ śakyam /
svābhāvikaścedagnyudātmanaḥ svabhāvaḥ sa na śakyate puruṣavyāpārānubhāvīti vaktum /
na hyagnerauṣṇyaṃ prakāśo vāgnuvyāpārānantarānubhāvī /
agnivyāpārānubhāvī svābhāvikaśceti vipratiṣiddham /
jvalanavyāpānānubhāvitvamuṣṇaprākāśaguṇābhyāmabhivyajyate tannāgnyepekṣayā kiṃ tarhyanyadṛṣṭeragnerauṣṇyaprakāśau dharmau vyavahitai kasyaciddṛṣṭyā tvasaṃbadhyamānau jvalanāpekṣayā vyadhānāpagame dṛṣṭerabhivyajyete tadapekṣayā bhrāntirupajāyate jvalanapūrvakāvetāviṣṇaprākāśau dharmau jātāviti /
yadyuṣṇaprakāśayorapi svābhāvikatvaṃ na syāt /
yaḥ svābhāvaki'gnerdharmastamudāhariṣyāmaḥ /
na ca svābhāviko dharma eva nāsti padārthānāmiti śakyaṃ vaktum /
na ca nigaḍabhaṅga ivābhāvabhūto mokṣo bandhananivṛttirupapadyate /
paramātmaikatvābhyupagamāt 'ekamevādvitīyam'iti śruteḥ /
na cānyo baddho 'sti yasya nigaḍanivṛttivadbandhananivṛttarmokṣaḥ syāt /
paramātmavyatirekeṇānyasyābhāvaṃ vistareṇāvādiṣma /
tasmādavidyānivṛttimātre mokṣavyavahāra iti cāvocāma yathā rajjvādau sarpādyajñānanivṛttau sarpādinivṛttiḥ /
ye 'pyācakṣate mokṣe vijñānāntaramānandāntaraṃ cābhivyajyata iti sairvaktavyo 'bhivyaktiśabdārthaḥ /
yadi tāvatlaukikikyevopalabdhiviṣayavyāptirabhivyaktiśabdārthaḥ /
tato vaktavyaṃ kiṃ vidyamānamabhivyajyate 'vidyamānamiti vā /
vidyamānaṃ cedyasya muktasya tadabhivyajyate tasyā'tmabhūtameva tadityupalabdhivyavadhānānupapatternityābhivyaktatvānmuktasyābhivyajyata iti viśeṣavacanamarthakam /
atha kadācidevābhivyajyata upalabdhivyavadhānādanātmabhūtaṃ tadityanyato 'bhivyaktiprasaṅgaḥ /
tathā cābhivyaktisādhanāpekṣayā /
upalabdhisamānāśrayatve tu vyavadhānakalpanānupapatteḥ sarvadābhivyaktiprasaṅgaḥ /
tathā cābhivyaktisādhanāpekṣatā /
upalabdhisamānāśrayatve tu vyavadhānakalpanānupapatteḥ sarvadābhivyaktiranabhivyaktirvā /
natvantarālakalpanāyā pramāṇamasti /
na ca samānāśrayaṇāmekasyā'tmabhūtānāṃ dharmāṇāmitaretaraviṣayaviṣayitvaṃ saṃbhavati /
vijñānasukhayoṣca prāgabhivyakteḥ saṃsāritvamabhivyaktyuttarakālaṃ ca muktatvaṃsya so 'nyaḥ parasmānnityābhivyaktajñānasvarūpādatyantavailakṣaṇyācchaityamivauṣṇyāt /
paramātmabhedakalpanāyāñca vaidikaḥ kṛtāntaḥ parityaktaḥ syāt /
mokṣasyedānīmiva nirviśeṣatve tadarthādhikayatnānupapattiḥ śāstravaiyarthyaṃ ca prāpnotīti cenna /
na, avidyābhramāpohāpthatvāt /
na hi vastuto muktāmuktatvāviśeṣo 'sti /
ātmano nityākarūpatvāt /
kintu tadviṣayāvidyāpohyate śāstropadeśajanitavijñānena /
prāktadupadeśaprāptestadarthaśca prayatna upapadyata eva /
avidyāvato 'vidyānivṛtyanivṛttikṛto veśeṣa ātmanaḥ syāditi cet /
avidyākalpanāviṣayatvābhyupagamādrajjūṣaraśuktakāgaganānāṃ sarvodakarajatamalinatvādivadadoṣa ityavocāma /
timirātimitaradṛṣṭivadavidyākartṛtvākatṛtvākṛta ātmano viśeṣaḥ syāditi cet /
na /
dhyātīva lelāyatīveti svato 'vidyākartṛtvasva pratiṣiddhatvā /
anekavyāpārasannipātajanitatvāccāvidyābhramasya /
viṣatvopapatteṣca /
yasya cāvidyābhramo ghaṭādivadvivikto gṛhyate sa nāvidyābhramavān /
ahaṃ na jāne mugdhe 'smīti pratyatadarśanādavidyābhramavatvameveti cenna /
tasyāpi vivekagrahaṇāt /
na hi yo yasya vivekena grahītā sa tasminbhrānta ityucyate /
tasya ca vivekagrahaṇaṃ tasminneva ca bhrama iti vipratiṣiddham /
na jāne mugdho 'smīti dṛśyata iti bravīṣi taddarśinaścājñānaṃ mugdharūpatā dṛśyata iti ca taddarśanasya viṣayo bhavati karmatāmāpadyata iti tatkathaṃ karmabhūtaṃ satkartṛsvarūpadṛśiviśeṣaṇajñānamugdhate syātām /
atha dṛśiviśeṣaṇatvaṃ tayoḥ kathaṃ karma syātāṃ dṛśinā vyāpyete /
karma hi kartṛkriyayā vyāpyamānaṃ bhavati /
anyacca vyāpyamanyadvyāpakaṃ na tenaiva tadvyāpyate /
vada kathamevaṃ satyajñānamugdhate dṛśiviśeṣaṇe syātām /
na cājñānāvivekadarśyajñānamātmanaḥ karmabhūtamupalabhamāna upalabdhṛdharmatvena gṛhmāti śarīre kārśyarūpadādavattathā /
sukhaduḥkhecchāprayatnādīnsarvo loko gṛhṇātīti cet /
tathāpi grahīturlokasya vivaktataivābhyupagatā syāt /
na jāne 'haṃ tvaduktaṃ mugdha eveti cet /
bhavatvajño mugdho yastvevandarśū taṃ jñamamugdhaṃ pratijānīmahe vayam /
tathā vyosenoktam /
icchādi kṛtsnaṃ kṣetraṃ kṣetrī prakāśayatīti /
"samaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣu tiṣṭhantaṃ parameśvaram /
vinaśyatsvavinaśyantam"ityādi śataśa uktam /
tasmānnā'tmanaḥ svato baddhamuktajñānakṛto viśeṣo 'sti /
sarvadā samaikarasasvābhāvyābhyupagamāt /
children.translated_text: Because the acceptance that [the Self] is always of one uniform intrinsic nature is [established].

children.text: ye tvato 'nyathā'tmavastu parikalpya bandhamokṣādiśāstriṃ cārthavādamāpādayanti ta utsahante khe 'pi śākunaṃ padaṃ draṣṭuṃ khaṃ vā muṣṭinā'kraṣṭuṃ carmavadveṣṭitum /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But those who, conceiving the nature of the self otherwise than this, reduce the scripture on bondage, liberation, and the like to mere laudatory passages (<s>arthavāda</s>) — they venture to see a bird's footprint even in the sky, or to grasp the sky with a fist, or to roll it up like leather.

children.text: vayaṃ tu tatkartumaśaktāḥ sarvādā samaikaramasadvaitamavikriyamajamajaramamaramamṛtamabhayamātmatattvaṃ brahmaiva sma ityeṣa sarvavedāntaniścitor'tha ityevaṃ pratipadyāmahe /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But we, being unable to do such things, understand thus: 'We are indeed <s>Brahman</s> — the reality of the self that is always the same, one, without a second (<s>advaita</s>), without modification, unborn, free from old age, free from death, immortal, and fearless' — this is the conclusion established by all the <s>Vedānta</s> [texts] — thus we accept.

children.text: tasmādbrahmāpyetītyupacāramātrametadvipīratagrahavaddehasaṃtatervi cchedamātraṃ vijñānaphalamapekṣya //4,4.6//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the expression '<s>Brahman</s> reaches' is merely figurative — like [the expression about] a released planet (<s>graha</s>); it merely denotes the cessation of the continuity of bodies, in view of the fruit of knowledge. (4.4.6)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.6:] On this subject, this verse, this <s>mantra</s> too, is pertinent. 'It goes to that very [thing]' — it goes to that very [object]; the meaning is: being attached, being fixed [on an object] with longing that has arisen toward it. How does it go? Together with <s>karma</s> — being attached to the fruit of <s>karma</s>, by that very <s>karma</s> which it performed, it goes together [with it]; it goes to the fruit of that [karma]. What is the distinguishing mark (<s>liṅga</s>)? The mind. Because the mind is predominant among the distinguishing marks, the mind is called the distinguishing mark. Alternatively, that by which one indicates, comprehends, understands — that is the distinguishing mark, that is the mind — wherever it is fixed, attached with certainty, with longing that has arisen — [it is the mind] of this transmigrating being. For it was out of that longing that he performed that <s>karma</s>. Therefore, through the power of mental attachment, through that <s>karma</s>, the attainment of its fruit [occurs] for this [being]. From this it is established that desire (<s>kāma</s>) is the root of <s>saṃsāra</s>. Therefore, for one whose desires have been cut off, even the <s>karmas</s> that exist for the knower of <s>Brahman</s> become barren — like the offspring of a barren woman. As the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'For one whose desires are fulfilled, who has attained the Self — all desires dissolve right here' (MuṇḍUp 3.2.2). Furthermore, having reached the end of <s>karma</s> — having reached and experienced the end, the termination, of that <s>karma</s>'s fruit — having reached the end, from that world he returns again, he comes back to this world, for the sake of <s>karma</s>. For this world is dominated by <s>karma</s>; therefore it says 'for <s>karma</s>.' Again, for the purpose of performing <s>karma</s> — having performed <s>karma</s> again, through the power of attachment to its fruit, he goes again to that [other] world. Thus indeed, in this way, one who desires transmigrates. He who desires in this way alone transmigrates — therefore, one who does not desire does not transmigrate anywhere. For the path of one attached to fruit has been described. For one without desire, since action is not possible [without desire], one who does not desire is indeed liberated. How then does one become free from desire? He who becomes desireless — that one is free from desire. How does he become desireless? This is stated: he who is <s>niṣkāma</s> — one from whom desires have departed — he is this desireless one. How do desires depart? He who becomes <s>āptakāma</s> (one whose desires are fulfilled) — one whose desires have been attained — he is <s>āptakāma</s>. How are desires attained? Through being <s>ātmakāma</s> (one whose desire is the Self alone) — for whom the Self alone, and no other object that is a thing different [from the Self], is to be desired. The Self alone — without interior or exterior, entire, a solid mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), of one taste — [extending] not upward, not sideways, not downward — there is no object other than the Self to be desired. For one for whom everything has become the Self alone — by what and whom would he see, hear, think, or know? And knowing thus, whom would he desire? For an object that is known as other is [alone] capable of being desired. But there is nothing other [than the Self] for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>āptakāma</s>. He who, through being <s>ātmakāma</s>, is <s>āptakāma</s> — he is <s>niṣkāma</s>, desireless, free from desire — and [thus] is liberated. For one for whom everything has become the Self alone — for him there is no non-self to be desired. And [the proposition that] there is a non-self to be desired, and yet everything has become the Self alone — these are mutually contradictory. For one who sees the Self in all things, because there is nothing to be desired, action is impossible. But those who postulate <s>karma</s> even for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, for the purpose of avoiding <s>pratyavāya</s> (the sin of omission) — for them everything [follows]; for the <s>pratyavāya</s> that is to be avoided is intended as something other than the Self. But him whom we call a knower of <s>Brahman</s> — one who has transcended hunger and the like, who is perpetually free from <s>pratyavāya</s> — whose Self has been known. He perpetually sees the Self as having transcended hunger and the like. And for one who sees nothing to be avoided as other [than the Self], and nothing to be adopted — for him, <s>karma</s> simply cannot be connected [with him]. But for one who is not a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, there indeed exists <s>karma</s> for the purpose of avoiding <s>pratyavāya</s> — there is no contradiction [in that]. Therefore, because of the absence of desire, one who does not desire is not born — he is indeed liberated. For this one who does not desire, in the absence of <s>karma</s>, because of the absence of a cause for departure, the <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the rest — do not depart, do not rise upward from the body. And that wise one, the <s>āptakāma</s>, through being <s>ātmakāma</s>, is <s>Brahman</s> right here [in this very life]. For the Self of all, of <s>Brahman</s>, this form was shown as an illustration: 'This is the <s>āptakāma</s>, <s>ātmakāma</s>, desireless form.' For this illustrated counterpart (<s>dārṣṭāntika</s>) is here drawn together by [the passage beginning with] 'now, one who does not desire' and so forth. How is such a one liberated? This is stated: he who sees the Self as it is in deep sleep — undifferentiated, non-dual, whose nature is the undiminished light of consciousness — for that one alone who does not desire, in the absence of <s>karma</s>, because of the absence of a cause for departure, the <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the rest — do not depart. Rather, the wise one, right here, is <s>Brahman</s>. Although he appears to possess a body, he, being <s>Brahman</s>, attains <s>Brahman</s>. Because desires, which are the causes of delimiting [the Self] as non-<s>Brahman</s>, do not exist for him — therefore, right here, being <s>Brahman</s>, he attains <s>Brahman</s> — not [only] after the fall of the body at some future time. For the knower who has died does not undergo transformation into another state of being; the statement 'he attains <s>Brahman</s>' is made merely on account of the absence of reconnection with another body — not because of any actual other-becoming while alive. For if there were transformation into another state of being, the purpose of all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> — namely the oneness of the Self — which is the desired teaching of <s>mokṣa</s>, would be contradicted. And <s>mokṣa</s> would be caused by <s>karma</s>, not by knowledge. And that is undesirable, and the impermanence of <s>mokṣa</s> would follow. For no result produced by action has ever been seen to be permanent. But <s>mokṣa</s> is accepted as permanent — from the <s>mantra</s> text: 'This is [his] eternal greatness' (BṛUp 4.4.6). And nothing permanent can be imagined other than an intrinsic nature that is [already] one's own nature. And if the intrinsic nature of the Self is like [the heat and light] of fire, then it cannot be said to depend on human effort for its realization. For neither the heat nor the light of fire depends on human effort. [To say that it is] dependent on human effort and yet intrinsic — this is contradictory. The dependence [of fire's heat and light] on the act of ignition is [merely] made manifest by the qualities of heat and light. That [dependence] is not in relation to fire [itself]; rather, the heat and light, which are properties of fire, being obstructed from someone's vision by something intervening — when the obstruction is removed by means of ignition, [the heat and light] are made manifest. In relation to that [ignition], the misconception arises: 'These two properties, heat and light, have been produced subsequent to ignition.' But if even heat and light were not intrinsic [to fire], then we would [have to] point out what intrinsic property of fire [there is]. And it cannot be said that things have no intrinsic properties at all. Nor is <s>mokṣa</s> tenable as a mere absence [of bondage], like the breaking of fetters — a negative entity [that is merely] the cessation of bondage. Because the oneness with the supreme Self is accepted — from the <s>śruti</s>: 'One only, without a second' (ChUp 6.2.1). And there is no other bound being for whom <s>mokṣa</s> would be the cessation of bondage like the removal of fetters. We have stated at length the non-existence of any [being] other than the supreme Self. Therefore, we have also stated that <s>mokṣa</s> consists merely in the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> — just as the cessation of the [imagined] snake and the like [occurs] upon the cessation of the ignorance regarding a rope and the like. Those who say that in <s>mokṣa</s> a different consciousness and a different bliss are made manifest — they must explain what they mean by 'manifestation' (<s>abhivyakti</s>). If the meaning of 'manifestation' is merely the pervasion of the domain of worldly perception — then one must say whether what is manifested is [already] existent or non-existent. If it is existent — for the liberated one for whom it is manifested, it is his very self — since there can be no obstruction of perception [of one's own self], and since [the self] is eternally manifest for the liberated one, the specific statement 'it is manifested for the liberated one' is meaningless. But if it is manifested only sometimes — since there is obstruction of perception, it is not the self [of the liberated one] — [and then there would be] the unwanted consequence of [its] being manifested by something else. And also, because of dependence on a means of manifestation. If [bliss and consciousness] share the same locus as perception, then since the supposition of obstruction is untenable, there would be either perpetual manifestation or never manifestation. And there is no evidence for imagining an intermediate [state]. And among [entities] sharing the same locus, which are the very self [of the person], it is not possible for one to be the object and another the subject of each other. And if consciousness and bliss are in a state of <s>saṃsāra</s> before manifestation and in a state of liberation after manifestation — then [the liberated one] would be different from the supreme [Self] whose knowledge-nature is eternally manifest, being utterly dissimilar — like coldness from heat. And the imagination of difference from the supreme Self would mean the abandonment of the Vedic doctrine. [Objection:] If <s>mokṣa</s> is, as [you say,] featureless — like the present [state before liberation] — then the pursuit of extra effort for its sake would be untenable, and scripture would be purposeless. [Reply:] No — because [the effort and scripture] are for the purpose of removing the delusion of <s>avidyā</s>. For in reality there is no distinction between the liberated and the non-liberated. Because the Self is eternally of an unchanging nature. Rather, the <s>avidyā</s> pertaining to it is removed by the knowledge born of scriptural teaching. And prior to the attainment of that teaching, the effort for that purpose is entirely tenable. [Objection:] For one who possesses <s>avidyā</s>, there would be a distinction in the Self — created by the cessation or non-cessation of <s>avidyā</s>? [Reply:] Since <s>avidyā</s> is admitted to be the domain of imagination — this is no defect — as we have stated: just as the rope, conch-shell, sky, and the like [are not actually affected by] water, silver, and impurity and the like [superimposed upon them]. [Objection:] Like the distinction in vision caused by the eye-disease <s>timira</s> (cataract) versus freedom from <s>timira</s>, there would be a distinction in the Self caused by the [presence or absence of] agency of <s>avidyā</s>? [Reply:] No — because agency [of <s>avidyā</s>] is denied by 'it thinks, as it were; it moves, as it were' (BṛUp 4.3.7) [which shows that] the agency of <s>avidyā</s> is intrinsically negated. And because the delusion of <s>avidyā</s> is produced by the concurrence of multiple factors. And because it is tenable as an object [rather than a property of the Self]. And he for whom the delusion of <s>avidyā</s> is grasped as separate — like a pot [is grasped as separate from the seer] — he is not one who possesses the delusion of <s>avidyā</s>. [Objection:] But from the direct experience 'I do not know; I am confused' — the possession of the delusion of <s>avidyā</s> [is established]? [Reply:] No — because even that [confusion] is grasped discriminately [as an object]. For one who grasps something discriminately, as separate from himself, is not said to be deluded with respect to it. And [the claim that] there is discriminate grasping of it and also delusion with respect to it — these are mutually contradictory. [You say:] 'I do not know; I am confused — this is seen [in experience].' You are saying that ignorance and the state of confusion are seen for the one who sees them — and being seen, they become objects, they assume the status of objects (<s>karmatā</s>). How then can ignorance and confusion — being objects — be properties [qualifying] the seer, the subject, whose nature is seeing? And if they are properties of the seer, how can they be objects? They are pervaded by the seer. For an object is that which is pervaded by the agent's action. And what is pervaded is one thing, what pervades is another — it is not pervaded by that very [pervader]. Tell me: how, this being so, can ignorance and confusion be properties of the seer? And one who perceives ignorance and the non-discrimination of ignorance as objects — as <s>karma</s> belonging to the Self — does not [thereby] apprehend [them] as properties of the perceiver — just as in the case of leanness, physical form, and the like [which are properties] of the body. [Objection:] But all people apprehend pleasure, pain, desire, effort, and the like [as properties of the Self]? [Reply:] Even so, the distinctness of the apprehending world would be conceded. [Objection:] 'I do not know — I am confused, just as you said'? [Reply:] Let the ignorant one be confused; but him who sees thus — we declare him to be a knower, not confused. As <s>Vyāsa</s> too has said: 'The <s>kṣetrin</s> (knower of the field) illuminates desire and the entire <s>kṣetra</s> (field)' (BhG 13.6). And '<s>Sama</s> (equal) in all beings, the supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), the imperishable within the perishable' (BhG 13.27) — and so on, has been stated hundreds of times. Therefore, there is no distinction in the Self itself, created by the knowledge or ignorance of the bound and liberated states.

children.text:
tad eṣa śloko bhavati --
yadā sarve pramucyante kāmā ye 'sya hṛdi śritāḥ |
atha martyo 'mṛto bhavaty atra brahma samaśnuta iti |
tad yathāhinirlvayanī valmīke mṛtā pratyastā śayīta |
evam evedaṃ śarīraṃ śete |
athāyam aśarīro 'mṛtaḥ prāṇo brahmaiva teja eva |
so 'haṃ bhagavate sahasraṃ dadāmīti hovāca janako vaidehaḥ || BrhUp_4,4.7 ||
children.translated_text: Regarding this, there is this verse: 'When all desires that dwell in the heart are released, then the mortal becomes immortal — here one attains <s>Brahman</s>.' Just as the slough of a snake lies dead and cast off on an anthill, even so does this body lie. Then this one — bodiless, immortal — is <s>prāṇa</s> (life itself), <s>Brahman</s> indeed, light indeed. 'I, sir, give your honor a thousand [cows]' — thus said <s>Janaka</s>, [king] of <s>Videha</s>. (BṛUp 4.4.7)

ato na sarvameva nivedayati /
śrutvābhipretaṃ yājñavalkyātpunarante nivedayiṣyāmīti hi manyate /

arthaśeṣopapatteśca /

nanvevaṃ satyata ūrdhvaṃ vimokṣāyaiveti vaktavyam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] If this is so, then [<s>Janaka</s>] should say: 'From here onward, please speak only for liberation.'

children.text: naiṣa dauṣaḥ ātmajñānavadaprayojakaḥ saṃnyāsaḥ pakṣe pratipattikarmavaditi hi manyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This is no fault — for he thinks that <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, like self-knowledge, is not efficacious on its own [as a separate means of liberation] — in the alternative view, [he considers it] like rites of attainment (<s>pratipatti-karma</s>).

children.text: "saṃnyāsena tanuṃ tyajet"iti smṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the <s>smṛti</s>: 'Through <s>saṃnyāsa</s> one should abandon the body' (ManuSm).

children.text: sādhutvāpakṣe 'pi nāta ūrdhvaṃ vimokṣāyaiveti praśnamarhati mokṣasādhanabhūtātmajñānaparipākārthatvāt //4,4.7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Even if [<s>saṃnyāsa</s>] is regarded as beneficial [but not independently efficacious], he does not deserve to ask 'From here onward, please speak only for liberation' — because it serves the purpose of bringing self-knowledge to maturity. (4.4.7)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.7:] The <s>saṃsāra</s> that is the illustrated counterpart of the illustration of traversal between dream and waking has been described. The cause of <s>saṃsāra</s> too — the prior cognition (<s>pūrvaprajñā</s>) consisting of <s>vidyā</s> and <s>karma</s> — has been described. And the effects and instruments that constitute the limiting adjuncts through which [the self] experiences the condition of being a <s>saṃsārin</s> — those too have been stated. Of these, having made a prima facie case (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>) that <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are the direct impellers, it was determined that desire alone [is the cause]. And just as this meaning was determined by the prose (<s>brāhmaṇa</s>), so too by a verse (<s>mantra</s>) — having stated bondage and the cause of bondage, the section was concluded with 'thus [it is for] the one who does not desire.' Then, beginning with 'but the one who is without desire,' <s>mokṣa</s> was stated as the illustrated counterpart of the illustration of deep sleep — the state of being the self of all (<s>sarvātmabhāva</s>). And the cause of <s>mokṣa</s> was stated: the condition of being one whose desires are fulfilled (<s>āptakāmatva</s>) through being one whose desire is the self (<s>ātmakāmatā</s>). And since, by virtue of its purport, the condition of being one whose desires are fulfilled through desiring the self is impossible without knowledge of the self — by this purport, <s>Brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>) alone has been stated as the cause of <s>mokṣa</s>. Therefore, even though desire was stated as the root, nevertheless, by the converse of the cause of <s>mokṣa</s>, <s>avidyā</s> as the cause of bondage has also been stated. Here too, <s>mokṣa</s> and the means of <s>mokṣa</s> have been stated by the prose. For the purpose of confirming that very [teaching], a verse (<s>mantra</s>) — designated by the word '<s>śloka</s>' — is cited: 'that' — on that very topic — 'this verse is.' When (<s>yadā</s>) — at whatever time — all (<s>sarve</s>) — all the desires, the various forms of craving — are released (<s>pramucyante</s>). By one who has knowledge of the self and desires the self, they are uprooted and destroyed. Those which are well-known in the world, directed toward the objects of this world and the next — characterized by the longing for sons, wealth, and worlds — belonging to this well-known person — dwelling in the heart, in the intellect, lodged [there] — then (<s>atha tadā</s>) the mortal, the one subject to the law of death — through the separation from desire, from its very root — becomes immortal. Here — in this very body while still living — one attains <s>Brahman</s>, reaches the state of <s>Brahman</s>, attains <s>mokṣa</s> — this is the meaning. Therefore, <s>mokṣa</s> does not require going to another place or the like. Therefore, for the knower, the <s>prāṇas</s> do not depart — they are dissolved right where they stand, in their own cause, in the <s>puruṣa</s>. For it was said: 'Only a name remains' (BṛUp 3.2.12). But how is it that, when the <s>prāṇas</s> are dissolved and the body too has merged into its cause, the knower who is liberated here — being the self of all — while still continuing, does not again, as before, attain embodiment characterized by <s>saṃsāra</s>? To this it is said: there — in that regard — this illustration: just as in the world, a snake (<s>ahi</s>) — its <s>nirvayanī</s> (slough), its shed skin — the snake's slough — on an anthill, the dwelling of snakes, and such places — this is the meaning. Dead, cast off — thrown away with the sense of 'this is not me' by the snake — it lies. Even so — as is this illustration — this body, cast off by the liberated one — who is in the position of the snake — with the sense of 'this is not me,' lies dead, as it were. Then — the other one, who is in the position of the snake — the liberated one, being the self of all, even though continuing right there, is bodiless — like the snake [continuing without its slough]. He does not again, as before, become embodied. For previously he was embodied and mortal through the sense of 'I am the body' impelled by desire and <s>karma</s>. Having separated from that — now, therefore — bodiless, and for that very reason immortal. '<s>Prāṇa</s>' — because it is the life of all (<s>prāṇiti</s>), it is called <s>prāṇa</s>. For the upcoming verse says: 'the <s>prāṇa</s> of <s>prāṇa</s>' (BṛUp 4.4.18). And another <s>śruti</s>: 'Mind is the bond of <s>prāṇa</s>' (ChUp 6.8.2). From the force of the context and the purport of the sentences, it is the supreme self alone that is denoted here by the word '<s>prāṇa</s>.' <s>Brahman</s> indeed — the supreme self indeed. What further? Light (<s>tejas</s>) indeed — consciousness, the luminosity by which [the self] is self-luminous and by which the world is illuminated. [The self] stands as endowed with the light of consciousness, as the guide of cognition, never departing [from its nature].
The question about desire, whose purpose was <s>vimokṣa</s> (liberation), and the boon granted by <s>Yājñavalkya</s> to <s>Janaka</s> — [describing] bondage and <s>mokṣa</s> together with their causes, in the form of the illustrated counterpart — all this has been conclusively determined, in full detail, by the <s>śruti</s> taking the form of the narrative of <s>Janaka</s> and <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. The means of liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> has been taught to living beings. Now the <s>śruti</s> itself states that it was said by <s>Janaka</s> as follows — for the purpose of discharging [the debt of] gratitude for the knowledge. How? 'I' — thus instructed, thus liberated by you — sir, to the venerable one — 'I give a thousand as the fee for this knowledge' — thus (<s>ha</s>) indeed (<s>kila</s>) spoke, said <s>Janaka</s>, [king] of <s>Videha</s>.
Here [one may ask]: when the entire meaning of <s>vimokṣa</s> has been determined, why does he not offer up the kingdom of <s>Videha</s> and his own self, but gives only a thousand — as in the earlier occasions when only a part [of the teaching] was given? What is the intention behind this? Some explain this [as follows]: <s>Janaka</s>, being devoted to the knowledge of the self, wishes to hear again through verses what has already been heard as meaning. Therefore he does not offer everything. He thinks: 'Having heard what is intended from <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, I shall offer everything at the end.' And [he thinks:] 'If I offer everything right here, this one [<s>Yājñavalkya</s>], his desire being satisfied, will not recite the verses regarding [this topic]' — and out of fear of this, the gift of a thousand serves to indicate his continued desire to hear. All of this is incorrect — because it is unfitting to attribute deceitful intention to the <s>śruti</s>, which has the status of a means of valid knowledge, just as to a person. And because a subsidiary purpose is possible: even though the meaning of <s>vimokṣa</s> has been stated, there remains a subsidiary topic to be stated — namely the renunciation of all desires (<s>sarveṣaṇāparityāga</s>), called <s>saṃnyāsa</s>, which is the means of self-knowledge and forms the complement of self-knowledge. Therefore, the supposition that [<s>Janaka</s> gave only a thousand because he wished] merely to hear the verses is not straightforward. For the supposition that a previously stated meaning is being repeated is a last resort when no other interpretation is possible. And that [supposition] is unfitting when another interpretation is possible. Nor did we say that it is merely praise [of the previously stated teaching].

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.8]

children.text:
tad ete ślokā bhavanti --
aṇuḥ panthā vitataḥ purāṇo māṃ spṛṣṭo 'nuvitto mayaiva |
tena dhīrā apiyanti brahmavidaḥ svargaṃ lokam ita ūrdhvaṃ vimuktāḥ || BrhUp_4,4.8 ||
children.translated_text: Regarding this, there are these verses: Subtle is this path, extended, ancient — it has touched me, it has been found by me. By it the wise, the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, go upward from here to the heavenly world, [being already] liberated. (BṛUp 4.4.8)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.8 ātmakāmasya brahmavido mokṣa ityetasminnarthe mantrabrahmaṇokte vistarapratipādakā ete ślokā bhavanāti /
aṇuḥ sūkṣmaḥ panthā durvijñeyatvādvitato vistīrṇo vispaṣṭataraṇahetutvādvā vitara iti pāṭhāntarānmokṣasādhano jñānamārgaḥ purāṇaścirantano nityaśrutiprakāśitatvānna tārkikabuddhiprabhavakudṛṣṭimārgavadarvākkāliko mā spṛṣṭo mayā labdha ityarthaḥ /
yo hi yena labhyate sa taṃ spṛśatīva saṃbadhyate tenāyaḥ brahmavidyālakṣaṇo mokṣamārgo mayā labdhatvānmā spṛṣṭa ityucyate /
na kevalaṃ mayā labdhaḥ kintvanuvitto mayaiva /
anuvedanaṃ nāma vidyāyāḥ paripākāpekṣayā phalāvasānatāniṣṭhā prāptiḥ /
bhujeriva tṛptyavasānatā /
pūrvaṃ tu jñānaprāptisaṃbandhamātrameveti viśeṣaḥ /
kimasāvena mantradṛgeko brahmavidyāphalaṃ prāpto nānyaḥ prāptavānyenānuvitto mayāvetyavadhārayati /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
asyāḥ phalamātmasākṣikamanuttamamiti brahmavidyāyāḥ stutiparatvāt /
evaṃ hi kṛtārthātmābhimānakaramātmapratyayasākṣikamātmajñānaṃ kimataḥ paramanyatsyāditi brahmavidyā stauti /
na tu puranyo brahmavittatphalaṃ na prāpnotīti /
"tadyo yo devānām"iti sarvārthaśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'whoever among the gods [awakened to this, became <s>Brahman</s>]' (BṛUp 1.4.10) — which teaches that all [who know attain the same result].

children.text: tadevā'ha-tena brahmavidyāmārgeṇa dhīrāḥ prajñāvanto 'nye 'pi brahmavida ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This very thing is stated: by that path of <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, the wise (<s>dhīrāḥ</s>), those endowed with discernment — others too who are knowers of <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: apiyantpigacchanti brahmavidyāphalaṃ mokṣaṃ svargaṃ lokam svargalokaśabdaviṣṭapavācyamapi sanniha prakaraṇānmokṣābhidhāyakaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] They go (<s>apiyanti</s>) — they attain <s>mokṣa</s>, the fruit of <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. The heavenly world (<s>svargaṃ lokam</s>) — though the word '<s>svarga</s>' can denote a celestial abode, here, due to the context, it designates <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text: ito 'smāccharīrapātādūrdhvaṃ jīvanta eva vimuktāḥ santaḥ //4,4.8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From here — from the fall of this body — upward, having been liberated while still living. (4.4.8)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.8:] On this very topic — that <s>mokṣa</s> belongs to the knower of <s>Brahman</s> who desires the self — since this has been stated by both the prose (<s>brāhmaṇa</s>) and the verse (<s>mantra</s>), these verses (<s>ślokas</s>) serve to expound it in detail. Subtle (<s>aṇu</s>) — fine, because it is difficult to know. Extended (<s>vitata</s>) — widespread, because it is the cause of the clearest [realization]; or according to the variant reading '<s>vitara</s>' [meaning 'more extensive']. [This is] the path of knowledge leading to <s>mokṣa</s>. Ancient (<s>purāṇa</s>) — of great antiquity, because it is always illuminated by the eternal <s>śruti</s> — not of recent origin like the path of false views produced by the intellect of logicians. 'It has touched me' (<s>mā spṛṣṭaḥ</s>) — 'it has been attained by me' — this is the meaning. For he who is attained by something has, as it were, been touched by it, comes into contact with it. Therefore, this path of <s>mokṣa</s> characterized by <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, having been attained by me, is said to have 'touched me.' Not only has it been attained by me, but it has been found, fully realized, by me indeed. '<s>Anuvedana</s>' (full realization) means — with reference to the maturation of knowledge — the culmination of fruition, the attainment of the final result. Like the culmination in satisfaction that comes from eating. The first [stage], however, was merely the initial contact with knowledge — this is the distinction. [Objection:] Is this seer of the verse alone the one who has attained the fruit of <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, and has no one else attained it — [since he says] 'found by me'? This is no fault — because the statement is intended to praise <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, [declaring that] its fruit is witnessed by the self alone and is unsurpassed. For thus, with the sense of one who has accomplished his purpose, with self-knowledge witnessed by the self alone — 'what could be higher than this?' — he praises <s>Brahmavidyā</s>. But it is not that no one else, being a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, attains its fruit.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.9
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.9]

children.text:
tasmiñ śuklam uta nīlam āhuḥ piṅgalaṃ haritaṃ lohitaṃ ca |
eṣa panthā brahmaṇā hānuvittas tenaiti brahmavit puṇyakṛt taijasaś ca || BrhUp_4,4.9 ||
children.translated_text: In it, they say, there is white, and blue, and tawny, and green, and red. This path was found by <s>Brahman</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). By it goes the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the doer of merit, and the luminous one. (BṛUp 4.4.9)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.9 tasminmokṣasādhanamārge vipratipattirmumukṣūṇām /
katham /
tasmiñśuklaṃ śuddhaṃ vimalamāhuḥ kecinmumukṣavo nīlamanye piṅgalamanye haritaṃ lohitaṃ ca yathādarśanam /
nāḍhyastvetāḥ suṣumnādyāḥ śleṣmādirasaṃsaṃpūrṇāḥ śuklasya nīlasya piṅgalasyetyādyuktatvāt /
ādityaṃ vā mokṣamārgamevaṃvidhaṃ manyante /
"eṣa śukla eṣa nīlaḥ"ityādiśrutyantārāt /
darśanamārgasya śuklādivarṇāsaṃbhavāt /
sarvathāpi tu prakṛtādbrahmavidyāmārgādanya ete śuklādayaḥ /
nanu śuklaḥ śuddho 'dhvataiyamārgaḥ /
naḥ nīlapūtādiśabdairvarṇavācakaiḥ sahānudravaṇāt /
yāñśuklādīnyogino mokṣapathānāhurna te mokṣamārgāḥ saṃsāraviṣayā ve hi te /
cakṣuṣo vā mūrdhno vānyebhyo vā śarīradeśebhya iti śarīdeśānniḥsaraṇasaṃbandhāt /
brahmādilokaprāpakāhi te /
tasmādayameva mokṣamārgo ya ātkāmatvenā'ptakāmatayā sarvakāmakṣe gamanānupapattau pradīpanirvāṇavaccakṣurādīnāṃ kāryakaraṇānāmatraiva samavanaya ityeṣa jñānamārgaḥ panthā brahmaṇā paramātmasvarūpeṇaiva brāhmaṇena tyaktasarvaiśaṇenanānuvittaḥ /
tena brahmavidyāmārgeṇa brahmavidanyo 'pyeti /
kīdṛśo brahmavittenaitītyucyate-pūrvaṃ puṇyakṛdbhūtvā punastyaktuputrādyeṣaṇaḥ parātmatejasyātmānaṃ saṃyojya tasminnabhinirvṛttastaijamasaścā'tmabhūta ihaivetyarthaḥ /
īdṛśo brahmavittena mārgeṇaiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Such a knower of <s>Brahman</s> goes by that path.

children.text: na punaḥ puṇyādisamuccayakāriṇo grahaṇaṃ virodhādityavocāma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] But [our] position, as we have already stated, is that the acceptance of one who combines merit and the like [with knowledge] is [ruled out] because of contradiction.

children.text: "apuṇyapuṇyoparame yaṃ punarbhavanirbhāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [As the <s>smṛti</s> says:] 'When both merit and demerit have ceased, those who are free from rebirth,

children.text: śāntāḥ saṃnyāsino yānti tasmai mokṣātmane namaḥ //
children.translated_text: peaceful, and renunciants — they go to that [state] whose nature is <s>mokṣa</s>. Salutation to that!

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.9:] Regarding that path leading to <s>mokṣa</s>, there is a divergence of opinion among seekers of liberation. How? In that [path], some seekers of liberation say there is white — pure, spotless. Others [say] blue; others tawny; others green and red — according to their respective views. However, these [colors refer to] the <s>nāḍīs</s> such as <s>suṣumnā</s> and others, filled with the essences of phlegm and the like — because it was stated that they are 'of white, blue, tawny' colors and so forth. Or they consider the sun, which is of such a description, to be the path of <s>mokṣa</s> — because of the other <s>śruti</s>: 'This is white, this is blue' and so forth (ChUp 8.6.1). Because the attribution of colors such as white to the path of contemplation is impossible. In any case, however, these [paths of] white and the like are different from the path of <s>Brahmavidyā</s> that is the topic at hand. [Objection:] But the white, pure path is indeed this very path [of knowledge]! [Reply:] No — because it runs together with the words 'blue' and so forth, which denote colors. The paths that the yogins declare as paths of <s>mokṣa</s> characterized by white and other [colors] — those are not paths of <s>mokṣa</s>; they pertain to the domain of <s>saṃsāra</s>. For they are connected with departing from specific locations of the body — from the eye, or from the crown of the head, or from other parts of the body. For they lead to the worlds of <s>Brahmā</s> and the like. Therefore, this alone is the path of <s>mokṣa</s>: that through being one whose desire is the self (<s>ātmakāmatva</s>), through being one whose desires are fulfilled (<s>āptakāmatva</s>), upon the cessation of all desires — when going [anywhere] is impossible — the effects and instruments such as the eyes and the like are dissolved right here, like the extinguishing of a lamp — this is the path of knowledge. This path was found by <s>Brahman</s> — by the supreme self in its own nature, by [one who is] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, one who has renounced all desires. By that path of <s>Brahmavidyā</s>, another knower of <s>Brahman</s> too goes. What kind of knower of <s>Brahman</s> goes by this? It is said: one who was previously a doer of merit (<s>puṇyakṛt</s>), and then, having renounced the desire for sons and the rest, having united the self with the light of the supreme self, having become established in that — the luminous one (<s>taijasa</s>), one who has become the self — he goes, right here — this is the meaning.

children.text: iti ca smṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus [says] the <s>smṛti</s>.

children.text: tyaja dharmamadhramaṃ ca"ityādipuṇyāpuṇyatyāgopadeśāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And because of the teaching to abandon both merit and demerit [in the instruction:] 'Abandon <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> [alike]' and so forth.

children.text: "nirāśiṣamanārambhaṃ nirnamaskāramastutum /
children.translated_text: "Free from desires, free from undertakings, free from salutations, free from praise,

children.text: akṣoṇaṃ kṣīṇakarmāṇaṃ taṃ devā brāhmaṇaṃ viduḥ" //
children.translated_text: Undiminished, with <s>karma</s> (actions) exhausted — him the <s>devas</s> (gods) know as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (knower of Brahman)."

children.text: "naitādṛśaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti vittaṃ yathaikatā samatā satyatā ca /
children.translated_text: "There is no wealth for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> such as this: oneness, equanimity, and truthfulness,

children.text: śīlaṃ sthitirdaṇḍanidhānamārjavaṃ tatastataśtoparamaḥ kriyābhyaḥ" //
children.translated_text: Good conduct, steadfastness, laying down the rod, straightforwardness, and then gradually, cessation from all ritual actions."

children.text: ityādismṛtibhyaśca /
upadekṣyati cehāpi tu"eṣa nityo mahimā brahmaṇasya na vardhate karmaṇā no kanīyān"iti karmaprayojanābhāve hetumuktavā"tasmādevavicchānto dānta"ityādinā sarvakriyoparamam /
children.translated_text: And here too [the Upaniṣad] will teach: "This is the eternal greatness of <s>Brahman</s> — it is not increased by <s>karma</s> (action), nor made less" — having stated the reason for the absence of purpose in action, [it teaches] the cessation of all activities through the passage beginning with "therefore, indeed, the one who is tranquil, self-controlled."

children.text: tasmādyathāvyākhyātameva puṇyakṛtvam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the meaning of 'one of meritorious deeds' is exactly as explained.

children.text: athavā yo brahmavittenaiti sa puṇyakṛtaijasaśceti brahmavitsutireṣā /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, 'he who knows <s>Brahman</s> goes by this [path]' — 'he is one of meritorious deeds and radiant' — this is the praise of the knower of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: puṇyakṛti taijase ca yogini mahābhāgyaṃ prasiddhaṃ loke tābhyāmato brahmavitsatūyate prakhyātamahābhāgyatvālloke //4,4.9//
children.translated_text: The great fortune of one who performs meritorious deeds and of a radiant <s>yogin</s> is well known in the world; by comparison with these two, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> is praised, because his great fortune is renowned in the world. [4.4.9]
This is established from these and other <s>smṛti</s> (traditional scripture) passages as well.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.10]

children.text:
andhaṃ tamaḥ praviśanti ye 'vidyām upāsate |
tato bhūya iva te tamo ya u vidyāyāṃ ratāḥ || BrhUp_4,4.10 ||
children.translated_text: Into blind darkness enter those who worship <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance); into still greater darkness, as it were, enter those who delight in <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) alone. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.10]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.10 andhamadarśanātmakaṃ tamaḥ saṃsāraniyāmakaṃ praviśanti pratipadyante /
ke /
ye 'vidyāṃ vidyāto 'nyāṃ sādhyasādhanalakṣaṇamupāsate karmānuvartanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who worship <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — that which is other than <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), characterized by means and ends — meaning, those who follow <s>karma</s> (ritual action).

children.text: tatastasmādapi bhūya iva bahutaramiva tamaḥ praviśanti /
children.translated_text: They enter into darkness even greater, as it were, even more abundant than that.

children.text: ke /
children.translated_text: Who?

children.text: ya u vidyāyāmavidyāvastupratipādikāyāṃ karmārthāyāṃ trayyāmeva vidyāyāṃ ratā abhiratāḥ vidhipratiṣedhapara eva vedo nānyo 'stītyupaniṣadarthānapekṣiṇa ityarthaḥ //4,4.10//
children.translated_text: Those who delight in <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) alone — that is, in the threefold <s>Veda</s> which deals with objects of <s>avidyā</s> and serves the purpose of <s>karma</s> — those who are devoted exclusively to injunctions and prohibitions, holding that 'there is no Veda other than this,' disregarding the meaning of the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. [4.4.10]
[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.10:] They enter — that is, they attain — blind, that is, of the nature of non-seeing, darkness that governs <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth). Who?

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.11
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.11]

children.text:
anandā nāma te lokā andhena tamasāvṛtāḥ |
tāṃs te pretyābhigacchaty avidvāṃso 'budhā janāḥ || BrhUp_4,4.11 ||
children.translated_text: Joyless indeed are those worlds, enveloped in blind darkness; to them, after death, go those people who are ignorant and unenlightened. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.11]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.11 yadi te 'darśanalakṣaṇaṃ tamaḥ pravisanti ko doṣa ityucyate-anandā anānandā asukhā nāma te lokāstenāndhenādarśanalakṣaṇena tamasā'vṛtā vyāptāste tasyājñānatamaso gocarāstāṃste pretya mṛtvābhigacchantyabhiyānti /
ke /
ye 'vidvāṃsaḥ /
kiṃ sāmānyenāvidvattāmātreṇa netyucyate-abudhaḥ /
budheravagamanārthasya dhātoḥ kvippratyayāntasya rūpam /
children.translated_text: '<s>Abudha</s>' is the form of the root '<s>budh</s>' (to know) with the <s>kvip</s> suffix, having the meaning of understanding.

children.text: ātmāvagamavarjitā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The meaning is: those devoid of self-knowledge.

children.text: janāḥ prakṛtā eva /
children.translated_text: '<s>Janāḥ</s>' (people) means the very same ones under discussion,

children.text: jananadharmiṇo vetyetat //4,4.11//
children.translated_text: Or it means those subject to the law of birth. [4.4.11]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.11:] If they enter darkness characterized by non-seeing, what is the fault? It is said — those worlds are <s>anandā</s> (joyless), devoid of joy, enveloped in that blind darkness;

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.12
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.12]

children.text:
ātmānaṃ ced vijānīyād ayam asmīti puruṣaḥ |
kim icchan kasya kāmāya śarīram anu saṃjvaret || BrhUp_4,4.12 ||
children.translated_text: If a person were to know the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as 'I am this,' then desiring what, for whose sake, would he suffer along with the body? [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.12]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.12 ātmānaṃ svaṃ paraṃ rūpaṃ sarvaprāṇimanīṣitajñaṃ hṛtsthamaśanāyādidharmātītaṃ codyadi vijānīyātsahasreṣu kaścit /
cedityātmavidyāyā durlabhatvaṃ darśayati /
kathamayaṃ para ātmā sarvaprāṇipratyayasākṣī yo neti netītyādyukto yasmānnānyo 'sti draṣṭā śrotā mantā vijñātā samaḥ sarvabhūtastho nityaśuddhabuddhamuktasvabhāvo 'smi bhavāmīti pūruṣaḥ puruṣaḥ /
sa kimicchaṃstatsavarūpavyatiriktamanyadastu phalabhūtaṃ kimicchankasya vānyasyā'tmano vyatiriktasya kāmāya prayojanāya /
na hi tasyā'tmana eṣṭavyaṃ phalam /
na cātmano 'nyosti yasya kāmāyecchati sarvasyātmabhūtatvāt /
ataḥ kimicchankasya kāmāya śarīramanusaṃjvaredbhraṃśet /
śarīropādhikṛtaduḥkhamanuduḥkhī syāt /
children.translated_text: He would suffer along with the body — that is, he would experience the suffering conditioned by the body.

children.text: śarīratāpamanutapyeta /
children.translated_text: He would burn along with the body's afflictions.

children.text: anātmadarśino hi tadvyatiriktavastavantarepsoḥ mamedaṃ syātputrasyedaṃ bhāryāyā idamityevamīhamānaḥ punaḥ punarjananamaraṇaprabandharūḍhaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who does not see the <s>Ātman</s>, desiring real objects different from it, striving thus — 'may this be mine, may this be my son's, may this be my wife's' — he undergoes birth and death again and again.

children.text: śarīrarogamanu rujyate sarvātmadarśinastu tadasaṃbhava ityetadāha //4,4.12//
children.translated_text: He is afflicted along with the body's disease. But for the seer of the <s>Ātman</s> in all, this is impossible — this is what is stated. [4.4.12]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.12:] If one were to know one's own supreme nature — the <s>Ātman</s> who knows the thoughts of all beings, who dwells in the heart, who transcends attributes such as hunger — among thousands,

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.13]

children.text:
yasyānuvittaḥ pratibuddha ātmāsmin saṃdehye gahane praviṣṭaḥ |
sa viśvakṛt sa hi sarvasya kartā tasya lokaḥ sa u loka eva || BrhUp_4,4.13 ||
children.translated_text: He whose <s>Ātman</s> (Self) has been found and awakened, having entered this perilous, impenetrable [body] — he is the maker of everything, for he is the creator of all; his is the world, indeed he is the world itself. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.13]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.13 kiñca yasya brāhmaṇasyānuvitto 'nulabdhaḥ pratibuddhaḥsākṣātkṛtaḥ katham? ahamasmi paraṃ brahmetyevaṃ pratyagātmatvenāvagata ātmā asminsaṃdahye saṃdehe 'nekānarthasaṃkaṭopacaye gahane viṣame 'nekaśatasahasravivekavijñānapratipakṣe viṣame praviṣṭaḥ sa yasya brāhmaṇasyānuvittaḥ pratibodhenetyarthaḥ /
sa viśvakṛdviśvasya kartā /
kathaṃ viśvakṛttavaṃ tasya? kiṃ viśvakṛditi nāmetyāśaṅkyā'ha - sa hi yasmātsarvasya kartā na nāmamātraṃ na kevalaṃ viśvakṛtparaprayuktaḥ san /
kiṃ tarhi tasya lokaḥ sarvaḥ /
kimanyā loko 'nyo 'sāvityucyate - sa u loka eva /
lokaśabdenā'tmocyate /
tasya sarva ātmā sa ca sarvasyā /
ña'tmetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: the meaning is 'the Self.'

children.text: ya eṣa brāhmaṇena pratyagātmā pratibuddhatayānuvitta ātmānarthasaṃkaṭe gahane praviṣṭaḥ sa na saṃsārī kintu para eva /
children.translated_text: This <s>Ātman</s>, the inner Self, who has been found by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> as awakened, having entered into the perilous, impenetrable [body] — he is not a <s>saṃsārin</s> (transmigrating being), but indeed the Supreme itself.

children.text: yasmādviśvasya kartā sarvasyā'tmā tasya ca sarva ātmā /
children.translated_text: Because he is the creator of the universe, the Self of all, and the Self of that [universe] is the Self of all —

children.text: eka evādvitīyaḥ para evāsmītyanusaṃdhātavya iti ślokārthaḥ //4,4.13//
children.translated_text: One alone, without a second — one should reflect 'I am indeed the Supreme.' This is the meaning of the verse. [4.4.13]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.13:] Moreover, for that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose <s>Ātman</s> has been found, that is, attained, and awakened, that is, directly realized — how? Through the realization 'I am the supreme <s>Brahman</s>,' thus

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.14
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.14]

children.text:
ihaiva santo 'tha vidmas tad vayaṃ na ced avedir mahatī vinaṣṭiḥ |
ye tad vidur amṛtās te bhavanty athetare duḥkham evāpiyanti || BrhUp_4,4.14 ||
children.translated_text: While still here [in this life], we have come to know that. If we had not known, great destruction [would follow]. Those who know that become immortal; but the others attain nothing but suffering. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.14]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.14 kiñcehaivālekārthasaṃkule santo bhavantojñānadīrghanidrāmohitāḥ santaḥ kathañcidiva brahmatattvamātmatvenātha vidmo vijānīmaḥ /
tadetadbrahma prakṛtamaho vayaṃ kṛtārthā ityabhiprāyaḥ /
yadetadbrahma vijānīmastanna cedviditavanto vayaṃ vedanaṃ vedo vedo 'syāstīti vedī vedyeva vedirna vediravediḥ /
tato 'hamavediḥ syām /
yadyavediḥ syāṃ ko doṣaḥ syānmahatyanantaparimāṇā janmamaraṇādilakṣaṇā vinaṣṭirvinaśanam /
aho vayamasmānmahato vinaśanānnirmuktā yadadvayaṃ brahma viditavanta ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alas, we are freed from this great destruction, having known that non-dual <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: yathā ca vayaṃ brahma viditvāsmādvinaśanādvipramuktā evaṃye tadviduramṛtāste bhavanti ye punarnaiva brahma vidusta itare brahmavidbhyo 'nye 'brahmavida ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: And just as we, having known <s>Brahman</s>, are freed from this destruction, so those who know that become immortal; but those who do not know <s>Brahman</s> — those others —

children.text: duḥkhameva janmamaraṇādilakṣaṇamevāpiyanti pratipadyante na kadācidapyaviduṣāṃ tato vinivṛttirityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: They attain, they reach nothing but suffering characterized by birth, death, and the like; there is never any release from that for the ignorant — this is the meaning.

children.text: duḥkhameva hi ta ātmatvenopagacchanti //4,4.14//
children.translated_text: For they accept suffering itself as their very Self. [4.4.14]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.14:] Moreover, while still here in this world crowded with manifold purposes, being alive though bewildered by the long sleep of ignorance, somehow, as it were, we have come to know <s>Brahman</s> as the Self —

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.15
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.15]

children.text:
yadaitam anupaśyaty atmānaṃ devam aṅjasā |
īśānaṃ bhūtabhavyasya na tato vijugupsate || BrhUp_4,4.15 ||
children.translated_text: When one directly sees this <s>Ātman</s> (Self) as God, the Lord of past and future, one does not shrink from it. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.15]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.15 yadā punaretamātmānaṃ kathañcitparamakāruṇikaṃ kañcidācāryaṃ prāpya tato labdhaprayādaḥ sannanu paścātpaśyati sākṣātkaroti svamātmānaṃ devaṃ dyotanavantaṃ dātāraṃ vā sarvaprāṇikarmaphalānāṃ yathākarmānurūpamañjasā sākṣādīśānaṃ sāvāminaṃ bhūtabhavyasya kālatrayasyetyetat /
na tatastasmādīśānāddevādātmānaṃ viśeṣeṇa jugupsate gopāyitumicchati /
sarvo hi leka īśvarādguptamicchati bhederśī /
ayaṃ tvekatvadarśī na bibheti kutaścana /
children.translated_text: This seer of oneness does not fear from anything.

children.text: ato na tadā vijugupsate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, he does not then shrink away.

children.text: yadeśānaṃ devamañjasā'tmatvena paśyati na tadā nindati vā kiñcit /
children.translated_text: When one directly sees <s>Īśāna</s> (the Lord), the <s>deva</s> (shining one), as one's own Self, one does not then condemn anything,

children.text: sarvamātmānaṃ hi paśyati sa evaṃpaśyankamasau nindyāt //4,4.15//
children.translated_text: For he sees everything as the Self. Seeing thus, whom would he condemn? [4.4.15]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.15:] But when, somehow obtaining a supremely compassionate teacher and thereby gaining the means, one afterwards, step by step, directly perceives this <s>Ātman</s> —

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.16
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.16]

children.text:
yasmād arvāk saṃvatsaro 'hobhiḥ parivartate |
tad devā jyotiṣāṃ jyotir āyur hopāsate 'mṛtam || BrhUp_4,4.16 ||
children.translated_text: Below which the year revolves with its days — that, the gods worship as the light of lights, as life, as immortality. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.16]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,4.16 kiñca yasmādīśānādarvāgyasmādanyaviṣaya evetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.16:] Moreover, below which <s>Īśāna</s> (Lord) — meaning, within the domain of something other than Him —

children.text: saṃvatsaraḥ kālātmā sarvasya janimataḥ paricchettā yamaparicchindannarvāgeva vartate 'hobhiḥ svāvayavairahorātrairityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The year, the time-self, the measurer of everything that is born — revolving below Him, with its constituent days and nights — this is the meaning.

children.text: tajjyotiṣāṃ jyotirādityādijyotiṣāmapyavabhāsakatvādāyurityupāsane tasmādāyuṣmantaste /
children.translated_text: That light of lights — being the illuminator even of the lights such as the sun — is worshipped as <s>āyus</s> (life); therefore they become long-lived through that worship.

children.text: tasmādāyuṣkāmenā'yurguṇenopāsyaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ //4,4.16//
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who desires long life should worship <s>Brahman</s> with the attribute of <s>āyus</s> (life) — this is the meaning. [4.4.16]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.17
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.17]

children.text:
yasmin pañca pañcajanā ākāśaś ca pratiṣṭhitaḥ |
tam eva manya ātmānaṃ vidvān brahmāmṛto 'mṛtam || BrhUp_4,4.17 ||
children.translated_text: That in which the five peoples and space are established — that alone I regard as the <s>Ātman</s> (Self); knowing [it as] <s>Brahman</s>, the immortal, I am immortal. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.17]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,4.17 kiñca yasminyatra brahmaṇi pañca pañcajanā gandharvādayaḥ pañcaiva saṃkhyātā gandharvāḥ pitaro devā asurā rakṣāṃsi niṣādapañcamā vā varṇā ākāśaścāvyākṛtākhyo yasminsūtramimotaṃ ca protaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.17:] Moreover, in which — in this <s>Brahman</s> — the five peoples, counted as five groups — <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), <s>Devas</s> (gods), <s>Asuras</s> (demons),

children.text: yasminpratiṣṭhita etasminnu khalvakṣare gārgyākāśa ityuktaṃ tamevā'tmānamamṛtaṃ brahma manye 'haṃ na cāhamātmānaṃ tato 'nyatvena jāne /
children.translated_text: In which [all] are established — as was said, 'In this imperishable, O <s>Gārgī</s>, space [is woven]' — that alone I regard as the <s>Ātman</s>, the immortal <s>Brahman</s>; and I do not consider my Self as different from that.

children.text: kiṃ tarhyamṛto 'haṃ brahma vidvānsannajñānamātreṇa tu martyo 'hamāsaṃ tadapagamādvidvānahamamṛta eva //4,4.17//
children.translated_text: Rather, I am immortal. As a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, I am immortal; but through ignorance alone I was mortal. With the removal of that [ignorance], as a knower, I am indeed immortal. [4.4.17]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.18
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.18]

children.text:
prāṇasya prāṇam uta cakṣuṣaś cakṣur uta śrotrasya śrotram manaso ye mano viduḥ |
te nicikyur brahma purāṇam agryam || BrhUp_4,4.18 ||
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) of <s>prāṇa</s>, the eye of the eye, the ear of the ear, and the mind of the mind — they have realized <s>Brahman</s>, the ancient, the foremost. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.18]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,4.18 kiñca tena hi caitanyātmajyotiṣāvabhāsyamānaḥ prāṇa ātmabhūtena prāṇīti tena prāṇasyāpi prāṇaḥ sa taṃ prāṇasya prāṇam /
tathā cakṣuṣo 'pi cakṣuruta śrautrasyāpi śrotram /
children.translated_text: Likewise, the eye of the eye, and the ear of the ear.

children.text: brahmamaśaktyodhiṣṭhitānāṃ hi cakṣurādīnāṃ darśanādisāmarthyaṃ svataḥ kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamāni hi tāni caitanyātmajyotiḥśūnyāni /
children.translated_text: For the eyes and other sense organs, when not presided over by the power of <s>Brahman</s>, have no capacity for seeing and so forth; deprived of the light of consciousness, they are like wood or stone.

children.text: manaso 'pi mana iti ye viduścakṣuradāvyāpārānumitāstivaṃ pratyāgātmānaṃ na viṣayabhūtaṃ ye viduste nicikyurniścayena jñātavanto brahma purāṇaṃ cirantanamagryamagre bhavam /
children.translated_text: And those who know the mind of the mind — that is, those who know the inner Self inferred through the activity of the eye and other senses, not as an object [of knowledge] — they have realized with certainty, they have known

children.text: "tadyadātmavido viduḥ"iti hyātharvaṇe //4,4.18//
children.translated_text: the ancient, primeval <s>Brahman</s>. As it is said in the <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>: 'that which the knowers of the Self know.' [4.4.18]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.18:] Moreover, because illuminated by that light of consciousness, <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) breathes by virtue of its own essential nature of consciousness; therefore it is the <s>prāṇa</s> of <s>prāṇa</s>. Those who know that <s>prāṇa</s> of <s>prāṇa</s> —

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.19
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.19]

children.text:
manasaivānudraṣṭavyaṃ neha nānāsti kiṃ cana |
mṛtyoḥ sa mṛtyum āpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati| BrhUp_4,4.19 ||
children.translated_text: By the mind alone is it to be perceived — there is no diversity here whatsoever. He who sees as if there is diversity here goes from death to death. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.19]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.19 tadbrahmadarśane sādhanamucyate manasaiva paramārthajñānasaṃsakṛtenā'cāryovadeśāpūrvakaṃ cānudraṣṭavyam /
tatra ca darśanaviṣaye brahmaṇi neha nānāsti kiñcana kiñcidapu /
asati nānātve nānātvamadhyāropayatyavidyayā /
sa mṛtyormaraṇān mṛtyuṃ maraṇamāpnoti /
children.translated_text: He attains death after death, that is, dying after dying.

children.text: ko 'sau /
children.translated_text: Who is this?

children.text: ya iha nāneva paśyati /
children.translated_text: He who sees as if there is diversity here.

children.text: avidyādhyāropaṇavyatirekeṇa nāsti paramārthato dvaitamityarthaḥ //4,4.19//
children.translated_text: Apart from the superimposition of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), there is no duality in the ultimate sense — this is the meaning. [4.4.19]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.4.19:] The means for the vision of that <s>Brahman</s> is stated: by the mind alone — purified by the knowledge of ultimate reality, preceded by the teaching of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) — it is to be perceived.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.20
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.4.20]

children.text:
ekadhaivānudraṣṭavyam etad apramayaṃ dhruvam |
virajaḥ para ākāśād aja ātmā mahān dhruvaḥ || BrhUp_4,4.20 ||
children.translated_text: It should be perceived as one alone — this immeasurable, unchanging [<s>Brahman</s>]. The <s>Ātman</s> (Self), stainless, beyond space, unborn, great, and eternal. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.20]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.20 yasmādevaṃ tasmādedhaivaikenaiva prakāreṇa vijñānaghanaikarasaprakāreṇā'kāśavannirantareṇānudraṣṭavyam /
yasmādetadbrahmāprameyam /
sarvaikatvāt /
anyena hyanyatpramīyata idaṃ tvekamevāto 'prameyam dhruvaṃ nityaṃ kūṭasthamavicālītyarthaḥ /
nanu viruddhamidamucyate 'prameyaṃ jñāyata iti ca /
jñāyata iti pramāṇairmīyata /
ityartho 'prameyamiti ca tatpratiṣedhaḥ /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
anyadavastuvadanāgamapramāṇaprameyatvapratiṣedhārthatvāt /
yathā'nyāni vastūnyāgamanirapekṣaiḥ pramāṇairviṣayīkriyante na tathaitadātmatatvaṃ pramāṇāntareṇa viṣayīkartuṃ śakyate /
sarvasyā'matve kena kaṃ paśyedvijīnāyaditi pramātṛpramāṇādivyāpārapratiṣedhenaivā'gamo 'pi vijñāpayati na tvabhidhānābhidhelakṣaṇavākyadharmāṅgīkaraṇena /
tasmānnā'gamanāpi svargamervādivattatpratipādyate /
pratipādayitrātmabhūtaṃ hi tat /
pratipādayituḥ pratipādanasya pratipādyaviṣayatvāt /
bhede hi sati tadbhavati /
jñānaṃ ca tasminparātbhāvanivṛttireva /
na tasminsākṣādātmabhāvaḥ kartavye vidyamānvādātmabhavasya /
nityo hyātmabhāvaḥ sarvasyātadviṣaya iva pratyavabhasate /
tasmādatadviṣayāvabhāsanivṛttavyatirekeṇa na tasminnātmabhāvo vidhīyate /
anyātbhāvanivṛttāvātmabhāvaḥ svātmani svābhāviko yaḥ sa kevalo bhavatītyātmā jñāyata ityucyate /
svataścāprameyaḥ pramāṇāntareṇa na viṣayīkriyata ityuccayate /
svataścāprameyaḥ pramāṇāntareṇa na viṣayīkriyata ityubhayamapyaviruddhameva /
virajo vigatarajo rajo nāma dharmādharmādimalaṃ tadrahita ityetat /
paraḥ paro vyatiriktaḥ sūkṣmo vyāpī vā'kāśādapyavyākṛtākhyāt /
ajo na jāyate janmapratiṣedhāduttare 'pi bhāvavikārāḥ pratiṣiddhāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Aja</s> (unborn) — it is not born; through the denial of birth, the subsequent modifications of existence are also denied.

children.text: sarveṣāṃ janmāditvāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because all [modifications] have birth as their origin.

children.text: ātmā mahānparimāṇato mahatatraḥ sarvasmāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The self is great (<s>mahān</s>) — in measure, it is greater than everything.

children.text: dhruvo 'vināśī //4,4.20//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Dhruva</s> (firm) — indestructible. // 4.4.20 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 4.4.20: Since this is so, therefore it should be contemplated in this one way alone — in the manner of a mass of consciousness (<s>vijñānaghana</s>), of one flavor (<s>ekarasa</s>), without intervals, like space.
Because this <s>Brahman</s> is immeasurable (<s>aprameya</s>),
because everything is one [with it].
For one thing is measured by another; but this is one alone — therefore it is immeasurable. '<s>Dhruva</s>' means permanent, eternal, immovable (<s>kūṭastha</s>), unwavering — this is the meaning.
[Objection:] But this is contradictory — [you say] 'immeasurable' and yet 'it is known'!
'It is known' means: it is measured by means of valid knowledge;
this is the meaning. And 'immeasurable' is the denial of that.
[Reply:] This is not a fault.
Because the denial of measurability by means of valid knowledge applies [only] in the sense of [denying measurability as] something non-existent, something not established by scripture.
Just as other objects are made the object of means of valid knowledge independent of scripture — the essential nature of the self cannot be made an object in that way by any other means of valid knowledge.
[The <s>śruti</s>] 'When everything has become the self alone, then by what would one see whom, by what would one know whom?' — even scripture (<s>āgama</s>) communicates [the self] only through the negation of the operations of knower, means of knowledge, and the like — not through the acceptance of the properties of sentences characterized by designation and designatum.
Therefore, even by scripture, it is not established [as an object] like heaven and the like.
For it is the very self of the one who would establish it.
Because the establishing, the act of establishing, would make the establisher himself the object.
For that [relation of knower-known] obtains only when there is a distinction [between them].
And knowledge of it is nothing but the cessation of the notion of otherness.
It is not that the state of being the self is something to be accomplished with respect to it, since the state of being the self already exists.
For the state of being the self is eternal for everyone — it only appears as if [directed toward] something other than itself.
Therefore, apart from the cessation of the appearance [directed toward] what is not-self, no state of being the self is enjoined with respect to it.
When the notion of otherness ceases, the state of being the self — which is natural, inherent in one's own self — remains alone — and [then] it is said: 'the self is known.'
And it is inherently immeasurable — it is not made an object by any other means of valid knowledge — both [statements] are entirely non-contradictory.
<s>Viraja</s> (free from passion) — <s>rajas</s> means the impurity of <s>dharma</s>, <s>adharma</s>, and the like; free from that — this is the meaning.
<s>Para</s> (supreme) — distinct, subtle, all-pervading — even beyond space, [beyond] the unmanifest (<s>avyākṛta</s>).

children.text:
tam eva dhīro vijñāya prajñāṃ kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ |
nānudhyāyād bahūñ chabdān vāco viglāpanaṃ hi tad iti || BrhUp_4,4.21 ||
children.translated_text: Having known that very [self], a wise <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should cultivate insight (<s>prajñā</s>). He should not reflect upon many words, for that is mere weariness of speech. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.21 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,4.21 tamīdṛśamātmānameva dhīro dhāmānvijñāyopadeśataḥ śāstrataśca prajñāṃ śāstrācāryopadiṣṭaviṣayāṃ jijñāsāparisamāptikarīṃ kurvīta brāhmaṇaḥ /
evaṃ prajñākaraṇasādhanāni saṃnyāsaśamadamoparamatitikṣāsamādhānāni kuryīdityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [The meaning is:] thus he should undertake the means for cultivating insight — <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation), <s>śama</s> (tranquility), <s>dama</s> (self-control), <s>uparati</s> (cessation), <s>titikṣā</s> (endurance), and <s>samādhāna</s> (concentration).

children.text: nānudhyāyānnānucintayedbahūnprabhūtāñchabdān /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He should not reflect upon (<s>anudhyāyāt</s>) — should not ponder — many (<s>bahūn</s>), numerous words (<s>śabdān</s>).

children.text: tatra bahutvapratiṣedhātkevalātmakatvapratipādakāḥ svalpāḥ śabdā anujñāyante"omityevaṃ dhyāyatha ātmānam anyā vāco vimiñcatha"iti cā'tharvaṇe /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, by the prohibition of multiplicity, a few words that establish the nature of the self alone are permitted — [as in the <s>Atharvaṇa</s>]: 'Meditate upon the self by <s>Om</s> alone; abandon other words.'

children.text: vāco viglāpanaṃ viśeṣeṇa glānikaraṃ śramakaraṃ hi yasmāttadbahuśabdābhidhyānamiti //4,4.21//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Vāco viglāpanam</s>' — particularly conducive to weariness, fatigue-producing — because that meditation on many words [is such]. // 4.4.21 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 4.4.21: Having known that very self of such a nature — the wise one (<s>dhīra</s>), the intelligent one — through instruction and through scripture, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should cultivate insight (<s>prajñā</s>) — [insight] that pertains to the subjects taught by scripture and teacher, that brings the inquiry to its consummation.

children.text:
sa vā eṣa mahān aja ātmā yo 'yaṃ vijñānamayaḥ prāṇeṣu |
ya eṣo 'ntar hṛdaya ākāśas tasmiñ chete |
sarvasya vaśī |
sarvasyeśānaḥ |
sarvasyādhipatiḥ |

eṣa sarveśvaraḥ |
eṣa bhūtādhipatiḥ |
eṣa bhūtapālaḥ |
eṣa setur vidharaṇa eṣāṃ lokānām asaṃbhedāya |

children.translated_text:
That indeed is the great, unborn self (<s>mahān aja ātmā</s>), which is made of consciousness (<s>vijñānamaya</s>), [dwelling] among the <s>prāṇas</s>.
That which is the space within the heart — in that [space] it reposes.
It is the controller of all (<s>sarvasya vaśī</s>),
the lord of all (<s>sarvasyeśāna</s>),
the sovereign of all (<s>sarvasyādhipati</s>).
It does not become greater by good action,
nor lesser by bad action.
This is the lord of all (<s>sarveśvara</s>).
This is the ruler of beings (<s>bhūtādhipati</s>).
This is the protector of beings (<s>bhūtapāla</s>).
This is the bridge (<s>setu</s>), the support (<s>vidharaṇa</s>), for the non-confusion of these worlds.
This [self] — <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know through the recitation of the <s>Vedas</s>, through sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), through gifts (<s>dāna</s>), through austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and through fasting (<s>anāśaka</s>).
Having known this alone, one becomes a <s>muni</s> (sage).
Desiring this world alone, wandering mendicants (<s>pravrājins</s>) go forth [into renunciation]. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 4.4.22 //
