<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 4.4.22: Bondage and liberation together with their causes have been stated by the <s>mantra</s> and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [portions]; and by the verses (<s>ślokas</s>), the nature of liberation has been explained in detail once more. Now, [it needs to be shown] how, in this subject of the self, the entire <s>Veda</s> becomes applicable — that is to be stated accordingly. For this purpose, this section (<s>kaṇḍikā</s>) is commenced.
And what was stated in this way in this lesson (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>), with its purpose — [that material] is being summarized (<s>anūdya</s>) here to show the application: the entire action-portion (<s>karmakāṇḍa</s>) of the <s>Veda</s>, except for the portion relating to [fulfillment of] desires, is subordinate [to <s>brahmavidyā</s>] — such is the purpose of restating what was already said, beginning with '<s>sa vā eṣa</s>' and so forth.
'<s>Sa</s>' (that) — is for the purpose of referring back to what was stated.
Who is this one being referred to? [The text] indicates him: 'this one who is <s>vijñānamaya</s>' (made of consciousness).
Lest there be a confusion with the [<s>vijñānamaya</s>] stated in a proximate passage — [the text says] 'this one' (<s>ya eṣa</s>).
Which one is this? — It is said: '<s>vijñānamaya</s>, [dwelling] among the <s>prāṇas</s>.'
The reference to the subsequent passage is for the purpose of removing doubt.
For it was stated earlier, at the commencement of <s>Janaka</s>'s question: 'which self?' — 'this one who is <s>vijñānamaya</s>, among the <s>prāṇas</s>' and so forth.
The import is: this self-luminous self who was described by the passage beginning with 'this one who is <s>vijñānamaya</s>, among the <s>prāṇas</s>' — he, through the demonstration that desire, <s>karma</s>, and <s>avidyā</s> are not properties of the self, has been liberated, brought to the state of the supreme self — this one is verily the supreme, not other — [therefore] this very one is directly called 'the great, unborn self.'
'This one who is <s>vijñānamaya</s>, among the <s>prāṇas</s>' — the meaning is as previously explained.
'This one who is the space within the heart' — within the heart, in the interior of the heart-lotus — this space is the supreme self itself, unconditioned. Of the <s>vijñānamaya</s> [self] — its own nature (<s>svasvarūpa</s>) — in that own nature, the supreme self called space, it reposes.
This has been explained as the fourth [state], as the reply to the question 'where was this one then?'
And it is the controller (<s>vaśī</s>) of all — of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the rest.
For everything exists under its control.
And it was stated: 'Under the rule of this Imperishable (<s>Akṣara</s>)' [do all things operate].
Not merely the controller — it is the lord (<s>īśāna</s>) of all; and the lordship over <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and the rest is not something occasionally produced by birth, as in the case of a prince [who becomes lord] over even stronger servants — lest it be [thought] so, [the text] says: it is the sovereign (<s>adhipati</s>) of all — one who governs and protects independently — this is the meaning.
Not like a prince who is dependent upon ministers and other servants.
All three [terms] — controllership and the rest — are in the form of cause and effect.
Because it is the sovereign of all, therefore it is the lord of all.
For it is well known that one who governs and protects another is the lord of that [other].
And because it is the lord of all, therefore it is the controller of all.
Moreover, this being of such nature — the light-person within the heart, the <s>vijñānamaya</s> — does not become greater (<s>bhūyān</s>) by good action, by action enjoined by scripture — it does not increase from its previous state by any attribute whatsoever.
Nor indeed does it become lesser (<s>kanīyān</s>) — diminished from its previous state — by bad action, by action prohibited by scripture — it is not diminished — this is the meaning.
Moreover, [one might ask:] everyone who governs, protects, and so forth, and who grants favor or inflicts punishment upon others, is subject to the <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> [arising from that]; but how can this one be free from that?
It is said: because this one is the lord of all (<s>sarveśvara</s>) — whose nature (<s>śīla</s>) it is to be the lord even of <s>karma</s> itself — therefore it is not affected by <s>karma</s>.
Moreover, this one is the ruler of beings (<s>bhūtādhipati</s>) — the ruler of all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass — this is a term with an already stated meaning.
This one is the protector of beings (<s>bhūtapāla</s>) — the guardian, the preserver of those very [beings].
This one is the bridge (<s>setu</s>).
Of what nature? [The text] says: the support (<s>vidharaṇa</s>) — the upholder of the order of the <s>varṇas</s> and <s>āśramas</s>.
This is what [the text] says — for the non-confusion (<s>asaṃbheda</s>) of these worlds — from <s>Bhūḥ</s> up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s> — for the preservation of their boundaries.
For the worlds, if not upheld like a bridge by the supreme lord, would have their boundaries confused.
Therefore, this supreme lord, who is none other than the self-luminous self, is the bridge-like [upholder] for the non-confusion of the worlds.
The one who knows thus — 'controller of all' and so forth — [this] has been indicated as the fruit of <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>).
Now, in this <s>brahmavidyā</s> prescribed in the sixth lesson (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>) beginning with 'What is the light of the person?' — in this [<s>brahmavidyā</s>] whose fruit is thus [described] — the entire <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritualistic portion), except for the section on desire-prompted [rites], becomes subordinate to it — for this purpose, the restatement of what was already said [is made], beginning with '<s>sa vā eṣa</s>.' It is said: this very self — the <s>Aupaniṣada Puruṣa</s> (the person taught by the <s>Upaniṣads</s>) — <s>brāhmaṇas</s> seek to know through the recitation of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>vedānuvacana</s>) — through the study of the <s>mantras</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, characterized as the daily recitation (<s>nityasvādhyāya</s>) — they desire to know.
Who [does so]? <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
The use of the word '<s>brāhmaṇa</s>' is for illustrative purposes.
For the eligibility of all three <s>varṇas</s> is equal.
Alternatively, by the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> — the <s>mantras</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — through Vedic recitation, they seek to know.
How do they seek to know? — It is said: 'through sacrifice' and so forth.
But those who explain [it as:] 'they seek to know [<s>Brahman</s>] as illuminated by the Vedic recitation characterized by the <s>mantras</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>' — for them, the Vedic recitation would be only the <s>Āraṇyaka</s> portion.
For the supreme self is not illuminated by the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s>.
Moreover, because of the specific statement '<s>aupaniṣadam</s>' (pertaining to the <s>Upaniṣads</s>);
and because '<s>vedānuvacana</s>' is used without restriction — this statement encompasses the whole.
And it is not proper to exclude a part of it.
[Objection:] But even on your interpretation, there would be a partial exclusion — namely, excluding [everything] other than the <s>Upaniṣads</s>.
[Reply:] No — in our first explanation, there is no fault, because there is no contradiction.
When by the term '<s>vedānuvacana</s>' the daily recitation (<s>nityasvādhyāya</s>) is enjoined, the <s>Upaniṣads</s> are also included — thus a part of the meaning of the term '<s>vedānuvacana</s>' is not abandoned.
And because it is listed alongside sacrifice and the rest —
since [the text] is going to enumerate [other] actions such as sacrifice and the rest, it employs the term '<s>vedānuvacana</s>'
— therefore it is understood that action alone is denoted by the term '<s>vedānuvacana</s>.'
For daily recitation is [a form of] <s>karma</s> (action).
But how do they seek to know the self through actions such as daily recitation and the rest?
For these [actions] do not illuminate the self as the <s>Upaniṣads</s> do.
This is not a fault — because actions serve as the cause of purification.
For those who have been refined by actions, whose selves have been purified — they are able to know the self illuminated by the <s>Upaniṣads</s>, without obstruction.
As the <s>Atharvaṇa</s> also [says]: 'One of purified essence (<s>viśuddhasattva</s>) then sees that partless [self] through meditation.' And the <s>smṛti</s> also: 'Knowledge arises in people from the destruction of sinful <s>karma</s>' and so forth.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When the desired object has been attained, what wise person would make effort?' (4.4.22)

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.22, continued:] Thus.
'By sacrifice' — material sacrifices (<s>dravyayajña</s>) and knowledge-sacrifices (<s>jñānayajña</s>) serve the purpose of purification (<s>saṃskāra</s>).
And for one who has been purified, whose <s>sattva</s> (inner nature) has become pure, the arising of knowledge will occur without obstruction — therefore, one 'wishes to know' (<s>vividiṣṭi</s>) by means of sacrifice.
'By charity' (<s>dāna</s>) — charity too, because it is a cause of the destruction of sin and because it is a cause of the increase of <s>dharma</s>.
'By austerity' (<s>tapas</s>) — when, by the general term '<s>tapas</s>' (austerity), practices such as <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and the like are implied, the qualifying term is '<s>anāśaka</s>' (fasting).
'Fasting' (<s>kāmānāśana</s>) means the cessation of desires (<s>anāśaka</s>), not the cessation of eating; for if one ceases eating, one simply dies — there is no self-knowledge [thereby].
By the words 'Vedic recitation' (<s>vedānuvacana</s>), 'sacrifice' (<s>yajña</s>), 'charity' (<s>dāna</s>), and 'austerity' (<s>tapas</s>), all obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) actions are indicated.
Thus, the entire class of obligatory actions, excluding desire-prompted (<s>kāmya</s>) actions, attains the status of being a means to liberation through the gateway of the arising of self-knowledge.
Thus is understood its syntactical unity with the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual portion [of the Veda]).
Thus, by the method stated above, having known this very self as it has been elucidated, one becomes a <s>muni</s> (sage) — a <s>muni</s> from <s>manana</s> (reflection); a <s>yogī</s> — this is the meaning.
Having known this [self] alone, one becomes a <s>muni</s>, not [by knowing] anything else.
[Objection:] But even by knowing something else, one might become a <s>muni</s> — how is it determined that [it is] 'this alone'?
[Reply:] Indeed, even by knowing something else, one might become a <s>muni</s>.
But by knowing something else, one would not be exclusively a <s>muni</s> — what then? One would also be an agent of <s>karma</s>.
But having known this <s>Upaniṣadic</s> person (<s>aupaniṣada puruṣa</s>), one would be exclusively a <s>muni</s>, not an agent of <s>karma</s>.
Therefore, the exclusive <s>muni</s>-hood intended here is determined by [the word] 'this alone.'
For when this [self] is known, 'with what would one see whom?' — thus, because of the impossibility of action, there would be reflection (<s>manana</s>) alone.
Furthermore, desiring this very self as their world (<s>loka</s>), the <s>pravrajins</s> (renunciants) — those whose nature is renunciation — go forth (<s>pravrajanti</s>), meaning: they go forth completely, they renounce all actions — this is the meaning.
From the emphatic restriction 'desiring this world alone,' it is understood that those who desire the three external worlds do not have the qualification for <s>pārivrājya</s> (the monastic life).
For one who is a resident of the <s>Kāśī</s> region and wishes to reach <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s> (Haridwar) does not set out facing eastward.
Therefore, for those who seek the three external worlds, sons, <s>karma</s>, and the knowledge of the lower <s>Brahman</s> are the means.
Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'By a son is this world conquered, not by any other action.'
And therefore, it is not proper for those who seek that [lower goal] to reject the means of sons and the like and adopt <s>pārivrājya</s> (renunciation),
because <s>pārivrājya</s> is not a means for that [goal].
Therefore, the emphatic restriction 'desiring this [self] alone as their world, they go forth' is appropriate.
For the attainment of the world of the self is nothing but abiding in one's own self upon the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).
Therefore, for one who desires the self as his world, the complete cessation of all activity is the primary, most intimate means for the vision of the self,
just as sons and the like are [the means] for the three external worlds.
Because of the inefficacy of the <s>karma</s> of sons and the like for [attaining] the world of the self —
we have stated the contradiction due to impossibility.
Therefore, 'desiring the self alone as their world, they go forth' — meaning: they would certainly desist from all activities.
And just as for those who seek the three external worlds, the specific means such as sons and the like are prescribed, even so, for those who seek the world of the self, the cessation of all desires — <s>pārivrājya</s> (renunciation) — is indeed prescribed for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>.
But why then do those who seek the world of the self go forth? On this, [the text] adduces a statement having the form of an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage) as evidence:
'This is indeed so' — this is the reason stated for <s>pārivrājya</s>: in ancient times, the learned ones — knowers of the self — [did not desire] offspring, <s>karma</s>, or the knowledge of the lower <s>Brahman</s>.
For these three — offspring and the rest — are indicated as the means for the three external worlds.
'Offspring' — what about it? They did not desire it — they did not practice the means of sons and the like for the three external worlds — this is the meaning.
[Objection:] But surely they do practice the meditation on the lower <s>Brahman</s>!
For from its strength arises engagement [in worldly activity].
[Reply:] No — because of the sublation (<s>apavāda</s>) [of the lower <s>Brahman</s>].
'<s>Brahman</s> has abandoned him who knows <s>Brahman</s> as other than the self' — 'everything has abandoned him' — thus even the meditation on the lower <s>Brahman</s> is sublated.
Because even the lower <s>Brahman</s> is included within 'everything.'
And because [the <s>śruti</s> says]: 'Where one does not see another.'
And because of the negation of the perception of prior, posterior, external, and internal: 'without prior, without posterior, without internal, without external.'
And: 'With what would one see whom, with what would one know?' and so forth.
Therefore, [the self-knower] does not require any other cause of engagement apart from the vision of the self.
What then was the intention of those [ancient seers]? It is stated: What purpose, what fruit, what goal shall we accomplish by means of offspring and other instruments?
For offspring has been ascertained to be the means for the external worlds.
And that external world does not exist for us as something other than the self.
For everything is our very self, and we are the self of everything.
And the self, being the self, is not to be produced, obtained, modified, or refined by any means whatsoever. And as for those who perform self-sacrifice (<s>ātmayājin</s>) — [even] the <s>karma</s> that is for the purpose of purification — that too pertains only to the vision of the self as consisting of effects and instruments.
[For the <s>śruti</s> says:] 'This limb of mine is purified by this' — because of the hearing of [terms implying] the relationship of part and whole.
For one who sees [the self as] a mass of consciousness of one taste, without interior, the attribution of the relation of part and whole or of purification is impossible.
Therefore, we shall accomplish nothing by means of offspring and other instruments.
For the fruit [to be accomplished] by means of offspring and other instruments belongs to the ignorant.
For one who sees water in a mirage and, having set forth to drink that water, [is corrected] — for that very person who sees the water there — the engagement [in drinking] is appropriate only where there is mere saline soil and no water [to be found].
Even so, for us who see the world of the self as the ultimate reality, engagement in the goal attainable by means of offspring and the like — which is comparable to a mirage, being the domain of the ignorant's vision — is not appropriate — this is the intention.
This is what is stated: For us who see the ultimate reality — this self of ours, free from hunger and the like, unmodifiable by good and evil — this is the desired world, the desired fruit.
And for this self — which is free from all the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s> such as what-is-to-be-accomplished and the means-of-accomplishment — no means whatsoever is to be sought.
For the search for means is undertaken only for what is to be accomplished.
To search for means for what is not to be accomplished would be like [attempting to] cross on dry land with the idea of water, or like searching for the footprints of birds in the sky.
Therefore, having known this self, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> should go forth; they should not undertake <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning.
Since the ancient <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, being learned thus, did not desire offspring —
those, thus condemning the conventional transaction of what-is-to-be-accomplished and the means-of-accomplishment as 'this is the domain of the ignorant' — what did they do? It is stated: They, having risen above the desire for sons, the desire for wealth, and the desire for worlds — adopted the life of mendicancy (<s>bhikṣācarya</s>) — and so forth, as already explained.
Therefore, 'desiring the self alone as their world, they go forth' — and this injunction (<s>vidhiḥ</s>) is consistent with the laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>).
For this laudatory passage is suitably directed toward the praise of the world [of the self, as a motive for renunciation].
'They go forth' — it is indeed the subsequent passage, 'This is indeed so,' and what follows, that has the form of an <s>arthavāda</s> for [the injunction] 'they go forth.'
[Objection:] But if it is an <s>arthavāda</s>, it should not depend on another <s>arthavāda</s>.
[Reply:] But [the phrase] 'This is indeed so' and what follows is the <s>arthavāda</s> on which 'they go forth' depends.
Since the ancient seers, having desisted from the actions of offspring and the like, went forth — therefore, even those of the present day go forth, should go forth — when connected in this way, [the passage] cannot become directed toward the praise of the world [alone].
[We have stated that] because of the teaching that the same agent [performs both <s>vedānuvacana</s> and <s>pārivrājya</s>].
And because of its being recited together with <s>vedānuvacana</s> (Vedic recitation) and the like.
Just as <s>vedānuvacana</s> and the rest, which are enjoined as means for self-knowledge, have their literal meaning and are not [mere] <s>arthavāda</s>, even so, <s>pārivrājya</s> (renunciation), being recited along with those very [practices], [and] being a means for the attainment of the world of the self — it is inappropriate [to regard it] as <s>arthavāda</s>.
And because of the teaching of distinction of fruits:
'Having known this very self as the world' — [the text] distinguishes the self from the other, external world, as a distinct fruit.
Just as 'By sons alone is this world conquered, not by any other action; by <s>karma</s>, the world of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.' 
And 'they go forth' is not directed solely toward the praise of that [external] world.
Like a principal [injunction], the [passage] depending on an <s>arthavāda</s>, having been heard once, would [otherwise] be complete.
Therefore, this very [notion] that [the passage] is directed toward the praise of the world — is simply a delusion.
Nor is praise appropriate for something that is to be practiced, like <s>pārivrājya</s>.
For if <s>pārivrājya</s>, even though something to be practiced, were to be used for the praise of something else, then even the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and other [rituals], which are also things to be practiced, could be used as praise for something else.
Nor is there any other subject known to be actionable beyond this, such that [<s>pārivrājya</s>] would serve the purpose of praising it here.
But if an injunction of <s>pārivrājya</s> were to be postulated anywhere, it could primarily be here alone, not elsewhere.
As for the postulation of <s>pārivrājya</s> regarding a subject for which one is not qualified — in that case, even tree-climbing and the like could be postulated as <s>pārivrājya</s>,
because there is no difference in [both] being unknown as things-to-be-done.
Therefore, even a trace of [the notion of] praise cannot be imagined here.
[Objection:] If the self is desired as the world, why should one not undertake actions as the means for its attainment — what is [the need for] <s>pārivrājya</s>?
[Reply:] To this it is said: Because of the absence of any connection between this world of the self and actions.
The self that those desiring it should seek through renunciation — that self cannot be connected with actions in any manner whatsoever — neither as something producible, nor as a fruit, nor in any other mode —
Therefore, this self is 'not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>) — ungraspable, for it is not grasped — and so forth, having such characteristics.
Since the self has such characteristics — unconnected with the fruits and means of <s>karma</s>, distinct in character from all the <s>dharmas</s> of <s>saṃsāra</s>, transcending hunger and the like, having the nature of 'not gross' and the like, unborn, unaging, undying, immortal, fearless, having the nature of a mass of consciousness like a lump of salt, self-luminous, one alone, non-dual, without prior, without posterior, without interior, without exterior — [all this has been] established from scripture (<s>āgama</s>) and reasoning (<s>tarka</s>), and in particular in this dialogue between <s>Janaka</s> and <s>Yājñavalkya</s> — therefore, when the self of such characteristics is known as the self, the undertaking of action is simply not tenable.
Therefore, the self is without distinctions.
For one who has eyes, proceeding on a path, does not fall into a pit or onto thorns.

children.text:
"sarvaṃ karmākhilaṃ pārthaṃ jñāne parasamāpyate" /
iti gītāmu /
ihāpi caitasyaiva paramānandasya brahmavitprāpyasyānyāni bhūtāni mātrāmupajīvantītyuktam /
ato brahmavidā na karmārambhaḥ /
yasmātsarvaiṣaṇāvinivṛttaḥ sa eva neti netyātmānamātmatvenopagamya tadrūpeṇaiva vartate tasmādetamevavidaṃ neti netyātmabhūtamu haivaite vakṣyamāṇe na tarato na prāpnuta iti yuktameveti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
ke te ityucyate- ato 'smānnimittāccharīradhāraṇādihetoḥ pāpamapuṇyaṃ karmākaraṃ kṛtavānasmi kaṣṭaṃ khalu mama vṛttamanena pāpena karmaṇāhaṃ narakaṃ pratipatsya iti yo 'yaṃ paścātpāpaṃ karma kṛtavataḥ paritāmapaḥ sa enaṃ neti netyātmabhūtaṃ na tarati /
yathātaḥ kalyāṇaṃ phalaviṣayakāmānnimittādyajñadānādilakṣaṇaṃ puṇyaṃ śobhanaṃ karma kṛtavānasmi /
jato 'hamasya phalaṃsukhamupabhokṣya dehāntara ityeṣo 'pi harṣastaṃ na tarati /
ubhe u haivaiṣa brahmavidete karmaṇī tarati puṇyapāpalakṣaṇe /
evaṃ brahmavidaḥ saṃnyāsina ubhe api karmaṇo kṣīyate pūrvajanmani kṛte ye te cāpūrve ca nā'rabhyete /
kiñca nainaṃ kṛtākṛte kṛtaṃ nityānuṣṭhānamakṛtaṃ tasyaivākriyā te api kṛtākṛte enaṃ na tapataḥ /
anātmajñaṃ hi kṛtaṃ phaladānenākṛtaṃ pratyavāyotpādanena tapataḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who does not know the Self, 'the done' torments by [the obligation of] yielding its fruit, and 'the not-done' torments by producing the sin of omission (<s>pratyavāya</s>).

children.text: ayaṃ tu brahmavidātmavidyāgninā sarvāṇi karmāṇi bhasmīkaroti"yathedhāṃsi samidvo 'gniḥ" ityādismṛteḥ /
children.translated_text: But this knower of <s>Brahman</s> reduces all <s>karmas</s> to ashes by the fire of self-knowledge — as the <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'Just as a blazing fire [reduces] fuel [to ashes]' (BhG 4.37) and so forth.

children.text: śarīrārambhakayostūpabhogenaiva kṣayaḥ /
children.translated_text: But for those [<s>karmas</s>] that have initiated the [present] body, their destruction comes only through [actual] experience [of their fruits].

children.text: ato brahmavidakarmasaṃbandhī //4,4.22//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> has no connection with <s>karma</s>. // 4.4.22 //

'All action in its entirety, O <s>Pārtha</s>, culminates in knowledge' (BhG 4.33) — thus says the <s>Gītā</s>. Here too it has been stated that other beings live upon a mere fraction of this very supreme bliss that is attainable by the knower of <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, the knower of <s>Brahman</s> does not undertake [ritual] action. Because he who has renounced all desires — he alone, having accepted the Self described as '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) as his own self, abides in that very form. Therefore, 'this one, having known him as the Self that is <s>neti neti</s>' — the forthcoming [statements] — 'he does not cross over, he does not attain' — this is entirely fitting. This is the remainder of the sentence. Who are those [who do not cross over]? This is stated: due to this reason — on account of maintaining the body and the like — 'I have committed sinful, unmeritorious action; alas, miserable indeed has been my conduct; by this sinful action I shall fall into hell' — this remorse (<s>paritāpa</s>) that arises afterwards in one who has committed sinful action — that does not overcome him who has become the Self described as '<s>neti neti</s>.' Similarly, 'I have performed auspicious, meritorious action — sacrifice, charity, and the like — motivated by desire for a fruit; therefore I shall enjoy happiness as its fruit in another body' — even this joy does not overcome him. Indeed, this knower of <s>Brahman</s> crosses over both these actions characterized by merit and demerit. Thus, for the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the renunciant, both types of <s>karmas</s> — those performed in previous births — are destroyed, and no new ones are undertaken. Furthermore, 'the done and the not-done do not torment him' — 'the done' means regular obligatory actions performed, and 'the not-done' means the non-performance of those same [duties]. These too — the done and the not-done — do not torment him.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.23
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.23]

children.text:
tad etad ṛcābhyuktam --
eṣa nityo mahimā brāhmaṇasya na karmaṇā vardhate no kanīyān |
tasyaiva syāt padavittaṃ viditvā na lipyate karmaṇā pāpakeneti |
tasmād evaṃvic chānto dānta uparatas titikṣuḥ samāhito bhūtvātmany evātmānaṃ paśyati |
sarvam ātmānaṃ paśyati |
nainaṃ pāpmā tarati |
sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ tarati |
nainaṃ pāpmā tapati |
sarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ tapati |
vipāpo virajo 'vicikitso brāhmaṇo bhavati |
eṣa brahmalokaḥ samrāṭ |
enaṃ prāpito 'sīti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
so 'haṃ bhagavate videhān dadāmi mām cāpi saha dāsyāyeti || BrhUp_4,4.23 ||
children.translated_text:
This has been declared by a <s>ṛk</s> (verse):
'This is the eternal greatness of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — it is not increased by <s>karma</s>, nor diminished.
One should know the track of that [greatness] alone; knowing it, one is not tainted by evil action.'
Therefore, one who knows thus, being tranquil (<s>śānta</s>), self-controlled (<s>dānta</s>), withdrawn (<s>uparata</s>), patient (<s>titikṣu</s>), and concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>), sees the Self in the Self alone.
He sees everything as the Self.
Evil does not overcome him;
he overcomes all evil.
Evil does not torment him;
he burns up all evil.
Free from evil, free from impurity, free from doubt — he becomes a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.
'This is the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, O Emperor.
I have led you to it' — thus said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.
[<s>Janaka</s> replied:] 'I give your honor the <s>Videhas</s> [kingdom] and myself as well, to be your servant.' // BṛUp 4.4.23 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.23 tadetadvastu brāṅmaṇenoktamṛcā mantreṇābhyuktaṃ prakāśitam /
eṣa neti netyādilakṣaṇo nityo mahimā /
anye tu mahimānaḥ karmakṛtā ityanityāḥ /
ayaṃ tu tadvilakṣaṇo mahimā svābhāvikatvānnityo brahmavido brāhmaṇasya tyaktasarveṣaṇasya /
kuto 'sya nityatvamiti hetumāha- karmaṇā na vardhate śubhalakṣaṇena kṛtena vṛdvilakṣaṇāṃ vikriyāṃ na prāpneti /
aśubhena karmaṇā no kanīyānnāpyapakṣayalakṣaṇāṃ vikriyāṃ prāpnoti /
upacayāpacayahetubhūtā eva hi sarvā vikriyā ityetābhyāṃ pratiṣidhyante /
ato 'vikriyatvānnitya eṣa mahimā /
tasmāttasyaiva mahimnaḥ syādbhavetpadavitpadasya vettā padyate gamyate jñāyata iti mahimnaḥ svarūpameva padaṃ tasya padasya veditā /
kiṃ tatpadavedanena syādityucyate-taṃ viditvā mahimānaṃ na lipyate na saṃbadhyate karmaṇā pāpakena dharmādharmalakṣaṇenobhayamapi pāpakameva viduṣaḥ /
tasmādevamakarmasaṃbandhyeṣa brāhmaṇasya mahimā neti netyādilakṣaṇastasmādevaṃvicchānto bāhyendriyavyāpārata upaśāntastathā dānto 'ntaḥ karaṇatṛṣṇāto nivṛtta uparataḥ sarvaiṣaṇāvinirmuktaḥ saṃnyāsī titikṣurdvandvasahiṣṇuḥ samāhita indriyāntaḥ karaṇācalanarūpādvyāvṛtyaikāgryarūpeṇa samāhito bhūtvā /
tadetaduktaṃ purastādbālyaṃ ca pāṇḍityaṃ ca nirvidyeti /
ātmanyeva sve kāryakaraṇasaṃghāta ātmānaṃ pratyakcetayitāraṃ paśyati /
tatra kiṃ tāvanmānnaṃ paricchinaṃ netyucyatesarvaṃ samastamātmānameva paśyati nānyadātmavyatiriktaṃ vālāgramānnamapyastītyevaṃ paśyati /
mananānmunirbhavati jāgratsvapnasuṣuptākhyaṃ sthānannayaṃ hitvā /
evaṃ paśyantaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ nainaṃ pāpmā puṇyapāpalakṣaṇastarati na prāpneti /
ayaṃ tu brahmavitsarvaṃ pāpmānaṃ taratyātmabhāvenaiva vyāpnotyatikrāmati /
nainaṃ pāpmā kṛtākṛtalakṣaṇastapatīṣṭaphalapratyavāyotpādanābhyām /
sarvaṃ pāpmānamayaṃ tapati brahmavitsarvatmadarśanavahrinā bhasmīkaroti /
sa eṣa evaṃvidvipāyo vigatadharmādharmo birajo vigatarajo rajaḥkāmo vigatakāmo 'vicikitsaśchinnasaṃśayo 'hamasmi sarvātmā paraṃ brahmeti niścitamatirbrāhmaṇo bhavati /
ayaṃ tvevaṃbhūta atasyāmavasthāyāṃ mukhyo brāhmaṇaḥ prāgetasmādbrahmasvarūpāvasthānādgauṇamasya brāhmaṇyam /
eṣa brahmaloko brahmaiva loko brahmaloko mukhyo nirupacaritaḥ sarvātmabhāvalakṣaṇo he smāraṭ /
enaṃ brahmalokaṃ pariprāpito 'syabhayaṃ neti netyādilakṣaṇamiti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'I have led you to this <s>Brahmaloka</s> — the fearless, characterized as <s>neti neti</s> and the rest' — thus spoke <s>Yājñavalkya</s>.

children.text: evaṃ brahmabhūto janako yājñavalkyena brahmabhāvamāpāditaḥ pratyāha-so 'haṃ tvayā brahmabhāvamāpāditaḥ sanbhagavate tubhyaṃ videhāndeśānmama rājya samastaṃ dadāmi māṃ ca saha kartavyatākā /
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Janaka</s>, having been brought to the state of <s>Brahman</s> by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, replies: 'I, having been brought by you to the state of <s>Brahman</s>, give to your honor, the Venerable One, the <s>Videha</s> kingdom — my entire realm — and myself as well, to be at your service.'

children.text: parisamāptaḥ paramapuruṣārthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The supreme goal of human life (<s>paramapuruṣārtha</s>) has been brought to completion.

children.text: etāvatpuruṣeṇa kartavyameṣā niṣṭhaiṣā parā gatiretanniḥśreyasametatprāpya kṛtakṛtyo brāhmaṇo bhavatyetatsarvavedānuśāsanamiti //4,4.23//
children.translated_text: This much is to be accomplished by a person — this is the conclusion, this is the supreme goal, this is the highest good. Having attained this, one becomes a fulfilled <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. This is the teaching of all the <s>Vedas</s>. // 4.4.23 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.23:] That very reality — by a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [passage], by a <s>ṛk</s> (verse), a <s>mantra</s> — has been declared, made luminous. This eternal greatness, characterized as '<s>neti neti</s>' and the rest, is the eternal greatness — while other greatnesses, produced by <s>karma</s>, are impermanent. But this greatness, being different from those, is eternal because it is intrinsic — [it is the greatness] of the knower of <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has renounced all desires. Why is it eternal? The reason is stated: by <s>karma</s> — by auspicious action that has been performed — it does not increase, it does not undergo the modification of increase. Nor by inauspicious action is it diminished — it does not undergo the modification of decrease. For all modifications are either of the nature of increase or decrease — and by these two [modifications], all [other modifications] are negated. Therefore, because of being free from modification, this greatness is eternal. Therefore, one should know the track (<s>padavit</s>) of that very greatness — the knower of the 'track' (<s>pada</s>), that which is reached, known — the very nature of the greatness is the 'track'; the knower of that track. What results from knowing that track? This is stated: having known it — having known that greatness — one is not tainted, not connected with evil action (<s>pāpaka</s>) characterized by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, for both are indeed evil for the wise person. Therefore, one who knows thus — whose greatness is unconnected with action, characterized as '<s>neti neti</s>' — therefore, one who knows thus becomes <s>śānta</s> — tranquil, withdrawn from the activity of the external sense-organs; likewise <s>dānta</s> — internally restrained, withdrawn from the craving of the internal organ; <s>uparata</s> — freed from all desires, a renunciant (<s>saṃnyāsin</s>); <s>titikṣu</s> — patient, tolerant of the pairs of opposites; <s>samāhita</s> — concentrated, having turned from the agitation of the sense-organs and internal organ to the form of single-pointedness. This has been stated previously: '<s>bālya</s> (childlike simplicity) and <s>pāṇḍitya</s> (erudition) — having transcended [both]...' In the Self alone — in one's own [Self], in the aggregate of effects and instruments — one sees the Self, the inner witness-consciousness. Therein — does one see [it] as measured, as limited? No — this is stated: one sees everything as the Self alone; not even a hair's-breadth of anything other than the Self exists — thus one sees. Through contemplation (<s>manana</s>), one becomes a <s>muni</s> (sage), abandoning the states called waking, dream, and deep sleep. One who sees thus as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — evil characterized by merit and demerit does not overcome him, does not reach him. Rather, this knower of <s>Brahman</s> overcomes all evil — pervades it by virtue of being the Self of all, transcends it. Evil characterized by the done and the not-done does not torment him — through [the obligation of] yielding desired fruits and producing the sin of omission. Rather, this knower of <s>Brahman</s> burns up all evil — reduces it to ashes by the fire of seeing the Self in all things. He, thus knowing, becomes free from evil (<s>vipāpa</s>) — free from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; free from impurity (<s>viraja</s>) — free from passion (<s>rajas</s>), where <s>rajas</s> means desire, free from desire; free from doubt (<s>avicikitsa</s>) — with doubt destroyed, with the firm conviction 'I am the Self of all, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — he becomes a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. But in this condition, this is the primary <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; before this establishment in the nature of <s>Brahman</s>, his <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood was merely figurative. This is the <s>Brahmaloka</s> — <s>Brahman</s> itself is the world, the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, the primary, non-figurative [one], characterized by the state of being the Self of all — O Emperor!

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.24
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.24]

children.text:
sa vā eṣa mahān aja ātmānnādo vasudānaḥ |
vindate vasu ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_4,4.24 ||
children.translated_text: This great, unborn Self is the eater of food, the giver of wealth. He who knows thus finds wealth. // BṛUp 4.4.24 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,4.24 yo 'yaṃ janakayājñavalkyākhyāyikāyāṃ vyākhyāta ātmā sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmānnādaḥ sarvabhūtasthaḥ sarvānnānāmattā vasudāno vasu dhanaṃ sarvaprāṇikarmaphalaṃ tasya dātā prāṇināṃ yathākarma phalena yojayitetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.24:] The Self that has been explained in the narrative of <s>Janaka</s> and <s>Yājñavalkya</s> — this great, unborn Self is the eater of food (<s>annāda</s>) — abiding in all beings, consuming the food of all; the giver of wealth (<s>vasudāna</s>) — the giver of wealth, of all the fruits of the <s>karmas</s> of all living beings, meaning: the one who connects living beings with the fruit according to their <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tamekamajamannādaṃ vasudānamātmānamannādavasudānaguṇābhyāṃ yuktaṃ yo veda sa sarvabhūteṣvātmabhūto 'nnamatti vindate ca vasu sarvaṃ karmaphalajātaṃ labhate sarvātmatvādena ya evaṃ yathoktaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: He who knows this one, unborn Self — the eater of food and the giver of wealth — as endowed with the qualities of eating food and giving wealth — he, being the Self of all beings, eats food and finds (<s>vindate</s>) wealth — obtains the entirety of all fruits of <s>karma</s>, because of being the Self of all. Thus does he who knows thus, as stated, [attain this].

children.text: athavā dṛṣṭaphalārthibhirapyevaṅguṇa upāsyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Alternatively, even for those who desire visible results, [the Self] endowed with such qualities is to be meditated upon.

children.text: tenānnādo vasośca labdhā dṛṣṭenaiva phalenānnātṛtvena goścādinā cāsya yogo bhavatītyarthaḥ //4,4.24//
children.translated_text: Thereby [one becomes] an eater of food and an obtainer of wealth — with the visible result alone, namely the capacity to eat and [the possession of] cattle and the like — this is the connection. // 4.4.24 //

children.text: START BrhUp 4,4.25
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.4.25]

children.text:
sa vā eṣa mahān aja ātmājaro 'maro 'mṛto 'bhayo brahma |
abhayaṃ vai brahma |
abhayaṃ hi vai brahma bhavati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_4,4.25 ||
children.translated_text: This great, unborn Self is ageless, deathless, immortal, fearless — <s>Brahman</s>. Fearless indeed is <s>Brahman</s>. He who knows thus indeed becomes fearless <s>Brahman</s>. // BṛUp 4.4.25 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,4.25 idānīṃ samastasyaivā'raṇyarakasya yor'tha uktaḥ sa samuccityāsyā kaṇḍikāyāṃ nirdiśyata etāvānsamastāraṇyakārtha iti /
sa vā eṣa mahānaja ātmājaro na jīryata iti na vipariṇamata ityarthaḥ /
amaro yasmāccājarastasmādamaro na mriyata ityamaraḥ /
yo hi jāyate jīryate ca sa vinaśyati mriyate vā /
ayaṃ tvajatvādajaratvāccāvināśī yato 'ta evāmṛtaḥ /
yasmājjaniprabhṛtistribhirbhāvaviripairvarjitastasmāditarairapi bhāvavikāraistribhistatkṛtaiśca kāmakarmamohādibhirmṛtyurūpairvījata ityetat /
abhayo 'ta eva /
yasmāccaivaṃ pūrvoktaviśeṣaṇastasmasmādbhayavarjitaḥ bhayaṃ ca hi nāmāvidyākāryaṃ tatkāryapritiṣedhena bhāvavikārapratiṣedhena cāvidyāyāḥ pratiṣedhaḥ siddho veditavyaḥ /
abhaya ātmaivaṅguṇaviśiṣṭaḥ kimasau brahma parivṛḍhaṃ niratiśayaṃ mahadityarthaḥ /
abhayaṃ vai brahma /
prasiddhametalloke 'bhayaṃ brahmeti /
tasmādyuktamevaṅguṇaviśiṣṭa ātmā brahmeti /
ya evaṃ yathoktamātmānamabhayaṃ brahma veda so 'bhayaṃ hi vai brahma bhavati /
eṣa sarvasyā upaniṣadaḥ saṃkṣiptor'tha uktaḥ /
etasyaivārthas samyakprabodhāyotpattisthitipralayādikalpanā kriyākārakaphalādhyāropaṇā cā'tmani kṛtā tadapohena ca neti netītyadhyāropitāviśeṣāpanayadvāreṇapunastatvamāveditam /
children.translated_text: For the purpose of the complete awakening to this very meaning — the imagining of creation, maintenance, dissolution, and the like, and the superimposition of action, agent, and fruit upon the Self, were performed; and by their removal through '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this) — by the method of negating the superimposed distinctions — the reality has been made known again.

children.text: yathaikaprabhṛtyāparārdhasaṃkhyāsvarūpaparijñānāyā rekhādhyāropaṇaṃ kṛtvaikeyaṃ rekhā daśeyaṃ śateyaṃ sahasreyamiti grāhayatyavagamayati saṃkhyāsvarūpaṃ kevalaṃ na tu saṃkhyāyā rekhātmatvameva yathā cākārādīnyakṣarāṇi grāhayati tathā cehotpatyādyanekopāyamāsthāyaikaṃ brahmatattvamāveditam /
children.translated_text: Just as, for the purpose of fully understanding the nature of numbers from one to a <s>parārdha</s> (a very large number), one draws lines and teaches: 'this line is one, this is ten, this is a hundred, this is a thousand' — making known the nature of number alone, while the numbers are not [actually] identical with the lines — and just as one teaches the letters <s>a-kāra</s> and the rest [by writing them down] — even so, here, by resorting to multiple means such as creation and the rest, the one reality of <s>Brahman</s> has been made known.

children.text: punastatkalpitopāyajanitaviśeṣapariśodhanārthaṃ neti netīti tattvopasaṃhāraḥ kṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, for the purpose of purifying the distinctions generated by those imagined means, the summarizing conclusion of reality through '<s>neti neti</s>' was performed.

children.text: tadupasaṃhṛtaṃ punaḥ pariśuddhaṃ kevalameva saphalaṃ jñānamante 'sya kaṇḍikāyāmiti //4,4.25//
children.translated_text: That which has been thus concluded — the purified, mere, fruitful knowledge alone — [comes] at the end of this section. // 4.4.25 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.4.25:] Now, the meaning of the entire <s>Āraṇyaka</s> that has been stated is gathered together and indicated in this section — 'This much is the meaning of the entire <s>Āraṇyaka</s>.' This great, unborn Self — ageless (<s>ajara</s>): it does not decay, meaning it does not undergo transformation. Deathless (<s>amara</s>): because it is ageless, therefore it is deathless — it does not die, hence it is deathless. For that which is born and decays — that perishes, that dies. But this [Self], because of being unborn and ageless, is imperishable — therefore it is immortal (<s>amṛta</s>). Because it is free from the three states of change beginning with birth, therefore it is also free from the other three states of change, and from desire, <s>karma</s>, delusion, and the like — which are forms of death created by those [changes]. This indeed is [its nature]. Therefore it is fearless (<s>abhaya</s>) — because it is endowed with the aforementioned qualities, it is free from fear. For fear is indeed an effect of <s>avidyā</s>; by the negation of its effects and the negation of the states of change, the negation of <s>avidyā</s> itself is to be understood as established. This fearless Self, endowed with such qualities — is it <s>Brahman</s>? — [meaning] the all-pervading, unsurpassable, the great — this is the meaning. 'Fearless indeed is <s>Brahman</s>' — this is well-known in the world, that fearless is <s>Brahman</s>. Therefore, it is entirely fitting that the Self endowed with such qualities is <s>Brahman</s>. He who knows the Self thus, as described — the fearless <s>Brahman</s> — he indeed becomes fearless <s>Brahman</s>. This is the meaning of the entire <s>Upaniṣad</s>, stated in summary.

children.text: iti caturthaṃ brāhmaṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. //

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.5.1]

children.text:
atha ha yājñavalkyasya dve bhārye babhūvatur maitreyī ca kātyāyanī ca |
tayor ha maitreyī brahmavādinī babhūva |
strīprajñaiva tarhi kātyāyanī |
atha ha yājñavalkyo 'nyad vṛttam upākariṣyan || BrhUp_4,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> had two wives — <s>Maitreyī</s> and <s>Kātyāyanī</s>. Of them, <s>Maitreyī</s> was a discourser on <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brahmavādinī</s>), while <s>Kātyāyanī</s> had only a woman's [ordinary] understanding. Then <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, being about to commence another mode of life — // BṛUp 4.5.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,5.1 āgamapradhānena madhukāṇḍena brahmatattvaṃ nirdhāritam /
punastasyaivopattipradhānena yājñavalkīyena kāṇḍena pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahaṃ kṛtvā vigṛhyavādena vicāritam /
śaiṣyācāryasaṃbandhena ca ṣaṣṭhe praśnaprativacananyāyena savistaraṃ vicāryopasaṃhṛtam /
athedānīṃ nigamanasthānīyaṃ maitreyībrāhmaṇamārabhyete /
ayaṃ ca nyāyo vākyakovidaiḥ parigṛhīto hetvapadeśātpratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ nigamanamiti /
athavā'gamapradhānena madhukāṇḍena yadamṛtatvasādhanaṃ sasaṃnyāsabhātmajñānamabhihitaṃ tadeva tarkeṇāpyamṛtatvasādhanaṃ sasaṃnyāsamātmajñānamadhigamyate /
tarkapradhānaṃhi yājñavalkīyaṃ kāṇḍam /
tasmācchāstratarkābhyāṃ niścitametadyadetadātmajñānaṃ sasaṃnyāsamamṛtatvasādhanamiti /
tasmācchāstraśraddhāvadbhiramṛtatvapratipitsubhiretatpratipattavyamiti /
āgamopapattibhyāṃ hi niścitor'thaḥ śraddheyo bhavatyavyabhicārāditi /
akṣarāṇāṃ tu caturthe yathā vyākhyātor'thastathā pratipattavyo 'trāpi /
yānyakṣarāṇyavyākhyātāni tāni vyākhyāsyāmaḥ /
atheti hetūpadeśānantaryapradarśanārthaḥ /
hetupradhānāni hi vākyānyatītāni tadanantaramāgamapradhānena pratijñātor'tho nigamyate maitreyībrāhmaṇena /
haśabdo vṛttāvadyotakaḥ /
children.translated_text: The particle 'ha' indicates a well-known past event.

children.text: yājñavalkyasyarṣeḥ kila dve bhārye patnyau babhūvaturāstāṃ maitreyī ca nāmata ekāparā kātyāyanī nāmataḥ tayorbhāryayormaitreyīha kila brahmavādinī brahmavadanaśīlā babhūvā'sīt /
children.translated_text: The sage <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, it is said, had two wives. One was <s>Maitreyī</s> by name, and the other was <s>Kātyāyanī</s> by name. Of these two wives, <s>Maitreyī</s> was indeed a <s>brahmavādinī</s> (one given to discoursing on <s>Brahman</s>).

children.text: strīprajñā striyāṃ yocitā sā strīprajñā saiva yasyāḥ prajñā gṛhaprayojanānveṣaṇālakṣaṇā sā strīprajñaiva tarhi tasminkāla āsītkātyāyanī /
children.translated_text: <s>Strīprajñā</s> (woman's understanding) means that understanding which is appropriate to women — she whose understanding is characterized by concern for household affairs — such a one with merely womanly understanding was <s>Kātyāyanī</s> at that time.

children.text: athaivaṃ sati ha kila yājñavalkyo 'nyatpūrvasmādgārhasthyalakṣaṇādvṛttātpārivrājyalakṣaṇaṃ vṛttamupākariṣyannupācikīrṣuḥ san //4,5.1//
children.translated_text: Then, this being so, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, it is said, being about to undertake a different mode of life — that of renunciation (<s>pārivrājya</s>) — from his former mode of life characterized by the householder stage (<s>gārhasthya</s>), wishing to commence [it] — [4.5.1]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.1:] Through the <s>Madhu Kāṇḍa</s> (Honey Chapter), which is primarily based on scripture (<s>āgama</s>), the truth of <s>Brahman</s> was ascertained. Then, through the <s>Yājñavalkīya Kāṇḍa</s>, which primarily employs reasoning (<s>upapatti</s>), the same was examined through dialectical argument (<s>vigṛhyavāda</s>), taking up thesis and counter-thesis. And in the sixth [section], through the teacher-student relationship, it was thoroughly investigated by the method of question and answer, and concluded. Now the <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s>, which serves as the concluding restatement (<s>nigamana</s>), is begun. This principle has been accepted by those skilled in discourse: the restatement of the proposition after the presentation of reasons is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>). Alternatively, that knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> accompanied by renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>), which was stated through the scripture-based <s>Madhu Kāṇḍa</s> as the means to immortality, that very same knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> with renunciation is also arrived at as the means to immortality through reasoning. For the <s>Yājñavalkīya Kāṇḍa</s> is primarily based on reasoning. Therefore, it is established through both scripture and reasoning that this knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> accompanied by renunciation is the means to immortality. Therefore, those who have faith in the scriptures and desire to attain immortality should realize this. For a truth ascertained through both scripture and reasoning becomes worthy of faith, since it is unfailing. The words [of this section] should be understood here just as they were explained in the fourth [chapter]. We shall explain those words that were not explained [there]. The word 'atha' (now/then) indicates the sequence following the presentation of reasons. For the preceding passages were primarily concerned with reasons; following them, the meaning that was proposed is concluded through the scripture-based <s>Maitreyī Brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.2]

children.text:
maitreyīti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
pravrajiṣyan vā are 'ham asmāt sthānād asmi |
hanta te 'nayā katyāyanyāntaṃ karavāṇīti || BrhUp_4,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: "O <s>Maitreyī</s>," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, "I am about to renounce (<s>pravrajya</s>) from this station [of householder life]. Come, let me make a settlement between you and <s>Kātyāyanī</s>." [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.2]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.2 he maitreyīti jyeṣṭhāṃ bhāryāmāmantrayāmāsa /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.2:] Saying "O <s>Maitreyī</s>," he addressed his senior wife.

children.text: āmanñya covāca ha pravrajiṣyanpānivrājyaṃ kariṣyanvā are maitreyyasmātsthānādgārhasthyādahamasmi bhavāmi /
children.translated_text: Having addressed her, he said: "I am about to renounce, to undertake the life of a wandering mendicant (<s>pārivrājya</s>) — O <s>Maitreyī</s>, from this station, from the householder's life, I am [departing]."

children.text: maitreyyanujānīhi māṃ hantecchasi yadi te 'nayā kātyāyanyāntaṃ karavāṇotyādi vyākhyātam //4,5.2//
children.translated_text: "O <s>Maitreyī</s>, permit me. Come, if you wish, let me make a settlement between you and <s>Kātyāyanī</s>" — and so forth has been explained. [4.5.2]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.3-4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.3-4]

children.text:
sā hovāca maitreyī --
yan nu ma iyam bhagoḥ sarvā pṛthivī vittena pūrṇā syāt syāṃ nv ahaṃ tenāmṛtāho3 neti |
neti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ |
yathaivopakaraṇavatāṃ jīvitam |
tathaiva te jīvitaṃ syāt |
amṛtatvasya tu nāśāsti vitteneti || BrhUp_4,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s> said: "If, O Venerable One, this entire earth filled with wealth were mine, would I become immortal thereby, or not?" "No," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. "Your life would be just like the life of those who possess the means [of enjoyment]. But there is no hope of immortality through wealth." [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.3]

children.text:
sā hovāca maitreyī --
yenāhaṃ nāmṛtā syām kim ahaṃ tena kuryām |
yad eva bhagavān veda tad eva me brūhīti || BrhUp_4,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s> said: "What should I do with that by which I would not become immortal? What the Venerable One knows, that alone tell me." [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.4]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.3-4 saivamuktovāca maitreyī sarveyaṃ pṛthivī vittena pūrṇā syānnu kiṃ syāṃ kimahaṃ vittasādhyena karmaṇāmṛtā'ho na syāmiti /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.3-4:] Having been thus addressed, <s>Maitreyī</s> said: "If this entire earth were filled with wealth, would I — would I through action whose results are attainable by wealth — become immortal, or not?"

children.text: neti hovāca yājñavalkya ityādi samānamanyat //4,5.3-4 //
children.translated_text: "No," said <s>Yājñavalkya</s> — and the rest is the same [as explained before]. [4.5.3-4]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.5]

children.text:
sa hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ --
priyā vai khalu no bhavatī satī priyam avṛdhat |
hanta tarhi |
bhavaty etad vyākhyāsyāmi te |
vyācakṣāṇasya tu me nididhyāsasveti || BrhUp_4,5.5 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yājñavalkya</s> said: "Dear indeed you have always been to us, and now you have enhanced that dearness. Come then, noble lady, I shall explain this to you. But as I am explaining, meditate deeply upon it (<s>nididhyāsasva</s>)." [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.5]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.5 sa hovāca priyaiva pūrvaṃ khalu no 'smabhyaṃ bhavatī bhavanti sato priyamevāvṛdhadvardhitavatī nirdhāritavatyasi /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.5:] He said: "You were already dear to us before, and being [such a] dear one, you have indeed increased, confirmed, and established [our] affection."

children.text: atastuṣṭo 'haṃ hantecchasi cedamṛtatvasādhanaṃ jñātuṃ he bhavati te tubhyaṃ tadmṛtatvasādhanaṃ vyākhyāsyāmi //4,5.5//
children.translated_text: "Therefore I am pleased. Come, if you desire to know the means to immortality, O noble lady, I shall explain to you that means to immortality." [4.5.5]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.6]

children.text:
sa hovāca |
na vā are patyuḥ kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya patiḥ priyo bhavati |
na vā are jāyāyai kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya jāyā priyā bhavati |
na vā are putrāṇāṃ kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya putrāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are vittasya kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya vittaṃ priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are paśūnāṃ kāmāya paśavaḥ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya paśavaḥ priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are brahmaṇaḥ kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya brahma priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are kṣatrasya kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya kṣatraṃ priyaṃ bhavati |
na vā are lokānāṃ kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya lokāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are devānāṃ kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya devāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are vedānāṃ kāmāya vedāḥ priyā bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya vedāḥ priyā bhavanti |
na vā are bhūtānāṃ kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanty ātmanas tu kāmāya bhūtāni priyāṇi bhavanti |
na vā are sarvasya kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavaty ātmanas tu kāmāya sarvaṃ priyaṃ bhavati |
ātmā vā are draṣṭavyaḥ śrotavyo mantavyo nididhyāsitavyo maitreyi |
ātmani khalv are dṛṣṭe śrute mate vijñāta idaṃ sarvaṃ viditam || BrhUp_4,5.6 ||
children.translated_text: He said: "Verily, a husband is not dear for the sake of the husband; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) that the husband is dear. Verily, a wife is not dear for the sake of the wife; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that the wife is dear. Verily, sons are not dear for the sake of the sons; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that sons are dear. Verily, wealth is not dear for the sake of wealth; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that wealth is dear. Verily, cattle are not dear for the sake of cattle; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that cattle are dear. Verily, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class is not dear for the sake of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> class is dear. Verily, the <s>kṣatriya</s> class is not dear for the sake of the <s>kṣatriya</s> class; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that the <s>kṣatriya</s> class is dear. Verily, the worlds are not dear for the sake of the worlds; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that the worlds are dear. Verily, the gods are not dear for the sake of the gods; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that the gods are dear. Verily, the <s>Vedas</s> are not dear for the sake of the <s>Vedas</s>; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that the <s>Vedas</s> are dear. Verily, beings are not dear for the sake of beings; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that beings are dear. Verily, everything is not dear for the sake of everything; it is for the sake of the <s>Ātman</s> that everything is dear. Verily, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, the <s>Ātman</s> is to be seen, heard, reflected upon, and deeply meditated upon (<s>nididhyāsitavya</s>). Verily, when the <s>Ātman</s> has been seen, heard, reflected upon, and realized, all this becomes known." [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.6]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,5.6 ātmani khalvare maitreyī dṛṣṭe /
kathaṃ dṛṣṭa ātmanīti, ucyate-pūrvamācāryāgamābhyāṃ śrute punastarkeṇopapattayā mate vicārite /
śravaṇaṃ tvāgamamātreṇa mata upapattyā paścādvijñāna evametannānyatheti nirdhārite /
children.translated_text: 'Hearing' (<s>śravaṇa</s>) is by means of scripture alone; 'reflection' (<s>manana</s>) is through reasoning; and afterwards, 'realization' (<s>vijñāna</s>) is the firm ascertainment that 'it is exactly thus and not otherwise.'

children.text: kiṃ bhavatītyucyata idaṃ viditaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: What happens then? It is said: 'all this becomes known.'

children.text: idaṃ sarvamiti yadātmano 'nyat /
children.translated_text: 'All this' means whatever is other than the <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: ātmavyatirekeṇābhāvāt //4,5.6//
children.translated_text: Because apart from the <s>Ātman</s>, [nothing else] has [independent] existence. [4.5.6]

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.6:] "Verily, O <s>Maitreyī</s>, when the <s>Ātman</s> has been seen" — how is it 'seen'? It is explained: first it is 'heard' (<s>śravaṇa</s>) through the teaching of the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) and scripture (<s>āgama</s>); then it is 'reflected upon' (<s>manana</s>), that is, examined through reasoning and logical demonstration.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.7-10
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.7-10]

children.text:
brahma taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmano vedān veda |
kṣatraṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ kṣatraṃ veda |
lokās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano lokān veda |
devās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano devān veda |
vedās taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano vedān veda |
bhūtāni taṃ parādur yo 'nyatrātmano bhūtāni veda |
sarvaṃ taṃ parādād yo 'nyatrātmanaḥ sarvaṃ veda |
idaṃ brahmedaṃ kṣatram ime lokā ime devā ime vedā imāni bhūtānīdaṃ sarvaṃ yad ayam ātmā || BrhUp_4,5.7 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> (the priestly class) forsakes him who knows <s>Brahman</s> as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. The <s>kṣatra</s> (the ruling class) forsakes him who knows the <s>kṣatra</s> as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. The worlds forsake him who knows the worlds as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. The gods forsake him who knows the gods as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. The <s>Vedas</s> forsake him who knows the <s>Vedas</s> as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. Beings forsake him who knows beings as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. Everything forsakes him who knows everything as different from the <s>Ātman</s>. This <s>Brahman</s>, this <s>kṣatra</s>, these worlds, these gods, these <s>Vedas</s>, these beings, this everything — all is this <s>Ātman</s>. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.7]

children.text:
sa yathā dundubher hanyamānasya na bāhyāñ chabdāñ chaknuyād grahaṇāya |
dundubhes tu grahaṇena dundubhyāghātasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ || BrhUp_4,5.8 ||
children.translated_text: Just as when a drum is being beaten, one cannot grasp the external sounds separately, but by grasping the drum or the beater of the drum, the sound is grasped — [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.8]

children.text:
sa yathā śaṅkhasya dhmāyamānasya na bāhyāñ chabdāñ chaknuyād grahaṇāya |
śaṅkhasya tu grahaṇena śaṅkhadhmasya vā śabdo gṛhītaḥ || BrhUp_4,5.9 ||
children.translated_text: Just as when a conch is being blown, one cannot grasp the external sounds separately, but by grasping the conch or the blower of the conch, the sound is grasped — [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.9]

children.text:
sa yathā vīṇāyai vādyamānāyai na bāhyāñ chabdāñ chaknuyād grahaṇāya |
vīṇāyai tu grahaṇena vīṇāvādasya vā śabdo grhītaḥ || BrhUp_4,5.10 ||
children.translated_text: Just as when a <s>vīṇā</s> is being played, one cannot grasp the external sounds separately, but by grasping the <s>vīṇā</s> or the player of the <s>vīṇā</s>, the sound is grasped — [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.10]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.7-10 tamayathārthadarśitaṃ parādātparākuryātkaivalyāsaṃbandhinaṃ kuryādayamanātmasvarūpeṇa māṃ paśyatītyaparādhāditi bhāvaḥ //4,5.7-10 //
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.7-10:] 'Forsakes him' means it would reject him, make him devoid of connection with its true nature — [thinking] 'this one sees me as something other than the <s>Ātman</s>' — such is the idea of the offence. [4.5.7-10]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.11-12
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.11-12]

children.text:
sa yathārdraidhāgner abhyāhitasya pṛthag dhūmā viniścaranty evaṃ vā are 'sya mahato bhūtasya niḥśvasitam etad yad ṛgvedo yajurvedaḥ sāmavedo 'tharvāṅgirasa itihāsaḥ purāṇaṃ vidyā upaniṣadaḥ ślokāḥ sūtrāṇy anuvyākhyānāni vyākhyānanīṣṭaṃ hutam āśitaṃ pāyitam ayaṃ ca lokaḥ paraś ca lokaḥ sarvāṇi ca bhūtāni |
asyaivaitāni sarvāṇi niśvasitāni || BrhUp_4,5.11 ||
children.translated_text: Just as from a fire kindled with damp fuel, various clouds of smoke issue forth, even so, from this great Being have been breathed forth the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the <s>Sāmaveda</s>, the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>, <s>itihāsa</s> (epics), <s>purāṇa</s> (ancient lore), <s>vidyā</s> (sciences), <s>upaniṣads</s>, <s>ślokas</s> (verses), <s>sūtras</s> (aphorisms), <s>anuvyākhyānas</s> (elucidations), <s>vyākhyānas</s> (commentaries), oblations offered, oblations poured, food given, drink given, this world and the other world, and all beings. All these are breathed forth from that [great Being]. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.11]

children.text:
sa yathā sarvāsām apāṃ samudra ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ sparśānāṃ tvag ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ gandhānāṃ nāsike ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ rasānāṃ jihvaikāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ rūpāṇāṃ cakṣur ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣaṃ śabdānāṃ śrotram ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ saṃkalpānāṃ mana ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarvāsāṃ vidyānāṃ hṛdayam ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ hastāv ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣām ānandānām upastha ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ visargāṇāṃ pāyur ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣām adhvanāṃ pādāv ekāyanam |
evaṃ sarveṣāṃ vedānāṃ vāg ekāyanam || BrhUp_4,5.12 ||
children.translated_text: Just as the ocean is the one goal of all waters, so the skin is the one goal of all touches; the nostrils are the one goal of all smells; the tongue is the one goal of all tastes; the eye is the one goal of all forms; the ear is the one goal of all sounds; the mind is the one goal of all intentions; the heart is the one goal of all forms of knowledge; the hands are the one goal of all actions; the organ of pleasure is the one goal of all joys; the organ of excretion is the one goal of all evacuations; the feet are the one goal of all travels; speech is the one goal of all <s>Vedas</s>. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.12]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.11-12 caturthe śabdaniḥśvāseneva lokādyarthaniḥśvāsaḥ sāmarthyādikto bhavatīti pṛthaṅnoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.11-12:] In the fourth [chapter, earlier], the breathing forth of objects such as the worlds was implicitly indicated by the breathing forth of words, by virtue of the capacity [of words to denote objects], and therefore was not stated separately.

children.text: iha tu sarvaśāstropa saṃhāraṃ iti kṛtvār'thaprāpto 'pyarthaḥ spaṣṭīkartavya iti pṛthagucyate //4,5.11-12 //
children.translated_text: But here, since this is the recapitulation of all the teachings, the meaning — though already arrived at [implicitly] — is to be made explicit, and so it is stated separately. [4.5.11-12]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.13]

children.text:
sa yathā saindhavaghano 'nantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsno rasaghana eva |
evaṃ vā are 'yam ātmānantaro 'bāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānaghana eva |
etebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ samutthāya tāny evānuvinayati |
na pretya saṃjñāstīty are bravīmi |
iti hovāca yājñavalkyaḥ || BrhUp_4,5.13 ||
children.translated_text: Just as a lump of salt is without interior, without exterior, entirely a mass of taste alone, even so this <s>Ātman</s> is without interior, without exterior, entirely a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>) alone. Having arisen from these elements, it disappears along with them. After departing [from the body], there is no [particular] consciousness — thus I say, said <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.13]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.13 sarvakāryapralaye vidyānimitte saindhavaghanavadanantaro 'vāhyaḥ kṛtsnaḥ prajñānadhana eka ātmāvatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: [<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.13:] Upon the dissolution of all effects, caused by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), the one <s>Ātman</s> alone remains — without interior, without exterior, entirely a mass of pure consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>), like a lump of salt.

children.text: pūrvaṃ tu bhūtamānnāsaṃsargaviśeṣallabdhaviśeṣavijñānaḥ san /
children.translated_text: Previously, however, through contact with the particular modifications of the elements, [the <s>Ātman</s>] had obtained differentiated consciousness.

children.text: tasminpravilāpite vidyayā viśeṣavijñāne tannimitte ca bhūtasaṃsarge na pretya saṃjñāstītyevaṃ yājñavalkyenoktā //4,5.13//
children.translated_text: When that differentiated consciousness is dissolved through <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), and the combination of elements that caused it [is also dissolved], there is no [particular] consciousness after departing — thus was stated by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>. [4.5.13]

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.14
children.translated_text: [Beginning of <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad</s> 4.5.14]

children.text:
sā hovāca maitreyī --
atraiva mā bhagavān mohāntam āpīpadat |
na vā aham imaṃ vijānāmīti |
sa hovāca -- na vā are 'haṃ mohaṃ bravīmi |
avināśī vā are 'yam ātmānucchittidharmā || BrhUp_4,5.14 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Maitreyī</s> said: "Here indeed, O Venerable One, you have led me to utter confusion. I do not at all understand this." He said: "Verily, I do not speak of confusion. This <s>Ātman</s> is indeed imperishable, of indestructible nature." [<s>BṛhUp</s> 4.5.14]

children.text: BrhUpBh_4,5.14 sā hovācātraiva mā bhagavānetasminnaiva vastuni prajñānaghana eva na pretya saṃjñā'stīti mohāntaṃ mohamadhyamāpīpidāpīpadadavagamitavānasi saṃsohitavānasītyarthaḥ /
ato na vā ahamimamātmānamuktalakṣaṇaṃ vijānāmi vivekata iti /
children.translated_text: "Therefore I do not at all understand this <s>Ātman</s> of the description stated above, I cannot discern it clearly."

children.text: sa hovāca nāhaṃ mohaṃ bravīmyavināśī vā are 'yamātmā yato vina(naṃ)ṣṭuṃ śīlamasyeti vināśī na vināśyavināśī vināśabdena vikriyāvināśītyavikriya ātmetyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: He said: "I do not speak of confusion. This <s>Ātman</s> is imperishable (<s>avināśī</s>) — 'avināśī' means that whose nature (<s>śīla</s>) it is not to perish (<s>vinaṣṭum</s>); it does not perish; 'avināśī' means, by the prefix 'vi-', free from all modification (<s>vikriyā</s>) — that is, the <s>Ātman</s> is without modification" — this is the meaning.

children.text: are maitreyyayamātmā prakṛto 'nucchittidharmā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] O <s>Maitreyī</s>, this self that is the topic [of discussion] is of the nature of non-annihilation (<s>anucchittidharman</s>).

children.text: ucchittiruccheda ucchedo 'nto vināśa ucchittirdharmo 'syetyucchittirardharmā nocchittidharmānucchittidharmā nāpi vikriyālakṣaṇo nāpyapacchedalakṣaṇo vīnāśo 'sya vidyata ityarthaḥ //4,5.14//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Ucchitti</s>' means destruction; destruction means end, annihilation. That whose nature (<s>dharma</s>) is <s>ucchitti</s> is called '<s>ucchittidharman</s>.' [The self is] '<s>anucchittidharman</s>' — not of the nature of annihilation. Neither does it possess a destruction characterized by modification, nor does it possess a destruction characterized by being cut off — this is the meaning. (4.5.14)

[<s>Śaṅkara's</s> commentary on 4.5.14:] She said: "Here indeed, O Venerable One, regarding this very matter — that the <s>Ātman</s> is a mass of pure consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>) alone, and that there is no consciousness after departing — you have led me to the very heart of confusion; you have bewildered me" — this is the meaning.

children.text: START BrhUp 4,5.15
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 4.5.15]

children.text:
yatra hi dvaitam iva bhavati tad itara itaraṃ paśyati, tad itara itaraṃ jighrati, tad itara itaraṃ rasayate, tad itara itaram abhivadati, tad itara itaraṃ śṛṇoti, tad itara itaraṃ manute. tad itara itaraṃ spṛśati, tad itara itaraṃ vijānāti |
yatra tv asya sarvam ātmaivābhūt tat kena kaṃ paśyet tat kena kaṃ jighret tat kena kaṃ rasayet tat kena kam abhivadet tat kena kaṃ śṛṇuyāt tat kena kaṃ manvīta tat kena kaṃ spṛśet tat kena kaṃ vijānīyāt |
yenedaṃ sarvaṃ vijānāti taṃ kena vijānīyāt |
sa eṣa neti nety ātmā |
agṛhyo na hi gṛhyate |
aśīryo na hi śīryate |
asaṅgo na hi sajyate |
asito na vyathate na riṣyati |
vijñātāram are kena vijānīyād ity uktānuśāsanāsi maitreyi |
etāvad are khalv amṛtatvam iti hoktvā yājñavalkyo vijahāra || BrhUp_4,5.15 ||
children.translated_text: For where there is duality, as it were, there one sees the other, one smells the other, one tastes the other, one speaks to the other, one hears the other, one thinks of the other, one touches the other, one knows the other. But where everything has become the self alone, then by what would one see whom? By what would one smell whom? By what would one taste whom? By what would one speak to whom? By what would one hear whom? By what would one think of whom? By what would one touch whom? By what would one know whom? By what would one know that by which all this is known? The knower — by what would one know it? This self is [described as] '<s>neti neti</s>' (not this, not this). It is ungraspable, for it is not grasped. It is indestructible, for it is not destroyed. It is unattached, for it does not attach itself. It is unfettered — it neither trembles nor is injured. 'By what would one know the knower?' — thus you have been instructed, O <s>Maitreyī</s>. This much indeed is [the means to] immortality.' Having said this, <s>Yājñavalkya</s> departed [into renunciation]. (BṛUp 4.5.15)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_4,5.15 caturṣvapi prapāṭhakeṣveka ātmā tulyo nirdhāritaḥ paraṃ brahma /
upāyaviśeṣastu tasyādhigame 'nyaścānyaśca /
upeyastu sa evā'tmā yaścaturthe 'thāta ādeśo neti netīti nirdiṣṭaḥ /
sa eva pañcame prāṇapaṇopanyāsena śākalyayājñavalkyasaṃvāde nirdhāritaḥ /
punaḥ pañcamasamāptau /
punarjanakayājñavalkyasaṃvāde /
punarihopaniṣatsamāptau /
caturṇāmapi prapāṭhakānāmetadātmaniṣṭhatā nānyo 'ntarāle kaścidapi vivakṣiter'tha ityetatpradarśanāyānta upasaṃhāraḥ sa eṣa neti netyādiḥ /
yasmātprakāraśatenāpi nirūpyamāṇe tattave neti netyātmaiva niṣṭhā nānyopalabhyate tarkeṇa vā'gamena vā tasmādetadevāmṛtatvasādhanaṃ yadetanneti netyātmaparijñānaṃ sarvasaṃnyāsaścetyetamarthamupasaṃjihīrṣannāha-etāvadetāvanmātraṃ yadetanneti netyadvaitātmadarśanamidaṃ cānyasahakārikāraṇanirapekṣamevāre maitreyyamṛtatvasādhanam /
yatpṛṣṭatyasi yadeva bhagavānveda tadeva me brūhyamṛtatvasādhanamiti tadetāvadevetu vijñeyaṃ tvayeti haivaṃ kilāmṛtatvasādhanamātmajñānaṃ priyāyai bhāryāyā uktvā saṃnyāsaparyavasānā /
etāvānupadeśa etadvedānuśāsanameṣā paramaniṣṭhaiṣa puruṣārthakartavyatānta iti /
idānīṃ vicāryate śāstrārthavivekapratipattaye /

yata ākulāni hi vākyāni dṛśyante"yāvajjīvamagnihotraṃ juhuyāt" "yāvajjīvaṃ darśapūrṇamāsābhyāṃ yajeta" "kurvanneveha karmāṇi jijīviṣecchataṃ samāḥ" "etadvai jarāmaryaṃ sarvaṃ yadagnihotram"ityādīnyaikāśramyājñāpakānyāni cā'śramāntarapratipādakāni vākyāni"viditvā vyutthāya pravrajanti" "brahmacaryaṃ samāpya gṛhī bhavedgrahādvanī bhūtvā pravrajet" "yadi vetarathā brahmacaryādeva pravrajedgṛhādvā vanādvā"iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the scriptural statements appear to be confused: 'One should offer the <s>Agnihotra</s> as long as one lives'; 'One should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> as long as one lives'; 'Performing actions here, one should wish to live a hundred years' (ĪśUp 2); 'This <s>Agnihotra</s> ritual is that which conquers old age and death' — these and such statements prescribe a single <s>āśrama</s> (life-stage). And other statements prescribe different <s>āśramas</s>: 'Having known [<s>Brahman</s>], having arisen, they renounce' (BṛUp 3.5.1); 'Having completed <s>brahmacarya</s> (studentship), one should become a householder; having been a householder, one should become a forest-dweller, and then renounce'; 'Or, alternatively, one may renounce directly from <s>brahmacarya</s>, or from the household, or from the forest' (JābUp).

children.text: "na karmaṇā na prajayā dhanena tyāgenaikemṛtatvamānaśuḥ"ityādīni /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Not by action, not by offspring, not by wealth — by renunciation alone did some attain immortality' (MahNārUp / KaivUp) — and such [statements].

children.text: tathā smṛtayaśca-"brahmacaryavānpravrajati" "aviśīrṇabrahmacaryo yamicchattamāvaseti"tasyā'śramamavikalpamekebruvate"tathā-"vaidānanadhītya brahmacaryeṇa putrapautrānicchetpāvanārthaṃ pitṛṇām /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Likewise, the <s>smṛtis</s> [say]: 'One who has maintained <s>brahmacarya</s> may renounce'; 'One whose <s>brahmacarya</s> is unbroken may remain in whichever [<s>āśrama</s>] one wishes' — for that [self], some state that the <s>āśramas</s> are without alternatives [i.e., sequential]. Likewise: 'Having studied the <s>Vedas</s> with <s>brahmacarya</s>, desiring sons and grandsons for the purification of the ancestors,

children.text: agnīnādhāya vidhivacceṣṭayajño vanaṃ praviśyātha munirbubhūṣet" //
children.translated_text: having established the [sacrificial] fires according to the prescribed rules, having performed the requisite sacrifices, one should enter the forest — and then one who wishes to become a <s>muni</s> (silent sage) [should renounce].'

[Commentary on BṛUp 4.5.15:] In all four chapters (<s>prapāṭhakas</s>), one and the same self has been equally determined as the supreme <s>Brahman</s>. But the specific means for its realization differs in each. The self that is to be realized, however, is the same one that was indicated in the fourth [chapter] as '<s>neti neti</s>' — 'now, therefore, the description: not this, not this.' That very same [self] was determined in the fifth [chapter] through the offering of <s>prāṇas</s> in the <s>Śākalya</s>-<s>Yājñavalkya</s> dialogue. Again, at the conclusion of the fifth [chapter]. Again, in the <s>Janaka</s>-<s>Yājñavalkya</s> dialogue. And again here, at the conclusion of this <s>upaniṣad</s>. That all four chapters culminate in this very self — and that no other meaning whatsoever is intended in between — to demonstrate this, there is a concluding summary [beginning with] 'This self is <s>neti neti</s>' and so forth. Since, even when the truth is examined in a hundred ways — by reasoning or by scripture — the conclusion is nothing but '<s>neti neti</s>' — the self — and nothing else is apprehended; therefore, this alone is the means to immortality — namely, this knowledge of the self as '<s>neti neti</s>' together with the renunciation of all [desires]. Wishing to conclude this meaning, [the text] says: 'This much' — just this much — namely, this vision of the non-dual self as '<s>neti neti</s>' — and this, without depending on any other auxiliary cause whatsoever — O <s>Maitreyī</s> — is the means to immortality. That which you asked — 'Whatever the venerable one knows, tell me that — the means to immortality' — that is just this much — thus it should be understood. Having thus spoken the means to immortality — the knowledge of the self — to his beloved wife, culminating in <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (renunciation) — [the text states:] this much is the instruction; this is the teaching of the <s>Veda</s>; this is the supreme culmination; this is the end of what is to be done as the highest aim of human existence. Now, [a question] is examined for the purpose of discerning the meaning of the scripture.

children.text: "prājāpatyāṃ nirupyeṣṭiṃ sarvavesadakṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: 'Having performed the <s>Prājāpatya iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice to <s>Prajāpati</s>), with all one's possessions as the sacrificial fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>),

children.text: ātmanyagnīnsamāropya brāhmaṇaḥ pravrajedgṛhāt" //
children.translated_text: having deposited the [sacrificial] fires in oneself, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should renounce from the household.'

children.text:
ityādyāḥ /
evaṃ vyutthānavikalpakramayateṣṭāśramapratipattipratāpādakāni hi śrutismṛtivākyāni śataśa upalaṃbhyanta itaretaraviruddhāni /
ācāraśca tadvidām /

tasmādeṣāṃ viṣayavibhāgajñāpanāya yathābuddhisāmarthaṃya vicārayiṣyāmaḥ /

tasyā śāstre 'dhikāro 'smiñjñeyo nānyasya kasyacit"iti /
samantrakaṃ hi yatkarma vedeneha vidhīyate tasya śmaśānāntatāṃ darśayati smṛtiḥ /

anyārthatvādvyutthānādiśrutīnām /
