kāṇakubjādayo 'pi karmaṇyanadhikṛtā anugrāhyā eva śrutyeti vyutthānādyāśramāntaravidhānaṃ nānupapannam /
pārivrājyākramavidhānasyānavakāśatvamiti cet /
na /
viśvajitsarvamedhayoryāvajjīvavidhyapavādatvāt /
yāvajjīvāgnihotrādividherviśvajitsarvamedhayorevāpavādastatra ca kramapratipattisaṃbhavo"brahmacaryaṃ samāpya gṛhī bhavedgṛhādvanī bhutvā pravrajedi"ti virodhānupapatteḥ /
na hyevaṃviṣayatve pārivrājyakamavidhānavākyasya kaścidvirodhaḥ kramapratipatteḥ /
anyaviṣayaparikalpanāyāṃ kaścidbādhaḥ /
nā'tmajñānasyāmṛtatvahetutvābhyupagamāt /
yattāvadātmetyevopāsītetyārabhya sa eṣa neti netyetadantena granthena yadupasaṃhṛtamātmajñānaṃ tadamṛtatvasādhanamityabhyupagataṃ bhavatā /
tatraitāvadevāmṛtatvasādhanamanyanirapekṣamityetanna mṛṣyate /
tatra bhavantaṃ pṛcchāmi kimarthamātmajñānaṃ marṣayati bhavāniti /
śṛṇu tatra kāraṇaṃ yathāsvargakāmasya svargaprāptyupāyamajānato 'gnihotrādi svargasādhanamabhyupagamyate tathehāpyātmajñānam /
yathā jñāpyate tatābhūtamevāmṛtatvasādhanamātmajñānamabhyupagantuṃ yuktam tulyaprāmāṇyādubhayatra /
yadyevaṃ kiṃ syāt /
sarvakarmahetūpamardakatvādātmajñānasya vidyodbhave karmanivṛttiḥ syāt /
dārāgnisaṃbaddhānāṃ tāvadagnihotrādikarmaṇāṃ bhedabuddhiviṣayasaṃpradānakārakasādhyatvam /
anyabuddhiparacchedyāṃ hyagnyādidevatāṃ saṃpradānakārakabhūtāmantreṇa na hi tatkarma nirvartyate /
yayā hi saṃpradānakārakabuddhyā saṃpradānakārakaṃ karmasādhanatvenopadiśyate seha vidyayā nivartyate"anyo 'sāvanyo 'hamasmīti na sa veda" "devāstaṃ parāduryo 'nyatrā'tmano devānveda" "mṛtyo sa mṛtyumāpnoti ya iha nāneva paśyati" "ekadhaivānudraṣṭavyaṃ sarvamātmānaṃ paśyati"ityādiśrutibhyaḥ /
na ca deśakālanimitta dyapekṣatvaṃ vyavasthitātmavastuviṣayatvādātmajñānasya /
kriyāyāstu puruṣatantratvātsyāddeśakālanimittādyepekṣatvam /
jñānaṃ tu vastutantratvānna deśakālanimittādyapekṣate /
yathāgniruṣṇa ākāśo 'mūrta iti tathā'tmavijñānamapu /
nanvevaṃ sati prāmāṇabhūtasya karvidhernirodhaḥ syāt /
na ca tulyapramāṇayoritaretaranirodho yuktaḥ /
na /
svābhāvikabhedabuddhimātranirodhakatvāt /
na hi vidhyantaranirodhakamātmajñānam svābhāvikabhedabuddhimātraṃ niruṇaddhi /
tathāpi hetvapahārātkarmānupapattervidhainirodha eva syāditi cet /
na /
kāmapratiṣedhātkāmyapravṛttinirodhavadadoṣāt /
yathā svargakāmo yajeteti svargasādhane yāge pravṛttasya kāmapratiṣevidheḥ kāme vihate kāmyayāgānuṣṭhānapravṛttirnirudhyate /
na caitāvatā kāmyavidhirniruddho bhavati /
kāmapratiṣedhavidhinā kāmyavidheranarkatvajñānātpravṛtyanupapattiriti cet /
ananuṣṭheyatve 'nuṣṭhāturabhāvādanuṣṭhānavidhyānarthakyādaprāmāṇyameva karmavidhīnāmiti cet /
na /
prāgātmajñānātpravṛtyupapatteḥ svābhāvikasya kriyākārakaphalabhedavijñānasya prāgātmajñānātkarmahetutvamupapadyata eva /
yathā kāmaviṣaye doṣavijñānotpatteḥ prākkāmyakarmapravṛttihetutvaṃ syādeva svargādīcchāyāḥ svābhāvikyāstadvāt /
tathā satyanarthārtho veda iti cet /
na /
arthānarthayorabhiprātatantratvāt /
mokṣamekaṃ varjayitvānyasyāvidyāviṣayatvāta /
puruṣābhiprāyatantrau hyārthānarthau /
maraṇādikāmyeṣṭadarśanāt /
tasmādyāvadātmajñānavidherābhimukhyaṃ tāvadeva karmavidhaya /
tasmānnā'tmajñānasahabhāvitvaṃ karmaṇāmityataḥ siddhamātmajñānamevāmṛtatvasādhanametāvadare khalvamṛtatvamiti /
karmanirapekṣatvājjñānasya /
ato viduṣastāvatpārivrājyaṃ siddhaṃ saṃpradānādikarmakārakajātyādiśūnyāvikriyabrahmātmadṛḍhapratipattimātreṇa vacanamantareṇāpyuktanyāyataḥ /
tathāca vyākhyātametat"yeṣāṃ no 'yamātmāyaṃ loka"iti hotuvacanena /
pūrve vidvāsaḥ prajāmakāmayamānā vyuttiṣṭhantīti pārivrājyaṃ viduṣāmātmalokāvabodhādeva /
tathāca vividiṣorapu siddhaṃ pārivrājyam /
"etamevā'tmānaṃ lokamicchantaḥ pravrajanti"iti vacanāt /
karmaṇāṃ cāvidvadviṣayatvamavocāma /
avidyāviṣaye cotpatyāptivikārasaṃskārthāni karmāṇītyataḥ ātmasaṃskāradvaireṇā'tmajñānasādhanatvamapi karmaṇāmavocāma yajñādibhirvividaṣantīti /
children.translated_text: And in the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), <s>karmas</s> serve the purposes of production, attainment, modification, and purification (<s>saṃskāra</s>) — therefore we have also stated that <s>karmas</s> serve as means to knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> through the purification of the <s>Ātman</s>: 'Through sacrifices and so forth, they seek to know.'

children.text: athaita satyavidviṣayāṇāmāśramakarmaṇāṃ balābalavicāraṇāyāmātmajñānotpādanaṃ prati yamapradhānānāmamānitvādīnāṃ mānasānāṃ ca dhyānajñānavairāgyādīnāṃ sannipatyopakāratvam /
children.translated_text: Now, in the investigation of the relative strength and weakness of the <s>āśrama</s>-<s>karmas</s> that pertain to the domain of the ignorant, with respect to the generation of knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>: the mental [disciplines] such as non-conceit (<s>amānitva</s>) and so forth, which are principally restraint (<s>yama</s>), together with meditation, knowledge, and dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), cooperate by coming together [to produce knowledge].

children.text: hiṃsārāgadveṣādibāhulyādbahukliṣṭakarmavimiśritā itara ityataḥ pārivrājyaṃ mumukṣūṇāṃ praśaṃsanti-"tyāga eva hi sarveṣāmuktānāmapi karmaṇām /
children.translated_text: Because the other [<s>āśramas</s>], due to the preponderance of harm, passion, hatred, and so forth, are mixed with much afflicted <s>karma</s> — therefore they commend renunciation (<s>pārivrajya</s>) for those who desire liberation: 'Renunciation alone is [the best] of all the rites that have been proclaimed.'

children.text: vairāgyaṃ punaretasya mokṣasya paramo 'vadhiḥ" //
children.translated_text: Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) is indeed the ultimate limit of this liberation.

[Commentary:] — and so forth. Thus, the statements of <s>Śruti</s> and <s>Smṛti</s> that establish the sequence of renunciation, the alternative [orders of life], and the attainment of the various <s>āśramas</s> are found by the hundreds, mutually contradictory. And the conduct of those who know [the tradition varies]. And the disagreement among those who comprehend the meaning of the scriptures is manifold, even among the learned. Therefore, the meaning of the scriptures cannot be ascertained with discrimination by those of dull intellect. Only those who have firmly established understanding of scriptural reasoning can determine the proper domain of these statements. Therefore, in order to make known the distinction of domains [of these statements], we shall investigate according to the capacity of our understanding. The meaning of the <s>Veda</s> terminates in ritual action, since the statements 'as long as one lives' and so forth in <s>Śruti</s> cannot have any other meaning. 'They burn him with the sacrificial vessels' — from the hearing of this final rite, and from the hearing [of the rule] that [life ends in] old age and death, and from the indication that 'the body ends in ashes.' For in the case of renunciation (<s>pārivrajya</s>), the body would not end in ashes. And the <s>Smṛti</s> [states:] 'He for whom a rite accompanied by <s>mantras</s> is prescribed, from the prenatal ceremony (<s>niṣeka</s>) to the cremation ground — his alone is the qualification for this scripture; no one else's.' For the <s>Smṛti</s> shows that the rite prescribed by the <s>Veda</s> with <s>mantras</s> ends at the cremation ground. And since the absence of qualification is demonstrated, it is understood that one who does not perform rituals is entirely excluded from the domain of <s>Śruti</s>. And from the prohibition against extinguishing the fire: 'He who extinguishes the fire is a slayer of the heroes among the gods.' [Objection:] But the termination of the <s>Veda's</s> meaning in ritual action is only optional, because of the prescribed renunciation and other [alternatives]. [Response:] No. Because the statements regarding renunciation and so forth have a different meaning. Since the <s>Śruti</s> statements 'As long as one lives, one offers the <s>Agnihotra</s>,' 'As long as one lives, one should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' — and so forth — have life alone as their occasion, when their meaning cannot be construed otherwise, then the statements about renunciation and so forth can be understood as pertaining to those not qualified for ritual action. And from the <s>mantra</s> text: 'Performing rites here, one should wish to live a hundred years.' And from [the statement:] 'Either by old age alone is one released from death' — since apart from old age and death there is no opportunity for separation from ritual action, the ending of ritualists at the cremation ground is not merely optional. The <s>kāṇas</s> (one-eyed), <s>kubjas</s> (hunchbacks), and others who are not qualified for ritual are indeed to be aided by <s>Śruti</s> — therefore the prescription of renunciation and other alternative <s>āśramas</s> is not untenable. [Objection:] If it be said that the sequential prescription of renunciation has no scope — [Response:] No. Because the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Sarvamedha</s> sacrifices are exceptions to the 'as long as one lives' prescription. The exception to the lifelong <s>Agnihotra</s> and other [rites] applies only to the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Sarvamedha</s>, and there the sequential attainment is possible: 'Having completed <s>brahmacarya</s>, one becomes a householder; having been a householder, one becomes a forest-dweller; having become a forest-dweller, one should renounce' — since there is no contradiction. For when this is the domain [of the prescription], there is no contradiction in the statement prescribing the sequence of renunciation, since the sequential attainment [is maintained]. The objection arises only when one tries to assign a different domain. [Response:] This is not [a problem], because of the acceptance that knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> is the cause of immortality. Now, with the passage beginning 'One should meditate: it is the <s>Ātman</s>' and concluding with 'It is not this, not this' (<s>neti neti</s>) — whatever knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> has been summarized by that text, it is accepted by you that this is the means to immortality. But that this alone is the means to immortality, independent of anything else — this [you] do not accept. In that regard, I ask you: for what reason do you accept knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>? Listen to the reason: just as for one who desires heaven, not knowing the means to attain heaven, the <s>Agnihotra</s> and so forth are accepted as means to heaven — so too here, knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>. As it is made known, so it is proper to accept knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> as the real means to immortality, since there is equal authority in both cases. [Objection:] If so, what would follow? [Response:] Since knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> destroys the causes of all <s>karma</s>, upon the arising of knowledge there would be cessation of <s>karma</s>. For rites such as the <s>Agnihotra</s>, which are connected with wife and fire, are accomplished through the recipient-agent (<s>saṃpradānakāraka</s>) that is the object of the cognition of difference. For the ritual is not completed without the <s>mantra</s> addressed to the deity such as <s>Agni</s>, conceived as a recipient-agent distinct [from the sacrificer]. And that cognition of the recipient-agent, by which the recipient-agent is taught as a means of ritual accomplishment — that is here negated by knowledge: 'He who thinks "he is other, and I am other" — he does not know'; 'The gods reject him who knows the gods as other than the <s>Ātman</s>'; 'He who sees manifoldness here obtains death after death'; 'Everything should be seen as the <s>Ātman</s> alone' — from these <s>Śruti</s> [passages]. And knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> does not depend on place, time, or occasion, because it has as its object the established reality of the <s>Ātman</s>. Ritual action, being dependent on the person [performing it], may depend on place, time, occasion, and so forth. But knowledge, being dependent on the object [known], does not depend on place, time, occasion, and so forth. Just as [one knows that] fire is hot, space is formless — so too is knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>. [Objection:] But if so, there would be the negation of the authoritative ritual prescription. And the mutual negation of two equally authoritative [injunctions] is not proper. [Response:] No. Because [knowledge] merely negates the natural cognition of difference. Knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> does not negate another prescription — it merely negates the natural cognition of difference. [Objection:] Even so, since the cause [of ritual] is removed, ritual would be impossible, and so the prescription would be negated. [Response:] No. Because it is like the cessation of desire-prompted activity through the prohibition of desire — and this is not a fault. Just as for one who desires heaven and undertakes the sacrifice as a means to heaven, when desire is negated by the prohibition of desire, the inclination to perform the desire-prompted sacrifice ceases — yet the optional prescription itself is not thereby negated. [Objection:] Since through the prohibition of desire one knows the purposelessness of the optional prescription, the inclination [to act] is impossible. [Objection:] If there is nothing to be performed, then there is no performer, and hence the injunctive prescriptions become purposeless — so there would be the very invalidity of ritual prescriptions. [Response:] No. Because the inclination [to act] is justified prior to knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>. The natural cognition of the difference between action, agent, and result — prior to knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> — does serve as a cause of <s>karma</s>. Just as the inclination toward desire-prompted ritual would exist prior to the arising of knowledge of the faults in the objects of desire, due to the natural [inclination toward] desire for heaven and so forth — so it is here. [Objection:] If so, then the <s>Veda</s> is purposely useless. [Response:] No. Because what is beneficial and what is harmful depend on one's intention. Because everything other than <s>mokṣa</s> alone is in the domain of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). For what is beneficial and what is harmful are dependent on human intention. As seen from the desire for death and other [inauspicious things]. Therefore, only as long as one is facing toward the prescription of knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>, only that long do the ritual prescriptions [apply]. Therefore, since <s>karma</s> does not coexist with knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s>, it is established that knowledge of the <s>Ātman</s> alone is the means to immortality — 'this much indeed is immortality.' Because knowledge is independent of <s>karma</s>. Therefore, for the knower, renunciation (<s>pārivrajya</s>) is established — merely through the firm conviction of the actionless, undifferentiated <s>Brahman</s>-<s>Ātman</s>, devoid of the distinctions of recipient-agent and other ritual factors, of species and so forth — even without [an explicit] verbal injunction, by the reasoning already stated. And thus this has been explained by the statement of the <s>Hotṛ</s>: 'For those whose [only] world is this <s>Ātman</s>.' The ancient sages, not desiring progeny, renounced — thus renunciation is [established] for the wise through the realization of the world of the <s>Ātman</s> alone. And likewise, for one who desires to know (<s>vividiṣu</s>), renunciation is also established — from the statement: 'Desiring this world of the <s>Ātman</s>, they renounce.' And we have stated that all <s>karmas</s> pertain to [the domain of] the ignorant.

children.text: "kiṃ te dhanena kimu bandhubhiste kiṃ te dārairbrāhmaṇa yo mariṣyasi /
children.translated_text: What use is wealth to you? What use are relatives to you? What use is a wife to you, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, who are going to die?

children.text: ātmānamanviccha guhā praviṣṭaṃ pitāmahāste kva gatāḥ pitā ca //
children.translated_text: Seek the <s>Ātman</s> who has entered the cave! Where have your grandfathers gone? And your father?

children.text:
"evaṃ sākhyayogaśāstreṣu ca saṃnyāso jñānaṃ prati pratyāsanna ucyate /
kāmapravṛttyabhāvācca /
kāmapravṛtterhi jñānapratikūlatā sarvaśāstreṣu prasiddhā /
tasmādviraktasya mumukṣorvināpi jñānena brahmacaryādeva pravrajedityādyūpapannam /
nanu sāvakāśatvādanadhikṛtaviṣayametadityuktaṃ yāvajjīvaśrutyuparodhāt /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
nitarāṃ sāvakāśatvādyāvajjīvaśrutīnām /
avadvitkāmikartavyatā hyavocāma sarvakarmaṇām /
na tu nirapekṣameva jīvananimittameva kartavyaṃ karma /
prāyeṇahi puruṣāḥ kāmabahulāḥ /
kāmaścānekaviṣayo 'nekakarmasādhanasādhyaśca /
anekaphalasādhanāni ca vaidikāni karmāṇi dārāgnisaṃbandhapuruṣakartavyānu punaḥ punaścānuṣṭhīyamānānu bahuphalānu kṛṣyādivadvarṣaśatasamāptīni ca gārhasthye vāraṇye vātastadapekṣayā yāvajjīvaśrutayaḥ /
'kurvanneveha karmāṇi' iti ca mantravarṇaḥ /
tasmiṃśca pakṣe viśvajitsarvamedhayoḥ karmaparityāgaḥ /
yasmiṃśca pakṣe yāvajjīvānuṣṭhānaṃ tadā śmaśānāntatvaṃ bhasmāntatā ca śarīrasya /
itaravarṇāpekṣayā vā yāvajjīvaśrutiḥ /
na hi kṣattriyavaiśyayo pārivrājyapratipattirasti /
tathā 'mantrairyasyodito vidhiḥ' /
'aikāśramyaṃ tvācāryā' ityevamādīnāṃ kṣatriyavaiśyāpekṣatvam /
children.translated_text: 'But the teachers [hold that there is] only one <s>āśrama</s>' — and so forth — these [statements] pertain to <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s>.

children.text: tasmātpuruśasāmarthayajñānavairāgyakāmādyapekṣayā vyutthānavikalpakramapārivrājyapripattaprakārā na virudhyante /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the modes of attaining renunciation — whether through renunciation, through alternatives, or through the sequence — do not contradict each other, depending on the person's capacity, knowledge, dispassion, and desire.

children.text: anadhikṛtānāṃ ca pṛthagvidhānātpārivrājyas 'snātako vāsnātako votsannāgniranagniko ve'tyādinā /
children.translated_text: And since for those not [otherwise] qualified, there is a separate prescription of renunciation: 'Whether a graduate (<s>snātaka</s>) or a non-graduate, whether one whose fires have been extinguished or one without fire' — and so forth.

children.text: tasmātsiddhāśramāntarāṇyadhikṛtānāmeva //4,5.15//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the other <s>āśramas</s> are established for those who are qualified. (4.5.15)

Thus in the <s>Sāṃkhya</s> and <s>Yoga</s> scriptures too, renunciation (<s>saṃnyāsa</s>) is said to be proximate to knowledge. And because of the absence of desire-prompted activity. For the opposition of desire-prompted activity to knowledge is well-known in all scriptures. Therefore, for a dispassionate person who desires liberation, even without knowledge, [the sequence] 'from <s>brahmacarya</s> itself one should renounce' and so forth is justified. [Objection:] But it has been said that this pertains to those not qualified [for ritual], since the [renunciation prescription] has scope — because of the obstruction of the 'as long as one lives' <s>Śruti</s>. [Response:] This is not a fault. Because the 'as long as one lives' <s>Śruti</s> statements have abundant scope [even without restricting renunciation]. For we have said that all <s>karmas</s> are to be performed by the ignorant who have desires. But <s>karma</s> is not to be performed merely on account of being alive, without qualification. For generally, human beings are full of desires. And desire has many objects and is accomplishable through many <s>karmas</s>. And Vedic <s>karmas</s> are means to many results, connected with wife and fire, to be performed by the qualified person — and being repeatedly performed, yielding many results, like agriculture, lasting a full hundred years — whether in the householder or forest-dweller [stage]. With reference to those, the 'as long as one lives' <s>Śruti</s> statements [apply]. And the <s>mantra</s> text: 'Performing rites here [one should wish to live a hundred years].' And in that case, the <s>Viśvajit</s> and <s>Sarvamedha</s> [involve] the relinquishment of [all] <s>karma</s>. And in the case where there is lifelong performance, then [the body] ends at the cremation ground and in ashes. Or the 'as long as one lives' <s>Śruti</s> is with reference to the other classes (<s>varṇas</s>). For <s>Kṣatriyas</s> and <s>Vaiśyas</s> have no attainment of renunciation. Likewise: 'He for whom a rite is prescribed with <s>mantras</s>.'

children.text: iti pañcamaṃ brāhmaṇam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.

children.translated_text: That (<s>adaḥ</s>) is full (<s>pūrṇa</s>); this (<s>idam</s>) is full. From the full, the full arises. Taking the full from the full, the full alone remains. <s>Kham</s> (space/ether) is <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Kham</s> is the ancient one. '<s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is the <s>kham</s> (ether)' — thus indeed <s>Kauravyāyaṇīputra</s> used to say. 'This is the <s>Veda</s> that the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> know. Through it one knows what is to be known.' (BṛUp 5.1.1)

BrhUpBh_5,1.1 pūrṇamadaḥ pūrṇaṃ na kutaścid vyāvṛttaṃ vyāpītyetat /
niṣṭhā ca kartari draṣṭavyā /
ada iti parokṣābhidhāyi sarvanāma, tatparaṃ brahmetyarthaḥ /
tat sampūrṇamākāśavad vyāpi nirantaraṃ nirupādhikaṃ ca tadevedaṃ sopādhikaṃ nāmarūpasthaṃvyavahārāpannaṃ pūrṇaṃ svena rūpeṇa paramātmanā vyāpyeva nopādhiparicchinnena viśeṣātmanā /
tadidaṃ viśeṣāpannaṃ kāryātmakaṃ brahma pūrṇāt kāraṇātmana udacyata udricyata udgacchatītyetat /
yadyapi kāryātmanodricyate tathāpi yat svarūpaṃ pūrṇatvaṃ paramātmabhāvaṃ tanna jāhāti pūrṇamevodricyate /
pūrṇasya kāryātmano brahmaṇaḥ pūrṇa pūrṇatvamādāya gṛhītvā ātmasvarūpaikarasatvamāpadya, vidyayā avidyākṛtaṃ bhūtamātropādhisaṃsargajamanyatvāvabhāsaṃ tiraskṛtya pūrṇamevānantaramavāhyaṃ prajñānaghanaikarasasvabhāvaṃ kevalaṃ brahmāvaśiṣyate /
yaduktaṃ brahma vā idamagra āsīttadātmānamevāvettasmāttatsarvamabhavadityeṣo 'sya mantrasyārthaḥ /
tatra brahmetyasyārthaḥ pūrṇamada iti /
idaṃ pūrṇamiti brahma vā idamagra āsīdityasyārthaḥ /
tathā ca śrutyantaram-"yadeveha tadamutrayadamutra tadanviha"iti /
ato 'daḥśabdavācyaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahma tadevedaṃ pūrṇaṃ kāryasthaṃ nāmarūpopādhisaṃyuktamavidyayodriktam /
tasmādeva paramārthasvarūpādanyadiva pratyavabhāsamānam /
tadyadātmānameva paraṃ pūrṇaṃ brahma viditvāhamadaḥ pūrṇaṃ brahmāsmītyevaṃ pūrṇamādāya tiraskṛtyāpūrṇasvarūpatāmavidyākṛtāṃ nāmarūpopādhisaṃparkajāmetayā brahmavidyayā pūrṇameva kevalamavaśiṣyate /
tathā coktam"tasmāttatsarvamabhavat"iti /
yaḥ sarvopaniṣadartho brahma sa eṣo 'nena mantreṇānūdyata uttarasambandhārtham /
brahmavidyāsādhanatvena hi vakṣyamāṇāni sādhanānyoṅkāradamadānadayākhyāni vidhitsitāni khilaprakaraṇasambandhātsarvopāsanāṅgabhūtāni ca /
atraike varṇayanti-pūrṇātkāraṇātpūrṇaṃ kāryamudricyate /
udriktaṃ kāryaṃ vartamānakāle 'pi pūrṇameva paramārthavastubhūtaṃ dvaitarūpeṇa /
punaḥ pralayakāle pūrṇasya kāryasya pūrṇatāmādāyā'tmani dhitvā pūrṇamevāvaśiṣyate kāraṇarūpam /
evamutpattisthitipralayeṣu triṣvapi kāleṣu kāryakāraṇayoḥ pūrṇataiva /
sā caikaiva pūrṇatā kāryakāraṇayorbhedena vyapadiśyate /
evaṃ ca dvaitādvaitātmakamekaṃ brahma /
yathā kila samudro jalataraṅgaphenabudbudādyātmaka eva /

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Who is that [<s>Brahman</s>]?

children.text: yaṃ brāhmaṇā viduroṅkārāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The one whom the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> know through <s>Oṃkāra</s> (the syllable <s>Om</s>).

children.text: brāhmaṇānāṃ hyasau praṇavodgothādivikalpairvijñeyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, that [<s>Brahman</s>] is to be known through the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Om</s>), by means of the various forms such as <s>udgītha</s> and the like.

children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For when it [<s>Om</s>] is employed as a means, the entire <s>Veda</s> is [considered to be] employed. (5.1.1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.1.1:] '<s>Pūrṇam adaḥ</s>' — 'That is full' — means: it is not excluded from anything; it is all-pervading — this is the meaning.
And the sense-completion should be understood in the agent [noun].
'<s>Adas</s>' is a pronoun of indirect reference; [it refers to] the supreme <s>Brahman</s> — this is the meaning.
That [<s>Brahman</s>] is completely full, all-pervading like space, without gaps, and without limiting adjuncts (<s>nirupādhika</s>). That very same [<s>Brahman</s>], when endowed with limiting adjuncts (<s>sopādhika</s>), abiding in names and forms, having entered into conventional transaction — [is also] full, being pervaded by the supreme self in its own essential nature, not [merely] by the self delimited by limiting adjuncts.
This very [<s>Brahman</s>], having entered into particularization, having the nature of an effect — from the full, from the causal [<s>Brahman</s>], it arises, it emerges, it comes forth — this is the meaning.
Even though it emerges as having the nature of an effect, still, its essential nature of fullness, its state as the supreme self — that it does not abandon; it emerges as full itself.
Of the full — the <s>Brahman</s> having the nature of an effect — taking, grasping the fullness, arriving at the one-flavored nature of the essential self, by knowledge (<s>vidyā</s>), setting aside the appearance of otherness born of the association with the limiting adjuncts consisting merely of the elements, produced by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) — the full alone, without interior, without exterior, whose essential nature is a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>) of one taste — <s>Brahman</s> alone remains.
This is the meaning of the <s>mantra</s>, as stated: '<s>Brahman</s> indeed was this in the beginning; it knew itself alone; from that, it became all.'
Therein, the meaning of '<s>Brahman</s>' is '<s>pūrṇam adaḥ</s>' ('that is full').
The meaning of '<s>Brahman</s> indeed was this in the beginning' is '<s>idaṃ pūrṇam</s>' ('this is full').
And another <s>śruti</s> also [says]: 'Whatever is here, that is there; whatever is there, that is here.'
Therefore, the full <s>Brahman</s> denoted by the word '<s>adas</s>' (that) — that very same is this full [<s>Brahman</s>], abiding in effects, conjoined with the limiting adjuncts of name and form, emerged through <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance),
as if appearing different from its own essential nature as the ultimate reality.
When, having known the self itself as the supreme, full <s>Brahman</s> — 'I am that full <s>Brahman</s>' — thus taking the fullness, setting aside the state of non-fullness produced by <s>avidyā</s>, born of the association with the limiting adjuncts of name and form, by this knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> — the full alone, the absolute, remains.
As it was stated: 'From that, it became all.'
The <s>Brahman</s> that is the meaning of all the <s>Upaniṣads</s> — that is restated by this <s>mantra</s>, for the purpose of connection with what follows.
For the means that are to be prescribed — called <s>oṃkāra</s>, <s>dama</s> (self-restraint), <s>dāna</s> (charity), and <s>dayā</s> (compassion) — are intended to be enjoined as subsidiary to the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, and also as auxiliaries to all meditations, because of the connection with the supplementary section (<s>khila</s>).
Here, some explain [as follows]: From the full cause, the full effect emerges.
The emerged effect, even in the present time, is full — being the ultimately real substance — in the form of duality.
Again, at the time of dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), taking the fullness of the full effect, absorbing [it] into itself, the full alone remains in the form of the cause.
Thus, in all three times — creation, existence, and dissolution — there is nothing but fullness for both cause and effect.
And this single fullness is designated differently as [belonging to] cause and effect.
Thus, <s>Brahman</s> is constituted of both duality and non-duality.
Just as the ocean is indeed constituted of water, waves, foam, bubbles, and the like.
And just as water is real, and the waves, foam, bubbles, and the like that arise from it — being of the nature of the ocean — possess the character of appearance and disappearance, [yet] are ultimately real.
Even so, all this duality is ultimately real, corresponding to waves and the like, while the supreme <s>Brahman</s> corresponds to the ocean-water.
And thus, when duality is real, the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritualistic portion) has validity. But when duality is [merely] duality-like, produced by <s>avidyā</s>, unreal like a mirage, and non-duality alone is the ultimate reality — then the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s>, because of the absence of its subject-matter, becomes invalid.
And thus there would be a contradiction:
The <s>Upaniṣads</s>, being a part of the <s>Veda</s>, are a valid means of knowledge, because they establish the ultimately real non-dual reality; [but] the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> would be invalid, because its subject — duality — is unreal.
Out of the desire to avoid this contradiction, [they say,] the <s>śruti</s> has stated this — the reality of both cause and effect, like the ocean — through '<s>pūrṇam adaḥ</s>' and so forth.
[Reply:] That is not correct.
Because neither the alternative of a qualified exception (<s>apavāda</s>) nor [the alternative of] an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) is tenable.
For this interpretation is not well-conceived.
Why?
Just as in the domain of action, an exception (<s>apavāda</s>) is made in a specific area of what was established by a general rule (<s>utsarga</s>) — for instance, 'not harming any being' is the general prohibition of <s>hiṃsā</s> (violence) regarding all beings, but in the specific context of a <s>tīrtha</s> (sacrificial occasion), in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> and the like, [violence] is permitted.
But it is not possible, in the domain of reality (<s>vastu</s>), to establish non-duality of <s>Brahman</s> as a general rule and then sublate it in a particular area.
Because, since <s>Brahman</s> is non-dual, no 'particular area' is tenable.
Likewise, the option (<s>vikalpa</s>) is also untenable.
Just as in the case of the <s>Atirātra</s> [sacrifice] — 'one takes the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s> [cup]' or 'one does not take the <s>ṣoḍaśin</s>' — the option between taking and not taking is possible because [the choice] depends on the person [performing the ritual].
But here, in the domain of reality, the option — 'it may be dual or it may be non-dual' — is not possible, because the nature of the self is not dependent on the person (<s>apuruṣatantra</s>).
And because of the contradiction of duality and non-duality in one and the same [entity].
Therefore, this interpretation is not well-conceived.
And because of the contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and reasoning.
The <s>śrutis</s> — '[the self is] like a lump of salt, a mass of consciousness of one taste, without gaps, devoid of the distinctions of prior, posterior, exterior, and interior, without exterior and interior, unborn, <s>neti neti</s>, not gross, not atomic, unborn, unaging, fearless, immortal' — all these, having definite meaning, free from doubt, error, and suspicion — would all be cast into the ocean, becoming of no effect.
Likewise, there is a contradiction with reasoning — because it is untenable for something that has parts, that is manifold, that possesses action, to be eternal.
But the eternality of the self is inferred from observation of memory (<s>smṛti</s>) and the like.
And the non-eternality [of the self on their view] would contradict that.
And the futility of their interpretation [would follow].
Moreover, on this view, the futility of the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> is evident,
because of the consequence of [the faults of] obtaining what was not done and the loss of what was done (<s>akṛtābhyāgama</s> and <s>kṛtavipraṇāśa</s>).
[Objection:] But for the duality-cum-non-duality nature of <s>Brahman</s>, examples such as the ocean and the like are available — how can you say that duality-cum-non-duality in one [entity] is contradictory?
[Reply:] No.
Because [the examples] pertain to a different domain.
For we have stated the contradiction of duality-cum-non-duality with respect to a reality that is eternal and partless — not with respect to an effect that has parts.
Therefore, because of the contradiction with <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, and reasoning, this interpretation is untenable.
For this interpretation, it would be better to simply abandon the <s>Upaniṣads</s> entirely.
And because [the <s>Brahman</s> in question] is something to be meditated upon, this interpretation is not the intended meaning of the scripture.
For a <s>Brahman</s> that is entangled with hundreds of thousands of calamities such as birth, death, and the like, that has parts like the ocean, forests, and the like, and that is of many flavors — is not taught by the <s>śruti</s> as something to be meditated upon or to be known.
But [the <s>śruti</s>] teaches that [<s>Brahman</s>] is a mass of consciousness (<s>prajñānaghana</s>).
And that 'it should be perceived as one alone.'
And because of the sublation of seeing it as manifold: 'He goes from death to death who sees as if there is diversity here.'
And what is censured by the <s>śruti</s> should not be done.
And what is not done is not the meaning of the scripture.
The manifoldness and the many-flavored nature of <s>Brahman</s>, being of the form of duality, since it is censured, should not be contemplated.
Therefore, it is not the meaning of the scripture.
But the one-flavored nature of <s>Brahman</s> — that, being something to be contemplated, is commended; and being commended, it is fit to be the meaning of the scripture.
As for the objection that the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> would be invalidated in the domain of action if duality is absent and [only] non-duality [is real] —
that is not so.
Because [the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s>] has as its purpose the instruction of [what is relevant to] the conventional level (<s>yathāprāpta</s>).
For the scripture does not first ascertain whether the reality is dual or non-dual and then instruct regarding <s>karma</s> or <s>brahmavidyā</s> to a newly born person.
Nor does duality, being amenable to instruction, [need to be taught] — because duality is apprehended by the cognition of every newly born being.
Nor could anyone initially have the cognition that duality is unreal,
such that the scripture would first teach the reality of duality and then afterwards establish the validity of the self.
Not even those initiated by heterodox systems would fail to accept the validity of scripture.
Therefore, taking duality as it is — already encountered, produced by <s>avidyā</s>, natural — and taking the natural <s>avidyā</s> itself, for a person who is endowed [with <s>avidyā</s>], who is afflicted by the defects of attachment, aversion, and the like, the scripture first teaches <s>karma</s> as the means to achieve the desired human goal.
Afterwards, for one who, having become acquainted with the defects of the established nature of action, agent, and fruit, and desiring the fruit that consists of the state of indifference — the abiding in one's own essential nature, which is the opposite of that [saṃsāra] — and seeking the means for that, [the scripture] teaches the knowledge of <s>Brahman</s> in the form of seeing the oneness of the self.
And thus, when that fruit is attained — the abiding in the state of indifference, in one's own essential nature — the validity of the scripture, its status of being of service to that [person], ceases.
Because of the absence of that [utility], the scripture-hood of the scripture also ceases for that person.
Thus, the scripture is complete for each individual person — and therefore there is not even a trace of contradiction with the scripture.
Because the duality — [consisting of] scripture, student, instruction, and the like — has its terminus in the knowledge of non-duality.
For the contradiction would arise [only] if one of the two [duality or non-duality] remained permanently — because of the mutual dependence of [the existence of] scripture, student, instruction, and the like.
But when everything is complete, neither one of them remains.
And when [all is] complete, in the non-dual, auspicious [<s>Brahman</s>] alone being established — of what [and] for whom could contradiction be suspected?
Nor indeed [is there] non-contradiction for that very reason [either — since there is no one for whom either applies].
But even granting [the opponent's position], we say: Even if <s>Brahman</s> has the nature of duality-cum-non-duality, the contradiction with the scripture is the same.
For even if <s>Brahman</s> is one alone, having the nature of duality like the ocean — 'there is nothing else' — this [statement] is contradicted.
For the one in whose domain of duality there is mutual instruction — that one is different [from <s>Brahman</s>], and duality is also something different — and thus the illustration of the ocean is contradicted.
Nor can the construction be made — as in the case of <s>Devadatta</s>, who is constituted of duality and non-duality in the form of hands and the like — that speech, being a part of <s>Devadatta</s>, is the instructor, while the ear alone is the receiver of instruction, and <s>Devadatta</s> himself is neither the instructor nor the receiver of instruction.
Because <s>Devadatta</s> is of the nature of one consciousness, like the ocean being of one water-nature.
Therefore, on this interpretation, there would be both contradiction with <s>śruti</s> and reasoning, and failure to establish the intended meaning.
Therefore, the meaning of this <s>mantra</s> '<s>pūrṇam adaḥ</s>' is exactly as we have explained it.
'<s>Oṃ khaṃ brahma</s>' — this <s>mantra</s>, being unassigned elsewhere, is here assigned by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [portion] to the act of meditation.
And here, '<s>Brahma</s>' is the term denoting what is qualified, and '<s>kham</s>' is the qualifier.
The qualifier and the qualified are expressed in co-referential predication (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>), like 'blue lotus' — '<s>khaṃ brahma</s>.' 
The word '<s>Brahman</s>,' being applicable to any great reality without specification, is therefore specified: '<s>khaṃ brahma</s>' — '<s>Brahman</s> is space.'
That <s>Brahman</s> which is space (<s>kham</s>) — that is denoted by the syllable <s>Om</s>; or, it is of the very nature of the syllable <s>Om</s> — in either case, the co-referential predication is non-contradictory.
And here, the syllable <s>Om</s> is employed as a means for the meditation on <s>Brahman</s>.
As [known] from other <s>śrutis</s>: 'This is the best support; this is the supreme support'; 'One should unite the self through <s>Om</s>'; 'Through this very syllable, one should meditate upon the supreme person'; 'Meditate upon the self through <s>Om</s> alone' — and so forth.
And because no other purpose is possible for the instruction.
Just as elsewhere — 'He chants <s>Om</s>'; 'He sings the <s>udgītha</s> with <s>Om</s>' — and in the commencement and conclusion of Vedic recitation, the use of <s>oṃkāra</s> is understood from its specific application — but no such other purpose is understood here.
Therefore, the instruction of the syllable <s>Om</s> is solely as a means of meditation.
Although the words '<s>Brahman</s>,' '<s>ātman</s>,' and the like are designators of <s>Brahman</s>, still, by the authority of the <s>śruti</s>, <s>oṃkāra</s> is the nearest, most intimate designation of <s>Brahman</s>.
For this very reason, it is the supreme means for the realization of <s>Brahman</s>.
And that [means] is of two kinds: as a symbol (<s>pratīka</s>) and as a designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>).
As a symbol — just as the different images of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and the like [serve as symbols] — so too, <s>oṃkāra</s> should be understood as [a symbol of] <s>Brahman</s>.
For thus, <s>Brahman</s> is pleased for the one who uses <s>oṃkāra</s> as a support [of meditation].
As the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'This is the best support; this is the supreme support. Knowing this support, one is honored in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.'
Therein, lest [the word] '<s>kham</s>' (space) be understood as the physical space [of the elements], [the text] says: '<s>khaṃ purāṇam</s>' — 'the ancient space' — the space that is the supreme self — this is the meaning.
That which is the space of the supreme self, the ancient space — because it is beyond the reach of the eye and the other [senses], because it is without support, because it is impossible to grasp — through faith and devotion, and through a special mental disposition, one installs [it] in <s>oṃkāra</s>,
just as the world [installs] <s>Viṣṇu</s> in an image made of stone and the like, marked with the insignia of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
'<s>Vāyuram</s>' — the son of <s>Kauravyāyaṇī</s> [said]: '<s>Kham</s>' means the space in which wind (<s>vāyu</s>) exists; wind exists in this [space]; therefore '<s>vāyuram kham</s>' — mere space, space alone — is what is meant by '<s>kham</s>,' not the 'ancient space' — thus he says.
Who is he?
The son of <s>Kauravyāyaṇī</s>.
For in the space where wind [operates], the primary conventional usage of the word [<s>kham</s>] obtains; therefore, the understanding [of <s>kham</s>] as physical space is appropriate — so he thinks.
Therein, whether '<s>kham</s>' means the ancient space, <s>Brahman</s> in its unconditioned essential nature, or the space in which wind [exists], <s>Brahman</s> as conditioned — in either case, <s>oṃkāra</s> attains its status as a means [of meditation] solely as a symbol, like an image.
As [known] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'This <s>oṃkāra</s>, O <s>Satyakāma</s>, is indeed both the higher and the lower <s>Brahman</s>.'
The only disagreement is about the meaning of its own word [<s>kham</s>].
'<s>Vedaḥ</s>' — this <s>oṃkāra</s> is the <s>Veda</s>; it is the instrument of knowing (<s>veda</s>), it knows — by this, by this designation, one knows (<s>vijānāti</s>) whatever is to be known.
Therefore, '<s>vedaḥ</s>' — <s>oṃkāra</s> is the designation, the name.
By that designation, the <s>Brahman</s> that is to be known, being illuminated, being designated — the practitioner knows, realizes, apprehends [it].
Therefore, '<s>vedaḥ</s>' — 'it is the <s>Veda</s>' — thus the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> know.
Therefore, for the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the intended [use] of <s>oṃkāra</s> as a means [is] through its being a designation.
Alternatively, '<s>vedaḥ ayam</s>' and what follows is an <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passage).
How is <s>oṃkāra</s> enjoined as a symbol of <s>Brahman</s>?
'<s>Oṃ khaṃ brahma</s>' — through the co-referential predication, its praise is now [given] by calling it '<s>veda</s>' (the <s>Veda</s>).
For this entire <s>Veda</s> is nothing but <s>oṃkāra</s>.
Having this [<s>oṃkāra</s>] as its origin, having it as its essence — the entire [<s>Veda</s>], differentiated into the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>, and the like — is nothing but <s>oṃkāra</s>. As [known] from another <s>śruti</s>: 'Just as all leaves are held together by a stalk' and so forth.
Also for this reason, this <s>oṃkāra</s> is the <s>Veda</s>: whatever is to be known — all of that, the totality of what is to be known — <s>oṃkāra</s> [itself] is the <s>Veda</s> [that knows it].
The <s>Veda</s>-hood of the other <s>Veda</s> [i.e., the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, <s>Sāman</s>] is also for this very reason.
Therefore, this <s>oṃkāra</s> is distinguished [among means] and should be adopted as the means — thus it is.
Alternatively, '<s>vedaḥ saḥ</s>' — 'it is that [same] <s>Veda</s>.' (5.1.1)

trayāḥ prājāpatyāḥ prajāpatau pitari brahmacaryam ūṣuḥ |
devā manuṣyā asurāḥ |
uṣitvā brahmacaryaṃ devā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti |
tebhyo haitad akṣaram uvāca da iti |
vyajñāsiṣṭā3 iti |
vyajñāsiṣmeti hocuḥ |
dāmyateti na āttheti |
om iti hovāca vyajñāsiṣṭeti || BrhUp_5,2.1 ||
children.translated_text: The three kinds of <s>Prajāpati's</s> offspring lived as <s>brahmacārins</s> (students) with <s>Prajāpati</s>, their father: the gods, the humans, and the <s>asuras</s> (demons). Having completed their studentship, the gods said: 'Please instruct us, sir.' To them he uttered this one syllable: '<s>Da</s>.' 'Did you understand?' 'We understood,' they said. 'You are telling us: <s>dāmyata</s> — exercise self-control.' 'Yes (<s>Om</s>),' he said, 'you have understood.' (BṛUp 5.2.1)

BrhUpBh_5,2.1 adhunā damādisādhanatrayavidhānārthoṃ'yamārambhaḥ - trayāstrisaṃkhyākāḥ prajāpatyāḥ prajāpaterapatyāni prājāpatyāste kiṃ prajāpattau pitari brahmacaryaṃ śiṣyatvavṛtterbrahmacaryasya prādhānyācchiṣyāḥ santo brahmacaryamūṣuruṣitavanta ityarthaḥ /
ke te /
viśeṣato devā manuṣyā asurāśca /
te coṣitvā brahmacaryaṃ kimakurvannityucyate - teṣāṃ devā ūcuḥ pitaraṃ prajāpatim /
kimiti /
bravītu kathayatu no 'smabhyaṃ yadanuśāsanaṃ bhavāniti /
tebhya evamarthibhyo haitadakṣaraṃ varṇamātramuvāca da iti /
uktvā ca tānpapraccha pitā kiṃ vyajñāsiṣṭā3iti /
mayopadeśārthamabhihitasyākṣarasyārthaṃ vijñātavanta āhosvinneti /
devā ūcurvyajñāsiṣmeti vijñātavanto vayam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The gods said: 'We understood' — 'We have comprehended.'

children.text: yadyevamucyatāṃ kiṃ mayoktamiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'If so, state what I said.'

children.text: devā ūcurdābhyatādāntā yūyaṃ svabhāvato 'to dāntā bhavateti no 'smānāttha kathayati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The gods said: '<s>Dāmyata</s>' — 'Be self-controlled.' 'You, being by nature unrestrained, therefore: be self-controlled' — thus you are telling us, instructing us.

children.text: itara āhomiti samyagvyajñāsiṣṭeti //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The other [<s>Prajāpati</s>] said: '<s>Om</s>' — 'Yes, you have understood correctly.' (5.2.1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.2.1:] Now, this section is commenced for the purpose of prescribing the triad of means: <s>dama</s> (self-control), and the rest. The three — three in number — <s>prājāpatyas</s>, offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s> — being students, because of the preeminence of studentship within the mode of discipleship, they lived as <s>brahmacārins</s> with <s>Prajāpati</s>, their father — they dwelt — this is the meaning. Who are they? Specifically: the gods, the humans, and the <s>asuras</s>. Having completed their studentship, what did they do? — this is stated. Among them, the gods said to their father <s>Prajāpati</s>: 'What?' 'Please instruct us, teach us — whatever instruction you have, sir.' To them, who desired thus, he uttered this single syllable — a mere letter — '<s>Da</s>.' And having uttered it, the father asked them: 'Did you understand?' — 'Did you comprehend the meaning of the syllable uttered by me for the purpose of instruction, or not?'

children.text: START BrhUp 5,2.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.2.2]

children.text:
atha hainaṃ manuṣyā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti |
tebhyo haitad evākṣaram uvāca da iti |
vyajñāsiṣṭā3 iti |
vyajñāsiṣmeti hocuḥ |
datteti na āttheti |
om iti hovāca vyajñāsiṣṭeti || BrhUp_5,2.2 ||
children.translated_text: Then the humans said to him: 'Please instruct us, sir.' To them he uttered this very same syllable: '<s>Da</s>.' 'Did you understand?' 'We understood,' they said. 'You are telling us: <s>datta</s> — give.' 'Yes (<s>Om</s>),' he said, 'you have understood.' (BṛUp 5.2.2)

children.text: BrhUpBh_5,2.2 samānamanyat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 5.2.2:] Everything else is the same [as before].

children.text: svabhāvato lubdhā yūyamato yathāśakti saṃvibhajata datteti no 'smānāttha kimanyadbrūyānno hitamiti manuṣyāḥ //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'You are by nature greedy; therefore, distribute according to your capacity — give (<s>datta</s>)' — thus you are telling us, instructing us. 'What else could you tell us that is beneficial?' — [said] the humans. (5.2.2)

children.text: START BrhUp 5,2.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.2.3]

children.text:
atha hainam asurā ūcur bravītu no bhavān iti |
tebhyo haitad evākṣaram uvāca da iti |
vyajñāsiṣṭā3 iti |
vyajñāsiṣmeti hocuḥ |
dayadhvam iti na āttheti |
om iti hovāca vyajñāsiṣṭeti |
tad etad evaiṣā daivī vāg anuvadati stanayitnur da da da iti |
damyata datta dayadhvam iti |
tad etat trayaṃ śikṣed damam dānam dayām iti || BrhUp_5,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then the <s>asuras</s> said to him: 'Please instruct us, sir.' To them he uttered this very same syllable: '<s>Da</s>.' 'Did you understand?' 'We understood,' they said. 'You are telling us: <s>dayadhvam</s> — be compassionate.' 'Yes (<s>Om</s>),' he said, 'you have understood.' That is what the divine voice, the thunder, repeats: '<s>Da Da Da</s>' — meaning: <s>dāmyata</s> (be self-controlled), <s>datta</s> (give), <s>dayadhvam</s> (be compassionate). Therefore, one should learn this triad: self-control (<s>dama</s>), charity (<s>dāna</s>), and compassion (<s>dayā</s>). (BṛUp 5.2.3)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,2.3 tathāsurā dayadhvamiti /
krūrā yūyaṃ hiṃsādiparā ato dayadhvaṃ prāṇiṣu dayāṃ kuruteti /
tadetatprajāpateranuśāsanamadyāpyanuvartata eva /
yaḥ pūrvaṃ prajāpatirdevādīnanuśaśāsa so 'dyāpyanuśāstyeva daivyā stanayitnulakṣaṇayā vācā kathameṣā śrūyate daivo vāk /
kāsau stanayitnurda da da iti dāmyata datta dayadhvamityeṣāṃ vākyānāmupalakṣaṇāya trirdakāra uccāryate 'nukṛtirna tu stanayitnuśabdastrireva saṃkhyāniyamasya loko 'prasiddhatvāt /
yasmādadyāpi prajāpatirdāmyata datta dayadhvamityanuśāstyeva tasmātkāraṇādetattrayam /
kiṃ tat trayamityucyate damaṃ dānaṃ dayāmiti śikṣedupādadyātprajāpateranuśāsanamasmābhiḥ kartavyamityevaṃ kartavyamityevaṃ matiṃ kuryāt /
tathā ca smṛtiḥ - trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśatamātmanaḥ /
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetat trayaṃ tyajet iti /
asya hi vidheḥ śeṣaḥ pūrvaḥ /
tathāpi devādīnuddiśya kimarthaṃ dakāratrayamuccāritavānprajāpatiḥ pṛthaganuśāsanārthibhyaḥ /
te vā kathaṃ vivekena pratipannāḥ prajāpatermanogataṃ samānenaiva dakāravarṇamātreṇeti parābhiprāyajñā vikalpayanti /
atraika āhuradāntatvādānātvādayāsutvairaparādhitvamātmano manyamānāḥ śaṅkitā eva prajāpatāvūṣuḥ kiṃ no vakṣyatīti /
teṣāṃ ca dakāraśravaṇamātrādevā'tmāśaṅkāvaśena tadarthapratipattirabhūt /
loke 'pi hi prasiddhaṃ putrāḥ śiṣyāścānuśāsyāḥ santo doṣānnivartayitavyā iti /
ato yuktaṃ prajāpaterdakāramātroccāraṇam /
damāditraye ca dakārānvayādātmano doṣānurūpyeṇa devādīnāṃ vivekena pratipattuṃ ceti /
phalaṃ tvetadātmadoṣajñāne sati doṣānnivartayituṃ śakyate 'lpenāpyupadeśena dakāramātreṇeti /
nanvetat trayāṇāṃ devādīnāmanuśāsanaṃ devādibhirapyekaikamevopādeyamadyatve 'pi na tu trayaṃ manuṣyaiḥ śikṣitavyamiti /
atrocyate - pūrvairdaivādibhirapyekaikamevopādeyamadyatve 'pi na tu trayaṃ manuṣyaiḥ śikṣitavyamiti /
athavā na devā asurā vānye kecana vidyante manuṣyebhyaḥ /

manuṣyāṇāmevādāntā ye 'nyairuttamairguṇaiḥ saṃpannāste devā lobhapradhānā manuṣyāstathā hiṃsāparāḥ krūrā asurāsta eva manuṣyā adāntatvādidoṣakṣatrayamapekṣya devādiviśabdabhājo bhavantītarāṃśca guṇānsattvarajastamāṃsyapekṣya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Or alternatively, gods, <s>asuras</s>, and others are not different beings from humans. Rather, among humans alone, those who are unrestrained but endowed with other excellent qualities are the gods; those who are predominantly greedy are the humans [in this classification]; and those who are devoted to cruelty and violence are the <s>asuras</s>. These very humans, when classified with reference to the three faults of lack of restraint and the rest, become worthy of the designations 'gods' and the like; and with reference to the other qualities of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: ato manuṣyaireva śikṣitavyametat trayamiti tadapekṣayaiva prajāpatinopadiṣṭatvāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, it is by humans alone that this triad is to be practiced — because <s>Prajāpati's</s> instruction was given with reference to them.

children.text: tathā hi manuṣyaḥ adāntā lubdhāḥ krūrāśca dṛśyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For indeed, humans are seen to be unrestrained, greedy, and cruel.

children.text: tathā ca smṛtiḥ kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetat trayaṃ tyajet iti //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And thus the <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'Desire, anger, and greed — therefore one should abandon this triad' (BhG 16.21). (5.2.3)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.2.3:] Likewise, the <s>asuras</s> [understood]: '<s>Dayadhvam</s>' — 'Be compassionate.' 'You are cruel and devoted to causing harm; therefore, <s>dayadhvam</s> — have compassion toward all creatures, show mercy.' This instruction of <s>Prajāpati</s> continues even now. The same <s>Prajāpati</s> who instructed the gods and the rest in ancient times continues to instruct even now through the divine voice characterized by thunder. How is this divine voice heard? What is that thunder? '<s>Da Da Da</s>' — the syllable '<s>Da</s>' is uttered three times as a representation of the sentences '<s>Dāmyata</s>, <s>datta</s>, <s>dayadhvam</s>' — it is an imitation [of the teaching], not that thunder actually utters [the syllable] exactly three times, since the world is not familiar with a fixed threefold count [of thunderclaps]. Because <s>Prajāpati</s> continues even now to instruct thus — '<s>dāmyata</s>, <s>datta</s>, <s>dayadhvam</s>' — therefore, for this reason, this triad — what is that triad? — it is said: one should learn, one should adopt — self-control (<s>dama</s>), charity (<s>dāna</s>), and compassion (<s>dayā</s>) — from the instruction of <s>Prajāpati</s>, [thinking:] 'This is our obligation.' And thus the <s>smṛti</s> [says]: 'Threefold is this gate of hell, destructive of the self — desire, anger, and greed; therefore one should abandon this triad' (BhG 16.21). For this injunction [of <s>dama</s>, <s>dāna</s>, <s>dayā</s>] is the complement of that [prohibition]. Even so, why did <s>Prajāpati</s> utter the syllable '<s>Da</s>' three times, when each group — the gods and the rest — sought separate instruction? And how did they, with discernment, understand <s>Prajāpati's</s> intention from the same single syllable '<s>Da</s>'? They being perceivers of another's intention, [they] interpreted [the teaching] with discrimination. Some [commentators] say regarding this: knowing their own faults of being unrestrained, uncharitable, and uncompassionate — regarding them as offenses — the [gods and the rest] dwelt with <s>Prajāpati</s> in a state of apprehension: 'What will he say to us?' And upon merely hearing the syllable '<s>Da</s>', through the force of their self-doubt, the understanding of its meaning occurred. For it is well known in the world that sons and students, being instructable, are to be corrected of their faults. Therefore, <s>Prajāpati's</s> utterance of merely the syllable '<s>Da</s>' is fitting. And in the triad of <s>dama</s> and the rest, [each beginning with] the syllable '<s>Da</s>', each [group] understood with discernment in accordance with their own particular fault. And the fruit of this is: when there is knowledge of one's own faults, one is able to correct those faults even with the slightest instruction — merely [hearing] the syllable '<s>Da</s>.' [Objection:] But this instruction of the three — the gods and the rest — [implies that] each [group] should adopt only one [virtue]; however, all three should be practiced by humans. [Reply:] To this it is said: even those earlier [groups] — the gods and the rest — should adopt only one [virtue] each, even in the present time; nevertheless, all three are not to be practiced [only] by humans.

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya dvitīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //2//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s>. (5.2)

children.text: START BrhUp 5,3.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.3.1]

children.text:
eṣa prajāpatir yad dhṛdayam |
etad brahma |
etat sarvam |
tad etat tryakṣaraṃ hṛdayam iti |
hṛ ity ekam akṣaram |
abhiharanty asmai svāś cānye ca ya evaṃ veda |
da ity ekam akṣaram |
dadaty asmai svāś cānye ca ya evaṃ veda |
yam ity ekam akṣaram |
eti svargaṃ lokaṃ ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,3.1 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Prajāpati</s> is the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>). This is <s>Brahman</s>. This is all. This [word '<s>hṛdaya</s>'] consists of three syllables: '<s>hṛ</s>' is one syllable — his own people and others bring [offerings] to one who knows thus. '<s>Da</s>' is one syllable — his own people and others give to one who knows thus. '<s>Yam</s>' is one syllable — one who knows thus goes to the heavenly world. (BṛUp 5.3.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,3.1 damādisādhanatrayaṃ sarvopāsanaśeṣaṃ vihitam /
dānto 'lubdho dayāluḥ sansarvopāsaneṣvadhikriyate /
tatra nirupādhikasya brahmaṇo darśanamatikrāntamathādhunā sopādhikasya tasyaivābhyudayaphalāni vaktavyānītyevamartho 'yamārambhaḥ eṣa prajāpatiryaddhṛśyaṃ prajāpatiranuśāstītyanantaramevābhihitam /
kaḥ punarasāvanuśāstā prajāpatiriti /
ucyate - eṣa prajāpatiḥ /
ko 'sau yathṛdayaṃ hṛdayamiti hṛdayasthā buddhirucyate /
yasmiñśākalyabrāhmaṇānte nāmarūpakarmaṇāmupasaṃhāra ukto digvibhāgadvāreṇa tadetatsarvabhūtapratiṣṭhaṃ sarvabhūtātmabhūtaṃ hṛdayaṃ prajāpatiḥ prajānāṃ sraṣṭā /
etadbrahma bṛhattvātsarvātmatvācca brahma /
etat sarvam /
uktama pañcamādhyāye hṛdayasya sarvatvam /
tatsarvaṃ yasmāttasmādupāsyaṃ hṛdayaṃ brahma /
tatra hṛdayanāmākṣaraviṣayameva tāvadupāsanamucyate /
tadetaddhṛdayamiti nāma tryakṣaraṃ trīṇyakṣarāṇyasyeti tryakṣaram /
kāni punastāni trīṇyakṣarāṇyucyante /
hṛ ityekamakṣaram /
abhiharanti hṛterāhṛtikarmaṇo hṛ ityetadrūpamiti yo veda yasmāddhṛdayāya brahmaṇe svāścendriyāṇyanye ca viṣayāḥ śabdādayaḥ svaṃ svaṃ kāryamabhiharantihṛdayaṃ ca bhoktrarthamabhiharati /
ato hṛdayanāmno hṛ ityetadakṣaramiti yo vedāsmai viduṣe 'bhiharanti svāśca jñātayo 'nye cāsaṃbaddhāḥ /
balimiti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
vijñānānurūpyeṇaitatphalam /
tathā da ityetadapyekākṣarametadapi dānārthasya dadāterda ityetadrūpaṃ hṛdayanāmākṣaratvena nibaddham /
atrāpi hṛdayāya brahmaṇo svāśca karaṇānyanye ca viṣayāḥ svaṃ svaṃ vīryaṃ dadati hṛdayaṃ ca bhoktre dadāti svaṃ vīryamato dakāra ityevaṃ yo vedāsmai dadati svāścānye ca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here too, to this <s>Brahman</s> called the heart, his own faculties — the senses — and others — the sense-objects — give their respective power; and the heart too gives its own power to the experiencer. Therefore, [one who knows:] '<s>Da</s>' is the syllable — thus one who knows; to this knower, his own people and others give.

children.text: tathā yamityetadapyekamakṣaram /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Likewise, '<s>yam</s>' is also a single syllable.

children.text: iṇo gatyarthasya yamityetadrūpamasminnāmni nibaddhamiti yo veda sa svargaṃ lokameti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From the root '<s>iṇ</s>' meaning 'to go,' '<s>yam</s>' is its form, bound in this name — thus one who knows; he goes to the heavenly world.

children.text: evaṃ nāmākṣarādapīdṛśaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prāpnoti kimu vaktavyaṃ hṛdayasvarūpo pāsanāditi hṛdayastutaye nāmākṣaropanyāsaḥ //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, even from the mere syllables of the name [<s>hṛdaya</s>], such a distinguished fruit is obtained — how much more, then, from the meditation on the essential nature of the heart! — [this] is stated as a praise of the heart through the presentation of the syllables of the name. (5.3.1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.3.1:] The triad of means — <s>dama</s> and the rest — has been prescribed as subsidiary to all meditations. One who is self-controlled, non-greedy, and compassionate is qualified for all meditations. Therein, the vision of the unconditioned <s>Brahman</s> has already been treated. Now, the meditations on <s>Brahman</s> with limiting adjuncts (<s>sopādhika</s>), which yield results pertaining to worldly prosperity (<s>abhyudaya</s>), are to be stated — this is the purpose of this section's commencement. 'This <s>Prajāpati</s> is the heart' — <s>Prajāpati</s> instructs — this was stated immediately preceding. Who is that instructor <s>Prajāpati</s>? It is said: this <s>Prajāpati</s>. Who is he? The heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) — by '<s>hṛdaya</s>' is meant the intellect (<s>buddhi</s>) stationed in the heart. In which — at the conclusion of the <s>Śākalya brāhmaṇa</s> — the dissolution of name, form, and action was stated through the gateway of the directions [of space] — that [heart-intellect], being the abode of all beings and being the self of all beings, [that] heart is <s>Prajāpati</s>, the creator of beings. This is <s>Brahman</s> — because of its greatness and because of its being the self of all, it is <s>Brahman</s>. This is all — the totality of the heart was stated in the fifth <s>adhyāya</s>. Since it is all, therefore the heart is to be meditated upon as <s>Brahman</s>. Therein, a meditation pertaining to the mere syllables of the name '<s>hṛdaya</s>' is first stated. This — '<s>hṛdaya</s>' — the name, consists of three syllables (<s>tryakṣara</s>) — three syllables are its [components], hence '<s>tryakṣara</s>.' What are those three syllables? — they are stated. '<s>Hṛ</s>' is one syllable. They bring (<s>abhiharanti</s>) — from the root '<s>hṛ</s>' meaning 'to bring' — '<s>hṛ</s>' is its form — thus one who knows. Because to this <s>Brahman</s> called the heart, his own [faculties] — the senses — and others — the sense-objects such as sound and the like — each bring their respective function; and the heart too brings [everything] for the sake of the experiencer. Therefore, '<s>hṛ</s>' is this syllable of the name '<s>hṛdaya</s>' — thus one who knows; to this knower, his own relatives and others unrelated bring — '<s>bali</s>' (tribute) is the complement of the sentence. The fruit [of this knowledge] corresponds to the knowledge. Likewise, '<s>da</s>' — this too is a single syllable; this also, belonging to the root '<s>dadāti</s>' (to give), has '<s>da</s>' as its form, bound as a syllable of the name '<s>hṛdaya</s>'.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya tṛtīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //3//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the blessed <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s>. (5.3)

children.text: START BrhUp 5,4.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.4.1]

children.text:
tad vai tad etad eva tad āsa |
satyam eva |
sa yo haitaṃ mahad yakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti jayatīmāṃl lokān -- jita in nv asāv asat -- ya evam etan mahad yakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti |
satyaṃ hy eva brahma || BrhUp_5,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: That — verily, that — was this [<s>Brahman</s>]: it was <s>Satya</s> (truth) indeed. He who knows this great, first-born being (<s>yakṣa</s>) as '<s>Satya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — he conquers these worlds. 'Would that [enemy of his] be defeated?' — indeed, he who is unreal (<s>asat</s>) would be [defeated] — for one who thus knows this great, first-born being as '<s>Satya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' For <s>Satya</s> (truth) indeed is <s>Brahman</s>. (BṛUp 5.4.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,4.1 tasyaiva hṛdayākhyasya brahmaṇaḥ satyamityupāsanaṃ vidhitsannāha-tattaditi hṛdayaṃ brahma parāmṛṣṭam /
vā iti smaraṇārtham /
tadyaddhṛdayaṃ brahma smaryata ityekastacchabdaḥ /
tadetaducyate prakārāntaremeti dvitīyastacchabdaḥ /
kiṃ punastatprakārāntaram /
etadeva tadityetacchabdena saṃbadhyate tṛtīyastacchabdaḥ /
etaditi vakṣyamāṇaṃ buddhau saṃnidhīkṛtyā'ha /
āsa babhūva /
kiṃ punaretadevā'sa yaduktaṃ hṛdayaṃ brahmeti taditi tṛtīyastacchabdo viniyuktaḥ /
kiṃ taditi viśeṣato nirdiśati satyameva sacca tyacca mūrtaṃ cāmūrtaṃ ca satyaṃ brahma pañcabhūtātmakamityetat /
sa yaḥ kaścitsatyātmānametaṃ mahanmahattvādyakṣaṃ pūjyaṃ prathamajaṃ prathamajātaṃ sarvasmātsaṃsāriṇa etadevāgre jātaṃ brahmātaḥ prathamajaṃ veda vijānāti satyaṃ brahmeti /
tasyedaṃ phalamucyate-yathā satyena brahmaṇeme lokā ātmasātkṛtā jitā evaṃ satyātmānaṃ brahma mahadyakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda sa jayatīmāllokān /
kiñca jito vaśīkṛta innvitthaṃ yathā brahmaṇāsau śatruriti vākyaśeṣaḥ /
asaccāsadbhavedasau śatrurjito bhavedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'And that enemy would become <s>asat</s> (non-existent)' — meaning: the enemy would be defeated — this is the meaning.

children.text: kasyaitatphalamiti punarnigamayati-ya evametanmahadyakṣaṃ prathamajaṃ veda satyaṃ brahmeti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For whose benefit is this fruit? — [the text] reaffirms: one who thus knows this great being, the first-born, as '<s>Satya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: ato vidyānurūpaṃ phalaṃ yuktam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the fruit is appropriate to the knowledge.

children.text: satyaṃ hyeva yasmādbrahma //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For <s>Satya</s> (truth) indeed is <s>Brahman</s>. (5.4.1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.4.1:] Wishing to prescribe the meditation on <s>Satya</s> (truth) for this very <s>Brahman</s> known as the heart, [the text] says: '<s>Tat</s>' (that) — 'that' refers back to the heart-<s>Brahman</s>. '<s>Vai</s>' is for the purpose of recollection. '<s>Tat</s>' — since 'that heart-<s>Brahman</s>' is recalled — this is the first [occurrence of] the word '<s>tat</s>.' '<s>Tat</s>' — 'that which is being stated in another way' — this is the second [occurrence of] the word '<s>tat</s>.' What, then, is that other way? '<s>Etad</s>' (this) — connected by the word '<s>etad</s>' — this is the third [occurrence of] the word '<s>tat</s>.' '<s>Etad</s>' — having made present in the intellect what is about to be stated, [the text] says. '<s>Āsa</s>' — [it] was. What, then, is this that was — which was stated as 'the heart is <s>Brahman</s>' — '<s>tat</s>' — for this, the third [occurrence of] the word '<s>tat</s>' is employed. What is that? — [the text] specifically indicates: <s>Satya</s> (truth) indeed — <s>sat</s> (being) and <s>tyat</s> — the formed and the formless — <s>Satya</s>, the <s>Brahman</s> consisting of the five elements — this is the meaning. He who — whoever — knows this <s>Brahman</s> as having the nature of <s>Satya</s>, as the great being (<s>mahat</s>) — great because of its greatness — <s>yakṣa</s> — worthy of worship — first-born (<s>prathamaja</s>) — born first, before all <s>saṃsāric</s> beings; this very [<s>Brahman</s>] was born first, and from that everything else — therefore, 'first-born' — one who knows [it] as '<s>Satya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' The fruit of this [knowledge] is stated: just as the worlds have been mastered, made one's own, conquered by <s>Brahman</s> whose nature is <s>Satya</s> — even so, one who knows <s>Brahman</s> as the great being, the first-born, whose nature is <s>Satya</s> — he conquers these worlds. And furthermore — conquered, subdued — indeed, verily so — [his] enemy — would be [defeated] — this is the completion of the sentence.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya caturthaṃ brāhmaṇam //4//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the blessed <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. //4//

children.text: START BrhUp 5,5.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.1]

children.text:
āpa evedam agra āsuḥ |
tā āpaḥ satyam asṛjanta |
satyaṃ brahma |
brahma prajāpatim |
prajāpatir devān |
te devāḥ satyam evopāsate |
tad etat tryakṣaraṃ sa-ti-yam iti sa ity ekam akṣaram |
tīty ekam akṣaram |
yam ity ekam akṣaram |
prathamottame akṣare satyam madhyato 'nṛtam |
tad etad anṛtam ubhayataḥ satyena parigṛhītam |
satyabhūyam eva bhavati |
naivaṃvidvāṃsam anṛtaṃ hinasti || BrhUp_5,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Waters alone were this [universe] in the beginning. Those waters created <s>Satya</s> (Truth). <s>Satya</s> is <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Brahman</s> [created] <s>Prajāpati</s>. <s>Prajāpati</s> [created] the gods. Those gods meditate on <s>Satya</s> alone. That [word <s>satya</s>] has three syllables: sa-ti-yam. 'Sa' is one syllable, 'ti' is one syllable, 'yam' is one syllable. The first and last syllables are truth; in the middle is untruth. This untruth is enclosed on both sides by truth. It becomes predominantly truth. Untruth does not harm one who knows thus. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.1 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,5.1 satyasya brahmaṇaḥ stutyarthamidamāha /
mahadyakṣaṃ prathamajamityuktaṃ tatkathaṃ prathamajatvamiti /
ucyate-āpa evedamagra āsuḥ /
āpa iti karmasamavāyinyo 'gnihotrādyāhutayaḥ /
agnihotrādyāhiterdravātmakatvādaptvam /
tāścā'po 'gni hotrādikarmāpavargottarakālaṃ kenaciddṛṣṭena sūkṣmeṇā'tmanā karmasamavāyitvamaparityajantya itarabhūtasahitā eva na kevalāḥ /
karmasamavāyitvāttu prādhānyamapāmiti /
sarvāṇyeva bhūtāni prāgutpatteravyākṛtāvasthāni kartṛsahitāni nirdiśyanta āpa iti /
tā āpo bījabhūtā jagato 'vyākṛtātmanāvasthitāstā evedaṃ sarvaṃ nāmarūpavikṛtaṃ jagadagra āsurnānyatkiñcidvikārajātamāsīt /
tāḥ punarāpaḥ satyamasṛjanta /
tasmātsatyaṃ brahma prathamajam /
tadetaddhiraṇyagarbhasya sūtrātmano janma yadavyākṛtasya jagato vyākaraṇam /
tatsatyaṃ brahma kutaḥ /
mahattvāt /
kathaṃ mahattvamityāha /
yasmātsarvasya sraṣṭṭa /
katham /
yatsatyaṃ brahma tat prajāpatiṃ prajānāṃ patiṃ virājaṃ sūryādikaraṇamasṛjatetyanuṣaṅgaḥ /
prajāpatirdevānsa virāṭprajāpatirdeva nasṛjata /
yasmātsarvamevaṃ krameṇa satyādbrahmaṇo jātaṃ tasmānmahatsatyaṃ brahma /
kathaṃ punaryakṣamiti /
ucyate-ta evaṃ sṛṣṭā devāḥ pitaramapi virājamatītya tadeva satyaṃ brahmopāmate /
ata etatprathamajaṃ mahadyakṣam /
tasmātsarvātmanopāsyaṃ tattasyāpi satyasya brahmaṇo nāma satyamiti tadetattryakṣaram /
kāni tānyakṣarāṇītyāha-sa ityekamakṣaram /
tītyekamakṣaram /
tītīkārānubandho nirdeśārthaḥ /
yamityekamakṣaram /
tatra teṣāṃ prathamottame akṣare sakārayakārau satyam /
mṛtyurūpābhāvāt /
madhyato madhye 'nṛtam /
anṛtaṃ hi mṛtyuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For untruth is death.

children.text: mṛtyvanṛtayostakārasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the commonality of the letter 'ta' between death (<s>mṛtyu</s>) and untruth (<s>anṛta</s>).

children.text: tadetadanṛtaṃ takārākṣaraṃ mṛtyurūpamubhayataḥ satyena sakārayakāralakṣaṇena parigṛhotaṃvyāptamantarbhāvitaṃ satyarūpābhyāmato 'kiñcitkaraṃ tatsatyabhūyameva satyabāhulyameva bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This untruth, characterized by the syllable 'ta,' having the form of death, is enclosed on both sides — pervaded, absorbed — by truth characterized by the syllables 'sa' and 'ya'; therefore it is rendered powerless. It becomes predominantly truth — that is, truth is overwhelmingly predominant.

children.text: evaṃ satyabāhulyaṃ sarvasya mṛtyoranṛtasyākiñcitkaratvaṃ ca yo vidvāṃstamevaṃ vidvāṃsamanṛtaṃ kadācitpramādoktaṃ na hinasti //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One who knows this predominance of truth and the powerlessness of all death and untruth — such a knower is not harmed by untruth, even if spoken through negligence. //1//

[Commentary:] This is stated for the purpose of praising <s>Satya Brahman</s> (Truth-Brahman). It was said 'the great being, the first-born' — how is it first-born? It is answered: 'Waters alone were this [universe] in the beginning.' 'Waters' means the oblations such as <s>Agnihotra</s> and other rituals that are conjoined with <s>karma</s>. Their nature as 'waters' is because the <s>Agnihotra</s> and other offerings are of liquid form. And those waters — the <s>Agnihotra</s> and other ritual actions — after the conclusion of their results, by some unseen subtle essence, without abandoning their conjunction with <s>karma</s>, exist combined with other elements, not alone. But due to their conjunction with <s>karma</s>, the waters have predominance. All beings in their undifferentiated state prior to creation, together with the agent, are denoted as 'waters.' Those waters, being the seed of the universe, remaining in their undifferentiated form — they alone were this entire world of names and forms in the beginning; no other modification existed. Those waters then created <s>Satya</s> (Truth). Therefore <s>Satya Brahman</s> is first-born. This birth of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the <s>Sūtrātman</s>, is the differentiation of the undifferentiated universe. That <s>Satya</s> is <s>Brahman</s> — why? Because of its greatness. How is it great? He says: because it is the creator of all. How? That <s>Satya Brahman</s> created <s>Prajāpati</s>, the lord of creatures, <s>Virāj</s>, the instrument of the sun and other [cosmic bodies] — this is the continuation. '<s>Prajāpati</s> [created] the gods' — that <s>Virāj</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, created the gods. Since everything was thus born in succession from <s>Satya Brahman</s>, therefore <s>Satya Brahman</s> is great. But how is it a 'being' (<s>yakṣa</s>)? It is answered: those gods, thus created, surpassing even their father <s>Virāj</s>, meditate on that very <s>Satya Brahman</s>. Hence it is the first-born, the great being. Therefore it should be meditated upon with one's entire being. The name of that <s>Satya Brahman</s> too is explained —

children.text: START BrhUp 5,5.2
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.2]

children.text:
tad yat tat satyam asau sa ādityaḥ |
ya eṣa etasmin maṇḍale puruṣo yaś cāyaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣas tāv etāv anyo 'nyasmin pratiṣṭhitau |
raśmibhir eṣo 'smin pratiṣṭhitaḥ prāṇair ayam amuṣmin |
sa yadotkramiṣyan bhavati śuddham evaitan maṇḍalaṃ paśyati |
nainam ete raśmayaḥ pratyāyanti || BrhUp_5,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: Now, that which is <s>Satya</s> (Truth) — that is the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). The <s>puruṣa</s> (person) who is in that solar disc and the <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the right eye — these two are established in each other. The former is established in the latter through rays; the latter in the former through <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths). When one is about to depart [from the body], one sees this disc as pure and clear. Those rays no longer come to one. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.2 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,5.2 asyādhunā satyasya brahmaṇaḥ saṃsthānaviśeṣa upāsanamucyate-tadyat /
kiṃ tatsatyaṃ brahma prathamajaṃ kimasau saḥ /
ko 'sāvādityaḥ kaḥ punarasāvādityo ya eṣa ka eṣa ya etasminnādityamaṇḍale puruṣo 'bhimānī so 'sau satyaṃ brahma /
yaścāyamadhyātmaṃ yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣannakṣaṇi puruṣaḥ /
caśabdātsa ca satyaṃ brahmeti saṃbandhaḥ /
tāvetāvādityākṣisthau puruṣāvekasya satyasya brahmaṇaḥ saṃsthānaviśeṣau yasmāttasmādanyonyasminnitaretarasminnādityaścākṣuṣe cākṣuṣaścā'ditye pratiṣṭhitau /
adhyātmādhidaivatayoranyonyopakāryopakārakatvāt /
kathaṃ pratiṣṭhitāvityucyate raśmibhiḥ prakāśenānugrahaṃ kurvanneṣa ādityo 'smiṃścākṣuṣe 'dhyātme pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
ayaṃ ca cākṣuṣaḥ prāṇairādityamanugṛhṇannamuṣminnāditye 'dhidaive pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
so 'smiñcharīre vijñānamayo bhoktā yadā yasminkāla utkramiṣyanbhavati tadāsau cākṣuṣa ādityapuruṣo raśmīnupasaṃhṛtya kevalenaudāsīnyena rūpeṇa vyavatiṣṭhate /
tadāyaṃ vijñānamayaḥ paśyati śuddhameva kevalaṃ viraśmyetanmaṇḍalaṃ candramaṇḍalamiva /
tadetadariṣṭadarśanaṃ prāsahgikaṃ pradarśayate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He incidentally shows this sign of approaching death (<s>ariṣṭa-darśana</s>).

children.text: kathaṃ nāma puruṣaḥ karaṇīye yatnavānsyāditi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] So that a person may be diligent in what ought to be done.

children.text: nainaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ puruṣamurarīkṛtya taṃ pratyanugrahāyaite raśmayaḥ svāmikartavyavaśātpūrvamāgacchanto 'pi punastatkarmakṣayamanurudhyamānā iva nopayanti na pratyāgacchantyenam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Those rays, having previously come to favor the ocular <s>puruṣa</s> at the behest of their master, no longer approach him — they do not return to him — as if conforming to the exhaustion of his <s>karma</s>.

children.text: ato 'vagamyate parasparopakāryopakārakabhāvātsatyasyaivaikasyā'tmanoṃ'śā vetāviti //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From this it is understood that these two [<s>puruṣas</s>] are portions of the one <s>Satya</s> (<s>Ātman</s>) alone, because of their mutual relationship as benefactor and beneficiary. //2//

[Commentary:] Now a particular form of meditation on this <s>Satya Brahman</s> is taught: 'Now, that which —' What is that <s>Satya Brahman</s>, the first-born? What is 'that'? It is the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). Who then is this <s>Āditya</s>? Who is 'this one'? The <s>puruṣa</s> who presides over that solar disc — he is that <s>Satya Brahman</s>. And this one in the individual self — the <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the right eye. The word 'ca' (and) connects: he too is <s>Satya Brahman</s>. These two <s>puruṣas</s> — the one in the sun and the one in the eye — are particular forms of the one <s>Satya Brahman</s>; therefore they are established in each other — the solar [<s>puruṣa</s>] in the ocular one, and the ocular one in the solar.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,5.3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.3]

children.text:
ya eṣa etasmin maṇḍale puruṣas tasya bhūr iti śiraḥ |
ekaṃ śira ekam etad akṣaram |
bhuva iti bāhū |
dvau bāhū dve ete akṣare |
svar iti pratiṣṭhā |
dve pratiṣṭhe dve ete akṣare |
tasyopaniṣad ahar iti |
hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: Of the <s>puruṣa</s> who is in that [solar] disc, <s>Bhūḥ</s> is the head — one head, one syllable. <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> is the two arms — two arms, two syllables. <s>Svaḥ</s> is the feet — two feet, two syllables. Its secret name (<s>upaniṣad</s>) is <s>Ahar</s> (Day). One who knows thus destroys and abandons sin. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.3 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,5.3 tatra yo 'sau ko ya eṣa etasminmaṇḍale puruṣaḥ satyanāmā tasya vyāhṛtayo 'vayavāḥ /
katham /
bhūriti yeyaṃ vyāhṛtiḥ sā tasya śiraḥ /
prāthamyāt /
tatra sāmānyaṃ svayamevāha śruti-ekamekasaṃkhyāyiktaṃ śirastathaitadakṣaramekaṃ bhūriti /
bhuva iti bāhū dvitvasāmānyāddvau bāhū dve ete akṣare /
tathā svariti pratiṣṭhā dve pratiṣṭhe dve ete akṣare /
pratiṣṭhe pādau pratitiṣṭhatyābhyāmiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The feet (<s>pratiṣṭhe</s>) are so called because one stands (<s>pratitiṣṭhati</s>) upon them.

children.text: tasyāsya vyāhṛtyavayavasya satyasya brahmaṇa upaniṣadrahasyamabhidhānam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>upaniṣad</s> — the secret name — of this <s>Satya Brahman</s> whose limbs are the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> [is now stated].

children.text: yenābhidhānenābhidhīyamānaṃ tadbrahmābhimukho bhavati lokavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The name by which, when it is invoked, that <s>Brahman</s> becomes favorably inclined, just as in the world [a person responds to their name].

children.text: kāsāvityāha - ahariti ahariti caitadrūpaṃ hanterjahāteśceti yo veda sa hanti jahāti ca pāpmānaṃ ya evaṃ veda //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] What is it? He says — '<s>Ahar</s>.' And this form '<s>Ahar</s>' is derived from the roots 'han' (to destroy) and 'hā' (to abandon). One who knows thus destroys and abandons sin — one who knows thus. //3//

[Commentary:] Now, that [<s>puruṣa</s>] — who is the one in that disc, named <s>Satya</s> — the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) are his limbs. How so? '<s>Bhūḥ</s>' — this <s>Vyāhṛti</s> is his head, because it comes first. The <s>śruti</s> itself states the correspondence: one head, which is one in number, and likewise this syllable '<s>Bhūḥ</s>' is one. '<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>' is the two arms — because of the common feature of being two, two arms and two syllables. Likewise '<s>Svaḥ</s>' is the two feet — two feet and two syllables.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,5.4
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.4]

children.text:
yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣan puruṣas tasya bhūr iti śiraḥ |
ekaṃ śira ekam etad akṣaram |
bhuva iti bāhū |
dvau bāhū dve ete akṣare |
svar iti pratiṣṭhā |
dve pratiṣṭhe dve ete akṣare |
tasyopaniṣad aham iti |
hanti pāpmānaṃ jahāti ca ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: Of the <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the right eye, <s>Bhūḥ</s> is the head — one head, one syllable. <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> is the two arms — two arms, two syllables. <s>Svaḥ</s> is the feet — two feet, two syllables. Its secret name (<s>upaniṣad</s>) is <s>Aham</s> (I). One who knows thus destroys and abandons sin. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.5.4 ||
