children.text: BrhUpBh_5,5.4 evaṃ yo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe 'kṣanpuruṣastasya bhūriti śira ityādi sarvaṃ samānam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Similarly, of the <s>puruṣa</s> who is in the right eye, '<s>Bhūḥ</s>' is the head — and so on, all is the same [as before].

children.text: tasyopaniṣadahamiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Its secret name (<s>upaniṣad</s>) is '<s>Aham</s>' (I).

children.text: pratyagātmabhūtatvāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because it has become the inner self (<s>pratyagātman</s>).

children.text: pūrvavaddhānterjahāteśceti //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As before, [the etymology is] from the roots 'han' (to destroy) and 'hā' (to abandon). //4//

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya pañcamaṃ brāhmaṇam //5//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the blessed <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. //5//

children.text: START BrhUp 5,6.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.6.1]

children.text:
manomayo 'yaṃ puruṣo bhāḥsatyaḥ |
tasminn antar hṛdaye yathā vrīhir vā yavo vā |
sa eṣa sarvasyeśānaḥ sarvasyādhipatiḥ sarvam idaṃ praśāsti yad idaṃ kiñca || BrhUp_5,6.1 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>puruṣa</s> is <s>manomaya</s> (made of mind), whose true nature is light (<s>bhāḥ satya</s>). In the interior of the heart, he is like a grain of rice or a grain of barley. He is the ruler of all, the lord of all; he governs all this, whatever there is. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.6.1 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,6.1 upādhīnāmanekatvādanekaviśeṣaṇatvācca tasyaiva prakṛtasya brahmaṇo manaupādhiviśiṣṭasyopāsanaṃ vidhitsannāhamanomayo manaḥprāyo manasyupalabhyamānatvāt /
manasā copalabhata iti manomayo 'yaṃ puruṣo bhāḥ satyo bhā eva satyaṃ sadbhāvaḥ svarūpaṃ yasya so 'yaṃ bhāḥ satyo bhāsvara ityetat /
manasaḥ sarvārthāvabhāsamatvānmanomayatvāccāsya bhāsvaratvāt /
tasminnantarhṛdaye hṛdayasyāntastasminnityetat /
yathā vrīhirvā yavo vā pariṇamata evaṃ parimāṇastasminnantarhṛdaye yogibhirdṛśyata ityarthaḥ /
sa eṣa sarvasyeśānaḥ sarvasya svabhedajātasyeśānaḥ svāmī /
svāmitve 'pi sati kaścidamātyāditantro 'yaṃ tu na tathā kiṃ tarhyadhipatiradhiṣṭhāya pālayitā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Even though being the sovereign, some [king] may be dependent on ministers and others; but this one is not so. Then what? He is the supreme lord (<s>adhipati</s>) — one who rules by presiding over [all].

children.text: sarvamidaṃ praśāsti yadidaṃ kiñca yatkiñccitsarvaṃ jagattatsarvaṃ praśāsti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He governs all this, whatever there is — whatever the entire universe is, all that he governs.

children.text: eṃ manomayasyopāsanāttathārūpāpattireva phalam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, from the meditation on the <s>manomaya</s> [<s>puruṣa</s>], the fruit is attainment of that very form.

children.text: taṃ tathā yathepāsate tadeva bhavatīti brāhmaṇam //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] As one meditates on him, so one becomes — thus [concludes] the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. //1//

[Commentary:] Because of the multiplicity of limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) and the consequent multiplicity of qualifications, a meditation on that very same <s>Brahman</s> under discussion — qualified by the limiting adjunct of mind — is now intended to be taught. He says: '<s>manomaya</s>' — predominantly mind, because it is apprehended through mind. 'And it is apprehended by mind' — thus this <s>puruṣa</s> is <s>manomaya</s>. '<s>Bhāḥ satya</s>' — light (<s>bhā</s>) alone is the truth, the real nature, the essential form of this one; therefore he is '<s>bhāḥ satya</s>' — luminous. This is so because of mind's capacity to illuminate all objects, and because of this [<s>puruṣa</s>'s] luminosity due to being <s>manomaya</s>. 'In the interior of the heart' — in the interior of the heart, that is the meaning. Like a grain of rice or a grain of barley in size — he is seen by <s>yogins</s> in the interior of the heart, of such measure.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya ṣaṣṭhaṃ brāhmaṇam //6//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the blessed <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. //6//

children.text: START BrhUp 5,7.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.7.1]

children.text:
vidyud brahmety āhuḥ |
vidānād vidyut |
vidyaty enaṃ pāpmano ya evaṃ veda vidyud brahmeti |
vidyud dhy eva brahma || BrhUp_5,7.1 ||
children.translated_text: Lightning is <s>Brahman</s>, they say. It is called <s>Vidyut</s> (lightning) because of <s>vidāna</s> (splitting). It splits one asunder from sin — one who knows thus, [knowing] 'Lightning is <s>Brahman</s>.' For lightning indeed is <s>Brahman</s>. || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.7.1 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_5,7.1 tathaivopāsanāntaraṃ satyasya brahmaṇo viśiṣṭaphalamārabhyate - vidyudbrahmetyāhuḥ /
vidyuto brahmaṇo nirvacanamucyate - vidānādavakhaṇḍanāttamaso medhāndhakāraṃ vidārya hyavabhāsate 'to vidyut /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The etymology of <s>Vidyut</s> (<s>Brahman</s> as lightning) is stated: from <s>vidāna</s> — splitting, cleaving apart. For it shines forth by tearing apart the darkness and the dense obscurity; hence [it is called] <s>Vidyut</s>.

children.text: evaṃ guṇaṃ vidyudbrahmeti yo vedāsai vidyatyavakhaṇḍayati vināśayati pāpmana enamātmānaṃ prati pratikūlabhūtāḥ pāpmāno ye tānsarvānpāpmano 'khaṇḍayatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] One who knows lightning as <s>Brahman</s>, possessing such qualities — that [lightning] splits, cleaves, destroys the sins that are hostile to this self. It destroys all those sins — that is the meaning.

children.text: ya evaṃ veda vidyudbrahmeti tasyānurūpaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For one who knows thus — 'Lightning is <s>Brahman</s>' — the fruit is corresponding [to that knowledge].

children.text: vidyuddhi yasmādbrahma //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because lightning is indeed <s>Brahman</s>. //1//
[Commentary:] Similarly, another meditation on <s>Satya Brahman</s> with a specific fruit is commenced: 'Lightning is <s>Brahman</s>, they say.'

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya saptamaṃ brāhmaṇam //7//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the commentary on the blessed <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. //7//

children.text: START BrhUp 5,8.1
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.8.1]

children.text:
vācaṃ dhenum upāsīta |
tasyāś catvāraḥ stanāḥ |
svāhākāro vaṣaṭkāro hantakāraḥ svadhākāraḥ |
tasyai dvau stanau devā upajīvanti |
svāhākāraṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraṃ ca |
hantakāraṃ manuṣyāḥ |
svadhākāraṃ pitaraḥ |
tasyāḥ prāṇa ṛṣabho mano vatsaḥ || BrhUp_5,8.1 ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate on Speech (<s>Vāc</s>) as a cow (<s>dhenu</s>). She has four teats: the <s>Svāhā</s>-call, the <s>Vaṣaṭ</s>-call, the <s>Hanta</s>-call, and the <s>Svadhā</s>-call. The gods live on two of her teats — the <s>Svāhā</s>-call and the <s>Vaṣaṭ</s>-call. Humans [live on] the <s>Hanta</s>-call. The ancestors (<s>Pitaras</s>) [live on] the <s>Svadhā</s>-call. Her bull is <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath); her calf is the mind (<s>Manas</s>). || <s>BṛhUp</s> 5.8.1 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,8.1 punarupāsanāntaraṃ tasyaiva brahmaṇo vāgvai brahmeti vāgiti śabdasrayī tāṃ vācaṃ dhenuṃ dhenuriva dhenuryathā dhenuścaturbhiḥ stanaiḥ stanyaṃ payaḥ kṣarati vatsāyaivaṃ vāgdhenurvakṣyamāṇaiḥ stanaiḥ paya ivānnaṃ kṣarati devādibhyaḥ /
ke punaste stanā ye vā te yebhyaḥ kṣarati /
tasyā etasyā vāco dhenvā dvau stanau devā upajīvanti vatsasthānīyāḥ /
kau tau /
svāhākāraṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraṃ ca /
ābhyāṃ hi havirdīyate devebhyaḥ /
hantakāraṃ manuṣyāḥ /
hanteti manuṣyebhyo 'nnaṃ prayacchanti /
svadhākāraṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraṃ ca /
ābhyāṃ hi havirdīyate devebhyaḥ /
hantakāraṃ manuṣyāḥ /
hanteti manuṣyebhyo 'nnaṃ prayacchanti svadhākāraṃ ca vaṣaṭkāraṃ ca /
ābhyāṃ hi havirdīyate devebhyaḥ /
hantakāraṃ manuṣyāḥ /
hanteti manuṣyebhyo 'nnaṃ prayacchanti /
svadhākāraṃ pitaraḥ /
svadhākāreṇa hi pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāṃ prayacchanti /
tasyā dhenvā vācaḥ prāṇa ṛṣabhaḥ /
prāṇena hi vākprasūyate /
mano vatsaḥ /
manasā hi prasrāvyate /
children.translated_text: For [the milk of speech] is drawn forth by the mind.

children.text: manasā hyālocite viṣaye vākpravartate /
children.translated_text: For when the mind has contemplated an object, speech proceeds [toward it].

children.text: tasmānmano vatsasthānīyam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mind occupies the position of the calf.

children.text: evaṃ vāgdhenūpāsakastādbhāvyameva pratipadyate //1//
children.translated_text: Thus, one who meditates on [speech as] the cow attains identity with that [<s>Brahman</s>]. // 5.8.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.8.1:] Again, another meditation on that very <s>Brahman</s>: 'Speech is <s>Brahman</s>' — '<s>vāk</s>' (speech) means that which depends on sounds. That speech is [to be meditated upon as] a cow (<s>dhenu</s>) — just as a cow, by means of four teats, yields milk for the calf, even so the cow of speech yields, through the teats about to be mentioned, food like milk for the gods and others. What then are those teats, and for whom does it yield? Of this cow of speech, two teats are the ones upon which the gods subsist, occupying the position of calves. Which two? The exclamation <s>svāhā</s> and the exclamation <s>vaṣaṭ</s>. For by means of these two, oblations are given to the gods. The exclamation <s>hanta</s> ('come!') is for human beings — by saying '<s>hanta</s>,' food is given to humans. The exclamation <s>svadhā</s> is for the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>) — by the exclamation <s>svadhā</s>, offerings are given to the ancestors. Of that cow of speech, <s>prāṇa</s> is the bull (<s>ṛṣabha</s>) — for by <s>prāṇa</s>, speech is engendered. The mind is the calf.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasyāṣṭamaṃ brāhmaṇam //8//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the commentary on the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 8 //

children.text: START BrhUp 5,9.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.9.1]

children.text:
ayam agnir vaiśvānaro yo 'yam antaḥ puruṣe |
yenedam annaṃ pacyate |
yad idam adyate |
tasyaiṣa ghoṣo bhavati |
yam etat karṇāv apidhāya śṛṇoti |
sa yadotkramiṣyan bhavati nainaṃ ghoṣaṃ śṛṇoti || BrhUp_5,9.1 ||
children.translated_text: This fire, the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, is the one within the person, by which this food is digested — what is eaten here. This is its sound, which one hears when one covers the ears. When he is about to depart [from the body], he does not hear this sound. // BṛUp 5.9.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,9.1 ayamagnirvaiśvānanaraḥ pūrvavadupāsanāntaramayamagnirvaiśvānaraḥ /
ko 'yamagnirityāha-yo 'yamantaḥpuruṣe /
kiṃ śarīrārambhako netyucyate-yenāgninā vaiśvānarākhyenedamannaṃ pacyate /
kiṃ tadannam /
yadidamadyate bhujyate 'nnaṃ prajābhijaṭhiro 'gnirityarthaḥ /
tasya sākṣādupalakṣaṇārthamidamāha-tasyāgnerannaṃ pacato jāṭharasyaiṣa ghoṣo bhavati /
ko 'sau /
children.translated_text: What is that [sound]?

children.text: yaṃ ghoṣametaditi kriyāviśeṣaṇaṃ karṇāvapidhāyāṅgulībhyāmapidhānaṃ kṛtvā śṛṇoti taṃ prajāpatimupāsīta vaiśvānaramagnim /
children.translated_text: That sound which — '<s>etat</s>' (this) being an adverbial qualifier of the action — one hears when one covers the ears with the fingers — one should meditate upon that [sound] as <s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire.

children.text: atrāpi tādbhāvyaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: Here too, the fruit is identity with that [<s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: tatra prāsaṅgikamidamariṣṭalakṣaṇamucyate-so 'tra śarīre bhoktā yadotkramiṣyanbhavati nainaṃ ghoṣaṃ śṛṇoti //1//
children.translated_text: Therein, this incidental [teaching] of a sign of approaching death (<s>ariṣṭa</s>) is stated: he who is the experiencer in this body — when he is about to depart, he does not hear this sound. // 5.9.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.9.1:] 'This fire, the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>' — as before, another meditation: this fire is the <s>Vaiśvānara</s>. What fire is this? That which is within the person. What kind [of fire]? It is said: by which fire, called <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, this food is digested. What is that food? That which is eaten, consumed by beings — the meaning is: it is the fire of the belly (<s>jaṭhara</s>). For the purpose of directly recognizing that [fire], this is stated: of that fire — that belly-fire which digests food — this sound (<s>ghoṣa</s>) arises.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya navamaṃ brāhmaṇam //9//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the commentary on the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 9 //

children.text: START BrhUp 5,10.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.10.1]

children.text:
yadā vai puruṣo 'smāl lokāt praiti sa vāyum āgacchati |
tasmai sa tatra vijihīte yathā rathacakrasya kham |
tena sa ūrdhva ākramate |
sa ādityam āgacchati |
tasmai sa tatra vijihīte |
yathā lambarasya kham |
tena sa ūrdhva ākramate |
sa candramasam āgacchati |
tasmai sa tatra vijihīte |
yathā dundubheḥ kham |
tena sa ūrdhva ākramate |
sa lokam āgacchaty aśokam ahimam |
tasmin vasati śāśvatīḥ samāḥ || BrhUp_5,10.1 ||
children.translated_text: When a person departs from this world, he reaches the wind (<s>Vāyu</s>). There [the wind] opens up for him like the hole of a chariot-wheel. Through that he ascends upward. He reaches the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). There [the sun] opens up for him like the hole of a <s>lambara</s> drum. Through that he ascends upward. He reaches the moon (<s>Candramā</s>). There [the moon] opens up for him like the hole of a <s>dundubhi</s> drum. Through that he ascends upward. He reaches a world that is free from sorrow, free from cold. In that [world] he dwells for eternal years. // BṛUp 5.10.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,10.1 sarveṣāmasminprakaraṇa upāsanānāṃ gatiriyaṃ phalaṃ cocyate-yadā vai puruṣo vidvānasmāllokātpraiti śarīraṃ parityajati sa tadā vāyumāgacchatyantarikṣe tiryagbhūto vāyuḥ stimito 'bhedyastiṣṭhati /
sa vāyustatra svātmani tasmai samprāptāya vijihote svātmāvayavānvigamayati cchidrīkarotyātmānamityarthaḥ /
kiṃparimāmaṃ chidramiti /
ucyate-yathā ratha vakrasya khaṃ chidraṃ prasiddhaparimāṇam /
tena chidreṇa sa vidvānūrdhva ākramata ūrdhvaḥ sangacchati sa ādityamāgacchati /
ādityo brahmalokaṃ jigamiṣormārganirodhaṃ kṛtvā sthitaḥ so 'pyevaṃvida upāsakāya dvāraṃ prayacchati /
tasmai sa tatra vijihote /
yathā lambarasya khaṃ vāditraviśeṣasya cchidraparimāmaṃ tena sa ūrdhva ākramate sa candramasamāgacchati /
so 'pi tasmai tatra vijihīte /
yathā dundubheḥ khaṃ prasiddhaṃ tena sa ūrdhva ākramate sa lokaṃ prajāpatilokamāgacchati /
kiṃviśiṣṭam /
aśokaṃ mānasena duḥkhena vivarjitamityetat /
children.translated_text: Free from sorrow (<s>aśoka</s>) — free from mental suffering — this is the meaning.

children.text: ahimaṃ himavarjitaṃ śārīraduḥkhavarjitamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Free from cold (<s>ahima</s>) — free from cold, meaning free from physical suffering.

children.text: taṃ prāpya tasminvasati śāśvatīrnityāḥ samāḥ saṃvatsarānityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having reached that [world], he dwells there for eternal (<s>śāśvatī</s>) — permanent — years (<s>samāḥ</s>) — meaning for [many] years.

children.text: brahmaṇo bahūnkalpānvasatītyetat //1//
children.translated_text: He dwells there for many <s>kalpas</s> of <s>Brahmā</s> — this is the meaning. // 5.10.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.10.1:] The path and the fruit of all the meditations in this section are stated here. When a person — a wise one — departs from this world, abandons the body, he then reaches <s>Vāyu</s> (the wind) — which stands in the atmosphere, horizontal, still, impenetrable. That <s>Vāyu</s>, there, in its own self, opens up for the one who has arrived — parts its own portions, makes an opening in itself — this is the meaning. Of what size is the opening? It is said: like the hole of a chariot-wheel — an opening of well-known size. Through that opening, the wise one ascends upward. He reaches <s>Āditya</s> (the sun). The sun, standing [as if] obstructing the path of one who wishes to go to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, also opens a door for such a meditator. For him it opens up there — like the hole of a <s>lambara</s>, a particular musical instrument — an opening of that size. Through that he ascends upward. He reaches <s>Candramā</s> (the moon). He too opens up for him there — like the hole of a <s>dundubhi</s> drum, a well-known [size]. Through that he ascends upward. He reaches a world — the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Of what kind?

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya daśamaṃ brāhmaṇam //10//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the commentary on the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 10 //

children.text: START BrhUp 5,11.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.11.1]

children.text:
etad vai paramaṃ tapo yad vyāhitas tapyate |
paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda |
etad vai paramaṃ tapo yaṃ pretam araṇyaṃ haranti |
paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda |
etad vai paramaṃ tapo yaṃ pretam agnāv abhyādadhati |
paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,11.1 ||
children.translated_text: This is the highest austerity (<s>tapas</s>): when one who is afflicted [by illness] suffers — he indeed wins the highest world who knows thus. This is the highest austerity: when one who has died is carried to the forest — he indeed wins the highest world who knows thus. This is the highest austerity: when one who has died is placed upon the fire — he indeed wins the highest world who knows thus. // BṛUp 5.11.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,11.1 etadvai paramaṃ tapaḥ /
kiṃ tat /
yadyāhito vyādhito jvarādiparigṛhītaḥ sanyattapyate tadetatparamaṃ tapa ityevaṃ cintayet /
duḥkhasāmānyāt /
tasyaivaṃ cintayato viduṣaḥ karmakṣayahetustadeva tapo bhavatyanindato 'viṣīdataḥ /
sa eva ca tena vijñānatapasā dagdhakilbaṣaḥ paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda /
children.translated_text: And he, with his sins burned by the fire of that knowledge-austerity, indeed wins the highest world — he who knows thus.

children.text: tathaitadvai paramaṃ tapo yaṃ pretamagnāvabhyādadhati /
children.translated_text: Similarly, 'this is the highest austerity: when one who has died is placed upon the fire' —

children.text: agnipraveśasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: because of the similarity with [being placed into] fire.

children.text: paramaṃ haiva lokaṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda //1//
children.translated_text: He indeed wins the highest world who knows thus. // 5.11.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.11.1:] 'This is the highest austerity.' What is that? When one who is afflicted (<s>vyāhita</s>) — afflicted by disease, seized by fever and the like — suffers, one should contemplate: 'This is the highest austerity.' Because of the similarity with suffering [in actual austerity]. For such a contemplating wise person, that very suffering becomes a cause of the destruction of <s>karma</s> — [provided he does] not blame [others] and does not despair.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasyaikādaśaṃ brāhmaṇam //11//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the commentary on the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 11 //

children.text: START BrhUp 5,12.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.12.1]

children.text:
annaṃ brahmety eka āhuḥ |
tan na tathā |
pūyati vā annam ṛte prāṇāt |
prāṇo brahmety eka āhuḥ |
tan na tathā |
śuṣyati vai praṇa ṛte 'nnāt |
ete ha tv eva devate ekadhābhūyaṃ bhūtvā paramatāṃ gacchataḥ |
tad dha smāha prātṛdaḥ pitaram |
kiṃ svid evaivaṃ viduṣe sādhu kuryāṃ kim evāsmā asādhu kuryām iti |
sa ha smāha pāṇinā mā prātṛda |
kas tv enayor ekadhābhūyaṃ bhūtvā paramatāṃ gacchatīti |
tasmā u haitad uvāca vīti |
annaṃ vai vi |
anne hīmāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni viṣṭāni |
ram iti |
prāṇo vai ram |
prāṇe hīmāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni ramante |
sarvāṇi ha vā asmin bhūtāni viśanti |
sarvāṇi bhūtāni ramante ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,12.1 ||
children.translated_text: Some say: 'Food is <s>Brahman</s>.' But it is not so — for food decays without <s>prāṇa</s>. Some say: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>.' But it is not so — for <s>prāṇa</s> dries up without food. These two deities, having become one, reach the highest state. Thereupon <s>Prātṛda</s> said to his father: 'What good could I do to one who knows thus? What wrong could I do to him?' [The father] said, [gesturing] with his hand: 'No, <s>Prātṛda</s>! Who indeed reaches the highest state by these two becoming one?' Then he told him this: '<s>Vi</s>' — food is indeed <s>Vi</s>, for all these beings are entered (<s>viṣṭa</s>) into food. '<s>Ram</s>' — <s>prāṇa</s> is indeed <s>Ram</s>, for all these beings delight (<s>ramante</s>) in <s>prāṇa</s>. All beings enter into him, all beings delight in him — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 5.12.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,12.1 annaṃ brahmeti /
tathaitadupāsanāntaraṃ vidhitsannāha-annaṃ brahmānnamadyate yattadbrahmetyeka ācāryā āhustanna tathā grahītavyamannaṃ brahmeti /
anye cā'huḥ prāṇo brahmeti tacca tathā na grahītavyam /
kimarthaṃ punarannaṃ brahmeti na grāhyam /
yasmātpūyati klidyate pūtibhāvamāpadyata ṛte prāṇāttatkathaṃ brahma bhavitumarhati /
brahma hi nāma tadyadavināśi /
astu tarhi prāṇo brahma /
naiva /
yasmācchuṣyati vai prāṇa ṛte 'nnāt /
attā hi prāṇaḥ /
ato 'nnenā'dyena vinā na śaknotyātmānaṃ dhārayitum /
tasmācchruṣyati vai prāṇa ṛte 'nnāt /
ata ekaikasya brahmatā nopapadyate yasmāttasmādete ha tvevānnaprāṇadevate ekadhābhūyamekadhābāvaṃ bhūtvā gatvā paramatāṃ paramatvaṃ gacchato brahmatvaṃ prāpnutaḥ /
tadetadevamadhyavasya ha smā'ha sma prātṛdo nāma pitarātmanaḥ kiṃsviditisviditi vitarke /
yathā mayā brahma parikalpitamevaṃ viduṣe kiṃsvitsādhu kuryāṃ sādhu śobhanaṃ pūjāṃ kāṃ tvasmai kuryāmityabhiprāyaḥ /
kinevāsmai viduṣe 'sādhu kuryāṃ kṛtakṛtyo 'sāvityabhiprāyaḥ /
annaprāṇau sahabhūto brahmeti vidvānnāsāvasādhukaramena khaṇḍito bhavati /
nāpi sādhukaraṇena mahīkṛtaḥ /
tadevaṃvādinaṃ sa pitā ha smā'ha pāṇinā hastena nivārayanmā prātṛda maivaṃ vocaḥ /
kastvenayorannaprāṇayorekadhābhūyaṃ bhūtvā paramatāṃ kastu gacchati na kaścidapi vidvānanena brahmadarśanena paramatāṃ gacchati /
tasmānnaivaṃ vaktumarhasi kṛtakṛtyo 'sāviti /
yadyevaṃ bravītu bhavānkathaṃ paramatāṃ gacchatīti /
tasmā u haitadvakṣyamāṇaṃ vaca uvāca /
kiṃ tat /
vīti /
kiṃ tadvīti /
ucyate-annaṃ vai vi /
anne hi yasmādimāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni viṣṭānyāśritānyato 'nnaṃ vītyucyate /
kiñca ramiti /
ramiti coktavānpitā /
kiṃ punastadram /
prāṇo vai ram /
kuta ityāha /
prāṇe hi kaścidanāyatano nirāśrayo ramate /
nāpi satyapyāyatane 'prāṇo durbalo ramate /
children.translated_text: Nor, even when a support exists, does a weak, lifeless [being] delight.

children.text: yadā tvāyatanavānprāṇī balavāṃśca tadā kṛtārthamātmānaṃ manyamāno ramate lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: But when one has a support and is alive and strong — then, considering oneself fulfilled, one delights in the world.

children.text: "yuvā syātsādhuyuvādhyāyakaḥ"ityādiśruteḥ /
children.translated_text: As the <s>śruti</s> [says]: 'Let him be young, a good young man, learned' (TaiUp 2.8.1) and so forth.

children.text: idānīmevaṃvidaḥ phalamāha - sarvāṇi ha vā asminbhūtāni viśantyannaguṇajñānātsarvāṇi bhūtāni ramante prāṇaguṇajñānādya evaṃ veda //1//
children.translated_text: Now the fruit for one who knows thus is stated: all beings enter into him — because of knowing the quality of food; all beings delight [in him] — because of knowing the quality of <s>prāṇa</s> — he who knows thus. // 5.12.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.12.1:] 'Food is <s>Brahman</s>' — thus, wishing to teach another meditation, [the text] says: 'Food is <s>Brahman</s>' — that which is eaten, that is <s>Brahman</s> — thus some teachers say. But it should not be taken thus — that food is <s>Brahman</s>. Others say: '<s>Prāṇa</s> is <s>Brahman</s>' — that too should not be taken thus. For what reason should food not be taken as <s>Brahman</s>? Because food decays — becomes moist, putrid — without <s>prāṇa</s>; how then can it be <s>Brahman</s>? For <s>Brahman</s> is that which is imperishable. Then let <s>prāṇa</s> be <s>Brahman</s>. Not so either — because <s>prāṇa</s> dries up without food. For <s>prāṇa</s> is an eater; therefore, without food to eat, it cannot sustain itself. Hence, <s>prāṇa</s> dries up without food. Therefore, the <s>Brahman</s>-hood of each one individually is untenable. Since that is so, these two deities, food and <s>prāṇa</s>, having become one — having attained oneness, having come together — reach the highest state, the state of being <s>Brahman</s>. Having determined this thus, <s>Prātṛda</s> by name said to his own father — '<s>sviditi</s>' indicating deliberation — 'Just as <s>Brahman</s> has been conceived by me, what good could I do to one who knows thus?' — meaning: 'What honor could I offer him?' — this is the intent. 'What wrong could I do to this wise one?' — meaning: 'He is one who has accomplished his purpose' — this is the intent. One who knows food and <s>prāṇa</s> together as <s>Brahman</s> — such a wise person is neither diminished by wrong treatment nor exalted by good treatment. To him who spoke thus, his father said, restraining [him] with his hand: 'No, <s>Prātṛda</s>, do not speak thus! Who indeed, through these two — food and <s>prāṇa</s> — having become one, reaches the highest state? No one at all, through this [limited] vision of <s>Brahman</s>, reaches the highest state. Therefore you should not say he has accomplished his purpose.' [<s>Prātṛda</s> asks:] 'If so, let your honor tell me how one reaches the highest state.' Then he told him the following words. What is that? '<s>Vi</s>' — what is that '<s>Vi</s>'? It is said: food is indeed <s>Vi</s> — because all these beings are entered into (<s>viṣṭa</s>), dependent upon food — therefore food is called '<s>Vi</s>.' Furthermore, '<s>Ram</s>' — the father also said '<s>Ram</s>.' What then is that '<s>Ram</s>'? <s>Prāṇa</s> is indeed <s>Ram</s>. Why? It is said: for without a support, without a foundation, no one (<s>prāṇa</s>) delights.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya dvādaśaṃ brāhmaṇam //12//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the commentary on the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 12 //

children.text: START BrhUp 5,13.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.13.1]

children.text:
uktham |
prāṇo vā uktham |
prāṇo hīdaṃ sarvam utthāpayati |
ud dhasmād ukthavid vīras tiṣṭhati |
ukthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,13.1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uktha</s> (recitation). <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>uktha</s>. For <s>prāṇa</s> raises up (<s>utthāpayati</s>) this entire [world]. From him rises a heroic son who is a knower of the <s>uktha</s>. He wins union and co-residence with the <s>uktha</s> — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 5.13.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,13.1 uktham /
tathopāsanāntaramukthaṃ śasram /
taddhi pradhānaṃ mahāvrate kratau /
kiṃ punastaduktham /
prāṇo vā uktham /
prāṇaśca pradhāna indriyāṇāmukthaṃ ca śasrāṇāmata ukthamityupāsīta /
kathaṃ prāṇa ukthamityāha-prāṇo hi yasmādidaṃ sarvamutthāpayati /
utthāpanāduktha prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Because of raising up (<s>utthāpana</s>), <s>prāṇa</s> is [called] <s>uktha</s>.

children.text: na hyaprāṇaḥ kaściduttiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: For without <s>prāṇa</s>, no one rises up.

children.text: tadupāsanaphalamāha-uddhāsmādevaṃvida ukthavitprāṇavidvīraḥ putra uttiṣṭhati ha dṛṣṭametatphalam /
children.translated_text: The fruit of that meditation is stated: from him — from such a knower — a heroic son who knows the <s>uktha</s>, who knows <s>prāṇa</s>, rises up — this is the visible fruit.

children.text: adṛṣṭaṃ tūkthasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda //1//
children.translated_text: The invisible [fruit] is: he wins union (<s>sāyujya</s>) and co-residence (<s>salokatā</s>) with the <s>uktha</s> — he who knows thus. // 5.13.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.13.1:] <s>Uktha</s> — thus, another meditation. <s>Uktha</s> is the <s>śastra</s> (recitation). For that [<s>uktha</s>] is the principal [element] in the <s>Mahāvrata</s> rite. What then is that <s>uktha</s>? <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>uktha</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the principal among the sense-organs, and <s>uktha</s> is [the principal] among the recitations — therefore one should meditate [on <s>prāṇa</s>] as <s>uktha</s>. How is <s>prāṇa</s> the <s>uktha</s>? This is stated: because <s>prāṇa</s> raises up (<s>utthāpayati</s>) this entire [world].

children.text: START BrhUp 5,13.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.13.2]

children.text:
yajuḥ |
prāṇo vai yajuḥ |
prāṇe hīmāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni yujyante |
yujyante hāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtāni śraiṣṭhyāya |
yajuṣaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,13.2 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yajus</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Yajus</s>. For in <s>prāṇa</s>, all beings are yoked (<s>yujyante</s>). All beings are yoked for supremacy for one who knows thus. He wins union with and the same world as the <s>Yajus</s>, who knows thus. (BṛUp 5.13.2)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,13.2 yajuriti copāsīta prāṇam /
prāṇau vai yajuḥ /
kathaṃ yujaḥ prāṇaḥ /
prāṇe hi yasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni yujyante /
na hyasati prāṇe kenacitkasyacidyogasāmarthyam /
ato yunaktīti prāṇo yajuḥ /
evaṃvidaḥ phalamāha-yujyanta udyacchanta ityarthaḥ /
hāsmā evaṃvide sarvāṇi bhūtāni śraiṣṭhyaṃ śreṣṭhabhāvastasmai śraiṣṭhyāya śreṣṭhabhāvāya naḥ śreṣṭho bhavediti /
yajuṣaḥ prāṇasya sāyujyamityādi sarva samānam //2 // //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Union with the <s>Yajus</s>, that is, with <s>prāṇa</s>, and the same world' — and so forth — everything is the same [as before]. (5.13.2)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.13.2:] One should meditate on <s>prāṇa</s> as '<s>Yajus</s>.' <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Yajus</s>. How is <s>prāṇa</s> the <s>Yajus</s>? Because in <s>prāṇa</s>, all beings are yoked (<s>yujyante</s>). For in the absence of <s>prāṇa</s>, no one has the capacity to be connected with anything. Therefore, because it yokes (<s>yunakti</s>), <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Yajus</s>. The fruit for one who knows thus is stated: they are yoked (<s>yujyante</s>) — meaning 'they strive, they exert themselves.' All beings [strive] for this knower, for supremacy (<s>śraiṣṭhya</s>) — for the state of being the best — [thinking] 'May he be the best among us.'

children.text: START BrhUp 5,13.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.13.3]

children.text:
sāma |
prāṇo vai sāma |
prāṇe hīmāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni samyañci |
samyañci hāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtāni śraiṣṭhyāya kalpante |
sāmnaḥ sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,13.3 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sāman</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Sāman</s>. For in <s>prāṇa</s>, all beings come together (<s>samyañci</s>). All beings come together for one who knows thus, being well-disposed toward his supremacy. He wins union with and the same world as the <s>Sāman</s>, who knows thus. (BṛUp 5.13.3)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,13.3 sāmeti copāsīta prāṇam /
prāṇo vai sāma /
kathaṃ prāṇaḥ sāma /
prāṇe hi yasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni samyañci saṃgacchante saṃgamanātsāmyāpattihetutvātsāma prāṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because in <s>prāṇa</s>, all beings come together (<s>samyañci saṃgacchante</s>) — because it is the cause of their coming together and reaching equality, <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Sāman</s>.

children.text: samyañci saṃgacchante hāsmai sarvāṇi bhūtāni /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Coming together (<s>samyañci saṃgacchante</s>) — all beings come together for this knower.

children.text: na kevalaṃ saṃgacchanta eva śreṣṭhabhāvāya cāsmai kalpante samarthyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Not only do they come together, but they are also well-disposed (<s>kalpante</s>) — they become capable — for his supremacy.

children.text: sāmnaḥ sāyujyamityādi purvavat //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Union with the <s>Sāman</s>' — and so forth, as before. (5.13.3)
[Commentary on BṛUp 5.13.3:] One should meditate on <s>prāṇa</s> as '<s>Sāman</s>.' <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Sāman</s>. How is <s>prāṇa</s> the <s>Sāman</s>?

children.text: START BrhUp 5,13.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.13.4]

children.text:
kṣatram |
prāṇo vai kṣatram |
prāṇo hi vai kṣatram |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣatra</s> (ruling power). <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Kṣatra</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Kṣatra</s> —

children.text:
trāyate hainaṃ prāṇaḥ kṣaṇitoḥ |
pra kṣatram atram āpnoti |
kṣatrasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,13.4 ||
children.translated_text: for <s>prāṇa</s> protects (<s>trāyate</s>) this [body] from injury (<s>kṣaṇitoḥ</s>). He attains the <s>kṣatra</s> (ruling power) that is without a protector (<s>atram</s>). He wins union with and the same world as the <s>Kṣatra</s>, who knows thus. (BṛUp 5.13.4)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,13.4 taṃ prāṇaṃ kṣattramityupāsīta /
prāṇau vai kṣattraṃ prasiddhametatprāṇo hi vai kṣattram /
kathaṃ prasiddhametatprāṇo hi vai kṣattram /
kathaṃ prasiddhatetyāha-trāyate pālayatyenaṃ piṇḍaṃ dehaṃ prāṇaḥ kṣaṇitoḥ śasrādihiṃsitātpunarmāṃsenā'pūrayati yasmāttasmātkṣatatrāṇātprasiddhaṃ kṣattratvaṃ prāṇasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] How is this well-known? — it says: [<s>Prāṇa</s>] protects (<s>trāyate</s>), preserves this body (<s>piṇḍa</s>) from injury (<s>kṣaṇitoḥ</s>) — from harm by weapons and the like — and replenishes it again with flesh. Because of this protection from injury (<s>kṣatatrāṇa</s>), the <s>Kṣatra</s>-nature of <s>prāṇa</s> is well-known.

children.text: vidvatphalamāha-pra kṣattramatraṃ na trāyate 'nyena kenacidityatraṃ kṣattraṃ prāṇaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The fruit for the knower is stated: '<s>Pra kṣatram atram</s>' — the <s>Kṣatra</s> that is '<s>atra</s>' — meaning: not protected by anything else — one attains [this] <s>Kṣatra</s>, the <s>prāṇa</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: śākhāntare vā pāṭhātkṣattramātraṃ prāṇo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Or, according to the reading in another <s>śākhā</s> (recension): one becomes nothing but <s>Kṣatra</s>, nothing but <s>prāṇa</s> — this is the meaning.

children.text: kṣattrasya sāyujyaṃ salokatāṃ jayati ya evaṃ veda //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He wins union with and the same world as the <s>Kṣatra</s>, who knows thus. (5.13.4)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.13.4:] One should meditate on that <s>prāṇa</s> as '<s>Kṣatra</s>' (ruling power). <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Kṣatra</s> — this is well-known. For <s>prāṇa</s> indeed is the <s>Kṣatra</s>. How is this well-known that <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Kṣatra</s>?

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya trayodaśaṃ brāhmaṇam //13//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth <s>adhyāya</s> in the blessed <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad Bhāṣya</s>. (5.13)

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.1]

children.text:
bhūmir antarikṣaṃ dyaur ity aṣṭāv akṣarāṇi |
aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padam |
etad u haivāsyā etat |
sa yāvad eṣu triṣu lokeṣu tāvad dha jayati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,14.1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhūmi</s> (earth), <s>antarikṣa</s> (atmosphere), <s>dyaus</s> (heaven)' — these are eight syllables. One foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> has eight syllables. This [threefold world] is indeed that [foot] of hers. He who knows this foot of hers conquers as much as there is in these three worlds. (BṛUp 5.14.1)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.1 brahmaṇo hṛdayādyanekopādhiviśiṣṭasyopāsanamuktamathedānīṃ gāyatryupādhiviśiṣṭasyopāsanaṃ vaktavyamityārabhyate /
sarvacchandasāṃ hi gāyatrīcchandaḥ pradhānabhūtam /
tatprayoktṛgayatrāṇādgāyatrīti vakṣyati /
na cānyeṣāṃ chandasāṃ prayoktṛprāṇatrāṇasāmarthyam /
prāṇātmabhūtā ca sā sarvacchandasāṃ cā'tmā prāṇaḥ /
prāṇaśca kṣatatrāṇātkṣattramityuktam /
prāṇaśca gāyatrī /
tasmāttadupāsanameva vidhitsyate /
dvijottamajanmahetutvācca /
gāyatryā brāhmaṇamasṛjata triṣṭubhā rājanyaṃ jagatyā vaiśyamati dvijottamasya dvitīyaṃ janma gāyatrīnimittam /
tasmātpradhānā gāyatrī brāhmaṇā vyutthāya brāhmaṇā abhivadanti sa brāhmaṇo vipāpo virajo 'vicikitso brāhmaṇo bhavatītyuttamapuruṣārthasaṃbandhaṃ brāhmaṇasya darśayati /
tacca brāhmaṇatvaṃ gāyatrījanmamūlamato vaktavyaṃ gāyatryāḥ satattvam /
gāyatryā hi yaḥ sṛṣṭo dvijottamo niraṅkuśa evottamapuruṣārthasādhane 'dhikriyate 'tastanmūlaḥ paramapuruṣārthasaṃbandhaḥ /
tasmāttadupāsanavidhānāyā'ha-bhūmirantarikṣaṃ dyaurityetānyaṣṭāvakṣarāṇi /
aṣṭākṣaramaṣṭāvakṣarāṇi yasya tadidamaṣṭākṣaram /
ha vai prasiddhāvadyotakau /
ekaṃ prathamaṃ gāyatryai gāyatryāḥ padam /
yakāreṇaivāṣṭatvapūraṇam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The completion of the [count of] eight is by the <s>ya</s>-sound [in '<s>dyaus</s>'].

children.text: etadu haivaitadevāsyā gāyatryāḥ padaṃ pādaḥ prathamo bhūmyādilakṣaṇasrailokyātmā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This indeed is that [foot] of hers — of this <s>Gāyatrī</s> — the first foot, consisting of the three worlds characterized by earth and the like, having [<s>prāṇa</s>] as its self.

children.text: aṣṭākṣaratvasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the commonality of having eight syllables.

children.text: evametattrailokyātmakaṃ gāyatryāḥ prathamaṃ padaṃ yo vedatasyaitatphalam-sa vidvānyāvatkiñcideṣu triṣu jetavyaṃ tāvatsarvaṃ ha jayati yo 'syā etadevaṃ padaṃ veda //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus, one who knows the first foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> consisting of the three worlds — the fruit for that knower is: whatever there is to be conquered in these three worlds — all of that he conquers, who knows this foot of hers in this way. (5.14.1)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.1:] The meditation on <s>Brahman</s> qualified by various limiting adjuncts such as the heart and the like has been stated. Now, the meditation on that same [<s>Brahman</s>] qualified by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as limiting adjunct is to be stated — [for this purpose] this section is commenced. For among all metres, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> metre is preeminent. Because it protects (<s>trāṇa</s>) the singer (<s>gāyatṛ</s>), it is called <s>Gāyatrī</s> — as will be stated [later]. And no other metre has the capacity to protect the singer through <s>prāṇa</s>. For <s>Gāyatrī</s> has <s>prāṇa</s> as its self; and <s>prāṇa</s> is the self of all metres. And <s>prāṇa</s>, because of its protection from injury (<s>kṣatatrāṇa</s>), was called <s>Kṣatra</s>. And <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Therefore, it is the meditation on that [<s>Gāyatrī</s>] that is being prescribed. And because it is the cause of the second birth of the foremost among the twice-born. [The <s>śruti</s> says:] 'By the <s>Gāyatrī</s> he created the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; by the <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the <s>kṣatriya</s>; by the <s>Jagatī</s>, the <s>vaiśya</s>' — thus the second birth of the foremost twice-born has the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as its cause. Therefore, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is preeminent. The <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having arisen [from initiation], address [each other as] <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: 'He becomes a sinless, passionless, doubtless <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — [this] shows the <s>brāhmaṇa's</s> connection with the supreme human goal. And that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood has its root in the <s>Gāyatrī</s>-birth; therefore, the true nature of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is to be stated. For one who is created by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — the foremost twice-born — is qualified without obstruction for the means to the supreme human goal; therefore, the supreme human goal is rooted in that [<s>Gāyatrī</s>]. For this purpose, in order to prescribe the meditation [on it, the text] says: '<s>Bhūmi</s>, <s>antarikṣa</s>, <s>dyaus</s>' — these are eight syllables. Eight-syllabled (<s>aṣṭākṣara</s>) — that which has eight syllables is this eight-syllabled [foot]. '<s>Ha vai</s>' are particles denoting [common] knowledge. One — the first — foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.2
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.2]

children.text:
ṛco yajūṣi sāmānīty aṣṭāv akṣarāṇi |
aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padam |
etad u haivāsyā etat |
sa yāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā tāvad dha jayati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,14.2 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Ṛcaḥ</s> (verses), <s>yajūṃṣi</s> (formulas), <s>sāmāni</s> (chants)' — these are eight syllables. One foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> has eight syllables. This is indeed that [foot] of hers. He conquers as much as this threefold knowledge [encompasses], who knows this foot of hers in this way. (BṛUp 5.14.2)

children.text: BrhUpBh_5,14.2 tadarco yajūṃsi sāmānīti trayīvidyānāmākṣarāṇyetānyapyaṣṭāveva tathaivāṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padaṃ dvitīyametadu haivāsyā etadṛgyajuḥsāmalakṣaṇamaṣṭākṣaratvasāmānyādeva /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.2:] Then — '<s>ṛcaḥ</s>, <s>yajūṃṣi</s>, <s>sāmāni</s>' — the syllables of the names of the threefold knowledge are also eight only. Likewise, one eight-syllabled foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — the second one. This indeed is that [foot] of hers — characterized by <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> — because of the commonality of having eight syllables.

children.text: sa yāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā trayyā vidyayā yāvatphalajātamāpyate tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etadgāyatryāsraividyalakṣaṇaṃ padaṃ veda //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He conquers as much fruit as is attainable by the threefold knowledge — all that he conquers, who knows this foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> characterized by the threefold knowledge. (5.14.2)

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.3]

children.text:
prāṇo 'pāno vyāna ity aṣṭāv akṣarāṇi |
aṣṭākṣaraṃ ha vā ekaṃ gāyatryai padam |
etad u haivāsyā etat |
sa yāvad idaṃ prāṇi tāvad dha jayati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda |
athāsyā etad eva turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ parorajā ya eṣa tapati |
yad vai caturthaṃ tat turīyam |
darśataṃ padam iti dadṛśa iva hy eṣaḥ |
parorajā iti sarvam u hy evaiṣa raja upary upari tapati |
evaṃ haiva śriyā yaśasā tapati yo 'syā etad evaṃ padaṃ veda || BrhUp_5,14.3 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>' — these are eight syllables. One foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> has eight syllables. This is indeed that [foot] of hers. He conquers as much as is living here, who knows this foot of hers in this way. Now, this is its fourth, visible foot, shining beyond the dust (<s>rajas</s>) — the one who blazes yonder [the sun]. 'Fourth' means <s>turīya</s>. 'Visible foot' — for he is, as it were, seen. 'Beyond the dust' — for he blazes above and above all this dust. Thus indeed does one blaze with glory and renown, who knows this foot of hers in this way. (BṛUp 5.14.3)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.3 tathā prāṇo 'pāno vyāna etānyapi prāṇādyabhidhānākṣarāṇyaṣṭau /
tacca gāyatryāstṛtīyaṃ padaṃ yāvadidaṃ prāṇijātaṃ tāvaddha jayati yo 'syā etadevaṃ gāyatryāstṛtīyaṃ padaṃ veda /
athānantaraṃ gāyatryāsripadāyāḥ śabdātmikāyāsturīyaṃ padamucyate 'bhidheyabhūtamasyāḥ prakṛtāyā gāyatryā etadeva vakṣyamāmaṃ turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ parorajā ya eṣa tapati /
turīyamityādivākyapadārthaṃ svameva vyācaṣṭe śrutiḥ-yadvai caturthaṃ prasiddhaṃ loke tadidaṃ turīyaśabdenābhidhīyate /
darśataṃ padamityasya kor'tha ityucyate-dadṛśa iva dṛśyata iva hyeṣa maṇḍalasthaḥ puruṣo rajo rajojātaṃ samastaṃ lokamityarthaḥ /
uparyuparyādhipatyabhāvena sarvaṃ lokaṃ rajojātaṃ tapati /
uparyuparīti vīpsā sarvalokādhipatyakhyāpanārthā /
nanu sarvaśabdenaiva siddhatvādvīpsānarthikā /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
yeṣāmupariṣṭātsavitā dṛśyate tadviṣaya eva sarvaśabdaḥ syādityāśaṅkānivṛttyarthā vīpsā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Objection:] But since the purpose is already accomplished by the word 'all' (<s>sarva</s>), the repetition is purposeless. [Reply:] This is no fault.

children.text: "ye cāmuṣmātparāñco lokāsteṣāṃ ceṣṭe devakānāṃ ca"iti śrutyanrāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the word 'all' might apply only to those worlds above which the sun is visible — for the purpose of removing this doubt, the repetition is used. Because of the <s>śruti</s>: 'And he rules over those worlds that are beyond that, and over the desires of the gods' (BṛUp 3.8.9).

children.text: tasmātsarvāvarodhārthā vīpsā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the repetition is for the purpose of including all [worlds].

children.text: yathāsau savitā sarvādhipatyalakṣaṇayā śriyā yaśasā ca khyātyā tapatyevaṃ haiva śriyā yaśasā ca tapati yo 'syā etadevaṃ turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ veda //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Just as that sun blazes with glory characterized by sovereignty over all, and with renown (<s>yaśas</s>), with fame — even so indeed, one blazes with glory and renown, who knows this fourth, visible foot [of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>] in this way. (5.14.3)

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.3:] Likewise, '<s>prāṇa</s>, <s>apāna</s>, <s>vyāna</s>' — these syllables of the names of the <s>prāṇas</s> are also eight. And this is the third foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. He conquers as much as there is of living beings here — who knows this third foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> in this way. Then — next — of this three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> that consists of words, the fourth foot is stated as the referent — of this <s>Gāyatrī</s> that is the topic — this, which is about to be stated, is the fourth, visible foot, [shining] beyond the dust, the one who blazes yonder [the sun]. '<s>Turīya</s>' and so forth — the sentence-words are explained by the <s>śruti</s> itself: what is well known in the world as the fourth (<s>caturtha</s>) — that is denoted here by the word '<s>turīya</s>.' 'Visible foot' — what is the meaning of this? It is said: '<s>dadṛśa iva</s>' — as it were, visible — for this <s>puruṣa</s> stationed in the solar disc [appears to be seen]. '<s>Rajas</s>' — the entirety of the world — this is the meaning. Above and above — in the capacity of sovereignty over all — he blazes over the entire world, the entirety of <s>rajas</s>. 'Above and above' — the repetition is for the purpose of indicating sovereignty over all worlds.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.4]

children.text:
saiṣā gāyatry etasmiṃs turīye darśate pade parorajasi pratiṣṭhitā |
tad vai tat satye pratiṣṭhitam |
cakṣur vai satyam |
cakṣur hi vai satyam |
tasmād yad idānīṃ dvau vivadamānāv eyātam aham adarśam aham aśrauṣam iti |
ya evaṃ brūyād aham adarśam iti |
tasmā eva śraddadhyāma |
tad vai tat satyaṃ bale pratiṣṭhitam |
prāṇo vai balam |
tat prāṇe pratiṣṭhitam |
tasmād āhur balaṃ satyād ogīya iti |
evaṃ v eṣā gāyatry adhyātmaṃ pratiṣṭhitā |
sā haiṣā gayāṃs tatre |
prāṇā vai gayāḥ |
tat prāṇās tatre |
tad yad gayāṃs tatre tasmād gāyatrī nāma |
sa yām evāmūṃ sāvitrīm anvāhaiṣaiva sā |
sa yasmā anvāha tasya prāṇāṃs trāyate || BrhUp_5,14.4 ||
children.translated_text: This <s>Gāyatrī</s> is established upon this fourth, visible foot, [shining] beyond the dust (<s>rajas</s>). And that indeed is established upon <s>Satya</s> (truth). For the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) is <s>Satya</s>. The eye indeed is <s>Satya</s>. Therefore, if two persons were to come disputing, one saying 'I saw' and the other 'I heard' — we should trust the one who says 'I saw.' And that <s>Satya</s> indeed is established upon strength (<s>bala</s>). <s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is strength. That [<s>Satya</s>] is established upon <s>prāṇa</s>. Therefore they say: 'Strength is mightier than truth.' Thus is this <s>Gāyatrī</s> established with reference to the self (<s>adhyātma</s>). She indeed protected (<s>tatre</s>) the <s>gayas</s> (vital breaths). The <s>prāṇas</s> indeed are the <s>gayas</s>. She protected the <s>prāṇas</s>. Because she protected the <s>gayas</s>, therefore she is called <s>Gāyatrī</s>. And that <s>Sāvitrī</s> which one recites — this is she indeed. And to whomever one recites it, she protects his <s>prāṇas</s>. (BṛUp 5.14.4)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.4 saiṣā tripadoktā yā trailokyatraividyaprāṇalakṣaṇā gāyatryetasmiṃścaturthe turīye darśate pade parorajasi pratiṣṭhitā /
mūrtāmūrtarasatvādādityasya /
rasāpāye hi vastu nīrasamapratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati /
yathā kāṣṭhādi dagdhasāraṃ tadvat /
tathā mūrtāmūrtarasatvādādityasya /
rasāpāye hi vastu nīrasamapratiṣṭhitaṃ bhavati /
yathā kāṣṭhādi dagdhasāraṃ tadvat /
tathā mūrtāmūrtātmakaṃ jagattripadā gāyatryāditye pratiṣṭhitā tadrasatvātsaha tribhiḥ pādaiḥ /
tadvai turīyaṃ padaṃ satye pratiṣṭhitam /
kiṃ punastatsatyamityucyate-cakṣurvai satyam /
kathaṃ cakṣuḥ satyamityāha-prasiddhametaccakṣurhi vai satyam /
kathaṃ prasiddhatetyāha-tasmādyadidānīmeva dvau vivadamānau viruddhaṃ vadamānāveyātāmāgaccheyātāmahamadarśaṃ dṛṣṭavānanasmītyanya āhāhamaśrauṣaṃ tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ na tathā tadvastviti tayorya evaṃ brūyādahamadrākṣamiti tasmā eva śraddadhyāma napunaryo brūyādahamaśrauṣamiti /
śroturmṛṣā śravaṇamapi saṃbhavati na tu cakṣuṣo mṛṣā darśanam /
tasmānnāśrauṣamityuktavate śraddadhyāma /
tasmātsatyapratipattihetutvātsatyaṃ cakṣustasminsatye cakṣuṣi saha tribhiritaraiḥ pādaisturīyaṃ padaṃ pratiṣṭhitamityarthaḥ /
uktaṃ ca sa ādityaḥ kasminpratiṣṭhita iti cakṣuṣīti /
tadvai turīyapadāśrayaṃ satyaṃ bale pratiṣṭhitam /
kiṃ punastadbalamityāha-prāṇo vai balaṃ tasminprāṇe bale pratiṣṭhitaṃ satyam /
tathā coktaṃ sūtre tadotaṃ ca protaṃ ceti /
yasmādbale satyaṃ pratiṣṭhitaṃ tasmādāhurbalaṃ satyādogīya ojīya ojastaramityarthaḥ /
loke 'pi yasminhi yadāśritaṃ bhavati tasmādāśritādāśrayasya balavattaratvaṃ prasiddham /
na hi durbalaṃ balavataḥ kvacidāśrayabhūtaṃ dṛṣṭam /
evamuktanyāyena u eṣā gāyatryadhyātmamadhyātme prāṇe pratiṣṭhitā /
saiṣā gāyatrī prāṇaḥ /
ato gāyatryāṃ jagatpratiṣṭhitam /
yasminprāṇe sarve devā ekaṃ bhavanti /
sarvaṃ vedāḥ karmāṇi phalaṃ ca saivaṃ gāyatrī prāṇarūpā satī jagata ātmā /
sā haiṣā gayāṃstatre trātavatī /
ke punargayāḥ prāṇā vāgādayo vai gayāḥ /
śabdakaramāt /
tāṃstatre saiṣā gāyatrī /
tattatra yadyasmādgayāṃstatre tasmādgāyatrī nāma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because (<s>yat</s>) — since she protected the <s>gayās</s> (vital powers), therefore she is called <s>Gāyatrī</s> by name.

children.text: gāyatrāṇādgāyatrīti prathitā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From the protecting of the <s>gayās</s> (<s>gāyatrāṇāt</s>), [she is] renowned as <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: sa ācārya upanīya māṇavakamaṣṭavarṣaṃ yāmevāmūṃ gāyatrīṃ sāvitrīṃ savitṛdevatākāmanvāha pacchordharcaśaḥ samastāṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), having initiated (<s>upanīya</s>) the boy (<s>māṇavaka</s>) of eight years, recites to him this very <s>Gāyatrī</s> as the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra] — which has <s>Savitṛ</s> as its deity — foot by foot, verse by verse, and also in its entirety.

children.text: eṣaiva sā sākṣātprāṇo jagata ātmā māṇavakāya samarpitehedānīṃ vyākhyātā nānyā sa ācāryo yasmai māṇavakāyānvāhānuvakti tasya māṇavakasya gayānprāṇāṃsrāyate narakādipatanāt //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This very one — directly <s>prāṇa</s>, the self of the world — is now explained as having been imparted to the boy. Not any other [<s>Gāyatrī</s>]. The teacher who recites [it] to whichever boy — that boy's vital powers (<s>gayās</s>), his <s>prāṇas</s>, [the teacher] protects from falling into hell and the like. // 5.14.4 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.4:] This <s>Gāyatrī</s>, spoken of as having three feet — characterized by the three worlds, the three <s>Vedas</s>, and the <s>prāṇas</s> — is established in this fourth, the <s>turīya</s> (fourth) foot, visible, beyond the dust (<s>parorajas</s>),
because <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is the essence of both the formed and the formless.
For when the essence departs from a thing, that thing becomes essence-less, without support —
just as wood and the like whose core has been burnt [become unsupported] — so it is.
Likewise, because <s>Āditya</s> (the sun) is the essence of the formed and the formless —
for when the essence departs from a thing, that thing becomes essence-less, without support —
just as wood and the like whose core has been burnt [become unsupported] — so it is.
Thus, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of three feet — [representing] the world consisting of the formed and the formless — is established in <s>Āditya</s> (the sun), because it is their essence, together with [its] three feet.
That very fourth foot is established in <s>satya</s> (truth).
What then is that <s>satya</s>? It is said: the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) indeed is truth.
How is the eye truth? [The text] says: this is well-known — the eye indeed is truth.
How is it well-known? [The text] says: therefore, if even now two persons were to come, disputing, speaking contradictory [things] — 'I saw it, I have seen it' says one; 'I heard it — what you saw is not so, that is not the reality' [says the other] — of these two, the one who says 'I saw it' — to him alone we would give credence, not to the one who says 'I heard it.'
For the hearer, false hearing is also possible; but for the eye, false seeing [is not possible].
Therefore, we would not give credence to the one who said 'I heard it.'
Therefore, because the eye is the cause of the ascertainment of truth — the eye is truth; in that truth, the eye, together with the three other feet, the fourth foot is established — this is the meaning.
And it was stated: 'In what is that <s>Āditya</s> established?' — 'In the eye.'
That very truth, which is the support of the fourth foot, is established in strength (<s>bala</s>).
What then is that strength? It is said: <s>prāṇa</s> (breath) is indeed strength; in that <s>prāṇa</s>, in that strength, truth is established.
And thus it was stated in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'By that [everything] is woven, warp and weft.'
Since truth is established in strength, therefore they say: strength is more powerful than truth — meaning: more vigorous, more forceful.
Even in the world, it is well-known that the support is stronger than what is supported by it.
For a weak [thing] is never seen to be the support of a strong [thing].
Thus, by the method stated, this <s>Gāyatrī</s> is — with reference to the individual self (<s>adhyātma</s>) — established in the <s>prāṇa</s>, in the individual self.
This <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>prāṇa</s>.
Therefore, the world is established in the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
In that <s>prāṇa</s>, all the gods become one.
All [things] — the <s>Vedas</s>, actions, and their fruits — this very <s>Gāyatrī</s>, being of the nature of <s>prāṇa</s>, is the self of the world.
She (<s>Gāyatrī</s>) has protected (<s>tatre</s>) the <s>gayās</s> (vital powers).
What then are the <s>gayās</s>? The <s>prāṇas</s> — speech and the rest — are indeed the <s>gayās</s> (vital powers).
Because of the etymology of the word [<s>gāyatrī</s> = <s>gayāṃs trāyate</s>].
She has protected those [vital powers] — this is [the meaning of] <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.5]

children.text:
tāṃ haitām eke sāvitrīm anuṣṭubham anvāhuḥ |
vāg anuṣṭup |
etad vācam anubrūma iti |
na tathā kuryāt |
gāyatrīm eva sāvitrīm ānubrūyāt |
yadi ha vā apy evaṃvid bahv iva pratigṛhṇāti na haiva tad gāyatryā ekaṃ cana padaṃ prati || BrhUp_5,14.5 ||
children.translated_text: Some recite to [the student] that <s>Sāvitrī</s> in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> metre, [saying:] 'Speech is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>; we are reciting this speech [to the student].' One should not do so. One should recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [metre] alone. Even if one who knows thus receives what appears to be a large [gift], that is not equal even to one foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. (BṛUp 5.14.5)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.5 tāmetāṃ sāvitrīṃ haike śākhino 'nuṣṭupchandaskāmanvāhurupanītāya /
tadabhiprāyamāha-vāganuṣṭup /
vākca śarīre sarasvatī tāmeva hi vācaṃ sarasvatīṃ māṇavakāyānubrūma ityetadvadantaḥ /
na tathā kuryānna tathā vidyādyatta āhurmṛṣaiva tat /
kiṃ tarhi gāyatrīmeva sāvitrīmanubrūyāt /
kasmāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Why?

children.text: yasmātprāṇo gāyatrītyuktam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because it has been stated that <s>prāṇa</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: prāṇa ukte vākca sarasvatī cānye ta prāṇāḥ sarvaṃ māṇavakāya samarpitaṃ bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When <s>prāṇa</s> is stated [as the <s>Gāyatrī</s>], and speech and <s>Sarasvatī</s> and the other <s>prāṇas</s> [are included therein], everything has been imparted to the boy.

children.text: kiñcedaṃ prāsaṅgikamuktvā gāyatrīvidaṃ stauti-yadi ha vā apyevaṃvidbahviva na hi tasya sarvātmano bahu nāmāsti kicitsarvātmakatvādviduṣaḥ pratigṛhṇāti na haiva tatpratigrahajātaṃ gāyatryā ekañcanaikamapi padaṃ prati paryāptam //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Furthermore, having stated this incidental [point], [the text] praises the knowledge of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>: Even if one who knows thus receives what appears to be a large [gift] — for indeed, for one who is the self of all, nothing is 'large,' because everything is the self of the knower — [even if he] receives [such a gift], that entire amount received is not equal to, is not sufficient for, even one, even a single foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. // 5.14.5 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.5:] This very <s>Sāvitrī</s> — some teachers of certain [Vedic] branches (<s>śākhin</s>) recite to the initiated [student] in the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> metre.
The [text] states their intention: 'Speech is <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.' And speech, in the body, is <s>Sarasvatī</s>. Saying 'We are reciting this speech, this <s>Sarasvatī</s>, to the boy' — thus they speak.
One should not do so — one should not hold that view. What they say is simply false.
What then? One should recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> in the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [metre] alone.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.6]

children.text:
sa ya imāṃs trīṃl lokān pūrṇān pratigṛhṇīyāt so 'syā etat prathamaṃ padam āpnuyāt |
atha yāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā yas tāvat pratigṛhṇīyāt so 'syā etad dvitīyaṃ padam āpnuyāt |
atha yāvad idaṃ prāṇi yas tāvat pratigṛhṇīyāt so 'syā etat tṛtīyaṃ padam āpnuyāt |
athāsyā etad eva turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ parorajā ya eṣa tapati |
naiva kena canāpyam |
kuta u etāvat pratigṛhṇīyāt || BrhUp_5,14.6 ||
children.translated_text: If someone were to receive [as a gift] these three worlds filled [with wealth], he would obtain [only] that first foot of hers [the <s>Gāyatrī</s>]. And if someone were to receive as much as this threefold knowledge [extends to], he would obtain [only] that second foot of hers. And if someone were to receive as much as there are living beings, he would obtain [only] that third foot of hers. But that fourth foot of hers — visible, beyond the dust (<s>parorajas</s>), the one who shines yonder — that is not attainable by anyone at all. How then could anyone receive so much? (BṛUp 5.14.6)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.6 sa ya imāṃsrīnsa yo gāyatrīvidimānbhūrādīṃsrīngo 'śvādidhanapūrṇāṃllokānpratigṛhṇīyātsa pratigraho 'syā gāyatryā etatprathamaṃ padaṃ yadvyākhyātamāpnuyātprathamapadavijñānaphalaṃ tena bhuktaṃ syānna tvadhikadoṣotpādakaḥ sa pratigrahaḥ /
atha punaryāvatīyaṃ trayī vidyā yastāvatpratigṛhṇīyātso 'syā etattṛtīyaṃ padamāpnuyāt /
tena tṛtīyapadavijñānaphalaṃ bhuktaṃ syāt /
kalpayitvedamicyate /
pādatrayasamamapi yadi kaścitpratigṛhṇīyāttatpādatrayavijñānaphalasyaiva kṣayakāraṇaṃ na tvanyasya doṣasya kartṛtve kṣamam /
na caivaṃ dātā pratigrahītā vā /
gāyatrīvijñānastutaye kalpyate /
dātā pratigrahītā ca yadyapyevaṃ saṃbhāvyate nāsau pratigraho 'parādhakṣamaḥ /
kasmādyato 'bhyadhikamapi puruṣārthavijñānamavaśiṣṭameva caturthapādaviṣayaṃ gāyatryāstaddarśayati /
athāsyā etadeva turīyaṃ darśataṃ padaṃ parorajā ya eṣa tapati /
yaccaitannaiva kenacana kenacidapi pratigraheṇā'pyaṃ naiva prāpyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] That which is indeed not attainable by anyone, by any receiving whatsoever — this is the meaning.

children.text: yathā pūrvoktāni trīṇi padāni /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Just as the aforementioned three feet [are not attainable].

children.text: etānyapi naivā'pyāni kenacitkalpayitvaivamuktaṃ paramārthataḥ kuta u etāvatpratigṛhṇoyāttrailokyādisamam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Even those are not attainable by anyone — this being stated as a hypothetical construction — how then, in ultimate reality, could anyone receive so much, equal to the three worlds and the rest?

children.text: tasmādgāyatryevaṃprakāropāsyetyarthaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of such a nature should be meditated upon — this is the meaning. // 5.14.6 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.6:] 'If someone' — if someone who knows the <s>Gāyatrī</s> were to receive these three [worlds] — the three worlds beginning with <s>Bhūḥ</s> — filled with wealth such as cows, horses, and the like — that receiving would [correspond to having] obtained the first foot of this <s>Gāyatrī</s>, namely that which was explained [earlier]. The fruit of the knowledge of the first foot would thereby be consumed — the receiving would not produce additional fault.
Furthermore, if someone were to receive as much as this threefold knowledge [extends to], he would obtain that third foot of hers.
The fruit of the knowledge of the third foot would thereby be consumed.
This is stated as a hypothetical construction.
Even if someone were to receive [a gift] equal to [all] three feet, that would be a cause for the consumption of the fruit of the knowledge of the three feet only, and would not be capable of producing any other fault.
Nor is there any such giver or receiver [in reality].
[This] is hypothetically constructed for the praise of the knowledge of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Even if a giver and receiver were thus imagined, that receiving would not be capable of causing harm.
Why? Because even greater — the knowledge of human purpose pertaining to the fourth foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — remains [unexhausted]. This [the text] shows:
But that fourth foot of hers — visible, beyond the dust (<s>parorajas</s>), the one who shines yonder —

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.7]

children.text:
tasyā upasthānam |
gāyatry asy ekapadī dvipadī tripadī catuṣpadi |
apad asi |
na hi padyase |
namas te turīyāya darśatāya padāya parorajase |
asāv ado mā prāpad iti |
yaṃ dviṣyād asāv asmai kāmo mā samardhīti vā |
na haivāsmai sa kāmaḥ samṛdhyate yasmā evam upatiṣṭhate |
aham adaḥ prāpam iti vā || BrhUp_5,14.7 ||
children.translated_text:
The <s>upasthāna</s> (salutation) to it [the <s>Gāyatrī</s>]:
'O <s>Gāyatrī</s>, you are one-footed, two-footed, three-footed, four-footed.
You are footless (<s>apad</s>), for you do not walk (<s>na hi padyase</s>).
Salutation to your fourth, visible foot, beyond the dust (<s>parorajas</s>)!
May that [enemy] not attain that [goal]!'
Or [one may recite:] 'May his desire not be fulfilled' — regarding one whom [the meditator] dislikes.
Indeed, that desire is not fulfilled for the one against whom [the meditator] thus makes this <s>upasthāna</s>.
Or [one may recite:] 'May I attain that [goal]!' (BṛUp 5.14.7)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.7 tasyā upasthānaṃ tasyā gāyatryā upasthānamupetya sthānaṃ namaskaraṇamanena mantreṇa /
kau'sau mantra ityāha-he gāyatryasi bhavasi trailokyapādenaikapadī trayīvidyārūpeṇa dvitīyena dvipadī /
prāṇādinā tṛtīyena tripadyasi /
caturthena turīyeṇa catuṣpadyasi /
evaṃ caturbhiḥ pādairupāsakaiḥ padyase jñāyase 'taḥ paraṃ pareṇa nirupādhikena svenā'tmanāpadasi /
avidyamānaṃ padaṃ yasyāstava yena padyase sā tvamapadasi yasmānnahi padyase neti netyātmatvāt /
ato vyavahāraviṣayāya namabhte turīyāya darśatāya padāya poradase /
asau śatruḥ pāpmā tvatprāptivighnakaro 'dastadātmanaḥ kāryaṃ yattvatprāptivighnakartṛtvaṃ mā prāpanmaiva prāpnotu /
itiśabdo mantraparisamāptyarthaḥ /
yaṃ dviṣyādyaṃ prati dveṣaṃ kuryātsvayaṃ vidvāṃstaṃ pratyanenopasthānamasau śatruramukanāmeti nāma gṛhṇīyādasmai yajñadattāyābhipretaḥ kāmo mā samṛddhi samṛddhiṃ mā prāpnotviti vopatiṣṭhate /
na haivāsmai devadattāya sa kāmaḥ samṛdhyate /
kasmai /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For whom [is it not fulfilled]?

children.text: yasmā evamupatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the one against whom he thus makes the <s>upasthāna</s>.

children.text: ahamado devadattābhipretaṃ prāpamiti vopatiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Or [one may say:] 'May I attain that [goal] desired by <s>Devadatta</s>' — thus one makes the <s>upasthāna</s>.

children.text: asāvado mā prāpadityāditrayāṇāṃ mantrapadānāṃ yathākāmaṃ vikalpaḥ //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Of these three <s>mantra</s>-phrases — 'May that one not attain that' and so forth — there is an option (<s>vikalpa</s>) according to one's wish. // 5.14.7 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.7:] 'The <s>upasthāna</s> to it' — the <s>upasthāna</s> of this <s>Gāyatrī</s> — meaning: the act of approaching and standing [before it], i.e., salutation — by means of this <s>mantra</s>.
What is that <s>mantra</s>? It is said: O <s>Gāyatrī</s>, you are — you exist — one-footed through the foot [consisting of] the three worlds; two-footed through the second [foot consisting of] the threefold knowledge;
three-footed through the third [foot consisting of] the <s>prāṇas</s> and the like;
four-footed through the fourth, the <s>turīya</s> [foot].
Thus, by [these] four feet, you are known (<s>padyase</s>) by the meditators. Beyond that, by your own unconditioned (<s>nirupādhika</s>) self, you are footless (<s>apad</s>).
You have no foot by which you could be known — you are footless — because you do not walk (<s>na hi padyase</s>) — because of the '<s>neti neti</s>'-nature of the self.
Therefore, salutation to the <s>turīya</s> (fourth), visible, foot, beyond the dust (<s>parorajas</s>) — which is accessible to conventional worship.
'May that enemy, that evil one who obstructs the attainment of you — may that action of his, namely the obstruction of your attainment — not succeed, not prevail!'
The word '<s>iti</s>' serves to conclude the <s>mantra</s>.
'Regarding one whom one dislikes' — against whomever the wise person himself bears ill-will — toward that one he makes this <s>upasthāna</s>: 'May the desired goal of this enemy, named so-and-so' — taking his name — 'of this <s>Yajñadatta</s>, not succeed, not attain fulfillment!' — thus one makes the <s>upasthāna</s>.
Indeed, for that <s>Devadatta</s>, that desire is not fulfilled.

children.text: START BrhUp 5,14.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.14.8]

children.text:
etad dha vai taj janako vaideho buḍilam āśvatarāśvim uvāca -- yan nu ho tad gāyatrīvid abrūthāḥ |
atha kathaṃ hastībhūto vahasīti |
mukhaṃ hy asyāḥ samrāṇ na vidāṃ cakareti hovāca |
tasyā agnir eva mukham |
yadi ha vā api bahv ivāgnāv abhyādadhati sarvam eva tat saṃdahati |
evaṃ haivaivaṃvid yady api bahv iva pāpaṃ kurute sarvam eva tat saṃpsāya śuddhaḥ pūto 'jaro 'mṛtaḥ saṃbhavati || BrhUp_5,14.8 ||
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> said to <s>Buḍila Āśvatarāśvi</s>: 'Well now, you used to say that you know the <s>Gāyatrī</s>. Then how is it that you have become an elephant and are carrying [burdens]?' [<s>Buḍila</s>] replied: 'Because I did not know its mouth (<s>mukha</s>), O Emperor.' Its mouth is fire (<s>Agni</s>). Even if one were to pile much [fuel] into fire, it burns everything. Even so, one who knows thus — even if he commits what appears to be much sin — he consumes (<s>saṃpsāya</s>) all of it and becomes pure, clean, unaging, and immortal. (BṛUp 5.14.8)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,14.8 gāyatryā mukhavidhānāyārthavāda ucyate-etaddha kila vai smaryate /
tattatra gāyatrīvijñānaviṣaye janako vaideho buḍilo nāmato 'śvatarāśvasyāpatyamāśvatarāśvistaṃ kiloktavān /
yannu iti vitarke ho aho ityetattadyattvaṃ gāyatrīvidbrūthā gāyatrīvidasmīti yadabrūthāḥ kimidaṃ tasya vacaso 'nanurūpam /
atha kathaṃ yadi gāyatrīvitpratigrahadoṣeṇa hastobhūto vahasīti /
sa pratyāha rājñā smārito mukhaṃ gāyatryā hi yasmādasyā he samrāṇna vidāñcakāra na vijñātavānasmīti hovāca /
ekāhgavikalatvādgāyatrīvijñānaṃ mamāphalaṃ jātam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Because my knowledge of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> was incomplete in one limb, it became fruitless for me.'

children.text: śṛṇu tarhi tasyā gāyatryā agnireva mukham /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Then hear! The mouth of that <s>Gāyatrī</s> is fire (<s>Agni</s>) alone.'

children.text: yadi ha vā api bahvivendhanamagnāvabhyādadhati laukikāḥ sarvameva tatsaṃdahatyevendhanamagnirevaṃ haivaivaṃvidgāyatryā agnirmukhamityevaṃ vettītyevaṃvitsyātsvayaṃ gāyatryātmāgnimukhaḥ san /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even if people pile much fuel into the fire — the ordinary [fire] — it burns all that fuel entirely. Even so, one who knows thus — who knows that the mouth of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> is fire — being himself of the nature of <s>Gāyatrī</s>, having fire as his mouth —'

children.text: yadyapi bahviva pāpaṃ kurute pratigrahādidoṣaṃ tatsarvaṃ pāpajātaṃ saṃpsāya bhakṣayitvā śuddho 'gnivatpūtaśca tasmātpratigrahadoṣādgāyatryātmājaro 'mṛtaśca saṃbhavati //8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Even if he commits what appears to be much sin — the fault of improper receiving and the like — he consumes (<s>saṃpsāya</s>), devours, all that accumulated sin, and becomes pure, like fire, and clean — therefore free from the fault of [improper] receiving — and unaging and immortal, being of the nature of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>-self. // 5.14.8 //'

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.14.8:] For the purpose of prescribing the mouth of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, a laudatory passage (<s>arthavāda</s>) is stated: 'This indeed' — this is remembered, this is well-known. In that — in the matter of the knowledge of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — <s>Janaka</s> of <s>Videha</s> is said to have spoken to <s>Buḍila</s> by name, a descendant of <s>Aśvatarāśva</s>, called <s>Āśvatarāśvi</s>.
'Well now' (<s>yan nu</s>) — expressing deliberation — '<s>ho</s>' means 'indeed' — 'that which you used to say: "I am a knower of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>"' — 'what about that claim, which is inconsistent with [your situation]?'
'Then how — if you are a knower of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — have you become an elephant through the fault of receiving [improper gifts] and are carrying [burdens]?'
He replied — reminded by the king — 'Because I did not know the mouth (<s>mukha</s>) of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, O Emperor, I did not know it' — thus he said.

children.text: iti śrīmadbṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadbhāṣye pañcamādhyāyasya caturdaśaṃ brāhmaṇam //14//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the commentary on the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 14 //

children.text: START BrhUp 5,15.1
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 5.15.1]

children.text:
hiraṇmayena pātreṇa satyasyāpihitaṃ mukham |
tat tvam pūṣann apāvṛṇu satyadharmāya dṛṣṭaye |
pūṣann ekarṣe yama sūrya prājāpatya vyūha raśmīn samūha tejaḥ |
yat te rūpaṃ kalyāṇatamam tat te paśyāmi yo 'sāv asau puruṣaḥ so 'ham asmi |
vāyur anilam amṛtam athedaṃ bhasmāntaṃ śarīram |
oṃ krato smara kṛtaṃ smara krato smara kṛtaṃ smara |
agne naya supathā rāye 'smān viśvāni deva vayunāni vidvān |
yuyodhy asmaj juhurāṇam eno bhūyiṣṭhāṃ te namauktiṃ vidhema || BrhUp_5,15.1 ||
children.translated_text: By a golden vessel is the face of truth covered. Do you, O <s>Pūṣan</s>, uncover it — for the one whose <s>dharma</s> is truth, for [his] seeing. O <s>Pūṣan</s>, O sole seer (<s>ekarṣi</s>), O <s>Yama</s>, O <s>Sūrya</s>, O son of <s>Prajāpati</s> — withdraw your rays, gather up your brilliance. That form of yours which is most auspicious — that [form] of yours I behold. He who is that person [in the sun] — I am he. [May my] breath [merge with] the immortal wind (<s>anila</s>), and then may this body [end] in ashes. <s>Oṃ</s>! O <s>Kratu</s> (resolve), remember! Remember what has been done! O <s>Kratu</s>, remember! Remember what has been done! O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to prosperity — O God, you who know all the ways [of beings]. Remove from us the crooked sin. We shall offer you the most abundant words of homage. // BṛUp 5.15.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_5,15.1 yo jñānakarmasamuccayakārī so 'ntakāla ādityaṃ prārthayati /
asti ca prasaṅgo gāyatryāsturīyaḥ pādo hi saḥ /
tadupasthānaṃ prakṛtamataḥ sa eva prārthyate /
hiraṇyamayena jyotirmayena pātreṇa yathā pātreṇeṣṭaṃ vastvapidhīyata evamidaṃ satyākhyaṃ brahma jyotirmayena maṇḍalenāpihitamivāsamāhitacetasāmadṛśyatvāttaducyate /
satyasyāpihitaṃ mukhaṃ mukhyaṃ svarūpaṃ tadapidhānaṃ pātramapidhānamiva darśanapratibandhakāraṇaṃ tattvaṃ he pūṣañjagataḥ poṣaṇatpūṣā savitāpāvṛṇvapāvṛtaṃ kuru darśanapratibandhakāraṇamapanayetyarthaḥ /
satyadharmāya satyaṃ dharmo 'sya mama so 'haṃ satyadharmā tasmai tvadātmabhūtāyetyarthaḥ /
dṛṣṭaye darśanāya /
pūṣannityādīni nāmānyāmantraṇārthani savituḥ /
ekarṣa ekaścāsāvṛṣiścaikarṣirdarśanādṛṣiḥ /
sa hi sarvasya jagata ātmā cakṣuśca sansarvaṃ paśyatyeko vā gacchatītyekarṣiḥ"sūrya ekākī carati"iti mantravarṇāt /
yama sarvaṃ hi jagataḥ saṃyamanaṃ tvatkṛtam /
sūrya suṣṭhu vīrayate rasānraśmīnprāṇāndhiyo vā jagata iti /
prājāpatya prajāpaterīśvarasyāpatyaṃ hiraṇyagarbhasya vā he prājāpatya vyūha vigamaya raśmīn /
samūha saṃkṣipā'tmanastejo yenāhaṃ śaknuyāṃ tvatsvarūpamañjasā draṣṭam /
vidyotana iva rūpāṇāmata upasaṃhara tejaḥ /
yatte tava rūpaṃ sarvakalyāṇānāmatiśayena kalyāṇaṃ kalyāṇatamaṃ tatte paśyāmi /
paśyāmo vayaṃ vacanavyatyayena /
yo 'sau bhūrbhuvaḥsvarvyāhṛtyavayavaḥ puruṣaḥ puruṣākṛtitvātpuruṣaḥ so 'hamasmi bhavāmi /
aharamiti copaniṣada uktatvādādityacākṣuṣayostadevedaṃ parāmṛśyate so 'hamasmyamṛtamiti saṃbandhaḥ /
mamāmṛtasya satyasya śarīrapāte śarīrastho yaḥ prāṇo vāyuḥ so 'nilaṃ bāhyaṃ vāyumeva pratigacchatu /
tathānyā devatāḥ svāṃ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ gacchantu /
athedamapi bhasmāntaṃ satpṛthivīṃ yātu śarīram /
athedānīmātmanaḥ saṃkalpabhūtāṃ manasi vyavasthitāmagnidevatāṃ prārthayate-oṃ krato /
oṃmiti krato iti ca saṃbodhanārthaveva /
oṅkārapratīkatvādom /
manomayatvācca kratuḥ /
he oṃ he krato smara smartavyamantakāle hi tvatsmaraṇavaśādiṣṭā gatiḥ prāpyate 'taḥ prārthyate yanmayā kṛtaṃ tatsmara punaruktirādarārthā /
kiñca he 'gne naya prāpaya supathā śobhanena mārgeṇa rāye dhanāya karmaphalaprāptaya ityarthaḥ /
na dakṣiṇena kṛṣṇena punarāvṛttiyuktena kiṃ tarhi śuklenaiva supathāsmānviśvāni sarvāṇi he deva vayunāni prajñānāni sarvaprāṇināṃ vidvān /
kiñca yuyodhyapanaya viyojayāsmadasmatto juhurāṇaṃ kuṭilamenaḥ pāpaṃ pāpajātaṃ sarvam /
tena pāpena viyuktā vayameṣyāma uttareṇa pathā tvatprasādāt /
kintu vayaṃ tubhyaṃ paricaryāṃ kartuṃ na śaknumo bhūyiṣṭhāṃ bahutamāṃ te tubhyaṃ namauktiṃ namaskāravacanaṃ vidhema namaskāroktyā paricaremetyarthaḥ /
anyatkartumaśaktāḥ santa iti //1 // //
children.translated_text: Being unable to do anything else. // 5.15.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 5.15.1:] He who is a practitioner of the combination of knowledge and <s>karma</s> (<s>jñānakarmasamuccaya</s>) — at the time of death, he entreats <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). And there is a contextual connection with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> — for the fourth foot [of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>] is he [the Sun]. The worship of that [fourth foot] is the subject at hand; therefore, it is that very [Sun] who is entreated. 'By a golden vessel' — by a vessel made of light — just as a desired object is covered by a vessel, even so this <s>Brahman</s> called 'Truth' (<s>Satya</s>) is as if covered by the luminous orb [of the Sun] — because it is invisible to those whose minds are not concentrated. That is what is said. The face of Truth is covered — the principal form, its essential nature. That covering vessel, as it were, is a cause that obstructs [its] seeing. 'You, O <s>Pūṣan</s>' — <s>Pūṣan</s> is <s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun), because of nourishing (<s>poṣaṇa</s>) the world — 'uncover' — make it uncovered, remove the cause that obstructs seeing — this is the meaning. 'For one whose <s>dharma</s> is truth' (<s>satyadharmāya</s>) — truth is the <s>dharma</s> of me — I am one whose <s>dharma</s> is truth — for such a one, meaning: for one who has become identical with you — this is the meaning. 'For seeing' (<s>dṛṣṭaye</s>) — for the purpose of seeing. '<s>Pūṣan</s>' and the other [words] are forms of address for <s>Savitṛ</s>. '<s>Ekar���i</s>' (sole seer) — he is one and a seer — hence <s>ekarṣi</s>; a seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>) because of seeing (<s>darśana</s>). For he is the self and the eye of the entire world — he sees everything. Or, he goes alone — hence <s>ekarṣi</s>, from the <s>mantra</s> text: '<s>Sūrya</s> moves alone' (RV). '<s>Yama</s>' — for all the restraint (<s>saṃyamana</s>) of the world is caused by you. '<s>Sūrya</s>' — because you thoroughly impel (<s>vīrayate</s>) the essences, rays, vital breaths, and intellects of the world. 'O son of <s>Prajāpati</s>' (<s>prājāpatya</s>) — O offspring of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the Lord, or of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — 'withdraw' (<s>vyūha</s>) — disperse, remove — your rays. 'Gather up' (<s>samūha</s>) — contract — your brilliance, so that I may be able to see your essential form directly. Just as brilliance [conceals] forms — therefore, withdraw your brilliance. That form of yours which is the most auspicious of all auspicious [forms] — the supremely auspicious — that [form] of yours I behold — we behold, by interchange of person. 'He who is that person' — who consists of the parts [designated by the syllables] <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s> — a person because of being person-shaped — 'I am he.' The connection is: 'I am the immortal one.' Since in the <s>Upaniṣad</s> it was stated that <s>Āditya</s> and the eye [of the person] are identical — that very [identity] is here referred to: 'I am he — the immortal one.' At the fall of the body, may the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), the <s>vāyu</s> (wind), that dwells in the body of me — the immortal, the true one — return to the external wind (<s>anila</s>). And likewise, may the other deities return to their respective sources. And then may this body too, ending in ashes, go to the earth. Now he entreats the deity of fire (<s>Agni</s>), who is established in the mind as the object of his contemplation: '<s>Oṃ</s>, O <s>Kratu</s>!' — '<s>O��</s>' and '<s>Kratu</s>' are both vocatives. [He is called] '<s>Oṃ</s>' because <s>Oṃkāra</s> is his symbol. [He is called] '<s>Kratu</s>' because he is constituted of mind. 'O <s>Oṃ</s>, O <s>Kratu</s>, remember!' — for at the time of death, by the power of your remembrance, the desired destination is attained — therefore [the prayer] is made: 'Remember what I have done!' The repetition is for emphasis. Furthermore, 'O <s>Agni</s>, lead' — cause to reach — 'by the good path' (<s>supathā</s>), by the auspicious path — 'to prosperity' (<s>rāye</s>), to wealth, meaning: for the attainment of the fruit of <s>karma</s>. Not by the southern, dark path that leads to return, but rather by the bright [northern] path alone — 'us' — O God, you who know all, all the cognitions of all beings. Furthermore, 'remove' (<s>yuyodhi</s>) — separate, disjoin — from us, from me — the crooked (<s>juhurāṇam</s>) sin (<s>enas</s>), all accumulated sin. Freed from that sin, we shall proceed by the northern path through your grace.
