But since we are unable to perform any other service to you, we shall offer you the most abundant — the most plentiful — words of homage (<s>namoukti</s>), words of salutation — we shall serve [you] through the utterance of homage — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the fifth chapter in the glorious <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. // 15 //

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadi pañcamodhyāyaḥ //5//

children.translated_text: Now the sixth chapter.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.1
children.translated_text: [Start of B���Up 6.1.1]

children.text:
yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca svānāṃ bhavati |
prāṇo vai jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca |
jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca svānāṃ bhavati |
api ca yeṣāṃ bubhūṣati |
ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_6,1.1 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the eldest and the best becomes the eldest and the best among his own [people]. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) indeed is the eldest and the best. He becomes the eldest and the best among his own [people], and also among those among whom he wishes to be so — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 6.1.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.1 oṃ prāṇo gāyatrītyuktam /
kasmātpunaḥ kāraṇātprāṇabhāvo gāyatryā na punarvāgādibhāva iti yasmājjyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca prāṇo na vāgādayo jyaiṣṭhyaśraiṣṭhyabhājaḥ /
kathaṃ jyeṣṭhatvaṃ śreṣṭhatvaṃ ca prāṇasyoti tannirdidhārayiṣayedamārabhyate /
athavokthayajuḥ sāmakṣattrādibhāvaiḥ prāṇasyaivopāsanamabhihitaṃ satsvapyanyeṣu cakṣurādiṣu /
tatra hetumātramihā'nantaryeṇa saṃbadhyate /
na punaḥ pūrvaśeṣatā /
vivakṣitaṃ tu khilatvādasya kāṇḍasya pūrvatra yadanuktaṃ viśiṣṭaphalaṃ prāṇaviṣayamupāsanaṃ tadvaktavyamiti /
yaḥ kaściddha vā ityāvadhāraṇarchai /
yo jyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhaguṇaṃ vakṣyamāṇaṃ yo vedāsau bhavatyeva jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca /
evaṃ phalena pralobhitaḥ sanpraśnāyāmukhībhūtastasmai cā'ha-prāṇo vai jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśceti /
kathaṃ punaravagamyate prāṇo jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśceti /
yasmānniṣekakāla eva śukraśoṇitasaṃmbandhaḥ prāṇādikalāpasyāviśiṣṭaḥ /
tathāpi nāprāṇaṃ śukraṃ virohatīti prathamo vṛttilābhaḥ prāṇasya cakṣurādibhyaḥ /
ataḥ jyeṣṭho vayasā prāṇaḥ /
niṣekakāladārabhya garbhaṃ puṣyati prāṇaḥ /
prāṇe hi labdhavṛttau paścāccakṣurādīnāṃ vṛttilābhaḥ /
atoyuktaṃ prāṇasya jyeṣṭhatvaṃ cakṣurādiṣu /
bhavati tu kaścitkule jyeṣṭho guṇahīnatvāttu na śreṣṭhaḥ /
madhyamaḥ kaniṣṭho vā guṇāḍhyatvādbhavecchreṣṭho na jyeṣṭhaḥ /
na tu tathehetyāha-prāṇa eva tu jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca /
kathaṃ punaḥ śraiṣṭhyamavagamyate prāṇasya tadiha saṃvādenadarśayiṣyāmaḥ /
sarvathāpi tu prāṇaṃ jyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhaguṇaṃ yo vedopāste sa svānāṃ jñātīnāṃ jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca bhavati /
jyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhaguṇopāsanasāmarthyātsvavyatirekeṇāpi ca yeṣāṃ madhye jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca bhaviṣyāmīti bubhūṣati bhavitumicchati teṣāmapi jyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhaprāṇadarśī jyeṣṭhaśca śreṣṭhaśca bhavati /
children.translated_text: By the power of meditating on [<s>prāṇa</s> as possessing] the qualities of being eldest and best — and even beyond his own [kinsmen], among whatever [group of people] he wishes to become the eldest and the best — for them too, the one who sees <s>prāṇa</s> as the eldest and best becomes the eldest and the best.

children.text: nanu vayenimittaṃ jyeṣṭhatvaṃ tadicchātaḥ kathaṃ bhavatītyucyate /
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But the quality of being eldest is caused by age — how can that come about through [mere] wish? This is said:

children.text: naiṣa doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is no defect —

children.text: prāṇavadvṛttilābhasyaiva jyeṣṭhatvasya vivakṣitatvāt //1//
children.translated_text: because what is intended by 'eldest-ness' is acquiring functioning first, like <s>prāṇa</s>. // 6.1.1 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.1.1:] '<s>Oṃ</s>. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the <s>Gāyatrī</s>' — this was stated. For what reason is <s>prāṇa</s> the [nature of] <s>Gāyatrī</s> and not speech and the rest? Because <s>prāṇa</s> is the eldest and the best, while speech and the rest do not partake of the qualities of being eldest and best. How is the eldest-ness and best-ness of <s>prāṇa</s> [established]? To determine that, this [section] is commenced. Alternatively: the meditation on <s>prāṇa</s> alone, under the forms of <s>uktha</s>, <s>yajus</s>, <s>sāman</s>, <s>kṣattra</s>, and the like, has been described, even though other [faculties] such as the eye and the rest exist. Therein, only the reason is connected here in sequence; it is not a continuation of the previous [section]. But what is intended — because of the supplementary nature of this chapter — is the teaching of the meditation on <s>prāṇa</s> with a special fruit that was not stated earlier. 'He who indeed' — '<s>ha vai</s>' is a particle of emphasis. He who knows the quality of being eldest and best — which is about to be described — he indeed becomes the eldest and the best. Thus, enticed by the fruit, one becomes ready for the inquiry. To such a one it is said: '<s>Prāṇa</s> indeed is the eldest and the best.' How is it known that <s>prāṇa</s> is the eldest and the best? Because at the very time of conception, the connection of the <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest with the semen and blood is undifferentiated. Even so, semen does not develop without <s>prāṇa</s> — therefore, <s>prāṇa</s> is the first to acquire functioning, before the eye and the rest. Hence, <s>prāṇa</s> is the eldest by age. From the time of conception, <s>prāṇa</s> nourishes the embryo. For when <s>prāṇa</s> has acquired its functioning, thereafter the eye and the rest acquire their functioning. Therefore, the eldest-ness of <s>prāṇa</s> among the eye and the rest is fitting. Now, someone in a family may be the eldest but, lacking qualities, not the best. The middle or youngest one, being rich in qualities, may be the best but not the eldest. But it is not so here — this [the text] says: <s>prāṇa</s> alone is both the eldest and the best. How then is the best-ness of <s>prāṇa</s> known? That we shall show here through the [forthcoming] debate (<s>saṃvāda</s>). In any case, he who knows <s>prāṇa</s> as endowed with the quality of being eldest and best — and meditates [on it thus] — becomes the eldest and the best among his own kinsmen.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.2

yo ha vai vasiṣṭhāṃ veda vasiṣṭhaḥ svānāṃ bhavati |
vāg vai vasiṣṭhā |
vasiṣṭhaḥ svānāṃ bhavati |
api ca yeṣāṃ bubhūṣati |
ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_6,1.2 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭha</s>) becomes the most excellent among his own [people]. Speech (<s>Vāk</s>) indeed is the most excellent. He becomes the most excellent among his own [people], and also among those among whom he wishes to be so — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 6.1.2 //
[Start of BṛUp 6.1.2]

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.2 yo ha vai vasiṣṭhāṃ veda vasiṣṭhaḥ svānāṃ bhavati /
taddarśanānurūpeṇa phalam /
yeṣāṃ ca jñātivyatirekeṇa vasiṣṭho bhavitumicchati teṣāṃ ca vasiṣṭho bhavati /
ucyatāṃ tarhi kāsau vasiṣṭheti /
vāgvai vasiṣṭhā /
vāsayatyatiśayena vaste veti vasiṣṭhā /
vāggmino hi dhanavanto vasantyatiśayena /
children.translated_text: For those who possess speech dwell in excellence, being wealthy.

children.text: ācchādanārthasya vā vaservasiṣṭhā /
children.translated_text: Or [she is called] <s>vasiṣṭhā</s> from <s>vasas</s> (garment), in the sense of covering [i.e. outshining] —

children.text: abhibhavanti hi vācā vāggmino 'nyān /
children.translated_text: for those who possess speech overpower others by speech.

children.text: tena vasiṣṭhaguṇavatparijñānādvasiṣṭhaguṇo bhavatīti darśanānurūpaṃ phalam //2//
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the complete knowledge of [speech as possessing] the quality of <s>vasiṣṭha</s>, one attains the quality of <s>vasiṣṭha</s> — the fruit corresponds to the vision. // 6.1.2 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.1.2:] 'He who knows the most excellent' — becomes the most excellent among his own [people]. The fruit corresponds to the vision [of the meditation]. Among those beyond his kinsmen, too, whoever he wishes to become the most excellent — among them also he becomes the most excellent. Then let it be told — what is that most excellent? Speech indeed is the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭhā</s>). [She is called <s>vasiṣṭhā</s>] because she causes [others] to dwell (<s>vāsayati</s>) in excellence, or because she dwells (<s>vaste</s>) most excellently.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.1.3]

children.text:
yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda pratitiṣṭhati same |
pratitiṣṭhati durge |
cakṣur vai pratiṣṭhā |
cakṣuṣā hi same ca durge ca pratitiṣṭhati |
pratitiṣṭhati same pratitiṣṭhati durge |
ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_6,1.3 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the firm foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>) stands firm on even [ground] and stands firm on rough [ground]. The eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) indeed is the firm foundation. For by the eye one stands firm on both even and rough [ground]. He stands firm on even [ground] and stands firm on rough [ground] — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 6.1.3 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.3 yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda pratitiṣṭhatyanayeti pratiṣṭhā tāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ pratiṣṭhāguṇavatīṃ yo veda tasyaitatphalaṃ pratitiṣṭhati same deśe kāle ca /
tathā durge viṣame ca durgamane ca deśe durbhikṣādau vā kāle viṣame /
yadyevamucyatāṃ kāsau pratiṣṭhā /
children.translated_text: If so, let it be said: what is that firm foundation?

children.text: cakṣurvai pratiṣṭhā /
children.translated_text: The eye indeed is the firm foundation.

children.text: kathaṃ cakṣuṣaḥ pratiṣṭhātvamityāha-cakṣuṣā hi same ca durge dṛṣṭavā pratitiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: How does the eye have the quality of firm foundation? This is stated: for by the eye, having seen both even and rough [terrain], one stands firm.

children.text: ato 'nurūpaṃ phalaṃ pratitiṣṭhati same pratitiṣṭhati durge ya evaṃ vedeti //3//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the fruit corresponds [to the meditation]: he stands firm on even ground, stands firm on rough ground — he who knows thus. // 6.1.3 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.1.3:] 'He who knows the firm foundation' — <s>pratiṣṭhā</s> is that by which one stands firm. He who knows that <s>pratiṣṭhā</s>, endowed with the quality of firm foundation — for him this is the fruit: he stands firm on even ground — in favorable place and time. Likewise on rough ground — in uneven, difficult-to-traverse terrain, or in adverse times such as famine and the like.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.1.4]

children.text:
yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai padyate yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate |
śrotraṃ vai saṃpat |
śrotre hīme sarve vedā abhisaṃpannāḥ |
saṃ hāsmai padyate yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate |
ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_6,1.4 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows prosperity (<s>saṃpad</s>) — for him is fulfilled whatever desire he desires. The ear (<s>śrotra</s>) indeed is prosperity. For in the ear all the <s>Vedas</s> have come together. For him is fulfilled whatever desire he desires — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 6.1.4 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.4 yo ha vai sampadaṃ veda sampadguṇayuktaṃ yo veda tasyaitatphalamasmai viduṣe saṃpadyate ha /
kim /
yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate sa kāmaḥ /
kiṃ punaḥ saṃpadguṇakam /
śrotraṃ vai saṃpat /
kathaṃ punaḥ śrotrasya saṃpadguṇatvamiti /
ucyate-śrotre sati hi yasmātsarve vedā abhisampannāḥ śrotrendriyavato 'dhyeyatvāt /
children.translated_text: It is said: because when the ear exists, all the <s>Vedas</s> have come together [in it] — because they are to be studied by one who possesses the sense of hearing.

children.text: vedavihitakarmāyattāśca kāmāstasmācchrotraṃ saṃpat /
children.translated_text: And desires depend on the actions prescribed by the <s>Vedas</s> — therefore the ear is prosperity.

children.text: ato vijñānānurūpaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the fruit corresponds to the knowledge.

children.text: saṃ hāsmai padyate yaṃ kāmaṃ kāmayate ya evaṃ veda //4//
children.translated_text: For him is fulfilled whatever desire he desires — he who knows thus. // 6.1.4 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.1.4:] 'He who knows prosperity' — he who knows [the faculty] endowed with the quality of prosperity — for him, the wise one, this is the fruit: that desire which he desires is fulfilled for him. What then possesses the quality of prosperity? The ear indeed is prosperity. How does the ear have the quality of prosperity?

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.1.5]

children.text:
yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatanaṃ svānāṃ bhavaty āyatanaṃ janānām |
mano vā āyatanam |
āyatanaṃ svānāṃ bhavaty āyatanaṃ janānām |
ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_6,1.5 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows the abode (<s>āyatana</s>) becomes the abode of his own [people], the abode of [all] people. The mind (<s>manas</s>) indeed is the abode. He becomes the abode of his own [people], the abode of [all] people — he who knows thus. // BṛUp 6.1.5 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.5 yo ha vā āyatanaṃ veda /
āyatanamāśrayastadyo vedā'yatanaṃ svānāṃ bhavatyāyatanaṃ janānāmanyeṣāmapi /
kiṃ punastadāyatanamiti /
ucyate-mano vā āyatanamāśraya indriyāṇāṃ viṣayāṇāṃ ca /
manaāśritā hi viṣayā ātmano bhogyatvaṃ pratipadyante /
children.translated_text: For objects that rest on the mind attain the status of being enjoyable for the self.

children.text: manaḥsaṃkalpavaśāni cendriyāṇi pravartante nivartante ca /
children.translated_text: And the sense-organs proceed and withdraw according to the volition of the mind.

children.text: ato mana āyatanamindriyāṇām /
children.translated_text: Therefore, the mind is the abode of the sense-organs.

children.text: ato darśanānurūpeṇa phalamāyatanaṃ svānāṃ bhavatyāyatanaṃ janānāṃ ya evaṃ veda //5//
children.translated_text: Therefore, the fruit corresponds to the vision [of the meditation]: he becomes the abode of his own [people], the abode of [all] people — he who knows thus. // 6.1.5 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.1.5:] 'He who knows the abode' — <s>āyatana</s> means a support, a resting-place. He who knows [the faculty possessing the quality of] <s>āyatana</s> becomes the abode of his own [kinsmen] and the abode of other people as well. What then is that abode? It is said: the mind indeed is the abode — the support of the sense-organs and objects.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.1.6]

children.text:
yo ha vai prajātiṃ veda prajāyate ha prajayā paśubhiḥ |
reto vai prajātiḥ |
prajāyate ha prajayā paśubhiḥ |
ya evaṃ veda || BrhUp_6,1.6 ||
children.translated_text: He who knows <s>prajāti</s> (procreation) is indeed endowed with offspring and cattle. <s>Retas</s> (semen) is indeed <s>prajāti</s>. He is endowed with offspring and cattle, he who knows thus. || BṛhUp 6.1.6 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,1.6 yo ha vai prajātiṃ veda prajāyate ha prajayā paśubhiśca sampanno bhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.1.6:] He who knows <s>prajāti</s> (procreation) is indeed endowed with offspring and cattle, and becomes prosperous.

children.text: reto vai prajātiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Retas</s> (semen) is indeed <s>prajāti</s>.

children.text: retasā prajananendriyamupalakṣyate /
children.translated_text: By <s>retas</s> (semen), the procreative faculty is indicated.

children.text: tadvijñānānurūpaṃ phalaṃ prajāyate ha prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda //6//
children.translated_text: The fruit corresponding to that knowledge is: he is endowed with offspring and cattle, he who knows thus.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.7
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.1.7]

children.text:
te heme prāṇā ahaṃśreyase vivadamānā brahma jagmuḥ |
tad dhocuḥ -- ko no vasiṣṭha iti |
tad dhovāca -- yasmin va utkrānta idaṃ śarīraṃ pāpiyo manyate sa vo vasiṣṭha iti || BrhUp_6,1.7 ||
children.translated_text: These <s>prāṇas</s> (vital functions), disputing among themselves about their respective superiority, went to <s>Brahma</s> (<s>Prajāpati</s>). They said to him: 'Who is the best among us?' He said: 'He upon whose departure this body is considered to be in the worst condition — he is the best among you.' || BṛhUp 6.1.7 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.7 te heme prāṇā vāgādayo 'haṃśreyase 'haṃ śreyānityetasmai prayojanāya vivadamānā biruddhaṃ vadamānā brahma jagmurbrahma gatavanto brahmaśabdavācyaṃ prajāpati gatvā ca tadbrahma hocuruktavantaḥ /
ko no 'smākaṃ madhye vasiṣṭhaḥ ko 'smākaṃ madhye vasati ca vāsayati ca /
tadbrahma taiḥ pṛṣṭaṃ saddhovācoktavadyasminvo yuṣmākaṃ madhya utkrānte nirgate śarīrādidaṃ śarīraṃ pūrvasmādatiśayena pāpīyaḥ pāpataraṃ manyate lokaḥ /
children.translated_text: That <s>Brahma</s> (<s>Prajāpati</s>), being asked by them, said: 'Upon whose departure from among you — that is, upon whose exit from the body — this body is considered by people to be in a worse condition, more sinful than before,

children.text: śarīraṃ hi nāmānekāśucisaṃdhātatvājjīvato 'pi pāpameva tato 'pi kaṣṭataraṃ yasminnutkrānte bhavati /
children.translated_text: for the body, being a composite of many impure substances, is indeed wretched even while one is alive; still more wretched does it become when one of you departs from it.

children.text: vairāgyārthamidamucyate-pāpīya iti /
children.translated_text: The word 'worse' (<s>pāpīyas</s>) is used here to produce dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>).

children.text: sa vo yuṣmākaṃ madhye vasiṣṭho bhaviṣyati jānannapi vasiṣṭhaṃ prajāpatirtovācāyaṃ vasiṣṭha itītareṣāmapriyaparihārāya //7//
children.translated_text: He shall be the best among you.' Though <s>Prajāpati</s> knew who the best was, he said this — rather than saying 'This one is the best' — in order to avoid displeasing the others.

[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.1.7:] These <s>prāṇas</s>, namely speech and the rest, disputing — that is, arguing in opposition — for the purpose of establishing 'I am superior,' went to <s>Brahma</s>, meaning they approached <s>Prajāpati</s>, who is denoted by the word <s>Brahma</s>, and having gone there, they said: 'Who is the best among us? Who among us dwells and causes others to dwell?'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.8
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.1.8]

children.text:
vāg ghoccakrāma |
sā saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca -- katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti |
te hocuḥ -- yathākalā avadanto vācā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasā prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti |
praviveśa ha vāk || BrhUp_6,1.8 ||
children.translated_text: Speech departed. Having stayed away for a year, it came back and said: 'How were you able to live without me?' They said: 'Just as the dumb live, not speaking with speech, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, knowing with the mind, and procreating with semen — so did we live.' Speech entered back. || BṛhUp 6.1.8 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,1.8 ta evamuktā brahmaṇā prāṇā ātmano vīryaparīkṣaṇāya krameṇoccakramuḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.1.8:] Those <s>prāṇas</s>, thus instructed by <s>Brahma</s> (<s>Prajāpati</s>), departed one by one in sequence to test their own power.

children.text: tatra vāgeva prathamaṃ hāsmāccharīrāduccakrāmotkrāntavatī /
children.translated_text: There, speech was the first to depart from this body.

children.text: sā cotkramya saṃvatsaraṃ proṣya proṣitā bhūtvā punarāgatyovāca-kathamaśakata śaktavanto yūyaṃ madṛte māṃ vinā jīvitumiti /
children.translated_text: Having departed and stayed away for a year, it came back and said: 'How were you — were you able to live without me?'

children.text: ta evamuktā ūcuryathā loke 'kalā mūkā avadanto vācā prāṇantaḥ prāṇanavyāpāraṃ kurvantaḥ prāṇena paśyanto darśanavyāpāraṃ cakṣuṣā kurvantastathā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasā kāryākāryādiviṣayaṃ prajāyamānā retasā putrānutpādayanta evamajīviṣma vayamityevaṃ prāṇairdattottarā vāgātmano 'sminnavasiṣṭhatvaṃ buddhvā praviveśa ha vāk //8//
children.translated_text: Thus addressed, they said: 'Just as in the world the dumb, those unable to speak, live without speaking with speech, performing the function of breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, performing the function of seeing with the eye, likewise hearing with the ear, knowing matters of right and wrong with the mind, begetting sons with semen — so did we live.' Speech, having been given this answer by the other <s>prāṇas</s>, understanding that it was not the most indispensable among them, entered back.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.9-12
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.1.9-12]

children.text:
cakṣur hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca -- katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti |
te hocuḥ -- yathāndhā apaśyantaś cakṣuṣā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasā prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti |
praviveśa ha cakṣuḥ || BrhUp_6,1.9 ||
children.translated_text: The eye departed. Having stayed away for a year, it came back and said: 'How were you able to live without me?' They said: 'Just as the blind live, not seeing with the eye, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, knowing with the mind, and procreating with semen — so did we live.' The eye entered back. || BṛhUp 6.1.9 ||

children.text:
śrotraṃ hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca -- katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti |
te hocuḥ -- yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā vidvāṃso manasā prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti |
praviveśa ha śrotram || BrhUp_6,1.10 ||
children.translated_text: The ear departed. Having stayed away for a year, it came back and said: 'How were you able to live without me?' They said: 'Just as the deaf live, not hearing with the ear, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, knowing with the mind, and procreating with semen — so did we live.' The ear entered back. || BṛhUp 6.1.10 ||

children.text:
mano hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca -- katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti |
te hocuḥ -- yathā mugdhā avidvāṃso manasā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa prajāyamānā retasaivam ajīviṣmeti |
praviveśa ha manaḥ || BrhUp_6,1.11 ||
children.translated_text: The mind departed. Having stayed away for a year, it came back and said: 'How were you able to live without me?' They said: 'Just as the witless live, not knowing with the mind, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, and procreating with semen — so did we live.' The mind entered back. || BṛhUp 6.1.11 ||

children.text:
reto hoccakrāma |
tat saṃvatsaraṃ proṣyāgatyovāca -- katham aśakata mad ṛte jīvitum iti |
te hocuḥ -- yathā klībā aprajāyamānā retāsā prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa vidvāṃso manasaivam ajīviṣmeti |
praviveśa ha retaḥ || BrhUp_6,1.12 ||
children.translated_text: Semen departed. Having stayed away for a year, it came back and said: 'How were you able to live without me?' They said: 'Just as the impotent live, not procreating with semen, but breathing with <s>prāṇa</s>, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, and knowing with the mind — so did we live.' Semen entered back. || BṛhUp 6.1.12 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,1.9-12 tathā cakṣurheccakrāmetyādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.1.9-12:] Similarly, 'the eye departed' and so on — this is to be understood as before.

children.text: śrotraṃ manaḥ prajātirita //9-12 //
children.translated_text: Likewise for the ear, the mind, and <s>prajāti</s> (the procreative function).

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.1.13]

children.text:
atha ha prāṇa utkramiṣyan yathā mahāsuhayaḥ saindhavaḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkhūnt saṃvṛhed evaṃ haivemān prāṇānt saṃvavarha |
te hocuḥ -- mā bhagava utkramīḥ |
na vai śakṣyāmas tvad ṛte jīvitum iti |
tasyo me baliṃ kuruteti |
tatheti || BrhUp_6,1.13 ||
children.translated_text: Then, when <s>Prāṇa</s> was about to depart, just as a great and excellent horse of <s>Sindhu</s> breed might pull up the tethering pegs, so indeed did it pull up all these <s>prāṇas</s> together. They said: 'O blessed one, do not depart! We shall not be able to live without you.' 'Then offer tribute to me,' it said. 'So be it,' they replied. || BṛhUp 6.1.13 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.13 atha ha prāṇa utkramiṣyannutkramamaṃ kariṣyaṃstadānīmeva svasthānātpracalitā vāgādayaḥ /
kimivetyāha-yathā loke mahāṃścāsau suhayaśca mahāsuhayaḥ śobhano hayo lakṣaṇopeto mahānparimāṇataḥ sindhudeśe bhavaḥ saindhavo 'bhijanataḥ paḍvīśaśaṅkūnpādabandhanaśaṅkūnpaḍvīśāśca te śaṅkavaśca tān saṃvṛhedudyacchedyugapadutkhanedaśvāroha ārūḍhe parīkṣaṇāya /
evaṃ haivemānvāgādīnprāṇānsaṃvavarhedyatavānsvasthānādbhraṃśitavān /
te vāgādayo hocurhe bhagavo bhagavanmotkramīryasmānnavai śakṣyāmastvadṛte tvāṃ vinā jīvitumiti /
yadyevaṃ mama śreṣṭhatā vijñātā bhavadbhirahamatra śreṣṭhastasya u me mama baliṃ karaṃ kuruta karaṃ prayacchateti /
ayaṃ ca prāṇasamvādaḥ kalpito viduṣaḥ śreṣṭhaparīkṣaṇaprakāropadeśaḥ /
anena hi prakāreṇa vidvānko nu khalvatra śreṣṭha iti parīkṣaṇaṃ karoti /
sa eṣa parīkṣaṇaprakāraḥ samvādabhūtaḥ kathyate /
children.translated_text: This method of investigation, which has taken the form of a dialogue, is being narrated.

children.text: na hyanyathā saṃhatyakāriṇāṃ satāmeṣāmañjasaiva saṃvatsaramātramevaikaikasya nirgamanādyupapadyate /
children.translated_text: For it is not otherwise possible that each of these, which act collectively, could actually depart individually for a year and so on.

children.text: tasmādvidvānevānena prakāreṇa vicārayati vāgādīnāṃ pradhānabubhutsurupāsanāya /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is only the wise person who, by this method, deliberates upon which among speech and the rest is the chief, for the purpose of meditation (<s>upāsanā</s>).

children.text: baliṃ prārthitāḥ santaḥ prāṇāstatheti pratijñātavantaḥ //13//
children.translated_text: The <s>prāṇas</s>, having been asked for tribute, assented saying 'so be it.'

[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.1.13:] Then, when <s>Prāṇa</s> was about to depart — was going to leave — at that very moment speech and the rest were dislodged from their own places. How so? He illustrates: just as in the world a great and excellent horse — <s>mahāsuhaya</s> meaning a fine horse, endowed with auspicious marks and large in size — born in the <s>Sindhu</s> region, hence called <s>Saindhava</s>, of noble breed, might pull up the tethering pegs — <s>paḍvīśa-śaṅkūn</s> means the pegs to which the feet are tied, <s>paḍvīśas</s> being the fetters and <s>śaṅkavas</s> being the pegs — might uproot them, pulling them all out at once, as when a horseman mounts to test it; so indeed did <s>Prāṇa</s> pull up all these <s>prāṇas</s>, speech and the rest — that is, it dislodged them from their respective places. They, speech and the rest, said: 'O blessed one, O lord, do not depart from us! We shall indeed not be able to live without you.' 'If thus my superiority is recognized by you — that I am the best here — then offer tribute to me, make an offering to me.' And this <s>prāṇa-saṃvāda</s> (dialogue of the vital functions) is a constructed teaching to instruct the wise person in the method of determining who is the best. For by this method the wise person investigates: 'Who indeed is the best here?'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,1.14
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.1.14]

children.text:
sā ha vāg uvāca -- yad vā ahaṃ vasiṣṭhāsmi tvaṃ tad vasiṣṭho 'sīti |
yad vā ahaṃ pratiṣṭhāsmi tvaṃ tat pratiṣṭho 'sīti cakṣuḥ |
yad vā ahaṃ saṃpad asmi tvaṃ tat saṃpad asīti śrotram |
yad vā aham āyatanam asmi tvaṃ tad āyatanam asīti manaḥ |
yad vā ahaṃ prajātir asmi tvaṃ tat prajātir asīti retaḥ |
tasyo me kim annaṃ kiṃ vāsa iti |
yad idaṃ kiñcā śvabhya ā kṛmibhya ā kīṭapataṅgebhyas tat te 'nnam |
āpo vāsa iti |
na ha vā asyānannaṃ jagdhaṃ bhavati nānannaṃ pratigṛhītaṃ ya evam etad anasyānnaṃ veda |
tad vidvāṃsaḥ śrotriyā aśiṣyanta ācāmanty aśitvācāmanti |
etam eva tad annam anagnaṃ kurvanto manyante || BrhUp_6,1.14 ||
children.translated_text: Speech said: 'That wherein I am the most excellent, therein you are the most excellent.' The eye said: 'That wherein I am the foundation, therein you are the foundation.' The ear said: 'That wherein I am prosperity, therein you are prosperity.' The mind said: 'That wherein I am the abode, therein you are the abode.' Semen said: 'That wherein I am procreation, therein you are procreation.' Then <s>Prāṇa</s> asked: 'What then is my food and what is my clothing?' They answered: 'Whatever there is here — even what is food for dogs, worms, insects, and moths — that is your food, and water is your clothing.' Verily, one who knows this food of <s>Ana</s> (<s>Prāṇa</s>) — nothing that he eats is non-food, nothing that he accepts is non-food. Therefore, the learned <s>Śrotriyas</s> (Vedic scholars) sip water before eating and sip water after eating; they think thereby they make this <s>Prāṇa</s> not naked (not without clothing). || BṛhUp 6.1.14 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,1.14 sā ha vākprathamaṃ balidānāya pravṛttā ha kilovācoktavatī yadvā ahaṃ vasiṣṭhāsmi yanmama vasiṣṭhatvaṃ tattavaiva tena vasiṣṭhaguṇena tvaṃ tadvasiṣṭho 'sīti /
yadvā ahaṃ pratiṣṭhāsmi tvaṃ tatpratiṣṭho 'si yā mama pratiṣṭhā sā tvamasīti /
cakṣuḥ /
samānamanyat /
sampadāyatanaprajātitvagiṇānkrameṇa samarpitavantaḥ /
yadyevaṃ sādhu baliṃ dattavanto bhavanto brūta tasya u ma evaṅguṇaviśiṣṭasya kimannaṃ kiṃ vāsa iti /
āhuritare-yadidaṃ loke kiñca kiñcidannaṃ nāmāpyā śvabhya ā kṛmibhya ā kīṭapataṅgebhyaḥ /
yacca śvānnaṃ kṛbhyannaṃ kīṭapataṅgānnaṃ ca tena saha sarvameva yatkiñcitprāṇibhiradyamānamannaṃ tatsarvaṃ tavānnaṃ sarvaṃ prāṇasyānnamiti dṛṣṭiratra vidhīyate /
kecitu sarvabhakṣaṇe doṣābhāvaṃ vadanti prāṇānnavidaḥ /
tadasat /
śāsrāntareṇa pratiṣiddhatvāt /
tenāsya vikalpa iti cet /
na /
avidhāyakatvāt /
na ha vā asyānannaṃ jagdhaṃ bhavatīti sarvaṃ prāṇasyānnamityetasya vijñānasya vihitasya stutyarthametat /
tenaikavākyatāpatteḥ /
na tu śāsrāntaravihitasya bādhane sāmarthyamanyaparatvādasya /
prāṇamātrasya sarvamannamityetaddarśanamihi vidhitsitaṃ na tu sarvaṃ bhakṣayediti /
yattu sarvabhakṣaṇe doṣābhāvajñānaṃ sanmithyaiva pramāṇābhāvāt /
viduṣaḥ prāṇatvātsarvānnopapatteḥ sāmarthyādadoṣa eveti cet /
na /
aśeṣānnatvānupapatteḥ /
satyaṃ yadyapi vidvānprāṇo yena kāryatakaraṇasaṃghātena viśiṣṭasya vidvattā tena kāryakaraṇasaṃghātena kṛmikīṭadevādyaśeṣānnabhakṣaṇaṃ nopapadyate /
tena tatrāśeṣānnabhakṣaṇe doṣābhāvajñāpanamanarthakam /
aprāptatvādaśeṣānnabhakṣaṇadoṣasya /
nanu prāṇaḥ sanbhakṣayatyeva kṛmikīṭādyannamapi /
bāḍham /
kintu na tadviṣayaḥ pratiṣedho 'sti /
tasmāddaivaraktaṃ kiṃśukaṃ tatra doṣābhāvaḥ /
atastadrūpeṇa doṣābhāvajñāpanamanarthakam /
aprāptatvādaśeṣānnabhakṣaṇadeṣasya /
yena tu kāryakaraṇasaṃghātasambandhena pratiṣedhaḥ kriyate tatsambandhena tviha naiva pratiprasavo 'sti /
tasmāttatpratiṣedhātikrame doṣa eva syādanyaviṣayatvānna ha vā ityādeḥ /
na ca brāhmaṇādiśarīrasya sarvānnatvadarśanamiha vidhīyate kintu prāṇamātrasyaiva /
yathā ca sāmānyena sarvānnasya prāṇasya kiñcidannajātaṃ kasyacijjīvanahetuḥ /
yathā viṣaṃ viṣajasya krimestadevānyasya prāṇānnamapi saddṛṣṭameva doṣamutpādayati maraṇādilakṣaṇam /
tathā sarvānnasyāpi prāṇasya pratiṣiddhānnabhakṣaṇe brāhmaṇatvādidehasaṃbandhāddoṣa eva syāt /
tasmānmithyājñānamevābhakṣyabhakṣaṇe doṣābhāvajñānam /
āpo vāsa ityāpo bhakṣamāṇā vāsaḥsthānīyāstava /
atra ca prāṇasyā'po vāsa ityetaddarśanaṃ vidhīyate /
na tu vāsaḥkārye āpo viniyoktuṃ śakyāḥ /
tasmādyathāprāpte 'bbhakṣaṇe darśanamātraṃ kartavyam /
na ha vā asya sarvaṃ prāṇasyānnamityevaṃvido 'nannamanadanīyaṃ jagdhaṃ bhuktaṃ na bhavati ha /
yadyapyanenānadanīyaṃ bhuktamadanīyameva bhuktaṃ syānna tu tatkṛtadoṣeṇa lipyata ityetadvidyāstutirityavocāma /
tathā nānannaṃ pratigṛhītaṃ yadyapyapratighrāhyaṃ hastyādi pratigṛhītaṃ syāttadapyannameva pratigrāhyaṃ syāttatrāpyapratigrāhyapratigrahadoṣeṇa na lipyata iti stutyarthameva ya evametadanasya prāṇasyānnaṃ veda /
phalaṃ tu prāṇātmabhāva eva na tvetatphalābhiprāyeṇa kiṃ tarhi stutyabhiprāyeṇeti /
nanvetadeva phalaṃ kasmānna bhavati /
na prāṇātmadarśinaḥ prāṇātmabhāva eva phalam /
tatra ca prāṇātmabhūtasya sarvātmano 'nadanīyamapyādyameva /
tathāpratigrāhyamapi pratigrāhyameveti yathāprāptamevopādāya vidyā stūyate /
ato naiva phalavidhisarūpatā vākyasya /
yasmādāpo vāsaḥ prāṇasya tasmādvidvāṃso brāhmaṇāḥ śrotriyā adhītavedā aśiṣyanto bhokṣyamāṇā ācāmantyapo 'śitvā'cāmanti bhuktyā cottarakālamapo bhakṣayanti /
tatra teṣāmācāmatāṃ ko 'bhiprāya ityāha-etamevānaṃ prāṇamanagnaṃ kurvanto manyante /
asti caitadyoyasmai vāso dadāti sa tamanagnaṃ karomīti hi manyate /
prāṇasya cā'po vāsa iti hyuktam /
yadapaḥ pibāmi tatprāṇasya vāso dadāmīti vijñānaṃ kartavyamityevamarthametat /
nanu bhokṣyamāṇo bhuktavāṃśca prayato bhaviṣyāmītyācāmati /
tatra ca prāṇasyānagnatākaraṇārthatve ca dvikāryatā'camanasya syāt /
na ca kāryadvayamācamanasyaikasya yuktam /
yadi prāyatyārthaṃ nānagnatārthamathānagnatārthaṃ na prāyatyārtham /
yasmādevaṃ tasmāddvitīyamācamanāntaraṃ prāṇasyānagnatākaraṇāya bhavatu /
na /
kriyādvitvopapatteḥ /
dve hyete kriye bhotryamāṇasya bhuktavataśca yadācamanaṃ smṛtivihitaṃ tatprāyatyārthaṃ bhavati /
kriyāmātrameva na tu tatra prāyatyaṃ darśanādyapekṣate /
tatra cā'camanāṅgabhūtāsvapsu vāsovijñānaṃ prāṇasyetikartavyatayā codyate na tu tasminkriyamāṇa ācamanasya prāyatyarthatā vādhyate kriyāntaratvādācamanasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And therein, with respect to the water that forms part of the <s>ācamana</s>, the contemplation 'water is the raiment of <s>prāṇa</s>' is enjoined as an ancillary duty (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) — but when this [contemplation] is performed, the purpose of <s>ācamana</s> as [effecting] ritual purity is not overridden, since <s>ācamana</s> is a separate action [in its own right].

children.text: tasmādbhokṣyamāṇasya bhuktavataśca yadācamanaṃ tatrā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, with respect to the <s>ācamana</s> of one about to eat and one who has eaten, therein —

children.text: āpo vāsaḥ prāṇasyeti darśanamātraṃ vidhīyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Water is the raiment of <s>prāṇa</s>' — only the contemplation (<s>darśanamātra</s>) is enjoined.

children.text: aprāptatvādanyataḥ //14//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because [the enjoining of contemplation] does not arise from elsewhere. // 14 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 6.1.14: Speech, being the first to commence offering its tribute (<s>bali</s>), indeed spoke as follows: 'Insofar as I am the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭhā</s>), whatever excellence belongs to me — by that very quality of excellence, you too are the most excellent.'
'Insofar as I am the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), you are the foundation — the foundation that is mine, that you are' — this is the meaning.
[Likewise for] the eye.
The rest is similar.
Having offered their excellences of endowment, support, and progeny in sequence.
'If this is so — you have offered your tribute well, good sirs — then tell me: for this one endowed with such qualities, what is the food and what is the raiment (<s>vāsas</s>)?'
The others reply: 'Whatever food there is in this world, of any kind whatsoever — down to dogs, down to worms, down to insects and moths.
Whatever is food for dogs, food for worms, food for insects and moths — together with all of that, whatever food is consumed by any living beings — all of that is your food.' All food belongs to <s>prāṇa</s> — this contemplation (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) is what is enjoined here.
Some, however, say that for one who knows <s>prāṇa</s>'s food, there is no fault in eating anything whatsoever.
That is wrong.
Because it is prohibited by other scriptures.
[Objection:] Then there would be an optional alternative between them.
[Reply:] No.
Because [this passage] is not an injunction [of action].
'Indeed, no food of his becomes un-eaten' — this, that 'all is food of <s>prāṇa</s>,' is for the purpose of praising the enjoined contemplation.
Therefore, it forms a single syntactic unit with it.
But it does not have the capacity to override what is enjoined by other scriptures, since its purport lies elsewhere.
The contemplation that is intended to be enjoined is: 'All is the food of <s>prāṇa</s> alone' — not: 'One should eat everything.'
And the notion that there is no fault in eating everything — that is simply a false cognition, because there is no valid ground for it.
[Objection:] Because the knower is <s>prāṇa</s>, and it is tenable that everything is his food — therefore, by virtue of [this identification's] efficacy, there is indeed no fault.
[Reply:] No.
Because it is not tenable that everything without exception is [his] food.
Truly, even though the knower is <s>prāṇa</s>, with whatever aggregate of body and sense-organs his status as a knower is particularized — by that same aggregate, it is not tenable that he should eat the food of worms, insects, gods, and everything without exception.
Therefore, the declaration that there is no fault in eating everything without exception is purposeless,
because the fault of eating everything without exception does not arise [in the first place].
[Objection:] But surely, being <s>prāṇa</s>, he does eat even the food of worms and insects and the like!
[Reply:] Certainly.
But there is no prohibition directed at that.
Therefore, that which is divinely brought about — like the red [color] of the <s>Kiṃśuka</s> [tree] — in that there is no fault.
Hence, the declaration of no-fault in that regard is purposeless,
because the fault of eating everything without exception does not arise [in the first place].
But with respect to the connection with a particular aggregate of body and senses by which a prohibition is made — with respect to that connection, there is no counter-exception (<s>pratiprasava</s>) here.
Therefore, in transgressing that prohibition, there would indeed be fault — because 'Indeed, no [food of his]...' and the like has a different purport.
And the contemplation that the body of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like [can eat] all food is not enjoined here — rather, [the contemplation applies to] <s>prāṇa</s> alone.
And just as, in general, some particular type of food that is the food of all <s>prāṇa</s> is the sustaining cause for some particular living being —
just as poison, which is the food of a poison-born worm, although it is food of <s>prāṇa</s>, produces a directly observed defect — namely death — for another [being] —
even so, for one who eats prohibited food, although everything is the food of <s>prāṇa</s> in general, there would indeed be fault because of the connection with a body such as that of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the like.
Therefore, the notion that there is no fault in eating what should not be eaten is nothing but a false cognition.
'Water is the raiment (<s>vāsas</s>)' — waters, when consumed, serve as raiment for you.
And here, the contemplation 'water is the raiment of <s>prāṇa</s>' is what is enjoined.
But water cannot be actually employed for the purpose of [making] garments.
Therefore, in the established practice of drinking water, only the contemplation is to be performed.
'Indeed, no food of his that is un-eatable becomes eaten' — for one who knows thus, of <s>prāṇa</s> whose food is everything, nothing un-eatable has been eaten.
Even if something un-eatable has been eaten by such a one, it would remain un-eatable food — but he would not be tainted by the fault arising from that — this is the praise of the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), as we have stated.
Likewise, nothing that should not be accepted becomes accepted — even if something unacceptable such as an elephant and the like has been accepted, that too would be acceptable food — and therein too, he is not tainted by the fault of accepting what is unacceptable — this is for the purpose of praise alone. 'He who knows this food of <s>prāṇa</s>, the eater (<s>anasya</s>).'
The fruit, however, is simply the state of being <s>prāṇa</s> — not this particular fruit; rather, [the passage is stated] with the intention of praise.
[Objection:] Why should this very thing not be the fruit?
[Reply:] No — for one who sees [oneself as] <s>prāṇa</s>, the state of being <s>prāṇa</s> itself is the fruit.
And there, for one who has become <s>prāṇa</s>, the universal self, even the un-eatable is indeed eatable;
likewise, even the unacceptable is indeed acceptable — taking what is already established as the basis, the <s>vidyā</s> is praised.
Therefore, the sentence does not have the character of an injunction of fruit.
Since water is the raiment of <s>prāṇa</s> — therefore, learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>śrotriyas</s> (those who have studied the <s>Vedas</s>), when about to eat, sip water (<s>ācamanti</s>); and after eating, they again consume water.
Therein, for those who sip [water], what is the intention? [The text] says: they consider that they are making this food, <s>prāṇa</s>, 'not naked' (<s>anagna</s>).
And this is so: whoever gives raiment to someone, he thinks 'I am making him not-naked.'
And it was stated that water is the raiment of <s>prāṇa</s>.
'When I drink water, I am giving raiment to <s>prāṇa</s>' — this contemplation is to be performed — such is the meaning of this [passage].
[Objection:] But one who is about to eat and one who has eaten sips water in order to become ritually pure (<s>prayata</s>).
If [<s>ācamana</s> were] also for the purpose of making <s>prāṇa</s> not-naked, then <s>ācamana</s> would have two purposes.
And it is not proper for a single <s>ācamana</s> to have two purposes.
If it is for ritual purity, it is not for making [<s>prāṇa</s>] not-naked; if it is for making [<s>prāṇa</s>] not-naked, it is not for ritual purity.
[Reply:] Since this is so, let a second, separate <s>ācamana</s> be performed for making <s>prāṇa</s> not-naked.
[Reply:] No.
Because the duality of actions is tenable.
For there are two actions — the <s>ācamana</s> of one about to eat and the <s>ācamana</s> of one who has eaten — and the <s>ācamana</s> enjoined by <s>smṛti</s> serves the purpose of ritual purity.
It is the action itself [that matters], not that ritual purity requires contemplation and the like in addition.

children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the sixth chapter in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> [Bhāṣya]. // 1 //

children.text:
śvetaketur vā āruṇeyaḥ pancālānāṃ pariṣadam ājagāma |
sa ājagāma jaivaliṃ pravāhaṇaṃ paricārayamāṇam |
tam udīkṣyābhyuvāda kumārā3 iti |
sa bho3 iti pratiśuśrāva |
anuśiṣṭo nv asi pitreti |
om iti hovāca || BrhUp_6,2.1 ||
children.translated_text:
<s>Śvetaketu</s>, the son of <s>Āruṇi</s>, came to the assembly (<s>pariṣad</s>) of the <s>Pañcālas</s>.
He came to <s>Jaivali Pravāhaṇa</s>, who was being attended upon [by his servants].
Looking up at him, [<s>Pravāhaṇa</s>] addressed him: 'Young man!' (<s>kumāra</s>).
He responded: 'Sir!' (<s>bho</s>).
'Have you been instructed by your father?'
'Yes,' he said. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 6.2.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.1 śvetaketurha vā āruṇeyaḥ ityasya saṃbandhaḥ /
khilādhikāro 'yaṃ tatra yadanuktaṃ taducyate /
saptamādhyāyānte jñānakarmasamuccayakāriṇāgnermārgayācanaṃ kṛtam-agne naya supatheti /
tatrānekeṣāṃ pathāṃ sadbhāvo mantreṇa sāmarthyātpradarśitaḥ /
supatheti viśeṣaṇāt /
panthānaśca kṛtavipākapratipattimārgāḥ /
vakṣyati ca yatkṛtvetyādi /
tatra ca kati karmavipākapratipattimārgā iti sarvasaṃsāragatyupasaṃhārārtho 'yamārambhaḥ /
etāvatī hi saṃsāragatiḥ /
etāvānkarmaṇo vipākaḥ svābhāvikasya śāsrīyasya ca savijñānasyeti /
yadyapi dvayā ha prājāpatyā ityatra svābhāvikaḥ pāpmā sūcitaḥ /
na ca tasyedaṃ kāryamiti vipākaḥ pradarśitaḥ /
śāsrīyasyaiva tu vipākaḥ pradarśitastryannātmapratipattyantena /
brahmavidyārambhe tadvairāgyasya vivakṣitatvāt /
tatrāpi kevalena karmaṇā pitṛloko vidyayā vidyāsaṃyuktena ca karmaṇā devaloka ityuktam /
tatra kena mārgeṇa pitṛlokaṃ pratipadyate kena vā devalokamiti noktam /
tacceha khilaprakaraṇe 'śeṣato vaktavyamityata ārabhyate /
ante ca sarvopasaṃhāraḥ śāsrasyeṣṭaḥ /
api caitāvadamṛtatvamityuktaṃ na karmaṇo 'mṛtatvāśāstīti ca tatra heturnoktastadarthaścāyamārambhaḥ /
yasmādiyaṃ karmaṇo gatirna nitye 'mṛtatve vyāpāro 'sti tasmādetāvadevāmṛtatvasādhanamiti sāmarthyāddhetutvaṃ saṃpadyate /
api coktamagnihotre na tvevainayostvamutkrātiṃ na gatiṃ na pratiṣṭhāṃ na tṛptiṃ na punarāvṛtiṃ na lokaṃ pratyutthāyinaṃ vettheti /
tatra prativacane te vā ete āhutī hute utkrāmata ityādinā āhuteḥ kāryamuktam /
taccaitatkarturāhutilakṣaṇasya karmaṇaḥ phalam /
na hi kartāramanāśrityā'hutilakṣaṇasya karmaṇaḥ svātantryeṇotkrāntyādikāryārambha upapadyate /
kartrarthatvātkarmaṇaḥ kāryārambhasya /
sādhanāśrayatvācca karmaṇaḥ /
tatrāgnihotrastutyarthatvādagnihotrasyaiva kāryamityuktaṃ ṣaṭ prakāramapi /
iha tu tadeva kartuḥ phalamityupadiśyate /
ṣaṭprakāramapi karmaphalavijñānasya vivakṣitatvāt /
taddvāreṇa ca pañcāgnidarśanamihottaramārgapratipattisādhanaṃ vidhitsitam /
evamaśeṣasaṃsāragatyupasaṃhāraḥ /
karmakāṇḍasyaiṣā niṣṭhetyetaddvayaṃ didarśayiṣurākhyāyikāṃ praṇayati /
śvetaketurnāmato 'ruṇasyāpatyamāruṇistasyāpatyamāruṇeyaḥ /
haśabda aitihyārthaḥ /
vai niścayārthaḥ /
pitrānuśiṣṭaḥ sannātmano yaśaḥprathanāya pañcālānāṃ pariṣadamāgatya jitvā rājño 'pi pariṣadaṃ jeṣyāmīti garveṇa sa ājagāma /
jīvalasyāpatyaṃ jevaliṃ pañcālarājaṃ pravāhaṇanāmānaṃsvabhṛtyaiḥ paricārayamāṇamātmanaḥ paricaraṇaṃ kārayantamityetat /
sa rājā pūrvameva tasya vidyābhimānagarvaṃ śrutvā vinetavyo 'yamiti matvā tamudīkṣyotprekṣyā'gatamātramevābhyuvādābhyuktavānkumārā3iti saṃbodhya /
bhartsanārthā plutiḥ /
evamuktaḥ sa pratiśuśrāva bho3iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Thus addressed, he responded: 'Sir!' (<s>bho</s>).

children.text: bho3ityapratirūpamapi kṣattriyaṃ pratyuktavānkruddhaḥ san /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He addressed even the <s>kṣatriya</s> with the inappropriate [response] '<s>bho</s>' — being angered.

children.text: anuśiṣṭo 'nuśāsito 'si bhavasi kiṃ pitretyuvāca rājā /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Have you been instructed?' — 'Are you instructed by your father?' — thus said the king.

children.text: pratyāhetara oṃmiti bāḍhamanuśiṣṭo 'smi pṛccha yadi saṃśayaste //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He replied: 'Yes' (<s>om</s>) — 'Indeed, I have been instructed. Ask, if you have any doubt.' // 1 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 6.2.1: '<s>Śvetaketu</s>, the son of <s>Āruṇi</s>' — this is its connection [with the preceding context].
This section pertains to the supplementary portion (<s>khila</s>); therein, what was not stated [earlier] is being stated.
At the end of the seventh chapter, the prayer for a path was made by fire for one who combines knowledge and action: '<s>Agne</s>, lead [us] by the good path.'
Therein, the existence of many paths was indicated by the force of the <s>mantra</s>,
because of the qualifier 'the good path' (<s>supathi</s>).
And the paths are routes for the attainment of the ripened fruits of <s>karma</s>.
And [the text] will state: 'Whatever [one] has done' and so forth.
Therein — how many are the paths for the attainment of the ripened fruits of <s>karma</s>? — this commencement is for the purpose of summarizing all the destinations of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
For this is the extent of the destinations of <s>saṃsāra</s>.
This is the extent of the ripening of <s>karma</s> — both natural and scriptural — accompanied by [particular] knowledge.
Although in 'The two types of <s>Prājāpatya</s> [offspring],' natural sin was indicated,
'this is not its fruit' — [thus] its ripening was not shown.
Rather, only the ripening of scriptural [<s>karma</s>] was shown, ending with the attainment of the three types of food.
Because at the commencement of <s>brahmavidyā</s> (knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>), dispassion toward that [<s>karma</s>] was intended.
Therein too, it was stated that by <s>karma</s> alone, [one attains] the world of the ancestors (<s>pitṛloka</s>); and by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) combined with <s>karma</s>, [one attains] the world of the gods (<s>devaloka</s>).
But by which path does one reach the <s>pitṛloka</s>, and by which path the <s>devaloka</s>? — this was not stated.
That is what is to be stated here in this supplementary section in its entirety — therefore it is commenced.
And at the end, a comprehensive summary of the entire [teaching] is desired.
Moreover, 'This much is immortality' was stated; and that '<s>karma</s> has no share in [true] immortality' — the reason for that was not stated there, and this commencement is for that purpose.
Since this is the [limited] destination of <s>karma</s>, and there is no role [for <s>karma</s>] in eternal immortality — therefore, 'this much alone is the means to immortality' — thus, by implication, the reason is established.
Moreover, in the <s>Agnihotra</s> [section], it was stated: 'But you do not know the departure, the path, the establishment, the satisfaction, the return, or the world that rises up of these two [oblations].'
Therein, in the reply, 'Those two oblations, having been offered, depart upward' and so forth — the effect of the oblation was stated.
And that effect pertains to the agent of the <s>karma</s> characterized as the oblation.
For without depending on the agent, it is not tenable that the <s>karma</s> characterized as the oblation should independently initiate effects such as departure and the like.
Because <s>karma</s> exists for the sake of the agent.
And because <s>karma</s> has a foundation in [its] means [of performance].
Therein, since [the passage] was for the purpose of praising the <s>Agnihotra</s>, the six-fold effect was stated as belonging to the <s>Agnihotra</s> alone.
But here, that very [six-fold effect] is taught as the fruit of the agent.
Because the six-fold knowledge of the fruit of <s>karma</s> was intended to be taught.
And through that [teaching], the doctrine of the five fires (<s>pañcāgnividyā</s>) is intended to be enjoined here as the means for attaining the northern path (<s>uttaramārga</s>).
Thus, a comprehensive summary of all the destinations of <s>saṃsāra</s> [is presented].
Wishing to demonstrate both of these — that this is the conclusion of the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritualistic section) — [the text] composes a narrative.
<s>Śvetaketu</s> by name — the offspring of <s>Aruṇa</s> is <s>Āruṇi</s>; his offspring is <s>Āruṇeya</s>.
The word '<s>ha</s>' indicates tradition.
The word '<s>vai</s>' indicates certainty.
Having been instructed by his father, and having come to the assembly of the <s>Pañcālas</s> for the purpose of spreading his own fame, having conquered [the assembly], [he thought:] 'I shall conquer even the king's assembly' — with such pride, he came.
The offspring of <s>Jīvala</s> is <s>Jaivali</s>, the king of the <s>Pañcālas</s>, named <s>Pravāhaṇa</s> — who was being attended upon (<s>paricārayamāṇam</s>) by his own servants — meaning: he was having his attendance performed.
That king, having previously heard of [<s>Śvetaketu</s>'s] pride in his knowledge, thinking 'This one should be disciplined,' looked up at him — observed him upon his arrival — and addressed him: 'Young man!' (<s>kumāra</s>), calling [him] thus.
The prolonged [vocative] is for the purpose of reproach.

neti hovāca |

neti haivovāca |

neti haivovāca |
vettho devayānasya vā pathaḥ pratipadaṃ pitṛyāṇasya vā |
yat kṛtvā devayānaṃ vā panthānaṃ pratipadyante pitṛyāṇaṃ vā |
api hi na ṛṣer vacaḥ śrutaṃ --
dve sṛtī aśṛṇavaṃ pitṝṇām ahaṃ devānām uta martyānām |
tābhyām idaṃ viśvam ejat sameti yad antarā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ceti |
