children.translated_text: ['Do you know how] these beings, having departed, go their separate ways?' 'No,' he said. 'Do you know how they return again to this world?' 'No,' he said indeed. 'Do you know how that world is never filled up, even though so many depart [to it] again and again?' 'No,' he said indeed. 'Do you know at which offering, when offered, the waters become possessed of a human voice and rise up and speak?' 'No,' he said indeed. 'Do you know the entrance to the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) or the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>)? — By doing what does one attain the path of the gods or the path of the ancestors? Have you not heard the saying of the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer): "I have heard of two paths — of the ancestors and of the gods and mortals. By these two, all that moves converges — whatever is between father and mother."' 'I do not know even one of these,' he said. (BṛUp 6.2.2)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.2 yadyevaṃ vettha vijānāsi kiṃ yathā yena prakāreṇemāḥ prajāḥ prasiddhāḥ prayatyo mriyamāṇā vipratipadyantā3iti vipratipadyante vicāraṇārthā plutiḥ /
samānena mārgeṇa gacchantīnāṃ mārgadvaividhyaṃ yatra kāścitprajā anyena mārgeṇa gacchanti kāścidanyeneti vipratipattiḥ /
yathā tāḥ prajā vipratipadyante tatkiṃ vetthetyarthaḥ /
neti hovācetaraḥ /
tarhi vettha u yathemaṃ lokaṃ punarāpadyantā3iti punarāpadyante yathā punarāgacchantīmaṃ lokam /
neti haivovāca śvetaketuḥ /
vettho yathāsau lokaḥ evaṃ prasiddhena nyāyena punaḥ punarasakṛtprayadbhirmariyamāṇairyathāyena prakāreṇa na saṃpūryatā3iti na saṃpūryate 'sau lokastatkiṃ vettha /
neti haivovāca /
vettho yatithyāṃ yatsaṃkhyākāyāmāhutyāmāhutau hutāyāmāpaḥ puruṣavācaḥ puruṣasya yā vāksaiva yāsāṃ vāktāḥ puruṣavāco bhūtvā puruṣaśabdavācyā vā bhūtvā /
yadā puruṣākārapariṇatāstadā puruṣavāco bhavanti /
samutthāya samyagutthāyodbhūtāḥ satyo vadantī3iti /
neti haivovāca /
puruṣākārapariṇatāstadā puruṣavāco bhavanti /
samutthāya samyagutthāyodbhūtāḥ satyo vadantī3iti /
neti haivovāca /
yadyevaṃ vettha u devayānasya patho mārgasya pratipadaṃ pratipadyate yena sā pratipattāṃ pratipadaṃ pitṛyāṇasya vā pratipadaṃ pratipacchabdavācyamarthamāha /
yatkarma kṛtvā yathāviśiṣṭaṃ karma kṛtvetyarthaḥ /
devayānaṃ vā panthānaṃ mārgaṃ pratipadyante pitṛyāṇaṃ vā yatkarma kṛtvā pratidyante tatkarma pratipadicyate tāṃ pratipadaṃ kiṃ vettha devalokapitṛlokapratipattisādhanaṃ kiṃ vetthetyarthaḥ /
apyatrāsyārthasya prakāśakamṛṣermantrasya vaco vākyaṃ naḥ śrutamasti /
mantro 'pyasyārthasya prakāśako vidyata ityarthaḥ /
ko 'sau mantra iti /
ucyate-dve sṛtī dvau mārgāvaśṛṇavaṃ śṛtavānasmi tayorekā pitṛṇāṃ prāpikā pitṛlokasaṃbaddhā tayā sṛtyā pitṛlokaṃ prāpnotītyarthaḥ /
ahamaśṛṇavamiti vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ /
devānāmutāpi devānāṃ saṃbandhinyanyā devānprāpayati sā /
ke punarubhābhyāṃ sṛtibhyāṃ pitṝndevāṃśca gacchantīti /
ucyate-utāpi martyānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ saṃbandhinyau manuṣyā eva hi sṛtibhyāṃ gacchantītyarthaḥ /
tābhyāṃ sṛtihyāmidaṃ viśvaṃ samastametadgacchatsameti saṃgacchate /
te ca dve sṛtī yadantarā yayorantarā yadantarā pitaraṃ mātaraṃ ca mātāpitrorantarā madhya ityarthaḥ /
kau tau mātāpitarau dyāvāpṛthivyāvaṇḍakapāle /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Who are those mother and father? Heaven and earth — the two halves of the cosmic egg.

children.text: iyaṃ vai mātāsau piteti hi vyākhyātaṃ brāhmaṇena /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'This [earth] is the mother, that [heaven] is the father' — thus it has been explained by the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [text].

children.text: aṇḍakapālayormadhye saṃsāraviṣaye evaite sṛtī nā'tyantikāmṛtatvagamanāya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Between the two halves of the cosmic egg — in the realm of <s>saṃsāra</s> — these two paths exist; [they are] not for the attainment of absolute immortality.

children.text: itara āha-nāhamato 'smātpraśnasamudāyādekañcanaikamapi praśnaṃ na veda nāhaṃ vedeti hovāca śvetaketuḥ //2//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The other [<s>Śvetaketu</s>] said: 'Not even one — not even a single question from this collection of questions — do I know. I do not know' — thus said <s>Śvetaketu</s>. // 6.2.2 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.2:] 'If so, do you know' — 'Do you know, do you understand, how — by what means — these well-known beings, having departed (<s>prayatya</s>), dying, go their separate ways (<s>vipratipadyante</s>)?' The prolonged vowel (<s>pluti</s>) is for the purpose of deliberation.
The divergence of paths — among those going by the same road — is where some beings go by one path and others by another; that divergence is the '<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>' (going in different directions).
How those beings go in different directions — do you know that? — this is the meaning.
'No,' said the other [<s>Śvetaketu</s>].
'Then, do you know how they return again (<s>punarāpadyante</s>) to this world — how they come back to this world?'
'No,' said <s>Śvetaketu</s> indeed.
'Do you know how that world — by this well-known process — is never filled up, even though so many depart [to it] again and again — by what means it is not filled up?'
'No,' he said indeed.
'Do you know at which numbered offering (<s>āhuti</s>) — when that offering has been offered — the waters become possessed of a human voice — the speech of a person, that is their voice, they become [endowed with] that — they become describable by the word "person." When they have transformed into human form, then they become possessed of a human voice.'
Rising up — having fully risen, having emerged — 'they speak' — [with prolonged vowel].
'No,' he said indeed.
[The text repeats:] 'When they have transformed into human form, then they become possessed of a human voice. Rising up — having fully risen, having emerged — they speak.' 'No,' he said indeed.
'If so, do you know the entrance (<s>pratipat</s>) to the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) or the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>)? — the entrance, what is denoted by the word <s>pratipat</s>, [the text] explains: by doing what action — meaning: by doing what specific action — does one attain the path of the gods or the path of the ancestors? — what action leads to the attainment of the world of the gods or the world of the ancestors? — that action is called <s>pratipat</s> (the entrance) — do you know that? — this is the meaning.'
Moreover, there is a verse (<s>mantra</s>) of a <s>ṛṣi</s> that illuminates this meaning — its words, its statement — have been heard by us.
The meaning is: there exists a <s>mantra</s> that illuminates this subject.
What is that <s>mantra</s>? It is said: 'Two paths (<s>sṛtī</s>) I have heard of' — I have heard of two paths. Of these, one is that which leads to the ancestors (<s>pitṛloka</s>), connected with the world of the ancestors — by that path, one reaches the world of the ancestors — this is the meaning.
'I have heard' — the connection is with the separated [phrase].
'And also (<s>uta</s>) [the path] of the gods' — another [path], connected with the gods, leads to the gods.
Who then go by these two paths to the ancestors and the gods?
It is said: 'And also (<s>uta</s>) of mortals' — the two paths are connected with human beings; it is humans indeed who go by these two paths — this is the meaning.
By these two paths, all this world — this entirety — goes, converges, comes together.
And these two paths — 'what is between' — between which two — 'between father and mother' — between mother and father — meaning: in between — this is the meaning.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.3
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.3]

children.text:
athainaṃ vasatyopamantrayāṃ cakre |
anādṛtya vasatiṃ kumāraḥ pradudrāva |
sa ājagāma pitaram |
taṃ hovāca -- iti vāva kila no bhavān purānuśiṣṭān avoca iti |
katham sumedha iti |
pañca mā praśnān rājanyabandhur aprākṣīt |
tato naikaṃ cana vedeti |
katame ta iti |
ima iti ha pratīkāny udājahāra || BrhUp_6,2.3 ||
children.translated_text: Then [the king] invited him to stay [as a guest]. Not heeding the invitation to stay, the boy (<s>kumāra</s>) ran away. He came to his father. He said to him: 'Thus indeed, sir, you told us before that we were well-instructed!' 'How [is that], O intelligent one?' 'A mere <s>kṣatriya</s> asked me five questions, and I did not know even one of them.' 'What were those [questions]?' He recited the opening words [of the questions]. (BṛUp 6.2.3)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.3 athānantaramapanīya vidyābhimānagarvamenaṃ prakṛtaṃ śvetaketuṃ vasatyā vasatiprayojanenopamantrayāñcakre /
iha vasantu bhavantaḥ pādyamarpyaṃ cā'nīyatāmityupamantraṇaṃ kṛtavānrājā /
anādṛtya tāṃ vasatiṃ kumāraḥ śvetaketuḥ pradudrāva pratigatavānpitaraṃ prati /
sa cā'jagāma pitaramāgatya covāca taṃ kathamiti vāva kilaivaṃ kila no 'smānbhavānpurā samāvagatavānpitaraṃ prati /
sa cā'jagāma pitaramāgatya covāca taṃ kathamiti vāva kilaivaṃ kila no 'smānbhavānpurā samāvartanakāle 'nuśiṣṭānsarvābhirvidyābhiravoco 'vocaditi /
sopālambhaṃ putrasya vacaḥ śrutvā'ha pitā /
katha kena prakāreṇa tava duḥkhamupajātaṃ he sumedhaḥ śobhanā medhā yasyeti sumedhāḥ /
śṛṇu mama yathā vṛttaṃ pañca pañcasaṃkhyākānpraśnānmā māṃ rājanyabandhū rājanyā bandhavo yasyeti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having heard the reproachful words of the son, the father said: 'How — by what means — has grief come upon you, O <s>Sumedha</s> (O intelligent one)?' — <s>Sumedha</s> means one whose <s>medhā</s> (intelligence) is excellent.

children.text: paribhavavacanametadrājanyabandhuriti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Listen to what happened to me: five — five in number — questions — a <s>rājanyabandhu</s> [asked me]' — '<s>rājanya</s>' means <s>kṣatriya</s>, and one whose relatives (<s>bandhu</s>) are <s>rājanya</s>.

children.text: aprākṣītpṛṣṭavāṃstatastasmānnaikañcanaikamapi na veda na vijñātavānasmi /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This [word] '<s>rājanyabandhu</s>' is a term of contempt.

children.text: katame te rājñāḥ pṛṣṭāḥ praśnā iti pitroktaḥ putra ime ta iti ha pratīkāni mukhāni praśnānāmudājahārodāhṛtavān //3//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '[He] asked me' — 'from that, not even one, not a single one, do I know — I did not understand.' 'What are those questions asked by the king?' — thus asked by the father, the son [said] 'these are they' — and recited (<s>udājahāra</s>) the opening words (<s>pratīkāni</s>), the beginnings of the questions. // 6.2.3 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.3:] Then — immediately afterwards — having removed his pride born of the conceit of learning, the king invited the said <s>Śvetaketu</s> to stay (<s>vasati</s>) — with the purpose of hospitality.
'Let the honored ones stay here; let water for washing the feet and <s>arghya</s> (offering) be brought' — thus the king made the invitation.
Not heeding, disregarding that invitation to stay, the boy (<s>kumāra</s>) <s>Śvetaketu</s> ran away — went back, toward his father.
And he came to his father, and having come, said to him — 'How' — meaning: 'Thus indeed, in this manner — we were told by you, sir, earlier, at the time of our graduation (<s>samāvartana</s>) — [that we were] instructed in all branches of learning — [you] said thus.'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.4]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- tathā nas tvaṃ tata jānīthā yathā yad ahaṃ kiṃca veda sarvam ahaṃ tat tubham avocam |
prehi tu tatra |
pratītya brahmacaryaṃ vatsyāva iti |
bhavān eva gacchatv iti |
sa ājagāma gautamo yatra pravāhaṇasya jaivaler āsa |
tasmā āsanam āhṛtyodakam āhārayāṃ cakāra |
atha hāsmā arghyaṃ cakāra |
taṃ hovāca -- varaṃ bhagavate gautamāya dadma iti || BrhUp_6,2.4 ||
children.translated_text: He [the father] said: 'Know us, my child, in this way — that whatever I knew, all that I have told you. But come, let us go there. Having gone [to the king], we shall live as <s>brahmacārins</s> (students).' [The son said:] 'Let your honor go.' So <s>Gautama</s> came to where <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> was. [The king] offered him a seat and had water brought for him. Then he offered him the <s>arghya</s> (honorific offering). He said to him: 'We give a boon to the venerable <s>Gautama</s>.' (BṛUp 6.2.4)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.4 sa hovāca pitā putraṃ kruddhamupaśamayaṃstathā tena prakāreṇa no 'smāṃstvaṃ he tāta vatsa jānīthā gṛhṇīthā yathā yadahaṃ kiñca vijñānajātaṃ veda sarvaṃ tatubhyamavocamityeva jānīthāḥ /
ko 'nyo mama priyataro 'sti tvatto yadarthaṃrakṣiṣye /
ahamapyetanna jānāmi yadrājñā pṛṣṭam /
tasmātprehyāgaccha tatra pratītya gatvā rājñi brahmacaryaṃ vatsyāvo vidyārthamiti /
sa āha bhavāneva gacchatviti nāhaṃ tasya mukhaṃ nirīkṣitumutsahe /
sa ājagāma gautamo gotrato gautama āruṇiryatra pravāhaṇasya jaivalerāsā'sanamāsthāyikā ṣaṣṭhīdvayaṃ prathamamāsthāne /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] So <s>Gautama</s> — <s>Gautama</s> by family lineage, <s>Āruṇi</s> — came to where <s>Pravāhaṇa Jaivali</s> was. [The text uses] a double sixth [case] — the first [sixth-case ending] is with respect to his seat (<s>āsthāna</s>).

children.text: tasmai gautamāyā'gatāyā'sanamanurūpamāhṛtyodakaṃ bhṛtyairāhārayāñcakāra /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For that <s>Gautama</s> who had arrived, [the king] had a suitable seat brought and had water brought by servants.

children.text: atha hāsmā ardhyaṃ purodhasā kṛtavānmantravanmadhuparkaṃ ca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then [the king] had the <s>arghya</s> (honorific offering) performed through the priest, together with <s>mantras</s> and the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-mixture offering).

children.text: kṛtvā caivaṃ pūjāṃ taṃ hovāca varaṃ bhagavate gautamāya tubhyaṃ dadbha iti gośvādilakṣaṇam //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And having performed such worship, he said to him: 'We give a boon to the venerable <s>Gautama</s>, to you' — [a boon] characterized by cows, horses, and the like. // 6.2.4 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.4:] He — the father — said, appeasing the angry son: 'In this way, by this means — know us, know about us, O <s>tāta</s> (dear child) — that whatever knowledge I possessed, all that I have told you — know [us] thus.
Who else is dearer to me than you, for whose sake I would withhold [knowledge]?
I too do not know that which was asked by the king.
Therefore, go — go there. Having gone (<s>pratītya</s>), we shall live as <s>brahmacārins</s> (students) at [the court of] the king, for the sake of knowledge.'
He [<s>Śvetaketu</s>] said: 'Let your honor go' — 'I cannot bear to face him [the king].'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.5]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- pratijñato ma eṣa varaḥ |
yāṃ tu kumārasyānte vācam abhāṣathās tāṃ me brūhīti || BrhUp_6,2.5 ||
children.translated_text: He [<s>Gautama</s>] said: 'That boon has already been promised to me. Tell me the words that you spoke in the presence of [my] boy.' (BṛUp 6.2.5)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,2.5 sa hovāca gautamaḥ pratijñāto me mamaiṣa varastvayāsyāṃ pratijñāyāṃ dṛḍhī kurvātmānaṃ yāṃ tu vācaṃ kumārasya mama putrasyānte samīpe vācamabhāṣathāḥ praśnarūpāṃ tāmeva me brūhi sa eva no vara iti //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.5:] <s>Gautama</s> said: 'This boon of mine has been promised by you' — thus confirming himself in this promise. 'But the words that you spoke to [my] boy — in the presence of my son — those words in the form of questions — tell them to me. That itself is our boon.' // 6.2.5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.6]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- daiveṣu vai gautama tad vareṣu |
mānuṣāṇāṃ brūhīti || BrhUp_6,2.6 ||
children.translated_text: He [the king] said: 'That, O <s>Gautama</s>, is among the divine boons. Mention one of the human [boons].' (BṛUp 6.2.6)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,2.6 sa hovāca rājā daiveṣu vareṣu tadvai gautama yastvaṃ prārthayase mānuṣāṇāmanyatamaṃ prārthaya varam //6//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.6:] The king said: 'That which you request, O <s>Gautama</s>, is among the divine boons. Ask for some other human boon.' // 6.2.6 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.7]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- vijñāyate hāstihiraṇyasyāpāttaṃ goaśvānāṃ dāsīnāṃ pravārāṇāṃ paridhānasya |
mā no bhavān bahor anantasyāparyantasyābhyavadānyo bhūd iti |
sa vai gautama tīrthenecchasā iti |
upaimy ahaṃ bhavantam iti |
vācā ha smaiva pūrva upayanti |
sa hopāyanakīrtyovāsa || BrhUp_6,2.7 ||
children.translated_text: He [<s>Gautama</s>] said: 'It is known that I have a sufficient quantity of gold and silver, cattle and horses, maidservants, retinue, and garments. Do not, sir, be ungenerous to us regarding that which is great, infinite, and boundless.' [The king replied:] 'Then, <s>Gautama</s>, you desire [to ask] in the proper manner (<s>tīrthena</s>).' 'I approach you [as a student],' [said <s>Gautama</s>]. In earlier times, [students] used to approach [teachers] by speech alone. So [<s>Gautama</s>], having merely declared his coming (<s>upāyanakīrti</s>), stayed [with the king]. (BṛUp 6.2.7)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.7 sa hovāca gautamo bhavatāpi vijñāyate ha mamāsti saḥ /
na tena prārthitena kṛtyaṃ mama yaṃ tvaṃ ditsasi mānuṣaṃ varam /
yasmānmamāpyasti hiraṇyasya prabhūtasyāpāttaṃ prāptaṃ go'aśvānānāmāpāttamastīti sarvatrānuṣaṅgo dāsīnāṃ pravārāṇāṃ parivārāṇāṃ paridhānasya ca /
na ca yanmama vidyamānaṃ tattvattaḥ prārthanīyaṃ tvayā vā deyam /
pratijñātaśca varastvayā tvameva jānīṣe yadatra yuktaṃ pratijñā rakṣaṇīyā taveti /
mama punarayamabhiprāyo mā bhūnno 'smānabhyasmāneva kevalānprati bhavānsarvatra vadānyo bhūtvāvadānyo mā bhūtkadaryo mā bhūdityarthaḥ /
bahoḥ prabhūtasyānantasyānantaphalasyetyetat /
aparyantasyāparisamāptikasya putrapautrādigāmikasyetyetat /
īdṛśasya vittasya māṃ pratyeva kevalamādātā mā bhūdbhavān /
na cānyatrādeyamasti bhavataḥ /
evamukta āha-sa tvaṃ vai he gautama tīrthena nyāyena śāsravihitena vidyāṃ matta icchāsā icchānvāptumityukto gautama āha-upaimyupagacchāmi śiṣyatvenāhaṃ bhavantamiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In earlier times, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, being seekers of knowledge, used to approach <s>kṣatriyas</s> — or <s>vaiśyas</s> — or <s>kṣatriyas</s> [used to approach] <s>vaiśyas</s> — as students, by speech alone, merely by verbal declaration, not with gifts, service, and the like.

children.text: vācā ha smaiva kila pūrva brāhmaṇāḥ kṣattriyānvidyārthinaḥ santo vaiśyānvā kṣattriyā vā vaiśyānāpadyupayanti śiṣyavṛttyā hyupacchanti nopāyanaśuśrūṣādibiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore —

children.text: ataḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] [Blank/transition]

children.text: sa gautamo hopāyanakortyopagamanakīrtanamātreṇaivovāsoṣitavānnopāyanaṃ cakāra //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] <s>Gautama</s>, with merely the declaration of his coming (<s>upāyanakīrti</s>) — merely by announcing his approach — stayed, resided [with the king]. He did not make [any formal] offering (<s>upāyana</s>). // 6.2.7 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.7:] <s>Gautama</s> said: 'Even by your own knowledge, it is known that I have — he [<s>Gautama</s>] has — [enough of material things].
I have no need for the human boon that you wish to give.
Because I already have abundant gold — already obtained; likewise cattle and horses — already obtained — and this should be supplied throughout — maidservants, retinues, and garments.
Nor is what I already possess something I should request from you, nor something you should give.
And the boon has been promised by you — you yourself know what is proper here — the promise is to be kept by you.'
'My intention is this: do not, sir, be — toward us, toward us alone — ungenerous. In all other respects, having been generous, do not be ungenerous, do not be miserly — this is the meaning.
Regarding that which is great — abundant; infinite — of infinite fruit — this is the meaning;
boundless — unending, extending to sons and grandsons — this is the meaning.
Regarding knowledge of such a nature, do not be one who gives only to me — do not become ungenerous.
Nor is there anything else that your honor ought to give [instead].'
Thus addressed, [the king] said: 'Well then, O <s>Gautama</s>, you desire [to ask] in the proper manner (<s>tīrthena</s>), by the correct method prescribed by scripture, to obtain knowledge from me.' Thus addressed, <s>Gautama</s> said: 'I approach you — I come as a student to your honor.'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.8]

children.text:
sa hovāca -- tathā nas tvam gautama māparādhās tava ca pitāmahāḥ |
yatheyaṃ vidyetaḥ pūrvaṃ na kasmiṃś cana brāhmana uvāsa |
tāṃ tv ahaṃ tubhyaṃ vakṣyāmi |
ko hi tvaivaṃ bruvantam arhati pratyākhyātum iti || BrhUp_6,2.8 ||
children.translated_text: He [the king] said: 'Do not take offense, O <s>Gautama</s> — neither you nor your forefathers. For this knowledge has never before dwelt in any <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. But I shall tell it to you. For who could refuse you when you speak thus?' (BṛUp 6.2.8)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,2.8 evaṃ gautamenā'padantara ukte sa hovāca rājā pīḍitaṃ matvā kṣāmayaṃstathā no 'smānprati māparādhā aparādhaṃ mā kārṣīrasmadīyo 'parādho na grahītavya ityarthaḥ /
tava ca pitāmahā asmatpitāmaheṣu yatāparādhaṃ na jagṛhustathā pitāmahānāṃ vṛttamasmāsvapi bhavatā rakṣaṇīyamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Just as your grandfathers did not take offense from our grandfathers — so too, the conduct of the grandfathers should be maintained toward us by you' — this is the meaning.

children.text: yatheyaṃ vidyā tvayā prārthitetastvatsaṃpradānātpūrvaṃ prāṅna kasminnapi brāhmaṇa uvāsoṣitavatītathā tvamapi jānīṣe sarvadā kṣattriyaparamparayeyaṃ vidyā'gatā sā sthitirmayāpi rakṣaṇīyā yadi śakyata ityuktaṃ daiveṣu gautama tadvareṣu mānuṣāṇāṃ brūhīti na punastavādeyo vara itītaḥ para na śakyate rakṣitum /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Just as this knowledge, sought by you — prior to its being transmitted to you — had never dwelt in any <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, even so, you too should know: this knowledge has always come through the succession of <s>kṣatriyas</s>. That tradition should be maintained by me too, if possible' — thus it was said. 'In matters relating to the gods, O <s>Gautama</s>, of those boons, tell [me] human [ones]' — meaning 'another boon is not to be given to you.' 'Beyond this, I cannot maintain [the tradition of keeping this knowledge secret from <s>brāhmaṇas</s>].'

children.text: tāmapi vidyāmahaṃ tubhyaṃ vakṣyāmi ko hyanyo 'pi hi yasmādevaṃ bruvantaṃ tvāmarhati pratyākhyātuṃ na vakṣyāmīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'I shall tell that very knowledge to you. For who else indeed could venture to refuse you who speaks thus, [saying:] "I will not tell"?'

children.text: ahaṃ punaḥ kathaṃ na vakṣye tubhyamiti //8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'How indeed should I not tell it to you?' (6.2.8)

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.8:] Thus, when <s>Gautama</s> was told a different [answer than expected], the king said — thinking him to be hurt — 'Forgive us! Do not hold it against us' — meaning: 'Do not take our offense; the offense is ours, not to be held [against you].'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.9
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.9]

children.text:
asau vai loko 'gnir gautama |
tasyāditya eva samit |
raśmayo dhūmaḥ |
ahar arciḥ |
diśo 'ṅgārāḥ |
avāntaradiśo viṣphuliṅgāḥ |
tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhutyai somo rājā saṃbhavati || BrhUp_6,2.9 ||
children.translated_text: That world yonder is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. Its fuel is the sun itself. Its smoke is the rays. Its flame is the day. Its embers are the directions. Its sparks are the intermediate directions. In this fire the gods offer <s>śraddhā</s> (faith/oblation). From that offering <s>Soma</s> the king is born. (BṛUp 6.2.9)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.9 asau vai loko 'gnirgotametyādicaturthaḥ praśnaḥ prāthamyena nirṇīyate /
kramabhaṅgastvetannirṇayāyattatvāditaraprasnanirṇayasya /
asau dyaurloko 'gnirhe gautama dyuloke 'gnidṛṣṭiranagnau vidhīyate yathā yoṣitpuruṣayostasya dyulokāgnerāditya eva samitsamindhanāt /
ādityena hi samidhyate 'sau lokaḥ /
raśmayo dhūmaḥ samidha uththānasāmānyāt /
ādityāddhi raśmayo nirgatāḥ /
samidhaśca dhūmo loka uttiṣṭhati /
ahararciḥ prakāśasāmānyāt /
diśo 'ṅgārā upaśamasāmānyāt /
avāntaradiṣo visphuliṅgā visphuliṅgavadvikṣepāt /
tasminnetasminnevaṅguṇaviśiṣṭe dyulokāgnau devā indrādayaḥ śraddhāṃ juhvatyāhutidravyasthānīyāṃ prakṣipanti /
tasyā āhutyā āhuteḥ somo rājā pitṝṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca saṃbhavati /
tatra ke devāḥ kathaṃ juhvati kiṃvā śraddhākhyaṃ havirityata uktamasmābhiḥ saṃbandhe /
na tvevainayostvamutkrāntimityādipadārthaṣaṭkanirṇayārthamagnihotra uktam /
te vā ete agnihotrāhutī hute satyāvutkrāmataḥ /
te antarikṣamāviśataḥ /
te antarikṣamāhavanīyaṃ kurvāte vāyuṃ samidhaṃ marīcīreva śukrāmāhutim /
te antarikṣantarpayataḥ /
te tata utkrāmataḥ /
te divamāviśataḥ /
te divamāhavanīyaṃ kurvāte ādityaṃ samidhamityevamādyuktam /
tatrāgnihotrāhutī sasādhane evotkrāmataḥ /
yatheha yaiḥ sādhanairviśiṣṭe ye jñāyete āhavanīyāgnisamiddhūmāṅgāravisphuliṅgāhutidravyaiste tathaivotkrāmato 'smāllokādamuṃ lokam /
tatrāgniragnitvena samitsamittvena dhūmo dhūmatvenāṅgārā aṅgāratvena visphuliṅgatvenā'hutidravyamapi paya ādyāhutidravyatvenaiva sargādāvavyākṛtāvasthāyāmapi pareṇasūkṣmeṇā'tmanā vyavatiṣṭhate /
tadvidyamānameva sasādhanamagnihotralakṣaṇaṃ karmāpūrveṇā'tmanā vyavasthitaṃ sattatpunarvyākaraṇakāle tathaivāntarikṣādīnāmāhavanīyādyagnyādibhāvaṃ kurvadvipariṇamate /
tathaivedānīmapyagnihotrākhyaṃ karma /
evamagnihotrāhutyapūrvavipariṇāmātmakaṃ jagatsarvamityāhutyoreva stutyarthatvenotkrāntyādyā lokaṃ pratyutthāyināntāḥ ṣaṭ padārthāḥ karmaprakaraṇe 'dhastānnirṇītāḥ /
iha tu kartuḥ karmavivakṣāyāṃ dyulokāgnyādyārabhya pañcāgnidarśanamuttaramārgapratipattisādhanaṃ viśiṣṭakarmaphalopabhogāya vidhitsitamiti dyulokāgnyādidarśanaṃ prastūyate /
tatra ya ādhyātmikāḥ prāṇā ihāgnihotrasya hotārasta evā'dhidaivikatvena pariṇatāḥ santa indrādayo bhavanti ta eva tatra hotāro dyulokāgnau /
te cehāgnihotrasya phalabhogāyāgnihotraṃ hutavantaḥ /
ta eva phalapariṇāmakāle 'pi tatphalabhoktṛtvāttatra tatra hotṛtvaṃ pratipadyante tathā tathā vipariṇamamānā devaśabdavācyāḥ santaḥ /
atra ca yatpayodravyamagnihotrakarmāśrayabhūtamihā'havanīye prakṣiptamagninā bhakṣitamadṛṣṭena sūkṣmema rūpeṇa vipariṇataṃ saha kartrā yajamānenāmuṃ lokaṃ dhūmādikrameṇāntarikṣāddyulokamāviśati /
tāḥ sūkṣmā āpa āhutikāryabhūtā agnihotrasamavāyinyaḥ kartṛsahitāḥ śraddhāśabdavācyāḥ somaloke kartuḥ śarīrāntarārambhāya dyulokaṃ praviśantyo hūyante ityucyante /
tāstatra dyulokaṃ praviśya somamaṇḍale kartuḥ śarīramārabhante /
tadetaducyate devāḥ śraddhāṃ juhvati tasyā āhutyai somo rājā saṃbhavatīti /
"śraddhā vā āpaḥ"iti śruteḥ /
vettha yatithyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāmāpaḥ puruṣavāco bhūtvā samutthāya vadantoti praśnastasya ca nirṇayaviṣaye 'sau vai loko 'gniriti prastutam /
tasmādāpaḥ karmasamāvāyinyaḥ kartuḥ śarīrārambhikāḥ śraddhāśabdavācyā iti niścīyate /
bhūyastvādāpaḥ puruṣavāca iti vyapadeśo na tvitarāṇi bhūtāni na santīti /
karmaprayuktaśca śarīrārambhaḥ /
karma cāpsamavāyi /
tataścāpāṃ prādhānyaṃ śarīrakartṛtve /
tena cā'paḥ puruṣavāca iti vyapadeśaḥ /
karmakṛto hi janmārambhaḥ sarvatra /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the commencement of birth [in every case] is [caused] by the action of the performer.

children.text: tatra yadyapyagnihotrāhutistutidvāreṇotkrāntyādayaḥ prastutāḥ ṣaṭpadārthā agnihotre tathāpi vaidikāni sarvāṇyeva karmāṇyagnihotraprabhṛtīni lakṣyante /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therein, even though the six categories — departure and the rest — were introduced through the praise of the <s>Agnihotra</s> oblation, nevertheless, all Vedic <s>karmas</s> beginning with the <s>Agnihotra</s> are implied [here].

children.text: dārāgnisaṃbaddhaṃ hi pāṅktaṃ karma prastutyoktam-karmaṇā pitṛloka iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the <s>karma</s> that was introduced as the topic — connected with wife, fire, and the fivefold [series] — was stated [thus]: 'By <s>karma</s>, [one attains] the world of the <s>Pitṛs</s>.'

children.text: vakṣyati ca-atha ye yajñena dānena tapasā lokāñjayantīti //9//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And [the text] will say: 'But those who by sacrifice, charity, and austerity conquer the worlds' — and so forth. (6.2.9)

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.9:] 'That world yonder is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>' — and so forth. The fourth question is being answered first. The disruption of order is because the answers to the other questions depend upon the resolution of this one. That world — the heavenly world (<s>dyuloka</s>) — is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. In the heavenly world, the perception of fire is prescribed for what is not [literally] fire — just as [it is prescribed] for a woman and a man. Of that heavenly-world-fire, the sun itself is the fuel, because of its kindling [that world]. For by the sun, that world is kindled. The rays are the smoke, because of the commonality of rising from the fuel. For the rays emerge from the sun; and smoke rises from the fuel. The day is the flame, because of the commonality of luminosity. The directions are the embers, because of the commonality of subsidence. The intermediate directions are the sparks, because of the commonality of scattering, like sparks. In this fire — in this heavenly-world-fire thus qualified — the gods, <s>Indra</s> and the rest, offer (<s>juhvati</s>) <s>śraddhā</s> — they cast in the oblation-substance, as it were. From that oblation, <s>Soma</s> the king is born — [born] for the ancestors and the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Therein, who are the gods, how do they offer, and what is the oblation called <s>śraddhā</s>? — regarding this, we have spoken in the [section on] connection. However, in the <s>Agnihotra</s> [section], it was stated — not for the purpose of determining these six categories concerning <s>utkrānti</s> (departure) and the like, but for the praise of the <s>Agnihotra</s> oblations: 'These two <s>Agnihotra</s> oblations, having been offered — [being] truth — depart. They enter the atmosphere. They make the atmosphere the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, the wind the fuel, the rays the bright oblation. They gratify the atmosphere. They depart from there. They enter the heavenly world. They make the heavenly world the <s>Āhavanīya</s>, the sun the fuel' — and so forth. Therein, the <s>Agnihotra</s> oblations together with their apparatus depart. Just as here [in the earthly realm] the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, together with its fuel, smoke, embers, sparks, and oblation-substance, is known through specific means — even so, [the oblations] depart from this world to that world. Therein, the fire [continues] as fire, the fuel as fuel, the smoke as smoke, the embers as embers, the sparks as sparks, and the oblation-substance — milk and the like — continues as oblation-substance. Even at the beginning of creation, in the state of dissolution (<s>avyākṛta</s>), it persists in a subtle form through its higher, subtler self. That [oblation-substance], existing [thus], the <s>karma</s> characterized by <s>Agnihotra</s> — established in the form of <s>apūrva</s> (the unseen potency) together with its apparatus — at the time of re-manifestation, transforms itself again in just that way, making the atmosphere and the rest into <s>Āhavanīya</s> fires and the like. Even so now, the <s>karma</s> called <s>Agnihotra</s> [operates]. Thus, the entire universe being of the nature of the transformation of the <s>apūrva</s> of the <s>Agnihotra</s> oblation — the six categories from <s>utkrānti</s> (departure) to the world's rising up [to receive the transmigrating soul] were determined in the <s>karma</s> section below, solely for the purpose of praising the two oblations. But here, when the intention is to discuss the <s>karma</s> of the performer, the doctrine of the five fires beginning with the heavenly-world-fire is introduced — as the means for attaining the northern path (<s>uttaramārga</s>) — prescribed for the fruition of distinguished <s>karma</s>-results; therefore, the doctrine beginning with the heavenly-world-fire is introduced. Therein, the <s>prāṇas</s> that are the inner faculties — which here are the <s>hotṛs</s> (offerers) of the <s>Agnihotra</s> — those very same, having transformed into their cosmic (<s>ādhidaivika</s>) forms, become <s>Indra</s> and the rest. Those very ones are the <s>hotṛs</s> there, in the heavenly-world-fire. And they, having offered the <s>Agnihotra</s> here for the fruition of the result — those very same, even at the time of the fruit's manifestation, because they are the experiencers of that fruit, assume the status of <s>hotṛs</s> in each successive [fire], being denoted by the word 'gods' as they transform in various ways. And here, the milk-substance that was the basis of the <s>Agnihotra karma</s> — cast into the <s>Āhavanīya</s> [fire] here, consumed by fire, transformed by the unseen potency (<s>adṛṣṭa</s>) into a subtle form — enters the heavenly world together with the performer (the <s>yajamāna</s>), through the sequence of smoke and the rest, from the atmosphere to the heavenly world. Those subtle waters, being the effect of the oblation, conjoined with the <s>Agnihotra</s>, accompanying the performer — denoted by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>' — upon entering the heavenly world, [serve] for the commencement of another body for the performer; entering the heavenly world, they are said to be 'offered.' There, having entered the heavenly world, in the sphere of <s>Soma</s>, they commence a body for the performer. This is what is stated: 'The gods offer <s>śraddhā</s>; from that offering, <s>Soma</s> the king is born.' Because of the <s>śruti</s>: '<s>Śraddhā</s> is indeed water' (ChUp 5.2.1). And the question was: 'Do you know how, at the fifth oblation, the waters, having become person-voiced, rise up and speak?' — and its resolution pertains to [the topic of] 'that world yonder is the fire.' Therefore, it is determined that the waters — conjoined with <s>karma</s>, serving as the material cause of the performer's body — are denoted by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>.' Because of the preponderance [of water], the designation 'waters become person-voiced' [is used]; it is not that the other elements are absent. And the commencement of a body is impelled by <s>karma</s>. And <s>karma</s> is conjoined with water. Therefore, water's preeminence in body-creation [is established]. Hence the designation: 'waters become person-voiced.'

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.10
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.10]

children.text:
parjanyo vā agnir gautama |
tasya saṃvatsara eva samit |
abhrāṇi dhūmaḥ |
vidyud arciḥ |
aśanir aṅgārāḥ |
hrādunayo viṣphuliṅgāḥ |
tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhutyai vṛṣṭiḥ saṃbhavati || BrhUp_6,2.10 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-cloud) is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. Its fuel is the year itself. The clouds are the smoke. Lightning is the flame. The thunderbolt is the embers. The rumblings of thunder are the sparks. In this fire the gods offer <s>Soma</s> the king. From that offering, rain is born. (BṛUp 6.2.10)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.10 parjanyo vā agnirgautama dvitīya āhutyādhāra āhutyorāvṛttikrameṇa /
parjanyo nāma vṛṣṭyupakaraṇābhimānī devatātmā /
tasya saṃvatsara eva samit /
saṃvatsareṇa hi śaradādibhirgrīṣmāntaiḥ svāvayavairvaparivartamānena parjanyo 'gnirdīpyate /
abhrāṇi dhūmaḥ /
dhūmaprabhavatvāddhūmavadupalakṣyatvādvā /
vidyudarciḥ /
prakāśasāmānyāt /
aśaniraṅgārāḥ /
upaśāntakāṭhinyasāmānyābhyām /
hrādunayo hlādunayaḥ stanayitnuśabdā visphuliṅgāḥ /
vikṣepānekatvasāmānyāt /
tasminnetasminnityāhutyadhikaraṇanirdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'In this fire' — and so forth — is the designation of the receptacle of the oblation.

children.text: devā iti ta eva hotāraḥ somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'The gods' — those very same <s>hotṛs</s> — offer <s>Soma</s> the king.

children.text: yo 'sau dyulokāgnau śraddhāyāṃ hutāyāmabhinirvṛttaḥ somaḥ sa dvitīye parjanyāgnau hūyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The <s>Soma</s> that was born when <s>śraddhā</s> was offered in the heavenly-world-fire — that [<s>Soma</s>] is offered in the second fire, the <s>Parjanya</s>-fire.

children.text: tasyāśca somāhutervṛṣṭiḥ saṃbhavati //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From that offering of <s>Soma</s>, rain is born. (6.2.10)

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.10:] <s>Parjanya</s> is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s> — the second fire, which is the receptacle of the oblation, in the order of the cycle of the oblations. <s>Parjanya</s> is the deity-self presiding over the apparatus of rain. Its fuel is the year itself. For by the year, revolving through its own divisions from autumn to the end of summer, the <s>Parjanya</s>-fire is kindled. The clouds are the smoke — because they originate from smoke, or because they are perceived like smoke. Lightning is the flame — because of the commonality of luminosity. The thunderbolt is the embers — because of the commonality of rigidity and subsidence. The rumblings of thunder (<s>hrādunaya</s>) — the sounds of thunder — are the sparks — because of the commonality of scattering and multiplicity.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.11
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.11]

children.text:
ayaṃ vai loko 'gnir gautama |
tasya pṛthivy eva samit |
agnir dhūmaḥ |
rātrir arciḥ |
candramā aṅgārāḥ |
nakṣatrāṇi viṣphuliṅgāḥ |
tasminn etasminn agnau devā vṛṣṭiṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhutyā annaṃ saṃbhavati || BrhUp_6,2.11 ||
children.translated_text: This world here is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. Its fuel is the earth itself. Fire is the smoke. Night is the flame. The moon is the embers. The stars are the sparks. In this fire the gods offer rain. From that offering, food is born. (BṛUp 6.2.11)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.11 ayaṃ vai loko 'gnirgotama /
ayaṃ loka iti prāṇijanmopabhogāśrayaḥ kriyākārakaphalaviśiṣṭaḥ sa tṛtīyo 'gniḥ /
tasyāgneḥ pṛthivyeva samit /
pṛthivyā hyayaṃ loko 'nekaprāṇyupabhogasaṃpannayā samidhyate /
agnirdhūmaḥ /
pṛthivyāśrayotthānasāmānyāt /
pārthivaṃ hīndhanadravyamāśrityāgniruttiṣṭhati /
yathā samidāśrayena dhūmaḥ /
rātrirarciḥ /
samitsaṃbandhaprabhavasāmānyāt /
agneḥ samitsaṃbandhena hyarciḥ saṃbhavati /
tathā pṛthivīsamitsaṃbandhena śarvarī /
pṛthivīchāyāṃ hi śārvaraṃ taṃ ācakṣate /
candramā aṅgārāḥ /
tatprabhavatvasāmānyāt /
arciṣo hyaṅgārāḥ prabhavanti tathā rātrau candramāḥ /
upaśāntatvasāmānyādvā /
nakṣatrāṇi visphuliṅgāḥ /
bisphuliṅgavadvikṣepasāmānyāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the commonality of scattering, like sparks.

children.text: tasminnetasminnityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'In this fire' — and so forth — as before.

children.text: vṛṣṭiṃ juhvati tasyā āhuterannaṃ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'They offer rain; from that offering, food is born.'

children.text: vṛṣṭiprabhavatvasya prasiddhatvādvrīhiyavāderannasya //11//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the origin of food — such as rice, barley, and the like — from rain is well known. (6.2.11)

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.11:] This world here is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. This world — the support of the birth and enjoyment of living beings, qualified by action, agent, and fruit — that is the third fire. Its fuel is the earth itself. For by the earth — endowed with the means of enjoyment for numerous living beings — this world is kindled. Fire is the smoke — because of the commonality of rising from an earthly support. For fire rises depending on earthly fuel-substance. Just as smoke [rises] from the support of fuel. Night is the flame — because of the commonality of originating from the connection with fuel. For from the connection of fire with fuel, flame arises. Even so, from the connection of earth-as-fuel, [comes] the night. For they say that darkness is the shadow of the earth. The moon is the embers — because of the commonality of originating from that [night]. For embers originate from flame; even so, the moon [appears] in the night. Or, because of the commonality of subsidence. The stars are the sparks.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.12
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.12]

children.text:
puruṣo vā agnir gautama |
tasya vyāttam eva samit |
prāṇo dhūmaḥ |
vāg arciḥ |
cakṣur aṅgārāḥ |
śrotraṃ viṣphuliṅgāḥ |
tasminn etasminn agnau devā annaṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhutyai retaḥ saṃbhavati || BrhUp_6,2.12 ||
children.translated_text: Man (<s>puruṣa</s>) is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. His open [mouth] is the fuel. <s>Prāṇa</s> (breath) is the smoke. Speech is the flame. The eye is the embers. The ear is the sparks. In this fire the gods offer food. From that offering, semen is born. (BṛUp 6.2.12)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.12 puruṣo vā agnirgautama prasiddhaḥ śiraḥpāṇyādimānpuruṣaścaturtho 'gnistasya vyāttaṃ vivṛtaṃ mukhaṃ samit /
vivṛtena hi mukhena dīpyate puruṣo vacanasvādhyāyādau /
yathā samidhāgniḥ prāṇo dhūmastadutthānasāmānyāt /
mukhāddhi prāṇa uttiṣṭhati /
vākyaśabdo 'rcirvyañjakatvasāmānyāt /
arciśca vyañjakam /
tathā vākśabdo 'bhidheyavyañjakaḥ /
cakṣuraṅgārā upaśamasāmānyātprakāśāśrayatvādvā /
śrotraṃ visphuliṅgā vikṣepasāmānyāt /
tasminnannaṃ juhvati /
nanu naiva devā annamiha juhvato dṛśyante /
naiṣa doṣaḥ /
prāṇānāṃ devatvopapatteḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because the <s>prāṇas</s> are fittingly [designated as] gods.

children.text: adhidaivamindrādayo devāsta evādhyātmaṃ prāṇāste cānnasya puruṣe prakṣeptāraḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the cosmic realm (<s>adhidaiva</s>), <s>Indra</s> and the rest are the gods; those very same, in the individual realm (<s>adhyātma</s>), are the <s>prāṇas</s>. And they are the ones who cast food into the man.

children.text: tasyā āhute retaḥ saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] From that offering, semen is born.

children.text: annapariṇāmo hi retaḥ //12//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For semen is a transformation of food. (6.2.12)

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.12:] Man is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s> — the well-known man consisting of head, hands, and the like is the fourth fire. His open [mouth] — the opened mouth — is the fuel. For by the opened mouth, man is kindled — in speech, Vedic recitation, and the like. Just as fire [is kindled] by fuel. <s>Prāṇa</s> is the smoke — because of the commonality of rising from that [mouth]. For <s>prāṇa</s> rises from the mouth. The sound of speech is the flame — because of the commonality of making manifest. For flame makes manifest [what is in darkness]. Even so, the sound of speech makes manifest the meaning. The eye is the embers — because of the commonality of subsidence, or because of being the support of light. The ear is the sparks — because of the commonality of scattering. In that [fire], they offer food. [Objection:] But the gods are not seen to offer food here [in man]. [Reply:] This is no fault —

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.13
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.13]

children.text:
yoṣā vā agnir gautama |
tasyā upastha eva samit |
lomāni dhūmaḥ |
yonir arciḥ |
yad antaḥ karoti te 'ṅgārāḥ |
abhinandā viṣphuliṅgāḥ |
tasminn etasminn agnau devā reto juhvati |
tasyā āhutyai puruṣaḥ saṃbhavati |
sa jīvati yāvaj jīvati |
atha yadā mriyate || BrhUp_6,2.13 ||
children.translated_text: Woman (<s>yoṣā</s>) is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>. Her womb (<s>upastha</s>) is the fuel. The hairs are the smoke. The vulva (<s>yoni</s>) is the flame. What is done within — those are the embers. The pleasures are the sparks. In this fire the gods offer semen. From that offering, a man (<s>puruṣa</s>) is born. He lives as long as he lives. Then, when he dies — (BṛUp 6.2.13)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.13 yoṣā vā agnirgautama /
yoṣeti srī pañcamo homādhikaraṇo 'gnistasyā upastha eva samit /
tena hi sā samidhyate /
lomāni dhūmastadutthānasāmānyāt /
yonirarcirvarṇasāmānyāt /
yadantaḥ karoti te 'ṅgārā antaḥ karaṇaṃ maithunavyāpāraste 'ṅgārā vīryopaśamahetutvasāmānyāt /
vīryādyupaśamakāraṇaṃ maithunam /
tathāṅgārabhāvo 'gnerupaśamakāraṇam /
abhinandāḥ sukhalavāḥ kṣudratvasāmānyādvisphuliṅgāḥ /
tasminreto juhvati /
tasyā āhuteḥ puruṣaḥ saṃbhavati /
evaṃ dyuparjanyāyaṃlokapuruṣayoṣāgniṣu kramema hūyamānāḥ śraddhāsomavṛṣṭyannaretobhāvena sthūlatāratamyakramamāpadyamānāḥ śraddhāśabdavācyā āpaḥ puruṣaśabdamārabhante /
yaḥ praśnaścaturtho vettha yatithyāmāhutyāṃ hutāyāmāpaḥ puraṣavāco bhūtvā samutthāya vadantī3iti sa eṣa nirṇītaḥ /
pañcamyāmāhutau yoṣāgnau hutāyāṃ retobhūtā āpaḥ puruṣavāco bhavantīti /
sa puruṣa evaṃ krameṇa jāto jīvati /
children.translated_text: That person, born in this sequence, lives.

children.text: kiyantaṃ kālamiti /
children.translated_text: For how long?

children.text: ucyate-yāvajjīvati yāvadasmiñcharīre sthitinimittaṃ karma vidyate tāvadityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is said: as long as he lives — meaning: as long as the <s>karma</s> that is the cause of dwelling in this body exists.

children.text: atha tatkṣaye yadā yasmikāle mriyate //13//
children.translated_text: Then, upon the exhaustion of that [<s>karma</s>], at whatever time he dies — // 6.2.13 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.13:] 'A woman indeed is the fire, O <s>Gautama</s>.' <s>Yoṣā</s> means a woman — the fifth fire, the substrate of oblation. Her lap (<s>upastha</s>) is the fuel — for by that she is kindled. Her body-hair is the smoke — because of the similarity of rising [upward]. The vulva (<s>yoni</s>) is the flame — because of the similarity of color. The act of intercourse (<s>maithuna</s>) performed within — those are the embers, because of the similarity with being the cause of the subsiding of vigor. For intercourse is the cause of the subsiding of vigor and the like. Likewise, the ember-state of fire is the cause of [its] subsiding. The minor pleasures (<s>abhinanda</s>) — minute particles of pleasure — are the sparks, because of the similarity of smallness. In that [fire] they offer semen as an oblation. From that oblation, a person (<s>puruṣa</s>) comes into being. Thus, in the [five] fires of heaven, rain-cloud, this world, man, and woman — the oblations being offered in succession — the waters, denoted by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>' (faith), passing through the stages of <s>Soma</s>, rain, food, and semen, attaining progressively greater degrees of grossness — these waters, denoted by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>,' assume the designation of 'person' (<s>puruṣa</s>). The fourth question — 'Do you know at which oblation, offered [in sequence], the waters, having become person-voiced, rise up and speak?' — that has been resolved. At the fifth oblation, when offered in the fire of woman, the waters that have become semen become person-voiced.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.14
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.14]

children.text:
athainam agnaye haranti |
tasyāgnir evāgnir bhavati |
samit samit |
dhūmo dhūmaḥ |
arcir arciḥ |
aṅgārā aṅgārāḥ |
viṣphuliṅgā viṣphuliṅgāḥ |
tasminn etasminn agnau devāḥ puruṣaṃ juhvati |
tasyā āhutyai puruṣo bhāsvaravarṇaḥ saṃbhavati || BrhUp_6,2.14 ||
children.translated_text: Then they carry him to the fire. His fire itself becomes the [cremation] fire. The fuel becomes the fuel. The smoke becomes the smoke. The flame becomes the flame. The embers become the embers. The sparks become the sparks. In that very fire, the gods offer the person as an oblation. From that oblation, a person of radiant complexion comes into being. // BṛUp 6.2.14 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,2.14 atha tadainaṃ mṛtamagnaye 'gnyarthamevāntyāhutyai haranti śratvijastasyā'hutibhūtasya prasiddho 'gnireva homādhikaraṇaṃ na parikalpyo 'gniḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.14:] Then, at that time, they carry this dead person to the fire — for the purpose of fire indeed, for the final oblation. The <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) [carry him]. Of this one who has become an oblation, the well-known fire itself is the substrate of oblation — not an imagined fire.

children.text: prasiddhaiva samitsamiddhūmo dhūmo 'rcirarciraṅgārā aṅgārā visphuliṅgā visphuliṅgā yathāprasiddhameva sarvamityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: The well-known fuel itself is the fuel, the smoke is the smoke, the flame is the flame, the embers are the embers, the sparks are the sparks — everything is just as commonly known — this is the meaning.

children.text: tasminpuruṣamantyāhutiṃ juhvati tasyā āhutyā āhuteḥ puruṣo bhāsvaravarṇo 'tiśayadīptimānniṣekādibhirantyāhutyantaiḥ karmabhiḥ saṃskṛtatvātsaṃbhavati niṣpadyate //14//
children.translated_text: In that [fire], the person — as the final oblation — they offer. From that oblation, a person of radiant complexion, of exceedingly brilliant form, comes into being — being refined by the rites from conception through the final oblation — he is produced. // 6.2.14 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,2.15
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.2.15]

children.text:
te ya evam etad vidur ye cāmī araṇye śraddhāṃ satyam upāsate te 'rcir abhisaṃbhavanti |
arciṣo 'haḥ |
ahna āpūryamāṇapakṣam |
āpūryamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaṇ māsān udaṅṅ āditya eti |
māsebhyo devalokam |
devalokād ādityam |
ādityād vaidyutam |
tān vaidyutān puruṣo mānasa etya brahmalokān gamayati |
te teṣu brahmalokeṣu parāḥ parāvato vasanti |
teṣāṃ na punar āvṛttiḥ || BrhUp_6,2.15 ||
children.translated_text: Those who know this thus, and those who in the forest meditate on faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) and truth (<s>satya</s>) — they pass into the flame (<s>arcis</s>). From the flame, into the day. From the day, into the bright half of the month. From the bright half, into the six months during which the sun moves northward. From those months, into the world of the gods (<s>devaloka</s>). From the world of the gods, into the sun (<s>Āditya</s>). From the sun, into the region of lightning (<s>vaidyuta</s>). A person who is mental (<s>mānasa</s>) comes [to them] and leads them to the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>. In those worlds of <s>Brahman</s>, they dwell as the highest of the highest for [many] years. For them there is no return. // BṛUp 6.2.15 //

children.translated_text: In [the expression] 'tomorrow being the full-moon day,' [the word 'tomorrow'] qualifies the full-moon day's being-on-the-morrow, which is not otherwise known — therefore it is proper to specify it.

children.text: na hi tatra śvaākṛtiḥ śabdārtho vidyata iti śvaśabdo virarthaka eva prayujyate /
children.translated_text: For there, [the word] 'tomorrow' (<s>śvas</s>) has no [merely] formal meaning — so the word 'tomorrow' is used without [independent] purpose.

children.text: yatra tu viśeṣaṇaśabde prayukte 'nviṣyamāṇe viśeṣaṇaphalaṃ cenna gamyate tatra yukto nirarthakatvenotsraṣṭuṃ viśeṣaṇaśabdo na tu satyāṃ viśeṣaṇaphalāvagatau /
children.translated_text: But where a qualifying word, when used and examined, yields no result of qualification — there it is proper to discard the qualifying word as purposeless; but not when the result of qualification is [actually] understood.

children.text: tasmādasmātkalpādūrdhvamāvṛttirgamyate //15//
children.translated_text: Therefore, [only] return from this [present] <s>kalpa</s> onward is to be understood [as negated]. // 6.2.15 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.2.15:] Now, for the purpose of resolving the first question, [the text] says: 'those' — who? Those who know this — the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> (doctrine of the five fires), as described. By the word 'thus' (<s>evam</s>), the five fires, specified by [the particular] fire, fuel, smoke, flame, embers, sparks, faith, and the rest, are indicated — 'they know these five fires thus' — this is the meaning. [Objection:] But this doctrine pertains only to the <s>agnihotra</s> oblation — for there it was said, in the determination of the six categories beginning with departure: 'they make heaven itself the <s>āhavanīya</s>' and so forth. Here too, there is much similarity — 'that world is a fire, and the sun is the fuel' and so forth. Therefore, this doctrine is merely a supplement to that [<s>agnihotra</s>]. [Reply:] No — because of the inclusion in the question and answer of 'at which [number of oblation]' (<s>yatithyām</s>). Only to the extent that the question 'at which [number of oblation]' and its answer are encompassed — to that extent alone is it proper to refer [back to the earlier teaching] with the word 'thus.' Otherwise, since the question would be purposeless and the number [of fires] is already known, only the fires [themselves] would need to be stated. [Objection:] But even what is already known may be restated. [Reply:] Only the restatement of what is already established is proper — not [the statement that] 'that world is a fire.' [Objection:] But it is for the purpose of indication (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>). [Reply:] Even so, indication by the first and the last [fire] is proper. And from another <s>śruti</s> — for in the same context, the <s>Chāndogya</s> <s>śruti</s> uses [the phrase] 'knows the five fires,' thereby specifying only the number five — hence this is not a supplement to the <s>agnihotra</s>. [This is] the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> (five-fire doctrine). As for the similarity with fire, fuel, and the rest [in the <s>agnihotra</s>] — we have said that serves to praise the <s>agnihotra</s>. Therefore, the attainment of the path of light and the rest does not come from the knowledge of the six categories beginning with departure. [Rather,] from the word 'thus' (<s>evam</s>), which refers back to the subject at hand, the injunction of attaining the path of light and the rest [follows]. Who, then, are those who 'know thus'? Householders only? [Objection:] Surely, for them, the attainment of the path of smoke and the rest is intended through the means of sacrifice and the like? [Reply:] No — because even for householders who do not know thus, the means of sacrifice and the like are available. And because mendicants (<s>bhikṣu</s>) and forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprastha</s>) are included through their connection with the forest. And because the five-fire doctrine is connected with the householder's rites. Therefore, even celibate students (<s>brahmacārin</s>) are not to be understood as those who 'know thus.' For them, however, entry onto the northern path [is established] through the authority of <s>smṛti</s>: 'Eighty-eight thousand sages who were celibate — by the northern path of <s>Aryaman</s>, they attained immortality.' Therefore, those householders who know thus — 'I am born from fire, I am the offspring of fire' — who know thus in sequence, born from the fires, being of the nature of fire — they, and those in the forest — the forest-dwellers (<s>vānaprastha</s>) and wandering mendicants (<s>parivrājaka</s>) who are devoted to the forest life — possessed of faith, having bathed [in sacred knowledge], who meditate on truth, on <s>Brahman</s> of the nature of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> — but not [merely on] faith as a separate meditation — all of them pass into the flame (<s>arcis</s>). As long as householders do not know the <s>pañcāgnividyā</s> or <s>Brahman</s> as truth, they, through the sequence of oblations beginning with faith, when the fifth oblation is offered, being born from the fire of woman, rise up again to the world, become performers of rites such as the <s>agnihotra</s>. Through that <s>karma</s>, by the sequence of smoke and the rest, they go again to the world of the ancestors, and again by the sequence of rain-cloud and the rest, they revolve back to this [world]. Born again from the fire of woman, performing <s>karma</s> again — thus, like a water-wheel (<s>ghaṭīyantra</s>), through going and coming, they revolve again and again. But when they know thus, freed from the revolving of the water-wheel, they pass into the flame. '<s>Arcis</s>' does not mean merely the flame of a fire; rather, [it means] the deity presiding over the flame, denoted by the word '<s>arcis</s>' — a deity constituting a station on the subsequent path — that is established; they pass into that [deity]. For there is no direct connection of wandering mendicants with the flame of a fire. Therefore, the deity denoted by the word '<s>arcis</s>' is accepted. Therefore [they pass] to the deity of the day. Since it is untenable to fix the time of death to daytime, the word 'day' (<s>ahas</s>) also [denotes] a deity. For death occurs upon the exhaustion of one's lifespan. It is not possible to regulate that one who knows thus must die only during the day. Nor do those who have died at night wait for the day. From another <s>śruti</s>: 'As quickly as the mind [can travel], he reaches the Sun.' Having been conveyed by the deity of the day, they attain the deity of the bright fortnight — the deity of the <s>śuklapakṣa</s> (bright half of the month). From the bright fortnight, having been conveyed by the deity of the bright fortnight, they attain the [deities of the] six months during which the sun goes northward. From those months — the plural indicating that the six <s>uttarāyaṇa</s> deities are group-goers — having been conveyed by the deities of the six months, they attain the deity presiding over the world of the gods (<s>devaloka</s>). From the world of the gods, [they reach] the sun; from the sun, the <s>vaidyuta</s> — the deity presiding over lightning. Having reached the deity of lightning, a person (<s>puruṣa</s>) dwelling in the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, created mentally by <s>Brahmā</s> — hence <s>mānasa</s> (mental) — a certain [being], having come [to them], leads them to the worlds of <s>Brahman</s>. The worlds of <s>Brahman</s> — being differentiated into lower and higher levels — are [therefore] referred to in the plural, 'they are led to.' Because of the use of the plural. And because the gradation of meditations [warrants this]. They, having been led by that person, in those worlds of <s>Brahman</s>, being the highest (<s>parāḥ</s>) — being supreme — themselves being the highest, they dwell for excellent (<s>parāvatas</s>), distinguished years — for many years. They dwell for many <s>kalpas</s> of <s>Brahmā</s> — this is the meaning. For them who have gone to the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, there is no return — no coming back to this <s>saṃsāra</s> — 'no return here' — from the reading of another <s>śākhā</s> (recension). [Objection:] 'Here' (<s>iha</s>) is merely a phonetic form? Like [the phrase] 'tomorrow being the full-moon day' [where 'tomorrow' is merely expletive]? [Reply:] No — because the qualifier 'here' would be purposeless [if merely expletive]. For if they simply do not return at all, the word 'here' would be entirely meaningless.

atha ye yajñena dānena tapasā lokāñ jayanti te dhūmam abhisaṃbhavanti |
dhūmād rātrim |
rātrer apakṣīyamāṇapakṣam |
apakṣīyamāṇapakṣād yān ṣaṇ māsān dakṣiṇāditya eti |
māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokam |
pitṛlokāc candram |
te candraṃ prāpyānnaṃ bhavanti |
tāṃs tatra devā yathā somaṃ rājānam āpyāyasvāpakṣīyasvety evam enāṃs tatra bhakṣayanti |
teṣāṃ yadā tat paryavaity athemam evākāśam abhiniṣpadyante |
ākāśād vāyum |
vāyor vṛṣṭim |
vṛṣṭeḥ pṛthivīm |
te pṛthivīṃ prāpyānnaṃ bhavanti |
te punaḥ puruṣāgnau hūyante tato yoṣāgnau jāyante |
lokān pratyuthāyinas ta evam evānuparivartante |
atha ya etau panthānau na vidus te kīṭāḥ pataṅgā yad idaṃ dandaśūkam || BrhUp_6,2.16 ||
children.translated_text: But those who win worlds by sacrifice, charity, and austerity — they pass into the smoke. From the smoke, into the night. From the night, into the dark half of the month. From the dark half, into the six months during which the sun moves southward. From those months, into the world of the ancestors (<s>pitṛloka</s>). From the world of the ancestors, into the moon. Having reached the moon, they become food. There the gods consume them, just as [they consume] King <s>Soma</s> — 'increase! decrease!' — thus they consume them there. When that [merit] is exhausted, they fall into this very space. From space, into the wind. From the wind, into the rain. From the rain, into the earth. Having reached the earth, they become food. Then they are again offered in the fire of man, and thence are born in the fire of woman. Rising up to the worlds, they thus revolve again. But those who know neither of these two paths — they become insects, moths, and whatever bites here. // BṛUp 6.2.16 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,2.16 atha punarye naivaṃ vidurutkrāntyādyagnihotrasaṃbandhapadārthaṣaṭkasyaiva veditāraḥ kevalakarmiṇo yajñenāgnihotrādinā dānena bahirvedi bhikṣamāṇeṣu dravyasaṃvibhāgalakṣaṇena tapasā bahirvedyeva dīkṣādivyatiriktena kṛcchracāndrāyaṇādinā lokāñjayanti /
lokāniti bahuvacanāttatrāpi phalatāramyamabhipretam /
te dhūmamabhisaṃbhavanti /
uttaramārga ivehāpi devatā eva dhūmādiśabdavācyāḥ /
dhūmadevatāṃ pratipadyanta ityarthaḥ /
ātivāhikatvaṃ ca devatānāṃ tadvadeva /
dhūmādrātriṃ rātridevatāṃ tato 'pakṣīyamāṇapakṣadevatāṃ tato yānṣaṇmāsāndakṣiṇāṃ diśamāditya eti tānmāsadevatāviśeṣānpratipadyante /
māsebhyaḥ pitṛlokaṃ pitṛlokāccandram /
te candraṃ prāpyānnaṃ bhavanti tāṃstatrānnabhūtānyathā somaṃ rājānamiha yajña ṛtvija āpyāyasvāpakṣīyasveti bhakṣayantyevamenāṃścandraṃ prāptānkarmiṇo bhṛtyāniva svāmino bhakṣayantyupabhuñjate devāḥ āpyāyasvāpakṣīyasveti na mantraḥ kiṃ tarhyāpyāyyā'pyāyya camasasthaṃ bhakṣaṇenāpakṣayaṃ ca kṛtvā punaḥ punarbhakṣayantītyarthaḥ /
evaṃ devā api somaloke labdhaśarīrānkarmiṇa upakaraṇabhūtānpunaḥ punarviśrāmayantaḥ karmānurūpaṃ phalaṃ prayacchantaḥ /
taddhi teṣāmāpyāyanaṃ somasyā'pyāyanamivopabhuñjata upakaraṇabhūtāndevāḥ teṣāṃ karmiṇāṃ yadā yasminkāle tadyajñadānādilakṣaṇaṃ somalokaprāpakaṃ karma paryavaiti parigacchati parikṣīyata ityarthaḥ /
atha tademameva prasiddhamākāśamabhiniṣpadyante /
yāstāḥ śraddhāśabdavācyā dyulokāgnau hutā āpaḥ somākārapariṇatā yābhiḥ somaloke karmiṇāmupabhogāya śarīramārabdhamammayaṃ tāḥ karmakṣayāddhimapiṇḍa ivā'tapasaṃparkātpravilīyante /
pravilīnāḥ sūkṣmā ākāśabhūtā iva bhavanti tadidamucyata imamevā'kāśamabhiniṣpadyanta iti /
te punarapi karmiṇastaccharīrāḥ santaḥ purovātādinā itāścāmutaśca nīyante 'ntarikṣagāstadāha-ākāśādvāyumiti /

taduktam-parjanyāgnau somaṃ rājānaṃ juhvatīti /

te pṛthivīṃ prāpya vrīhiyavādyannaṃ bhavanti /
taduktamasmiṃlloke 'gnau vṛṣṭiṃ juhvati tasyā āhutyā annaṃ saṃbhavatīti /
te punaḥ puruṣāgnau hūyante 'nnabhūtā retaḥsici /
tato retobhūtā yoṣāgnau hūyante tato jāyante lokaṃ pratyutthāyinaste lokaṃ pratyuttiṣṭhanto 'gnihotrādikarmānutiṣṭhanti /
tato dhūmādinā punaḥ punaḥ somalokaṃ punarimaṃ lokamiti /
ta evaṃ karmiṇo 'nuparivartante ghaṭīyantravaccakrībhūtā baṃbhramantītyarthaḥ /
uttaramārgāya sadyomuktaye vā yāvadbrahma na viduḥ /
iti nu kāmayamānaḥ saṃsaratītyuktam /
atha punarya uttaraṃ dakṣiṇaṃ caitau panthānau na viduruttarasya dakṣiṇasya vā pathaḥ pratipattaye jñānaṃ karma vā nānutiṣṭhantītyarthaḥ /
te kiṃ bhavantīti /
ucyate-te kīṭāḥ pataṅgā yadidaṃ yaccedaṃ dandaśūkaṃ daṃśamaśakamityetadbhavanti /

tathā ca śrutyantaram-"tānīmāni kṣudrāṇyasakṛdāvartīni bhūtāni bhavanti jāyasva mriyasva"iti /
tasmātsarvotsāhena yathāśakti svābhāvikakarmajñānahānena dakṣiṇottaramārgapratipattisādhanaṃ śāsrīyaṃ karma jñānaṃ vānutiṣṭhediti vākyārthaḥ /
tathā coktam"ato vai khalu durniṣprapataraṃ tasmājjugupseta"iti śrutyantarānmokṣāya prayatetetyarthaḥ /
atrāpyuttaramārgapratipattisādhana eva mahānyatnaḥ kartavya iti gamyate /
evamevānuparivartanta ityuktatvāt /
evaṃ praśnāḥ sarve nirṇītāḥ /
esau vai loka ityārabhya puruṣaḥ saṃbhavatīticaturthaḥ praśno yatithyāmāhutyāmityādiḥ prathamyena /
pañcamastu dvitīyatvena devayānasya vā pathaḥ pratipadaṃ pitṛyāṇasya veti dakṣiṇottaramārgapratipattisādhanakathanena /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And the fifth [question is answered] by the second — by stating the means of attaining the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) or the path of the ancestors (<s>pitṛyāṇa</s>), i.e., the means for attaining the southern and northern paths.

children.text: tenaiva ca prathamo 'pyagnerābhya kecidarciḥ pratipadyante keciddhūmamiti vipratipattiḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And by the same [exposition], the first [question] too [is resolved]: 'From fire, some attain the flame [path]; some attain the smoke [path]' — thus the divergence [of paths is explained].

children.text: punarāvṛttiśca dvitīyaḥ praśna ākāśādikrameṇemaṃ lokamāgacchantīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And the return (<s>punarāvṛtti</s>) — the second question — [is resolved by showing that they] come back to this world by the sequence of space and the like.

children.text: tenaivāsau loko na saṃpūryate kīṭapataṅgādipratipatteśca keṣāñciditi tṛtīyo 'pi praśno nirṇītaḥ16 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And by the same [exposition], 'That world does not become full' — because some attain the [lowly] state of insects and moths — thus the third question too is resolved. // 16 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 6.2.16: But again, those who do not know thus — who are merely the knowers of the six categories connected with the <s>Agnihotra</s> beginning with departure, who are mere ritualists (<s>kevalakarmiṇas</s>) — by sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like, by charity (<s>dāna</s>) characterized by the distribution of goods to those begging outside the sacrificial enclosure, by austerity (<s>tapas</s>) performed outside the sacrificial enclosure alone, distinct from <s>dīkṣā</s> (consecration) and the like, such as <s>kṛcchra</s>, <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>, and the rest — they conquer worlds.
The plural 'worlds' indicates that a gradation of fruits is intended there too.
They attain smoke (<s>dhūma</s>).
As in the northern path, here too the words 'smoke' and the rest denote deities.
They reach the deity of smoke — this is the meaning.
And the function of the deities as transmitters (<s>ātivāhika</s>) is the same as [described] there.
From smoke to night — the deity of night; from there to the deity of the waning fortnight (<s>apakṣīyamāṇapakṣa</s>); from there, the six months during which the sun moves toward the southern direction — they reach the specific month-deities.
From the months to the world of the ancestors (<s>pitṛloka</s>); from the world of the ancestors to the moon (<s>candra</s>).
Having reached the moon, they become food. There, having become food — just as here in the sacrifice the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) consume King <s>Soma</s> [saying] 'Increase! Decrease!' — even so, the gods consume these ritualists who have reached the moon, as masters consume servants. '<s>Āpyāyasva apakṣīyasva</s>' is not a <s>mantra</s>; rather [the meaning is:] having caused them to increase again and again, and having diminished [them] by consuming the <s>soma</s> in the cup, they consume [them] again and again — this is the meaning.
Even so, the gods too, having given the ritualists who have obtained bodies in the world of <s>Soma</s> rest again and again as their instruments, bestow fruit proportionate to their <s>karma</s>.
For that indeed is their nourishment — just as the nourishment of <s>Soma</s> [is consumed by priests], so the gods enjoy those who have become instruments. When, at whatever time, that <s>karma</s> of those ritualists — characterized as sacrifice, charity, and the like, which brought them to the world of <s>Soma</s> — is exhausted (<s>paryavaiti</s>), becomes depleted — this is the meaning.
Then they descend into this very well-known space (<s>ākāśa</s>).
Those waters, denoted by the word '<s>śraddhā</s>' (faith), which were offered into the fire of the heavenly world, which had transformed into the form of <s>Soma</s> — by which the body made of food (<s>annamaya</s>) was produced for the enjoyment of the ritualists in the world of <s>Soma</s> — those, upon the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, dissolve like a ball of hail upon contact with heat.
Having dissolved, they become subtle, as if [merged with] space — this is what is stated: 'They descend into this very space.'
Those ritualists, still possessing those [subtle] bodies, are carried here and there by wind and the like, traveling through the atmosphere — therefore [the text] says: 'From space to wind.'
From wind they reach rain.
As it was stated: 'They offer King <s>Soma</s> into the fire of <s>Parjanya</s> (the rain-god).'
Then, having become rain, they fall upon this earth.
Having reached the earth, they become food such as rice, barley, and the like.
As it was stated: 'In this world, they offer rain into the fire; from that offering, food comes into being.'
Then, having become food, they are offered again into the fire of the man — into the semen.
Thence, having become semen, they are offered into the fire of the woman; from there they are born — they rise up into the world. Having risen up into the world, they perform <s>karma</s> such as the <s>Agnihotra</s> and the like.
From there, by smoke and the like, [they go] again and again to the world of <s>Soma</s> and again to this world.
These ritualists thus revolve repeatedly — going round and round like a water-wheel (<s>ghaṭīyantra</s>) — this is the meaning.
[They continue revolving] as long as they do not know [the path to] the northern route (<s>uttaramārga</s>) or immediate liberation (<s>sadyomukti</s>).
Thus it was stated: 'One who desires, transmigrates.'
But again, those who do not know either these two paths — the northern and the southern — who do not follow the knowledge or <s>karma</s> for the attainment of either the northern or the southern path — this is the meaning.
What do they become?
It is said: they become insects, moths, and whatever biting creatures there are — flies and mosquitoes — this is what they become.
For thus is this course of <s>saṃsāra</s> terrible; for one who has sunk into it, rescue is indeed rare.
As another <s>śruti</s> also [says]: 'These tiny creatures that revolve again and again — "Be born! Die!"'
Therefore, with all effort, according to one's capacity, abandoning natural [unsanctioned] <s>karma</s> and [unsanctioned] knowledge, one should practice the scriptural <s>karma</s> or knowledge that is the means for attaining the southern or northern path — this is the meaning of the passage.
As it was also stated: 'From this indeed it is difficult to escape; therefore one should feel revulsion' — meaning, from another <s>śruti</s>, one should strive for liberation.
Herein too, it is understood that the greatest effort should be made precisely for the means of attaining the northern path,
because it was stated: 'Thus they revolve again and again.'
Thus all the questions have been resolved.
Beginning with 'This world indeed...' up to 'A person comes into being' — the fourth question ['in which oblation does water come to be called "person"?'] [is answered] by the first [section on the five fires];

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya dvitīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //2//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the sixth chapter in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> [Bhāṣya]. // 2 //

children.text:
sa yaḥ kāmayeta -- mahat prāpnuyām ity udagayana āpūryamāṇapakṣasya puṇyāhe dvādaśāham upasadvratī bhūtvaudumbare kaṃse camase vā sarvauṣadhaṃ phalānīti saṃbhṛtya parisamuhya parilipyāgnim upasamādhāya paristīryāvṛtājyaṃ saṃskṛtya puṃsā nakṣatreṇa manthaṃ saṃnīya juhoti --
yāvanto devās tvayi jātavedas tiryañco ghnanti puruṣasya kāmān |
tebhyo 'haṃ bhāgadheyaṃ juhomi te mā tṛptāḥ sarvaiḥ kāmais tarpayantu svāhā |
yā tiraścī nipadyase 'haṃ vidharaṇī iti |
tāṃ tvā ghṛtasya dhārayā yaje saṃrādhanīm ahaṃ svāhā || BrhUp_6,3.1 ||
children.translated_text:
He who desires 'May I attain greatness' — during the northern course [of the sun], in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious day, having observed the <s>upasad</s> vow for twelve days, having gathered in a bowl or cup made of <s>udumbara</s> (fig-wood) all herbs and fruits, having swept and smeared [the ground], having placed the fire, having strewn [the sacred grass] around, having purified the clarified butter, and having prepared the <s>mantha</s> (stirred offering) under a masculine constellation (<s>nakṣatra</s>), he offers [with these <s>mantras</s>]:
'Whatever gods there are in you, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, who athwart destroy the desires of a person — to them I offer a share; may they, being satisfied, satisfy me with all desires. <s>Svāhā</s>!'
'O you who lie athwart — I am the support (<s>vidharaṇī</s>)!'
'With a stream of clarified butter, I worship you, O fulfiller (<s>saṃrādhanī</s>). <s>Svāhā</s>!' // <s>BṛhUp</s> 6.3.1 //

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,3.1 sa yaḥ kāmayeta /
jñānakarmaṇorgatiruktā /

taccāpratyavāyakāriṇopāyeneti tadarthaṃ manthākhyaṃ karmā'rabhyate mahattvaprāptaye /
mahattve ca satyarthasiddhaṃ hi vittam /
taducyate-sa yaḥ kāmayeta sa yo vittārthī karmaṇyadhikṛto yaḥ kāmayeta /
kim /
mahanmahattvaṃ prāpnuyāṃ mahānsyāmitītyarthaḥ /

smārtaṃ hīdaṃ manthakarma /

audumbara udumbaravṛkṣamaye kaṃse camase vā tasyaiva viśeṣaṇaṃ kaṃsākāre camasākāre vaudumbara eva /
ākāre tu vikalpo naudumbaratve /
etra sarvauṣadhaṃ sarvāsāmoṣadhīnāṃ samūhaṃ yathāsambhavaṃ yathāśakti ca sarvā oṣadhīḥ samāhṛtya tatra grāmyāṇāṃ tu daśa niyamena grāhyā vrīhiyavādyā vakṣyamāṇāḥ /
adhikagrahaṇe tu na doṣaḥ /
grāmyāṇāṃ phalāni ca yathāsambhavaṃ yathāśakti ca /
itiśabdaḥ samastasambhāropacayapradarśanārthaḥ /
anyadapi yatsambharaṇīyaṃ tatsarvaṃ saṃbhṛtyetyarthaḥ /
