agnimupasamādhāyeti vacanādāvasathye 'gnāviti gamyate /
ekavacanādupasamādhānaśravaṇācca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Because of the singular [number], and because the term '<s>upasamādhāna</s>' (placing) is heard.

children.text: vidyamānasyaivopasamādhānam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Upasamādhāna</s>' (placing) refers to [reviving] what already exists [i.e., the existing domestic fire].

children.text: paristīrya darbhānāvṛtā smārtatvātkarmaṇaḥ sthālīpākāvṛtparigṛhyate /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Having strewn around' (<s>paristīrya</s>) — <s>darbha</s> grass; the repetition [of procedures] is <s>smārta</s> — therefore the <s>sthālīpāka</s> repetition [pattern] is adopted, because the <s>karma</s> is <s>smārta</s>.

children.text: tayā'jyaṃ saṃskṛtya puṃsā nakṣatreṇa puṃnāmnā nakṣatreṇa puṇyāhasaṃyuktena manthaṃ sarvauṣadhaphalapiṣṭaṃ tatraudumbare camase dadhani madhuni ghṛte copasicyaikayopamanthanyopamaṃmathya saṃnīya madhye saṃsthāpyaudumbareṇa sruveṇā'vāpasthāna ājyasya juhotyetairmantrairyāvanto devā ityādyaiḥ //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] With that [repetition pattern], having purified the clarified butter; under a masculine constellation (<s>puṃsā nakṣatreṇa</s>) — a constellation bearing a masculine name, conjoined with an auspicious day — having prepared the <s>mantha</s>, which is the paste of all herbs and fruits, pouring <s>dadhi</s> (yogurt), honey, and clarified butter into that <s>audumbara</s> cup, stirring [it] with a churning stick, having placed [the offering] in the center, with an <s>audumbara</s> ladle (<s>sruva</s>), at the place of the supplementary offering, he offers the clarified butter with these <s>mantras</s> beginning with '<s>yāvanto devāḥ</s>' and the like. // 1 //

<s>BṛhUpBh</s> 6.3.1: 'He who desires' — the paths of knowledge and <s>karma</s> have been stated. Therein, knowledge is independent, but <s>karma</s> depends on two kinds of wealth — divine and human. Therefore, wealth must be acquired for the sake of <s>karma</s>.
And that [acquisition] should be by a method that does not incur sin — for that purpose, the ritual called <s>mantha</s> (the stirred offering) is commenced, for the attainment of greatness.
And when greatness is achieved, wealth is [automatically] accomplished.
This is stated: 'He who desires' — he who, being eligible for <s>karma</s> and seeking wealth, desires —
what? — 'May I attain greatness' (<s>mahat</s>) — may I become great — this is the meaning.
Therein, the time of the <s>mantha</s> ritual that is intended to be prescribed is stated: 'During the northern course [of the sun]' (<s>udagayana</s>) — everywhere where the sun [is moving northward], 'in the waxing fortnight' (<s>āpūryamāṇapakṣa</s>) — the bright fortnight.
Therein too, everywhere where [the bright fortnight occurs], 'on an auspicious day' (<s>puṇyāha</s>) — a day that is favorable, conducive to the success of one's <s>karma</s> — this is the meaning.
'For twelve days' — commencing from the auspicious day on which one wishes to perform the <s>karma</s>, counting back, beginning from the auspicious day itself, [one observes] the <s>upasad</s> vow for twelve days.
The <s>upasads</s> are well known in the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> [ritual]. There, the vow consists of drinking milk through the increase and decrease of the breast [i.e., regulated consumption]. Here too, since the ritual procedures of [the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>] are not carried over, only the bare milk-drinking, devoid of [specific] ritual requirements, is adopted.
[Objection:] But when the compound '<s>upasadvratī</s>' is analyzed [as a <s>tatpuruṣa</s>], all the ritual requirements in their entirety should be adopted — why then are they not adopted?
[Reply:] It is said: because the <s>karma</s> is <s>smārta</s> (based on <s>smṛti</s>).
For this <s>mantha</s> ritual is <s>smārta</s>.
[Objection:] But since it is prescribed by <s>śruti</s>, how can it be <s>smārta</s>?
[Reply:] This <s>śruti</s> is merely restating what is [already found in] <s>smṛti</s>.
For if it were <s>śrauta</s> (based on <s>śruti</s>), there would be a relationship of model (<s>prakṛti</s>) and derivative (<s>vikāra</s>), and consequently the derivative ritual would have to adopt the properties of the model — but that [<s>śrauta</s> character] does not apply here.
And for this very reason, this ritual is prescribed [to be performed] in the domestic fire (<s>āvasathya</s>).
And every repetition (<s>āvṛt</s>) is <s>smārta</s> only.
Having observed the <s>upasad</s> vow — meaning: having observed the milk-diet — this is the meaning.
'In an <s>audumbara</s>' — made from the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) tree — '<s>kaṃsa</s>' (bowl) or '<s>camasa</s>' (cup) — these are qualifiers of the same [vessel]: either bowl-shaped or cup-shaped, but [always] of <s>udumbara</s> [wood].
The option pertains to the shape, not to the [requirement of] <s>udumbara</s> [wood].
Therein, 'all herbs' (<s>sarvauṣadham</s>) — having gathered the collection of all herbs as far as possible, according to one's capacity — all herbs. But of the cultivated [plants], ten must be taken as a rule — rice, barley, and the rest, which will be mentioned [later].
But taking additional ones is not a fault.
And of the cultivated [plants], fruits too — as far as possible, according to one's capacity.
The word '<s>iti</s>' is for the purpose of indicating the entire collection of materials.
Whatever else is to be gathered — all of that [should be] gathered — this is the meaning.
The sequence [of procedures] therein should be seen as stated in the <s>Gṛhyasūtra</s>.
Sweeping and smearing is the preparation of the ground.
'Having placed the fire' (<s>agnim upasamādhāya</s>) — from this statement, it is understood [that the ritual is to be performed] in the domestic fire (<s>āvasathya</s>).

children.text: START BrhUp 6,3.2-3
children.translated_text: [Start of <s>BṛhUp</s> 6.3.2-3]

children.text:
jyeṣṭhāya svāhā śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati |
prāṇāya svāhā vasiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati |
vāce svāhā pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati |
cakṣuṣe svāhā saṃpade svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati |
śrotrāya svāhāyatanāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati |
manase svāhā prajātyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati |
retase svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃsravam avanayati || BrhUp_6,3.2 ||
children.translated_text:
'To the eldest, <s>svāhā</s>! To the best, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To <s>prāṇa</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the most excellent (<s>vasiṣṭhā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To speech, <s>svāhā</s>! To the foundation (<s>pratiṣṭhā</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To the eye, <s>svāhā</s>! To prosperity (<s>sampad</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To the ear, <s>svāhā</s>! To the abode (<s>āyatana</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To the mind, <s>svāhā</s>! To procreation (<s>prajāti</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To semen (<s>retas</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 6.3.2 //

children.translated_text:
'To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To <s>Soma</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'<s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'<s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'<s>Svaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'<s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To <s>Brahman</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To <s>Kṣatra</s> (the ruling power), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To the past (<s>bhūta</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To the future (<s>bhaviṣyat</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To the universe (<s>viśva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To all (<s>sarva</s>), <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>.
'To <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — having offered into the fire, he pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>. // <s>BṛhUp</s> 6.3.3 //

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,3.2-3 jyeṣṭhāya svāhā śreṣṭhāya svāhetyārabhya dve dve āhutī hutvā manthe saṃsravamavanayati /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.3.2-3:] Beginning with 'to the eldest, <s>svāhā</s>! to the best, <s>svāhā</s>!', having offered two oblations each, one pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s> (churned mixture).

children.text: sruvāvalepanamājyaṃ manthe saṃsrāvayati /
children.translated_text: One drains the ghee clinging to the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) into the <s>mantha</s>.

children.text: etasmādeva jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāyetyādiprāṇaliṅgājjyeṣṭhaśreṣṭhādiprāṇavida evāsminkarmaṇyadhikāraḥ /
children.translated_text: From this very indication of <s>Prāṇa</s> in 'to the eldest, to the best' and so on, only one who knows <s>Prāṇa</s> as the eldest, the best, and so forth has the right to perform this ritual.

children.text: retasa ityārambhaikaikāmāhutiṃ hutvā manthe saṃsravamavanayatyaparayopamanthanyā punarmathnāti //2-3 //
children.translated_text: Beginning with 'of semen,' having offered one oblation each, one pours the residue into the <s>mantha</s>; with the other churning stick one churns again. || 2-3 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 6,3.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.3.4]

children.text:
athainam abhimṛśati -- bhramad asi |
jvalad asi |
pūrṇam asi |
prastabdham asi |
ekasabham asi |
hiṅkṛtam asi |
hiṅkriyamānam asi |
udgītham asi |
udgīyamānam asi |
śrāvitam asi |
pratyāśrāvitam asi |
ārdre saṃdīptam asi |
vibhūr asi |
prabhūr asi |
annam asi |
jyotir asi |
nidhanam asi |
saṃvargo 'sīti || BrhUp_6,3.4 ||
children.translated_text: Then he touches it (saying) — 'You are moving! You are blazing! You are full! You are firm! You are the one resort! You are the <s>hiṅkāra</s> (humming sound) that has been made! You are the <s>hiṅkāra</s> being made! You are the <s>Udgītha</s> (chant) that has been sung! You are the <s>Udgītha</s> being sung! You are what has been called out! You are what has been responded to! You are kindled in a moist place! You are all-pervading! You are all-powerful! You are food! You are light! You are the final resting place! You are the all-absorber!' || BṛhUp 6.3.4 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,3.4 athainamabhimṛśati bhramadasītyanena mantreṇa //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.3.4:] Then he touches it with this <s>mantra</s> beginning 'You are moving.' || 4 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 6,3.5
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.3.5]

children.text:
athainam udyacchaty āmaṃsy āmaṃ hi te mahi |
sa hi rājeśāno 'dhipatiḥ |
sa māṃ rājeśano 'dhipatiṃ karotv iti || BrhUp_6,3.5 ||
children.translated_text: Then he lifts it up (saying): 'To you, O <s>Āman</s>, for your greatness is indeed vast! He indeed is the king, the sovereign lord, the ruler. May he make me the king, the sovereign lord, the ruler!' || BṛhUp 6.3.5 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,3.5 athainamucchati saha pātreṇa haste gṛhṇātyāmaṃsyāmaṃhi te mahītyanena //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.3.5:] Then he lifts it up — he takes it together with the vessel in his hand — with this <s>mantra</s>, 'To you, O <s>Āman</s>, for your greatness is indeed vast.' || 5 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 6,3.6
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.3.6]

children.text:
athainam ācāmati --
tat savitur vareṇyam |
madhu vātā ṛtāyate madhu kṣaranti sindhavaḥ |
mādhvīr naḥ santv oṣadhīḥ |
bhūḥ svāhā |
bhargo devasya dhīmahi
madhu naktam utoṣaso madhumat pārthivaṃ rajaḥ |
madhu dyaur astu naḥ pitā |
bhuvaḥ svāhā |
dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt |
madhumān no vanaspatir madhumāṃ astu sūryaḥ |
mādhvīr gavo bhavantu naḥ |
svaḥ svāhā |
sarvāṃ ca sāvitrīm anvāha |
sarvāś ca madhumatīr aham evedaṃ sarvaṃ bhūyāsaṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāheti antata ācamya pāṇī prakṣālya jaghanenāgniṃ prākśirāḥ saṃviśati |
prātar ādityam upatiṣṭhate |
diśām ekapuṇḍarīkam asi |
ahaṃ manuṣyāṇām ekapuṇḍarīkaṃ bhūyāsam iti |
yathetam etya jaghanenāgnim āsīno vaṃśaṃ japati || BrhUp_6,3.6 ||
children.translated_text: Then he sips it — 'That excellent glory of <s>Savitṛ</s>; the winds blow sweetness for the one who follows <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the rivers flow sweetness; may the herbs be sweet for us! <s>Bhūḥ svāhā</s>! May we meditate upon the radiance of the god; sweet be the night and dawn, sweet be the earthly region; sweet be heaven, our father! <s>Bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>! May he inspire our thoughts! Sweet be the lord of the forest for us, sweet be the sun; may the cows be sweet for us! <s>Svaḥ svāhā</s>!' He recites the entire <s>Sāvitrī</s> and all the <s>Madhumatī</s> verses. 'May I become all this! <s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>!' — thus at the end, having sipped, having washed his hands, he lies down behind the fire with his head facing east. In the morning he worships the sun: 'You are the one lotus of the directions. May I become the one lotus among men!' Having returned in this manner, sitting behind the fire, he recites the lineage. || BṛhUp 6.3.6 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,3.6 athainamācāmati bhakṣayati gāyatryāḥ prathamapādena madhumatyaikayā vyāhṛtyā ca prathamayā prathamagrāsamācāmati /
tathā gāyatrīdvitīyapādena madhumatyā dvitīyayā dvitīya yā ca vyahṛtyā dvitīyaṃ grāsam /
tathā tṛtīyena gāyatrīpādena tṛtīyayā madhumatyā tṛtīyayā ca vyāhṛtyā tṛtīyaṃ grāsam /
sarvāṃ sāvitrīṃ sarvāśca madhumatīruktvāhamevedaṃ sarvaṃ bhūyāsamiti cānte bhūrbhavaḥ svaḥ svāheti samastaṃ bhaśrayati /
yathā caturbhirgrāsaistaddravyaṃ sarvaṃ parisamāpyate tathā pūrvameva nirupyet /
yatpātrāvaliptaṃ tatpātraṃ sarvaṃ nirṇijya tūṣṇīṃ pivet /
children.translated_text: Whatever remains clinging to the vessel — having wiped the entire vessel clean, one should drink it silently.

children.text: pāṇī prakṣālyāpa ācamya jaghanenāgniṃ paścādagneḥ prākśirāḥ saṃviśati /
children.translated_text: Having washed his hands, having sipped water, he lies down behind the fire, to the west of the fire, with his head facing east.

children.text: prātaḥ saṃdhyāmupāsyā'dityamupatiṣṭhate diśāmekapuṇḍarīkamityanena mantreṇa /
children.translated_text: In the morning, having performed the <s>saṃdhyā</s> (twilight worship), he worships the sun with this <s>mantra</s>: 'You are the one lotus of the directions.'

children.text: yathetaṃ yathāgatametyā'gatya jaghanenāgnimāsīno vaṃśaṃ japati //6//
children.translated_text: Having returned as he went — having come back, sitting behind the fire, he recites the lineage (<s>vaṃśa</s>). || 6 ||

[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.3.6:] Then he sips it — he eats it: with the first <s>pāda</s> (quarter) of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one <s>Madhumatī</s> verse, and the first <s>Vyāhṛti</s>, he sips the first morsel. Similarly, with the second <s>pāda</s> of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the second <s>Madhumatī</s>, and the second <s>Vyāhṛti</s>, the second morsel. Similarly, with the third <s>pāda</s> of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the third <s>Madhumatī</s>, and the third <s>Vyāhṛti</s>, the third morsel. Having recited the entire <s>Sāvitrī</s> and all the <s>Madhumatī</s> verses, and saying at the end 'May I become all this! <s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>!', he consumes the whole together. One should determine beforehand how the entire substance is consumed in four morsels.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,3.7-12
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.3.7-12]

children.text: taṃ haitam uddālaka āruṇir vājasaneyāya yājñavalkyāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti || BrhUp_6,3.7 ||
children.translated_text: This indeed <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> told to his pupil <s>Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya</s>, saying: 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.' || BṛhUp 6.3.7 ||

children.text: etam u haiva vājasaneyo yājnavalkyo madhukāya paiṅgyāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti || BrhUp_6,3.8 ||
children.translated_text: This same thing <s>Vājasaneya Yājñavalkya</s> told to his pupil <s>Madhuka Paiṅgya</s>, saying: 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.' || BṛhUp 6.3.8 ||

children.text: etam u haiva madhukaḥ paiṅgyaś cūlāya bhāgavittaye 'ntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti || BrhUp_6,3.9 ||
children.translated_text: This same thing <s>Madhuka Paiṅgya</s> told to his pupil <s>Cūla Bhāgavitta</s>, saying: 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.' || BṛhUp 6.3.9 ||

children.text: etam u haiva cūlo bhāgavittir jānakaya āyaḥsthūṇāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti || BrhUp_6,3.10 ||
children.translated_text: This same thing <s>Cūla Bhāgavitta</s> told to his pupil <s>Jānaki Āyasthūṇa</s>, saying: 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.' || BṛhUp 6.3.10 ||

children.text: etam u haiva jānakir āyasthūṇaḥ satyakāmāya jābālāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti || BrhUp_6,3.11 ||
children.translated_text: This same thing <s>Jānaki Āyasthūṇa</s> told to his pupil <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, saying: 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.' || BṛhUp 6.3.11 ||

children.text:
etam u haiva satyakāmo jābālo 'ntevāsibhya uktvova -- acāpi ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti |
tam etaṃ nāputrāya vānantevāsine vā brūyāt || BrhUp_6,3.12 ||
children.translated_text: This same thing <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s> told to his pupils, saying: 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.' This one should not tell to one who is not a son or not a pupil. || BṛhUp 6.3.12 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,3.7-12 taṃ haitamuddālaka ityādi satyakāmo jābālo 'ntevāsibhya uktvovācāpi ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcejjāyerannevāsmiñśākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānītyevamantamenaṃ manthamuddālakātprabhṛtyekaikācāryakramāgataṃ satyakāma ācāryo bahubhyo 'ntevāsibhya uktvovāca /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.3.7-12:] 'This indeed <s>Uddālaka</s>' and so on — <s>Satyakāma Jābāla</s>, the teacher, told many pupils this <s>mantha</s> (teaching), which had come down through the succession of teachers one by one beginning from <s>Uddālaka</s>, ending with 'Even if one were to pour this on a dry stump, branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth.'

children.text: kimanyaduvācetyucyate-api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau gataprāṇe 'pyenaṃ manthaṃ bhakṣaṇāya saṃskṛtaṃ niṣiñcetprakṣipejjāyerannutpadyerannevāsminsthāṇau śākhā avayavā vṛkṣasya praroheyuśca palāśāni parṇāni yathā jīvataḥ sthāṇoḥ kimutānena karmaṇā kāmaḥ sidhyediti /
children.translated_text: What else did he say? This is stated — 'Even if one were to pour this, the <s>mantha</s> prepared for consumption, on a dry stump, one from which life has departed, branches — limbs of the tree — would be born, would arise in that very stump, and leaves would sprout forth, just as from a living tree. How much more then would one's desire be fulfilled by this ritual!' —

children.text: dhruvaphalamidaṃ karmeti karmastutyarthametat /
children.translated_text: This is a praise of the ritual to indicate that this ritual has unfailing results.

children.text: vidyādhigame ṣṭatīrthāni teṣāmiha saprāṇadarśanasya manthavijñānasyādhigame dve eva tīrthe anujñāyete putraścāntevāsī ca //8-12 //
children.translated_text: For the attainment of knowledge, there are prescribed sources. For the attainment of this knowledge of the <s>mantha</s> together with the vision of <s>Prāṇa</s>, only two sources are sanctioned — a son and a pupil. || 8-12 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 6,3.13
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.3.13]

children.text:
caturaudumbaro bhavati |
audumbaraḥ sruva audumbaraś camasa audumbara idhma audumbaryā upamanthanyau |
daśa grāmyāṇi dhānyāni bhavanti |
vrīhiyavās tilamāṣā aṇupriyaṃgavo godhūmāś ca masūrāś ca khalvāś ca khalakulāś ca |
tān piṣṭān dadhani madhuni ghṛta upasiñcati |
ājyasya juhoti || BrhUp_6,3.13 ||
children.translated_text: Four things are of <s>Udumbara</s> wood: the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) is of <s>Udumbara</s>, the <s>camasa</s> (cup) is of <s>Udumbara</s>, the fuel is of <s>Udumbara</s>, and the two churning sticks are of <s>Udumbara</s>. There are ten cultivated grains: rice, barley, sesame, beans, <s>aṇu</s> (millet), <s>priyaṅgu</s> (foxtail millet), wheat, lentils, <s>khalva</s> (a type of pulse), and <s>khalakula</s> (horse gram). Having ground them, one sprinkles them in curds, honey, and ghee. One offers ghee (as oblation). || BṛhUp 6.3.13 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,3.13 caturaudumbaro bhavatīti vyākhyātam /
daśa grāmyāṇi bhavanti grāmyāṇāṃ tu dhānyānāṃ daśa niyamena grāhyā ityavocāma /
ke ta iti nirdiśyante-vrīhiyavāstilamāṣā aṇupriyaṅgavo 'ṇavaścāṇuśabdavācyāḥ kvaciddeśe /
children.translated_text: What are they? They are specified: rice, barley, sesame, beans, <s>aṇu</s> and <s>priyaṅgu</s> — and <s>aṇu</s> is the term designated by the word '<s>aṇu</s>' in certain regions.

children.text: priyaṅgavaḥ prasiddhāḥ kaṅguśabdena /
children.translated_text: <s>Priyaṅgu</s> is well-known by the word '<s>kaṅgu</s>' (foxtail millet).

children.text: khalvā niṣpāvā vallaśabdavācyā loke khalakulāḥ kulatthāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Khalva</s> are <s>niṣpāva</s> (flat beans), known in common parlance by the word '<s>valla</s>'; <s>khalakula</s> are <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram).

children.text: etadvyatirekeṇa yathāśakti sarvauṣadhayo grāhyāḥ phalāni cetyavocāmāyājñikāni varjayitvā //13//
children.translated_text: Apart from these, all herbs and fruits should be taken as far as possible, as we have stated, excluding those not fit for ritual use. || 13 ||

[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.3.13:] 'Four things are of <s>Udumbara</s> wood' — this has been explained. 'There are ten cultivated grains' — we have stated that exactly ten of the cultivated grains are to be taken.

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya tṛtīyaṃ brāhmaṇam //2//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> of the sixth <s>Adhyāya</s> of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. || 2 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.1
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.4.1]

children.text:
eṣāṃ vai bhūtānāṃ pṛthivī rasaḥ |
pṛthivyā āpaḥ |
apām oṣadhayaḥ |
oṣadhīnāṃ puṣpāṇi |
puṣpāṇāṃ phalāni |
phalānāṃ puruṣaḥ |
puruṣasya retaḥ || BrhUp_6,4.1 ||
children.translated_text: Of these beings, earth is the essence. Of earth, water is the essence. Of water, herbs are the essence. Of herbs, flowers are the essence. Of flowers, fruits are the essence. Of fruits, <s>puruṣa</s> (the person) is the essence. Of <s>puruṣa</s>, semen (<s>retas</s>) is the essence. || BṛhUp 6.4.1 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.1"sarvebhyo 'ṅgebhyastejaḥ saṃbhūtam"iti śrutyantarāt //1//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛhUp 6.4.1:] From another <s>Śruti</s>: 'The radiance (<s>tejas</s>) is produced from all the limbs.' || 1 ||

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.2
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.4.2]

children.text:
sa ha prajāpatir īkṣāṃ cakre -- hantāsmai pratiṣṭhāṃ kalpayānīti sa striyaṃ sasṛje |
tāṃ sṛṣṭvādha upāsta |
tasmāt striyam adha upāsīta |
sa etaṃ prāñcaṃ grāvāṇam ātmana eva samudapārayat |
tenainām abhyasṛjata || BrhUp_6,4.2 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> reflected: 'Let me create a receptacle for this.' He created woman. Having created her, he worshipped her from below. Therefore one should worship woman from below. He extended this forward-projecting pressing stone from himself. With that he impregnated her. || BṛhUp 6.4.2 ||

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.2 yata evaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ sāratamametadreto 'taḥ kā nu khalvasya yogyā pratiṣṭheti sa ha sraṣṭā prajāpatirīkṣāñcake /
īkṣāṃ kṛtvā sa sriyaṃ sasṛje /
children.translated_text: Having reflected, he created woman.

children.text: tāṃ ca sṛṣṭvādha upāsta maithunākhyaṃ karmādhaupāsanaṃ nāma kṛtavān /
children.translated_text: And having created her, he worshipped her from below — he performed the act called sexual union, known as 'worship from below' (<s>adha-upāsana</s>).

children.text: tasmātsriyamadha upāsīta śreṣṭhānuśrayaṇā hi prajāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore one should worship woman from below, for offspring follow the pattern of the highest (model).

children.text: atra vājapeyasāmānyakḷptimāha-sa etaṃ prāñcaṃ prakṛṣṭagatiyuktamātmano grāvāṇaṃ somābhiṣavopalasthānīyaṃ kāṭhinyasāmānyātprajananendriyamudapārayadutpūritavānsrīvyañjanaṃ prati tenaināṃ sriyamabhyasṛjadabhisaṃsargaṃ kṛtavān //2//
children.translated_text: Here he states a similarity with the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice: he extended from himself this forward-moving, powerfully directed pressing stone — the reproductive organ, which corresponds to the stone for pressing <s>Soma</s>, on account of its similarity in hardness — he brought it forth as the mark of masculinity; with that he impregnated her — he performed union with the woman. || 2 ||
[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.4.2:] Since semen is thus the innermost essence of all beings, what indeed would be a fitting receptacle for it? — thus <s>Prajāpati</s>, the creator, reflected.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.3
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.4.3]

children.text:
tasyā vedir upasthaḥ |
lomāni barhiś |
carmādhiṣavaṇe |
samiddho madhyatas tau muṣkau |
sa yāvān ha vai vājapeyena yajamanasya loko bhavati tāvān asya loko bhavati |
ya evaṃ vidvān adhopahāsaṃ caraty āsāṃ strīṇāṃ sukṛtaṃ vṛṅkte |
atha ya idam avidvān adhopahāsaṃ caraty āsya striyaḥ sukṛtaṃ vṛñjate || BrhUp_6,4.3 ||
children.translated_text: Her lap is the altar. The hair is the sacred grass (<s>barhis</s>). The skin is the pressing board (<s>adhiṣavaṇa</s>). The two labia are the fire kindled in the middle. He who, knowing this, practices the act of sexual union — his world becomes as great as the world of one who performs the <s>Vājapeya</s> sacrifice. He who thus knows and practices conjugal union absorbs the merit of these women. But he who practices conjugal union without this knowledge — the women take away his merit. || BṛhUp 6.4.3 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,4.3 etaddha sma vai tadvidvānuddālaka āruṇirāhādhopahāsākhyaṃ maithunakarma vājapeyasampannaṃ vidvānityarthaḥ /
tathā nāko maudgalyaḥ kumārahāritaśca /
kiṃ ta āhurityujyate-bahavo maryā maraṇadharmiṇo manuṣyā brāhmaṇā ayanaṃ yeṣāṃ te brahmaṇāyanā brahmabandhavo jātimātropajīvina ityetat /
children.translated_text: What did they say? This is stated: 'Many mortals (<s>marya</s>) — mortal human beings who are <s>brāhmaṇāyana</s>, that is, those whose refuge is <s>Brahman</s> only in name, <s>brahma-bandhu</s>s (kinsmen of <s>Brahman</s> by birth alone), living merely by virtue of their caste' — this is the meaning.

children.text: nirindriyā viśliṣṭendriyā visukṛto vigatasukṛtakarmāṇo 'vidvāṃsau maithunakarmāsaktā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without vigor' (<s>nirindriya</s>) means those whose faculties have fallen apart; 'devoid of merit' (<s>visukṛta</s>) means those whose meritorious deeds are gone — meaning those who are ignorant and attached to the act of sexual union.

children.text: te kimasmāllokātprayanti paralokātparibhraṣṭā iti maithunakarmaṇo 'tyantapāpahetutvaṃ darśayati-ya idamavidvāṃso 'dhopahāsaṃ carantīti /
children.translated_text: 'They depart from this world' means they fall from the other world also — thus he shows that the conjugal act performed without knowledge is a cause of extreme sin: 'those who, not knowing this, practice conjugal union.'

children.text: śrīmanthaṃ kṛtvā patnyā ṛtukālaṃ brahmacaryeṇa pratīkṣate yadīda rataḥ skandati bahu vālpaṃ vā suptasya vā jāgrato vā rāgaprābalyāt //4//
children.translated_text: Having performed the <s>mantha</s> (churning ritual), one waits for the wife's fertile season with <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy). If semen is emitted, whether much or little, whether during sleep or waking, due to the force of passion — || 4 ||

[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.4.3:] This indeed, knowing this, <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> used to say — the meaning is: one who knows the conjugal act as endowed with the sanctity of the <s>Vājapeya</s>. Similarly <s>Nāka Maudgalya</s> and <s>Kumārahārita</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.4
children.translated_text: [Beginning of Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad 6.4.4]

children.text:
etad dha sma vai tad vidvān uddālaka ārunir āha |
etad dha sma vai tad vidvān nāko maudgalya āha |
etad dha sma vai tad vidvān kumārahārita āha -- bahavo maryā brāhmanāyanā nirindriyā visukṛto 'smāl lokāt prayanti ya idam avidvāṃso 'dhopahāsaṃ carantīti |
bahu vā idaṃ suptasya vā jāgrato vā retaḥ skandati || BrhUp_6,4.4 ||
children.translated_text: This indeed, knowing this, <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> used to say. This indeed, knowing this, <s>Nāka Maudgalya</s> used to say. This indeed, knowing this, <s>Kumārahārita</s> used to say — 'Many mortals of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> descent, without vigor, devoid of merit, depart from this world — those who, not knowing this, practice conjugal union.' Whether asleep or awake, much of this semen is spilled. || BṛhUp 6.4.4 ||

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,4.4 etaddha sma vai tadvidvānuddālaka āruṇirāhādhopahāsākhyaṃ maithunakarma vājapeyasampannaṃ vidvānityarthaḥ /
tathā nāko maudgālya- kumārahāritaśca /
kiṃ ta āhurityucyate-bahavo maryā maraṇadharmiṇo manuṣyā brāhmaṇā ayanaṃ yeṣāṃ te brāhmaṇāyanā brahmabandhavo jātimātropajīvina ityetat /
children.translated_text: What did they say? This is stated: 'Many mortals (<s>marya</s>) — mortal human beings who are <s>brāhmaṇāyana</s>, that is, those whose refuge is <s>Brahman</s> only in name, <s>brahma-bandhu</s>s (kinsmen of <s>Brahman</s> by birth alone), living merely by virtue of their caste' — this is the meaning.

children.text: nirindriyā viśilaṣṭendriyā visukṛto vigatasukṛtakarmāṇo 'vidvāṃsau maithunakarmāsaktā ityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Without vigor' (<s>nirindriya</s>) means those whose faculties have fallen apart; 'devoid of merit' (<s>visukṛta</s>) means those whose meritorious deeds are gone — meaning those who are ignorant and attached to the act of sexual union.

children.text: te kimasmāllokātprayanti paralokātparibhraṣṭā iti maithunakarmaṇo 'tyantapāpahetutvaṃ darśayati-ya idamavidvāṃso 'dhopahāsaṃ carantīti /
children.translated_text: 'They depart from this world' means they fall from the other world also — thus he shows that the conjugal act performed without knowledge is a cause of extreme sin: 'those who, not knowing this, practice conjugal union.'

children.text: śrīmanthaṃ kṛtvā patnyā śratukālaṃ brahmacaryeṇa pratīkṣate yadīda rataḥ skandati bahu vālpaṃ vā suptasya vā jāgrato vā rāgaprābalyāt //4//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having prepared the <s>śrīmantha</s> (a ritual drink), he waits for the time of his wife's season (<s>ṛtu</s>) with <s>brahmacarya</s> (continence). If his semen is emitted — whether much or little, whether in sleep or while awake — due to the strength of passion — // 6.4.4 //

[Commentary on BṛhUp 6.4.4:] This indeed, knowing this, <s>Uddālaka Āruṇi</s> used to say — the meaning is: one who knows the conjugal act as endowed with the sanctity of the <s>Vājapeya</s>. Similarly <s>Nāka Maudgalya</s> and <s>Kumārahārita</s>.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.5
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.5]

children.text:
tad abhimṛśed anu vā mantrayeta -- yan me 'dya retaḥ pṛthivīm askāntsīd yad oṣadhīr apy asarad yad apaḥ |
idam ahaṃ tad reta ādade |
punar mām aitu indriyaṃ punas tejaḥ punar bhagaḥ |
punar agnir dhiṣṇyā yathāsthānaṃ kalpantām |
ity anāmikāṅguṣṭhābhyām ādāyāntareṇa stanau vā bhruvau vā nimṛjyāt || BrhUp_6,4.5 ||
children.translated_text: He should touch it [the semen] or recite [the following <s>mantra</s>] over it: 'Whatever semen of mine has fallen on the earth today, whatever has flowed to the herbs, whatever to the waters — I take back that semen. Let virility return to me again, let brilliance (<s>tejas</s>) again, let fortune (<s>bhaga</s>) again. Let the fires [of the body] return to their proper places.' Having taken [the semen] with the ring-finger and thumb, he should rub it between the breasts or between the eyebrows. (BṛUp 6.4.5)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.5 tadabhimṛśedanumantrayeta vānujapedityarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.5:] 'He should touch it or recite the <s>mantra</s>' — meaning: he should mutter [the <s>mantra</s>].

children.text: yadābhimṛśati tadānāmikāṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ tadreta ādade ityevamantena mantreṇa punarmāmityetenanimṛjyādantareṇa madhye bhruvau bhruvervā stanau stanayorvā //5//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When he touches [the semen], [he should do so] with the ring-finger and thumb, reciting the <s>mantra</s> ending with 'I take back that semen'; then, [reciting] 'Let [virility] return to me again,' he should rub it in between — in the middle of — the eyebrows, or between the breasts. // 6.4.5 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.6
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.6]

children.text:
atha yady udaka ātmānaṃ paśyet tad abhimantrayeta -- mayi teja indriyaṃ yaśo draviṇaṃ sukṛtam iti |
śrīr ha vā eṣā strīṇāṃ yan malodvāsāḥ |
tasmān malodvāsasaṃ yaśasvinīm abhikramyopamantrayeta || BrhUp_6,4.6 ||
children.translated_text: And if he should see himself [reflected] in water, he should recite this <s>mantra</s> over it: 'May brilliance (<s>tejas</s>), virility (<s>indriya</s>), fame (<s>yaśas</s>), wealth (<s>draviṇa</s>), and meritorious deeds (<s>sukṛta</s>) [abide] in me.' She is indeed the glory of women — one whose soiled garments have been removed. Therefore, having approached [his wife] when her soiled garments have been removed and she is [adorned and] glorious, he should invite her. (BṛUp 6.4.6)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.6 atha yadi kadācidudaka ātmānamātmacchāyāṃ paśyettatrāpyatrimantrayetānena mantreṇa-mayi teja iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.6:] And if at some time he should see himself — his own reflection — in water, there too he should recite this <s>mantra</s>: 'May brilliance [abide] in me' and so forth.

children.text: śrīrha vā eṣā patnā srīṇāṃ madhye yadyasmānmalodvāsā udgatamalavadvāsāstasmāttāṃ malodvāsasaṃ yaśasvinīṃ śrīmatīmabhikramyābhigatyopamantrayetedamadyā'vābhyāṃ kāryaṃ yatputrotpādanamiti trirātrānta āplutām //6//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] She — the wife — is indeed the glory among women — when she has removed her soiled garments, i.e., when the garments stained with menstrual discharge have been removed. Therefore, having approached this woman who has removed her soiled garments — who is glorious, beautiful — having come to her, he should invite her [saying]: 'Today this act is to be done by us two — namely, the begetting of offspring' — [she should be invited] at the end of the three nights [of the menstrual period], having bathed. // 6.4.6 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.7
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.7]

children.text:
sā ced asmai na dadyāt kāmam enām avakriṇīyāt |
sā ced asmai naiva dadyāt kāmam enāṃ yaṣṭyā vā pāṇinā vopahatyātikrāmet |
indriyena te yaśasā yaśa ādada iti |
ayaśā eva bhavati || BrhUp_6,4.7 ||
children.translated_text: If she does not consent to him, he should buy her [consent with gifts]. If she still does not consent, he should strike her with a stick or with his hand and overpower her, [saying:] 'By my virility and fame, I take away your fame.' She indeed becomes without fame. (BṛUp 6.4.7)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.7 sā cedasmai na dadyānmaithunaṃ kartuṃ yatputrotpādanamiti trirātrānta jñāpayet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.7:] If she does not consent to him — does not agree to the act of union — [he should] inform her at the end of the three nights that 'this is for the purpose of begetting offspring.'

children.text: tathāpi sā naiva dadyātkāmamenāṃ yaṣṭyā vā pāṇinā vopahatyātikrāmenmaithunāya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Even so, if she still does not consent, he should strike her with a stick or with his hand and overpower her for the purpose of union.

children.text: śāpsyāmi tvāṃ durbhagāṃ kariṣyāmīti prakhyāpya tāmanena mantreṇopagacchedindriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādada iti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having declared 'I shall curse you, I shall make you unfortunate,' he should approach her with this <s>mantra</s>: 'By my virility and fame, I take away your fame.'

children.text: sā tasmāttadabhiśāpādvandhyā durbhageti khyātāyaśā eva bhavati //7//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] By that curse, she becomes barren, known as unfortunate — she indeed becomes without fame. // 6.4.7 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.8
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.8]

children.text:
sā ced asmai dadyād indriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādadhāmīti |
yaśasvināv eva bhavataḥ || BrhUp_6,4.8 ||
children.translated_text: If she consents to him, [he should say:] 'By my virility and fame, I bestow fame upon you.' Then both of them indeed become famous. (BṛUp 6.4.8)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.8 sā cedasmai dadyādanuguṇaiva syādbhartustadānena mantreṇopagacchendriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādadhāmīti tadā yaśasvināvevobhāvapi bhavataḥ //8//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.8:] If she consents to him — if she is agreeable to the husband — then he should approach her with this <s>mantra</s>: 'By my virility and fame, I bestow fame upon you.' Then both of them indeed become famous. // 6.4.8 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.9
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.9]

children.text:
sa yām icchet -- kāmayeta meti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyopastham asyā abhimṛśya japet --
aṅgād aṅgāt saṃbhavasi hṛdayād adhijāyase |
sa tvam aṅgakaṣāyo 'si digdhaviddhām iva mādayemām amūṃ mayīti || BrhUp_6,4.9 ||
children.translated_text: The woman whom he desires — '[Let her] desire me' — having inserted his member into her, joining mouth to mouth, and touching her genital organ, he should recite: 'You are born from every limb, you spring from the heart. You are the essence of the limbs. Intoxicate this woman — her, [named] so-and-so — with me, as if struck by a poisoned arrow.' (BṛUp 6.4.9)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.9 sa yāṃ svabhāryāmicchediyaṃ māṃ kāmayeteti tasyāmarthaṃ prajananendriyaṃ niṣṭhāya nikṣipya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyopasthamasyā abhimṛśya japedimaṃ mantramaṅgādaṅgāditi //9//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.9:] The woman whom — his own wife — he desires [thinking] 'May she desire me' — having inserted his member, his organ of procreation, into her; joining mouth to mouth; and touching her genital organ — he should recite this <s>mantra</s>: 'You are born from every limb' and so forth. // 6.4.9 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.10
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.10]

children.text:
atha yām icchen na garbhaṃ dadhīteti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyābhiprāṇyāpānyāt |
indriyeṇa te retasā reta ādada iti |
aretā eva bhavati || BrhUp_6,4.10 ||
children.translated_text: And the woman whom he desires [thinking] 'May she not conceive' — having inserted his member into her, joining mouth to mouth, he should first breathe in and then breathe out, [saying:] 'By my virility and semen, I take back the semen from you.' She indeed becomes without seed. (BṛUp 6.4.10)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.10 atha yāmicchenna garbhaṃ dadhīta na dhārayedgarbhiṇī mā bhūditi tasyāmarthamiti pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.10:] And the woman whom he desires [thinking] 'May she not conceive, may she not bear a child, may she not become pregnant' — into her, his member — as before.

children.text: abhiprāṇyābhiprāṇanaṃ prathamaṃ kṛtvā paścādapānyādindriyeṇa te retasā reta ādada ityanena mantreṇāretā eva bhavati na garbhiṇī bhavatītyarthaḥ //10//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having first breathed in (<s>abhiprāṇya</s>) and then breathed out (<s>apānya</s>) — with this <s>mantra</s>: 'By my virility and semen, I take back the semen from you' — she indeed becomes without seed, meaning: she does not become pregnant — this is the meaning. // 6.4.10 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.11
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.11]

children.text:
atha yām icched dadhīteti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyāpānyābhiprāṇyāt |
indriyeṇa te retasā reta ādadhāmīti |
garbhiṇy eva bhavati || BrhUp_6,4.11 ||
children.translated_text: And the woman whom he desires [thinking] 'May she conceive' — having inserted his member into her, joining mouth to mouth, he should first breathe out and then breathe in, [saying:] 'By my virility and semen, I bestow semen in you.' She indeed becomes pregnant. (BṛUp 6.4.11)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.11 atha yāmiccheddadhīta garbhamiti tasyāmarthamityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.11:] And the woman whom he desires [thinking] 'May she conceive' — into her, his member — and so forth, as before.

children.text: pūrvaviparyayeṇāpānyābhiprāṇyādindriyeṇa te retasā reta ādadhāmīti garbhiṇyeva bhavati //11//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] In the reverse order of the previous [procedure] — first breathing out and then breathing in — [reciting] 'By my virility and semen, I bestow semen in you' — she indeed becomes pregnant. // 6.4.11 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.12
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.12]

children.text:
atha yasya jāyāyai jāraḥ syāt taṃ ced dviṣyād āmapātre 'gnim upasamādhāya pratilomaṃ śarabarhiḥ stīrtvā tasminn etāḥ śarabhṛṣṭīḥ pratilomāḥ sarpiṣāktā juhuyāt |
mama samiddhe 'hauṣīḥ |
prāṇāpānau ta ādade 'sāv iti |
mama samiddhe 'hauṣīḥ |
putrapaśūṃs ta ādade 'sāv iti |
mama samiddhe 'hauṣīḥ |
iṣṭāsukṛte ta ādade 'sāv iti |
mama samiddhe 'hauṣīḥ |
aśāparākāśau ta ādade 'sāv iti |
sa vā eṣa nirindriyo visukṛto 'smāl lokād praiti yam evaṃvid brāhmaṇaḥ śapati |
tasmād evaṃvitśrotriyasya dāreṇa nopahāsam icchet |
uta hy evaṃvit paro bhavati || BrhUp_6,4.12 ||
children.translated_text: And if someone's wife has a lover, and he wishes to harm that [lover], he should set up a fire in an unbaked vessel, spread the arrow-grass in reverse order, and offer in that [fire] these arrow-tips in reverse order, smeared with clarified butter, [reciting]: 'You have offered in my fire! I take away your <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s>, [named] so-and-so.' 'You have offered in my fire! I take away your sons and cattle, [named] so-and-so.' 'You have offered in my fire! I take away your meritorious deeds, [named] so-and-so.' 'You have offered in my fire! I take away your hopes and expectations, [named] so-and-so.' He indeed departs from this world devoid of virility and devoid of merit — he whom a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus curses. Therefore, one should not jest with the wife of a learned <s>śrotriya</s> (Vedic scholar). For one who knows thus is indeed powerful. (BṛUp 6.4.12)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.12 atha punaryasya jāyāyai jāra upapatiḥ syāttaṃ ceddviṣyādabhicariṣyāmyenamiti manyeta tasyedaṃ karma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.12:] And if someone's wife has a lover — a paramour — and if he dislikes that [lover] and thinks 'I shall perform a rite of imprecation (<s>abhicāra</s>) against him' — for such a one, this is the ritual.

children.text: āmapātre 'gnimupasamādhāya sarvaṃ pratilomaṃ kuryāttasminnagnāvetāḥ śarabhṛṣṭīḥ śareṣīkāḥ pratilomāḥ sarpiṣāktā ghṛtābhyaktā juhuyānmama samiddhe 'hauṣīrityādyā āhutīrante sarvāsāmasāviti nāmagrahaṇaṃ pratyekam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having set up fire in an unbaked vessel, he should do everything in reverse order. In that fire, he should offer these arrow-tips — the reed-stalks of arrows — in reverse order, smeared with clarified butter, with the oblations [beginning with] 'You have offered in my fire' — and at the end of each oblation, the name [of the lover] should be taken individually.

children.text: sa eṣa evaṃvidyā brāhmaṇaḥ śapati sa visukṛto vigatapuṇyakarmā praiti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He — the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows this knowledge — whom he curses, that one departs devoid of meritorious <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tasmādevaṃvicchrotrisya dāreṇa nopahāsamicchennarmāpi na kuryātkimutādhopahāsaṃ hi yasmādevaṃvidapi tāvatparo bhavati śatrurbhavatītyarthaḥ //12//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, one should not jest with the wife of a learned <s>śrotriya</s> — one should not engage in even playful banter, let alone improper conduct. For one who knows thus is indeed powerful — becomes an adversary, an enemy — this is the meaning. // 6.4.12 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.13
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.13]

children.text:
atha yasya jāyām ārtavaṃ vindet tryahaṃ kaṃse na pibet |
ahatavāsāḥ |
naināṃ vṛṣalo na vṛṣaly apahanyāt |
trirātrānta āplutya vrīhīn avaghātayet || BrhUp_6,4.13 ||
children.translated_text: And when someone's wife is in her menstrual period, she should not drink from a bronze vessel for three days. She should wear fresh garments. No <s>śūdra</s> man or <s>śūdra</s> woman should touch her. At the end of the three nights, having bathed, she should be made to pound rice. (BṛUp 6.4.13)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.13 atha yasya jāyāmārtavaṃ vindedṛtubhāvaṃ prāpnuyādityevamādigranthaḥ śrīrha vā eṣā srīṇāmityataḥ pūrvaṃ draṣṭavyaḥ sāmarthyāt /
tryahaṃ kaṃsena pibedahatavāsāśca syāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For three days, she should drink from a bronze vessel (<s>kaṃsa</s>), and should wear fresh garments.

children.text: naināṃ snātāmasnātāṃ ca vṛṣalo vṛṣalī vā nopahanyānnopaspṛśet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] No <s>śūdra</s> man or <s>śūdra</s> woman should touch her — neither the bathed nor the unbathed [woman should be touched].

children.text: trirātrānte trirātravratasamāptāvāplutya snātvāhatavāsā syāditi vyavahitena saṃbandhaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] At the end of the three nights — at the completion of the three-night observance — having bathed, she should wear fresh garments — the connection is with the separated [phrase].

children.text: tāmāplutāṃ vrīhīnavaghātayedvrīhyavaghātāya tāmeva viniyuñjyāt //13//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Her, having bathed, he should employ for the pounding of rice — he should engage her for the purpose of pounding rice. // 6.4.13 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.13:] And when someone's wife has her menstrual period — attains the state of <s>ṛtu</s> (season/period) — and so forth. This passage, beginning [here], should be read as coming before [the passage] 'She is indeed the glory of women' — because of the contextual fitness.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.14
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.14]

children.text:
sa ya icchet -- putro me śuklo jāyeta vedam anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti kṣīraudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām |
īśvarau janayitavai || BrhUp_6,4.14 ||
children.translated_text: If one desires — 'May a fair (<s>śukla</s>) son be born to me, may he recite one <s>Veda</s>, may he live a full lifespan' — having cooked rice boiled in milk with clarified butter, they should eat. They are capable of begetting [such a son]. (BṛUp 6.4.14)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.14 sa ya icchetputro me śuklo varṇato jāyeta vedamekamanubruvīta sarvamāyuriyādvarṣaśataṃ kṣīraudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantamaśnīyātāmāśvarau samarthau janayitavai janayitum //14//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.14:] If one desires — 'May a son fair in complexion be born to me, may he recite one <s>Veda</s>, may he live the full lifespan of a hundred years' — having cooked rice boiled in milk, with clarified butter, they should eat. They are capable — competent — of begetting [such a son]. // 6.4.14 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.15
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.15]

children.text:
atha ya icchet -- putro me kapilaḥ piṅgalo jāyeta dvau vedāv anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti dadhyodanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām |
īśvarau janayitavai || BrhUp_6,4.15 ||
children.translated_text: And if one desires — 'May a tawny (<s>kapila</s>) or reddish-brown (<s>piṅgala</s>) son be born to me, may he recite two <s>Vedas</s>, may he live a full lifespan' — having cooked rice with curd and clarified butter, they should eat. They are capable of begetting [such a son]. (BṛUp 6.4.15)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.15 dadhyodanaṃ dadhnā caruṃ pācayitvā dvidevaṃ cedicchati putraṃ tadaivamaśananiyamaḥ //15//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.15:] Rice cooked with curd — a <s>caru</s> (oblation) prepared with curd — if one desires a son of that description, then this is the dietary rule. // 6.4.15 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.16
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.16]

children.text:
atha ya icchet -- putro me śyāmo lohitākṣo jāyeta trīn vedān anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti udaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām |
īśvarau janayitavai || BrhUp_6,4.16 ||
children.translated_text: And if one desires — 'May a dark (<s>śyāma</s>), red-eyed son be born to me, may he recite three <s>Vedas</s>, may he live a full lifespan' — having cooked rice with water and clarified butter, they should eat. They are capable of begetting [such a son]. (BṛUp 6.4.16)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.16 kevalameva svābhāvikamodanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.16:] [One should eat] naturally plain rice boiled in water.

children.text: udagrahaṇamanyaprasaṅganivṛttyatham //16//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The specification of 'water' is for the purpose of excluding other [liquids such as milk or curd]. // 6.4.16 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.17
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.17]

children.text:
atha ya icched -- duhitā me paṇḍitā jāyeta sarvam āyur iyād iti tilaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām |
īśvarau janayitavai || BrhUp_6,4.17 ||
children.translated_text: And if one desires — 'May a learned daughter be born to me, may she live a full lifespan' — having cooked rice with sesame and clarified butter, they should eat. They are capable of begetting [such a daughter]. (BṛUp 6.4.17)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.17 duhituḥ pāṇḍityaṃ gṛhatantraviṣayameva vede 'nadhikārāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.17:] The learning of the daughter pertains to household management alone — because of the absence of qualification for Vedic [study].

children.text: tilaudanaṃ kṛtaram //17//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Rice cooked with sesame — the prepared [dish]. // 6.4.17 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.18
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.18]

children.text:
atha ya icchet -- putro me paṇḍito vigītaḥ samitiṃgamaḥ śuśrūṣitāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣitā jāyeta sarvān vedān anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti māṃsaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām |
īśvarau janayitavāi |
aukṣeṇa vārṣabheṇa vā || BrhUp_6,4.18 ||
children.translated_text: And if one desires — 'May a learned son be born to me, celebrated, a frequenter of assemblies, a speaker of pleasing words, may he recite all the <s>Vedas</s>, may he live a full lifespan' — having cooked rice with meat and clarified butter, they should eat. They are capable of begetting [such a son] — [the meat should be] of a young bull or of a full-grown bull. (BṛUp 6.4.18)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,4.18 vividhaṃ gīto vigītaḥ prakhyāta ityarthaḥ /
samitiṅgamaḥ sabhāṃ gacchatīti pragalbha ityarthaḥ /
pāṇḍityasya pṛthaggrahaṇāt /
śuśrūṣitāṃ śrotumiṣṭāṃ ramaṇīyāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣitā saṃskṛtāyā arthavatyā vāco bhāṣitetyarthaḥ /
māṃsamiśramodanaṃ māṃsaudanam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Rice mixed with meat is <s>māṃsaudana</s> (meat-rice).

children.text: tanmāṃsaniyamārthamāha-aukṣeṃ vā māṃsena /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] For the purpose of specifying the meat, [the text] says: with the meat of a young bull (<s>ukṣa</s>).

children.text: ukṣā secanasamarthaḥ puṅgavastadīyaṃ māṃsam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] An <s>ukṣa</s> is a bull capable of insemination — its meat [is referred to].

children.text: ṛṣabhastato 'pyadhikavayāstadīyamārṣabhaṃ māṃsam //17//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] An <s>ṛṣabha</s> (full-grown bull) is one of even greater age — its meat is <s>ārṣabha</s>. // 6.4.18 //

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.18:] '<s>Vigīta</s>' — variously celebrated, meaning renowned. '<s>Samitiṅgama</s>' — one who goes to assemblies, meaning bold and eloquent — this is the meaning. Because 'learned' is mentioned separately. 'A speaker of pleasing words' — words that are desired to be heard, delightful — meaning: a speaker of well-formed, meaningful speech.

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.19
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.19]

children.text:
athābhiprātar eva sthālīpākāvṛtājyaṃ ceṣṭitvā sthālīpākasyopaghātaṃ juhoty agnaye svāhānumataye svāhā devāya savitre satyaprasavāya svāheti |
hutvoddhṛtya prāśnāti |
prāśyetarasyāḥ prayacchati |
prakṣālya pāṇī udapātraṃ pūrayitvā tenaināṃ trir abhyukṣati --
uttiṣṭhāto viśvāvaso 'nyām iccha prapūrvyām |
saṃ jāyāṃ patyā saheti || BrhUp_6,4.19 ||
children.translated_text: Then, toward morning, having performed the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering) ritual and the clarified butter [offering], he makes offerings from the <s>sthālīpāka</s>, [saying:] 'To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Anumati</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, the impeller of truth, <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered, he takes out [a portion] and eats. Having eaten, he gives [a portion] to the other [his wife]. Having washed his hands and filled a water-vessel, he sprinkles her three times with it [reciting:] 'Rise up, O <s>Viśvāvasu</s>! Seek another young woman. [Leave] the wife together with her husband.' (BṛUp 6.4.19)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.19 athāmiprātareva kāle 'vaghātanirvṛttāṃstaṇḍulānādāya sthālīpākāvṛtā sthālīpākavidhinā'jyaṃ ceṣṭitvā'jyasaṃskāraṃ kṛtvā caruṃ śrapayitvā sthālīpākasyā'hutīrjuhotyupaghātamupahatyopahatyāgnaye svāhetyādyāḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.19:] Then, toward morning — at the appropriate time — having taken the rice grains produced by pounding, he performs the <s>sthālīpāka</s> ritual: having prepared the clarified butter according to the <s>sthālīpāka</s> procedure — having done the <s>ājyasaṃskāra</s> (purification of the butter) — having cooked the <s>caru</s> (oblation), he makes the offerings of the <s>sthālīpāka</s>, offering repeatedly — 'To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' and so forth.

children.text: gārhyaḥ sarvo vidhirdraṣṭavyo 'tra hutvoddhṛtya caruśeṣaṃ prāśnāti svayaṃ prāśyetarasyāḥ patnyai prayacchatyucchiṣṭam /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] The entire domestic (<s>gṛhya</s>) ritual procedure should be understood here. Having offered and taken out the remainder of the <s>caru</s>, he eats it himself. Having eaten, he gives the leftovers to the other — to [his] wife.

children.text: prakṣālya pāṇī ācamyodapātraṃ pūrayitvā tenodakenaināṃ trirabhyukṣatyena mantreṇottiṣṭhāta iti sakṛnmantroccāraṇam //19//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Having washed his hands, having sipped water (<s>ācamya</s>), having filled a water-vessel, he sprinkles her three times with that water, [reciting] this <s>mantra</s>: 'Rise up' — the <s>mantra</s> is recited once [for all three sprinklings]. // 6.4.19 //

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.20

athainām abhipadyate -- amo 'ham asmi sā tvam |
sā tvam asy amo 'ham |
sāmāham asmi ṛk tvam |
dyaur aham pṛthivī tvam |
tāv ehi saṃrabhāvahai saha reto dadhāvahai |
puṃse putrāya vittaya iti || BrhUp_6,4.20 ||
children.translated_text: Then he approaches her [reciting:] 'I am <s>Ama</s> (life-force), you are <s>Sā</s> (she). You are <s>Sā</s>, I am <s>Ama</s>. I am the <s>Sāman</s>, you are the <s>Ṛk</s>. I am heaven, you are earth. Come, let us unite together, let us deposit the semen together — for the sake of a son, of a male child, for the sake of prosperity.' (BṛUp 6.4.20)
[Start of BṛUp 6.4.20]

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.20 athaināmabhimantrya kṣīraudanādi yathāpatyakāmaṃ bhuktveti kramo draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.20:] Then, having consecrated her with <s>mantras</s>, having eaten rice cooked in milk and the like, according to the desire for offspring — this is the sequence to be observed.

children.text: saṃveśanakāle 'mo 'hamasmītyādimantreṇābhipadyate //20//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] At the time of lying together, he approaches [her] with the <s>mantra</s> beginning with 'I am <s>Ama</s> (that one)' and so forth. (6.4.20)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.21
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.21]

children.text:
athāsyā ūrū vihāpayati -- vijihīthāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī iti |
tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāya trir enām anulomām anumārṣṭi --
viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu |
ā siñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te |
garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi pṛthuṣṭuke |
garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāv ādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajau || BrhUp_6,4.21 ||
children.translated_text: Then he spreads apart her thighs [with the words:] 'Spread apart, O heaven and earth!' Having completed the act in her, joining mouth to mouth, he strokes her three times from head downward [with the <s>mantra</s>:] 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb; may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fashion the forms; may <s>Prajāpati</s> pour forth; may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo in you. Place the embryo, O <s>Sinīvālī</s>; place the embryo, O you of broad braids. May the two <s>Aśvins</s>, the gods garlanded with lotuses, place the embryo in you.' (BṛUp 6.4.21)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.21 athāsyā ūrū vihāpayati vijihīthāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī ityanena /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.21:] Then he spreads apart her thighs with [the <s>mantra</s>:] 'Spread apart, O heaven and earth.'

children.text: tasyāmarthamityādi pūrvavat /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Having completed the act in her' — and so forth, as before.

children.text: trirenāṃ śiraḥ prabhṛtyanulomāmanumārṣṭi viṣṇuryonimityādi pratimantram //21//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] He strokes her three times from the head downward, [reciting] the <s>mantra</s> 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb' — and so forth, for each [successive line of the] <s>mantra</s>. (6.4.21)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.22
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.22]

children.text:
hiraṇmayī araṇī yābhyāṃ nirmanthatām aśvinau |
taṃ te garbhaṃ havāmahe daśame māsi sūtaye |
yathāgnigarbhā pṛthivī yathā dyaur aindreṇa garbhiṇī |
vāyur diśāṃ yathā garbha evaṃ garbhaṃ dadhāmi te 'sāv iti || BrhUp_6,4.22 ||
children.translated_text: 'Golden are the two fire-sticks from which the <s>Aśvins</s> churned [fire]. That embryo of yours we invoke for delivery in the tenth month. Just as the earth is pregnant with fire, just as the heaven is pregnant with <s>Indra's</s> [thunderbolt], just as <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is the embryo of the directions — even so I place an embryo in you, O [name]!' (BṛUp 6.4.22)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.22 ante nāma gṛhṇātyasāviti tasyāḥ //22//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.22:] At the end [of the <s>mantra</s>], he utters the name — 'O [name]!' — [meaning] her name. (6.4.22)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.23
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.23]

children.text:
soṣyantīm adbhir abhyukṣati --
yathā vāyuḥ puṣkariṇīṃ samiṅgayati sarvataḥ |
evā te garbha ejatu sahāvaitu jarāyuṇā |
indrasyāyaṃ vrajaḥ kṛtaḥ sārgalaḥ sapariśrayaḥ |
tam indra nirjahi garbheṇa sāvarāṃ saheti || BrhUp_6,4.23 ||
children.translated_text: He sprinkles with water the one about to give birth [with the <s>mantra</s>:] 'Just as the wind agitates a lotus pond from all sides, even so may your embryo stir and come forth together with the afterbirth (<s>jarāyu</s>). This enclosure of <s>Indra</s> has been made with a bolt and a fence. O <s>Indra</s>, come forth with it — with the embryo and the afterbirth!' (BṛUp 6.4.23)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.23 soṣyantīmadbhirabhyukṣati prasavakāle sukhaprasavanārthamanena mantreṇa /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.23:] He sprinkles with water the one about to give birth — at the time of delivery, for the purpose of easy delivery, with this <s>mantra</s>.

children.text: yathā vāyuḥ puṣkariṇīṃ samiṅgayati sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Just as the wind agitates a lotus pond from all sides —

children.text: evā te garbha ejatviti //23//
children.translated_text: even so may your embryo stir.' (6.4.23)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.24

jāte 'gnim upasamādhāyāṅka ādhāya kaṃse pṛṣadājyaṃ saṃnīya pṛṣadājyasyopaghātaṃ juhoti --
asminsahasraṃ puṣyāsam edhamānaḥ sve gṛhe |
asyopasandyāṃ mā chaitsīt prajayā ca paśubhiś ca svāhā |
mayi prāṇāṃs tvayi manasā juhomi svāhā |
yat karmaṇātyarīricam yad vā nyūnam ihākaram |
agniṣṭat sviṣṭakṛd vidvān sviṣṭaṃ suhutaṃ karotu naḥ svāheti || BrhUp_6,4.24 ||
children.translated_text: When [the child] is born, having prepared the fire and placed [the child] on his lap, having mixed <s>pṛṣadājya</s> (curd mixed with ghee) in a bronze vessel, he offers an oblation of <s>pṛṣadājya</s> [with the <s>mantras</s>:] 'In this [child], may I prosper a thousandfold, thriving in my own home. May [fortune] not be cut off in his lineage — in offspring and in cattle. <s>Svāhā</s>! The <s>prāṇas</s> that are in me — those I mentally offer in you. <s>Svāhā</s>! Whatever I have done too much in ritual action, or whatever too little I have done here — may <s>Agni</s>, the knower, the one who makes the offering well-offered, make [the ritual] well-offered and well-sacrificed for us. <s>Svāhā</s>!' (BṛUp 6.4.24)
[Start of BṛUp 6.4.24]

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.24atha jātakarma /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.24:] Now, the birth ceremony (<s>jātakarma</s>).

children.text: jāte 'gnimupasamādhāyāṅka ādhāya putraṃ kaṃse pṛṣadājyaṃ saṃmīya saṃyojya dadhi ghṛte pṛṣadājyasyopaghātaṃ juhotyasminsahasramityādyāvāpasthāne //24//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] When [the child] is born, having prepared the fire and placed the son on his lap, having mixed — that is, combined — curd and ghee (<s>pṛṣadājya</s>) in a bronze vessel, he offers an oblation of <s>pṛṣadājya</s> [with the <s>mantra</s>:] 'In this [child], may I prosper a thousandfold' — and so forth, up to the concluding formula. (6.4.24)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.25
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.25]

children.text:
athāsya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇam abhinidhāya vāg vāg iti triḥ |
atha dadhi madhu ghṛtaṃ saṃnīyānantarhitena jātarūpeṇa prāśayati |
bhūs te dadhāmi bhuvas te dadhāmi svas te dadhāmi bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ sarvaṃ tvayi dadhāmīti || BrhUp_6,4.25 ||
children.translated_text: Then, placing [his mouth] near [the child's] right ear, [he says] '<s>Vāk</s>, <s>Vāk</s>!' (Speech! Speech!) three times. Then, having mixed curd, honey, and ghee, he feeds [the child] with an uninterrupted [piece of] gold [spoon, saying:] 'I place <s>Bhūḥ</s> (earth) in you. I place <s>Bhuvaḥ</s> (atmosphere) in you. I place <s>Svaḥ</s> (heaven) in you. <s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s> — I place everything in you.' (BṛUp 6.4.25)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.25 athāsya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamabhinidhāya svaṃ mukhaṃ vāgvāgiti trirjapet /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.25:] Then, placing [his mouth] near the child's right ear, with his own mouth [he utters] '<s>Vāk</s>, <s>Vāk</s>!' — he should recite [this] three times.

children.text: atha dadhi madhu ghṛtaṃ saṃnīyānantarhitenāvyavahitena jātarūpeṇa hiraṇyena prāśayatyetairmantraiḥ pratyekam //25//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Then, having mixed curd, honey, and ghee — with an uninterrupted, unbroken [piece of] gold (<s>jātarūpa</s>) [used as a spoon] — he feeds [the child] with these <s>mantras</s>, one for each [substance]. (6.4.25)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.26
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.26]

children.text:
athāsya nāma karoti vedo 'sīti |
tad asyaitad guhyam eva nāma bhavati || BrhUp_6,4.26 ||
children.translated_text: Then he gives [the child] a name: 'You are the <s>Veda</s>.' This becomes his secret name. (BṛUp 6.4.26)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.26 athāsya nāmadheyaṃ karoti vedo 'sīti /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.26:] Then he performs the naming ceremony (<s>nāmadheya</s>): 'You are the <s>Veda</s>.'

children.text: tadasya tadguhyaṃ nāma bhavati veda iti //26//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] This becomes his secret name — '<s>Veda</s>.' (6.4.26)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.27
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.27]

children.text:
athainaṃ mātre pradāya stanaṃ prayacchati -- yas te stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr yo ratnadhā vasuvid yaḥ sudatraḥ |
yena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi sarasvati tam iha dhātave kar iti || BrhUp_6,4.27 ||
children.translated_text: Then he presents [the child] to the mother and offers the breast [with the <s>mantra</s>:] 'That breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which is delightful, which is the giver of treasures, the finder of wealth, the bountiful giver — O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, bring that [breast] here for nourishment.' (BṛUp 6.4.27)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.27 athainaṃ mātre pradāya svāṅkasthaṃ stanaṃ prayacchati yaste stana ityādimantreṇa //27//
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.27:] Then, presenting [the child] to the mother, [he] places [the child] on her lap and offers the breast with the <s>mantra</s> 'That breast of yours' and so forth. (6.4.27)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,4.28
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.4.28]

children.text:
athāsya mātaram abhimantrayate -- ilāsi maitrāvaruṇī vīre vīram ajījanat |
sā tvaṃ vīravatī bhava yāsmān vīravato 'karad iti |
taṃ vā etam āhuḥ -- atipitā batābhūḥ |
atipitāmaho batābhūḥ |
paramāṃ bata kāṣṭhāṃ prāpa śriyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena |
ya evaṃvido brāhmaṇasya putro jāyata iti || BrhUp_6,4.28 ||
children.translated_text: Then he addresses [the child's] mother [with the <s>mantra</s>:] 'You are <s>Ilā</s>, of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. A heroine, you have given birth to a hero. You who have made us parents of heroes — be yourself endowed with heroes!' Regarding this [son], they say: 'You have surpassed your father! You have surpassed your grandfather! He has truly reached the ultimate limit of glory, renown, and <s>brahmavarcas</s> (Vedic splendor) — he who is born as the son of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus!' (BṛUp 6.4.28)

children.text: BrhUpBh_6,4.28 athāsya mātaramabhimantrayata ilāsītyanena /
children.translated_text: [Commentary on BṛUp 6.4.28:] Then he addresses the [child's] mother with [the <s>mantra</s>:] 'You are <s>Ilā</s>' and so forth.

children.text: taṃ vā etamāhurityanena vidhinā jātaḥ putraḥ pitaraṃ pitāmahaṃ cātiśeta iti śriyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena paramāṃ niṣṭhāṃ prāpadityevaṃ stutyo bhavatītyarthaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Regarding this [son], they say' — [meaning:] a son born through this rite surpasses his father and grandfather — with glory, renown, and <s>brahmavarcas</s>, he reaches the ultimate culmination — thus he becomes worthy of praise — this is the meaning.

children.text: yasya caivaṃvido brāhmaṇasya putro jāyate sa caivaṃ bhavatītyadhyāhāryam //28//
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And of such a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who knows thus, when a son is born, he too becomes such — this is to be supplied. (6.4.28)

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya caturthaṃ brāhmaṇam //4//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the sixth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. (6.4)

children.text: START BrhUp 6,5.1-4
children.translated_text: [Start of BṛUp 6.5.1-4]

children.text:
atha vaṃśaḥ |
pautimāṣīputraḥ kātyāyanīputrāt |
kātyāyanīputro gautamīputrāt |
gautamīputro bhāradvājīputrāt |
bhāradvājīputraḥ pārāśarīputrāt |
pārāśarīputra aupasvastīputrāt |
aupasvastīputraḥ pārāśarīputrāt |
pārāśarīputraḥ kātyāyanīputrāt |
kātyāyanīputraḥ kauśikīputrāt |
kauśikīputra ālambīputrāc ca vaiyāghrapadīputrāc ca |
vaiyāghrapadīputrah kāṇvīputrāc ca kāpīputrāc ca |
kāpīputraḥ || BrhUp_6,5.1 ||
children.translated_text: Now the lineage (<s>vaṃśa</s>): <s>Pautimāṣīputra</s> [received this teaching] from <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s>; <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s> from <s>Gautamīputra</s>; <s>Gautamīputra</s> from <s>Bhāradvājīputra</s>; <s>Bhāradvājīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>; <s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Aupasvastīputra</s>; <s>Aupasvastīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>; <s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s>; <s>Kātyāyanīputra</s> from <s>Kauśikīputra</s>; <s>Kauśikīputra</s> from both <s>Ālambīputra</s> and <s>Vaiyāghrapadīputra</s>; <s>Vaiyāghrapadīputra</s> from both <s>Kāṇvīputra</s> and <s>Kāpīputra</s>; <s>Kāpīputra</s> — (BṛUp 6.5.1)

children.text:
ātreyīputrāt |
ātreyīputro gautamīputrāt |
gautamīputro bhāradvājīputrāt |
bhāradvājīputraḥ pārāśarīputrāt |
pārāśarīputro vātsīputrāt |
vātsīputraḥ pārāśarīputrāt |
pārāśarīputro vārkārunīputrāt |
vārkāruṇīputro vārkāruṇīputrāt |
vārkāruṇīputra ārtabhāgīputrāt |
ārtabhāgīputraḥ śauṅgīputrāt |
śauṅgīputraḥ sānkṛtīputrāt |
sāṅṛtīputra ālambāyanīputrāt |
ālambāyanīputra ālambīputrāt |
ālambīputro jāyantīputrāt |
jāyantīputro māṇḍūkāyanīputrāt |
māṇḍūkāyanīputro māṇḍūkīputrāt |
māṇḍūkīputraḥ śāṇḍilīputrāt |
śāṇḍilīputro rāthītarīputrāt |
rāthītarīputro bhālukīputrāt |
bhālukīputraḥ krauñcikīputrābhyām |
krauñcikīputrau vaidabhṛtīputrāt |
vaidabhṛtīputraḥ kārśakeyīputrāt |
kārśakeyīputraḥ prācīnayogīputrāt |
prācīnayogīputraḥ sāñjīvīputrāt |
sāñjīvīputraḥ prāśnīputrād āsurivāsinaḥ |
prāśnīputra āsurāyaṇāt |
āsurāyaṇa āsureḥ |
āsuriḥ| BrhUp_6,5.2 ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Ātreyīputra</s>; <s>Ātreyīputra</s> from <s>Gautamīputra</s>; <s>Gautamīputra</s> from <s>Bhāradvājīputra</s>; <s>Bhāradvājīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>; <s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Vātsīputra</s>; <s>Vātsīputra</s> from <s>Pārāśarīputra</s>; <s>Pārāśarīputra</s> from <s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s>; <s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s> from <s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s>; <s>Vārkāruṇīputra</s> from <s>Ārtabhāgīputra</s>; <s>Ārtabhāgīputra</s> from <s>Śauṅgīputra</s>; <s>Śauṅgīputra</s> from <s>Sāṅkṛtīputra</s>; <s>Sāṅkṛtīputra</s> from <s>Ālambāyanīputra</s>; <s>Ālambāyanīputra</s> from <s>Ālambīputra</s>; <s>Ālambīputra</s> from <s>Jāyantīputra</s>; <s>Jāyantīputra</s> from <s>Māṇḍūkāyanīputra</s>; <s>Māṇḍūkāyanīputra</s> from <s>Māṇḍūkīputra</s>; <s>Māṇḍūkīputra</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilīputra</s>; <s>Śāṇḍilīputra</s> from <s>Rāthītarīputra</s>; <s>Rāthītarīputra</s> from <s>Bhālukīputra</s>; <s>Bhālukīputra</s> from the two <s>Krauñcikīputras</s>; the two <s>Krauñcikīputras</s> from <s>Vaidabhṛtīputra</s>; <s>Vaidabhṛtīputra</s> from <s>Kārśakeyīputra</s>; <s>Kārśakeyīputra</s> from <s>Prācīnayogīputra</s>; <s>Prācīnayogīputra</s> from <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s>; <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s> from <s>Prāśnīputra</s> of the <s>Āsuri</s> school; <s>Prāśnīputra</s> from <s>Āsurāyaṇa</s>; <s>Āsurāyaṇa</s> from <s>Āsuri</s>; <s>Āsuri</s> — (BṛUp 6.5.2)

children.text:
yājñavalkyāt |
yājñavalkya uddālakāt |
uddālako 'ruṇāt |
aruṇa upaveśeḥ |
upaveśiḥ kuśreḥ |
kuśrir vājaśravasaḥ |
vājaśravā jīhvāvato bādhyogāt |
jīhvāvān bādhyogo 'sitād vārṣagaṇāt |
asito vārṣagaṇo haritāt kaśyapāt |
haritaḥ kaśyapaḥ śilpāt kaśyapāt |
śilpaḥ kaśyapaḥ kaśyapān naidhruveḥ |
kaśyapo naidhruvir vācaḥ |
vāg ambhiṇyāḥ |
ambhiṇy ādityāt |
ādityānīmāni śuklāni yajūṃṣi vājasaneyena yājñavalkyenākhyayante || BrhUp_6,5.3 ||
children.translated_text: from <s>Yājñavalkya</s>; <s>Yājñavalkya</s> from <s>Uddālaka</s>; <s>Uddālaka</s> from <s>Aruṇa</s>; <s>Aruṇa</s> from <s>Upaveśi</s>; <s>Upaveśi</s> from <s>Kuśri</s>; <s>Kuśri</s> from <s>Vājaśravas</s>; <s>Vājaśravas</s> from <s>Jihvāvat Bādhyoga</s>; <s>Jihvāvat Bādhyoga</s> from <s>Asita Vārṣagaṇa</s>; <s>Asita Vārṣagaṇa</s> from <s>Harita Kāśyapa</s>; <s>Harita Kāśyapa</s> from <s>Śilpa Kāśyapa</s>; <s>Śilpa Kāśyapa</s> from <s>Kāśyapa Naidhruvī</s>; <s>Kāśyapa Naidhruvī</s> from <s>Vāc</s> (Speech); <s>Vāc</s> from <s>Ambhinī</s>; <s>Ambhinī</s> from <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun). These white <s>Yajus</s> formulas are declared by <s>Yājñavalkya</s> of the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [school]. (BṛUp 6.5.3)

children.text:
samānam ā sāñjīvīputrāt |
sañjivīputro māṇḍūkāyaneḥ |
māṇḍūkāyanir māṇḍavyāt |
māṇḍavyaḥ kautsāt |
kautso māhittheḥ |
māhitthir vāmakakṣāyaṇāt |
vāmakakṣāyaṇaḥ śāṇḍilyāt |
śāṇḍilyo vātsyāt |
vātsyaḥ kuśreḥ |
kuśrir yajñavacasaḥ rājastambāyanāt |
yajñavacā rājastambāyanaḥ turāt kāvaṣeyāt |
turaḥ kāvaṣeyaḥ prajāpateḥ |
prajāpatir brahmaṇaḥ |
brahma svayaṃbhu |
brahmaṇe namaḥ || BrhUp_6,5.4 ||
children.translated_text: The same [lineage] up to <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s>. <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s> from <s>Māṇḍūkāyana</s>; <s>Māṇḍūkāyana</s> from <s>Māṇḍavya</s>; <s>Māṇḍavya</s> from <s>Kautsa</s>; <s>Kautsa</s> from <s>Māhitthi</s>; <s>Māhitthi</s> from <s>Vāmakakṣāyaṇa</s>; <s>Vāmakakṣāyaṇa</s> from <s>Śāṇḍilya</s>; <s>Śāṇḍilya</s> from <s>Vātsya</s>; <s>Vātsya</s> from <s>Kuśri</s>; <s>Kuśri</s> from <s>Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana</s>; <s>Yajñavacas Rājastambāyana</s> from <s>Tura Kāvaṣeya</s>; <s>Tura Kāvaṣeya</s> from <s>Prajāpati</s>; <s>Prajāpati</s> from <s>Brahman</s>. <s>Brahman</s> is self-born (<s>svayaṃbhu</s>). Salutation to <s>Brahman</s>! (BṛUp 6.5.4)

children.text:
BrhUpBh_6,5.1-4 athedānīṃ samastapravacanavaṃśaḥ /
srīprādhānyāt guṇavānputro bhavatīti prastutam /
ataḥ srīviśeṣaṇenaiva putraviśeṣaṇādācāryaparamparā kīrtyate /
tānīmāni śuklānītyavyāmiśrāṇi brāhmaṇena /
athavā yānīmāni yajūṃṣi tānī śuklāni śuddhānītyetat /
prajāpatimārabhya yāvatpautimāṣīputrastāvadadhomukho niyatācāryapūrvakramo vaṃśaḥ samānamāsāṃjīvīputrāt /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Beginning from <s>Prajāpati</s> down to <s>Pautimāṣīputra</s>, the lineage proceeds in descending order, with each teacher preceding [in a fixed succession]. The same [lineage applies] up to <s>Sāñjīvīputra</s>.

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ pravacanākhyasya /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Of the <s>Brahman</s> that is called 'teaching' (<s>pravacana</s>).

children.text: taccaitadbrahma prajāpatiprabandhaparamparayā'gatyāsmāsvanekadhāviprasṛtamanādyanantaṃ svayaṃbhu brahma nityaṃ tasmai brahmaṇe namaḥ /
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] And this <s>Brahman</s>, having come through the continuous succession beginning from <s>Prajāpati</s> and having spread among us in many branches — the beginningless and endless, self-born (<s>svayaṃbhu</s>), eternal <s>Brahman</s> — to that <s>Brahman</s>, salutation!

children.text: namastadanuvartibhyo gurubhyaḥ //1-4 //
children.translated_text: [Commentary:] Salutation also to the teachers who follow that [<s>Brahman</s>]! (6.5.1-4)

[Commentary on BṛUp 6.5.1-4:] Now, the complete lineage (<s>vaṃśa</s>) of the teaching. It was introduced [with the topic:] a son endowed with [good] qualities is born through the excellence of [the parents'] character. Therefore, the succession of teachers is recited with the designation referring to [each teacher's] character as the qualifier for the son. These — 'these white' — unmixed, [explained] by the prose (<s>brāhmaṇa</s>). Or alternatively: these <s>Yajus</s> formulas — they are white, meaning pure — this is the meaning.

children.text: iti bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhādhyāyasya pañcamaṃ brāhmaṇam //5//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the sixth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s>. (6.5)

children.text: iti vājasaneyake bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣadi ṣaṣṭhodhyāyaḥ //6//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth <s>adhyāya</s> of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> of the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [school]. (6)

children.text: iti vājasaneyakebṛhadāraṇyakakrameṇāṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ //8//
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>adhyāya</s> in the sequential [numbering] of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> of the <s>Vājasaneya</s> [school]. (8)

children.text: iti śuklayajurvedīyā bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣat saṃpūrṇā
children.translated_text: Thus is the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyakopaniṣad</s> of the <s>Śukla Yajurveda</s> complete.

children.text: oṃ pūrṇamadaḥ pūrṇamidaṃ pūrṇātpūrṇamudacyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. That is full; this is full. From the full, the full arises.

children.text: pūrṇasya pūrṇamādāya pūrṇamevāvaśiṣyate //
children.translated_text: Taking the full from the full, the full alone remains.

children.text: oṃ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ śāntiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>. Peace, peace, peace.
